synopsis: B747 Captain reported fuel was correctly loaded onto the aircraft, but the crossfeed valve was left open. Error was not discovered until midflight. Aircrew applied appropriate switches to solve the issue, but still declared minimum fuel into the arrival airport.
summary: During a ferry flight, the pilot disabled the fuel system logic during preflight, delaying the crossfeed valve warning until low fuel appeared. The crew activated override pumps, declared minimum fuel to avoid arrival delays, and landed normally after a late departure.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported a FLCT SPLR FAULT after takeoff. Crew followed recommended procedures. After discussion with Dispatch, the crew diverted for an uneventful landing.
summary: The Captain experienced a recurring FLCT SPLR FAULT on Engine 2 start and after takeoff, which cleared temporarily after a maintenance-instructed SEC 3 reset. The crew diverted to an alternate airport following ECAM procedures, managing fuel for an uneventful landing with no high roll rates or autopilot disconnects.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported track and altitude deviations resulted when they misunderstood the ATC clearance on arrival into DFW.
summary: The flight crew descended to 10,000 feet during moderate turbulence while mistakenly believing they were on the VKTRY arrival instead of the cleared JOVEM procedure. After ATC corrected them to cross VKTRY between 15,000 and 18,000 feet, the crew climbed back to 15,000 feet, attributing the error to distraction and confusingly similar arrival fixes.

synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported jet blast from a taxiing 757 blew construction materials and barriers across the taxiway and into their aircraft. The left engine was shut down to avoid damage to propellers. Aircraft returned to the gate.
summary: Pilots on a twin-engine aircraft holding on taxiway Echo secured the #1 engine after jet blast from a preceding 757 threw unsecured construction barriers toward the propeller. Maintenance found no damage, allowing the crew to single-engine taxi back to the gate, resulting in an 83-minute delay.

synopsis: Air carrier crew exited PHL Runway 27R on Taxiway K3 and failed to hold short of Taxiway K which resulted in a ground conflict with an aircraft which was forced to stop for them.
summary: The pilot exited runway 27R at taxiway K3 in PHL while Aircraft Y was approaching, resulting in a "cut off" situation. The pilot believed the exit complied with AIM 4-3-20, but ATC disagreed, attributing the conflict to a lack of coordination between tower and ground controllers.

synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported experiencing a runaway aileron trim malfunction. The flight returned to the departure airport after unsuccessful troubleshooting.
summary: During climbout, the First Officer encountered a runaway aileron trim that defaulted to full left wing down despite right trim inputs. The crew completed the emergency checklist, held wings level with control force, and executed a safe landing without evacuation after determining it was unsafe to burn fuel to reduce weight.

synopsis: B757 First Officer described the events leading up to the opening of the R1 door with the slide armed. He believes that he initially disarmed both doors and cracked the L1, but later closed the L1 and opened the R1 when the stairs were noted to be in position at that door. He may have rearmed the door just prior to opening. The slide dropped onto the stairs, but did not inflate.
summary: A flight attendant partially deployed an armed slide on the R1 door during post-flight shutdown after ramp crew moved stairs to that side. The incident likely resulted from the crew member accidentally rearming the slide or failing to disarm it, compounded by distraction from the stair repositioning.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported the stick shaker activated in a seemingly spurious manner not justified by the flown airspeeds.
summary: During a visual approach, the Captain and First Officer experienced momentary stick shaker activation while flying above stall speeds, prompting a go-around. The Captain reported no continuous ignition or stall warning lights and suspects the aircraft's "green line" speed reference is incorrectly set higher than VREF, causing a perception of flying under speed.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported that possible winter ground debris/ice accumulation may have blocked gear from completely retracting upon takeoff. Crew was able to overcome problem and landed normally.
summary: The flight crew experienced a gear disagree warning during initial climb in snowy conditions, likely caused by ice blocking nose gear sensors. After recycling the gear successfully, they continued to the destination and landed safely, though the aircraft was later grounded for maintenance.

synopsis: Pilot reported TRACON issued him a route that included a decommissioned VOR and non-existent airway.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ received a full route clearance from Potomac TRACON containing the non-existent airway V6 due to the decommissioned SKY VOR. The reporter attributed this safety hazard to the controller using obsolete charts or outdated software.

synopsis: Corporate jet with passengers attempted a landing at an uncontrolled airport with heavy traffic in the pattern. Additionally, windshear conditions existed prompting a go-around. Because of the heavy workload there was a lapse in the coordination with ATC.
summary: The crew of a passenger aircraft executing an RNAV approach to Runway 31 performed a go-around due to wind shear and coordinated with jumpers on UNICOM. High workload from gusty winds and pattern traffic caused the crew to neglect contacting ATC for a published missed approach, resulting in a regulatory lapse.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Helicopter encroached on airport airspace without being in contact with UNICOM frequency. Reporter of departing aircraft had near miss with encroaching airplane.
summary: A departing fixed-wing pilot on runway 14 encountered a low-flying helicopter on a collision course at 50 feet AGL. The pilot avoided impact by diving below the tree line, attributing the near miss to the helicopter pilot's inattentive treetop joyriding.

synopsis: BE-55 pilot reported that their autopilot disconnected inadvertently in turbulence which resulted in an altitude and course deviation. Contributing factors included Center radar down, ATC confusion on destination flight plan, a frequency change, and moderate to occasionally severe turbulence which created distressed passengers.
summary: The pilot flying to BGF experienced severe turbulence and an autopilot disconnect after ATC descended the aircraft into clouds due to a lost flight plan and wrong destination. The pilot deviated from altitude while distracted by communication failures and passenger distress, eventually receiving a corrected clearance to climb after clarifying the destination.

synopsis: A pilot had issues with the NAV database in the GPS system. There were also discrepancies as to the functionality of the arrival VOR. The pilot elected to return to point of departure because of these issues.
summary: During a medevac en route to ZZZ, the pilot discovered the Garmin 750 GPS database contained incorrect fixes due to an update activated before its effective date. After ATC reported the ZZZ VOR was NOTAM'd out of service despite no visible NOTAMs, the crew diverted back to the departure airport and logged a maintenance discrepancy.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: I90 TRACON Controller reported on an air carrier Flight Crew report of a near miss with a UAV while on approach to IAH.
summary: An air carrier pilot reported a near miss with an unlit, grey, 3-5 ft tubular UAV at 8,500 ft while approaching IAH in Class-B airspace. The controller could not identify the object on radar, but the crew continued the approach with no further sightings.

synopsis: An aircraft reported severe wake turbulence.
summary: Aircraft X was arriving at 15,000 feet while Aircraft Y stopped short at 14,000 feet. Aircraft Y passed 5-6 miles behind Aircraft X and encountered severe wake turbulence, prompting a call for better wake turbulence awareness.

synopsis: Ramp Supervisor reported that their air carrier's CRJ-700 crews' seem to leave their right engine running long after ground power has been plugged in, jeopardizing ground safety.
summary: A CRJ-700 flight crew kept the right engine running for three minutes while passengers deplaned, delaying ramp access until the ramp supervisor signaled shutdown. The reporter states this common practice compromises employee safety and operational performance by forcing unsafe approaches to running engines.

synopsis: First Officer's seat slid back during first part of takeoff roll. Throttles came briefly out of Takeoff Go Around (TOGA) settings, but were quickly re-set.
summary: During takeoff, the First Officer's seat slid aft due to an unengaged adjustment lever, causing thrust levers to drop from TOGA to climb detent. The Captain restored thrust, the crew continued the flight, and maintenance was notified upon arrival.

synopsis: An Air Taxi First Officer reported receiving an ambiguous ATC clearance which caused them to misidentify the landing aircraft, resulting in a runway incursion and ground conflict.
summary: The flight crew received a confusing clearance to line up and wait behind a landing Beechcraft while another Beechcraft was on final approach. Air Traffic Control subsequently issued an immediate takeoff clearance, which the crew attributed to a retroactive instruction based on an aircraft that had not yet landed.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported the filed arrival into DFW was the FINGR 5 for DAL which is 'ATC assigned only for DFW'. The Captain told the dispatcher they would correct it. After the crew checked in with Center they were cleared for the BRDJE 3 to DFW. The crew never received an amended release.
summary: The Captain discovered a filed FINGR 5 arrival for DFW instead of DAL while 80 miles east of LIT under Memphis ATC. Memphis Center issued a conflicting BRDJE 3 arrival, but the crew resolved the discrepancy before any diversion occurred, completing the flight without event.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer noted his company's iPad charts do not include suitable emergency diversion airports in the area between DEN and SLC.
summary: During a westbound flight over J58 near MLF VOR, the crew identified CDC and SGU as suitable diversion airports but found terminal charts unavailable in their onboard charting product. This lack of data prevented them from safely executing an instrument approach to the nearest suitable airport in an emergency, despite the airports having adequate runway lengths.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew and Local Controller reported the First Officer accepted a takeoff clearance that was not for them and they took off while a business jet was crossing downfield. The Local Controller mistakenly said 'cleared for takeoff' with the call sign of an aircraft on final when he meant to say 'cleared to land.'
summary: An air carrier pilot and a Local Assist controller reported a runway incursion on Runway XXL where a business jet crossed during the carrier's takeoff roll. The incident occurred because the controller mistakenly issued a takeoff clearance to the holding carrier instead of a landing clearance for another flight.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 Captain reported dry ice loaded in the aft cargo bin, a hazmat violation in this aircraft type. Additionally, ground personnel began the pushback without crew clearance after brake release. Ground personnel training appears to be a problem.
summary: The flight crew and rampers on an ERJ175 encountered unauthorized dry ice loading and an unauthorized pushback caused by a tug driver misinterpreting a green nose gear light. The crew corrected the cargo error and stopped the premature pushback, attributing the incident to inadequate ramber training and defective headset communication.

synopsis: On a B737-700 an incorrect MEL was applied for the auto-stow feature of the speed-brake.
summary: The crew and dispatch discovered maintenance incorrectly applied a 737-800 MEL to a 737-700, causing the computer to omit a landing weight penalty. This error resulted in four prior illegal dispatches before the correct MEL was applied and the flight was re-released.

synopsis: B737 Captain was informed by the Lead Flight Attendant that a passenger is down in the aft galley, but it is not necessary to contact Medlink at this time. The Captain disagrees and contacts Medlink, which upsets the lead Flight Attendant.
summary: During cruise, the pilot contacted Medlink regarding an incoherent passenger despite the Lead Flight Attendant's refusal to cooperate or provide medical history. The resulting communication breakdown and the attendant's opposition to seeking medical advice were identified as safety concerns by the pilot.

synopsis: After slowing for the final approach at 4,000 feet, an A320 ECAM alerted ENG 1 THRUST LEVER DISAGREEMENT. The ECAM procedure was completed and the approach continued with the engine at idle. Maintenance found a failed Thrust Level Angle (TLA) Indicator Sensor.
summary: During the base leg of an A320 approach, the number one engine failed to spool up due to a Thrust Lever Angle sensor failure causing a thrust lever disagreement. The crew followed ECAM procedures and landed safely with the number one engine at idle.

synopsis: As he prepared to taxi, a FBO Lineman notified the BE-400XP Captain the GPU plug into the aircraft overheated and damaged the aircraft's ground electrical connector. The connector was deferred by Maintenance.
summary: During engine start, a lineman disconnected the GPU, which subsequently overheated and caught fire, damaging the aircraft's external power receptacle. Maintenance confirmed no structural damage except a possible pin issue, but the FBO refused to provide a written statement regarding the incident.

synopsis: A U.S. air carrier departed MMGL Runway 28 and while climbing through 7,000 feet responded to a TCAS RA from a domestic Mexican airline aircraft speaking Spanish with ATC after initiating a go-around. The event resulted in a NMAC with no prior warning from ATC.
summary: The crew departed MMGL runway 28 and received a TCAS RA to descend at 7,000 feet MSL due to an overtaking airline aircraft executing a go-around. The reporter attributed the conflict to a lack of traffic information from controllers, who were communicating in Spanish with another aircraft.

synopsis: Ramp Agent reported observing a ground crew opening cargo doors and moving belt loaders into position before the number one engine had been shut down and the beacon turned off.
summary: A pilot observed Ramp Service Employees performing unsafe duties on an Airbus A320 at the gate with Engine #1 running at high idle. The crew connected ground power and operated cargo equipment within the safety zone without landing gear chocks, violating Standard Operating Procedures.

synopsis: An Airbus A320 series flight crew reported descending on the CLT IVANE 5 RNAV they were assigned a 250 kt restriction. While in managed speed, the FMC ignored the MAYOS altitude constraint and projected missing the KIYEN altitude constraint. The aircraft had difficulty flying a modified RNAV optimal profile descent.
summary: Pilots flying at FL320 experienced an uncommanded rapid acceleration and descent below the speed window while executing a modified IVANE5 arrival. They manually captured FL220 to stop the deviation, attributing the FMS anomaly to manipulating the optimal profile descent outside database parameters.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A CRJ-900 FO reported receiving an EGPWS alert from a nearby tower while on a visual approach to Runway 14R at OMA. They were outside the FAF and below the glideslope intercept altitude.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to runway 14R at OMA received an EGPWS 'Obstacle' alert while descending toward a 1807 MSL tower. They executed a climb from 2100 to 2400 MSL to avoid the obstacle and subsequently completed a normal landing.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported having to brake abruptly to avoid a string of bag carts while eastbound on Taxiway C at LAX.
summary: While taxiing at LAX at 10 knots, the crew applied maximum brakes to avoid a baggage tug crossing taxiway Charlie, stopping within 5 feet of the vehicle. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the ground vehicle failing to check for clearances before crossing, though all passengers and crew remained uninjured.

synopsis: DHC-8-100 Flight Crew reported receiving a cabin pressure warning at FL220 seven minutes after leveling off. ATC was advised and a descent was initiated with the bag door warning light illuminated passing FL200. The crew elected to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid depressurization and bag door warning at FL220, suspecting a compromised bag door caused the pressurization failure. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 ft, diverted to ZZZ1, and landed safely with no injuries after fire rescue confirmed no structural damage.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported having to make an abrupt stop to avoid a collision with another taxiing aircraft at AFW.
summary: The Captain and First Officer nearly collided with Aircraft Y while taxiing to Runway 16L after ATC cleared Aircraft Y to line up and wait despite it being on a taxiway. The incident occurred because the single controller managing multiple positions lost situational awareness of Aircraft Y's location, resulting in a stop less than 30 feet from the other aircraft's propeller.

synopsis: First Officer of a jumbo cargo aircraft reported a high speed rejected takeoff due to a flap configuration warning light. The takeoff was aborted successfully, however the spoilers failed to deploy as designed resulting in several main gear tires deflating due to aggressive braking and subsequent heat buildup.
summary: The pilot reported a rejected takeoff at 145 knots due to a 'CONFIG FLAPS' warning, followed by manual spoiler deployment. Subsequent communication difficulties and rising brake temperatures led to seven flat tires, leaving the aircraft stuck on an active taxiway as the mechanic advised against towing.

synopsis: While in the traffic pattern, a SR20 instructor reported an abnormal cylinder head indication. He advised the Tower and made a successful precautionary landing.
summary: The instructor reported high CHT and engine roughness while on upwind, requesting priority landing. Tower cleared the aircraft for Runway ZA, where a precautionary landing was made; CHT and engine operation returned to normal after landing.

synopsis: Falcon 50 flight crew reported the cabin did not pressurize during climbout because the engine bleed air switches were off. They selected switches to AUTO and regained pressurization. Crew returned to departure airport to have O2 masks reset.
summary: Maintenance replaced a fuel XFR pump switch overnight, inadvertently leaving all three Bleed Air switches OFF. The crew discovered the error at FL230 when cabin altitude warnings triggered, forcing a descent and return to reset masks after selecting the switches to AUTO.

synopsis: Hawker 4000 Captain reported being struck on the left wingtip by a bag cart rolling in the wind as he taxied out of the FBO. The engines were shut down and the aircraft was towed back to the ramp for maintenance.
summary: The pilot and First Officer taxied a company aircraft in strong winds when an unsecured FBO baggage cart wrapped around the left wingtip. The crew stopped the aircraft, sustaining damage to the left navigation and recognition lights, while passengers were later rebooked on a replacement flight.

synopsis: PA28 flight instructor and trainee reported a runway excursion on takeoff when the trainee's foot got stuck with full right rudder and brake engaged.
summary: During a student flight review takeoff, the student's foot became stuck under the aircraft after applying the right brake, preventing rudder release. The instructor attempted to correct with left rudder, but the aircraft skidded off the runway to the right.

synopsis: RV6 pilot reported a ground loop during landing with winds reported as calm. Once stopped near the windsock a direct tailwind of 5-7 knots was noted.
summary: The pilot landed on Runway 3 based on AWOS calm wind reports but encountered a 5-7 knot tailwind, causing a ground loop and right landing strut damage. The pilot attributed the incident to relying solely on AWOS without verifying wind conditions via CTAF or the windsock.

synopsis: BD700 Captain reported that while using a 75 ft runway to taxi, the bottom of the wing made contact with the nose of one of the parked aircraft. The runway was reportedly being used as a designated event parking area.
summary: The pilot taxied a large aircraft along a runway used for parking and struck the left wing on a protruding parked aircraft due to insufficient clearance and lack of wing walkers. The incident resulted from inadequate ground guidance and improper aircraft positioning, prompting future reliance on outside personnel for confined taxi operations.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain climbing out of SHV reported taking evasive action to avoid a small aircraft.
summary: During departure, the pilot experienced weak radio reception and missed an ATC altitude reduction from 12,000 to 5,000 feet, causing a TCAS RA with a single-engine aircraft. The pilot executed an avoidance maneuver, and the controller later admitted he did not realize the crew's climb profile would prevent timely compliance with the new altitude.

synopsis: PA23 pilot experienced an unexplained power loss on the right engine at 9,000 feet. The aircraft was allowed to descend from assigned altitude while troubleshooting before engine power was restored and assigned altitude was regained. The event repeated within ten minutes, but the reporter elected to continue to the destination with VFR weather.
summary: The Aztec pilot experienced a sudden right engine power loss likely due to a fuel issue while in IFR conditions, causing an unintentional descent to 8,000–8,500 feet. After regaining control and stabilizing the engine, the pilot descended to 5,000 feet to land uneventfully at ZZZ for evaluation.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate Captain reported a delay in starting the descent on the KEFFR 3 Arrival to SNA which led to an overshoot at an intermediate level off. ZLA Controller reported a loss of separation with an aircraft descending to PSP.
summary: Pilots and controllers reported a loss of separation between two aircraft on the KEFFR THREE arrival due to conflicting descent instructions and a missing altitude restriction. The controller's failure to issue a restriction to separate the arrival from landing traffic, combined with confusing expedite commands, caused one aircraft to descend below FL180.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported using Foreflight to find the TPA for 01G and inadvertently selected the altitude for PEO due to the lack of familiarity with the Foreflight A/FD tab. PEO has a 570 foot lower field elevation resulting in the traffic pattern being flown very low initially.
summary: A pilot using Foreflight mistakenly viewed traffic pattern altitude for Penn Yan instead of Perry Warsaw while on downwind. This error caused the aircraft to fly too low over houses before the pilot corrected the altitude and identified the mistake on the ground.

synopsis: Grumman American AA-5 pilot reported flying in VFR conditions when the weather closed in and they found themselves in IMC.
summary: The pilot and a non-pilot passenger flew a WAAS-GPS equipped aircraft VFR at 1,000ft AGL in rain and mist, descending below terrain and briefly entering restricted airspace while drawn to sunlight. They landed safely but aborted the trip due to worsening destination weather, attributing the low altitude to following weather lower than intended.

synopsis: While flying in a Cessna Skymaster T337 in icing conditions the right wing de-icing boot failed to de-ice the wing.
summary: The pilot encountered moderate icing and suspected de-icing boot failure during an approach, while also discovering the pitot heat was accidentally switched off. Despite asymmetric ice accumulation and unreliable airspeed, the pilot hand-flew the aircraft to a safe landing and subsequently requested a mechanic inspection.

synopsis: MSP Local Controller reported of a windshear at the airport. Reporter stated they should stop arrivals to a specific runway 35. Arrivals continued for an other 22 minutes before stopping.
summary: A controller reported that despite multiple wind shear reports and strong gusts, Minneapolis-St. Paul continued arrivals to Runway 35 for 22 minutes instead of stopping them per SOPs. The controller stated they would have halted operations to Runway 35 and departures for safety as previously briefed.

synopsis: MSP Controller reported of windshear at the airport and management not changing the runway configuration.
summary: Pilots reported 15-knot airspeed fluctuations on Runway 35 during converging operations in gusty winds, but supervisors failed to require the term "windshear" per MSP SOP. Consequently, operations continued despite a direct violation of safety procedures by the tower management team.

synopsis: PCT Supervisor reported failing to not make the correct system macro entries after de-combining a sector. The Restricted Area status displayed not in use on the Controller's radar display when it was actually in use. The Controller allowed an aircraft to enter the Restricted Area.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X at 8,000 feet into an active restricted area because a STARS display error showed it inactive after sector decombination. The controller corrected the flight path after the receiving controller advised the true status, noting this known software issue has occurred previously.

synopsis: B737 First Officer experienced a loss of cabin pressurization at FL360 while deviating around weather. ATC is advised and the flight descends to 10,000 feet diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL360 while deviating for weather, the crew received a cabin altitude warning and descended to divert after determining they could not control the rising cabin altitude. The aircraft landed uneventfully with EMS standing by, following coordination with ATC, dispatch, and cabin crew.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported being cleared to cross Runway 25R at LAX, but made an incorrect turn and ended up on the runway. They exited at the next intersection.
summary: The First Officer and Captain inadvertently entered Runway 25R while taxiing instead of crossing it on Taxiway P. The First Officer attributed the runway incursion to failing to verbally alert the Captain during radio communications, noting that gestures were too slow to prevent the error.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported that shortly after landing and while exiting the Runway, a left engine low pressure fuel pump failed which resulted in a decreasing RPM and high EGT. The engine was shutdown, the QRH completed and the flight taxied to the gate.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine failure during taxi, indicated by low oil pressure, rising EGT, and N1 dropping to 5.0. The Captain ordered fuel cutoff and QRH procedures, securing the engine before taxiing to the gate where maintenance identified a left engine low-pressure pump issue.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported responding to a 'Check Weights' message in flight and discovered that there was a discrepancy in the weight and balance information. They were approximately 20,000 pounds heavier because of a mistake in the total souls on board.
summary: Flight crew discovered a 20,000 lb weight discrepancy caused by an erroneous load closeout showing 29 instead of 137 passengers. The aircraft departed safely using calculated V speeds, but the error risked incorrect stabilizer trim settings due to a policy gap preventing passenger count verification.

synopsis: At approximately 100 knots, the A330 Crew was instructed by the Tower to reject the takeoff due to a runway incursion alert.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff at 100 KIAS after Tower instruction regarding a taxiway-runway conflict. Following brake cooling, the aircraft taxied to the terminal for refueling and departed, though the reporter noted the wet runway and heavy weight could have created a hazardous situation.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported a bird strike near rotation and the subsequent return to the departure airport minutes later.
summary: The flight crew experienced a bird strike during takeoff roll at Runway XX, causing Engine 1 to surge, fail, and generate severe vibrations. Despite workload saturation and procedural errors, the Captain maintained control, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: A B737-800 aft cargo compartment floor was damaged after six 210 pound unsecured pallets were placed in it. The crew was additionally concerned about the unsecure cargo shifting at Vr. The pallets were removed and the aircraft taken out of service.
summary: The First Officer and Crew Chief discovered heavy, unsecured metal cargo damaged the B737-800's rear cargo floor during preflight, grounding the aircraft. The reporter attributed the damage to improper loading of dense items that could not be anchored, warning that a shift during takeoff could have caused a tailstrike or catastrophic control issues.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported being confused by the BRDJE3 arrival to DFW, which they were originally cleared for, and the SEEVR3 which was what ATC believed they issued to the crew. Both arrivals use the same waypoints to BRDJE and both use BRDJE and SEEVR. BRDJE3 is SEEVR.BRDJE3 in the FMC and SEEVR3 is SEEVR.SEEVR3.
summary: During descent to FL240 at DFW, the flight crew descended via the BRDJE3 arrival instead of the amended SEEVR3 due to ATC failing to communicate the change. This miscommunication, compounded by similar arrival names and shared fixes, required a 360-degree turn to correct the route, though the flight completed safely.

synopsis: A PA31 pilot reported abnormal engine indications while attempting to set takeoff power. Numerous run ups and checks fail to achieve normal power and the aircraft is grounded. Maintenance Control indicated that they have been having trouble with fuel controllers for the past six months.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine power failure during takeoff preparation on a Chieftain, where RPM would not exceed 1,400 despite normal manifold pressure. Maintenance attributed the issue to known fuel controller problems, resulting in the flight being cancelled and the crew returning via a reserve pilot.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Aircrew encountered a tow aircraft with glider attached while practicing an ILS approach. Evasive action was taken. Tow aircraft flew through holding fix for the ILS.
summary: A pilot practicing an ILS approach at 4,000 feet encountered a glider under tow at the same altitude near the HAIGS intersection. The pilot executed evasive action due to the tow plane's lack of landing lights and failure to coordinate with air traffic control or monitor relevant frequencies.

synopsis: A pilot shut down a single engine after it was running rough and then executed a dead stick landing. There was minimal damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of an Experimental Home-built aircraft experienced excessive engine roughness at 5,500 MSL, necessitating a dead stick landing in a clearing with minimal damage. Subsequent inspection revealed the cause was improperly secured engine counterweights.

synopsis: Fuel selector switched off during take off then rapidly corrected. Engine quit momentarily then take off continued.
summary: The pilot accidentally moved the fuel selector during takeoff, causing an engine failure. After restarting the engine upon touchdown, the pilot continued the takeoff because the runway was too short to stop.

synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported that strong winds from surrounding weather caused the aircraft to drift off the centerline on a wet runway while lining up for takeoff. The pilot cancelled the takeoff request and re-attempted the departure successfully.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing to hold on the runway, the aircraft skidded right and crossed the centerline. Differential power on the left engine corrected the path, leading to a cancelled takeoff clearance, an exit, and a subsequent successful departure.

synopsis: Beech 58 pilot reported the nose gear collapsed upon landing. The aircraft was secured and evacuated.
summary: The pilot landed a twin-engine aircraft in gusty 20-knot crosswinds with 10 knots over Vref. Upon lowering the nose gear to the runway, it collapsed, stopping both propellers, though no fire occurred and the pilot immediately secured the engines and notified FSS.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported inadvertently entering Restricted Area 3002 after changing his destination and losing GPS signal in his portable GPS.
summary: The pilot unintentionally entered a restricted area while en route to a fuel stop at Thomasville Regional Airport. The infringement resulted from failing to notice the proximity on Foreflight, low cockpit lighting, and a temporary GPS signal loss.

synopsis: A PHL Tower Controller reported of a pilot making comments about the taxi instructions. The pilot complained about the way he was to taxi to the gate. The reporter advised the LOA was a safety hazard and created traps.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a pilot argued with Ground Control about taxi routes after landing, causing distracting transmissions. The controller stated the new Letter of Agreement creates safety hazards, including loss of positive control and runway compression, and requested a return to previous procedures.

synopsis: A B757 Captain reported a flap anomaly during approach. Checklists to apply were reported to have been somewhat ambiguous but the flight landed uneventfully.
summary: The PNF and First Officer experienced a TE Flap Disagree warning during approach, causing confusion over conflicting checklist landing configurations. After consulting maintenance, they landed with leading edge slats only and 30-degree reference, resulting in a safe termination with no brake overheating.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a near collision with a bus while taxiing at ORD.
summary: The pilot stopped the aircraft during initial taxi after observing a ground employee bus speeding on a parallel service road. The pilot determined the aircraft's turning wing would have struck the bus, which subsequently stopped without causing injury or damage.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Flight crew reported arriving at their gate late, due to hotel transportation problems, to find their flight in the process of boarding with no Flight Attendants on board. The passengers are asked to deplane and another security sweep of the aircraft is accomplished, before reboarding and departing late.
summary: Due to a late van, the crew arrived late to find gate agents had boarded 120 passengers without verifying crew presence. The flight was delayed for deplaning and re-screening, attributed to agents prioritizing on-time departures over standard boarding procedures.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported receiving a terrain warning received during a visual approach at night. The warning was triggered by the uniqueness of surrounding terrain, man-made structures, and the descent rate during approach. The crew executed mild evasive procedures and landed uneventfully.
summary: The crew received a GPWS terrain warning and a tower low altitude alert while descending visually into AVP over a ridge line north-east of the final approach course. The First Officer executed an escape maneuver, and the aircraft landed uneventfully after the crew confirmed adequate clearance from the 2,125-foot tower.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Taxi flight crew reported a nose gear collapsed upon landing roll out. No abnormal indications were present prior to landing.
summary: During landing, the nose gear handle snapped up after initial touchdown, causing the aircraft to rest on the nose gear doors with grinding metal and a blaring unsafe horn. The Pilot in Command and Second in Command escaped without injury, and no fire or fuel leakage was observed.

synopsis: A B767 crew member's child was inadvertently admitted to the cockpit in flight.
summary: During cruise, a relief First Officer and a Flight Attendant allowed a non-crew child to enter the cockpit due to a misunderstanding of a request to view Greenland. The Captain secured the door and had them exit, attributing the incident to the Flight Attendant's failure to clarify the instruction or refuse the unauthorized entry.

synopsis: A321 flight crew experienced an ECAM message for FUEL R WING TK OVERFLOW during fueling. The fueler is instructed to stop fueling but not before fuel is vented out the right wing vent causing a fuel spill. The right wing had been filled beyond capacity, indicating that auto shut off had not occurred.
summary: During pre-flight fueling of an A321, a fueler ignored a hose drip and overfilled the right wing tank, causing a 20-30 gallon spill and triggering an overflow ECAM. The crew stopped fueling, evacuated passengers, and maintenance transferred the excess fuel, attributing the incident to the fueler's failure to monitor the operation.

synopsis: At the start of the takeoff roll flight attendants witnessed flames coming out of one engine and informed the Captain. The Captain elected to do an immediate abort at low speed. The flight returned to the gate.
summary: The Captain aborted takeoff at 70 knots after a flight attendant reported flames from the left engine, despite no cockpit fire warnings. Fire trucks inspected the aircraft and found no fire or damage, leading to a tow back to the gate.

synopsis: Captain reported malfunction of the APU at the gate resulting in smoke throughout the aircraft. Crash Fire Rescue (CFR) was called while personnel left the aircraft. APU was shut down.
summary: During preflight, smoke entered the flight deck from air vents, intensifying when air conditioning packs were reselected. Onboard mechanics identified the APU compartment as the source after opening access doors, leading to a full depower and CFR inspection which found no fire.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they encountered birds just after takeoff. One bird is believed to have struck the engine resulting in some blade damage.
summary: During takeoff, a bird crossed the flight path and entered the left engine, causing a pitch change heard by the onboard mechanic. Post-flight inspection confirmed a bird strike that damaged fan blade 17 beyond repair, though the flight proceeded to destination with normal engine indications.

synopsis: When clearing an MEL item on a B737-700 the Mechanic found an improper seal installed (zip tie) on a life vest pouch. The zip tie was installed by someone other than Maintenance.
summary: A mechanic cleared an MEL on aircraft X by removing a zip tie installed by an OPS supervisor that prevented life vest use. The mechanic replaced the seal, while the Captain remained unaware of the unauthorized zip tie.

synopsis: Five minutes prior to scheduled departure, the leader of the pushback crew advised the B787 Captain that the ground crew was ready for pushback with no response. The Captain eventually responded that he was not ready and the tug was taken to push another aircraft. While waiting for the tug to return the Captain became ready for pushback, turned on the beacon, and released the brakes without consulting with the ground crew.
summary: A ground handler reported that the flight crew released brakes and moved the aircraft without a tow tractor, startling a mechanic. The handler intervened to stop the movement, and after the tug arrived, the pushback and departure were completed normally.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Tower issued a clearance not coordinated with TRACON. Pilot and ATC resolved the ambiguity while airborne.
summary: The pilot filed an IFR flight plan with a /U equipment suffix but received a conflicting clearance from SMO Ground to fly direct to Seal Beach instead of the filed SMON7 TEC route. This discrepancy caused confusion at 5,000 feet when the en route controller expected the pilot to follow the TEC route, while the direct clearance inadvertently aligned the aircraft with LAX approach segments.

synopsis: A BE55 pilot reported receiving an altimeter setting of 30.41 prior to departure but enters 29.41 in error. On departure he leveled off 1,000 feet above the assigned altitude of 3,000 feet causing a loss of separation.
summary: The pilot departed HAO in a Baron with an incorrect altimeter setting of 29.41 instead of 30.41, causing the aircraft to fly at 4,000 feet while believing it was at 3,000. This error created a separation conflict with another Baron, requiring deviation instructions and a post-flight report to ATC.

synopsis: CE550 Captain reported an airborne conflict with a single engine low wing aircraft at 3,000 feet while on right downwind for Runway 19 at TEB. Evasive action is taken.
summary: A pilot on right downwind for ILS 19 at TEB at 3,000 feet observed a co-altitude TCAS target and executed a climb after an initial turn. The other pilot admitted violating Class B airspace, and the flight landed uneventfully.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported an airspace violation while experiencing radio difficulties. Pilot questioned if he should have continued inbound or if ATC was ignoring him do to traffic load.
summary: A pilot flying a general aviation aircraft into APA entered Class D airspace without establishing two-way radio contact with the tower after a delayed handoff from Denver Approach. The pilot attributed the communication failure to potential radio malfunction or controller overload, resulting in an outbound turn before landing.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported detecting a slight drop in RPM during climbout followed by an oil warning light and low oil pressure.
summary: The pilot of an SR22T experienced an oil pressure drop and warning light at 5,000 feet shortly after departure, prompting an immediate return. The crew attributed the rapid oil consumption to a fault following a cylinder replacement, leading to an engine removal for manufacturer inspection.

synopsis: Bellanca Viking pilot reported exiting the runway at high speed, resulting in landing gear collapse.
summary: The pilot exited the marked runway and turned too fast on a rough taxi area, causing ruts to collapse the right gear. All three landing gears were damaged with minor cosmetic wing contact, but no prop strike or structural damage occurred.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft Pilot departed from an uncontrolled field while on the incorrect UNICOM frequency. Pilot experienced a near miss with another departing aircraft on a crossing runway.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing for departure on runway 9, failed to retune the radio to UNICOM after receiving an IFR clearance via cellphone. This error prevented communication with traffic on runway 3, resulting in an inadequate separation during takeoff behind another aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported not being handed off to MYF Tower by SCT TRACON. Pilot was VFR and did not avoid delta airspace. Pilot reported he had been under IFR training lately and was expecting a handoff from the TRACON to the Tower.
summary: A VFR pilot descending into MYF Class D airspace entered the zone without a handoff from SoCal Approach due to an incorrect assumption about ATC instructions. The pilot subsequently contacted the tower on the correct frequency, received traffic instructions, and completed a flustered landing, attributing the deviation to overreliance on IFR procedures.

synopsis: ZLA controllers reported a UAV that could not accept holding instructions and was not allowed in restricted airspace. One Controller was confused and had busy airspace. The MOS did not have any special instructions to help and the UAV made circles until a resolution was found.
summary: An air traffic controller handling Aircraft X in a busy sector faced confusion when the pilot requested a "delay" instead of standard holding instructions to avoid restricted airspace. The resulting operational distraction and lack of clear drone procedures created an unsafe situation, though no incident occurred.

synopsis: TWF Tower Controller reported of a pilot that reported a UAV was 200 feet above the pilot's aircraft at 5500 feet MSL. Controller reported there is a UAS field 3 miles south of the airport and this was the second time this has happened.
summary: A VFR pilot at 5,500 feet reported a UAS operating 200 feet above his altitude within Twin Falls Class Delta airspace, exceeding the 800-foot AGL limit. The controller attributed the violation to the UAS operator's lack of real-time altitude equipment and warned of future accident risks.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported responding to a TCAS RA on approach to DEN.
summary: The crew encountered a TCAS climb alert while descending to 10,000 ft on downwind to Denver due to unseen VFR traffic. Communication issues with ATC and the required climb resulted in a high, tight approach that nearly became unstabilized before a safe landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew reported communication difficulties with their pushback crew during pushback at LGA. The instructions from Ground Control were somewhat complicated and the flight crew was unable to talk to the tug driver while he was operating the tug.
summary: The flight crew and pushback tug driver at LGA experienced a dangerous pushback where the driver ignored multiple radio commands to stop and reposition the aircraft on Taxiway A. The incident occurred because the driver claimed he could not listen to the headset while driving, resulting in a complete loss of communication until the crew flashed the taxi light to halt the tug.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an aircraft swap caused a departure delay for an international flight. Some flight attendants go illegal and were taken off the flight as reserves were summoned. The flight departed with only 13 of the 15 flight attendants on the weight and balance and without the flight crew being aware.
summary: The flight crew departed a replacement aircraft after maintenance issues and crew scheduling conflicts caused delays, resulting in an invalid weight and balance due to unreported cabin crew changes. The crew reported that ground and operations personnel prioritized departure over safety, leaving the flight with incorrect staffing and weight data.

synopsis: B747-400 Captain reported returning to the departure airport when they experienced an engine failure shortly after takeoff.
summary: During climbout, the flight crew experienced a loud bang and shudder, resulting in ENG FAILURE 2 and GEN DISC 2. They secured the #2 engine, dumped 200,000 pounds of fuel, and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reported going around at low altitude from an approach to Runway 4R at EWR due to windshear. They then discovered that they were in conflict with a departure from Runway 4L and level off at 1,500 feet just as TCAS announces the conflict. Post flight reveals that the EWR2 SID and the missed approach procedure for Runway 4L are initially identical.
summary: The crew of an MD-11 executing a go-around from Runway 4R at EWR due to wind shear encountered a departing regional jet from Runway 4L. They avoided a potential conflict by leveling at 1,500 feet and turning right, attributing the risk to crossing departure paths and radio congestion.

synopsis: MD-11 SLAT DISAG alert was received during slat retraction after takeoff. The SLAT DISAG checklist was completed, fuel dumped, and the crew returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a stick shaker and Level 2 'Slats Disag' alert immediately after slat retraction during climb to 16,000 ft. They completed the associated checklists, dumped fuel to reduce gross weight, and landed safely using a 28/EXT configuration.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported experiencing a great deal of confusion during a weather diversion to DFW which resulted in the flight almost landing at DAL. Factors cited as contributing included pilot unfamiliarity with the area, communication issues with ATC, weather, and fuel concerns.
summary: The crew diverted from Dallas Love Field (DAL) to Dallas Fort Worth (DFW) due to severe weather but mistakenly approached DAL runway 13L instead. The error resulted from high workload, unfamiliarity with the area, and MFD display issues, leading to a go-around at 750 feet after the DAL tower questioned their destination.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported a cracked right forward wind screen at FL320. QRH procedures were complied with and the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot reported that the right forward windshield arched and spider webbed at FL320, likely due to an electrical short in the window heat. The outer pane shattered but remained intact, prompting a QRH-compliant descent and diversion without incident.

synopsis: B757-200 First Officer reported he and the Captain committed several errors on their flight because of fatigue and workload.
summary: Fatigued pilots on a six-day pairing failed to meet a 9,000 ft crossing restriction at DQO due to FMS programming difficulties and an unexpected auto-flight speed bug failure at 10,000 ft. The crew manually intervened to stabilize the descent in IMC conditions, attributing the event to fatigue, complex routing, and system anomalies.

synopsis: B737 flight crew was informed by ATC that they were 400 to 500 feet low as they crossed each waypoint on the RAVNN6 arrival to BWI. However, the FMC showed the crossings being made correctly. After descending below FL180 and setting the altimeters to the airport setting, the crossings were made correctly.
summary: Pilots flying a Boeing arrival into BWI on RAVNN6 reported the FMC calculated VNAV paths 400–500 feet low above FL180 despite correct standard pressure settings. The crew intervened to prevent restriction violations, suspecting the FMC incorrectly applied the airport QNH from the forecast page while the aircraft remained in standard pressure.

synopsis: Commercial Drone Operator reported having conducted a photo shoot job using a company-owned drone within 500 feet of personnel on the ground which is a violation of their authorization to film during commercial UAV operations.
summary: A UAV pilot with a Section 333 Exemption violated the 500-foot proximity rule while filming a commercial golf course, flying 20 to 200 feet from people. The pilot attributed the violation to ignorance of the requirement for a Motion Picture and Television Operations Manual and plans to cease such operations while applying for the manual.

synopsis: While taxiing in a J3 Piper Cub, a large helicopter was passing over so the Pilot of the J3 Cub stopped and set his brakes. The rotor wash was strong wash enough to move the airplane.
summary: A pilot on taxiway Hotel stopped their 743-pound empty aircraft to avoid a large helicopter proceeding to a helipad. Strong rotor wash moved the aircraft despite set brakes, leading the pilot to call for helicopter regulation similar to fixed-wing aircraft.

synopsis: A C150 pilot experienced an engine failure in the flare after a 5.9 hour flight. Post flight revealed that there were 4.9 usable gallons of fuel remaining in the left tank that apparently could not get to the engine.
summary: The pilot of a C-150 experienced an engine stoppage on final approach due to fuel exhaustion in the right tank, despite gauges indicating fuel remained. After a partial restart using the primer, the engine failed again, requiring a tow to the ramp where maintenance confirmed a fuel system issue rather than an engine failure.

synopsis: A Piper Arrow made a gear-up landing on a highway due to an engine failure. The engine failed due to loss of oil because of an incorrect 'quick drain' oil plug installed.
summary: A mechanic installed an incorrect quick drain valve on a Piper Arrow during an oil change, causing oil loss and engine failure at cruising altitude. The pilot executed a gear-up landing on a highway, sustaining airframe damage but no injuries.

synopsis: A departing BE99 aircraft assigned 3,000 feet climbed to 3600 feet conflicting with 4,000 foot crossing traffic.
summary: A Local Control trainee issued conflicting altitude clearances to a departing prop aircraft, causing it to climb into an arriving aircraft at 4000 feet. The resulting unsafe proximity was attributed to ambiguous phraseology regarding SID versus radar vector clearances, leading to a pilot deviation and a collision alert.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU Controller instructed a descending aircraft to maintain 13,000 feet for opposite direction traffic. The Controller did not realize the flight crew did not hear and acknowledge the clearance resulting in a loss of required separation.
summary: An ARTCC controller and a trainee Radar Assist managed Aircraft X and Y during arrival, where incomplete coordination and a missed readback of an altitude amendment to 13,000 feet caused Aircraft Y to descend below its clearance. This resulted in potential loss of separation as Aircraft X descended through 12,000 feet while Aircraft Y descended to 11,400 feet before climbing back.

synopsis: BUR Local Controller reported of a loss of separation due to lack of understanding of wake turbulence rules.
summary: An air traffic controller on Local Control cleared a B757 and another aircraft for takeoff from intersecting runways based on inaccurate RECAT briefings and supervisor approval. The controller attributed the incident to premature briefing on unimplemented rules and management confirmation of the procedure.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported misunderstanding an ATC clearance on arrival into SMF.
summary: The flight crew descended to FL280 while en route to SMF, initially believing they were cleared for the SUUTR 2 arrival before ATC clarified to maintain FL280. Although ATC later queried a possible pilot deviation, the crew reported no altitude deviation or separation issues, attributing the incident to ambiguous clearance phrasing.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported receiving less than he felt was appropriate cooperation from ATC during a passenger illness event.
summary: The flight crew managed an in-flight medical emergency involving an initially unresponsive passenger who later stabilized with oxygen and IV fluids. After ATC denied priority handling and a landing opposite direction, the crew declared an urgent situation, landed uneventfully, and deplaned the passenger despite some confusion with ground EMTs.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported receiving an EICAS message LE FLAPS ASYM on approach.
summary: During approach at 4000 ft, the crew received an LE Flap Asym message after slowing to 180 knots, causing a missed approach and non-normal landing setup. The PF and FO managed the situation with good CRM, executing an uneventful ILS landing at 175–180 KIAS with minimal brake temperatures.

synopsis: An EMB-190 Captain reported requesting an autoland from the Tower in VMC in order to return the system to service after maintenance. The response is OK. During the flare, Ground Control taxis an aircraft through the localizer requiring the Captain to take over manually.
summary: Pilots conducting an autoland function check in VMC conditions had to disconnect the autopilot when ATC allowed an aircraft to taxi through the ILS critical area, causing erratic localizer signals. The reporter attributed the incident to ATC error for failing to protect the critical area during the approach.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported extreme fatigue resulted from his three day assignment that included a 'red eye' leg on day two.
summary: A pilot reported that a company pairing with mid-trip red-eye legs caused severe fatigue, resulting in nearly 29 hours awake and falling asleep while driving home. The pilot attributed this unsafe condition to scheduling practices that prioritized legal compliance over human factors and adequate rest.

synopsis: A DHC8-100 flight crew experienced the failure of the primary inverter detected initially by the sound of the circuit breaker tripping and a puff of white smoke, followed by warning lights. The crew elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at 11,000 feet, the pilot flying reported a circuit breaker pop and smoke from the captain's panel, causing instrument failure. The crew diverted to ZZZ, landed safely with no injuries, and attributed the event to a primary and auxiliary inverter malfunction.

synopsis: A Challenger 300 crew reported that due to incorrect fuel consumption information they had to divert during a gear down ferry flight.
summary: A pilot conducting a gear-down ferry flight diverted due to critically low fuel caused by dispatch providing an incorrect 8% fuel burn increase instead of the manual's 80%. The crew landed with emergency fuel after discovering the performance data error, which the pilot attributed to missing manual modules and a lack of clear guidance.

synopsis: B737 crew reported loss of pressurization shortly after level off. Crew executed an emergency descent, complied with procedures, and returned to departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a cabin altitude warning at FL310, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 ft where pressurization stabilized in Standby Mode. The crew returned to land without injury, suspecting a Pressurization Mode Controller malfunction or indicator fault.

synopsis: After takeoff in an Airbus A300, the crew got an ECAM Warning of a 'Main Deck Cargo Fire'. There was a thick Air Conditioning Pack smell.
summary: The crew reported a main deck cargo fire ECAM and AC pack smell after takeoff. They executed an overweight visual approach with fire trucks meeting them on the runway, which found no hot spots, leading to a taxi back to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported not reading the 10-7A crew briefing page for LAS requiring that crews departing maintenance spots 1-3 contact Ground Control for coordination. The aircraft had to be pulled back into the spot after pushing back onto Taxiway Delta without clearance.
summary: The First Officer reported that during pushback from an LAS maintenance spot, the aircraft was pushed onto Taxiway Delta without clearance, blocking traffic. The incursion occurred because the crew missed a 10-7A note requiring ground control coordination for this specific ramp area.

synopsis: During inspection on a B757 engine due to a bird strike, company supervisor threatened the inspectors with insubordination if they inspected beyond what was required per the maintenance card.
summary: Three inspectors and a supervisor disagreed on the scope of a Fluorescent Penetrant Inspection for a 757 engine bird strike. The supervisor mandated inspecting only the visible strike area on the Outlet Guide Vanes, threatening insubordination charges for extending the inspection, which the crew feared violated FAA safety standards.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna pilot reported an NMAC with another Cessna while rolling out on final to FHR.
summary: A pilot executing a traffic pattern at a non-tower airport observed a Cessna on the runway centerline below during final approach. The pilot performed a go-around after the intruder, who had been handed off by Approach Control, reported overflying the field.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: SAT Approach Controller reported a loss of separation due to two aircraft possibly taking each other's instructions. Reporter stated there is a language barrier with one of the pilots and this pilot is a problem every time they are in the area.
summary: An Approach West controller managed Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during IFR arrivals, where Aircraft Y failed to follow multiple heading and altitude instructions. The controller attributed the resulting spacing conflict and re-sequencing to Aircraft Y's pilot consistently delaying instruction execution due to a language barrier and non-compliance.

synopsis: DAY Controller reported an airborne conflict that was not resolved by Approach Control. Local DAY Control resolved the situation.
summary: CMH Approach cleared Aircraft X for a visual approach to runway 6L without resolving a conflict with Aircraft Y, causing X to descend directly toward Y. The DAY controller intervened to prevent loss of separation, but the reporter cited CMH's failure to resolve conflicts prior to clearance as the dangerous cause.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: CKB Controller reported an aircraft returned to the airport due to an opened cargo door. The Controller forgot to issue an approach clearance back to the airport.
summary: An air traffic controller assisted Aircraft X, which departed with a cargo door opening and reported incorrect Mode C altitude, by guiding it to a safe landing. The controller admitted forgetting to issue a visual approach clearance due to the urgency of the situation but confirmed the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: Aircraft on a SID off one airport was in direct conflict with a VFR departure from another airport next to it.
summary: A departing pilot and ATC controllers reported a near-midair collision between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during departure due to delayed frequency transfer and poor coordination with an adjacent airport. The pilot executed an immediate left turn to avoid the conflict, and the aircraft passed without incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: ZAB Controller reported of an aircraft under his control that was lower than the MIA. Controller climbed aircraft, but had already entered the higher airspace, resulting in an airspace deviation.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an immediate climb to FL120 for Aircraft X at FL110 after an MSAW alert indicated a conflict with a FL115 block. The aircraft entered the block at FL111 and cleared FL115 shortly after, an event the controller attributed to a simple oversight.

synopsis: ERI TRACON Controller reported of a situation where he thought he had time to do a few tasks, but ended having to point out an aircraft at the last minute.
summary: An air traffic controller working West radar became distracted by a student pilot's routing request and failed to monitor Aircraft X. This distraction caused Aircraft X to approach Dresdens airspace without a point out, requiring the controller to immediately contact Dresden sector to resolve the situation.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer described a windshear event on final to ABQ Runway 21 which resulted in a go-around and ultimately a Runway 8 approach and uneventful landing. A flap overspeed occurred during the go-around.
summary: The First Officer and Captain encountered windshear and a microburst during an RNAV approach to ABQ, triggering a go-around and flap overspeed warning. After holding and declining Runway 21 due to shifting winds, they successfully landed on Runway 8 following a second approach.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer became highly distracted after mis-programming the FMS for a visual approach. The Captain commented First Officer's personal matters made him unable to perform his flying duties well.
summary: The First Officer, distracted by personal difficulties, failed to descend properly on a visual approach due to incorrect LNAV/VNAV programming and missed a Tower landing clearance. The Captain intervened to disengage automation and follow the ILS, resulting in a safe landing and subsequent taxi clearance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported becoming unstable inside DATLE after a late runway change and an intercept vector just outside DATLE in IMC. A caution obstacle is heard and a go-around is initiated. The second approach is successful.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around on a Delta flight during an ILS approach to Runway 31R in IMC after ATC issued a late runway change and a tight vector that caused an excessive descent rate and obstacle caution. The crew subsequently completed a safe second approach and landing after requesting a wider intercept distance.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported the rudder trim required 5 units of left trim during climb but increased to 15 units at cruise with 8-9 unit of aileron trim. The flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported progressive left trim drift during climb and cruise, requiring up to 15 units with no rudder or yoke movement. The Captain ordered a return to the departure airport, where the crew landed the aircraft overweight with no further incident.

synopsis: A regional jet flight crew reported experiencing a minimum fuel condition due to ongoing delays at the destination airport, which were attributed to multiple runway changes. They also cited their company's fuel policy as a contributing factor to their fuel situation.
summary: Pilots reported that ATC repeatedly changed runways and vectored them off course at DCA, causing fuel to drop to minimum levels and a brief flap overspeed during configuration. The crew attributed the near-emergency to poor ATC sequencing and an inadequate company fuel program that left no margin for delays.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported a 'moderate to severe' wake turbulence encounter shortly after takeoff from Runway 25R at LAX in trail of an A321.
summary: A heavy A321 crew encountered severe wake turbulence at 400 ft AGL during departure from LAX 25R behind another A321. The aircraft banked violently up to 40 degrees with significant airspeed fluctuations, requiring a left turn to recover while all passengers remained safe.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC-8 Flight Crew reported rejecting a takeoff at low speed when the takeoff warning horn sounds. After close examination it is determined that with the flap handle in the flap 5 detent the flap indicator shows the flap position slightly beyond the 5 degree position. The flight returns to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 40 knots due to a configuration warning caused by a faulty flap indicator showing flaps outside the 5-degree range. Maintenance replaced the indicator, resolving the issue after the aircraft returned to the gate and passengers deplaned.

synopsis: Cessna Model Citation Excel/XLS Captain reported the rigging procedures for the Elevator Trim system were unclear and inconsistent. The 'Nose-up/Nose-down' limits were unclear while accomplishing their preflight checks.
summary: A pilot reported improper elevator trim rigging and unclear limit markings on an Excel/XLS aircraft during pre-flight inspections. The issue caused the trim pointer to stop short of limits, risking autopilot disengagement and pitch upset, prompting a call for standardized maintenance marking and crew guidance.

synopsis: CE-560XL Captain reported that his company has a new maintenance checklist to ensure that all actions taken to maintain the aircraft are entered into the log book. It appears to the Captain, that Maintenance Control and the mechanics that do the work are not familiar with it however.
summary: A pilot observed FBO mechanics servicing an aircraft's nose tire without a work order or logbook entry after finding it under-inflated at 115 PSI. The pilot intervened to enforce maintenance manual requirements, prompting Maintenance Control to order a tire replacement and highlighting a procedural gap where checklists were bypassed.

synopsis: Flight crew reported that after landing with an ill passenger and obtaining emergency status, the crew still had difficulty expediting a direct route to the gate to get medical attention.
summary: Pilots reported a medical emergency involving a seizing passenger after landing, requiring priority handling. Delays occurred due to conflicting ramp and ground clearances, a distant gate assignment, and the absence of EMS upon arrival, though the flight concluded safely.

synopsis: A320 crew reported that a general aviation aircraft completing their run up was completely over the hold short line for the runway and they should not have been cleared to takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that while back-taxiing for departure on Runway XX, another aircraft completed its run-up on Taxiway Y but encroached over the runway hold-short line. The pilot noted that ground and tower controllers failed to detect this incursion before clearing the pilot for takeoff, though the departure continued without incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported consistently receiving a clearance route different from the one normally filed by company Dispatch. Captain recommended that the normal route filed by Dispatch be changed to that assigned by ATC.
summary: A flight crew departing JFK experienced CPDLC login failures and conflicting route clearances between ground and en route phases. After receiving a CPDLC clearance differing from verbal instructions, the crew discovered at 17,000 feet that New York Departure showed a different route, raising concerns about separation conflicts and system reliability.

synopsis: A Ramp Agent reported Maintenance personnel started an aircraft engine at the gate with no ramp observer and ground traffic nearby. Also Maintenance personnel near the engine wore hats and loose clothing.
summary: Maintenance personnel started the #2 engine at the gate without notifying ramp traffic or securing loose items like hats. This created a safety hazard as staff worked near the turning engine in violation of standard loose item protocols.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being advised of an unruly passenger while taxiing to the gate. The passenger, who had struck a Flight Attendant, was handcuffed by air marshals and delivered to local airport police authorities at the gate.
summary: During taxi to the gate, a passenger struck a flight attendant after leaving her seat, prompting Air Marshals to handcuff her. Police deplaned the passenger, the flight attendant was uninjured, and the crew operated the return flight without further incident.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported that the weights generated by the Airbus onboard computer were inaccurate and resulted in hard landings. Captain reported the issue to Maintenance.
summary: The pilot reported abnormally high flap speeds and heavy landings on an Airbus A319 due to incorrect Flight Augmentation Computer weight data. After manually correcting the weight input, the crew achieved a normal landing and notified maintenance of the discrepancy.

synopsis: Pilot reported being notified by ATC that the aircraft was below minimum vectoring altitude for the VOR DME approach being flown. Pilot missed the notation on the approach plate of the altitude requirement for the approach segment in question.
summary: Two pilots flying to MMSD descended to 3,600 feet on a managed approach, violating the 6,000-foot minimum segment altitude they missed during briefing. ATC alerted them to the deviation, but they continued visually and landed safely after discovering the overlooked chart notation.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported improper communication procedures by the pushback ground crew after experiencing a tug driver headset malfunction.
summary: During pushback, a faulty headset caused audio feedback, leading ramp agents to disconnect the towbar without flight deck confirmation or a face-to-face briefing. The aircraft was left with brakes unset, creating a risk of uncontrolled movement and potential damage or injury.

synopsis: The Captain of a medevac helicopter flight reported that an external inspection access door opened in flight and struck the rotor blades. The flight landed safely and there were no injuries reported.
summary: Two flight crew members on a medical transport aircraft experienced a hydraulic cowling opening on approach, striking the rotor blades. The pilot attributed the incident to a deficient pre-flight inspection caused by distractions from other factors.

synopsis: The flight crew of a Boeing cargo aircraft reported experiencing windshear conditions during landing. A go-around was executed followed by a diversion to an alternate airport. At some point an engine pod made contact with the ground, which was verified on post flight inspection.
summary: The Captain flew a manual ILS approach into LAX in gusty winds, executing a go-around after a wind shear warning and right wing dip. Although Tower initially reported a possible engine strike, post-flight inspection confirmed engine damage despite no in-flight indications or runway debris.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported that on BNN 1B STAR to LHR they did not enter the holding pattern correctly.
summary: A 777 Captain and First Officer incorrectly entered a holding pattern at BNN while approaching LHR due to misinterpreting a partial iPad chart and rushing to time a CAT 3 auto land. Air Traffic Control vectored them back to re-enter the hold correctly, after which they completed a successful landing with no loss of separation.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 Captain reported an overspeed in climb that he felt was related to a recent change in procedure that calls for a high speed climbout.
summary: During a climb from LAS on the Shead 9 departure, the crew experienced an overspeed warning when autothrottles advanced faster than the autopilot pitched up while using Cost Index 70. The First Officer manually reduced the climb speed to 320 KIAS, citing that the new SOP's 335 KIAS target leaves an unsafe margin below VMO.

synopsis: Pilot reported an NMAC on approach to AUS.
summary: A pilot on a visual ILS approach to a parallel runway encountered a Cessna that crossed overhead at 300–400 feet AGL after being vectored to follow the pilot due to a runway closure. The Cessna pilot likely misidentified the target aircraft and executed an evasive climb, resolving the conflict without the reporting pilot taking evasive action.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported their radios became unusable due to P-static and elected to begin the descent into DEN per NORDO procedures. Communication improved descending through FL 250.
summary: The flight crew experienced severe precipitation static on Comm 1 while approaching the SLMON fix on the KOHOE3 arrival, causing a loss of communication with Denver Center. They squawked 7600 and initiated a descent without clearance due to being high on profile, resolving the static at FL250 and landing normally after confirming no traffic conflicts.

synopsis: A B777 First Officer reported diverting to an alternate airport after a missed approach was executed.
summary: The flight crew encountered strong gusty winds and excessive hold times while arriving at Narita, leading to an expedited clearance after refusing a lengthy EFC. A wind shear warning during the ILS approach to 16R forced a go-around and a diversion to Yokota due to fuel state.

synopsis: B757 pilots and a Flight Attendant reported that the aft cabin door would not arm before departure. The door assist bottle was triggered while attempting to cycle the door handle.
summary: The Captain and a Flight Attendant experienced a Right Aft door failure during pre-departure where the handle jammed, hinges fell off, and the slide bottle discharged. The Captain attributed the cause to internal fatigue from repeated catering cycles rather than crew error, resulting in a late departure on a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported descending on approach before being cleared by ATC. Traffic was crossing in front and below for a parallel runway.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain, operating his first flight after a downgrade, inadvertently captured the glide slope below the assigned 5000 ft altitude due to a misunderstanding of visual approach clearance. This resulted in a 300-400 ft altitude deviation while maintaining visual separation from crossing traffic, with no loss of separation or TCAS alerts.

synopsis: A PC-12 pilot reported that while on downwind ATC released another PC-12 for takeoff from a crossing way, resulting in an airborne conflict that required evasive action.
summary: While on an extended left downwind for Runway 16 at 1,900 feet, the pilot's aircraft was forced to execute a climbing left turn to avoid a collision with a departing PC-12 from Runway 11. The reporter attributes the conflict to Tower clearing the PC-12 for takeoff before the downwind traffic had crossed the departure end of Runway 11.

synopsis: An instructor pilot reported being unable to restart the left engine in a PA-44 after conducting single engine training with a student. A successful single engine approach and landing was made.
summary: During single-engine training, the left engine failed to restart while the right engine overheated, forcing a cooling descent from 7,000 feet. The instructor coordinated with ATC for a direct approach to Runway 9L and executed a single-engine landing.

synopsis: When a ferry permit was requested for an Airbus 319, the Maintenance Controller refused because he was uncomfortable with the items that were deferred.
summary: A maintenance controller refused to issue a ferry permit for an Airbus with worn elevator hinges and misadjusted servos due to safety concerns. The Shift Manager bypassed the controller, directing an unqualified relief controller to sign off the discrepancies and issue the permit despite the aircraft being out of Airworthiness Directive compliance.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: After pushback, a Mechanic reported the flight crew failed to set the parking brake and ended up stopping the aircraft abruptly after it began rolling.
summary: A ramp agent reported that after pushback, the flight crew started engines while a marshaller remained in front of the aircraft, causing it to move unexpectedly.
