The crew applied brakes after the marshaller moved aside, an incident attributed to rushing, potential miscommunication, or lack of awareness regarding ground crew clearance.

synopsis: A pilot reported a near mid-air collision while maneuvering and distracted with on-board equipment.
summary: A pilot conducting an air survey at 4,100 feet received a traffic alert while distracted by the flight computer during a left turn. The pilot executed an immediate climbing left turn to avoid a collision, attributing the near miss to fatigue, turbulence, radio chatter, and divided attention between flying and the camera system.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental aircraft reported unknowingly descending below National Seashore altitude restrictions while observing sea life.
summary: A pilot flying an Experimental aircraft alone descended to 250 ft over water and the beach to view sea animals, inadvertently violating National Seashore altitude requirements. The pilot discovered post-flight that a charted dotted line imposed a 2,000 ft limit, which was unknown during the operation.

synopsis: A pilot was instructed by MYF Tower to make a 10 degree right turn. Instead the pilot made a right 360 degree turn due to concerns of violating Gillespie's (SEE) airspace.
summary: The pilot, while southbound on an extended downwind for landing, inadvertently executed an extra 360-degree right turn instead of a 10-degree turn to avoid another tower's airspace. Post-landing, the pilot acknowledged this independent action was unnecessary and wrong, noting that air traffic control is responsible for airspace separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft reported contact with another small aircraft from behind and above. Both aircraft were able to continue for normal landing.
summary: Two Cessna 172s collided near ZZZ while Aircraft X departed and Aircraft Y approached. Aircraft Y struck Aircraft X's left wing from behind and above at 3,000 feet, causing a small dent and scrape marks, though both aircraft remained airworthy and landed safely.

synopsis: Learjet 60 Captain reported an overheat condition on the left bleed air. Light went out after running checklist. Flight continued to destination at lower altitude.
summary: The crew experienced a left bleed air overheat on departure, which cleared after running the checklist. They continued the flight on a single bleed system, forgoing the planned FL450 climb to avoid an overweight landing, though the pilot later noted a lower altitude diversion would have been preferable.

synopsis: The pilot of a M20J reported control problems on landing rollout due to a failed tire on the left main landing gear.
summary: The pilot reported a left main landing gear tire blowout during landing on Runway 03, causing the aircraft to skid left. Directional control was regained using rudder and brakes, allowing the aircraft to remain on the runway with no injuries or property damage.

synopsis: Phenom 300 Captain experienced a TCAS RA and NMAC at 6000 feet during vectors for approach. A VFR Cessna climbing to 5500 feet with the same Controller had continued to climb resulting in evasive action and a NMAC.
summary: During descent into SDL, a crew under Phoenix Approach control received a TCAS resolution advisory when a VFR Cessna failed to level at 5,500 feet and climbed toward their 6,000-foot path. The crew descended to 5,200 feet to avoid the conflict, attributing the near-miss to the Cessna violating its clearance rather than controller error.

synopsis: The pilot of a skydiving aircraft reported ATC gave late notice of a commercial aircraft transitioning the area.
summary: A skydiving pilot flying VFR at 13,500 feet in Class B airspace exited jumpers after a one-minute call, then received a conflicting "hold jumpers" instruction from Approach while descending. The pilot visually acquired a conflicting airliner and turned south to avoid it, attributing the incident to frequency saturation and delayed communications.

synopsis: Beech 23 pilot reported a conflict with an aircraft on the runway while landing at a non-Towered airport. A go-around was initiated at approximately 200 feet AGL.
summary: A VFR pilot experienced an electrical issue and inadvertently left COM1 volume off during a straight-in approach to Runway 15. The pilot executed a go-around at 200 feet after spotting a hidden aircraft on the runway, attributing the near miss to the volume error and improper traffic pattern entry.

synopsis: PA31 pilot reported diverting to an alternate airport when the right engine malfunctioned.
summary: The pilot of a PA31 Navajo Chieftain experienced right engine oil leakage and cylinder failure during initial climb. The pilot diverted to an alternate airport, shut down the engine, feathered the propeller, and landed safely without advising ATC due to being on CTAF.

synopsis: R44 flight instructor reported that a helicopter pilot in training inadvertently mistook the fuel shutoff for the collective friction adjustment after engine start.
summary: A student CFI mistakenly turned off the main fuel shutoff instead of adjusting collective friction during a preflight hydraulic check in a Robinson R-44II, causing an unexpected engine stop. The instructor identified this as a near miss that could have resulted in an in-flight fuel starvation had the error not been caught before liftoff.

synopsis: DA40 pilot reported that ATC had not passed on their request to extend a flight plan and that search and rescue may have been dispatched.
summary: A solo pilot flying a cross-country flight could not contact Flight Service Stations to amend their flight plan due to poor signal, so they requested Center to extend it. Center failed to pass the amendment to the briefer, who closed the plan upon landing, triggering an unnecessary search and rescue mission.

synopsis: The pilot of a C185 reported a loss of control during landing rollout due to a crosswind.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing on runway 26L with 40-degree flaps and no tail wheel lock, a right crosswind gust caused the aircraft to veer right and tip onto its left wingtip. The pilot attributed the incident to low speed, ineffective flight controls, and delayed brake application, though the aircraft settled with all systems normal.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports a Class B airspace incursion event.
summary: The pilot entered Class B airspace without a clearance while expecting one based on a previous flight's handoff. A controller subsequently queried the status and issued the clearance immediately, resulting in no harm but prompting the pilot to request clearance earlier in the future.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Cessna Citation 525 single pilot twice requested descent to 14,000 FT to make the MERMA restriction. Pilot was reportedly chastised by the Controller and felt he was vectored excessively by ATC.
summary: A single-pilot jet pilot encountered a hostile controller during descent who issued excessive vectors and small altitude clearances, causing the pilot to nearly miss a 14,000-foot restriction. The controller threatened regulatory violation for non-standard phraseology, but a supervisor later apologized and agreed the incident warranted a safety report.

synopsis: PHL Tower Controller states their facility LOA with Ramp Control is unsafe and is not being complied with.
summary: A pilot in Aircraft X ignored ATC taxi instructions and entered ramp control via an unauthorized taxiway, disrupting ground coordination. The reporter attributes this unsafe event to a flawed Ramp Letter of Agreement that prioritizes efficiency over safety and fails to account for controller workload.

synopsis: PHL Tower Controller states his facility Letter of Agreement with Ramp Control is not being complied with and is unsafe.
summary: Aircraft X entered ramp control via an unauthorized taxiway without ATC coordination, violating the current Letter of Agreement. The reporter attributes this unsafe practice to an efficiency-driven LOA that ignores controller workload and lacks proper feedback mechanisms.

synopsis: ZLC ARTCC Controller reported their facility has implemented rules in addition to the Federal Aviation Administration Handbook (FAAH) 7110.65 regarding issuing IFR clearances to departing aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an IFR clearance to Aircraft X in a non-radar environment using a fix not depicted on the chart, citing excessive workload. The controller reported that this FAAH 7110.65-based rule reduces safety and efficiency by restricting traffic control capabilities outside radar coverage.

synopsis: ZLC ARTCC Controller the facility issued a memo defining extra rules not contained in the Federal Aviation Administration Handbook (FAAH) 7110.65 handbook. The Controller did not comply with the local rules.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a new memo requiring fixes to be displayed on radar or overhead charts was dangerous and untrained. The controller cleared a flight "as filed" because the fix was not displayed, citing the memo as a misapplication of FAAH 7110.65 that complicates non-radar operations.

synopsis: A320 Captain experienced GPS signal interference and intermittent outages during arrival to PHX. The interference seemed to be connected with NOTAMs and RAIM (Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring) notices about GPS outages near El Paso.
summary: The flight crew experienced GPS2 faults and random map shifts while enroute to PHX at FL360, likely due to known GPS outages. They diverted to a less rigorous STAR under ATC direction, manually monitoring position until cleared for the BUNTR arrival.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 First Officers were informed by the cabin crew that there was smoke and fumes in the aft galley apparently from a failed oven. The oven was switched off and the circuit breaker was pulled, but the flight attendants wanted to return to the departure airport. However, the Captain believed the problem was solved. Maintenance Control was contacted and after some deliberation the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During the climb phase of an ETOPS flight, flight attendants reported smoke and a burning smell from a malfunctioning aft galley oven, prompting crew concern. The flight crew consulted Maintenance Control, decided to return to the departure airport, jettisoned 100,000 lbs of fuel, and landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an EGPWS alert while on initial approach into an airport surrounded by high terrain.
summary: The flight crew received an EGPWS terrain warning while descending to 4300 feet near PETIS, prompting a climb to 4900 feet. ATC confirmed 4300 feet as the minimum vectoring altitude, and the aircraft subsequently completed an uneventful ILS 26L landing.

synopsis: B737-900 flight crew reported that while in flight the Crew Oxygen had lost all its pressure. He mentioned he and FO did notice an air wooshing sound on takeoff.
summary: The flight crew discovered zero flight deck oxygen pressure during descent from FL350, tracing the cause to a missing bottle that created a takeoff noise. With no checklist guidance, they descended to FL240 and secured a portable oxygen bottle for emergency use.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reset Gen 1 for a GEN 2 caution message, therefore the air driven generator automatically deployed. He was busy on approach with an IOE student.
summary: During an IOE final approach, the Pilot Monitoring misidentified a GEN 2 caution as GEN 1 due to distraction while instructing the student, causing an unnecessary ADG deployment. The crew correctly reset GEN 2 and landed uneventfully, with the PM accepting full responsibility for the error.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported rejecting the takeoff at about 80 knots after a Flight Attendant notified the crew about flames from an engine tailpipe detected by passengers. A failed oil seal was found.
summary: During takeoff roll, flight attendants reported a left engine fire based on passenger observations, prompting the crew to abort at 80 knots. Post-flight inspection revealed an oil leak caused by a failed O-ring following recent servicing, with no cockpit indications present during the event.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a UAV at 8,000 feet near Jamesburg, NJ while on vectors to LGA Runway 4.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft receiving radar vectors to runway 4 at LGA encountered a stationary black UAV at 8,000 feet. The object was located a few hundred feet to the left while the crew flew an easterly heading over New Jersey near Turnpike exit 8A.

synopsis: CRJ900 First Officer reported a TCAS event during vectors to EWR with VFR traffic 500 feet above. TCAS showed the altitude difference to be 300 feet and commanded, 'Monitor Vertical Speed' possibly due to IFR traffic 1000 feet below.
summary: The flight crew received a TCAS "monitor vertical speed" resolution advisory while being vectored for a visual approach to EWR 22L due to conflicting traffic. The captain maintained level flight, resulting in a minimum separation of 300 feet before the alert cleared and the approach continued.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An aircraft climbing out of 5,800 feet northwest of PHX, had a near miss with a non transponder equipped aircraft near the Pleasant Valley glider port.
summary: A flight school pilot and backseater climbing northbound over Pleasant Valley at 5,800 feet avoided a collision with a non-transponder aircraft by descending. The other aircraft crossed 200 feet overhead without reacting, and the lack of TCAS warning was attributed to the intruder's missing transponder.

synopsis: Pilot reported drifting off the right side of the runway in a tailwheel aircraft after a normal three point touchdown with a very slight left crosswind. Postflight inspection of the tailwheel revealed no anomalies. Three landings were made with a stronger left crosswind with no control difficulties noted.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel airplane drifted off Runway 2 during a full-stall landing due to ineffective left rudder and tailwheel control. After inspecting the mechanism and finding it normal, the pilot successfully completed three subsequent landings by holding the stick full aft.

synopsis: DA42 flight instructor reported a NMAC with a DA40 while on the PVU PROVO4 SID near the FFU VOR.
summary: During a DA40 instrument training flight, the instructor took control to climb to 9,000 feet after a TIS alert revealed another DA40 turning into their path 50 feet below. The near-miss occurred because the other aircraft appeared to be holding at 8,500 feet without that information being communicated to ATC or the pilot.

synopsis: SR20 instructor pilot reported feeling rushed by an ATC clearance with a short void time and missed seeing a C172 on short final at an uncontrolled airport. He felt that the short void time created an unnecessary hazard.
summary: A student pilot and instructor rushing to meet a short void time at MQJ nearly collided with an aircraft on final approach while taxiing to runway 25. The instructor stopped before entering the runway, attributing the incident to insufficient clearing of the approach course caused by the pressure of the tight clearance deadline.

synopsis: CE560 flight crew reported a loss of GPS signal west of LLO due to military jamming at the White Sands Missile Range. They were vectored by ATC to LLO and the KIDDZ2 Arrival to HOU. During the arrival, the AAHZZ crossing restriction of 10000 feet was overshot due to unknown automation issues.
summary: Pilots flying a jet from ABQ to HOU descended below 10,000 feet northwest of AAHZZ while executing the KIDDZ2 arrival. The crew realized they missed charted altitude restrictions at KIDDZ, apologized to ATC, and climbed back to 10,000 feet with no loss of separation.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported mistaking BEC for AAO during a visual approach and landing. The reporter was distracted by the need to continually wipe fog that formed on the inside of the windscreen during the approach.
summary: The pilot descended to land at Jabara Field (AAO) but mistakenly landed at nearby Beech Field (BEC) due to distraction from severe windshield fogging. This distraction prevented the pilot from updating the GPS to confirm the correct airport, though no collision occurred and the pilot was cleared to taxi to the intended destination.

synopsis: A procedure allowing pilot provided visual separation between successive departures caused a conflict between an A321 aircraft climbing at a much slower airspeed than a B737-800 departing behind the A321.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in the Departure sector managed a compressing separation between a slow-climbing A321 and a trailing B737-800 using pilot-provided visual separation. The controller broke noise abatement procedures to initiate an early turn for the B737-800, resolving the unsafe situation caused by the A321's slow climb performance.

synopsis: B737 flight crew was informed by a Flight Attendant during climbout that they smelled smoke in the mid-cabin and there was a visible haze. The crew elected to return to the departure airport and landed overweight with the smoke having dissipated during the approach.
summary: During climb to 15,000 ft, flight attendants reported smoke in the aft cabin, prompting the flight crew to divert and perform an overweight landing. The crew did not don oxygen masks as no smoke was detected in the cockpit, and the aircraft returned to the gate with no further smoke indications.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain described the aircraft's condition after cold ground air conditioning operated all night condensing humid air. The flight station, passenger seats, and equipment were dripping liquid which was evaporated with warm APU air conditioning.
summary: The Captain and First Officer delayed departure of a Boeing 737 due to severe condensation drenching the cockpit and cabin caused by cold ground air and high humidity. They used the APU to evaporate the moisture before Contract Maintenance inspected and cleared the aircraft for a safe flight.

synopsis: A320 First Officer arrived early for a two leg trip and discovered that the APU is MEL'd. He informed the Captain of his findings in the hope that the aircraft would be refused, which eventually occurred. This caused a row with the Duty Manager.
summary: A First Officer refused to fly a scheduled leg to DEN due to an inoperative APU, citing safety concerns. The reporter described feeling intimidated and pressured by management, including an Assistant Chief Pilot, who allegedly attempted to override the refusal and dismiss the First Officer's input.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a near miss with a Citation 525 which had just cancelled IFR. The 757 leveled in response to a TCAS RA command.
summary: The relief pilot reported a TCAS RA while flying a Citation jet that had recently cancelled IFR. Approach called out unseen VFR traffic passing less than 500 feet below, prompting the crew to comply with a "level off" resolution advisory.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported windshear during two consecutive approaches resulting in go arounds. After noting that the warnings were for increasing airspeed the crew elects to fly a third approach and ignore the windshear warning should it occur, but it does not. Gate arrival fuel is 6,900 pounds.
summary: A 777 crew encountered two windshear warnings during approaches to Narita in 80-knot winds, executing two go-arounds that reduced fuel to 30 minutes. The aircraft overshot the approach course due to strong tailwinds, triggering a traffic alert before landing with low fuel.

synopsis: B777 Captain encountered wind shear at 1000 feet during approach, with minimum fuel and went around. Flight diverted to a nearby alternate and landed with approximately 10000 pounds of fuel.
summary: The flight crew encountered extended holds and minimum fuel status at KETAR and VEPOX before receiving vectors to RJAA. During the ILS 16R approach, a reactive wind shear alert at 1000 feet AGL triggered an escape maneuver, resulting in a diversion to the alternate airport with 10,000 LBS fuel remaining.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported responding to a RA on descent into CHA.
summary: The crew of an aircraft descending into CHA received a TCAS RA while level at 7000 ft after ATC amended their altitude. The conflict occurred because a VFR aircraft climbed directly through their altitude on an intercept course, forcing an aggressive descent to comply with the RA.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 EICAS alerted BRK LH FAULT and BRK RH FAULT when the landing gear were lowered. The crew incorrectly decided the EICAS was an advisory alert because it was colored blue. After landing, overheated brakes required the aircraft be chocked while Fire Crews cooled the brakes with fans prior to a tow to the gate.
summary: The pilot flying and captain received dual brake fault messages at 2,000 feet AGL but elected to land after misinterpreting the QRH. Post-landing brake overheat required fire crew cooling and a tow to the gate, attributed to a rushed decision influenced by message color.

synopsis: CL350 Captain reported being given vectors for a visual approach to Runway 32 at BBG but could not spot the field and Approach Control was not responsive initially. A conflict developed with a C208 at their altitude and the crew evaded on their own, until Approach noticed and issued a new altitude and heading.
summary: The flight crew experienced a near mid-air collision with a Cessna Caravan at 3200 feet while being vectored by Springfield Approach for a visual landing. The crew initiated an evasive turn after ATC failed to provide timely separation, attributing the incident to controller inattention and poor communication.

synopsis: The Captain of a B777 refused to accept the aircraft for flight due to an APU door open in flight. Fuel burn would have been excessive and the constant low oil quantity was a concern.
summary: The pilot rejected a B777 due to an unresolved APU oil leak and inoperative quantity sensing system. Despite mechanics attributing the loss to wind-milling, the crew refused the aircraft because the APU lacks automatic shutdown protection for low oil, posing a safety risk.

synopsis: CE560XL Captain reported he took evasive action to avoid jumpers who were released without proper notice in the area of HZL.
summary: The pilot reported an IFR arrival at an airport with parachute activity where jumpers descended through the right traffic pattern for Runway 28. The pilot executed a sharp turn to avoid the jumpers after failing to hear their release announcement on CTAF following the handoff from Wilkes-Barre Approach.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported a very strong fuel smell as the aircraft accelerates for takeoff. The odor was detected by the flight crew as well, but began to diminish passing through 10,000 feet. Other Flight Attendants detected the odor and some felt nausea but the flight continued to destination.
summary: Cabin crew and flight deck reported an extremely heavy fuel smell during takeoff and the climb to 10,000 feet, causing nausea and near-fainting. The odor subsided after 10,000 feet, but the reporter filed an injury report due to subsequent headaches and health concerns.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: An IFR light twin pilot in VMC was advised by ZMP Center about a single engine VFR aircraft at the same altitude. ATC assumed the light twin had TCAS, but it did not and the aircrafts had a near miss.
summary: The IFR pilot of a small transport at 6,000 feet and a VFR aircraft at 6,000 feet experienced a near mid-air collision while closing at 300 knots. The pilot initiated a deviation after ATC delayed separation instructions, resulting in the VFR aircraft passing 120 feet below and 30 feet left.

synopsis: An Airbus aircraft climbing out at much slower speeds than other similar aircraft could cause a loss of required separation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in the Departure sector managed a compressing separation between a slow-climbing Airbus and a trailing B737 using pilot-provided visual separation. The controller broke noise abatement procedures to initiate an early turn for the B737, preventing an incident caused by the Airbus's slower climb performance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZSE Controller issued VFR traffic to an aircraft and restricted the aircraft above the traffic. The Controller issued a pilot's discretion descent to the aircraft. The aircraft received an RA for the VFR traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a discretionary descent to Aircraft X regarding a VFR target at 17,500 feet, but the pilot executed a TCAS RA instead. The controller received a Performance Record of Conference for failing to provide positive separation, though the controller disputes the finding and feels targeted by the supervisor.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: S46 TRACON Controller reported an Airbus departure climbed at a much slower airspeed than subsequent departures requiring ATC to restrict and vector off course the trailing aircraft.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in the Departure sector stopped a B737 at 3,000 feet and restricted its speed due to a slow-climbing Airbus ahead during a visual separation departure. The controller terminated automatic releases and vectored the B737 northwest to maintain separation, attributing the event to the Airbus's slow climb rate and recommending LOA changes.

synopsis: DFW Tower Controller reported of a loss of separation on final due to speed overtake and the lack of timely go-around instructions.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a Local West controller failed to ensure visual separation between two arriving aircraft at DFW despite speed discrepancies and coordination requests. The reporter attributed the safety lapse to the controller's negative attitude regarding responsibility and retirement, recommending Professional Standards review and facility-wide safety training.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DFW Tower Controller described a possible loss of separation between two aircraft on final approach to Runway 36L.
summary: An air traffic controller at DFW allowed Aircraft X to lose 2.5 miles of separation on final to runway 36L while distracted by a relief briefing. The controller attributed the incident to inadequate monitoring by the final controller and an improper attempt to transfer position before resolving the spacing issue.

synopsis: A Controller radar identified a departure and noticed they had converging VFR traffic. The IFR departure was below the Minimum IFR Altitude so the Controller could not vector the aircraft to avoid the traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic advisories to a student pilot in Aircraft X executing a missed approach below the 2,500-foot Minimum IFR Altitude due to a conflicting VFR aircraft. The controller cleared the aircraft to turn only after it climbed above the MIA, later questioning if an emergency clearance below the altitude would have been safer.

synopsis: A HCF Controller reported of a spacing problem which led to a go around. When the aircraft was turned it entered an airspace of higher altitude, resulting in an airspace deviation.
summary: The controller climbed Aircraft X to 5,000 feet and resequenced it on downwind after Aircraft Y slowed from 170 to 90 knots on final to OGG Runway 2. The controller attributed the spacing loss to the tower's speed reduction for departures, potentially encroaching the 6,000-foot MVA.

synopsis: A CMH TRACON Controller failed to display 'touch and go' in an aircraft's data tag. The Controller forgot to issue communication change to the aircraft. The Tower Controller took no action to establish communications with the landing aircraft. The aircraft made a touch and go into confliction with a departing helicopter.
summary: A Radar controller reported that a Tower controller allowed Aircraft X to execute an unauthorized touch-and-go on the right runway without issuing a frequency change or light gun clearance. The Radar controller attributed the resulting unsafe situation to the Tower controller's deliberate failure to follow procedures and past reckless actions.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A ZMA Controller reported of an airborne conflict between an aircraft under ATC Control and an unknown aircraft. The unknown aircraft was found to be a high speed aircraft that was being worked under a special memorandum. The Controller wanted high speed aircraft to work under a LOA that might stop this problem.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 66/67 observed an untracked Mode C intruder, Aircraft Y, near Aircraft X at 10,000 feet, triggering a TCAS RA. The controller attributed the conflict to Aircraft Y operating under a Memorandum without requesting a transponder code or establishing two-way communication.

synopsis: A DFW Tower Controller issued a non-standard go-around instruction to an aircraft. The Tower Controller did not point out the aircraft to the appropriate TRACON sector.
summary: Local Control issued a left turn to Aircraft X to avoid Aircraft Y after Final Monitor cancelled the approach, but failed to coordinate a handoff to Departure. The reporter attributes the potential loss of separation to inadequate speed control by the arrival controller and a lack of tower training on TRACON airspace boundaries.

synopsis: A ZAU ARTCC Controller used incorrect clearance phraseology with a VFR-on-top clearance request. The Controller did not understand how to use the procedure and requested clarification.
summary: During training, a radar trainee issued a VFR-ON-TOP clearance to Aircraft X at 14,000 feet, which climbed to 14,500 feet and was told to maintain VFR. A neighboring sector later questioned the clearance, highlighting confusion over whether the aircraft remained IFR or became VFR after the "maintain VFR" instruction.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced a thrust reverser failure which was written up and MEL by Contract Maintenance. The Captain noted that the procedure was not completed properly and Maintenance was called back to complete the job. The Gate Agent attempted a manual weight and balance after being locked out of the automated computer system, but an error was made resulting in further delays.
summary: The Captain and Contract Maintenance addressed a deferred thrust reverser and load computer issues, causing a three-hour delay due to incomplete MEL procedures and manual loadsheet errors. The Captain ensured compliance before departure, highlighting the need for stricter oversight of contractors and clearer tarmac delay rules.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported the ingestion of an external air conditioning supply hose during engine start, damaging the engine. Both external electrical power and air conditioning were connected to the aircraft due to an inoperative APU.
summary: The Captain and First Officer started engine one with ground air connected, resulting in the ingestion of an air hose running under the engine. The engine surged and was shut down, causing passenger disembarkation and engine damage due to the crew's lack of situational awareness regarding the hose location.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an abnormal amount of rudder trim was required to maintain level flight. After consulting with Maintenance, a decision was made to return to the departure airport where an uneventful landing was accomplished.
summary: During climb and cruise, the pilot observed increasing left rudder trim requirements that eventually moved autonomously to the gauge's maximum limit. The crew returned to ZZZ after maintenance confirmed initial trim settings were within tolerance, though sufficient manual rudder control remained available.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported they were given a short taxi route to the runway which they were not able to comply with do to pre-takeoff tasks. The flight crew was told by the Tower Controller they were blocking traffic by not being ready for takeoff.
summary: The First Officer reported that while completing pre-takeoff duties at a short taxiway, a tower controller berated the crew for blocking traffic despite another aircraft also being unready. The pilot stated this verbal reprimand introduced an unnecessary threat and stress during a critical phase of flight preparation.

synopsis: A fatigued Airbus First Officer attempted a hand flown visual approach to PHL Runway 27R, but was forced to execute a go-around after failing to turn the flight directors off. Autothrust advanced power on the approach which also resulted in a flaps overspeed.
summary: A fatigued reserve pilot flying a visual approach to PHL 27R experienced an overspeed condition when active flight directors increased thrust during manual flap extension. The crew executed a go-around, corrected the automation error on a second attempt, and landed safely after acknowledging complacency and fatigue as causes.

synopsis: Pilot reported several non-standard issues at SPS mostly related to runway lighting and weather reporting.
summary: A pilot crew operating a night arrival into SPS, an Air Force base, landed on the lit Runway 15R after realizing the ILS for Runway 15C guided to an unlit runway due to non-functional pilot-controlled lighting. The report highlights risks from military-controlled operations, unavailable ASOS weather, and dimmed lights on Runway 17.

synopsis: HS-125 series Captain reported experiencing a loss of pressurization. The crew initiated an immediate descent and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During climb through FL270, a Hawker experienced rapid cabin depressurization following a muffled thump, prompting an immediate descent to 10,000 feet and diversion. Post-flight inspection revealed a significant bleed air leak with the APU running, mirroring a similar past incident.

synopsis: CL-350 First Officer reported an airborne conflict on approach to BBG that he felt was related to ATC Controller workload.
summary: A pilot monitoring reported a near-miss with a Cessna Caravan while approaching Branson, Missouri, in IMC conditions. The conflict occurred due to excessive vectoring delays by the Springfield Approach controller, who admitted the error after the crew executed a TCAS climb and turn to avoid the converging traffic.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 First Officer deadheading in the cabin questioned the airline's procedures for dealing with weight and balance issues.
summary: A passenger reported that a Flight Attendant and ramp agent moved oversized bags into the cabin to falsely claim the aircraft was no longer overweight. The passenger disembarked to reduce weight, noting the crew's procedure of discounting baggage weight lacks manual support and creates safety concerns.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain climbing through FL240 reported a near miss with a UAS approximately 2-3 feet in diameter.
summary: During an RNAV departure climb through FL240 to FL250, the pilot observed a 2-3 foot drone-like object crossing 200-300 feet in front of the aircraft. Fort Worth Center was notified but had no radar track, and no TCAS alert was generated.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported being cut off by numerous vehicles on the ramp in DFW while taxiing to the gate.
summary: The flight crew at DFW was repeatedly cut off by ground vehicles and baggage carts while taxiing to the gate, causing multiple stops and FOD removal. Due to a cart passing within 10 feet of the nose, the crew shut down engines and requested a tow to complete parking.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported losing contact with ZKC ARTCC in the vicinity of DSM.
summary: The crew discovered they were on an outdated Kansas City Center frequency while en route to Grand Forks, likely due to a missed ATC handoff or a squawk change. After a ten-minute delay using another aircraft to relay their position, they contacted Minneapolis Center and continued without safety concerns.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported of a mistake with similar spelled intersections. Pilots entered incorrect intersection into FMS and did not check with the PDC for correct spelling. Aircraft turned away from intended route when it went to the misspelled intersection.
summary: During initial climb, the crew inadvertently entered a misspelled fix (PUMKN instead of PMPKN) into the FMS due to distraction and poor cross-checking, causing an unexpected westward turn. ATC issued an immediate heading correction to 360 after querying the route, resolving the deviation without traffic conflict.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer Pilot reported confusion between two similar sounding fixes (airport Charlottesville and VOR Charleston).
summary: The pilot flying and captain were at cruising altitude when ATC issued a confusing clearance to proceed direct Charleston VOR (HVQ) instead of Charlottesville. The crew attributed the confusion to similar-sounding names and controller accent, noting that complacency prevented them from verifying the fix phonetically before complying.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported supervisors are pressuring flight attendants to board the aircraft before completing their pre-boarding SOPs.
summary: A flight attendant reported that an operations supervisor pressured the crew to board wheelchair passengers before security and equipment checks were complete. The reporter attributed this to supervisors prioritizing on-time performance over safety protocols and urged better coordination with the lead flight attendant before initiating boarding.

synopsis: While charging batteries in the shop, one of the batteries caught fire.
summary: A mechanic in a battery shop reported a small flame and pop on a battery cell while reaching over six batteries during charging. The mechanic extinguished the fire, discharged the battery, and attributed the incident to poor ventilation under the chargers and lack of air conditioning.

synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft reported an airborne conflict with another aircraft, identified to be from a flight school located at another airport.
summary: A pilot practicing a GPS approach at an uncontrolled airport broke off when a flight school aircraft entered a non-standard pattern and cut them off from 400 feet above. The pilot landed safely after the other aircraft cleared the runway, noting the instructor's unprofessional teaching despite no immediate danger.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 reported an elevator control problem during climb. Yoke movement became free after application of additional back pressure, and a noise was heard.
summary: The PIC experienced strong nose-up pitch and limited yoke movement during a practice traffic pattern, which resolved after a snapping sound upon applying back pressure. The aircraft landed safely, but the left tire blew on rollout; the pilot noted recent major elevator work during a 100-hour inspection.

synopsis: The pilot of a PA46 reported a critical ground conflict with a Citation after receipt of a clearance to taxi from Ground Control.
summary: The pilot, stationary with engines running, nearly collided with a moving Citation jet while executing a blind-side right turn after receiving taxi clearance from Ground. The pilot attributed the near-miss to Ground failing to warn of the crossing aircraft, forcing an emergency brake application to avoid impact.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper Aerostar reported an autopilot problem on approach that resulted in a descent below the glideslope before receiving an alert by ATC.
summary: The pilot experienced an autopilot malfunction during the first approach, resulting in a significant descent below the glide slope after ATC warnings. A go-around was executed, and the second approach was completed manually without incident while the cause is investigated.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 reported operating within close proximity to another aircraft while on VFR approach.
summary: The pilot, enroute VFR at 11,000 ft after canceling IFR, passed just in front and above traffic identified by Approach. The pilot attributed the loss of proper separation entirely to their own failure to maintain adequate distance during the descent.

synopsis: The pilot of a C206T reported a loss of engine power due to an apparent turbocharger failure.
summary: The pilot experienced power fluctuations and a zero turbine inlet temperature reading due to a suspected turbocharger failure. The engine seized completely during the base-to-final turn, but the pilot landed safely after the turbocharger reportedly broke apart.

synopsis: ZMP Controller reported of problems associated with a military flight break up after refueling. Controller reported this was a problem the day before and that it was reported to the FLM on duty.
summary: An air traffic controller and a trainee managed an ALTRV of two KC-35s and four F-15s where missing individual flight plans caused routing errors, NORDO status, and MARSA confusion during a break-up. The controller attributed the incident to poor filing procedures and the R-side controller's failure to establish separate altitudes before clearing the flights into the next sector.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported descending well below charted altitude on the HAWKZ 4 RNAV Arrival into SEA, citing lack of FMC mode awareness as a factor.
summary: The First Officer and Captain descended below the 12,000-foot restriction at PIKEZ while flying the HAWKZ4 arrival into Seattle due to the First Officer's failure to monitor altitude and reliance on automation. ATC instructed a climb to 10,000 feet, resulting in a pilot deviation report caused by fatigue and distraction.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported they experienced a runway incursion at IAH when they misunderstood an ATC clearance.
summary: Pilots of a flight at IAH crossed the 8R hold short line after receiving a garbled crossing clearance followed immediately by a "hold short" instruction. The controller ordered a go-around for an approaching aircraft, though the crew reported no collision risk and attributed the incident to rushed communications and confusion over clearance verification.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being advised of a vessel crossing their final approach path on approach to TNCA. Flight crew stated they did not fly over the ship.
summary: The flight crew on final approach to Runway 11 received an ATC alert regarding a cruise ship crossing their path at 1500 AGL. They slowed to final approach speed and fully configured the aircraft, allowing the ship to clear before landing normally without flying over it.

synopsis: A Captain flying the NAT C oceanic route westbound discovered the iPad JEPP PRO incorrectly depicted GAPLI as the Oceanic Gateway waypoint when DINIM at the EISN to EGGX airspace transition is the correct Gateway waypoint.
summary: The flight crew identified a discrepancy between Jepp Pro and paper charts regarding airspace boundaries and the oceanic entry point while filing a NAT C route. They confirmed with Shanwick that Dinim, not Gapli, was the correct entry point and reported the Jepp Pro error via ACARS.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported not noticing the 6000 ft minimum vectoring altitude between MARUX and the IAF on the MMSD VOR DME-2 Runway 16 Approach. The reporter stated the altitude is not coded into their navigation database.
summary: The non-flying pilot and Captain descended below 6000 feet on a VOR approach to MMSD, violating the Minimum Vectoring Altitude due to a missed chart restriction. ATC intervened, but the crew continued visually in VMC and landed safely after realizing the briefing error.

synopsis: During flight, in a De Havilland DHC-8-102, Number 1 Hydraulic System Failed due to loss of hydraulic fluid.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew experienced a Number 1 hydraulic system failure indicated by low quantity and pressure, causing loss of flaps and normal brakes. They diverted to an airport with a long runway, executed a flapless landing at 127 kts, and stopped safely with no fire or damage noted.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported experiencing a momentary loss of control following a wake vortex encounter in trail of a B757 on approach to LAX.
summary: An A319 crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B757 while on ILS 25L approach to LAX with only 3nm spacing. The upset caused temporary loss of control and flight control system faults, but the crew recovered and landed safely, attributing the incident to insufficient separation rules.

synopsis: The pilot of a C208 reported loss of control during turnoff of the runway due to standing water and a wind shift.
summary: The pilot reported that while exiting RWY 35L, sudden wind shear and standing water caused the aircraft to slide sideways, resulting in the propeller striking two runway lights. The pilot attributed the loss of control to these conditions and plans to wait for wind shear to clear or taxi at a crawling pace in the future.

synopsis: The pilot of a BE36 reported a loss of engine power due to a fuel bladder collapse and fuel mismanagement. ATC did not comprehend the conditions and attempted to request an altitude that the pilot was unable to maintain. Power was eventually regained and a successful precautionary landing was made.
summary: During cruise, a pilot experienced total power loss due to fuel exhaustion caused by a faulty gauge reading. Distractions from ATC instructions delayed tank switching, but the pilot eventually restarted the engine and landed safely after switching frequencies.

synopsis: The solo pilot was surprised to be advised in-flight that an sporting event TFR was in place around the ballpark when his weather briefer had been specifically stated that no TFR was planned during the flight briefing two hours prior.
summary: A pilot flying northbound along Route 101 after passing KSFO was instructed by tower to avoid a sporting event TFR despite a prior Flight Service briefing stating none existed. The pilot attributed this discrepancy to a failure in TFR dissemination to Flight Service, noting the event schedule was known well in advance.

synopsis: A BE76 flight instructor reported a runway excursion when the student did not react appropriately to a simulated engine failure during takeoff.
summary: During a multi-engine commercial rating training takeoff, an instructor simulated a left engine failure, but the student froze and locked the throttles open, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway. The instructor closed the good engine's mixture and applied right rudder to stop the plane on a 45-degree incline with no damage.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported two flight attendants were injured in a turbulence encounter at FL350.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence at FL350 while deviating around clouds, injuring two flight attendants and forcing a medical diversion. The incident occurred despite prior reports of smooth conditions and light chop, highlighting that turbulence can exist even when radar shows no returns.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported the flight attendants did not seem to be adequately trained to properly utilize ground medical resources.
summary: During a non-emergency medical event, a Flight Attendant conducted a ground communication call that was interrupted by the flight deck due to poor radio technique and irrelevant information. The reporter attributes the failure to inadequate cabin crew training in headset use and medical communication protocols.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported he was concerned with the behavior of a Flight Attendant who disregarded his direction to be seated during an expected turbulence encounter.
summary: During an enroute transoceanic flight, the Captain requested cabin crew to remain seated due to forecast severe turbulence, but one flight attendant left her jumpseat to perform galley tasks. The reporter described this behavior as reckless and a disregard for Captain's Authority, noting the attendant later criticized the safety directive as an exercise in authoritative management.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported two aircraft in two nights were taken out of service due to excessive hydraulic brake pressure decay.
summary: A pilot reported excessive brake pressure decay on two aircraft during preflight with hydraulic power off, causing both to be taken out of service. The pilot attributed the issue to potential leaks or improper valve positioning, noting a lack of specific flight manual guidance for detecting this malfunction.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the Captain took control of the aircraft after a crosswind approach and firm landing that produced several bounces.
summary: The Captain and First Officer flew a visual approach to RWY 26 in ABQ in gusty crosswinds. The aircraft bounced twice on touchdown, prompting the Captain to take control for a safe taxi to parking with no reported damage.

synopsis: Q400 Captain reported concern over lack of information on restrictions and regulations regarding carriage of lithium batteries in the cabin.
summary: During boarding, a Flight Attendant discovered a passenger's large case contained a drone and seven lithium batteries exceeding known limits. Operations removed the passenger and batteries after station agents failed to identify the hazard, highlighting a lack of clear guidance on battery carriage limits.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported that an unruly passenger disrupted the cabin shortly before landing.
summary: The First Officer reported that during the landing rollout at LAX, flight attendants used the emergency call button due to a belligerent, intoxicated passenger who had unbuckled and walked the cabin. The crew stopped the aircraft, coordinated with operations despite ACARS failure, and delayed deplaning until law enforcement arrested the passenger at the gate.

synopsis: During takeoff in a B737-800 the Flight Crew received a 'Tail Strike' warning. When returning to the departure airport the Flight Crew received a 'Landing Gear Unsafe' indications on all three gears accompanied by the audible gear warning.
summary: The crew returned to the departure airport after a tail strike annunciation and a subsequent false unsafe gear warning caused by a loose hydraulic fitting in the left main gear. Maintenance confirmed no tail strike occurred, fixed the leak, and the crew recommended clarifying QRH guidance and adding a gear warning silence capability.

synopsis: B767-300 First Officer reported losing the Flight Director command bars shortly after takeoff, but regaining them when the autopilot was turned on.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Flight Director bars disappeared above 400 feet AGL after takeoff. Engaging the autopilot restored the bars, allowing the crew to complete the departure, though a maintenance log entry was made for the momentary failure.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported a speed deviation on the RAZRR3 arrival into SJC when there was a misunderstanding with ATC as to their clearance.
summary: Pilots flying to SJC on the RAZRR3 arrival exceeded the STUBL speed restriction after ATC issued ambiguous "Normal Speed" clearances instead of "Comply With Speed Restrictions." The crew subsequently corrected the error and noted that conflicting altitude and speed constraints at the GOTEE fix created further operational confusion.

synopsis: Air carrier First officer reported confusion with ATC reference speed control and altitude descent.
summary: During the WEEDA 2 arrival into DTW, a pilot flying received conflicting speed and altitude instructions from one controller, including a mistaken order to slow to 200 knots and rapid changes between 5,000, 11,000, 9,000, and 7,000 feet. The crew corrected the errors after questioning the controller, who confirmed the instructions were for them before handing off to the next sector.

synopsis: MD83 Captain reported the takeoff was rejected due to the Wheel Not Turning light. The right hand brake temperature was over 250 degrees.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff due to a Wheel Not Turning light and excessive right inboard brake temperature, but a mechanic attempted to defer the indications without logging a subsequent anti-skid failure. The pilot refused the aircraft after the mechanic failed to record the new fault in the logbook, citing unacceptable safety practices.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported on climbout they noticed the #2 engine oil quantity was 0 and the oil temperature was rising toward the amber zone.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Number 2 engine oil quantity indication of zero and rising temperature during initial climb, stabilizing after reducing thrust at 12,000 ft. Following troubleshooting and coordination with Dispatch and Maintenance, the crew returned to the departure airport for an uneventful overweight landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff when another aircraft reported seeing flames from the left engine.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff at 10 knots after another aircraft reported flames from the left engine exhaust. No abnormal engine indications were found, emergency vehicles observed no issues, and the crew taxied back to the gate under their own power.

synopsis: LR-35 flight crew reported landing with a large fuel imbalance due to the fuel crossflow valve light being inoperative. An earlier fuel crossfeed had been set up to address a fuel imbalance and was never secured during the Approach Checklist, due to the missing light indication. The right wingtip tank was damaged during the landing.
summary: The SIC and PIC of a Learjet 35 experienced an unstable approach and runway excursion due to a fuel imbalance caused by an inoperative fuel pump light and poor panel illumination. The crew failed to verify the active fuel transfer switch during descent, leading to a right-wingtip strike upon landing.

synopsis: Falcon 20 First Officer reported encountering a dual fuel transfer light issue in flight that he stated was not well covered in the manual.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced dual fuel transfer light illuminations at FL350 while the autopilot was engaged. After checklist procedures failed to resolve the issue, the Captain took control, notified ATC, and prepared for landing, noting a need for a specific dual failure procedure.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported distractions caused her to miss a man wearing an orthopedic boot in the exit row.
summary: A gate agent placed four ineligible passengers, including a man with an orthopedic boot, in exit rows and distracted the flight attendant during boarding. The agent coached passengers to falsely confirm understanding and closed the door early, resulting in the flight attendant discovering the boot-wearing passenger only after tripping over his foot.

synopsis: While performing maintenance on an EC135 T2 Helicopter the Mechanic neglected to secure a panel in the lower half of the fuselage.
summary: Two mechanics performing routine maintenance on base overlooked reinstalling an access panel after one stopped work to verify the other's inspection. The incident resulted from a lack of communication, complacency, and distraction while rushing to return the aircraft to service.

synopsis: Technician reported he was assigned to update the navigation database of an A320 using a navigation database for a B737.
summary: A mechanic attempted a NAV data load on an aircraft during a through trip but found incorrect Boeing references and unverified, manually altered disks. Management directed use of the disks, but the download failed, forcing a software revert and causing a significant delay.

synopsis: During scheduled maintenance on a Helicopter ECD-EC135 a mechanic safety wired an O2 bottle manual shutoff valve in the closed position when it should have been in the open position.
summary: A mechanic safety wired the manual oxygen shut-off valve in the closed position instead of open after replacing the bottle assembly on an EC135. This error caused a lack of oxygen flow to service ports for five days while the aircraft remained in medical service until a second mechanic identified the closed valve.

synopsis: C182RG Instructor pilot reported taking off with the oil filler cap not installed.
summary: A student pilot and CFI forgot to replace the oil filler cap after checking levels during preflight, causing oil to leak during climb out. They landed safely with less than one quart lost, attributing the error to unclear roles in the preflight process.

synopsis: ATC advised GV flight crew of a track deviation while flying the PEBLE 6 Departure out of SAN, and stated they have seen other Honeywell FMS-equipped aircraft experience similar track deviations.
summary: The PIC and SIC inadvertently deviated from the PEBLE 6 departure due to a Honeywell FMS database error providing false turning cues. Contributing factors included crew failure to detect the 813 nm error during verification and delayed recognition of the heading deviation until ATC intervention.

synopsis: The flight crew of a G-IV reported descending below the assigned altitude after flying through the localizer in VMC conditions.
summary: During ILS approach vectors, the captain descended below assigned altitudes to 2,400 and 1,800 feet MSL while re-intercepting the localizer. The crew subsequently requested and received a visual approach clearance after visually acquiring the airport.

synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported an airspace violation and a terrain alert while climbing out from Ogden Utah.
summary: The pilot, climbing out southeast of Ogden, received a terrain alert while distracted by Hill Tower's closure, prompting an evasive maneuver that briefly entered SLC Bravo airspace without clearance. The incident resulted from the pilot's erroneous assumption that Hill Tower operates 24/7 and the restrictive local airspace geometry.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reported a near miss with a UAS at 1150 ft enroute to the RIISE waypoint between FME and ANP, 2 NM southeast of the WMPT TV tower.
summary: A pilot flying a Cirrus SR20 at 1150 ft near Annapolis, MD, encountered a large black and red drone at 1000–1100 ft while en route to FME. The pilot overtook the unreported UAS, which was not visible on TIS-B, and continued the flight without altering course or altitude.

synopsis: The pilot of a small airplane reported the loss of communication with ATC while enroute to a private airport that had not been shared with ATC. Later, law enforcement located the pilot to confirm a safe arrival.
summary: A pilot using a handheld radio due to a failed #1 comm experienced lost communications during descent and squawked 7600 before landing at a private airport. This triggered an unnecessary search because the pilot failed to contact Flight Service after landing to confirm the aircraft's status.

synopsis: The pilot of a BE36 reported a loss of electrical power and the steps taken to begin a diversion, regain the electrical system, and notify ATC while in a congested area with changing weather.
summary: During cruise climb, a pilot experienced a total electrical failure in a Bonanza, leaving only standby instruments and an iPad for navigation. Power was restored after cycling the master switch, allowing the pilot to coordinate with ATC and land safely at a diversion airport due to marginal weather.

synopsis: The pilot of a C172 reported initial notification of traffic from ATC followed by notice that there was no longer a traffic issue. The pilot was then surprised by a near-mid-air-collision that required both aircraft to take evasive action.
summary: The pilot received a traffic advisory from approach regarding a faster aircraft 300 feet above, but shortly after the alert was cancelled, a King Air appeared directly ahead. Both pilots executed evasive action to avoid a collision, and approach could not identify the intruder aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a PA46 reported becoming distracted while departing VFR from a non-towered airport and penetrating the nearby Class B airspace prior to receiving an IFR clearance.
summary: The pilot departed a non-towered airport in VMC intending to avoid Class B airspace but inadvertently climbed through the 1,800-foot floor without leveling off. The breach was attributed to distractions from avoiding the airspace, monitoring another aircraft, and destination weather, compounded by a GPS map zoom level that obscured the airspace boundaries.

synopsis: A Controller told an aircraft to hold short of a runway, but did not notice when the aircraft taxied onto the runway. The Controller had an arrival less than two mile final and had allowed another aircraft to cross the runway from an intersection.
summary: A student solo pilot (Aircraft X) taxied onto the runway without a Line Up and Wait clearance, likely misinterpreting instructions to a downwind aircraft, while the local controller failed to notice the incursion. The controller subsequently ordered an approaching aircraft (Aircraft Y) to go around after the student was directed to exit the runway.

synopsis: A Tower Local Controller observed the other Local Controller allow an aircraft to land with less than the required minimum separation from the preceding aircraft.
summary: A Final Monitor Controller and Local Controller managed Aircraft Y on final approach in MVFR weather, where speed differences threatened separation. The Local Controller declined to intervene despite the risk, citing an intent to retire, while the reporter noted a failure to enforce safety over efficiency.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: NCT Controller reported assigning an air carrier an altitude to stay above unidentified VFR traffic. The VFR traffic climbed toward the air carrier which responded to a TCAS RA alert.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an ILS approach clearance to Aircraft X but cancelled it upon observing an unidentified VFR aircraft at 4,000 feet in the flight path. The controller assigned 5,500 feet, but the VFR aircraft climbed rapidly, causing Aircraft X to respond to a resolution advisory to descend.

synopsis: Controller reported issuing traffic to an aircraft on a missed approach. Both aircraft were below the MIA and the Controller could not turn the aircraft to avoid traffic. Controller later questioned if he should have done something different.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic advisories to Aircraft X, a student pilot executing a missed approach at GHM, regarding a conflicting VFR aircraft at 2,200 feet. The controller delayed turning the aircraft below the 2,500-foot MIA due to uncertainty about terrain clearance, though later considered that an emergency turn below the MIA might have been safer.

synopsis: A Tower Controller was clearing helicopters to land and depart from a closed runway. The Controller allowed an aircraft to taxi across the closed runway with a helicopter on approach.
summary: A Local Controller cleared a helicopter for takeoff without scanning for conflicting traffic, while Ground Control crossed the runway without coordination during helicopter operations. The reporter questions if these actions comply with FAA Order JO 7110.704 regarding runway crossing and visual observation requirements.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: An unidentified VFR aircraft was maneuvering in the vicinity of main arrival routes to an airport. ATC had to vector and assign altitudes to several air carrier aircraft to avoid the VFR traffic.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a moderate arrival push into DFW when a Code 4402 aircraft climbed erratically, causing a TCAS resolution advisory for Aircraft Y and requiring traffic calls for Aircraft Z, Y, and A. The unidentified aircraft eventually landed at ZZZ airport after performing multiple 360-degree turns, prompting the controller to advise operators to exercise more caution.

synopsis: ZAU Controller reported that ZOB is routinely late on taking handoffs and that they do not answer landlines in a timely manner.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that ZOB Cleveland Center routinely delays accepting handoffs for aircraft like MIZAR3 at FL210 until less than one minute from the boundary. The controller attributed this to a lack of timely communication and recommended remedial training for ZOB staff.

synopsis: S46 controller reported of a loss of separation due to a particular type of aircraft that climbs out slower than most other aircraft. Controller would like to see LOA changed between Tower and TRACON to exclude this type of aircraft from use of visual separation during climb out.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Departure East sector stopped Aircraft Y at 3,000 feet and restricted its speed after it overtook the slow-climbing Aircraft X during visual separation. The controller terminated automatic releases and vectored Aircraft Y northwest to maintain separation, attributing the incident to Aircraft X's slow climb performance.

synopsis: CNO Tower Controller reported an NMAC when the Controller was expecting the first departure to turn southwest, but it actually turned WNW towards another departing aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft Y and Aircraft X for departure from parallel runways, but Aircraft Y deviated west-northwest without squawking the assigned code, causing a near mid-air collision with Aircraft X. The controller resolved the conflict by issuing a left turn to Aircraft X after initial confusion over conflicting "PRADO" waypoints and radio congestion.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU Controller reported ZOB ARTCC routinely does not accept automated handoffs in a timely manner.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that ZOB Center routinely delays accepting handoffs for Aircraft X until less than one minute from their boundary. The reporter attributed this to a lack of training on map settings and timely handoff acceptance procedures.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: S46 TRACON Controller stated Airbus type departing aircraft routinely climb at much slower airspeeds than similar size type aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a compressing separation between a slow-climbing Airbus and a trailing B738 during successive visual departures. The controller broke noise abatement procedures to initiate an early turn for the B738, attributing the unsafe situation to the Airbus's slow climb rate and recommending a Letter of Agreement change.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DPA Tower reporter TRACON transfers simultaneous Visual Approach arrivals to Tower without ensuring a sequence or separation of the aircraft.
summary: Tower reported that TRACON failed to coordinate two IFR aircraft on visual approaches, resulting in inadequate separation. The Tower controller attempted to notify TRACON of providing visual separation, but TRACON did not respond, creating an unsafe situation.

synopsis: CMH TRACON Controller forgot to coordinate an arrival aircraft's intentions or issue communication change to the Tower. The Tower Controller made no effort to establish communications with the aircraft or to reach out to the TRACON to coordinate. The aircraft made a touch and go into confliction with an intersecting runway departure.
summary: A Radar controller failed to assign a frequency change to Aircraft X, which executed an unauthorized touch-and-go on the right runway while a Medevac used the left. The reporter claims the Tower controller deliberately allowed this pilot deviation without attempting contact or light gun signals, creating an unsafe situation with a nearby helicopter.

synopsis: A military flight of two aircraft climbed above the altitude of their assigned departure procedure into confliction with enroute traffic.
summary: A TRACON controller reported that military Aircraft X violated an 8,000-foot clearance while climbing behind departing Aircraft Y, requiring a visual separation instruction. The controller attributed the incident to a pilot deviation and expressed concern that military crews are not held to the same standards as civilian pilots.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZAU Controller reported issuing a VFR on top clearance and confusion ensued as to what the pilot and Controller responsibilities were.
summary: An ATC trainee issued a VFR-ON-TOP clearance to Aircraft X climbing from 14,000 feet, which the pilot accepted and leveled at 14,500 feet. A subsequent inquiry from the receiving sector revealed confusion over whether the aircraft remained IFR or became VFR after being instructed to "maintain VFR."

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DFW Tower Controller reported an airspace violation. Aircraft was taken off approach due to a lack of separation and turned. Controllers did not make appropriate point out.
summary: Local West controller issued a left turn to Aircraft X to avoid a conflict with departing Aircraft Y after the Final Monitor cancelled the approach. The controller failed to point out Aircraft X to Meacham North, resulting in a potential loss of radar contact due to untrained airspace boundaries.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported of an NMAC. Local Controller turned one aircraft towards another aircraft making the second aircraft take evasive actions to avoid turning aircraft. Reporter wanted this to be looked at and stated it was due to the Local Controller having issues relating to home and fatigue.
summary: An air traffic controller instructed Aircraft X to turn right, causing it to conflict with Aircraft Y, which took evasive action to avoid a 300 to 400-foot separation loss. The reporter attributes the incident to the controller's recent fatigue and personal problems.

synopsis: An MRI Tower Controller observed the TRACON Controller terminate VFR services to an aircraft instead of handing off the aircraft to the Center.
summary: A Local Control controller reported that a TRACON controller terminated radar services for a departing VFR aircraft instead of handing it off to Center, despite a filed flight plan. This denied the pilot requested flight following services, creating a potentially dangerous situation contrary to FAA Order 7110.65.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported missing a crossing altitude on the RAVNN 6 Arrival into BWI citing ATC changes to the procedure as a factor in the incident.
summary: The Captain missed a FL230 restriction at FZEEK during the RAVNN 6 arrival into BWI due to degraded situational awareness caused by multiple ATC off-profile vectors, speed restrictions, and single-pilot workload while the First Officer communicated with cabin crew. The crew corrected the error with ATC assistance, attributing the incident to excessive arrival modifications and FMC reliability concerns.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported that a confrontation between the Gate Agent and the Captain before departure created a tense, unsafe atmosphere for the flight.
summary: A gate agent refused the Captain's request to board deadheading crew first, entered the flight deck, and made confrontational remarks heard by passengers. This created a tense, unsafe environment during pushback, prompting the Captain to involve a supervisor before the flight departed.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported responding to an RA on approach to LGA.
summary: During descent into LGA, the crew received a TCAS climb RA while level at 2500 ft despite an ATC traffic advisory for a Skyhawk at 2000 ft. The crew complied with the RA, observed the intruder 100 feet below on the display, and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported an unintentional cycling of the right engine fuel control switch during taxi in to the gate. A short time later, ground personnel reported a small flame coming from the engine.
summary: During taxi-in, the First Officer inadvertently moved the right fuel cutoff switch out of detent, causing the right engine to shut down and produce a minor flame upon fuel reintroduction. Ground personnel observed the flame and called the fire department, though no engine damage or abnormal indications occurred.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport when the left main landing gear failed to retract after takeoff.
summary: The crew diverted to a nearby airport after the left main landing gear failed to retract on departure, while the nose and right main gears retracted normally. Following fuel dumping, the aircraft made a soft, uneventful overweight landing, after which maintenance pinned the left gear as a precaution.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported difficulty stopping on the runway after finding braking action 'poor' rather than 'medium' as reported by Tower at MGGT.
summary: The pilot landed a max weight aircraft on Runway 20 in rain with a 5-knot tailwind using flaps 30 instead of the briefed flaps 40. Despite max braking, poor braking action caused the aircraft to stop with only 150 feet remaining, prompting a report of 'poor' conditions to the tower.

synopsis: A330 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff at 90 kts when the bulk cargo door light was annunciated.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 90 kts after a BULK CARGO ECAM warning appeared during the roll with Flex thrust set. Auto brakes stopped the aircraft, and a Fire Rescue inspection confirmed no damage before the flight returned to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported receiving an E2 FIRE DET FAIL EICAS message on climbout. They advised ATC and returned to their departure airport.
summary: During climbout through FL230, the crew received an E2 FIRE DET FAIL EICAS message and returned to ZZZ. Fire rescue inspected the number 2 engine, confirming a faulty fire loop, after which passengers were safely deplaned at the gate.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported a track deviation occurred on approach to MSP when the flight crew tuned in the wrong ILS frequency.
summary: During cruise, the pilot-in-command and pilot monitoring mistakenly briefed and hard-tuned the ILS 12L frequency instead of the intended 12R at MSP. The error was detected at 5,000 feet during approach mode engagement, corrected by re-entering the correct frequency, and attributed to a lack of FMS cross-checking and manual frequency tuning.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported a close UAS encounter at 1,600 feet on a four mile final to Runway 27 at SAN.
summary: A pilot on a visual RNAV final approach at 1,600 feet MSL sighted a large black drone approximately 200 feet above the aircraft. No evasive action was required as the drone passed overhead, but the pilot reported the incident to tower and ground control to warn other traffic.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported missing a crossing restriction on the BRUSR1 RNAV to PHX. ATC had assigned one altitude change and two speed adjustments during the arrival and the crew experienced a TCAS event just before the altitude overshoot.
summary: Pilots flying a BRUSR1 RNAV arrival into PHX descended below the BRIEZ restriction after ATC issued unpublished speed and altitude clearances. The crew attributed the error to failing to reset the MCP altitude when switching to LVL CHG due to a distracting TCAS alert.

synopsis: EC135 medevac pilot reported encountering unannounced jumpers in the air on arrival to an uncontrolled airport.
summary: A helicopter crew conducting a medical transfer at ZZZ encountered a skydiver at 1500 AGL during short final without prior Unicom notification of jump operations. The pilot continued the landing safely, but the military unit later acknowledged the lack of communication regarding the C-130 jump activity.

synopsis: Dash 8 flight crew reported they returned to departure airport after noting a FWD EXIT DOOR light.
summary: During climb through 15,000 feet, the FWD EXIT DOOR warning illuminated, prompting the crew to run the door and unpressurized flight checklists. The Captain leveled off, advised ATC, and returned to the departure airport for a safe landing.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported having difficulty complying with the taxi clearance at EWR citing fatigue, weather conditions, and taxiway markings as contributing.
summary: The pilot and first officer at EWR mistakenly turned onto taxiway Bravo instead of Delta due to confusing signage, rain, fatigue, and crew disagreement. The aircraft was stopped, and ground control issued amended instructions to reach the correct taxiway.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew reported crossing the ILS hold line while waiting for takeoff on Runway 04 at LGA. Crew was confused as conditions were VMC and ILS not in use. Crew later realized the ILS hold line is used for wingtip clearance for landing traffic.
summary: The flight crew taxied to Runway 4 at LGA and inadvertently crossed the ILS hold short line, causing an approaching aircraft to execute a go-around. The incident resulted from the crew missing the active ILS hold line requirement for wingtip clearance, which was not highlighted in NOTAMs or their charts despite being on the airport diagram.

synopsis: CE-560 pilot reported an NMAC with a high wing light aircraft while departing LOT airport.
summary: During takeoff from an uncontrolled airport, a jet crew encountered a C-172 converging vertically and horizontally due to poor visibility and lack of radio communication. The Pilot Monitoring grabbed controls to execute an aggressive turn, achieving approximately 500 feet of separation before the C-172 passed behind.

synopsis: The pilot of a Gulfstream G-IV reported a fuel leak from the left wing that resulted in a return to the field. It was later determined that a fuel system check valve was stuck open and venting fuel overboard.
summary: The flight crew observed intermittent fuel spray from the left wing during climb at 13,000 feet. They held altitude to burn fuel for a safe landing weight, then returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing and maintenance inspection.

synopsis: B737-700 Flight Attendant reported feeling ill from exposure to fumes in the cabin.
summary: Cabin crew and the flight deck experienced a strong, unidentified chemical odor during takeoff and descent, causing respiratory distress and dizziness. Post-landing testing confirmed carbon monoxide exposure, requiring medical treatment, while the reporter attributed delayed action to the Captain's dismissive attitude.

synopsis: ERJ-190 Flight Attendant reported the flight returned to the departure airport after the cabin filled with noxious fumes.
summary: A flight attendant reported a burning smell and passenger symptoms during climb, leading the captain to execute a precautionary return to the departure airport. No visible smoke was observed, but the crew attributed the diversion to the odor and resulting health effects.
