synopsis: DA-20 instructor pilot reported returning to the departure airport after the engine began to run rough and show a loss of oil pressure.
summary: A pilot and student experienced an engine failure shortly after takeoff in a single-engine aircraft due to a fractured front left cylinder. The incident caused oil loss, vibration, and a burnt smell, forcing an immediate return and safe landing with fire services standing by.

synopsis: BE400A Captain reported rejecting the takeoff when he noticed a yaw tendency. During the reject procedure, Tower advised the right main gear tire was on fire.
summary: The pilot of a Beechjet 400A aborted takeoff at 80 knots due to excessive left rudder input required to maintain the runway centerline. Tower reported a right tire fire, prompting the crew to evacuate the aircraft with two passengers after stopping right of the centerline.

synopsis: C172 pilot was advised by ATC he was in a hot restricted area that was shown cold during his preflight.
summary: A VFR pilot flying from HND to MHV entered active restricted area R2524 after relying on an FAA website showing it inactive and accepting an unclear ATC clearance. The pilot realized the error only after ATC notification, attributing the incident to failing to verify the area's actual status with controllers.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A flight instructor reported that his student damaged the high wing aircraft's wingtip, navigation light and lens while maneuvering in the WHP Runway 30 runup area. Reportedly, taxi lines may be too close to the boundary fence.
summary: A student pilot and CFI taxiing a general aviation aircraft at WHP scraped the left wingtip against a boundary fence while distracted by a radio call to change runways. The incident was caused by insufficient clearance between the yellow run-up lines and the fence, compounded by the CFI's unfamiliarity with the non-standard markings.

synopsis: A TRACON controller reported difficulty with handoffs from the Center. One of the data tags disappeared from the radar display and displayed a *splat* symbol. The other handoff data tag was in a different location than the TRACON controller's radar display indicated.
summary: A CHS controller experienced ARTS IIE radar data tag discrepancies during a handoff involving Aircraft X and Y, causing a 30-mile position jump and confusion with Aircraft Z. The reporter attributed the issue to incorrect beacon codes and requested an examination of the ARTS computer interface between CHS and Center.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: SAV TRACON Controller reported accepting an automated handoff of an aircraft with 'AMBQ' in the data tag. The actual position of the aircraft was ninety miles northwest of the position of the data tag the controller accepted for handoff.
summary: An air traffic controller accepted an AMBQ handoff of Aircraft X from Center despite protocol, later discovering the radar track was a false target with a real call sign tag. The actual aircraft was 90 miles away, and the controller attributed the dangerous situation to unfixable radar issues creating realistic false targets.

synopsis: B737 crew reported being cleared for takeoff while taking the runway at MSP. They switch frequencies to which a Clearance Delivery Controller answers and sends them back to previous Tower frequency. First Officer verifies they are still cleared for takeoff.
summary: The Tower Controller instructed the crew to switch frequencies while taxiing onto the runway for takeoff, causing confusion and distraction. The crew temporarily lost contact before the Controller clarified the error and reconfirmed the takeoff clearance, allowing the flight to depart safely.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported letting the airspeed get low on a go-around maneuver from an unstabilized approach.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway 27, the crew executed a go-around after Approach Control vectored them too high and close. The Pilot Flying mishandled pitch control causing two airspeed warnings, while the Pilot Monitoring failed to take control, resulting in poor coordination before a successful second approach.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported landing normally after receiving a TE Flap Disagree message on EICAS.
summary: The flight crew received a TE Edge flap disagree message on EICAS while transitioning from flaps 15 to 20 on approach. They leveled off at 5,000 feet and 180 knots, ran the checklist, and landed uneventfully 15 minutes later with flaps 20.

synopsis: Flight crew of a widebody transport cleared to a conflicting altitude during departure from RJAA resulting in a TA alert. Crew complied with a new cleared altitude and thus cleared the conflict.
summary: The flight crew climbing from RJAA on the Cupid departure received a clearance to maintain 9,000 feet after reporting traffic at 10,000 feet. Although the aircraft briefly reached 9,400 feet before descending, a Traffic Advisory occurred without a Resolution Advisory, and the crew confirmed no near miss despite passenger concerns.

synopsis: A ramp agent reported that while driving a second jet bridge to an aircraft's door 2, another ramp agent commanded a stop because the jet bridge was too close to the running engine 1, which may have ingested an air conditioning hose. Only a camera fed monitor is viewable by the jet bridge operator to check travel.
summary: A ramp agent stopped a second jetbridge moving toward door 2 while the aircraft's number 1 engine was running due to concerns about an air hose being sucked in. The reporter noted no specific policy prohibits this approach, though the bridge operator relied solely on a camera monitor without direct movement signals.

synopsis: MD-11 Relief Pilot reported the flight diverted after detecting a probable fuel leak.
summary: The crew executed a suspected fuel leak checklist after observing excessive fuel burn, diverting to the nearest suitable airport. Post-landing visual inspection by ground personnel revealed no signs of fuel leakage, and the aircraft was shut down safely.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported receiving a TA after the autopilot overshot a crossing restriction on descent into PHX.
summary: Pilots on a descent via the HYDRR1 arrival to PHX descended below the 9000 ft CHAVO restriction due to autopilot failure while distracted by two simultaneous TCAS Traffic Advisories. The crew manually intervened at 8700 ft to climb back to 9000 ft, later learning the conflicting CRJ received a Resolution Advisory.

synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported low cabin pressure resulted from failure to properly position the flow selector.
summary: The pilot flying and first officer experienced a cabin pressurization failure at 16,000 feet due to the bleed flow selector being left in the Min position during the after-takeoff flow. They descended to 10,000 feet, corrected the setting, and continued the flight without injury or mechanical damage.

synopsis: Dash 8 flight crew reported returning to the departure airport after experiencing a landing gear malfunction upon gear retraction.
summary: The flight crew experienced excessive nose gear rattling and an unsafe light during climb after gear retraction, prompting a return to ZZZ. After selecting the correct checklist and confirming no emergency, they executed a normal landing with the gear down and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: An air carrier relief pilot reported confusion accessing the data necessary to operate within a foreign country when using the ipad as compared to paper charts.
summary: A pilot reported that critical Tel Aviv FIR entry requirements were difficult to locate on the JeppView iPad app compared to paper charts during a flight to Tel Aviv. The reporter warned that relying on electronic charts without specific training or system alerts could lead crews to miss mandatory radio callouts.

synopsis: An Air Carrier flight crew reported a runway incursion that took place in PEK when the crew thought they were cleared for immediate takeoff and had crossed the hold short line. ATC then cleared them for takeoff, but when airborne advised they had not been given a line up and wait clearance.
summary: The flight crew entered Runway 19 without clearance due to a First Officer mic selector error and misunderstood tower instructions, compounded by language barriers and FMC distractions. A supervisor later advised the crew that the unauthorized lineup was dangerous, though no other traffic was impacted.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain reported both FMS's locked up for an unspecified period of time, but then returned to normal operation.
summary: The pilot reported that both Flight Management Systems involuntarily switched to the menu page and would not unlock, prompting a diversion to an alternate. The anomaly self-corrected after selecting heading mode, allowing the flight to continue to the original destination with no further issues.

synopsis: A Boeing 737 Captain reported a fuel imbalance condition which was the result of fuel crossfeed mismanagement and an intra cockpit communication breakdown. The situation was corrected and an uneventful landing was accomplished.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying rebalanced fuel alone during a bathroom swap at FL 350, causing a tank imbalance discovered later during descent. The pilot attributed the incident to performing the task without the First Officer present and failing to communicate the action upon his return.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported being informed after a flight that the Loadmaster had not accounted for additional passengers that were boarded at the previous stop resulting in a 3,900 KG error. The Loadmaster had been on the aircraft for 10 days and was very fatigued.
summary: The pilot reported that a fatigued load master provided an incorrect loading verification form, causing a 3,982 KG weight and balance discrepancy due to unaccounted passengers. Although the aircraft remained within limits, high workload from rejected flight plans prevented the pilot from verifying the error before departure.

synopsis: Wide body transport flight crew reported speed and altitude deviations resulting from an encounter with moderate to severe turbulence at FL370.
summary: The crew encountered moderate to severe turbulence 70 miles southeast of MCI at FL370, 60 miles upwind of convective weather. This caused a 20-knot speed increase triggering high-speed warnings and a 500-foot climb, but the aircraft was returned to FL370 within seconds.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported the Captain rejected the takeoff near V1 after noting a spoileron roll caution message.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff near V1 after receiving a spoileron roll caution message. Following a 15-minute wait and QRH checks, they continued to the destination, noting the decision was driven by the split-second nature of the warning.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported a diversion due to a fuel balance problem associated with misinterpretation of an MEL.
summary: The flight crew diverted a Boeing 737-900 due to a fuel imbalance caused by misinterpreting MEL instructions to keep the gravity X-flow valve open. The error prevented proper imbalance correction, leading to a precautionary landing with 500 lbs of remaining imbalance after the crew realized the valve should have been closed.

synopsis: A SR20 flight instructor reported a severe engine vibration in cruise that resulted in a return to the departure airport. It was later discovered that a cylinder valve was broken.
summary: The PIC reported severe engine shaking during cruise flight despite normal power and temperature indications. The aircraft returned to the departure airport after the pilot contacted approach.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beechcraft 99 reported smoke and smell in the aircraft during a training flight that resulted in a return to the departure airport and crew evacuation.
summary: During a VFR training flight, the pilot and trainee experienced an electrical fire with smoke entering the cockpit after landing, caused by an overheated gear motor. The crew evacuated the aircraft, and maintenance later confirmed the gear motor was too hot to touch, though the fire department could not identify the specific source.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported that while troubleshooting a Bombardier CRJ200 hydraulic overheat problem, the Mechanic and the Lead working the aircraft could not agree on what path to take to make a proper repair. The Mechanic and Lead also disagreed on an entry door seal repair due to a support wheel lock lever that was bent.
summary: A mechanic reported a bent passenger door support wheel lock lever and a faulty hydraulic pump 3a, but the lead mechanic aggressively pressured him to alter the write-ups and incorrectly diagnosed the hydraulic issue as a reservoir failure. The mechanic refused to falsify the reports, resulting in the aircraft being grounded for proper repairs while the lead exhibited threatening and bullying behavior.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 reported the factors that led to a gear-up landing.
summary: A pilot practicing touch-and-goes in a Cessna inadvertently raised the landing gear during a rushed final approach checklist. The aircraft landed gear-up, striking the propeller on the runway and causing damage to the propeller and undercarriage before skidding to a stop.

synopsis: A flight instructor reported a near mid-air collision due to miscommunication by ATC. Reportedly the incorrect, but similar, aircraft registration number was used by ATC to issue instructions.
summary: A pilot conducting touch-and-go maneuvers at a busy airport nearly collided with a Cessna on a parallel runway after the controller issued a "give way" instruction to the wrong aircraft. The pilot took evasive action and cited 14 CFR 91.3, noting the controller's error was confirmed by reviewing ATC recordings.

synopsis: CE-550 Captain reported experiencing a rapid decompression at FL360.
summary: The crew experienced a rapid decompression at FL360 and performed an emergency descent with checklists. No conflict occurred, and ATC facilitated the situation without the crew reporting an emergency.

synopsis: A C182 flight instructor and trainee reported a loss of control and runway excursion during a soft field takeoff due to excessive elevator input.
summary: During a soft field takeoff demonstration, the pilot lost directional control due to excessive nose-high attitude and light crosswind. The aircraft struck a runway light, scraped both wingtips and the horizontal stabilizer, and exited the runway before stopping.

synopsis: A Controller and a flight instructor reported that an aircraft assigned a vector for one approach intercepted and began descent on a different approach. The controller did not immediately notice because they left their control position to go to the bathroom.
summary: A student and instructor pilot mistakenly flew a VOR-A approach without clearance after ATC misrecorded their request and vectored them for an ILS while a controller was absent. The crew descended toward the airport until ATC detected the deviation and ordered an immediate climb, resulting in a missed approach and return to the departure airport.

synopsis: The Tower Controller reported that rescue/fire vehicles did not follow proper communication procedures during an emergency.
summary: The Tower Controller reported that during an inbound emergency, untrained fire trucks directly contacted Ground Control instead of Airport Command, causing confusion and an unverified runway crossing. The Fire Chief admitted the error was due to dispatcher training failures, yet the unsafe communication breakdown persists despite previous management reviews.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft on a Visual Approach overshot the final approach course and conflicted with an aircraft on approach to the parallel runway at PHL. The Tower Controller reported a NMAC. The flight crew of the deviating aircraft had the parallel traffic in sight.
summary: Aircraft Y on a visual approach to the left runway turned right toward Aircraft X on the right runway, nearly colliding due to deteriorating weather and parallel operations. Controllers subsequently suspended left runway arrivals after the near miss, though the pilots reported no evasive maneuvers were required.

synopsis: An ARTCC Controller worked a period of traffic of extreme complexity due to numerous weather deviations and too many aircraft routed through their airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that severe weather and high traffic volume caused radar data block overlap and frequency congestion across multiple ARTCC sectors. The supervisor requested Traffic Management Unit (TMU) reroutes, but TMU refused to act, leading the controller to criticize their lack of proactivity and accountability.

synopsis: An aircraft on a VFR flight landing at an alternate airport due to approaching inclement weather ran off the end of the runway.
summary: A trainee Radar Controller and supervisor assisted a VFR pilot of Aircraft X diverting due to severe weather. After the pilot landed at an alternate airport, a post-landing call revealed the aircraft overran the runway and ended up in a field at night.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported that an aircraft was cleared to depart towards an arrival conducting an opposite direction circling approach to the same runway. The TRACON Controller was not sure if facility opposite direction orders apply to circling approaches.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared an IFR aircraft for a VOR circle to Runway 13 without using Opposite Direction Operation phraseology, believing it was not required. A departing aircraft subsequently took off toward the circling aircraft, prompting the controller to request clarification on whether circling approaches constitute an ODO.

synopsis: NCT TRACON Controller reported releasing a departure from RHV without recognizing the runway in use was the opposite direction from what the controller planned. The controller had to vector the aircraft below the minimum vectoring altitude to avoid arrivals to nearby SJC.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly issued an IFR release to an RHV departure assuming Runway 30 instead of the active Runway 13, causing the aircraft to become airborne before the error was corrected. The controller directed the pilot to turn left heading 290, violating Minimum Vectoring Altitude, to avoid conflict with SJC arrival traffic.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported diverting to an alternate after one main landing gear failed to retract after takeoff.
summary: The crew experienced a false left main gear down warning shortly after takeoff at near maximum weight, prompting a fuel dump and diversion to an alternate. They executed a safe 380,000-pound landing with no issues, followed by brake cooling procedures on the ground.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported he noticed a fuel spill on the ramp and felt the lack of response from the fire department, airport, and company were troubling.
summary: The Captain observed a significant JET-A fuel spill from the left wing NACA vent during single-point fueling while maintenance was in the cockpit. Although the Captain requested fire services multiple times, an Airport Operations agent overrode the request based on the fueler's claim of a minor spill, resulting in no fire department response despite the large volume of fuel and strong fumes.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported confusion when ATC cleared him to 'descend via the PARQR1 arrival to CLT, landing south' without specifying the runway, leaving the final altitude in question.
summary: The pilot reported that the clearance to descend via PARQR1 for a south landing at CLT was ambiguous because the procedure requires different altitudes for Runway 23 versus Runways 18L/C/R. The reporter stated that using the phrase "landing south" is insufficient and that specific runway designations must be expressed to ensure correct altitude assignment.

synopsis: ERJ-190 flight crew reported two track deviations resulted when the FMS did not perform as expected.
summary: Pilots reported FMS malfunctions on HAARP3 and ROBUC1 arrivals where the system missed intersections by over 5 miles and 2.6 miles respectively, displaying two active legs simultaneously. Mechanics found no fault messages or database errors, suggesting a restart, while Approach Control noted the deviation was excessive for busy airspace despite no immediate safety compromise.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported executing a low altitude go-around at CLT when the flight ballooned as a result of either a gust of wind or a wake turbulence encounter.
summary: The crew executed a balked landing on a visual approach to RWY 23 after ballooning due to wake turbulence or wind, which caused an engine overspeed and ITT exceedance. They subsequently landed safely on RWY 18R after the pilot took control to correct glide slope deviation.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 flight crew reported what appeared to be pitot icing at FL370 in IMC. The equipment affected were both airspeed/Mach systems, Integrated Standby Instruments, FADEC, RUD LIMITER, STALL Warning, MACH TRIM and EFIS COMP MON. The crew diverted to the nearby airport for an uneventful landing. Descending through FL200 in VMC partial equipment functionality returned.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced blocked pitot tubes and erroneous airspeeds while circumnavigating weather at FL370, triggering multiple caution messages including Rudder Limiter faults. They descended to FL310, diverted to a nearby airport, and landed safely using backup instruments and CRM after the autopilot failed.

synopsis: CE-680 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after noting system multiple anomalies associated with probable pitot/static icing.
summary: During enroute descent into an alternate, the crew encountered thunderstorms and icing, triggering engine control faults, autopilot loss, and erroneous airspeed indications on the left side. The pilots manually controlled the aircraft to a visual landing at a nearby uncontrolled airport, attributing the failures to severe icing overwhelming the anti-ice systems.

synopsis: Aircrew of a jet transport executed a rejected take-off. Tower cleared aircraft to clear runway at a specific taxiway but due to the night conditions, lack of line guidance, and close proximity of the taxiway, the crew could not see the required taxiway.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff on Runway 9 at Boston due to an ADR 1 fault and received a clearance to turn left at intersection 'K'. Poor lighting and the lack of taxi lines caused confusion, but the aircraft held short of Runway 4L, forcing an arriving aircraft to go around without loss of separation.

synopsis: B787 Captain reported that the auto load function for engine thrust settings was acting improperly and required a manual override.
summary: The flight crew encountered a Flight Management Computer uplink discrepancy during pre-flight for runway 19, showing incorrect thrust derate and reduction altitude compared to the Takeoff Performance System. Manual corrections were made after a new performance system confirmed the original data, resolving the anomaly previously seen on 787 and 777 aircraft.

synopsis: First Officer reported taxiing into position on runway without clearance. The flight was subsequently cleared for takeoff.
summary: The First Officer and Captain inadvertently taxied onto the runway without clearance due to a communication mishap and language barrier while holding short. Although the Tower initially questioned the movement, the crew received a takeoff clearance, and the reporter stated no other traffic was affected.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported not fully configuring the aircraft at the appropriate time per company procedures during a circling maneuver off the VOR DME Runway 07 at MROC to land Runway 25. The procedure calls for the pattern to be flown at 4,000 MSL which is less than 1,000 feet AGL.
summary: The flight crew arrived at MROC in a jet, flying a VOR DME Runway 07 approach to transition to an RNAV Runway 25 landing. They delayed full configuration until 1,000 feet AGL due to unfamiliarity with the maneuver, but corrected the error by climbing and configuring early while maintaining VFR.

synopsis: CRJ-200 crew reported they executed missed approaches at their destination and alternate airport due to deteriorating weather conditions. They reported landing at an airport that was not approved for their operations with ATC assistance.
summary: The flight crew diverted to an unapproved airport south of their position due to deteriorating weather and low fuel reserves after missing approaches at the destination and alternate. They landed safely despite lacking charts, relying on ATC vectors and visual confirmation of clear skies to ensure a secure landing environment.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported an inflight distraction was a factor in her not properly securing the galley carts, several of which rolled down the aisle after landing.
summary: A flight attendant lost track of time after retrieving broken watch pieces post-10,000 feet, leading to missed cart brake checks. Upon landing, two carts rolled down the aisle, but the crew member secured them and confirmed all passengers were uninjured.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot and student flying the RNM RNAV (GPS)-B Approach reported a near miss near JLI VOR at 7,700 ft.
summary: While descending to 7,700 feet for an RNAV-B approach, the pilot reported a VFR aircraft deliberately following and overtaking them near the JLI VOR. The pilot contacted TRACON and RNM Tower, who confirmed no communication with the other aircraft, which subsequently landed ahead on a VOR approach.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAN Controller described a situation where the trainee he was instructing did not ensure the correct facility was coordinated with. This caused an error of altitude to be coordinated with another Center.
summary: A trainer and trainee mistakenly approved Aircraft X for FL360 instead of FL350 while climbing to Oakland airspace due to misreading a coordination window. The error occurred because they viewed coordination from PAZA rather than KZAK, and the subsequent discrepancy alert was ignored as the aircraft was still climbing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ICT Approach Controller reported a loss of separation that he attributed to an aircraft not descending like he thought it would. Aircraft in question started out with a higher rate of descent, but must have changed when the aircraft got closer to the airport.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a business jet (Aircraft X) descending to 4,000 ft and another aircraft (Aircraft Y) at 6,000 ft near ICT. A computer conflict alert triggered when Aircraft X descended slowly on a converging course, though the controller judged no actual conflict occurred and attributed the alert to the jet's reduced descent rate.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport because of weather at the destination.
summary: The crew encountered wind shear and severe thunderstorms during the approach to the destination, triggering a missed approach. After ATC denied a requested weather avoidance turn due to traffic, the crew diverted to their alternate airport.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported calling in fatigued after cancellation the previous day, being unable to rest due to no air conditioning at the hotel and changed circadian rhythm.
summary: A crew member reported fatigue after a mechanical return to the gate prevented rest due to a hotel room with only heating available. The pilot contacted the Crew Desk at XA15 local and declared unfit for duty after obtaining only one hour of sleep.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experienced a fuel pump failure thereby degrading fuel transfer between wing tanks. Communication with company resources to determine legality to continue flight were difficult because of the distance from land based transmitter. Crew would have liked to have had satellite phone capabilities.
summary: The flight crew encountered a fuel pump failure and imbalance during initial climb, delaying ETOPS entry decisions due to poor HF radio communications. The reporter attributes the resulting miscommunication and operational delays solely to the aircraft's lack of SATCOM equipment.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff due to an engine over temperature.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff shortly after the 100-knot call due to observed debris and a left engine over-temperature warning. The aircraft taxied back to the gate for maintenance inspection, which cleared it for flight after brake temperatures cooled.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer described a fatiguing trip and mistakes that he made, necessitating a fatigue call.
summary: A fatigued First Officer, suffering from poor sleep and a delayed duty day, made multiple communication and FMC errors during the approach to LAX. The Captain intervened to correct the mistakes, and the First Officer removed himself from flight status upon blocking in.

synopsis: B737 crew reported a tail strike due to a bounced landing during touchdown.
summary: The Captain landed the aircraft in IMC conditions, executing a firm touchdown and bounce after lowering the nose to avoid landing long. This resulted in a tail strike and a flight attendant suffering a neck strain due to the hard landing.

synopsis: A B777 equipment cooling fan and associated wiring caught fire and subsequently burned through the forward cargo sidewall and insulation into the cargo compartment. The flight crew and local maintenance technicians refused to release the aircraft for a night ETOPS flight over several managers' objections.
summary: The flight crew refused to accept an aircraft parked at the gate after a maintenance technician reported an equipment cooling fan fire in the forward cargo bin that caused charred wiring and a hole in the insulation. Despite pressure from Maintenance Control to operate under the MEL, the pilots cancelled the flight due to safety concerns regarding the fire damage and lack of parts for an ETOPS night flight.

synopsis: Three airline ticket agents contend that the redesign of the baggage scales to near floor level causes a personal safety issue for the agents if passengers chose to walk behind the counter. The additional distance that bags need to be lifted to the bag belt is also causing back strain.
summary: Ticket counter agents reported daily back, neck, and eye strain, plus four injuries, caused by a lobby remodel featuring trip-hazard scales, high bag belts, distant monitors, and insufficient customer dividers. The design forces staff to lift heavy bags alone while facing security risks from passengers reaching over counters or standing too close.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew experienced increasing airspeed while descending on the VEPLI1 RNAV arrival to WSSS. Speed intervene had no apparent effect, but the autopilot was not disengaged until the overspeed warning sounded ultimately being exceeded by 15 knots before slowing.
summary: During a VEPLI1B RNAV arrival into WSSS, the crew experienced an inadvertent overspeed to 340 KTS while descending in VNAV. The aircraft failed to respond to speed interventions, requiring autopilot disengagement to level off at FL250 before continuing to the cleared FL240.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a TCAS RA on final into CLT. Pilot responded to the RA by climbing 100 feet. The resolution cleared and the aircraft landed on the assigned runway. Traffic was for a parallel runway.
summary: The flight crew received a TCAS climb resolution advisory while being vectored for ILS 18L at 3,000 feet due to traffic 300 feet below. After climbing 100 feet to clear the conflict, they descended back to 3,000 feet and continued the approach after notifying ATC.

synopsis: An air carrier crew climbing on the FLL ARKES 4 RNAV SID took evasive action from an unreported single engine aircraft at 8,500 following a TCAS TA which then quickly became a TCAS RA.
summary: The crew of an aircraft on the ARKES 4 departure received a TCAS RA while climbing to 16,000 feet after being switched to MIA Center. The conflict with an unreported single-engine VFR aircraft 1,000 feet above was caused by the lack of traffic information from Departure, requiring an immediate level-off to avoid a collision.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant and Captain reported a loose galley cart after takeoff that injured passengers and one Flight Attendant. The cart may not have been properly secured and fatigue was possibly a factor.
summary: A forward beverage cart came loose after takeoff, injuring seven passengers and the C Flight Attendant due to a broken or unlatched latch. The crew treated injuries onboard, consulted Medlink, and continued to the destination where EMTs met the aircraft.

synopsis: EMB-175 Flight Attendant reported being reprimanded by a Station Manager for holding up the boarding process to attend to first class passengers.
summary: A flight attendant halted boarding to complete pre-flight safety checks and service first class passengers, but a gate manager boarded and aggressively demanded she stop service to expedite boarding. The manager shouted at the crew member in front of passengers, causing stress and embarrassment, which the reporter attributes to gate personnel overstepping their role and ignoring safety procedures.

synopsis: The pilot of a general aviation aircraft reported a near mid-air collision after ATC issued a turn that the pilot felt exasperated an opposite direction traffic condition.
summary: A pilot approaching PAE received an inappropriate instruction from the tower to turn west while descending through 2400 MSL, causing a near-miss with departing traffic on a converging course. The pilot complied but noted the instruction violated standard right-turn separation procedures, though vertical separation prevented a collision.

synopsis: The pilot of a C210 was alerted to a near-mid-air-collision by the onboard traffic system. ATC was reported to have tried to contact both aircraft, but an unknown communication problem existed.
summary: The pilot reported a Traffic Avoidance System alert while cleared direct to the destination at 3,000 feet, identifying traffic 500 feet left and 100 feet higher. The controller stated he attempted to call both pilots, but the reporter did not hear the transmission, likely due to task focus or a communications issue.

synopsis: The pilot of a PA46 landed on a closed runway at a non-towered airport. Although the runway had an 'X' over the runway number, it was reported to have been very difficult to see.
summary: A pilot inadvertently touched down on Runway 35 during short final due to a small, obscured yellow 'X' marking that was difficult to visualize against haze, shadows, and runway numbers. The report notes no accident occurred but recommends larger, more visible closure markings to prevent future occurrences.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A Pilot departed on the CHS PLFMD 1 RNAV and noted Note 1 states 'At or above 560'' while the INITIAL CLIMB instructions state to 560'. Both are minimum constraints climbing to 4,000'.
summary: A pilot reported confusion regarding the PLFMD 1 departure procedure due to conflicting altitude instructions. The narrative states one section directs a turn at 560 feet while another specifies turning above 560 feet.

synopsis: RSW TRACON Controller reported he lost radio contact with a VFR aircraft and observed the aircraft's target merge with another aircraft target 100 feet apart. The Controller reported facility radios do not provide radio coverage for all of their airspace.
summary: A Radar controller lost two-way radio contact with Aircraft X due to limited frequency coverage, resulting in a 100-foot separation conflict with traffic near an uncontrolled field. The controller attributed the incident to inadequate radio range and criticized Tech Ops for discouraging reports of these coverage gaps.

synopsis: STP Tower Controller reported an aircraft landed at the wrong airport and a second aircraft went missed approach. Both aircraft were lined up for the wrong airport. Pilot that landed on the wrong airport also reported the event.
summary: An IFR pilot vectored by Center to SGS mistakenly landed at STP, while a second VFR aircraft also arrived at STP thinking it was SGS. The controller identified the error after landing, coordinated with both pilots to return to SGS, and noted that Center failed to distinguish the airports during vectoring.

synopsis: D10 TRACON Controller and three pilots involved in an airborne conflict between a B767 departing DFW and a B737 departing DAL reported their actions during the encounter. Reportedly the TCAS commanded an increased climb rate then reversed to a descent.
summary: An ATC controller and B767 crew reported a near-miss with a B737 during departure due to conflicting climb instructions and controller tunnel vision. The B767 crew executed TCAS RAs while the B737 turned left, resulting in a final separation of 0.5 miles laterally and 100 feet vertically.

synopsis: D21 TRACON and DTW Tower Controllers reported a loss of separation due to different climb rates on two departures.
summary: A West Jet Departure controller observed Aircraft Y rapidly closing on Aircraft X after both departed DTW on a 040-degree heading. The controller attributed the loss of separation and wake turbulence risk to Aircraft X's slow climb gradient and the Tower's failure to extend the standard two-minute wake separation interval for heavy long-haul aircraft.

synopsis: HCF Controller reported of an emergency inbound and the tower crash phone being out of service. Tower Supervisor called the Ramp Tower as per the SOP and made appropriate notifications. People at the Ramp Tower did not know what they were supposed to do. While aircraft was over the numbers the emergency equipment arrived.
summary: A pilot reported smoke in the cockpit while Aircraft X was returning to HNL, but emergency response was delayed because the tower crash phone was out of service and Ramp Control was unaware of the alternate notification procedures. Although the aircraft landed safely, the incident highlighted a failure to brief controllers on emergency protocols documented only in CEDAR.

synopsis: ZOB Controller reported an Airborne Conflict event contributed to the lack of experience among some of the controllers involved.
summary: An experienced controller relieved an inexperienced team in a saturated AIR/CKB complex where staffing errors and high volume caused EDST failures and a loss of separation at FL270. The reporter attributes the incident to poor supervisor assignments, lack of experienced personnel, and ineffective TMU traffic management.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller and two flight crews describe a serious airborne conflict which developed after an air taxi inexplicably climbed from their assigned FL270 into an air carrier at FL280. The aircraft at their closest were 100 feet vertically and about 1 mile horizontally.
summary: An Air Taxi pilot climbed through their assigned FL270 to FL279, causing a loss of separation with an Air Carrier at FL280. The Air Carrier crew executed a TCAS climb RA while the controller issued a left turn to the Air Taxi, resulting in a closest point of one mile and 100 feet.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The Tower Controller in Charge observed a truck entering a taxiway. The Ground Controller did not see the truck. The CIC reports this portion of the airport is blocked from the view of the Local and Ground controllers.
summary: The Controller In Charge observed a box truck entering a taxiway near a Cessna, noting Ground Control could not see the vehicle due to a blind spot. The reporter states the truck caused no incident but argues the Ground Control position must be moved to fix a long-standing visibility issue that previously blocked views of taxiways and runways.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a drone encounter near OLCYK on the PANGG3 Arrival to MDW.
summary: During the PANGG arrival 2.5 miles east of OLCYK, a drone passed 200 feet above and 500–1000 feet laterally. The crew reported the incident to ATC, Dispatch, and the Chief Pilot without requiring evasive maneuvers.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported he was uncomfortable with the distance to a skydiver aircraft and jumpers on the PINNG1 arrival into PHX.
summary: A Boeing 737 crew on the PINNG1 arrival into PHX encountered a parachute jump aircraft at 1.2 miles and 2,000 feet separation while descending through 14,500 feet. The crew reported the jumpers exited in extremely close proximity to the arrival corridor, creating a hazardous situation despite ATC awareness.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported they deviated from SOP when they pulled and reset a TCAS circuit breaker in flight to restore the system to operation.
summary: The pilot reported cycling a non-tripped TCAS circuit breaker at 10,000 feet during a hold due to opposite traffic, restoring the system but later realizing this violated Aircraft Operation Manual criteria. Maintenance cleared the system upon arrival, and the pilot notified Dispatch and the Chief Pilot regarding the procedural deviation.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported discovering there were two Company flights with the same flight number in the air at the same time.
summary: The Duty Manager allowed two flights with identical flight numbers to launch and operate simultaneously. The crew subsequently corrected one flight number to the intended value, prompting a recommendation for an automation tool to alert managers of such conflicts.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported returning to departure airport following the loss of the pressurization auto mode on the takeoff roll.
summary: The flight crew encountered a pressurization auto fail light during climb and questioned the QRH's instruction to manually operate the outflow valve while alternate mode functioned normally. After consulting maintenance and the chief pilot, they paused the checklist, returned to the departure airport, and executed an overweight landing.

synopsis: Captain reported an NMAC with a light aircraft on approach to AEX.
summary: A new hire First Officer and Captain flying a visual approach to Runway 14 encountered a TCAS Resolution Advisory during a widened base turn. The crew complied with the climb RA, resolving the conflict with a small low-wing aircraft at approximately 3,000 feet before landing safely.

synopsis: EMB-145LR flight crew reported returning to departure airport after losing their pitch trim system.
summary: During climb at 6,000 feet, the crew experienced a pitch trim failure caused by a popped PITCH TRIM 1 breaker and a melted recently replaced switch. They returned to the departure airport, landed safely using QRH procedures without pitch trim, and maintenance later confirmed the issue was a reoccurrence of a patched repair.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported they failed to comply with an MEL restricting the use of the FMS to non-RNAV arrivals.
summary: The Captain and First Officer operated an aircraft with an FMS Navigation database MEL restriction prohibiting RNAV arrivals. The Captain inadvertently accepted an RNAV arrival clearance while distracted, but the MEL was later cleared by maintenance before the next departure.

synopsis: A B747-400 was unable to accept the cleared SID because no SIDs were available in their FMC for the only operational Runway. After hand flying the departure on vectors, the nose gear door did not close so as the First Officer dealt with the gear, the Captain overshot the 5,000 feet level off altitude assignment.
summary: The flight crew departed Runway 23R without a SID due to FMS limitations and experienced a nose gear door fault during climb. The autopilot overshot the cleared FL050 to FL057 because the close proximity of the 4,500-foot transition altitude disrupted automation, requiring manual correction.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported diverting to an alternate following the failure of the #3 hydraulic system.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a HYD 3 LO PRESS caution and diverted after an O-ring failure on pump 3A caused total fluid loss in system 3. The aircraft landed with fire trucks standing by due to lost brakes and required towing because of no nose wheel steering.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported the #2 engine failed during a go-around from an unstabilized approach. Crew reported the aircraft performed poorly in the single-engine climb.
summary: The flight crew initiated a go-around at 30–50 feet due to wind gusts, followed by a loud pop and right roll. They secured the damaged #2 engine, which had seized with significant N2 damage, and landed safely after executing single-engine procedures.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported diverting to a nearby alternate after experiencing a loss of thrust on the left engine at FL380.
summary: The crew experienced a loud rumble and thrust loss from the left engine at FL380, causing yaw and vibration. They diverted to the nearest airport, landed safely on one engine, and ground inspection revealed no visible damage to the left engine.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported executing a go-around after responding to an RA on the DEN ILS Runway 35R.
summary: The flight crew executing a Cat 3 ILS approach to Denver 35R received a TCAS descent resolution advisory while below the glide path. The pilot flying initiated a go-around to resolve the conflict, after which ATC cleared them to maintain 9000 feet for a successful second approach.

synopsis: Medium transport flight crew reported that a special company EAT departure procedure conflicts with ATC expectations.
summary: The crew departed EAT Runway 30 under a VFR climb to fly a company engine-inoperative turn procedure after the controller refused to approve or deny the request. ATC later instructed them to follow the published Obstacle Departure Procedure, causing a disconnect due to unclear restrictions on the abnormal departure method.

synopsis: First Officer reported he was concerned with an ATC procedure at HNL that he felt could lead to an unsafe conflict if a go-around was required.
summary: The pilot reported a potential conflict while landing on runway 8L at HNL when another aircraft crossed the approach at 500 feet above. The pilot attributed the risk to ATC sequencing errors that placed both aircraft near the threshold simultaneously, creating a hazard if a go-around had been required.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported confusion in the cockpit resulted when Houston Center and TRACON changed their arrival assignment multiple times.
summary: The flight crew experienced confusion during the IAH arrival due to frequent changes between SKNRD4, ZEEKK1, and DOOBI2 arrivals. The pilot attributed this to potential communication breakdowns between Houston Center and Approach, though no separation issues occurred.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A319 flight crew reported they were confused when MZBZ ATC assigned an approach that was not in their EFB.
summary: The flight crew and approach controller experienced confusion during arrival at Belize due to radar outages and a language barrier. The controller issued a VOR/ILS/DME Runway 07 clearance not available in the crew's Jeppesen FD-Pro, forcing a VFR resolution to complete a safe landing.

synopsis: The pilot of a PC-12 reported a malfunction of the engine torque indication that resulted in a diversion to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise, erratic engine torque indications triggered CAS messages, prompting the crew to consult the QRH and divert to the nearest airport. The unreliable torque display persisted through descent and landing, resulting in a White Engine Exceedance CAS message after touchdown.

synopsis: The Captain of a CRJ200 reported missing the notes on an electronic chart that made the clearance in conflict with the aircraft MEL restrictions.
summary: Pilots flew an aircraft with four MELs, including inoperative GPS and GPWS, and inadvertently accepted an RNAV1 arrival clearance not authorized by the MELs. They attributed the error to missing chart notes on zoomed electronic charts and acknowledged a need for greater proficiency with irregular operations.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Flight Attendant reported the passenger entry door handrail came forward more than it should not allowing the door to close using the normal procedures due to a missing retaining clip.
summary: Cabin crew discovered the entry door handrail was loose due to missing spring bracket clips, preventing door closure and creating a safety hazard. Maintenance confirmed an engineering notice authorized the clip removal, which caused the issue, and recommended reinstalling the clips to stabilize the rail.

synopsis: A SF-340 Flight Attendant preflighting her cabin, closed the LAV Trash Receptacle door and the Halon fire extinguishing agent discharged onto her. She was removed from the trip feeling ill and sweating with a foul taste when swallowing.
summary: A cabin crew member was exposed to Halon fire extinguisher fumes during preflight checks when the unit discharged in the lavatory. The crew member subsequently felt unwell, was deemed unfit to fly, and was removed from the trip.

synopsis: Technician reported an Agusta-A119 helicopter shifted because the tail rotor was not connected correctly while doing ground runs after maintenance was performed.
summary: A mechanic installed a tail rotor control tube and performed a Required Inspection Item, but missed a rigging check step requiring special tools. This oversight caused the aircraft to shift during ground runs, as the static check felt normal despite the improper installation.

synopsis: Contract Technician reported the right Main Landing Gear of a B777 contacted taxiway edge lights and damaged three Main Landing Gear tires during a taxi move.
summary: Two pilots taxiing a B777 between terminals contacted a taxiway edge light with the right main gear, damaging tires #8 and #12. The reporter attributed the incident to reduced situational awareness caused by illness and limited sleep.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot, performing an autorotation reported narrowly missing a C172 as it passed under on short final. It was discovered later that the C172 student pilot was returning from a failed check ride and was not using the correct CTAF nor did he ever see the helicopter.
summary: A helicopter CFI and student on final autorotation to Runway 5 evaded a Cessna 172 that landed underneath them without radio contact. The Cessna student pilot was at fault for monitoring the wrong CTAF frequency and failing to see and avoid the helicopter during the landing phase.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reported increased workload resulted when he was cleared on a different route than filed to CLT perhaps due to an LOA between GSO and CLT TRACONS.
summary: A single-pilot IFR flight from ZZZ to CLT experienced high workload when GSO ATC issued a reroute using VHF descriptors instead of RNAV names, forcing the pilot to manually program the GPS in turbulence and bright sun. The pilot attributed the issue to unpublished LOAs and requested systemic changes to ATC communication and route publication.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 Captain reported being assigned the STYCK2 departure departing IAH including a 5000 foot altitude limit which is not placed in the MCP altitude window. A TCAS alert was generated passing 5,000 feet and ATC was advised, sending the reporter back to 5,000 feet.
summary: The pilot, unfamiliar with the KHOU STYCK3.DOLEY SID, entered 16,000 ft instead of the cleared 5000 ft into the autopilot, triggering a traffic alert in IMC near 5600 ft. The pilot descended to 5000 ft after ATC instruction, attributing the error to high workload and a misleading chart that did not reflect the local altitude restriction.

synopsis: The pilot of a M20 reported becoming distracted by time pressure, an engine indication problem and advanced avionics familiarization, which led to several human errors, culminating in a successful return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot, rushing to pick up a Mooney with new avionics after waiving a test flight, became distracted by equipment and a pegged CHT gauge during departure. This led to getting behind the airplane, an altitude deviation near a commercial flight, and an immediate return to the airport.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 reported a loss of control on landing rollout in windy conditions that led to a runway excursion and contact with a runway edge light.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft on Runway 22 in gusty crosswinds, overcorrected on rollout, and veered off the runway, breaking a window and striking an edge light. The pilot executed a go-around and landed safely on Runway 17, attributing the incident to excessive approach speed and a strong gust during rollout.

synopsis: The pilot of a Maule M5 reported a hard landing that resulted in a subsequent landing gear failure.
summary: Two occupants in a single-engine aircraft experienced a hard landing bounce during a sunset approach, causing right gear damage that led to a collapse and propeller strike on the subsequent rollout. The pilot attributed the initial hard landing to a misjudged sink rate in waning light, resulting in no injuries but structural damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus reported an increase in single pilot IFR workload when ATC attempted to shorten the planned route of flight.
summary: A single-pilot hand-flying an aircraft on the ARSNL4.MRB departure from HEF exceeded 4000 ft to 4600 ft while programming a non-IAF fix into the GPS. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation to excessive workload caused by rapid controller instructions and approach queries during the initial climb.

synopsis: GLF5 Captain reported a very high workload resulted from a late runway change on arrival to LAX.
summary: The pilot reported that while cleared for the RIIVR2 approach to runway 25L, a last-minute change to runway 24R at the RIIVR intersection caused FMS sequencing errors. The crew resolved the issue using step-down fixes but advised against changing runways at the initial fix to allow proper FMS loading.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22T elected to return to the departure airport due to high engine oil temperature.
summary: During a post-annual maintenance IFR test flight, the pilot and an A&P mechanic returned to base after high engine oil temperature warnings reached 245°F. Although no emergency was declared, ATC provided priority vectors for a visual approach to Runway 35 while the shop investigates the cause, noting cylinders 3 and 4 were recently replaced.

synopsis: PA34 pilot, using an Aspen Evolution 1000 and Garmin 530, reported being confused when the autopilot turned the wrong way from what he expected while intercepting the ILS. He disconnected the autopilot and hand flew the approach successfully.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR ILS approach experienced an autopilot deviation when the Aspen Evolution 1000 PFD displayed reverse sensing due to a retained course setting from months prior. The pilot disconnected the autopilot, hand-flew the approach using a backup ILS, and landed safely, attributing the incident to a logic flaw in the display's course selection.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Two separate pilots reported communication issues with ATC while attempting to cancel IFR flight plans during approach to C09.
summary: The pilot attempted to cancel an IFR flight plan on final approach at 1,500 MSL but failed due to poor reception on 119.35 and an incorrect TRACON cell number. The flight plan remained open until the airport manager notified the pilot the following day, highlighting the risks of uncancelled approaches.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Taxi Captain reported an unsafe gear indication when the gear was selected down for landing. The QRH procedure was complied with but only the right main and nose gear were successfully extended. A landing with the left main gear retracted was then accomplished and the crew exited the aircraft.
summary: The crew experienced a landing gear malfunction on arrival at ZZZ, where only the right main and nose gear extended after executing the QRH procedure. With low fuel, they performed a low pass for visual confirmation and executed a successful single-gear landing on runway XXL, exiting the aircraft safely with no fire.

synopsis: The pilot of a C207 reported a runway excursion while landing in crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that upon touchdown in 10-15 knot winds with a 40-degree left crosswind, the aircraft veered left despite full right brake and rudder application, causing it to exit the runway.

synopsis: A Diamond DA-40-180 pilot reported that while flying whenever they transmitted on frequency 133.600 MGhz (Atlanta Center) the Emergency Locator Transmitter would start going off blocking all frequencies.
summary: During an IFR flight, transmitting on 133.600 MHz triggered the ELT, blocking all radio communications and forcing the crew to squawk 7600. Maintenance attributed the issue to rare frequency interference, which resolved after transferring to a different approach controller.

synopsis: It was reported that a Sikorsky S76B Helicopter had evidence of severe skin corrosion where a lap joint had separated and rivets popped. This area was covered with 'Bondo', painted and the aircraft was put back into service.
summary: Management pressured the Director of Maintenance to return a Sikorsky S76B to charter service with severe skin corrosion and separated lap joints after halting its 100-hour inspection. A non-licensed technician painted over the damage with Rustoleum, violating repair manuals and returning the aircraft to flight crews without proper repairs or documentation.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Flight Crew reporting departing DAL with a clearance to level at 5000 feet and was instructed to continue climbing to 17000 feet but the MCP altitude window was not adjusted and the aircraft leveled off. The clearance was reissued and the crew started to climb but not in time to avoid a loss of separation with a Regional Jet departing DFW.
summary: Aircraft X crew leveled at 5,000 feet instead of climbing to 17,000 feet due to distraction from flap retraction and poor intercom communication, causing a 1.66-mile proximity with a Regional Jet. The crew subsequently received a Traffic Advisory, disconnected the autopilot, and initiated an aggressive climb to resolve the conflict.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZTL Controller reported of holding aircraft for CLT due to thunderstorms. One aircraft was assigned holding instructions but kept on busting altitude. Controller moved aircraft away from other traffic and then the aircraft did not fly as instructed.
summary: A CLT controller vectored Aircraft X away from a congested holding pattern after the pilot failed to maintain assigned altitude and heading. The aircraft subsequently turned south into CLT airspace, requiring further vectoring, while coordination with the adjacent sector was likely delayed due to frequency congestion.

synopsis: ZOA Controller reported seeing a confusing data block. Controller checked with pilot and then called transferring Controller to verify what had been done. Reporter then discussed the actions with the transferring Controller.
summary: An air traffic controller in Area North observed Aircraft X level at FL350 despite a data block showing a climb to FL370, suspecting a handoff error from Sector 32. The controller cleared the aircraft to FL370 and attributed the incident to Sector 32 failing to hand off the aircraft at its assigned altitude, creating a potential conflict risk.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A Center Controller received a handoff on an aircraft at an altitude not in compliance with the facility SOP manual.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X descended to Flight Level 310 instead of the assigned Flight Level 240 while being vectored near the sector boundary. The controller attributed the altitude deviation to the pilot's non-compliance and the previous sector's failure to follow facility standard operating procedures.

synopsis: Flight crew reported they failed to follow SOP after receiving a GPWS obstacle caution while on approach to DAL.
summary: The First Officer flying a night visual approach to Runway 31L at DAL received a GPWS "too low obstacle" caution at 2,200 feet and initiated a go-around. Although the warning ceased upon climbing, the crew incorrectly elected to continue the approach instead of completing the go-around as required.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer as the Pilot Monitoring noted that the aircraft had reverted from VNAV PATH to VNAV SPEED while descending to make a crossing restriction. The Captain attempted to use vertical speed and the speed brake to make the restriction with the autopilot engaged, but Altitude Acquire occurs a 1,000 feet above and the fix is crossed 400 feet high.
summary: The crew descended from 39,000 feet to cross OHHMY at 31,000 feet but remained high after the autopilot reverted to VNAV SPEED and entered ALT ACQ. The Pilot Flying delayed increasing the descent rate, resulting in a 400-foot altitude deviation above the restriction.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported diverting to the nearest suitable airport after the left engine failed shortly after takeoff.
summary: The pilot flying reported a number one engine failure shortly after takeoff, causing severe left yaw and wind-milling at 7% N1. The crew executed severe engine damage procedures, diverted to a suitable airport, and landed safely with no fire or hot spots found on the engine.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a rejected takeoff in ABQ at 110 KTS in response to a takeoff configuration warning light for an unknown reason.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff at 110 knots on Runway 21 in ABQ after the Takeoff Configuration Warning horn sounded with flaps 1 and speedbrakes down. A 75-minute brake cooling delay and mechanic inspection followed, though the crew noted resistance from Maintenance Control to investigate the warning's cause.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported deviating from the cleared RNAV arrival altitude constraints when the FMS dropped out of VNAV.
summary: During a descent on the DANDD Arrival into DEN, the crew descended below the assigned 17,000 ft to nearly 16,000 ft after the autopilot unexpectedly reverted from VNAV to CWS P. The pilots manually recovered the altitude before crossing DANDD, attributing the event to unreliable software and a lack of aural warnings for mode changes.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the Captain chose to reject the takeoff at approximately 110 kts when a door warning light was illuminated.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff at 121 kts after a Master Caution and FWD ENTRY door light illuminated, influenced by a past cargo door incident. Maintenance later confirmed the door handle was not fully down, requiring a 70-minute brake cooling delay before the flight continued.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported he had to use paper charts because his iPad started an update on its own at the gate before departure, failed to finish, and was therefore unusable during the flight.
summary: During pre-departure briefing, an automatic update to the iPad Flight Deck Pro app rendered it unusable before the download completed. The pilot was forced to use paper charts for the flight.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported the flight attendants used the onboard emergency medical kit and a passenger who was an RN to treat a passenger who was having an allergic reaction. Captain also stated the RN reported the quality of the kit was questionable and that flight attendant familiarity with the kit was lacking.
summary: During a B767-300 flight, a passenger suffered an allergic reaction, prompting the crew to administer medication and land safely with EMTs on standby. Post-flight, a registered nurse reported that the EEMK stethoscope was broken, the blood pressure cuff was out of calibration, and flight attendants lacked familiarity with the emergency equipment.

synopsis: B737-900ER flight crew reported experiencing a tail strike on landing after a normal, stable approach.
summary: The pilot of a 737-900ER reported that after a normal landing, the nose rose while engaging reverse thrust, causing the tail to scrape the runway. The pilot attributed the tail strike to insufficient forward pressure on the control column to counter the increasing pitch attitude.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported they failed to follow SOP after receiving a takeoff warning horn on initial throttle application. A late runway change and new performance data procedures were cited as contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew experienced a flap configuration warning during takeoff on runway 25L after misreading the flap indicator following a last-minute runway change. The pilot attributed the error to high stress from the new performance procedure and the busy airport environment, noting they should have rejected the takeoff instead of correcting the flaps in flight.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported experiencing a lightning strike while deviating around thunderstorms.
summary: The CRJ-900 flight crew encountered unforecast severe turbulence and a possible lightning strike while descending through 20,000 feet MSL near Little Rock. The event caused minor injuries to a flight attendant, leading the crew to log the incident and ferry the aircraft for inspection.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reported returning to departure airport and evacuating the aircraft after experiencing smoke in the cabin. They were advised after landing the smoke was probably due to over-servicing the oil.
summary: The pilot reported smoke and an activated lav detector, prompting a return to the departure airport for a visual approach and landing. Passengers were evacuated after parking, and mechanics attributed the smoke to the aircraft being over-serviced with oil the previous night.

synopsis: While at flight level 240 the crew of an Embraer EMB145LR became aware of smoke in the cabin.
summary: The flight crew experienced smoke in the cockpit and cabin at FL240, prompting an emergency descent and oxygen mask use. The smoke cleared during descent, but a PACK 2 overheat warning occurred after landing, leading the crew to speculate a PACK issue caused the incident.

synopsis: EMB-145LR Captain reported his aircraft rolled 50 degrees after encountering wake turbulence in trail of an A380.
summary: During arrival at IAH, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding A380 despite ATC warnings, causing a 50-degree roll, autopilot disengagement, and altitude loss. The First Officer recovered control, and the flight landed uneventfully after requesting vectors off the airway.

synopsis: EMB-145XR flight crew reported they were advised by ATC of non-compliance with a speed restriction on the GUSHR3 arrival into IAH. The flight crew was confused about the advisory, since they were not on the published arrival, but were cleared direct to a point on the arrival.
summary: The flight crew received a direct clearance to REFYN on the GUSHR3 arrival and debated whether the 280 KIAS restriction applied while off the published route. They slowed to 280 KTS by REFYN and landed safely, but remain unclear if such speed notes apply to aircraft vectored off the published arrival path.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported losing communication and operational control of one of his flights because of a software glitch.
summary: The pilot reported that a flight operated late from the prior day with a new flight number caused ACARS communication failure, likely due to flight planning software conflicts. The crew reverted to alternate radio, warning that dispatchers unaware of this glitch might lose operational control.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported noticing that hydraulic system #2 was losing quantity. Flight continued to destination and landed with quantity at 56%.
summary: The Captain and First Officer observed a gradual drop in Hydraulic System 2 quantity and Emergency Accumulator pressure during cruise and descent. They monitored the leak, reviewed the QRH for total system loss, and landed safely without incident.

synopsis: CE-560XL First Officer reported several instances of pressure from his company to ignore maintenance items during preflight, including corrosion issues.
summary: Pilots conducting preflight inspections on two Citation Excel aircraft found extensive corrosion, a faulty seat, damaged grommets, and an APU fluid leak. They reported that maintenance personnel responded with hostility and intimidation when the crew documented these discrepancies, raising concerns about a deteriorating safety culture and inadequate corrosion prevention.

synopsis: HS-125 Captain reported experiencing an extended period of no communications with ATC. Reporter cited chronic fatigue as a contributing factor.
summary: A fatigued flight crew lost radio contact at FL390 due to task fixation on arrival planning and chronic fatigue from a demanding schedule. The pilot removed himself from duty after landing, attributing the communication blackout to exhaustion and a potential call sign confusion.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported the aircraft climbed prematurely from an altitude constraint on the EEONS5 SID, presumably to assure the next restriction was met.
summary: During departure from Denver on an Airbus, the aircraft automatically climbed above the 12,000 ft SHOBO restriction to satisfy a future 14,000 ft LUPTN constraint. The crew manually descended to correct the deviation, attributing the event to the flight management system prioritizing downstream constraints over immediate crossing restrictions.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported a track deviation resulted when they mis-programmed the FMS following a revised route clearance they received on the runway just before takeoff.
summary: Pilots received a reroute clearance while holding on the runway due to weather, leading to an initial navigation error after takeoff. The crew corrected the course, attributing the deviation to the pressure of the long runway hold and a lack of proactive routing from dispatch.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported the loss of the First Officer's roll command on the flight director during an approach. Later they discovered that they had failed to note equipment limitations during the preflight MEL review.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed LGA one hour late after resolving new maintenance discrepancies, which distracted them from reviewing an active MEL item for the First Officer's inoperative radio altimeter. This oversight caused the First Officer's flight director roll command to disappear during the ILS approach, though the crew completed a visual landing safely.

synopsis: Captain of air carrier extended the roll out on landing due to traffic of the exit taxiway. This necessitated a go-around by another approaching airplane.
summary: The pilot continued to turnoff BB because a stationary aircraft on turnoff AA blocked the runway exit. The tower issued a late clearance to follow the stationary aircraft, forcing the pilot to expedite to BB and causing a landing aircraft behind to go around.

synopsis: A B737 had a ground interrupt due to the exterior 1L door handle reported as being extended. Aircraft returned to the gate and Maintenance was called.
summary: A gate agent reported an extended exterior 1L door handle on Aircraft X, but ramp control instructed her to ignore it and proceed with push-out to ensure a timely departure. The crew chief and mechanic later discovered ramp control had been meddling with the aircraft instead of addressing the safety concern.

synopsis: Concerned San Diego citizen wondered why an aircraft flew an abnormal path over Point Loma.
summary: A resident reported that a large aircraft departing San Diego deviated from its filed flight plan over the Point Loma peninsula without weather justification. The reporter requested an explanation for the route change and noted no involvement from local airport authority or the FAA in the incident.

synopsis: A pilot received confusing instructions from the Center controller. The pilots delayed complying with the instruction until they were able to verify the instruction with the Controller.
summary: Pilots at 27,000 feet hesitated to climb after a controller issued a confusing correction for a different aircraft, delaying their ascent to Flight Level 290. The reporter attributed the confusion to missing "Break" phraseology but confirmed no separation issues occurred and the climb was completed within the required time.

synopsis: The cabin depressurized in a Mitsubishi MU-2B-60 in cruise due to a cracked window.
summary: The pilot reported a loud crack and cabin depressurization at FL230 caused by a cracked left forward window. The crew initiated an emergency descent, squawked 7700, and diverted to ZZZ after stabilizing the aircraft.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reported executing a go-around after losing communication and navigation radios on approach. During the go-around, there were track and altitude deviations.
summary: During an IFR approach, a crew experienced dual radio and GN530W navigation failures caused by a chattering 30-year-old relay. Distracted by system resets, they inadvertently climbed to 6,000 feet before establishing contact, landing, and receiving a reprimand for not executing the published missed approach.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported engine failure shortly after takeoff.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot experienced a sudden engine power loss to idle and cockpit light flickering below 200 feet. The pilot extended gear and flaps, then landed safely on grass beyond the runway end with no damage or injuries.

synopsis: PA-25 pilot towing a glider on takeoff maneuvered to avoid opposite direction traffic that had not checked in on the common frequency.
summary: A pilot towing a heavy two-place glider on runway 30 encountered a Cessna taxiing toward the intersection after landing on runway 34. The Cessna pilot was on the wrong frequency (122.9 instead of 123.00) and failed to stop, forcing the tow pilot to sidestep north and release the glider to avoid a collision.

synopsis: C182 pilot on a VFR flight plan at 17,500 feet reported encountering cloud tops above his altitude and a solid under cast below. A request for climb into Class A is granted until the cloud tops are passed. Onboard weather using Foreflight, including SIGMETS and weather radar was in use.
summary: A VFR pilot flying at 17,500 ft inadvertently entered Class A airspace near Washington while climbing to 19,500 ft to avoid building cloud tops. The controller vectored the aircraft 340 degrees out of the airspace, allowing the pilot to continue to destination and land safely.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ERI TRACON Controller reported a bad radio transmitter and receiver which limits the amount of traffic allowed into and out of JHW airport.
summary: An air traffic controller at JHW lost communication with departing and arriving aircraft due to a failed 126.05 MHz ground transmitter. This outage caused significant delays and forced the controller to issue approach clearances and hold instructions via landline while unable to monitor non-radar traffic below 4,000 feet.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on the HYDRR1 Arrival into PHX.
summary: During the HYDRR arrival, the pilot encountered moderate wake turbulence roll and yaw due to tailwinds and close proximity to a preceding aircraft. Radio congestion delayed a request to deviate 10 degrees from the corridor until clearance was received to return to course.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported a track deviation resulted when there was confusion regarding a clearance received via CPDLC.
summary: The First Officer accepted a revised CPDLC departure clearance without consulting the Captain, resulting in an incorrect route and conflicting instructions from Clearance Delivery and Departure Control. The crew later agreed they should have rejected the clearance and clarified the route before acceptance.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported taxiing to the wrong de-ice pad at DEN because of workload and distraction issues.
summary: The Captain reported that an inattentive First Officer failed to assist during taxi, leading the Captain to taxi solo and mistakenly turn left into the wrong deice pad due to expectation bias. The Captain corrected the error after being alerted by ramp personnel, noting this was the seventh such incident that day.

synopsis: A maintenance technician reported that after removing the tail stand it was observed the Teflon tip remained attached to the aircraft.
summary: During tail stand removal training, a mechanic observed the Teflon tip detach and remain affixed to the aircraft. The reporter expressed concern that if this tip is not removed before flight, it could cause fuselage damage, create runway FOD, or result in an FAA violation.

synopsis: The procedure(s) as to where to position a ground air start unit on an Embraer 170 are not defined clearly. The procedures which engine to start first is also not defined.
summary: A Ramp Service Employee reported that on an E170, the crew connected an air start to the right side while the pilot started engine #2, forcing the agent near the running engine. The reporter noted no manual guidance on positioning or start sequence, suggesting a communication failure or lack of visual confirmation by the flight crew.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier regional jet Captain reported receiving a GPWS Terrain warning during a night visual approach to CRW.
summary: The flight crew accepted a "close in" visual approach clearance at dusk to an unfamiliar airport, triggering a terrain warning during the base leg. The crew executed a go-around, attributing the unwanted aircraft state to accepting a challenging clearance that compromised terrain clearance.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported exceeding maximum speed following a high workload approach and go-around.
summary: The flight crew flying a KLNDR arrival to DFW experienced multiple ATC vectors and an autothrottle malfunction that caused an overspeed in full flaps. The pilots manually managed thrust and flap configuration to recover speed and safely complete the approach.

synopsis: First Officer reported a track deviation on approach to MSLP, citing crew unfamiliarity with the airport and poor ATC communication as factors.
