summary: During an ILS final approach, the crew executed a go-around after tower reported FOD in the touchdown zone. Excessive nose-up trim delayed autopilot engagement, causing the aircraft to climb to 3,500 feet before receiving VFR downwind clearance, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Flight crew misunderstood ATC routing and altitude clearance for the expected approach procedure. ATC alerted the crew to the fact that they had descended below minimum vectoring altitude. The crew regained the assigned altitude and completed the approach and landing uneventfully.
summary: The pilot and First Officer descended below the 7000-foot minimum vectoring altitude while approaching PSP, misinterpreting a clearance to descend for the RNAV Visual as an immediate approach clearance. Air Traffic Control issued a low altitude alert, prompting a climb to 7000 feet before re-clearing the approach, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A Boeing 737 Captain reported that a published RNAV approach to MGGT airport resulted in a glideslope indication that appeared to be lower than normal. The crew transitioned to a visual glideslope reference and landed uneventfully.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 737 on final approach to MGGT Runway 20 abandoned the RNAV (RNP) glide path after indications placed the aircraft below the PAPI and normal angle. They disregarded the flight director to establish a safe descent, noting the procedure requires flight testing to confirm safety parameters.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a Regional Jet taxied in front of him abruptly, almost causing a collision.
summary: The pilot of an aircraft on taxiway M6 reported that a Regional Jet cut between their aircraft and an MD-80 while crossing runway 17R. The pilot applied brakes to avoid a collision, attributing the incident to the Regional Jet pilot's unsafe maneuvering.

synopsis: Bowers Fly Baby pilot reported losing directional control on landing roll, resulting in a ground loop and a scraped wingtip.
summary: The pilot of a Bower's Fly Baby experienced a ground loop during the landing roll on runway 11 after attempting to correct a left drift with right rudder and brake. The resulting left wingtip scrape caused an engine stall, requiring a pushback to the ramp with only minor damage reported.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported a King Air at SDL entered the runway and began their takeoff roll with no communication while they were on short final.
summary: A pilot and student conducting a night training flight at SDL executed a go-around when a King Air entered RWY 21 without radio contact or holding short. The reporter attributed the near-miss to the King Air's failure to communicate and the unavailability of SDL Tower during the incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA controllers reported believing they had handed off an aircraft to the adjacent ARTCC, but the handoff had not been completed. The adjacent Center Controller had to restrict the aircraft's climb for opposite direction traffic.
summary: A pilot training a developmental controller and an inexperienced radar controller failed to properly hand off Aircraft X, leaving the data block under their control while Sector 33 and ZLC 44 assumed responsibility. This communication breakdown caused a conflict alert with a LAS arrival, requiring ZLC 44 to intervene and stop the climb due to unverified handoffs and assumptions.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: RSW Tower Controller in Charge (CIC) reported the TRACON CIC did not follow published procedures concerning changing active runways.
summary: Local Control and TRON CICs failed to coordinate a runway change from 24 to 6, leaving the Local CIC unaware of the switch while aircraft were vectored for Runway 6. The TRON CIC neglected the required checklist, creating an unsafe situation where a departure could have been launched on the wrong runway.

synopsis: ORD Tower Controller reported clearing an aircraft for takeoff. Pilot reported they had 'red lights on the runway'. Controller advised pilot to hold position and observed an automobile on the runway. After vehicle was cleared aircraft was given takeoff clearance again. Controller liked the fact that the Runway Safety Lights Worked.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway 28R, but the pilot reported red Runway Safety Lights (RWSL). The controller identified an unidentified vehicle crossing at Taxiway F, held the aircraft, and re-cleared it after the conflict was resolved.

synopsis: MYF Local Controller Instructor reported of a runway incursion and ground conflict because of an aircraft that crossed halfway onto the runway while a departure aircraft was told to stop twice. The crossing aircraft read back hold short instructions.
summary: During local training, an OJTI intervened after a student controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was crossing Runway 28L following an incomplete hold short readback. The OJTI canceled the takeoff clearance twice, preventing a runway incursion as Aircraft X crossed the runway and received a Brasher warning.

synopsis: A90 TRACON Controller reported a B737-900 flight crew executed a missed approach while complying with a published charted visual. The aircraft was reportedly to high on approach. This type of occurrence is allegedly common to newer airframe aircraft according to the Controller. The descent rate is slower.
summary: A B737-900 executing a visual approach to RWY 33L went missed approach after climbing and veering off course near LYHTT. The controller attributed the event to the approach's flyability and the aircraft's difficulty in descending and slowing at high efficiency.

synopsis: A90 TRACON Controller reported an aircraft conducting a published charted visual approach descended below the minimums and executed a missed approach.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X for a Light Visual Approach to runway 33L at BOS, where the pilot descended rapidly from 1800 to 1000 feet despite low altitude alerts. The controller attributed the incident to the approach's inherent complexity and safety risks, though the aircraft eventually landed without incident after being vectored for a straight-in approach.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew flying the LGA Runway 31 LOC Approach reported the aircraft descended below the calculated glide path to arrive at the derived decision altitude (DDA) prior to where the correct glide path would have placed the aircraft. The flight crew received an EGPWS 'Caution, Obstacle' alert, leveled the aircraft, and proceeded to land uneventfully.
summary: The Captain flew a LOC 31 approach to LGA and descended below the 650-foot DDA due to unadjusted vertical speed in headwinds, triggering an obstacle caution. The crew manually corrected the flight path and completed an uneventful landing after receiving clearance.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported they lost the flight directors and autopilot following a static discharge.
summary: The flight crew experienced a lightning strike on climbout, causing a throttle split, radio static, and loss of autopilot, flight director, and FMC data. They manually flew the aircraft to a safe landing after ATC provided vectors, with maintenance later logging the event as a static discharge.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a Learjet flew about 20-30 feet over their aircraft as they crossed the runway with a valid clearance.
summary: A pilot reported a near-midair collision at Hobby Airport while crossing Runway 12L under a combined Ground/Tower frequency. A Learjet descended 20–30 feet above the aircraft due to a runway clearance miscommunication, which the pilot attributed to excessive radio traffic from the single-controller setup.

synopsis: ERJ-190 Captain reported an NMAC with another aircraft in the vicinity of LGA.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS RA at 4,000 ft caused by another aircraft passing 400 ft above instead of the expected 4,500 ft. ATC apologized for failing to inform the crew of the traffic.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported #1 engine fail message appeared after ingesting a Mylar balloon on a taxiway in MMMX.
summary: While parked on taxiway C with one engine running, a Mylar balloon entered the no. 1 engine, causing an engine failure. The crew shut down the affected engine, started the second engine, and taxied to the gate uneventfully.

synopsis: While rotating on takeoff, a B777's number two engine failed. The takeoff continued, flight vectored away from the airport for fuel dumping, checklists completed, and the flight returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.
summary: The crew experienced a right engine failure on takeoff due to an internal mechanical failure, not the initially suspected bird strike. They secured the engine, jettisoned fuel, and returned for a safe landing with no fire damage, though the engine seized and brakes overheated.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported rejecting his takeoff early in the roll when he heard another aircraft cleared for takeoff on the same runway.
summary: The pilot stopped takeoff after Tower cleared a second company aircraft for an intersection departure while the pilot had barely added power. Tower subsequently cancelled the second clearance and confirmed the pilot remained cleared for takeoff, noting the intersection was behind them.

synopsis: CE-750 flight crew reported a loss of cabin pressure when operating with one PACK at FL410.
summary: The crew of a Citation X with a deferred PACK diverted after cabin altitude surged to 9,000 ft at FL410, exceeding MEL limits. They performed a rapid descent to FL380 and landed safely at an alternate, attributing the failure to the aircraft's age and recommending a lower single-PACK altitude limit.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 Captain described a trip during hot weather in aircraft with either the APU or a pack MELed, multiple MELs, ATC reroutes in weather and a return to the departure airport following a lightning strike. The crew ultimately called in fatigued.
summary: A fatigued crew on a multi-day trip with multiple MELs and no APU encountered navigation failures and a lightning strike while avoiding storms, leading to a return to the departure airport. The pilot attributed the safety issues to excessive MELs, poor maintenance practices, and rushed decision-making caused by extreme cockpit heat.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after experiencing an apparent fuel leak.
summary: The flight crew diverted an enroute aircraft to an alternate due to a suspected fuel leak causing a 5,000 lb right-wing imbalance. They executed a smooth overweight landing with Fire/ARFF escort after inspecting the wings and coordinating with dispatch and ATC.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported being dispatched to an airport before the Tower opened with weather near CAT I minima and automated approaches NOTAMed not applicable. After Tower opened, weather improved and the flight landed following the fourth approach. With poor weather, the flight should have been dispatched to arrive after the Tower opened.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a NOTAM prohibiting coupled approaches on a Boeing 757, causing two autopilot-induced go-arounds due to glideslope failures. After switching to hand-flown operations, a third go-around resulted in a flap overspeed from task saturation, but the crew successfully landed on the fourth attempt at CAT I minimums.

synopsis: B737 Captain, on the ILS Runway 07 approach to MROC at 500 feet, reported seeing four white lights on the PAPI and ducks under the glideslope. A GPWS glideslope warning sounds at 300 feet and the reporter corrects back toward the glideslope and landing in the touchdown zone. The fact that the PAPI had been NOTAMed out of service had been forgotten.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a GPWS glide slope warning during a hand-flown ILS approach to RWY 07 at SJO in thunderstorms. The false perception of being high, caused by an out-of-service PAPI and visual illusions, led to an unnecessary descent correction before a normal landing.

synopsis: A Ramp Agent servicing the aircraft's water was distracted with also connecting ground power then failed to disconnect the water hose prior to leaving the aircraft. The water hose and aircraft water hose coupler were damaged.
summary: A ground handler servicing forward potable water on an aircraft with running engines pulled away while still connected, damaging the water cart hose and aircraft coupler. The incident occurred due to distraction from connecting ground power and rushing to service four aircraft within 30 minutes.

synopsis: Q400 First Officer reported operating their aircraft with less than cleared fuel because of a gauge error.
summary: Flight crew and maintenance reported a fuel quantity indication error on the #1 tank during climb and cruise, caused by faulty gauges and refueling panel readings. The aircraft landed safely, but post-flight inspection revealed the crew departed with 900 lbs less fuel than indicated, creating a potential fuel exhaustion risk had delays occurred.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew experienced a lightning strike during descent into ZBAA. No anomalies were noted in flight, but maintenance did find evidence of strike on the right side during post flight inspection.
summary: The crew of an aircraft arriving at ZBAA was struck by lightning while descending in clear air after deviating to avoid weather. Although no system malfunctions occurred and initial inspections found no damage, maintenance later confirmed visible damage on the aircraft's right side.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported another Flight Attendant was injured after the aircraft encountered wake turbulence.
summary: The purser reported that during descent, unreported wake turbulence injured a flight attendant who struck her head and back against door 2R. Paramedics removed the injured crew member in a wheelchair after landing, though the requested inflight supervisor was not present.

synopsis: PA-46 pilot reported losing directional control on landing roll following an apparent main gear tire failure.
summary: The pilot reported a suspected blown right tire at touchdown caused the aircraft to veer right, then left, and depart the runway at a 45-degree angle after braking. The aircraft skidded 75 feet off the runway with substantial right wheel damage and a ground-struck propeller before being towed to a hangar.

synopsis: BE36 instructor and student pilot reported striking the wingtip following a stall during the flare.
summary: A student pilot and instructor practicing power-off spot landings in a turbo-normalized aircraft stalled at five feet due to low airspeed and delayed engine response. The left wingtip tank struck the ground hard, causing damage that grounded the aircraft, though the instructor took control to execute a safe go-around.

synopsis: Challenger 600 flight crew reported experiencing multiple instrument malfunctions which lead to an altitude deviation on climbout. After landing the crew discovered that an access door in front of the First Officer's pitot tube was open and disrupted airflow around the pitot tube.
summary: Two separate incidents occurred: First, a crew experienced air data failures during departure caused by an open nose door disrupting pitot airflow. Second, a newly upgraded Captain inadvertently disconnected pitch trim during climbout, causing a 250-foot altitude deviation until the trim was re-engaged.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported an NMAC on final at MYF.
summary: The pilot on ILS 28R final to MYF reported unable to see traffic on downwind despite tower advisories. The conflicting aircraft appeared below and climbing through the pilot's altitude on short final, prompting the tower to issue a go-around.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported throttle cable issues resulted in a forced landing in a field.
summary: A pilot and photographer flying a Cessna at 700 ft AGL experienced unresponsive throttle controls due to a snapped cable. They executed an immediate landing in a hay field, resulting in no injuries or damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: C180 pilot reported losing directional control after landing resulting in a ground loop.
summary: The pilot landed on runway 25 in crosswind transitioning to a quartering tailwind. Wind pushed the tail right, causing a ground loop that damaged the left wing, elevator, and wheel rim, though no occupants were injured and the aircraft taxied off safely.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported he took off at a non-towered airport on a runway that had a truck parked on it when the truck failed to communicate effectively.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot on takeoff at ZZZ encountered a truck towing a glider that remained on the active runway despite the pilot's radio calls and visual checks. The pilot could not abort safely after lifting off, resulting in a close call while the truck driver later protested over the radio.

synopsis: RV-6A pilot reported becoming alarmed at a banging noise in flight that turned out be a jacket sleeve that was drawn out of the canopy and was striking the fuselage.
summary: A pilot flying at 8,000 ft MSL heard a loud banging noise caused by a passenger's jacket sleeve being pulled through a 1/8-inch canopy gap. The pilot descended to investigate, confirmed no engine failure, and resumed the flight after retrieving the sleeve.

synopsis: Private pilot undergoing training in a new LSA reported a botched landing during which the CFI took control of the aircraft for a go-around. The CFI was unable to maintain control and the right wing tip made contact with the runway then the left before the aircraft nosed over collapsing the nose gear and coming to rest off the runway.
summary: A student pilot and CFI conducting landing training in a new aircraft experienced a hard landing due to gusty quartering winds. The CFI initiated a go-around, but subsequent wingtip contact with the runway caused the aircraft to nose over, breaking the front landing gear and propeller.

synopsis: PHL Local Controller reported a new Letter of Agreement procedure creates an unsafe situation for aircraft taxiing to the ramp.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a Letter of Agreement with ramp control created a safety hazard during high-density operations. Aircraft X ignored ATC taxi instructions to contact ramp control, blocking a runway exit and forcing the controller to divert attention from separating converging aircraft.

synopsis: Controllers had a disagreement over the requirement to hand off a VFR aircraft from a TRACON to an ARTCC.
summary: During OJT, a VFR flight-following aircraft climbed into Center airspace without a handoff due to trainee distraction and conflicting interpretations of 7110.65 regarding VFR coordination. The OJTI cited Chapter 5 requirements, but the aircraft entered the sector before a handoff or climb restriction could be issued, resulting in no loss of separation.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DCA Ground Controller cleared an aircraft to cross a runway that another aircraft was beginning its takeoff roll on.
summary: The controller directed Aircraft X to cross Runway 1 while Aircraft Y was beginning its departure roll. Aircraft X crossed the hold short line, forcing Aircraft Y to abort takeoff after the controller issued a late hold short instruction.

synopsis: ZLC Controller worked an aircraft below the Minimum Enroute Altitude of a low altitude airway.
summary: An air traffic controller accepted a handoff of Aircraft X at 11,000 feet, below the 12,400-foot Minimum Enroute Altitude on V235. The controller climbed the aircraft to 13,000 feet after the previous controller apologized and transferred control.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported returning to departure airport after receiving a GEAR DISAGREE warning light after takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that after takeoff, the left main landing gear failed to retract, triggering a 'GEAR DISAGREE' message. Following checklist procedures and fuel dumping to reduce weight, the crew returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing with emergency vehicles standing by.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported experiencing a NMAC while flying the DARTZ6 departure from DFW.
summary: The flight crew departing DFW 17R on the DARTZ6 RNAV departure received a TCAS TA at 3000 ft from an intruder 300 ft below. ATC issued an immediate left turn to heading 140, resolving the conflict when the aircraft were 100 ft apart, though the crew noted they should have turned sooner.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Tailwheel pilot reported striking runway edge lights on an approach and landing to AAT airport in gusty crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel aircraft with an aft CG attempted a landing at Alturas Airport in 21-knot crosswinds and mechanical turbulence. The pilot lost lateral control during the first touchdown, executed a go-around that struck a runway light with the right main gear, and successfully landed on the second attempt.

synopsis: Beech 36 pilot reported returning to the departure airport after experiencing a loss of AHRS and autopilot.
summary: A pilot and instructor in a G1000-equipped aircraft experienced AHRS and autopilot failure en route, prompting a return to the departure airport. While instructed to remain VFR at 2,500 ft, the pilot inadvertently descended to 1,800 ft due to deteriorating weather and instrument loss, requiring an immediate ATC climb clearance for a conflicting Learjet.

synopsis: A Helicopter Pilot at 1,500 feet reported sighting a large UAV at about 1,300 feet near the VFR Helicopter Throgs Route.
summary: A VFR helicopter pilot on the Throgs Route in LGA Class B airspace reported a four-rotor drone at 1,300 feet passing one mile to the right. The pilot initially mistook the drone for a helicopter or balloons before confirming the sighting with LGA Tower and the opposing helicopter.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot ferrying a light twin to SAF unexpectedly encountered thunderstorms and, while deviating, climbed to 12,500 ft, entered restricted airspace, and inadvertently entered IMC flight.
summary: The PIC and a student co-pilot diverted a twin-engine ferry flight to E14 due to deteriorating weather, fatigue, and suspected hypoxia. The pilot attributed the incident to poor decision-making under stress and accepted remedial training and operational restrictions.

synopsis: On a Dassault Falcon 7X the basic inspection procedures were not being followed per the aircraft maintenance manual.
summary: The chief pilot reported that a Falcon 7X flew a trip after a required Basic inspection was missed during an A inspection at a manufacturer service center. The error occurred due to the service center overlooking a manual caveat and the pilot's lack of maintenance expertise and failure to verify sign-offs before release.

synopsis: ZID Controller reported having to plug in with an unfamiliar Developmental during a checkride on a position the Supervisor was not checked out on. An airspace violation ensued when a handoff was not accepted until a phone call was made with the aircraft in the other sector's airspace.
summary: An OJTI monitored a developmental controller during a certification check ride in a busy sector while a supervisor observed. The OJTI assisted the developmental with traffic conflicts and a delayed handoff to Sector 66, attributing the stress to the supervisor's lack of position certification, background drilling noise, and the OJTI's inability to access equipment.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after losing part of the right engine cowling on takeoff.
summary: During climb after takeoff, a flight attendant reported a passenger saw debris from the right side, later confirmed as missing inboard right engine cowling. The crew returned to the departure airport, where ATC confirmed the cowling was found on the runway, and the aircraft landed safely with no further incident.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported being unable to comply with taxi instructions at Rio De Janeiro Airport (SBGL) because the airport taxiway depiction, provided on the current Jeppesen charts, did not agree with the actual signage on the field. A 'follow me' vehicle was required to assist the crew with the taxi clearance.
summary: The flight crew experienced conflicting taxi instructions and unmarked taxiways at Rio de Janeiro (SBGL) due to discrepancies between Jeppesen charts 10-9 and 10-9B and ground control. A Follow-Me vehicle was required to guide the aircraft out after the crew stopped to verify the correct exit.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an autopilot and glideslope anomaly during a visual approach to Runway 28 at SYR. This resulted in a descent well below the glideslope just inside the FAF. The autopilot was disengaged and the aircraft was returned to the now stable glideslope and a normal landing ensued.
summary: During a visual approach to runway 28, the autopilot failed to capture the glide slope at the FAF, causing an altitude deviation and triggering GPWS obstacle warnings. The First Officer disconnected the autopilot to level the aircraft, attributing the incident to autopilot failure, delayed disconnection, and fatigue.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported a traffic conflict that initially resulted in less than optimum guidance from the TCAS system presumably due to the fact the other aircraft was not TCAS equipped.
summary: During climb from ZZZ, haze prevented visual contact with a non-TCAS Cessna, triggering a TCAS RA to climb then descend. The crew followed the RA, established visual contact, and resumed climb, attributing the initial conflicting resolution to the other aircraft's lack of TCAS equipment.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew encountered insufficient lighting at SFB for taxi to the ramp area while the Tower was closed. The NOTAM did not sufficiently describe the issues with the field lighting.
summary: The pilot reported that while runway edge lights appeared dim and taxiway edge lights were inoperative during arrival at Sanford, the approach and landing were completed normally in clear weather. The reporter attributed the lighting issues to a potentially unclear NOTAM regarding the Pilot Control feature and requested clarification on which specific lighting systems were out of service.

synopsis: SR22 pilot was advised by customs personnel in HPN that he had not followed proper procedures in his flight to the U.S. from Canada.
summary: The Pilot-in-Command of a Part 91 flight from Canada to KHPN received a verbal warning from US Customs for failing to obtain specific entry permission despite filing eAPIS and IFR clearances. The violation occurred because the pilot misunderstood an email confirmation and did not directly coordinate with the port of entry as required.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported taxiing into another aircraft following brake failure.
summary: During a taxi test, the pilot lost brakes while returning to the ramp and collided with another aircraft. The incident caused minimal damage to the other aircraft and broke the pilot's left wing taxi light.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported possible flight below 1000 ft AGL in residential area of rising terrain north of ONT.
summary: A pilot departing RIR north of ONT Class C airspace turned west at 2,000 ft MSL and potentially flew less than 1,000 ft AGL over rising terrain due to failing to note nearby residences. The pilot attributed the incident to inadequate flight plan review in familiar airspace.

synopsis: Glider pilot reported an airborne conflict, and questioned the practice of C-17 aircraft flying through the glider release area east of EPH at 4,000 feet.
summary: A glider pilot reported a C-17 flying through a known high glider traffic area at the pilot's altitude, passing less than a mile away. The pilot attributes the unsafe proximity to repeated low-level military missions crossing this active VFR zone.

synopsis: SCT ATC Front Line Manager reported losing all data tags on the Stadium Radar scope. The Front Line Manager reported the confidence level in the equipment is low due to a decrease in reliability.
summary: An air traffic controller experienced a total loss of data and radar on the new STAR (Stadium) scope during a busy Los Angeles arrival push. The controller used the adjacent DNYR scope to maintain services, attributing the failure to recent software updates and expressing a lack of confidence in the system's reliability.

synopsis: ATC controller reported an aircraft flying the wrong departure route, and the pilot reported that they had not noticed the revised routing and failed to enter it into their FMC.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X departed Charlotte International Airport but deviated from the new ADAR routing after the RDU VORTAC by following an old route due to missing a revised segment on the PDC printout. The controller corrected the deviation, noting no separation loss occurred, attributing the error to human oversight amidst frequent navigation procedure changes.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: TOL TRACON Controller reported a loss of separation related to an opposite direction operation. The arrival and departure were not within the tolerance limits.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a separation issue during IFR practice approaches when Aircraft Y reached the 7 NM cutoff while Aircraft X was still over the threshold due to radar gaps. The controller attributed the difficulty to unclear "airborne" status and suggested changing the procedure to use "rolling" calls with an increased cutoff distance.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported executing a go-around at PHX following an unstable approach that resulted from an RA encounter with parallel traffic.
summary: The crew of a jet vectored for a visual approach to Runway 25L at PHX received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb due to a conflict with a Regional Jet. The RA caused the aircraft to overshoot the final approach path, resulting in a go-around and a subsequent uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported returning to the gate after a pilot in an aircraft behind them reported a tailpipe fire.
summary: Multiple pilots and passengers reported seeing flames from the number one engine while the aircraft was taxiing for takeoff. The crew executed the Engine Tailpipe Fire Checklist, returned to the gate, and the aircraft was taken out of service after external reports indicated the flames had extinguished.

synopsis: Dash-8 Captain reported returning to the gate after failure of the auto-feather system was noted on the takeoff roll.
summary: The crew rejected two takeoffs due to an Auto-feather system failure to arm. After a ground test found no faults, the aircraft was returned to the gate and MEL'd as an administrative control item.

synopsis: Dash-8 First Officer and Flight Attendant reported returning to departure airport following failure of #2 engine.
summary: Pilots and cabin crew experienced a number two engine torque spike and failure at 700 feet during departure, causing yaw and emergency light flicker. The crew executed an overweight landing, returned to the gate with fire crew assistance, and were held at the airport for two hours by scheduling despite requesting rest.

synopsis: Pilots, dispatcher and maintenance controller reported that prior to push-back, an A300 APU failed and was deferred. After starting both engines using an air cart, the #2 engine bleed valve failed closed.
summary: The flight crew and dispatcher encountered an APU failure and No. 2 bleed fault during pushback, requiring pneumatic engine starts. The dispatcher incorrectly processed a flagged MEL item via release document instead of a conference call, though the flight proceeded with fuel and altitude restrictions to avoid icing.

synopsis: PC-12 pilot reported they returned to departure airport following false stall warnings shortly after takeoff that may have been related to a bird strike on an AOA vane.
summary: During an IFR takeoff, the crew experienced false stall warnings and shaker activation likely caused by a bird strike near the right AOA vane. They returned for a safe landing with stiff controls and distracting aural alerts, noting they could have muted the warnings using the inhibit switch.

synopsis: B737 flight attendants became aware during boarding that there were 12 lap children on the flight and only 10 infant life vests aboard. The operations agent was made aware and she provided two more life vests. This appeared to comply with the letter of the FAR but the reporters were not sure.
summary: Flight attendants discovered 12 lap children on a flight with only 10 spare life vests, prompting the Captain and Operations Agent to approve adding two extra vests to avoid an oversell. Upon arrival, the Operations Agent claimed this violated regulations and demanded the vests be surrendered, though the crew believed they complied with the requirement for one vest per passenger.

synopsis: B737-700 flight attendant reported new Company door-disarm procedures are potentially dangerous.
summary: A flight attendant disarmed an armed aft galley door before the required PA announcement after a provisioner attempted to open it while the jetway was moving. The incident, caused by the provisioner ignoring the red armed strap, created a risk of slide deployment and injury to both parties.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported confusion regarding a restricted area that was subject to an 'Altitude Reservation' procedure.
summary: A pilot receiving flight following from Patuxent Approach was vectored away from restricted area R-4006 while cruising at 3,000 feet. The pilot later learned an unbriefed Altitude Reservation extended the restriction to the surface, which would have caused a penetration without the controller's intervention.

synopsis: A pilot reported that power lines with about 24 inch orange warning spheres on them are aligned with Taxiway A, not Runway 33. The spheres are less than a quarter mile from Runway 33 and misleading.
summary: A pilot reported that power pole markings south of Runway 33 are incorrectly aligned with Taxiway A instead of the runway. This misalignment creates a potential confusion hazard for pilots operating in that area.

synopsis: PA-32 pilot reported noticing his instruments were not responding as expected, and found that selecting an alternate static source solved the problem.
summary: The pilot experienced a pitot-static system failure during a descent from 8,000 to 6,000 feet, indicated by unresponsive altimeter and vertical speed readings. Switching to the alternate static source corrected the instruments, allowing the pilot to stabilize at 6,000 feet after notifying Air Traffic Control.

synopsis: A pilot reported concerns regarding the continuing disruption of GPS signals by the military testing jamming equipment.
summary: A pilot reported that military GPS interference testing (NAFB 16-03) grounded Phenom 300s and all IFR aircraft above FL240 in the Southwest due to potential signal loss. The reporter stated this testing threatens aviation safety while ground-based NAVAIDs are being decommissioned.

synopsis: A pilot reported discovering after landing that the airport was closed. He acknowledged failing to read the airport NOTAMs and adding that the only visible barriers were from the runway to the taxiways. The runway had no X indicating closed.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight landed at an airport after ATC cleared a visual approach, unaware the field was closed per NOTAMS. The pilot discovered the closure only after landing when barricades blocked the taxiway, noting the runway lacked proper closed markings and ATC never advised of the status.

synopsis: The pilot and Tower controller reported an aircraft that landed on a parallel taxiway rather than the runway.
summary: A King Air pilot, cleared for a visual approach to runway 32, inadvertently landed on taxiway A after misaligning during a modified S-turn. The pilot attributed the error to shock upon seeing the taxiway centerline, which delayed a go-around, though no collision occurred as the taxiway was clear.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Center Controller reported a handoff of an aircraft whose radar data indicated it was climbing to 35,000 feet. The aircraft was climbing to 39,000 feet, and conflicting with traffic at 36,000 feet.
summary: An air traffic controller and two aircraft (X and Y) experienced a potential conflict during a climb to FL390 when ZLA incorrectly entered an interim altitude of FL350 in the data tag. The controller missed the pilot's climb clearance and the pilot failed to acknowledge a traffic call, though the aircraft ultimately maintained separation.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported ATC cleared them for a final altitude that was lower than planned and revised performance information was not readily available.
summary: The Pilot-in-Command of an EMB145 declared minimum fuel after ATC insisted on a descent to 6,000 feet despite a lack of low-altitude performance data in the cockpit. This declaration secured a revised clearance to 16,000 feet and a shortcut, allowing the flight to land safely with 3,160 lbs of fuel.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported returning to departure airport following loss of a main hydraulic system shortly after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew reported excessive fluid gushing from the right side and a HYD LO PRES caution on engine 2 after takeoff. They returned to the airport, where a Fire Marshall inspection found no visible damage or leaks, allowing the aircraft to taxi to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: B757 Captain on approach experienced a TCAS RA generated by an Airbus approaching 16L. The Captain was the monitoring pilot with the traffic in sight and instructed the First Officer to continue the approach. The RA was calling for a climb initially, with the traffic clearly above.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring on an Airbus approach to 16R ignored conflicting TCAS "Climb" and "Descend" RAs at 2,000 and 1,700 feet AGL because visual contact showed parallel traffic above and to the left. The crew continued the approach safely, concluding that following the RAs would have caused a collision with the visible aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General aviation pilot in the pattern at 4B9 reported a loss of control after a wake turbulence encounter with a B737 inbound to BDL.
summary: A pilot on crosswind at Simsbury Airport (4B9) encountered severe wake turbulence from a nearby Boeing 737, likely vectored by BDL ATC. The turbulence caused extreme rolls and a violent downward slam, injuring the pilot and damaging cockpit equipment.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate pilot reported receiving a TCAS climb RA at 1,000 feet on the SNA Runway 20 visual approach. After landing he learned an avionics shop in the vicinity of his alert causes occasional false TCAS alerts.
summary: A single-pilot aircraft on visual approach for Runway 20R received a false TCAS "Climb" resolution advisory due to a nearby avionics shop. The pilot manually climbed to comply, but ATC confirmed no traffic existed, attributing the event to a known sporadic anomaly.

synopsis: C206 pilot reported loosing control while landing in a cross wind and departing the runway. The aircraft was stopped in the grass without hitting any lights or signs.
summary: The pilot experienced a runway departure during a left crosswind landing when a strong gust lifted the left wing before nose wheel contact, causing a loss of control authority. The aircraft stopped in the grass without injury or damage, attributed to carrying excess approach speed that increased vulnerability to the gust.

synopsis: Light transport aircraft pilot reported a brief deviation below glideslope after safety pilot simulated a single engine approach.
summary: During flight training, a safety pilot simulated an engine failure, causing the aircraft to descend below the glide slope while the crew performed the emergency checklist. The pilot reported maintaining visual clearance above terrain by hundreds of feet.

synopsis: PA18 floatplane pilot reported being unable to comply with his taxi clearance on Lake Hood due to a strong quartering tailwind. He ended up drifting into a water lane causing a conflict with an aircraft on final approach.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing for takeoff at Lake Hood, strong gusts at Airmen's Point prevented a maneuver across the North/South water lane, pushing the aircraft into the Southeast lane. Although another aircraft on final was asked to go around, it continued landing safely, resulting in no conflict or evasive maneuvers.

synopsis: CHS Tower Controller reported of a problem with traffic into the airport. The pattern traffic was working until the reporter was given a point out on a Lifeguard aircraft which caused the pattern to be disrupted and caused a wake turbulence problem.
summary: The Tower controller managed Aircraft X's complex pattern entry and missed approach while coordinating with TRACON and West Radar. The controller issued a second go-around to Aircraft X to prevent a loss of wake turbulence separation with a priority helicopter and adjusted arrival sequencing for Aircraft Y and others.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew in an emergency descent received an RA on traffic below it that being vectored out of the way.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a Citation with pressurization loss and a trailing Aircraft Y misheard a coordination instruction, incorrectly turning Aircraft Y left instead of right. This error caused the aircraft to converge before the controller corrected the heading, allowing the Citation to descend safely while maintaining separation.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZAB Center Controller reported of a mid-shift that was busy with weather deviations. Controller reported being so busy that he could not coordinated as needed.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that heavy convective weather and low staffing caused airspace saturation, preventing proper coordination and deviation reporting per 7110.65. The controller attributed the safety risk to a lack of Traffic Management Initiatives and ground delays, which allowed excessive aircraft volume to overwhelm the sector.

synopsis: ORL Tower Controller reported of an unfamiliar operation that led to an operational error. TRACON did not want to change runways but due to winds the Tower Controller took the aircraft and one ended up circling to the runway and then causing a loss of separation.
summary: The Local Control Air Traffic Controller at ORL managed two aircraft circling to land Runway 7 during sudden heavy rain and strong gusts after a delayed runway change. The controller attributed the situation to the TRACON's inflexibility, inadequate weather coordination by the Ground controller, and a lack of training for handling simultaneous circling approaches in deteriorating conditions.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported possibly encountering a drone that flew by the right wing while descending through 9000 ft on approach to ATL near POORS.
summary: During descent through 9,000 ft on arrival, the First Officer observed an object, possibly a drone, pass the right wing while the Captain did not see it. The crew reported the incident to Air Traffic Control.

synopsis: After arrival at HNL, international arriving passenger exit to Customs on buses after ascending an escalator to a 30' X 30' waiting pad. Too many people were on the pad but the escalator continued delivering people who had no where to go and no available escalator shutoff.
summary: Ground agents failed to control passenger flow from a foreign arrival onto an escalator leading to a customs bus area. The small 30x30 foot waiting pad at the top became overcrowded, causing the escalator to clog and resulting in passengers tripping and falling.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported falling into the old Airbus FMS altitude constraints deleted above cruise altitude trap during descent on the CHSLY1. The flight had originally been cruising at FL220 which automatically deleted the BURRZ FL240 restriction. The flight was then cleared to FL240 for traffic and the BURRZ restriction was forgotten about.
summary: Pilots on an Airbus at FL240 descended below the deleted FL240 constraint at BURRZ on the CHSLY1 arrival due to an FMS trap and early descent. The crew lost 500 feet before stopping the descent and climbing back to FL240 after ATC queried their altitude.

synopsis: Flight crew reported going around from 50 feet due to a departing aircraft not having rotated yet. The go around was self initiated and resulted in these two aircraft climbing in close proximity to each other without any direction from the tower.
summary: The crew of an aircraft on short final at CLT executed a go-around after ATC cleared two departures despite insufficient runway space. The controller's decision to launch the second aircraft caused an extremely close overtake, resulting in a significant event classification and an apology.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported severe VHF radio static at FL360 in the vicinity of thunderstorms while IMC. ATC relayed the flight a new frequency through guard to clear communications.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the crew deviated right of thunderstorms and entered IMC, causing both radios to fail with loud static. The pilot suspects improperly bonded or damaged static dischargers caused the interference, which persisted even after switching frequencies to regain communication.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported executing a go-around after experiencing a wake turbulence encounter on approach into ORD.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft at 3,500 feet while on a visual approach to ORD, causing significant rolling. They executed a missed approach to 4,000 feet, stabilized, and subsequently landed safely on runway 9L.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A fractional operator flight crew reported that during an approach into Aspen, CO was advised of departing traffic and to descend early to avoid conflict. The flight received both EGPWS and TCAS RA alerts while the airport, terrain, and other aircraft were in sight.
summary: The pilot monitoring reported EGPWS warnings and a TCAS RA during a visual approach into Aspen, CO, caused by early descent to avoid a conflicting departing jet. The crew viewed both alerts as non-events since they maintained visual separation from terrain and traffic throughout the maneuver.

synopsis: SA227 Captain reported a taxiway excursion after exiting the landing runway on a high speed taxiway. The park button had no apparent effect on the nose wheel steering angle. The right propeller struck a taxiway light and the engine was shut down for taxi in.
summary: The pilot reported that during a high-speed turnoff after landing, the aircraft veered wide and struck a taxi light due to excessive speed and a malfunctioning nose wheel steering park button. The pilot feathered the right engine after hearing a noise from the propeller and taxied in on one engine.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported being notified that another air carrier also on approach to SFO would be landing on a parallel runway. The crew then received a TCAS RA from a small aircraft that was below them.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach to SFO Runway 28R received a TCAS Resolution Advisory and leveled off to avoid a VFR aircraft 300 feet below. The pilot attributed the near mid-air collision risk to unsafe wingtip flying practices and a company SOP requiring TCAS RA deactivation when parallel traffic is in sight.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot transiting the Sierra Nevada Mountain Range at 12,000 feet encountered an overcast layer and was cleared VFR on top at 14,500 ft when clouds and icing were encountered. The pilot descended and diverted to TVL in order to clear the clouds.
summary: A pilot departing O57 VFR encountered rising cloud tops, entered IMC, and experienced icing that prevented maintaining altitude. The pilot filed IFR, received vectors from ATC to descend below clouds, and landed safely at TVL, attributing the incident to a judgment error regarding weather conditions.

synopsis: A DJI Inspire 1 Pro UAS owner lost communication with the aircraft which then did not return 'home' but hit a tall building destroying the UAS and breaking a window 25 stories up.
summary: A pilot operating a DJI Inspire 1 Pro drone lost signal at 400 feet, causing the aircraft to fly away and crash through a window 25 stories down. The incident resulted in approximately $500 in property damage to an unoccupied space with no injuries, and the drone was recovered and returned to the pilot.

synopsis: A flight instructor reported that while working on power off 180 and short field techniques in a Beechcraft BE-33, the pilot found himself in a higher than normal pitch attitude which caused the plane to stall, resulting in the wingtip contacting the runway.
summary: During a training flight practicing power-off 180s and short field techniques, the instructor took controls on final approach to demonstrate a ground effect stall. The instructor misjudged altitude, causing an unexpected stall and right wing drop that resulted in a hard landing and bent right wingtip.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate turbojet Captain reported not noticing the altitude restrictions on the electronic chart display.
summary: The flight crew missed a 7,000-foot crossing restriction at SIGME while descending via the HYPER 6 arrival into IAD due to distraction from weather radar, fatigue, and failing to notice a small note on electronic charts referencing an insert. Approach instructed a descent to meet the next restriction at MOWAT, highlighting the crew's concern that scattered chart information increases workload and error risk.

synopsis: Carbon Cub pilot reported the right cockpit window came loose after takeoff and eventually separated from the aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying a Carbon Cub experienced a right side window detachment during climb out due to an improperly secured front latch. The window broke away at high airspeed, causing damage to the wing, fuselage, and stabilizer, attributed to low aircraft experience and aggressive slipstream forces.

synopsis: C172 pilot and safety pilot reported diverting to a nearby alternate airport when the engine began to backfire.
summary: The pilot and safety pilot experienced an engine failure during a VFR flight near Class Bravo airspace after an unplanned climb and turn. The pilot executed a precautionary landing at an uncontrolled airport following loud engine noises, attributing the incident to poor pre-flight communication regarding altitude and route.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light Jet Air taxi First Officer reported a near miss with a UAV at 7,000 ft while flying a straight in visual approach to SBY Runway 14. TRACON Controller showed no interest in the event.
summary: The First Officer reported a drone passing within 300 feet of the aircraft at 6,800 feet MSL during pre-landing duties. The controller acknowledged the report but showed no concern, leaving the crew worried about the unreported, non-TCAS-equipped drone's proximity.

synopsis: PC-12 flight crew reported a rag was left in such a location so as to prevent full retraction of the flaps after takeoff. The distraction led to failure to retract the landing gear.
summary: The crew continued a flight with flaps stuck at 3 degrees due to a rag in the actuator and a missed popped gear circuit breaker from a rushed preflight. They landed safely after verifying the gear was down despite the lever being up, attributing the errors to schedule pressure and fixation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Air taxi pilot reported confusion with his clearance while attempting an intersection takeoff at ISP airport.
summary: The pilot at Islip was cleared for an intersection takeoff on Runway 33L but was ordered to abort after lining up due to a misunderstanding where the tower expected a takeoff on Runway 24. No violation occurred, and the pilot was subsequently cleared for an immediate takeoff on Runway 24 with no incidents reported.

synopsis: Eclipse 500 First Officer reported experiencing an electrical bus failure. Running the QRH checklist restored normal operation.
summary: During a Part 91 repositioning flight departing Las Vegas, the crew experienced simultaneous failures of the autopilot, yaw damper, generator #1, and trim controls at FL160, causing a runaway stabilator. The pilot reset the electric system bus in flight to restore all systems, and the flight concluded uneventfully, though the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: A pipeline patrol pilot reported a near mid-air collision with an aerial application aircraft.
summary: A pilot conducting a low-level pipeline patrol at 300 AGL encountered a turbine-powered aerial application aircraft on an unpredictable flight path. The pilot executed aggressive evasive maneuvers to avoid a near collision, estimating a final separation of 250 feet horizontal and 40 feet vertical, attributing the risk to the other aircraft's failure to see and avoid.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Corporate Captain reported that the published NOTAM was ambiguous using two airports rather than one.
summary: The pilot and copilot overlooked a Shelbyville (SYI) runway closure NOTAM during enroute and descent phases because the alert was incorrectly prefixed with the Nashville (BNA) identifier. The crew diverted to Nashville, noting the error resulted from the non-standard NOTAM presentation format.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported failing to extend the landing gear resulting in a gear up landing with minimal damage.
summary: The pilot, flying a personal aircraft for over 40 years, missed the gear extension checklist item during landing after a three-hour leg in moderate turbulence. The pilot attributed the error to fatigue, resulting in minimal airframe damage.

synopsis: Be400A Captain reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of an Airbus on approach to SAN.
summary: The pilot flying into SAN encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus while descending to 4,000 ft and slowing to 180 kts. The turbulence rocked the wings, forcing an autopilot disengagement and level flight, but no further action was required.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: An air taxi Captain reported that the flight crew had difficulty in managing the radio panel.
summary: During a line-check, the acting captain and non-flying pilot lost crew intercom and experienced split radio communications due to an activated 'Split Mode' switch. This caused both pilots to transmit on different frequencies, confusing Cleveland Center until the crew deactivated the switch and restored shared communication on COM-1.

synopsis: The Captain of a transport aircraft on a training flight reported that smoke from nearby fire obscured portions of the final approach segments even though the airport was reporting VFR visibilities.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that while being vectored for a visual approach to LAX runway 24R, smoke reduced inflight visibility to 1-2 SM, causing the crew to lose sight of lead traffic and undershoot the localizer. The controller broke the aircraft out and re-vectored it, after which the crew completed the approach, noting that the visual clearance was inappropriate given the actual visibility conditions.

synopsis: Flight attendants on international flight reported a chronic issue with insufficient water to last the duration of the trip.
summary: Cabin crew reported a potable water shortage and Waste tank 1 failure during the arrival phase, rendering four lavatories unusable. The reporter attributed this ongoing two-year issue to inadequate company maintenance, creating unsanitary conditions and a health hazard for passengers and crew.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported passengers were evacuated to the terminal via aircraft entry doors after a start cart caught fire on the ramp next to them.
summary: Cabin crew reported that while attempting to start engines using four start carts, one cart under the wing caught fire. Passengers were evacuated through the boarding door without deploying slides after smoke entered the cabin.

synopsis: Sailplane instructor and student reported lifting conditions diminished greatly and the pilots were unable to maintain their block assignment or contact ATC directly. The pilots turned back toward the departure airport before ATC clearance could be received.
summary: A glider pilot encountered severe mountain wave sink and lost radio contact with Oakland ATC while operating in Class A airspace. The pilot was forced to turn north to maintain glide and cancel IFR after another aircraft diverted to avoid a near miss caused by frequency congestion and unexpected terrain separation requirements.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A VFR pilot did not comply with Local Control's instructions in the pattern. The pilot in the pattern flew into the path of a departure causing a NMAC.
summary: Local South cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X, a solo VFR pilot, was off course and descended to 1800 feet, causing a near midair collision requiring evasive maneuvers. The reporter attributes the incident to Local South's poor decision to clear the departure and lack of positive control, though the pilot also failed to follow instructions to stay on the airport road at 2100 feet.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: PRC Tower Controller reported of constant wind changes and trying to get all aircraft to land safely. Towers SAWS (Stand Alone Weather Sensors) was out of service and the Controller had to cross the room to read the ASOS (Automated Surface Observation System).
summary: An air traffic controller managed multiple aircraft during erratic winds and convective activity while primary wind sensors (SAWS) and ASOS failed. Despite instrument outages and combined staffing duties, the controller used wind socks to sequence a corporate jet, high-wing aircraft, and air taxi for safe landings on Runways 21L and 03R.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Due to weather deviations, sectors at ZKC ARTCC became saturated with traffic. Controllers stated the supervisors were not doing enough to relieve the congestion. A Controller issued an instruction to an aircraft which the aircraft did not respond to causing conflict with another aircraft at the same altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 84 reported a loss of separation between two aircraft caused by sector saturation, poor routing, and inadequate supervisor support. The controller issued emergency turns and descents after failing to hear a pilot's blocked clearance, attributing the event to complex weather, ineffective flow control, and insufficient coordination.

synopsis: Kansas City Center Controller reported missing a handoff due to weather, workload, traffic deviating, and having to come up with deviation routes on the fly.
summary: An air traffic controller in ZKC Sector 84 missed a handoff to ZKC XA due to sector saturation caused by poor TMU coordination, unusable routing, and weather deviations. The controller was forced to manually reroute converging ORD arrival streams and shut down traffic after supervisors failed to address the ineffective flow plan.

synopsis: Kansas City Center [ZKC] Controller reported of a loss of separation due to weather, workload, traffic deviating, and having to come up with deviation routes on the fly. Reporter wanted to accept the aircraft instead of taking a point out but did not and a loss of altitude separation ensued.
summary: An air traffic controller in ZKC84 reported a loss of separation between SKW3113 and SKW5365 caused by a ZKC94 controller expediting a descent through traffic due to missed altitude restrictions. The incident resulted from poor TMU coordination, ineffective supervisor oversight, and weather-induced routing issues that saturated the sector.

synopsis: Tower Controller issued a cancel takeoff directive to a Part 121 aircraft during it's take off roll prompting a high speed abort.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 110 knots on Runway 26L at ATL after Tower clearance was cancelled due to a Caravan taxiing on Taxiway D. The aircraft returned to the gate for a maintenance inspection and brake cooling, with the pilot requesting a dedicated PA microphone for future announcements.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported not making a crossing restriction on the FRNCH3 STAR to DEN.
summary: Fatigued pilots on a three-day trip descended below the 13,000-foot restriction at BABAA during the FRNCH3 arrival because the Captain failed to reselect VNAV while in Level Change. Air Traffic Control queried the altitude, prompting an immediate climb to 13,000 feet before the crew completed the arrival.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported overshooting an altitude clearance they never acknowledged in descent following multiple STAR clearance changes.
summary: Pilots reported multiple STAR changes and a runway switch at HOU caused confusion regarding descent clearances. A controller initially claimed a 11,000-foot limit was issued, but after the crew stated they never heard it, the controller cleared them to descend to 6,000 feet.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a Tower Controller's landing and arrival sequence plan was unsafe.
summary: A pilot on short final to SFO Runway 28R reported a runway incursion risk involving a preceding aircraft and another taking off from Runway 1R. The pilot attributed the unsafe situation to the controller's refusal to acknowledge potential errors and poor spacing, particularly given limited night visibility.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experienced an engine compressor stall during takeoff. Procedures were followed ending with a return to the departure airport.
summary: During takeoff after rotation, the crew received an ENG 2 EGT Overlimit warning followed by multiple compressor stalls on engine 2. They returned for an overweight landing, and maintenance later reported that the N1 Fan section of the engine had seized.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Fractional Flight Crew reported descending below 3,000 ft, the floor of the Class B airspace, while on approach to TEB.
summary: The flight crew diverted to TEB after finding the destination runway too short and the alternate closed, then climbed from 2500 to 3000 ft after a new controller cited minimum vectoring altitude. The reporter attributed the confusion to high traffic volume, runway closures, and pilots rejecting visual approaches.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew experienced smoke in the cockpit and cabin during cruise flight phase. Packs and fans were shut down, the flight diverted, and the smoke abated. Landing was uneventful.
summary: During climb through FL250, a Pack 1 overload and subsequent smoke in the cockpit and cabin prompted an emergency descent to 10,000 ft. The smoke dissipated after turning off both packs and the recirculation fan, allowing a safe landing at ZZZ with no injuries or visible abnormalities found.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff on a hot day at a high elevation airport when the #2 engine ITT was exceeded.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 105 kts due to an Engine 2 ITT exceedance, resulting in a brake overheat warning. The aircraft returned to the gate for inspection, was grounded overnight, and passengers were deplaned while awaiting a replacement.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported an inflight engine malfunction. Flight diverted to an enroute field and landed uneventfully.
summary: During climb through FL320, the crew experienced engine stalls, oil clogging, and cabin smoke, prompting an expedited descent and overweight landing. The left engine was shut down on the ground after ARFF reported smoke, allowing for a normal passenger deplaning.

synopsis: An EMB-175 Captain reported being advised by a Flight Attendant that a passenger witnessed a dark grey, spherically shaped UAS three feet long flew near their aircraft's wingtip at some point during departure.
summary: A passenger reported a large, dark grey drone with a camera and green light flying near the right wingtip at approximately 17,000 ft. The drone reportedly just missed the aircraft's wing.

synopsis: Global 6000 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff when the pilot flying engaged the autothrottles before runway lineup was completed resulting in a temporary loss of directional control.
summary: Two pilots rejected a takeoff on Runway 19R at LAS after the Pilot Flying overshot the centerline while following green taxi lights for the parallel runway and engaged auto-throttles. The aircraft veered right, prompting an abort; the crew later attributed the error to the Pilot Flying's confusion and dismissal of the safety risk.

synopsis: Seaplane pilot landed on the water with the wheels extended resulting in the aircraft nosing over in the lake.
summary: The pilot in command of an amphibious aircraft landed with wheels extended due to distraction, causing the nose to submerge and the cockpit to flood. The pilot escaped uninjured, attributing the incident to pilot error, while minor wing damage occurred later during recovery in shallow water.

synopsis: BE55 instructor pilot reported the ailerons locked up and it took considerable effort to break them free. Post flight inspection revealed the aileron linkage was caught on a fuel pressure gauge line.
summary: During a training flight performing unusual attitudes, the pilot experienced a momentary aileron lock caused by linkage catching on a fuel pressure gauge line. Maintenance repaired the defect after the pilot landed and reported the urgent situation to Air Traffic Control without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: A pilot called Flight Service to file an SFRA (Special Flight Rules Area) flight plan, a flight service specialist replied that she could not accept the flight plan over the 1-800-WXBRIEF line.
summary: A pilot filing an SFRA flight plan from KRIC to ZZZ was incorrectly told by a Flight Service Specialist that the 1-800-WXBRIEF line could not accept the request. The pilot subsequently air-filed the plan via Leesburg Radio, noting the specialist likely confused SFRA procedures with FRZ requirements.

synopsis: An agriculture Helicopter flight struck power lines while conducting its mission.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting agricultural cherry drying operations suspected a power line strike after observing downed lines but continued the mission due to urgency. Upon landing, a slight dent was found on one main rotor blade, leading the general contractor to ground the aircraft for further inspection.

synopsis: BE33 pilot reported diverting to a nearby airport when the landing gear failed to fully retract. Gear was extended via the emergency method resulting in an uneventful landing.
summary: The pilot experienced an electrical failure and burning odor after retracting landing gear at 300 feet AGL, causing avionics loss and gear malfunction. After diverting to a nearby airport, the passenger manually cranked the gear down, allowing for a safe landing with the gear confirmed extended.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported landing on a highway after the engine quit because of fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced an in-flight engine stoppage and landed on a highway. Investigation revealed incorrect fuel gauges as the cause; after refueling and testing, the pilot successfully took off from the highway and flew to the airport without further issues.

synopsis: TB20 pilot reported an NMAC with an aircraft that had released jumpers in the vicinity of HWY airport.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a skydiving aircraft during an IFR descent to 7,500 feet. The jumper pilot ignored ATC instructions, dived within a few hundred yards, and failed to maintain separation while attempting to reach the ground before the jumpers.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: BED Tower controllers reported an aircraft was supposed to make a 360 on downwind, but did not and caused a conflict with a helicopter.
summary: An air traffic controller training a developmental controller failed to broadcast a second 360-degree maneuver by Aircraft X to Aircraft Y, causing a traffic conflict and evasive action. The incident occurred during a busy period with combined positions, a helicopter blocking the frequency, and simultaneous coordination calls, leading the controller to admit scanning errors.

synopsis: San Jose Tower Controller reported misapplying new wake recategorization rules and having a loss of separation. Reporter stated staffing issues and having to work local combined with Controller in Charge duties contributed to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller misapplied wake recat rules by clearing a PA24 from RWY30L/D simultaneously with a B787 from RWY30R/A1. The controller attributed the error to chronic understaffing, which forced them to work the CIC position while on local, preventing a second controller from catching the mistake.

synopsis: Two B737 pilots and a ZDC Controller involved described a failure to communicate the planned weather avoidance route. ATC believed the crew was trying to create a short cut and the crew stated they were merely trying to stay on the upwind side of a large thunderstorm.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X deviated left of J42 GVE at FL350 to avoid thunderstorms, rejecting ATC's suggestion to turn right due to observed rough air. The crew received a supervisor call order and experienced an altitude clearance confusion during handoff, which they attributed to communication breakdowns and reduced situational awareness in their older aircraft.

synopsis: An NCT Controller reported releasing a departure on a departure procedure which reverses course towards inbound traffic. The pilot of the departing aircraft did not contact the Controller in time for the Controller to vector the departure out of the way of two arrivals.
summary: An IFR departure from SQL failed to contact departure frequency, merging with a VFR inbound aircraft and losing lateral separation from an IFR arrival. The controller issued vectors to maintain separation, but the questionable VFR downwind departure procedure caused conflicting traffic flows and proximity to minimum safe altitudes.

synopsis: ZAB Center Controller denied a turn to the west due to weather and Special Use Airspace. Transferring foreign Controller shipped aircraft deviating to the west. Reporter stated this type of issue happens with this foreign Center whenever weather is an issue.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Mazatlan Center disregarded an "unable" clearance for Aircraft X to deviate west of VYLLA into active military airspace due to weather. The aircraft entered the restricted area despite the controller's refusal, while a second aircraft also deviated west after an eastward turn was deemed too late.

synopsis: Tower Front Line Manager reported of a loss of separation during a skill check on local position. Developmental did not fix a separation problem and switched both aircraft to Departure Control.
summary: During a Local Control skill check, a trainee unexpectedly transferred a Hawker 25B to TRACON while it was in close proximity to a Cessna 152. The Hawker subsequently received a Resolution Advisory and descended 200 feet, passing within 1/3 NM laterally and 100 feet vertically of the Cessna.

synopsis: Aircraft parking chocks were removed without the parking brake being set causing the aircraft to move a short distance.
summary: After parking, the jetway moved uncommanded and struck the forward entry door while the tug remained attached and chocks were removed. The crew attributed the movement to an unknown cause, resulting in cosmetic door damage and a passenger being pulled from the closing gap.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a go-around followed an unstable approach related to incorrect programming of FMC on the arrival into LAS.
summary: The flight crew executing an RNAV visual approach to Runway 19L at LAS selected the incorrect RNVV procedure instead of RNVS, causing altitude and speed discrepancies. Recognizing they were too high to meet restrictions at the EASTR waypoint, they initiated a go-around and were subsequently vectored for a visual approach to Runway 7R.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer flying the LAX SADDE 6 Arrival failed to see or hear the autopilot disconnect and as the aircraft turned at SADDE it continued descending to 9,400 ft before the Captain called 'altitude.' As the flight climbed back to 10,000 ft, ATC asked them to ident at which time the Captain found the First Officer had turn the transponder OFF.
summary: During the LAX arrival, the crew deviated 600 feet below 10,000 feet and overflew SADDE due to an unannounced autopilot disconnect and a premature turn. The incident resulted from the Pilot Monitoring failing to verbalize the disconnect and the Pilot Flying being distracted by conflicting ATC clearances and FMC inputs.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew on an oceanic crossing reported experiencing galley smoke and fumes. Flight crew elected to divert to nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ due to an unexplained electrical burning smell in the aft galley, overriding dispatch pressure to land elsewhere. After receiving incorrect landing data, they landed safely, but fire crews were delayed by a late jet bridge connection, causing a 30-minute deplaning delay.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being confronted with operational issues with a B777 model with which they were unfamiliar. Pilot handbooks provided scant information on the aircraft differences.
summary: A 777 crew encountered significant operational difficulties with a different 777 model variant during preflight, lacking knowledge of the weather radar, door controls, and hand microphone. The incident highlighted severe training gaps regarding aircraft differences, forcing the crew to rely on remote guidance and a flight attendant to identify system functions before deciding to cancel the flight.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported their Dispatcher flight planned through known turbulence areas for an oceanic flight.
summary: The crew and dispatcher disagreed on turbulence forecasts during flight planning, leading the captain to add 5,000 lbs of fuel to descend below the hazard. En route, a subsequent dispatcher confirmed the turbulence, and the crew descended to avoid it, resulting in a smooth flight.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew was notified by EWR Tower about an earlier UAS sighting. They also detected the UAS at about 420 feet, but the craft's details were difficult to determine.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer spotted a drone above and to the right of their flight path at 420 feet MSL while on ILS 22L into EWR. No deviation was required, and the aircraft landed normally after the crew reported the sighting to the tower and police.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an EGPWS 'TERRAIN, PULL UP' warning while flying a left descending base for a visual approach to TYS Runway 23L.
summary: The pilot reported an EGPWS warning while on the base leg for a visual approach to TYS 23L after being vectored high and fast. The crew executed an escape maneuver, climbing 400 feet to clear the warning, and landed uneventfully, attributing the event to poor speed/altitude management and possible false indication.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being given direct routings in mountainous terrain and repeatedly having to explain to ATC controllers that he wanted to remain on his filed route due to drift down considerations.
summary: Pilots departing 16L on the LEETZ departure requested to remain on route for drift down safety after controllers issued direct clearances to UPJAR and EKR. The crew reported that the second controller ignored their safety concerns regarding terrain clearance and expedited traffic instead of listening to their operational needs.

synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported that Maintenance Control discouraged him from writing up an aircraft that had an air conditioning problem due to it being a terminating flight. Captain reported writing up the aircraft as too hot.
summary: The pilot reported excessive cabin heat and poor airflow during cruise on a flight with 33 passengers, noting duct temperatures of 15C. Despite maintenance control pressuring the pilot not to log the issue due to it being a terminator, the pilot filed a write-up for the aircraft being too hot for service.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported at the gate in DFW, with an engine running and the beacon on, a fuel truck hooked up and began to fuel the aircraft in violation of company policy.
summary: The flight crew at the gate discovered unauthorized hot refueling while preparing for pushback with an engine running and passengers onboard. The ground fueling crew violated safety protocols by ignoring clear operational indicators, though no injury or damage occurred.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported a bird strike while taking off from MAZ. They indicated that the bird hazard at this airport is significant and needs to be mitigated.
summary: The pilot reported multiple bird strikes during takeoff from Mayaguez airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The reporter attributed the incident to cut grass and poor airfield conditions.

synopsis: A Boeing 757 Captain reported experiencing multiple electrical failures while descending for an approach. The crew accomplished all applicable abnormal checklists and safely landed at the destination airport.
summary: During an IOE approach to 23L, a compound electrical failure caused left generator and bus tie failures, leaving the crew with limited systems. The captain executed a go-around to verify flap operation before landing safely, attributing the event to a sensed short that isolated the left side.

synopsis: During a Part 121 line check operation the Captain displayed difficulty with operating the automation. It was postulated that this was due to undetermined medical issues.
