aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the removal of two passengers who used abusive language toward the flight attendants and a Gate Agent during boarding.
summary: The Captain removed a male passenger and his sister from the aircraft before departure after they verbally abused a gate agent and Flight Attendant and refused crew instructions. Although the passenger cited a family emergency, both were denied boarding and required police assistance to leave the aircraft.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 Captain reported what he feels is a flaw in a company MEL procedure dealing with Forward Aux Transfer Pumps Inoperative.
summary: The pilot reported a potential conflict between MEL procedures and AFM limitations regarding unusable fuel in the FWD AUX tank with both transfer pumps inoperative. Despite multiple calls to load control confirming the loading was correct, the pilot questioned whether the MEL adequately addresses the resulting fuel balance condition.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reported rejecting takeoff due to a takeoff configuration warning. An FMC data entry error was identified.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a takeoff configuration warning and aborted departure due to a one-digit Center of Gravity error in the Flight Management Computer. The error, likely caused by mistyping or rounding, resulted in incorrect trim settings despite a deferred Weight and Balance system.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported using firewall thrust to cope with an unexpected tailwind shear event during takeoff from BOS.
summary: Boston flight crew encountered low-level wind shear during a max power takeoff on Runway 22R while executing the HYLND4 departure. They executed windshear escape procedures, climbed in takeoff configuration, and continued the flight with no damage or exceedances after receiving vectors to the SID.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported deviating to an alternate airport after encountering weather at GSP.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and autopilot roll deviations while deviating east of GSP to avoid thunderstorms. They diverted to ZZZ after Charlotte Approach recommended the alternate due to advancing weather, with no injuries reported in the cabin.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported deviating around an area of reported severe turbulence on a trans-Pacific flight without ATC approval.
summary: The Captain, enroute over the Pacific, deviated from ATC and Dispatch instructions to avoid a SIGMET for severe turbulence. Exercising authority, the crew turned north, offset 15 NM, and descended to FL270 below the hazard, completing a normal flight after notifying ATC and Dispatch.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported receiving a TA at FL340 while on an ATC vector in the vicinity of EWC.
summary: A pilot climbing to FL350 received a 90-degree off-course vector and tight turn instruction from Chicago Center, resulting in a TCAS traffic advisory for an intruder at the same altitude. The intruder climbed 1,000 feet above the aircraft, avoiding a resolution advisory, after which the crew was cleared direct to EWC and resumed climbing to FL350.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported their flight tracking tool displaying an airborne aircraft's position was off by over a thousand miles from their correct location.
summary: Flight Explorer incorrectly displayed Aircraft X's position by over a thousand miles. Manual position report retrieval via ACARS failed to resolve the display error.

synopsis: ERJ170 flight crew, Dispatcher, and Maintenance Supervisor reported that an engine anti-ice valve had been deferred open, but the valve was mistakenly closed.
summary: Flight crew encountered an Engine Anti-Ice failure caused by maintenance incorrectly securing the valve closed instead of open at ZZZ. Despite the error, the crew managed icing exposure en route to ZZZ1, landed safely, and noted that better MEL review could have prevented the issue.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported the Data Acquisition Unit (DAU) 1A unit failed in flight accompanied by a thump. After landing the crew's company asked that they ferry the aircraft to a Maintenance Station. The crew refused successive days because icing conditions existed and gear down ferry was high risk. The company asked another crew to ferry the aircraft, but would not allow the two crews to discuss mutual concerns.
summary: The flight crew refused to reposition an ERJ145 with a DAU 1A failure and untrustworthy gear indications due to moderate icing and withheld maintenance history regarding a nose gear oscillation. Company attempts to prevent crew debriefing and pressure to fly the unsafe aircraft were rejected, resulting in the flight being cancelled.

synopsis: The flight crew of a ERJ-190 reported they experienced a door warning light shortly after takeoff and elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight attendant and crew experienced a false door arming indication that resolved before departure, but a DOOR FWD SERV OPEN warning occurred on climbout. The aircraft returned for an overweight landing, and maintenance later found broken glass at the bottom of the door.

synopsis: Flight crew of a Large Transport aircraft reported descending approximately 700 feet due to using the local altimeter setting instead of 29.92. ATC asked about their altitude change and then assigned FL200 to fix the discrepancy.
summary: Pilots climbing from KBTV descended after switching to standard altimeter settings caused a false high indication, revealing their true altitude was below the assigned 18,000 ft. The incident resulted from filing an unusable flight level due to low local pressure, prompting a climb to FL200 after controller coordination.

synopsis: An air carrier crew reported taxi instruction confusion resulting from ambiguous, conflicting taxi instructions after landing on SDF Runway 17L with clearance across the airport on Runway 29.
summary: The flight crew and ground controller at SDF experienced confusion during arrival and taxi due to incorrect STAR fixes and ambiguous instructions to cross an unusable taxiway marked only by chevrons. The pilot attributed the incident to controller complacency and a lack of reflective markings or chart notes indicating the taxiway was unusable.

synopsis: MD-11 First Officer reported returning to the departure airport after experiencing a leading edge slat issue.
summary: The crew executed a missed approach on final due to a slat disagree alert and flight control malfunction, causing severe airspeed tape fluctuations. After communication difficulties with ATC, they returned to the departure airport and landed uneventfully with flaps 28.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew and Flight Attendant reported returning to the airport immediately after departure after smelling a burning odor throughout the aircraft.
summary: During departure rotation, the flight crew detected a burning odor in the cabin and returned to the field for a precautionary landing. Although no fire was found, the First Officer required medical evaluation for eye irritation, and the Captain acknowledged errors in crew coordination and failing to don oxygen masks.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dash-8 flight crew reported receiving intermittent erroneous GPWS alerts while being vectored for an ILS approach.
summary: The flight crew received false GPWS terrain warnings while being vectored for an ILS approach in IMC at 3,000 feet. After verifying their safe altitude with ATC and confirming no terrain on the display, they inhibited the system and filed a maintenance report for the erroneous alerts.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported receiving a GPWS warning for improper flap configuration on final approach. The crew selected the correct flap selection and landed safely.
summary: The Captain and First Officer forgot to extend flaps to 45 on final approach due to fatigue and workload, triggering a GPWS "Too low, terrain" alert. They elected to land with flaps 30 rather than go around, attributing the error to missed checklist items and high-speed descent instructions.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported firing both bottles into #2 engine after they experienced a hung start and an engine fire on the ramp after pushback.
summary: During engine start, the crew identified a hung start followed by apron reports of an engine fire and fuel on the ground. They executed the emergency checklist, discharged both fire bottles, and evacuated the aircraft to the gate under tow after firefighters confirmed no active fire remained.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician working on an Airbus A319 reported that they were unable to accomplish a task for engine vibration due to a lack of information.
summary: Two maintenance personnel on Aircraft X could not complete required engine inspections for high fan vibration because they never received confirmation of icing conditions from dispatch. Consequently, the reporter believes mandatory borescope and fluorescent penetrant inspections were not performed.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician working on a Global 5000 reported that after accomplishing some operational checkouts and resetting some circuit breakers the air data probes heated and two probe test adapters and the two aircraft air data probes were damaged.
summary: During a transponder checkout, a mechanic failed to pull probe heater breakers before powering the aircraft, causing uncommanded heating that damaged two test adapters and two airdata probes. The incident occurred because the maintenance manual's warning to collar these breakers was not followed, resulting in equipment damage.

synopsis: PA28R pilot and instructor reported a gear up landing due to distraction following a steep spiral maneuver.
summary: A student pilot and instructor landed a training aircraft with the gear retracted after performing steep spirals and a power-off 180. The incident occurred because the crew ignored the continuous landing gear horn due to habituation and stress, failing to complete the landing checklist.

synopsis: Cessna 208 First Officer reported receiving an engine fire warning on approach, but no evidence of fire was found after landing.
summary: During the downwind arrival, the pilot experienced a temporary engine fire warning and power rollback while descending from 6,000 to 4,000 ft. Despite normal engine instruments, the crew diverted to an immediate ILS approach and landed safely with no fire present.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported a loss of oil pressure while on approach.
summary: The pilot of an IFR flight experienced a steady oil pressure decline at 3,000 feet while being vectored for a visual approach. After requesting priority and descending to 1,600 feet, the pilot landed immediately to avoid an imminent engine failure over a populated area, noting significant oil loss and black smoke.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported an engine failure on climbout that resulted in a successful return to the field.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss and severe vibration at 1,000 ft after takeoff, caused by a #1 cylinder head temperature pegged in the red. The crew executed a return landing on Runway YY, secured the engine, and egressed while awaiting fire support.

synopsis: BE58 pilot reported a nose and main gear collapse during rollout from a normal landing.
summary: The aircraft's nose and main gears collapsed after touchdown, causing it to slide off the runway into grass. No injuries occurred, but the aircraft damaged one REIL.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported an airspace violation due to confusion and miscommunication with ATC.
summary: The pilot departed a Class D airport underlying Class C airspace and received conflicting instructions regarding a 2,500-foot climb while remaining clear of the Class C veil. Confusion during clearance relay and the pilot's assumption that the clearance ensured separation caused a potential airspace incursion, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reported departing with the assumption weather would remain the same as the arrival, but ice accumulated unexpectedly during climb.
summary: The pilot encountered unexpected rime icing while climbing to 5,000 feet on an IFR flight plan despite a Zulu forecast. After requesting and receiving clearance to 7,000 feet to break out of clouds, the pilot descended VFR below the clouds to avoid further icing and landed safely.

synopsis: Glasair III pilot reported a wake turbulence encounter departing LNC with a B737 inbound to another airport. Reporter expressed concern that his NavWorx TIS-B unit did not alert him to the traffic.
summary: A pilot climbing through 3,000 ft MSL after takeoff encountered a B737 at approximately 3,500 ft MSL while rolling out on course. The pilot executed evasive action after the NavWorx ADS-B TIS-B failed to alert, resulting in a near-loss of control due to the jet's wake turbulence.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported returning to the departure airport twice after experiencing a compressor stall shortly after both takeoffs.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud bangs and shuddering shortly after 500ft on two heavy weight departures, initially suspecting structural damage but later identifying severe compressor stalls on engine three. Both incidents resulted in air turnbacks, fuel jettison to 120,000 lbs, and holding at 11,000ft before normal landings, with the second event requiring throttle management to recover the engine.

synopsis: PA28R pilot experienced a failure of the right main gear to lock in position when extended. After landing the gear collapsed.
summary: The right main gear collapsed on landing because it never locked into position despite all attempts to secure it. The incident resulted in minor aircraft damage and no injuries.

synopsis: PRC Local Controller observed an aircraft that had been established on final maneuvered on its own to a base leg position on a conflicting course with downwind traffic.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing a busy pattern reported a near mid-air collision between Aircraft X and Aircraft Z after Aircraft X deviated inside the downwind without notification. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot's failure to advise of the maneuver, which prevented timely traffic advisories.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after both IRS DC fail lights illuminated in cruise.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced dual IRS DC failures and low battery voltage, prompting a precautionary diversion to a nearby alternate. The aircraft landed safely, but the APU failed to start at the gate as predicted by the QRH.

synopsis: An air carrier crew reported confusion caused while flying the ATL WINNG 1 STAR after ATC cleared them for visual approach, uncleared them with a vector then recleared them for the visual.
summary: Pilots flying a visual approach to Atlanta Runway 27L were queried by an Approach Controller after complying with a clearance to cross POSEY at 8000 feet. The Controller canceled the visual clearance due to confusion over the pilots' route, issued a heading and altitude restriction, and later recleared them for the approach, which the reporter attributed to unrealistic ATC expectations.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported diverting to an alternate after experiencing windshear on two consecutive approaches to BWI.
summary: The flight crew encountered windshear twice during visual approaches to BWI, executing a go-around and diverting to an alternate with minimum fuel. The pilot attributed the situation to severe weather and criticized Dispatch for lacking situational awareness and failing to support the diversion decision.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported window visibility issues when flying in heavy rain.
summary: A Boeing 737NG pilot reported inadequate forward visibility during a heavy rain approach due to windshield wipers failing to clear the "sheet of water." The pilot concluded the wipers are unsafe in heavy rain and recommended disallowing approaches in +RA until visibility limitations are tested and resolved.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported receiving a #1 ILS fault then a FLT CNTL FLAP 1 SYS fault and a third GPWS fault. A normal approach and landing ensued.
summary: The crew encountered multiple ECAM faults including ILS, flap control, and GPWS failures during descent below 15,000 feet. They deviated from the QRH by not pulling circuit breakers due to low altitude, landed uneventfully, and swapped aircraft after maintenance found hydraulic fluid leaking from the nosewheel doors.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported returning to the departure airport after a Flight Attendant reported a burning smell in the cabin.
summary: During climb at 4000 MSL, a flight attendant reported a cabin burning smell, prompting the pilot to return for an overweight landing. Fire personnel found no fire source, but the landing caused hot brakes, which were inspected and deemed safe for taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: Captain observed Flight Attendants' non-compliance with company policies and FAR's on several flights as a commuting passenger.
summary: A pilot passenger reported that during moderate turbulence, flight attendants failed to check passenger seat belts or clear the aisle of 14 standing passengers despite the captain's announcement. The reporter fears this lack of cabin monitoring will result in serious injuries and FAA violations.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported executing a go-around after receiving a low altitude alert from the Tower during the Stadium Visual to EWR Runway 29.
summary: The flight crew executing a Stadium Visual approach to Runway 29 at Newark received an altitude alert and obstacle warning due to missing FMC vertical constraints on their Jepp chart. They executed a go-around and landed uneventfully on ILS 22L, attributing the incident to an oversight in reviewing special airport remarks regarding the available RNVV 29- procedure.

synopsis: Two MD11 first officers reported compressor stalls on the number three engine during the first turn on the departure at 500 feet AGL. After dumping 120,000 pounds of fuel the flight returns to the departure airport. The engine was inspected with no anomalies noted. The aircraft was refueled and departed with the same result.
summary: The crew experienced loud bangs and shuddering shortly after 500 ft on two heavy departures, initially suspecting structural damage but later identifying severe compressor stalls on engine three. They executed two air turnbacks with fuel jettison to hold at 11,000 ft, landing safely at maximum weight after the engine recovered.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having some doubts about the accuracy and reliability of weather reporting at MYAM.
summary: The pilot reported inaccurate weather observations at MYAM, leading to a diversion hold and a delayed IFR departure based on a certified observer's unverified report. The incident highlighted risks from the lack of automated weather, radar, and published instrument approach procedures at the uncontrolled field.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported ATC issued a low altitude alert to them on approach into SDF.
summary: The flight crew vectored for ILS 35R at SDF became high and fast, leading to an overspeed warning and low altitude alert after the First Officer looked down to set a frequency. The Captain corrected the deviation and speed, and the aircraft landed normally, though the reporter noted a go-around should have been initiated.

synopsis: A320 Captain experienced a ground conflict with a tug pulling carts requiring a sudden stop of the aircraft. Taxi into the gate was delayed further by the late arrival of the left Wing Walker and his seemingly inability to perform his job according to SOPs.
summary: The pilot emergency stopped the aircraft during gate entry to avoid a speeding tug that failed to yield. Subsequent gridlock occurred because an experienced left wing walker refused to follow standard operating procedures until a ramp manager counseled him.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported clipping a tree on final approach to HPN Runway 29. Darkness and the lack of a VASI were reported as contributing factors.
summary: A solo pilot conducting night stop-and-go practice at KHPN clipped a tree on final approach to Runway 29 due to low altitude, lack of VASI, and displaced threshold. The pilot executed a go-around and landed safely on Runway 34, sustaining aircraft damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Two Cessna 177RG pilots reported a gear up landing due to distraction and lack of checklist usage.
summary: Pilots conducting touch-and-go training in gusty winds experienced intercom failure and task saturation, leading to a missed landing checklist. The aircraft landed with gear up, striking the propeller on the ground, resulting in no injuries but requiring an emergency shutdown.

synopsis: Two Mooney pilots reported a gear up landing for unknown reasons.
summary: The pilot and instructor landed a training aircraft without the gear extended, causing runway scraping and smoke. The cause was attributed to desensitization from prior gear warning horn exposure and distraction by non-standard ATC instructions, resulting in a safe emergency shutdown.

synopsis: T-38 pilot reported he was unable to maintain altitude after one engine failed and was forced to descend through conflicting traffic.
summary: During a Functional Check Flight, a pilot experienced a single engine failure at FL450 and descended after ATC denied requests due to traffic, causing a TCAS Resolution Advisory with an airliner. The engine restarted at lower altitude, and the flight returned to base uneventfully.

synopsis: DA-50 First Officer reported a fueling light illuminated in flight with no apparent abnormalities, however the fueling panel door was found missing upon arrival.
summary: During climb and descent, the flight crew experienced a fueling light at 15,000 feet and a one-minute vibration near 30,000 feet. The crew determined the fuel panel door had departed the aircraft, a finding confirmed upon landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: LAX Tower Local Assist reported releasing an aircraft off SMO. There was a loss of separation between it and a LAX departure.
summary: A Local Assist controller released Aircraft Y from SMO while a second aircraft was airborne, resulting in both being just under 4 miles apart. The controller attributed the loss of separation to assuming the departing aircraft was still taxiing due to a delayed release from Malibu sector.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA ARTCC Controller reported a loss of separation due to an aircraft not descending as fast as the Controller assumed it would.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 27 lost separation between Aircraft X and Y due to high workload, staffing shortages, and fatigue while managing traffic over MAP limits. The controller failed to notice Aircraft X floating through 32,900 feet past Aircraft Y at 32,000 feet, resulting in a conflict that automated alerts did not detect.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain at FL410 heard the aircraft above him request descent and start down without clearance. ATC questioned the descending aircraft and was informed that a flame out had occurred and descent was a necessity. ATC issued a heading to the B737 Captain who was already turning and descending in response to a TCAS RA.
summary: During cruise at FL410, the pilot executed a TCAS RA descent after another aircraft in FL430-450 flamed out and descended without declaring an emergency. The conflict was resolved at FL390, though the pilot noted that an earlier emergency declaration would have prevented the near-miss.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being cleared to depart LGA via the LGA 5 Whitestone climb. The First Officer attempted to fly the Maspeth climb until the Captain and ATC intervened.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed LGA Runway 13 in VNAV mode, but the First Officer followed an incorrect 4.1 DME turn point due to a highlighted error on his iPad. This caused a deviation from the cleared heading, requiring ATC intervention to correct the flight path before entering JFK airspace.

synopsis: A Boeing 737 flight crew reported that a tail stand, used to protect against a tail-tip situation, was not installed by the ground crew in a timely fashion.
summary: The Captain received an ACARS alert regarding a potential tail tip condition on arrival in DEN. After visually confirming the tail stand was not yet in place, the Captain delayed deplaning and kept the seatbelt sign on until the ramp crew positioned the stand, preventing a potential jet bridge collision.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported executing a go-around on final approach after encountering wake turbulence in trail of a heavy B767 that had executed a go-around as well.
summary: Pilots conducting an ILS approach behind a heavy 767 encountered wake turbulence at 900 ft AGL, causing significant rocking and airspeed variations. The crew initiated a go-around to power out of the wake and avoid worsening conditions, resulting in no further significant events.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported hearing his company call, without numbers, after being cleared for takeoff by the Tower. At the time the aircraft was accelerating rapidly and the call could not be clarified before V1 was announced.
summary: During a line check takeoff from ORD Runway 22L, the Captain was distracted by an incomplete tower call and momentarily failed to guard thrust levers while reaching for the FMS. The check airman corrected the error, and the flight continued safely after the controller clarified the intended heading change.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported missing an alternate airport requirement, attributing the error to being ill and not wanting to leave due to a company 'negative attendance' policy.
summary: A flight dispatcher, while ill with a stomach virus, missed adding an alternate airport due to a TAF change before departure. The dispatcher amended the flight plan via ACARS prior to top of climb after calculating fuel requirements for the actual payload.

synopsis: DHC-8-300 flight crew reported that part of the ceiling panel fell during climb.
summary: During initial climbout, a flight attendant reported a cracked sidewall light cover fell on passengers, posing a danger with sharp edges. The flight returned to the departure airport for maintenance to repair the loose cover, which had cracked around the screw holes.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported encountering icing conditions and landed at the nearest airport.
summary: A pilot on a medical mission encountered unexpected windscreen icing during flight, forcing an emergency descent and safe landing. Later, while attempting to reposition the helicopter to a nearby hospital, the pilot observed worsening freezing conditions and ice accumulation on the blades and airframe.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dash-8 Captain reported rejecting takeoff when the number one engine torque began to drop. The flight returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: During the takeoff roll, the First Officer rejected the takeoff at 60 knots after hearing an audible change and observing a left yaw and torque drop on engine 1. The aircraft was taxied off the runway, returned to the gate, and maintenance was notified after both engines appeared normal during taxi.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC-8 Dispatcher reported an aircraft was dispatched after a post maintenance inspection ferry flight that indicated the aircraft needed additional maintenance.
summary: A dispatcher sent an amended release for Flight 5678 with an open maintenance item after selecting "Yes" to a system warning, without consulting maintenance control. Consequently, the aircraft departed for ZZZ2 without the necessary actions to clear it for revenue flying, despite the crew being unaware of the pending maintenance requirements.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported an unexplained decrease in right outer fuel quantity and diverted.
summary: During climbout past 18,000 feet, the crew observed an unexplained decrease in right outer fuel quantity despite following QRH procedures and consulting maintenance. The aircraft diverted and landed exceeding outer tank limits, with fuel continuing to drop on the ground with engines and pumps off.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer landing at LSE received a field conditions report indicating good braking action. The braking action was not good and there was unreported snow on the runway.
summary: The crew encountered unexpected slippery runway conditions with snowdrifts upon landing at LSE due to a FICON report containing outdated data. The station manager admitted to updating old reports with current timestamps without verifying actual field conditions, leading the crew to state they would have diverted had accurate information been available.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported that when asked to set the brakes he turned the handle the wrong way.
summary: During pushback of an Airbus NEO, the captain accidentally released the parking brake while distracted by flight plan input. Although the aircraft did not move because the captain's feet remained on the brake pedals, the ground crew noticed the error and confirmed the situation was safe.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported that a B737 had to return to the gate because of a Reverser fault light.
summary: A mechanic refused an operating manager's demand to perform undocumented Engine Accessory Unit resets on Aircraft X while parked on an active taxiway. The aircraft was subsequently returned to the gate for proper, documented maintenance in accordance with General Maintenance Manual procedures.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported they were late to lower the landCRJ-900 Captain reported being late to lower the landing gear, but elected to land rather than go-around for an unstabilized approach.
summary: The Captain and First Officer failed to lower the landing gear on approach, configuring the aircraft near 1000 feet AGL instead of executing a go-around. They attributed the error to fatigue and complacency after a long day, though the landing occurred without incident.

synopsis: Bonanza pilot reported being distracted by conversation with a passenger and forgot to lower the landing gear.
summary: The pilot, distracted by explaining setup procedures to a passenger pilot during approach, failed to notice the landing gear did not deploy, resulting in a gear-up landing. The gear subsequently deployed after the circuit breaker was reset when the aircraft was raised.

synopsis: SR22T pilot reported the CO2 alarm activated during cruise and he landed as a precaution.
summary: During cruise at 6,500 feet MSL, the pilot experienced intermittent CO2 alarms. After turning the air on and opening vents, the alarm ceased, prompting a precautionary landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: LAX Tower Controller reported of a loss of separation when a SMO departure was too close to an LAX departure.
summary: Local Assist 2 controller released SMO departure Aircraft Y while Aircraft X was on takeoff roll, resulting in 2.75 miles separation. The controller attributed the reduced spacing to Aircraft Y accelerating quickly and Aircraft X climbing slowly, though subsequent departures maintained adequate separation.

synopsis: C90 TRACON Controller reported while providing On the Job Training Instruction, an aircraft did not turn as instructed. The developmental turned the aircraft to a different heading and complicated matters, which led to the loss of separation.
summary: During an OJTI, a trainee controller issued conflicting headings to Aircraft X and Y, while Aircraft X deviated due to incorrect FMS programming. The supervising controller intervened to separate the aircraft, and the pilot later confirmed the deviation caused by navigating to the wrong waypoint.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the field conditions and PIREP at PVD did not accurately portray the braking action he encountered.
summary: A Boeing 757 pilot reported medium braking action during landing at PVD in 1/2 mile visibility with thin snow, despite a previous report of good braking. The pilot noted the aircraft slowed gradually despite full brake application and requested an analysis of brake pressure data and RCAM usage standards.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the Number 1 left slat transit light was illuminated although the slat appeared to be extended. The trailing edge flaps could not be extended beyond 25 degrees and the approach was continued to landing.
summary: The crew experienced a false LE FLAPS TRANSIT light and slat indication during a visual approach, with trailing edge flaps failing to extend to 30. They landed safely with flaps 25 after confirming the leading edges were physically extended and the aircraft was stabilized.

synopsis: Air carrier Load Planner reporting receiving an 8,340 lbs revision (1.74% of TOGW) after the affected flight had been airborne for two hours.
summary: Load Planning corrected an 8,340 lb weight error two hours after takeoff due to a cargo system constraint preventing data transfer. The final loading documents were updated after the help desk forwarded the airway bill, resulting in a 1.74% change to the original takeoff weight.

synopsis: Ground personnel and a Captain of a B737 reported that the tow bar got disconnected without the brakes being set.
summary: During a pushback, a tow driver signaled to move the aircraft forward, but wing-walkers misinterpreted the signal and disconnected the tow bar, causing the aircraft to roll. The driver instructed the captain to set brakes, stopping the aircraft without damage or injury.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a heading deviation when they accepted a clearance for another flight with a similar call sign.
summary: The flight crew departing OAK on runway 30 mistakenly set FL190 after hearing a similar call sign respond to a clearance. Confusion caused by similar flight numbers and a busy frequency led to a dual input, but the crew corrected the aircraft to heading 270 and 10,000 feet.

synopsis: G-IV flight crew was chastised for exceeding their cleared altitude by ATC during departure. Upon arrival at their destination ATC advised that the mistake was made by Clearance Delivery.
summary: The flight crew received a clearance from Clearance Delivery to climb and maintain 10,000 feet, but Departure ATC initially suspected a pilot deviation because they believed the assigned altitude was 5,000 feet. ATC later admitted the error was on their end, confirming no pilot deviation occurred as the controller had incorrectly issued the initial altitude.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported a primary flaps failure and ran the appropriate checklist. They opted to deviate from the checklist and land with more flaps than the checklist dictated.
summary: During a night arrival at ZZZ, the crew received a 'PRIMARY FLAPS FAIL' alert while configuring for Runway XXL. The Pilot Monitoring elected to continue the stabilized approach with flaps 30 and gear down, citing heavy traffic and sufficient go-around performance, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported mistakenly turning onto Taxiway Golf from Alpha towards a construction area during night operations.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of an aircraft taxiing at CLT mistakenly turned onto Taxiway Golf instead of Charlie due to unfamiliarity, poor lighting, and a confusing diagram. They aborted a 180-degree turn in a construction zone and required a follow-me vehicle to reach Runway 18L.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer and D10 TRACON Controller reported that a clearance to descend was given, but due to a congested radio frequency the instruction was misunderstood.
summary: A pilot and controller at DFW experienced blocked transmissions and altitude confusion during a busy arrival, causing Aircraft X Heavy to hold at 11,000 feet. The controller subsequently vectored the aircraft to avoid climbing traffic, resulting in a 2.8-mile separation and zig-zagging maneuvers attributed to frequency congestion and poor southeast radio reception.

synopsis: A B767 Captain reported receiving a late runway change for the ILS on a parallel runway. The Captain was unstable on approach, but elected to continue landing due to the potential conflict with a departing aircraft if they would have gone around.
summary: The crew received a late runway change from an overtasked arrival controller while high on the ILS 4L profile, causing a scramble to configure. They continued the approach despite being fast at 500 feet due to a departing aircraft, landing safely after stabilizing on short final.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported commencing a low altitude go-around, but when the main gear touched the ground the Captain pulled the power levers back and performed the landing.
summary: The First Officer hand-flew a visual approach to RWY 22, prematurely shallow-out below 100 feet AGL, causing a main gear touchdown during a go-around attempt. The Captain aborted the go-around, landed safely, and attributed the hard landing to the First Officer's inadequate instrument scan as a new turbo-jet pilot.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician working on a Bombardier CRJ-700 reported that the steering tiller was installed incorrectly.
summary: A mechanic installed the captain's steering tiller backwards on a CRJ-700 in the hangar, an error missed during the operations check because the tiller design allowed correct nose wheel response regardless of orientation. The mechanic attributed the mistake to complacency and a failure to double-check the installation orientation despite having the manual available.

synopsis: The First Officer of an Airbus A320 reported they were issued a proper clearance, but asked for clarification to ensure the proper altitude.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ queried a departure controller regarding a "climb via" clearance to confirm the top altitude was 16,000 feet. The controller verified the altitude, but the pilot noted that including the specific altitude in the initial clearance would reduce confusion and radio congestion.

synopsis: A Flight Instructor in a Cessna 172 reported that they took-off with the tow bar still attached.
summary: A flight instructor left a tow bar attached to a Cessna during preflight due to rushing in cold, dark conditions while waiting for a student. The bar detached during takeoff and landed on the runway, but maintenance confirmed no aircraft damage occurred.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 172 reported a near collision while flying under foggles.
summary: A student pilot under foggles during an ILS approach at a non-towered airport experienced a near collision with another aircraft. The incident occurred because the safety pilot failed to monitor traffic, resulting in a close call resolved only after the student removed foggles and the other aircraft turned away.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported extreme downdrafts in the vicinity of JLI VOR.
summary: A pilot and student flying IFR on V460 encountered severe mountain wave downdrafts, descending from 10,000 to 7,000 feet despite ATC vectoring. The incident was caused by unforecast turbulence associated with strong winds, which the pilot attributed to relying on online briefings and IFR charts lacking specific turbulence warnings.

synopsis: Light sport aircraft pilot reported a runway excursion during takeoff roll.
summary: A pilot practicing touch-and-gos at Centennial Airport veered off Runway 17R during takeoff due to sudden wind shifts from 110 to 310 degrees. The reporter attributes the instability and hard stop in the grass to the rapid wind change while ATC had not yet switched the traffic pattern to Runway 35R.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: General Aviation pilot reported a runway incursion resulted at STS airport due to the lack of familiarity with the airport and a miscommunication with Ground Control.
summary: A pilot training a developmental controller misinterpreted a taxi clearance to the Runway 14/20 run-up area as authorization to cross the Runway 20 approach hold zone. This unauthorized incursion, caused by pilot unfamiliarity with the airport layout, resulted in a Brasher warning from Local Control.

synopsis: C208B flight crew reported a NMAC shortly after takeoff when they took a takeoff clearance meant for another aircraft with a similar call sign.
summary: The pilot mistakenly believed they were cleared for takeoff while taxiing and initiated a roll, but Tower instructed a left turn upon seeing a converging air carrier aircraft. The pilot attributed the error to mishearing the clearance during the checklist, the controller failing to correct the readback, and similar flight numbers.

synopsis: Pilot conducting aerial survey work in a single engine aircraft reported an in-flight event of partial power loss resulting in a forced landing at a nearby airport. Additionally the landing gear would not extend and with no ability to troubleshoot resulted in a gear up landing.
summary: The pilot and sensor operator experienced a progressive engine power loss during aerial survey operations, leading to a forced belly landing at ZZZ. The landing gear failed to extend due to insufficient power for a go-around, but both occupants evacuated uninjured after skidding to a stop on the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: AFW Tower Controller reported not observing an aircraft that turned base late until it was in conflict with a strain in traffic. After a go around, the Controller forgot he had cleared the same aircraft to land and did not notice it on short final when he cleared an aircraft for takeoff.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing complex traffic on Runway 16R lost visual contact with Aircraft X, which deviated from downwind instructions and turned hard base. This caused Aircraft X to execute a go-around just as Aircraft Y began its takeoff roll, an outcome the controller attributed to position fatigue and drift.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported being issued an unsatisfactory performance report by their supervisor, but feels they did nothing wrong.
summary: An approach controller sequenced an IFR arrival and four military VFR aircraft, but a local controller in training issued a conflicting heading of 010 degrees that created a potential conflict. The reporter disputes the supervisor's finding of unsafe operations, attributing the incident to the local controller's error rather than the approach clearance.

synopsis: Captain of B737 reported the lack of visual cues needed to safely park the aircraft in the presence of close proximity ground equipment and material.
summary: A pilot taxiing at FLL stopped due to parked equipment near a construction fence lacking wing clearance markings. After requesting and receiving wing walkers, the aircraft safely entered the gate, though the pilot warned that the lack of painted lines or equipment removal could cause future incidents.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a complete loss of GPS signal in the vicinity of Manila (RPLL). This anomaly was observed both during the arrival and subsequent departure to the airport and was not mentioned in neither the NOTAM nor ATIS information.
summary: The crew experienced complete GPS signal loss during takeoff from RPLL until crossing the coast and again while crossing the coast en route to RPLL. The reporter noted no relevant information was available in NOTAMs or the RPLL ATIS.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported experiencing gusty wind conditions which necessitated a go-around followed by a successful second approach and landing.
summary: Pilots on an ILS 34L approach to RJAA encountered performance-increasing wind shear and a flap discrepancy where the handle was at 30 degrees but indicated 25 degrees. A GPWS "Too low, terrain" warning prompted an immediate go-around, followed by a successful second landing after declaring minimum fuel.

synopsis: A B767-300 pilot reported that center tank fuel was used primarily by the right engine leaving the amount of fuel in the wing tanks unbalanced.
summary: The pilot reported that during cruise at FL340, a Fuel Config EICAS message indicated all center tank fuel was consumed by the right engine despite both pumps being on. The crew balanced the fuel, the flight continued normally, and the system was logged.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported returning to departure airport when the landing gear failed to retract following the loss of hydraulic system 1 shortly after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear retraction failure and a Hyd Sys 1 Fail caution after departure. They manually extended the gear using checklists and safely returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: ERJ-170 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing a WOW (Weight on Wheels) system failure on gear retraction.
summary: During pre-departure, the crew sheared a tow bar shear pin while pushing back. After takeoff, a Landing Gear Weight on Wheels system failure prompted an immediate return, soft landing, and tow to the gate, where a sharp turn by the tug triggered a steering failure message.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light Transport flight crew reported experiencing communication issues with Miami Center and Nassau Approach. Flight crew elected to divert due to departing traffic from the original destination and the inability of the ZMA Controller to give them a missed approach clearance.
summary: The crew lost two-way communications with Miami Center and Nassau Approach while descending to 3000 ft near MYAM due to intermittent radio coverage. They climbed VFR to 7500 ft to avoid TCAS traffic and re-establish contact, eventually diverting to MYGF after Miami issued new clearance instructions.

synopsis: The Captain of a Falcon 2000 reported that many write-ups were sign-off but never repaired by Maintenance.
summary: A pilot reported that a maintenance vendor failed to fix four inoperative cockpit lights and three fuel-leaking screws on a Falcon 2000, despite signing the aircraft airworthy. The pilot suspects cost concerns caused the initial neglect and requested the vendor be removed from working on the aircraft.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: C680 Pilot reported having issues with the FMS while flying a STAR requiring a large turn and altitude restriction.
summary: The crew flying an arrival into DAL via the JFRYE3, NUKLZ transition experienced an unusually wide left turn past GREGS while on autopilot. ATC queried the deviation and assigned a southerly heading to exit unprotected airspace, prompting a post-flight discussion with Center.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported he was assigned to an acceptance flight following multiple writeups for fumes in the cockpit that neither he nor the Captain were comfortable accepting, given the oxygen limitations involved.
summary: A reserve pilot and Captain cancelled a maintenance acceptance flight for an aircraft with four recent cabin fume write-ups. They determined insufficient oxygen existed for four occupants to wear masks at 100% during the planned 30,000-foot flight, and the Captain refused to conduct the test as unqualified line pilots.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported the flying First Officer responded to a 'level off' RA by climbing several hundred feet.
summary: While being vectored at 4,000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA to level off due to unidentified VFR traffic climbing from 3,500 feet. The First Officer manually climbed 200–300 feet to comply, notified Approach, and returned to the assigned altitude with no further incident.

synopsis: C130 Instructor Pilot reported they landed on the wrong runway when they experienced dual compass malfunction.
summary: The PIC and student pilots landed on the wrong runway due to a drifting primary compass that caused incorrect heading indications. Although cleared for Runway XY, the crew mistakenly aligned with and landed on Runway XZ, but no safety issues occurred because of visual conditions and tower flexibility.

synopsis: Medium Large Transport First Officer reported flying outside the boundaries of the training area during a flight test.
summary: During a flight loads survey test at FL330-360, the test aircraft exited the Training Area northern border while recovering from a high-speed sideslip maneuver. The violation resulted from rapid boundary approach due to high speed and strong winds, compounded by reduced flight deck communication caused by an activated high-speed warning.

synopsis: G650 Captain reported overshooting their level off at 25,000 feet and received a RA for a climbing aircraft.
summary: The flight crew descended at 1,600 ft/min to reach 25,000 ft but delayed reducing the rate, triggering a TCAS RA for a 300 ft climb. The crew observed the traffic on the TRFC and determined it was not a factor.

synopsis: ZLA Controller reported a pilot deviation descending from an assigned altitude, which resulted in being in conflict with climbing traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X and Y near LAX, where Aircraft X descended below assigned altitudes and failed to respond to traffic calls. The controller attributed the loss of separation to the pilot's repeated failure to comply with clearances and lack of communication.

synopsis: ZLA Controller and helicopter pilot reported of incorrect information which led to an airspace deviation. The Controller had advised the pilot that the restricted airspace was inactive, approved the flight through the airspace when the airspace was actually active.
summary: A helicopter pilot received clearance from LA Center to transit restricted area R-2510, which the controller incorrectly reported as inactive due to a system display error. The pilot encountered four fighter jets performing aerobatics within the active airspace, climbed to 3,000 MSL for separation, and was later cleared of fault after the controller admitted the schedule conflict.

synopsis: S56 TRACON Controller reported an A320 on a vector to intercept a Localizer flew through the Localizer course placing the aircraft below the MVA.
summary: Air Traffic Control issued a heading to Aircraft X, which overshot and descended below the 110-foot minimum vectoring altitude. Although the instructor intervened to reintercept the localizer, the aircraft continued descending below the MVA while in a 30-degree bank.

synopsis: ZMP Controller reported of a pilot deviation. Pilot read back correct altitude to descend to but went through the cleared altitude. No Separation was lost due to the descent rate of the deviating aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent to FL370 for Aircraft X, but the pilot descended to FL270, violating airspace and passing through traffic at FL360 and FL350. The controller attributed the incident to a pilot deviation and a delayed reaction, noting that no separation was lost despite the potential for TCAS alerts.

synopsis: TWF Approach controllers approved an aircraft entering their airspace at an altitude below their Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An approach controller cleared Aircraft X to cross GABBY at 9,000 feet for an ILS approach after ZLC coordination, despite a local 9,500-foot Minimum IFR Altitude and a Letter of Agreement requiring 11,000 feet. The incident highlighted conflicting minimum altitude charts between facilities and a reliance on Center requests over local safety constraints.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a track deviation occurred when the First Officer had difficulty interpreting the new flight director's guidance.
summary: The First Officer overshot the assigned departure heading by 70 degrees due to confusion with a new flight director interface, requiring the Captain to take control and level off at 3000 feet. The incident was caused by the First Officer's lack of familiarity with the new cross-hairs display, which replaced the previous chevron guidance.

synopsis: The flight crew of an Airbus A320 reported they noticed a Number 2 Eng Fire push button light illuminated on the overhead panel. No other indications of a fire.
summary: During cruise, the Captain and First Officer experienced intermittent Engine 2 and Engine 1 fire warning lights without ECAM indications. Suspecting a detection system failure, the Captain used emergency authority to disregard maintenance guidance, kept both engines running, and diverted to land normally at ZZZ.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported missing a crossing restriction on arrival into ORD, citing fatigue, strong tailwinds, and automation dependency as factors.
summary: The crew descended into ORD on the BENKY 4 RNAV STAR with high tailwinds and a direct clearance, causing an unexpected speed increase and a high crossing of BENKY at 13,000 ft instead of 12,000 ft. The pilot attributed the deviation to reduced descent distance and noted ATC did not comment on the altitude violation.

synopsis: Captain reported that EWR policy has changed to tolerate departures with tailwind conditions even when braking action reports are present.
summary: A pilot reported operating departures from runway 22 at EWR in light snow with sustained tailwinds of 5 to 7 knots. The pilot noted this recent runway configuration reduces safety margins and requested an explanation for the change, as no specific reason was provided.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an event of changing visibilities late in the approach from VMC to IMC with the field and runway in sight throughout the approach and landing.
summary: The crew lost Approach contact due to a stuck microphone on final to Runway 34L and switched to Tower for a visual approach. When Tower reported visibility dropping to 2 miles, the crew continued landing with the runway in sight, despite the 1000-foot and 3-mile requirement for the visual approach.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported they returned to departure airport after flight attendants reported a strong burning odor in the cabin.
summary: Pilots and a flight attendant reported a strong electric fire odor and screams from the cabin just after rotation, though no flames or flight deck warnings were observed. The crew returned to the departure airport, coordinated with fire/rescue, and landed uneventfully after the odor subsided and no abnormalities were found.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported executing a go-around after receiving a 'Too low terrain' alert on short final at RJAA.
summary: Pilots on approach to RJAA for ILS 34L encountered performance-increasing wind shear and a flap discrepancy where the handle was at 30 degrees but indicated 25. A "Too low terrain" GPWS warning prompted an immediate go-around, though the subsequent approach and landing were uneventful.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing landing gear retraction issues related to low fluid quantity in the left hydraulic system.
summary: The crew experienced a persistent 'Gear Doors' EICAS message and 'DOORS' light after takeoff, followed by a decreasing left hydraulic quantity indication. They returned to the departure airport and executed an uneventful overweight landing after consulting maintenance and completing QRH checklists.

synopsis: Ground operations reported a significant increase in cargo for a flight just before departure.
summary: Station personnel requested a flight unlock to add cargo, claiming 1,800 lbs, but an estimated 24,000 lbs was added instead. This discrepancy occurred during ground operations due to a significant error in the reported weight.

synopsis: A Captain of a Bombardier CRJ-700 reported that the entire overhead panel was completely dark.
summary: During the arrival phase, the flight crew discovered the entire overhead panel was dark due to a technician incorrectly applying an MEL that permitted night flight. A ground technician in ZZZ repaired the lighting system in ten minutes, though the crew noted the error could have caused dire consequences during a night emergency.

synopsis: BE-400 Flight Crew reported an Status Data Unit error message followed by intermittent PFD and Navigational Display failures on both the Captain and First Officer's displays.
summary: The crew experienced Flight Director and MAG flags during taxi, followed by intermittent Status Display Unit failures during climb. They returned to ZZZ for a normal landing, where maintenance advised a shutdown and reset that cleared the indications.

synopsis: Captain reported a violently ill passenger who was unable to move out of the restroom for the entire flight including the landing.
summary: During cruise on a Boeing 737, a pilot managed a passenger with severe food poisoning confined to the forward lavatory. The crew used Infectious Control Kits to contain the mess and deviated from SOP to keep the passenger in the lavatory for landing, where EMTs met the aircraft to assist deplaning.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a possible aircraft volcanic ash encounter during night cruise.
summary: The dispatcher and captain operated a night flight to SJO despite a nearby VASH SIGMET, relying on multiple ATC and PIREP checks confirming clear conditions. The captain reported a possible ash encounter northwest of the field after landing, though he remained unsure, leading the dispatcher to notify maintenance.

synopsis: Air carrier Ground Operations employee reported that unqualified personnel were assigned to air-start an aircraft resulting in extreme risk to personnel and equipment.
summary: Local management assigned unqualified personnel to perform an air-start on an aircraft with an inoperative APU. Confusion arose when the flight deck started engine 2 instead of the required engine 1, placing an agent dangerously close to the running engine while disconnecting the airstart unit.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported attempting to reconfigure their aircraft after receiving and ATC directed go-around, initially climbed into a 'monitor vertical speed' TCAS Resolution Advisory.
summary: Pilots on an LAX ILS 24R approach experienced ambiguous ATC instructions and task saturation, leading to a confused "half go-around" and autopilot disconnect. This resulted in a Resolution Advisory climb of approximately 100 feet, which was resolved before the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported that after a windshear encounter and go-around, it was discovered that the First Officer had calculated 'ice speeds' rather than normal speeds due to a miscommunication.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a windshear caution during final approach due to the aircraft being incorrectly configured for ice speeds without an EICAS message. The First Officer misunderstood the Captain's precautionary request, resulting in high approach speeds and a go-around before a successful second landing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported encountering a terrain warning at night on approach to BTV and took evasive action.
summary: The crew received an EGPWS 'PULL UP' warning at 5,500ft near JANUD and climbed to 7,500ft. ATC stated the Minimum Vectoring Altitude was 5,300ft and attributed the false warning to known system occurrences before clearing the approach.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported they got EICAS messages for Number 1 and Number 2 ENG BLEED LEAK.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X experienced dual engine bleed leak EICAS messages during climb from ZZZ. They executed QRH procedures, returned to ZZZ for a normal landing, and swapped aircraft, attributing the issue to frequent pack and bleed problems on the E145 fleet.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported while descending the preselected altitude was never captured and the aircraft started climbing.
summary: During a visual approach vector, the crew failed to notice the Flight Mode Annunciator switching to pitch mode, causing an unintended climb 900 ft above the assigned 3000 ft and significant airspeed decay. The pilots corrected the climb by adding thrust and descending back to altitude after ATC queried the deviation.

synopsis: Air carrier Relief Pilot reported descending to 2200 feet after being cleared for the CYHM ILS Runway 12 direct APGOM. Pilot cited confusion as to the allowable minimum no procedure turn (NoPT) altitude and noted a disparity between the ILS Runway 12 NoPT (2200 feet) and ILS CAT II Runway 12 NoPT (2700 feet) altitudes.
summary: An additional crewmember on a flight to CYHM reported that the aircraft descended to 2200 ft instead of the required 2700 ft MSA while cleared to the APGOM fix for an ILS approach. The reporter attributed this altitude deviation to ambiguous approach plate design regarding minimum altitudes for the No-PT routing versus the MSA.

synopsis: SA-227AC pilot reported rejecting the takeoff after the left and right generator fail lights illuminated.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff after both generator fail lights illuminated three to four seconds after advancing power levers. Unable to re-engage the left generator during troubleshooting, the pilot returned to parking.

synopsis: NKT TRACON Controller reported an ATCAA (Air Traffic Control Assigned Airspace) activated even though there was an aircraft within the airspace.
summary: Approach East and West managed Aircraft X and Y on conflicting courses while Approach North activated the Burner ATCAA without coordination. This unauthorized activation occurred while Aircraft X penetrated the airspace, violating procedures and creating an unsafe situation despite no loss of separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An Ercoupe 415 pilot reported that the fuel indicator for the header tank indicated he was losing fuel.
summary: The pilot of an Ercoupe en route to ZZZ reported a descending header tank sight gauge, prompting a diversion to ZZZ2 due to fear of fuel exhaustion. Post-flight inspection revealed normal fuel levels and operation, leading the pilot to conclude the issue was an unexplained anomaly in the sight gauge float rather than a fuel transfer failure.

synopsis: PA-28 student pilot reported a loss of directional control on landing that resulted in a runway excursion and damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing, an early flare caused oscillation and a tail-first touchdown, leading to a loss of directional control. The aircraft fishtailed off the runway onto a taxiway, resulting in a collapsed nose wheel and propeller ground strike.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-46 found that the elevator was very stiff to operate and got stiffer during flight.
summary: The pilot reported stiff elevator controls during the climb in cold weather, worsening to the point of requiring an immediate landing. Piper suggested the cause was a frozen plastic roller within the control column, which later became immovable from the outside.

synopsis: C172 instructor reported a loss of control during taxi with high winds resulting in flipping over into a snow bank.
summary: The pilot reported that during a crosswind landing and taxi transition, a gust lifted the wing and pushed the aircraft into a snowbank. Loss of directional control caused the nose to dig in and the aircraft to flip onto its back, attributed to insufficient control input and lack of planning.

synopsis: Smyth Sidewinder pilot reported losing directional control on the landing roll, departed the runway, and struck a sign.
summary: The pilot flew an experimental Smyth Sidewinder during a purchase evaluation in gusty winds. Upon touchdown in light turbulence, the aircraft veered sharply left despite full right rudder and braking, resulting in a collision with a runway sign.

synopsis: PC-12 flight crew reported during climb they encountered ice when an amber caption denoting a failure of the deice system came on.
summary: During an IFR departure in icing conditions, the crew encountered a pneumatic de-ice boot failure at 8,500 feet MSL. They diverted to ZZZ1, descended to VMC, and executed a no-flap landing with no further assistance required.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC with parachutists in a known jump zone near MZJ.
summary: The pilot flying a high-speed aircraft on autopilot in a known parachuting area mistook skydivers for birds or balloons. The close encounter occurred because the pilot did not recognize the jumpers until too late, attributing the event to unfamiliarity with the autopilot system and the difficulty of spotting free-fallers at speed.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: SEE Local Controller and the involved pilots reported of confusion and an airborne conflict while on a circling approach.
summary: An air traffic controller and pilot of Aircraft X experienced a near-miss during a LOC circling approach to Runway 27R when the pilot mistakenly turned west, expecting a different runway. This deviation brought Aircraft X within 1.4 NM and 700 feet of an uncontrolled aircraft on an ILS approach, caused by the pilot's misunderstanding of local circling procedures.

synopsis: A Center Controller received aircraft from a sector that were issued direct to fixes off their assigned RNAV routes.
summary: A Sector 52 controller shortcut Aircraft X and Y to waypoints in the reporter's airspace, removing RNAV STAR altitude restrictions and creating a conflict. This forced the reporter to issue four separate altitude and speed clearances instead of one efficient descent clearance, increasing workload and reducing efficiency.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported an oil leak in flight that required them to divert.
summary: The crew of a flight at FL330 experienced a rapid oil leak in engine one, dropping from 98% to 10% while en route to ZZZZ. They executed a successful two-engine landing with flaps 15, and post-landing motoring confirmed a large leak from the accessory gear box.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported being directed onto the B737-800 parking spot which resulted in a close encounter with a jetway.
summary: During dark, wet taxiing to the gate, a 737-800 crew stopped to avoid a deice truck and APU in the safety zone before stopping eight feet past the line. The agent moved the jetway to avoid a one-foot clearance with the nacelle, and the supervisor attributed the incident to newly trained ground crew being paired too soon.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that during engine start ground personnel advised that fuel was leaking from the APU fuel drain.
summary: The Captain and First Officer observed APU fuel dripping at ZZZ before pushback and during engine start, initially accepting Maintenance Control's advice that it was normal. They later MEL'd the APU after landing, admitting they should have deferred it earlier due to expectation bias and a lack of clear manual guidance on acceptable drain limits.

synopsis: B737 Flight crew reported that ATC had to correct their route shortly after departure. Crew reported it was an issue with the Pre-Departure Clearance form of Clearance Delivery.
summary: The crew received a PDC with an amended routing but missed the change, causing the FMC to lack the HAWKN fix. Departure Control clarified the clearance source and issued a direct routing to HAWKN and ROBBY, which the crew loaded to proceed.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported that the company MELs contain excessive data on unrelated conditions or data pertinent to other aircraft models.
summary: A pilot on a -700 aircraft found a center boost pump Low Pressure light remained on during preflight. The pilot reported the MEL system was unsatisfactory because it provided six pages of non-pertinent data instead of specific guidance for the inoperative pump with fuel in the tank.

synopsis: Boeing 737 flight crew reported their electric elevator trim system failed after takeoff. They ran the checklist and returned to land at departure airport using the manual trim instead.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, the crew experienced a total loss of electric stabilizer trim on the aircraft. After cycling the circuit breaker with maintenance authorization, trim function recovered, but the crew returned to the origin airport due to fuel constraints and landed normally.

synopsis: The Captain of a B777 reported after landing, just prior to arriving at gate he received a report of loud banging noise and electrical smell in the aft cabin area.
summary: After landing and prior to gate arrival, the aft cabin crew reported a loud banging noise, electrical odor, and reduced visibility from insulation particles near rows 41-43. Ground Fire Rescue was dispatched as a precautionary measure to meet the aircraft at the gate.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported confusion due to a stepped on transmission from ATC. When they queried ATC, the Controller responded unprofessionally.
summary: The pilot reported that during the approach to runway 19R at SFO, a tower controller responded unprofessionally when the crew clarified a blocked call sign. The controller eventually issued a condescending clearance, prompting the pilot to file a formal complaint with the tower supervisor regarding the communication failure.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported they lost the #3 hydraulic system during flight.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid loss of Hydraulic System 3 fluid during climb, triggering multiple warnings and a system failure message. They continued to ZZZ, performed a manual gear extension, and landed safely before being towed to the ramp due to limited steering and a hydraulic spill.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported an outboard spoilers malfunction that caused an uncommanded roll, QRH procedures were followed and aircraft made a successful landing.
summary: During descent, the First Officer extended flight spoilers, causing an uncommanded roll and OB SPOILERONS/FLT SPOILERS cautions due to a jammed PCU. The crew landed safely on the longest runway with no injuries, then reset the circuit breaker to return the aircraft to service.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported a cockpit side window shattered at cruise altitude.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the Captain's left windshield shattered, prompting an immediate descent and diversion to ZZZ. The crew managed the emergency and landed safely, though the cause remained unknown and subsequent crew scheduling failures caused fatigue.

synopsis: The flight crew of an Airbus A321 reported they had a tail strike after landing.
summary: The Captain flew a normal visual approach and landing, but the aircraft bounced on touchdown. Although the pilot felt no abnormalities, a tail strike subsequently occurred.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported they operated an aircraft that had a tail strike two flights previous to their flight.
summary: The pilot reported that a tail strike occurred two flights prior, which was missed during the inbound flight and their preflight walk-around at ZZZ. The pilot attributed the oversight to misinterpreting the tail skid's condition and confusing normal fluid marks with actual damage.

synopsis: B737-800 Crew reported they operated an aircraft that had a tail strike prior to their flight.
summary: The pilot reported a possible tail strike on the previous leg into ZZZ but found no visible damage during a walk-around, noting only oil streaking. The subsequent flight to ZZZ1 with 26,000 motor and flaps 5 was normal, though the pilot suspects cleaning the belly might have revealed tail strut damage.

synopsis: A Ramp Agent reported that two separate aircraft experienced near misses with ground handling equipment on the apron because of NIL braking. The airport authority had issued a Field Conditions (FICON) report for the apron indicating dry snow over packed snow with braking action poor.
summary: Two aircraft taxiing on an apron with unreported ice and dry snow experienced locked brakes and near misses with ground equipment due to nil braking action. Ramp personnel signaled emergency engine cuts to stop the aircraft after the airport failed to remove snow or issue accurate field condition reports until pilots reported the actual conditions.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a complete electrical power loss and successful divert landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a total electrical failure at 8,500 feet MSL during cruise after canceling IFR, caused by a broken alternator belt. The pilot diverted to a non-towered airfield using a handheld radio, landed without damage, and recommended using external GPS devices for situational awareness.

synopsis: Cessna 425 pilot reported he encountered severe clear air turbulence on descent to APA on the LARKS8 Arrival.
summary: A Cessna 425 pilot encountered severe clear air turbulence at 12,500 MSL while descending on the LARKS8 arrival to APA, losing altitude and heading control. Denver Approach cleared the aircraft to 8,500 MSL where turbulence abated, resulting in an uneventful landing despite 30-knot gusts.

synopsis: Great Lakes instructor pilot reported the tail wheel tire blew out which caused a runway departure and ground loop. No damage.
summary: During a training flight landing, the tail wheel tire blew out below 20 knots, causing a left swerve, runway departure, and ground loop. The pilot reported no damage to the aircraft or property and taxied back to the hangar without Tower intervention.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported he flew into a POTUS TFR and was intercepted.
summary: The pilot miscalculated their course while attempting to circumvent the POTUS TFR near PBI, inadvertently entering the restricted airspace. Consequently, the aircraft was intercepted, prompting the pilot to commit to improved route planning and communication with the tower in the future.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: JAC Ramp Agent reported aircraft damage due to contact with a GPU during gate arrival when the flight crew could not stop due to snow and ice on the ramp. Conditions on the ramp were not NOTAM'ed.
summary: A Part 121 carrier skidded 20 feet on a snowy apron, striking a GPU and ingesting a chock due to unassessed conditions and lack of certified friction measuring equipment. The pilot reported NIL braking, prompting the airport authority to upgrade the condition to POOR despite reporting inaccurate snow depths.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ASE TRACON and ZDV ARTCC Controllers reported aircraft FMS databases are programmed incorrectly for the EGE Cottonwood 2 Departure causing aircraft to fly the incorrect departure procedure into confliction with ASE's ILS approach.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft Y incorrectly executed an engine-out departure procedure without an emergency due to FMS programming limitations, creating a conflict with descending Aircraft X. Denver ARTCC and ASE controllers intervened to deconflict the aircraft, resulting in a minimum separation of 3 miles and 300 feet.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU Controller and pilot reported the aircraft was at the wrong altitude due to an incorrect altimeter setting.
summary: A Part 91 pilot descending to 14,000 feet near MSN reported an altitude discrepancy caused by incorrectly setting the altimeter to 30.43 instead of 29.43 due to sun glare and distraction. This error resulted in a 1,000-foot deviation, temporary loss of communications, and a subsequent clearance to maintain 13,000 feet.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU Controller reported of an airspace violation by C90 TRACON.
summary: An air traffic controller in BEARZ observed Aircraft X, a LOT departure, enter their airspace without coordination after CRIBB assigned FL200. The reporter attributed the conflict to C90's lack of awareness regarding adjacent airspace boundaries and failure to use proper coordination procedures.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported they selected final flaps when the GPWS flap warning sounded on a night visual approach.
summary: During a night visual approach, the First Officer and Captain failed to extend flaps to 30 due to task saturation from an unusual interception inside the final approach point. The crew received a "too low flaps" warning at 200–300 feet, corrected the setting, and landed without further incident.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported refusing an aircraft with a history of FCU failures. The FCU was replaced by Maintenance, but failed enroute and the crew elected to divert due to low visibility at their destination.
summary: The crew refused an aircraft with a faulty FCU, but after a replacement, the autopilot failed repeatedly during cruise, forcing a diversion to ZZZ2 for an overweight landing. They later flew a spare aircraft to ZZZ1, completing a CAT2 autoland in heavy snow after resolving multiple dispatch and weight manifest errors.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew did not initially detect that the RNAV PRM Runway 10R Approach to ORD did not list LNAV only minimums, only LNAV/VNAV minimums. The aircraft was capable of LNAV only.
summary: The flight crew at ORD missed that the RNAV PRM 10R approach plate lacked LNAV minimums, incorrectly using LNAV/VNAV minimums instead. They realized this error during post-flight review, attributing it to infrequent RNAV operations and insufficient alertness to the unusual approach.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer and an airline employee reported IOE training was done by a Captain who had not received his certification by the FAA to be a check airman.
summary: A pilot reported that their captain, acting as a check airman for an IOE training flight, was not qualified because he had not received his final FAA check. The pilot was unaware of this disqualification until being advised after the flight.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported a lightning strike during arrival resulting in multiple system anomalies and possible ATC deviations.
summary: During a thunderstorm arrival, lightning struck the aircraft, causing EFIS failure and probe circuit breaker trips while the crew managed a bleed air malfunction. ATC broke the crew off the ILS approach after a large autopilot intercept turn, though the pilots maintained they did not deviate from their clearance.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported the aircraft 'snap-rolled violently' when they encountered wake turbulence inbound to LGA.
summary: The crew experienced a violent snap-roll while inbound to LGA at 18,000 ft, which they attributed to wake turbulence despite no observed traffic. The flight attendant remained uninjured due to the seat belt sign being on, though the pilot noted the potential for injury if passengers had been moving.
