summary: The flight crew executed two go-arounds at LAS while on a visual approach to Runway 25L after ATC sequenced a slower regional jet ahead and issued conflicting vectors. The Captain later reported that the controller's performance was unacceptable for placing a slower aircraft in front of a faster one and failing to provide proper descent vectors.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported encountering severe turbulence in the vicinity of TUL VOR at FL350.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence near a frontal boundary at FL350 east of Tulsa, causing autopilot disconnection, a 500-foot altitude excursion, and a brief overspeed. No injuries occurred as passengers were seated, and the crew descended to FL330 to improve conditions before logging the event.

synopsis: After a tight turn with wind shear in the area, a CRJ-200 First Officer reported that he experienced a stick shaker during approach.
summary: A reserve pilot hand-flew a jet approach into ZZZ in wind shear, activating the stick shaker and EGPWS glideslope warnings due to fixation and lack of proficiency from long breaks. The pilot recovered from the low-speed event but landed long after leveling off in response to the warnings.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported an encounter with a visually handicapped, dog-assisted passenger who refused a window seat thus failing to comply with company aisle obstruction regulations. The passenger voluntarily moved to a window seat after a threatened removal from the flight.
summary: A flight attendant reported a pre-boarding conflict where a passenger with a service dog refused to move from an aisle seat to a window seat to comply with safety regulations regarding aisle obstruction. After a 30-minute delay involving the captain, operations staff, and other passengers, the customer agreed to move, though police were never required to remove him.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported the trailing edge flaps were lowered and made contact with the open engine cowling.
summary: A mechanic performing a hydraulic leak check deployed flaps while an open thrust cowl, left by a second mechanic retrieving parts, interfered with flap transition. The incident occurred due to the mechanic's initial lack of knowledge regarding this interference.

aircraft: Robinson Helicopter; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported a NMAC with another helicopter at T57.
summary: A solo student pilot descending toward helipad T57 received a late traffic alert for a converging aircraft at the same altitude. The pilot climbed to pass overhead with approximately 300 feet vertical separation, attributing the close call to reduced traffic scanning due to low experience and focus on the helipad.

synopsis: C421 pilot reported returning to departure airport after noticing smoke and decreasing oil pressure associated with the right engine.
summary: Following maintenance on the right engine's pushrod seals, a pilot observed smoke and oil streaming from the nacelle during climb. The pilot returned, shut down the engine as a precaution due to decreasing oil pressure, and landed safely before maintenance corrected the issue.

synopsis: UAV Operator reported losing control input to the UAV which crashed in a wooded area.
summary: An unmanned aircraft lost connection and flew away. The report does not specify the phase of flight, personnel involved, or the cause of the connection loss.

synopsis: Two pilots in a PA28 reported they experienced a power loss when they ran a tank dry while engaged in conversation.
summary: The pilot and safety pilot experienced an engine power loss during cruise due to running out of fuel in the left tank, caused by distraction from personal conversation. After switching tanks at 1800ft MSL, the engine resumed normal operation and the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain, flying as a passenger on a B767-300ER, noted that the sun can be reflected off the wing at high latitudes and greatly heat the window shade and nearby fuselage. He suggested that the designers may not be aware of this phenomena.
summary: A passenger and a senior captain observed sunlight reflecting off a flexing B767-300ER wing during a northbound great circle flight, creating a focal point that overheated a window shade and a cell phone. The reporter theorized this concave mirror effect could cause accelerated fatigue or damage to fuselage materials, though no immediate safety incident occurred.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported striking a runway threshold light while practicing short field landings.
summary: During a short field landing practice, the pilot struck a threshold light with the left main tire while rounding out too low. The incident was caused by unanticipated lift loss due to stronger winds at 100 feet, resulting in no aircraft damage but destroying the light.

synopsis: Piper PA-28 flight instructor reported an aborted takeoff due to loss of power.
summary: A CFI candidate and instructor experienced a significant power loss during takeoff roll in a PA-28R-200 after switching fuel tanks. The instructor attributed the event to water contamination in the left tank, recommending against tank changes after runup and emphasizing thorough fuel draining.

synopsis: RV-7 Pilot reported taking off on a formation flight when they had only been cleared to taxi off the runway due to a momentary loss of communication.
summary: The wingman in an RV-7 took off without clearance at KSAF while following a lead RV aircraft that was actually fast-taxiing to return to the hangar. The incident occurred because the pilot misinterpreted the lead's taxi as a takeoff after missing the ground control clearance due to a radio failure.

synopsis: PA-22 pilot reported being unsure about the legality of taking off from a closed airport.
summary: A pilot departed a closed airport marked with yellow 'x's after the event coordinator verbally agreed to pause a kite festival. The pilot executed a short-field takeoff left of centerline to avoid a golf cart on the runway edge, later questioning the legality of the permission received.

synopsis: Cessna 210T pilot reported landing with the nose gear retracted after all efforts to extend it failed.
summary: The pilot experienced a nose gear failure during landing approach after unsuccessful normal and emergency extension attempts. Following practice landings, the pilot executed a controlled landing on the main gears only and exited the aircraft to await emergency crews.

synopsis: EA500 pilot reported multiple system failures in cruise flight that were apparently related to moisture accumulation in the pitot-static system.
summary: During cruise, the pilot experienced conflicting airspeed and altitude indications, autopilot disconnect, and stall warnings caused by moisture in the static system. The crew descended to FL280, manually managed altitude control, and resumed normal flight after the system cleared, prompting a recommendation to cover static ports during precipitation.

synopsis: CL300 Captain reported shutting down the left engine in flight after experiencing vibration and high engine ITT and oil pressure.
summary: The pilot experienced increasing vibration in the aircraft and controls, accompanied by high left engine ITT and oil pressure. The engine 'VIB' light illuminated, prompting the pilot to shut down and secure the left engine.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported that he serviced the rotor brake system on a Bell 206 after it was deferred.
summary: A mechanic serviced the rotor brake reservoir on a Bell 206 while an MEL was active, cutting and reapplying the safety wire per supervisor instructions. The reporter questions if this undocumented maintenance during in-service time constituted an MEL violation, noting the system remained unchanged and the safety was verified by the pilot.

synopsis: Beechcraft King Air F90 pilot reported that while descending from an RNAV Approach MDA he struck a tree branch, executed a go-around, and diverted to a field that was VFR. The pilot observed damage to the right wing.
summary: The pilot experienced a right low fuel pressure light and struck a tree branch during an RNAV approach to Runway XX at ZZZ in marginal visibility. After executing a go-around with inoperative airspeed and radio systems, the pilot diverted to ZZZ1 and landed safely using light gun signals.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC-8 Captain reported an excursion from a snow covered taxiway.
summary: The fatigued pilot taxied a snow-covered aircraft off the unplowed taxiway into grass while multitasking during low-light conditions. The incident resulted in no injuries, with the pilot citing fatigue, complacency, and failure to assess the situation as causal factors.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported landing on Runway 33 at S36 while another aircraft started to taxi into position on Runway 15.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 33 at a non-towered airport nearly collided with a Cessna attempting a tailwind takeoff on Runway 15. The Cessna pilot ignored multiple wind indicators and radio calls, only stopping after the landing pilot warned of the conflict.

synopsis: A Controller working alone on a mid shift reported leaving their radar position to enter a PIREP in to a computer and did not notice an aircraft descending below its assigned altitude below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller working alone issued a descent clearance to Aircraft X, then left the radar scope to log a turbulence PIREP, allowing the aircraft to descend below its assigned 9000 feet. The pilot attributed the error to cockpit workload from turbulence, and the controller noted that leaving the scope to enter the PIREP caused the altitude deviation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Controller reported a VFR aircraft depart an airport that was going to be in confliction with their aircraft on approach so they issued a vector away to the the VFR aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a VFR aircraft departing GYH converging with an aircraft on a practice approach to GMU. The controller coordinated with GYH tower to issue a heading change, resolving the conflict while noting that improved radar displays and lateral VFR departure procedures are needed to prevent future midair collisions.

synopsis: A flight crew and Dispatcher reported that the flight crew were pressured into flying a B737 with inadequate cockpit lighting.
summary: The Captain and First Officer reported that Maintenance and the Chief Pilot bypassed standard procedures to pressure them into flying an aircraft with marginal cockpit lighting under MEL 33-1-XY. This interference disrupted the crew's safety assessment, forcing them to use flashlights for critical instruments while facing glare issues during engine start and taxi.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported they received a GPWS terrain warning on a night visual approach to SFO Runway 19L.
summary: Pilots received a GPWS terrain warning at 3100 feet near BERKS while descending on ATC vectors to intercept the ILS 19L localizer. They executed an escape maneuver, climbed to 5000 feet, and subsequently completed a normal landing after reloading the approach.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported the crew rest bunk area is subject to random noise intrusions in flight that make it difficult to get quality rest.
summary: Pilots reported chronic loud knocking noises in the Pilot Crew Rest Facility that prevented adequate rest and caused fatigue. A Boeing representative suggested the noise was likely caused by oil-canning between the E&E compartment and deck floor due to pressure or temperature differentials.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported exceeding the speed restriction that limits aircraft to 250 knots until 13,000 feet on the ORD2 SID.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently exceeded the 250-knot speed restriction while climbing above 10,000 feet on the ORD2 departure after following flight director commands to accelerate to 300 knots. The violation was discovered only after ATC instructed them to resume normal speed, though the restriction was lifted near 13,000 feet.

synopsis: B737 crew reported a right engine shutdown due to low oil pressure during climb out. Crew reported uneventful recovery to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced low oil pressure on the right engine during climb out from ZZZ, despite recent maintenance for high consumption. They executed non-normal checklists, returned to ZZZ, and landed uneventfully with maintenance coordination.

synopsis: Air Carrier crew reported they received a TERRAIN warning on a night visual approach to runway 3 CHO. Crew reported climbing and made a successful landing.
summary: Pilots approaching CHO runway 3 on a visual approach received a Terrain EGPWS caution while descending to 2600' on the right downwind. The event was caused by misinterpreting the Gordonsville VOR-based MSA location, leading to proximity with terrain and a tower, requiring an immediate climb to 3000'.

synopsis: Flight crew reported ATC alerted them to a track deviation during a hold in the ASE area.
summary: The pilot reported that while ferrying to Aspen at FL310, ATC assigned a non-standard 20-mile leg hold at LOYYD not depicted on Jepp charts, causing confusion and FMS programming errors. The crew eventually cleared direct to Red Table VOR for approach after realizing the controller lacked specific hold details.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate when the weather at destination started to cause missed approaches. The forecast at departure did not require an alternate.
summary: The Captain diverted a flight en route to Palm Springs to Ontario due to airspace saturation and holding that depleted fuel reserves. The diversion was necessary because the flight plan lacked an alternate airport and sufficient hold fuel, though the aircraft landed safely with adequate reserves.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: CRJ First Officer reported catching his sleeve on the flap lever and moving it to the #1 position. He caught the error right away and moved the handle back to zero before the slats started to move.
summary: A pilot in cruise at 320 kts inadvertently moved the flap lever to Flaps 1 when a wristwatch caught on the sleeve. The lever was immediately returned to Flaps 0 before slats extended, resulting in no pitch change or system display, and maintenance was contacted after landing.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported a loss of directional control on landing roll and, despite the Instructor's efforts, the aircraft departed the runway and flipped onto its back.
summary: An instructor and student in a tailwheel aircraft ground looped during rollout after a second landing attempt, nosing over into a snowbank. Despite calm handling and no apparent mechanical failure or excessive control inputs, the cause of the loss of directional control remains unknown.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate aircraft crew reported the FMC did not execute a hold correctly but the crew allowed the aircraft to fly out of protected holding airspace and beyond TRACON radar before ATC intervened.
summary: The flight crew holding at FL220 over Red Table VOR in a Boeing 280 overshot the inbound turn due to suspected FMS automation failure and crew complacency. The controller lost radar contact, issued a vector, and advised the crew of a possible pilot deviation after they continued the outbound leg past the clearance limit.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported researching a planned TFR and believe was successful in avoiding it, but was advised by ATC of a possible pilot deviation.
summary: The pilot departed and landed at RBW while avoiding a 30 NM TFR radius around CHS VORTAC, believing the airport was excluded. ATC later contacted the pilot regarding a possible violation, which the pilot attributed to ambiguous NOTAM wording that mentioned RBW without clarifying its airspace inclusion.

synopsis: C172 Instructor Pilot reported that distraction led to departing on a training flight with the tow bar still in place, resulting in minor damage to the prop.
summary: An instructor and student flew a Cessna 172 with a tow bar still attached to the nose wheel due to distraction during pre-flight. The aircraft completed a full training flight with no major damage except a minor propeller nick, highlighting the need for a post-tow walk-around.

synopsis: A Center controller reported a military aircraft no longer on the frequency turned away from its intended route and toward departure traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X and VFR Aircraft Y during en route climb when Y executed uncoordinated 180-degree turns due to radio issues, causing two close passes over X. The controller issued traffic alerts and altitude restrictions, resulting in a TCAS alert for X, which the controller described as the closest call in their career.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported encountering tubulence so severe he compared it to his previous experience in planned hurricane penetration flights.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence east of the MHZ VOR while climbing from FL280 to FL340, causing violent aircraft movement and 30-knot airspeed deviations. Despite the intensity, no injuries occurred, and the crew completed the flight after the ride smoothed out near FL340.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported rejecting takeoff at approximately 120 kts after experiencing heavy vibrations related to tire failure.
summary: The pilot monitoring rejected takeoff at 120 kts due to heavy vibration and a dull thump before reaching V1 of 153 kts. The aircraft stopped safely with no injuries, but both left main tires failed, requiring passengers to deplane via air stairs.

synopsis: B737NG First Officer reported noticing indications of a malfunctioning FMC, including inconsistent maximum altitude indications.
summary: The flight crew experienced turbulence and FMC altitude anomalies after departing MCO, causing a descent from FL340 to FL268. The issue resolved itself after consulting dispatch and maintenance, with airspeed remaining safely above buffet limits throughout the event.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported overshooting a crossing restriction during the COWBY6 departure from LAS after a TCAS RA with a preceding aircraft distracted the flying First Officer.
summary: During a full-power departure from LAS in strong winds, the crew exceeded the ROPPR crossing altitude restriction due to distraction by a confusing display message and visual separation tasks. The resulting Traffic Alert and brief Resolution Advisory prompted an immediate descent to 7000 feet and ATC notification.

synopsis: Commercial flight crew reported departing ZGSZ on the SIE7W while the clearance was actually the SIE9W. Many distractions during preflight and the language barrier allowed the error to go undetected.
summary: The flight crew departed ZGSZ in a heavy aircraft, inadvertently flying the SIE7W SID instead of the assigned SIE9W due to expectation bias, distractions, and language barriers. ATC detected the deviation shortly after takeoff and issued a heading correction to align the aircraft with the correct route.

synopsis: The flight crew of a Bombardier CRJ-900 reported that they neglected to reduce thrust and passed through the assigned altitude resulted in requiring a turn to avoid traffic.
summary: The First Officer, flying manually in IMC, deviated above 11,000 feet while managing FMS changes and ATC vectors, causing a TCAS alert with another aircraft. The Captain attributed the error to task saturation and distraction from a cabin call regarding weather, compounded by ICS interference and high climb thrust.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew was cleared to descend to FL320 then via the TRUPS3 arrival. The Captain descended through FL320, which was acceptable, but had intended to stop at FL320 and climbed back up. This resulted in an admonishment from ATC.
summary: The pilot descended below a cleared FL320 while setting arrival altitudes, then climbed back to FL320 before switching to VNAV. Air traffic control informed the crew that climbing back to a previously crossed altitude was prohibited, though no traffic conflicts occurred.

synopsis: EMB-170 First Officer detected a strong yawing moment as thrust was advanced for takeoff and called for the reject. The Captain, seeing nothing wrong called for the takeoff to continue. The First Officer advanced the thrust levers, but not to the TOGA detent causing an 'ENG TLA NOT TOGA' message to be displayed and the takeoff rejected.
summary: During takeoff, the First Officer rejected due to an engine 1 N1 split and yaw, but the Captain initially overrode the decision. The crew aborted a second time after receiving a 'TLA NOT TOGA' message caused by improper lever placement, exiting at taxiway E3 and returning to the gate.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 First Officer reported a fuel burn of approximately 2,000 pounds over planned because climb temperatures were between ISA+15 and ISA+25 coupled with ATC delays.
summary: The flight crew experienced high fuel burn during climb and approach due to ISA+15 to ISA+25 temperatures and ATC constraints, including speed restrictions and a 45-mile downwind at ZZZ. These factors caused the aircraft to land just under reserve fuel, though the flight was never in jeopardy.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported climbing to 3000 feet instead of the correct 5000 feet while on climb out from CLE on the OBRLN 4 SID due to a confusing note on the Jeppesen chart.
summary: The crew departed CLE on the OBRLN 4 Departure after setting an incorrect initial altitude of 3,000 feet due to confusing chart boxes for multiple airports. ATC corrected the clearance to 5,000 feet, prompting the pilot to highlight the error and recommend chart changes to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer experienced a loss of hydraulic system fluid and failure of engine pump 1 during climb. The electric pump took over and maintained pressure, but the crew elected to divert to the nearest suitable airport. The QRH called for the electric pump to be turned off with hydraulic quantity low.
summary: During climb, the crew experienced a HYD SYS 1 low quantity and ENG 1 pump failure, prompting a divert to ZZZ. After landing, the system failed under spoiler and brake pressure, requiring a tug tow to the gate due to the mechanical issue.

synopsis: The flight crew of an A321 reported that on final approach they encountered severe turbulence, so they executed a go-around. They had continuous turbulence associated with wind-shear.
summary: The flight crew executing an ILS approach encountered severe wind shear and turbulence, causing autopilot pitch deviations and airspeed fluctuations that necessitated a go-around. The resulting flap/slat overspeed prevented immediate power reduction, leading to a diversion and maintenance log entry.

synopsis: CRJ-900 pilot reported of a final altitude of 8,000 feet for the flight from the New York area to Georgia.
summary: Pilots reported flying a regional jet from New York to Georgia at restricted altitudes of 8,000 and 6,000 feet due to congestion, resulting in two TCAS RAs with general aviation aircraft. The crew attributed the safety risk to ATC assigning low altitudes that placed them in conflict with GA traffic for an extended distance.

synopsis: A C152 pilot reported a partial electrical failure in night conditions and landed at a nearby towered airport without contacting the Tower.
summary: The pilot, flying an unfamiliar aircraft at night shortly after takeoff, experienced a partial electrical failure that disabled cockpit lights and radios. Unable to use navigation aids, the pilot landed at ZZZ airport using city lights and established radio contact with the tower immediately upon arrival without incident.

synopsis: G-550 Captain reported a TCAS RA and NMAC with a PA28 in marginal VFR conditions.
summary: The crew experienced a TCAS RA and Tower traffic advisory while climbing at 1,700 feet MSL after departure due to a PA28 VFR aircraft in rain and low ceilings. The PA28 passed 300 feet off the right wing at 2,100 feet, violating VFR separation rules, before the flight continued uneventfully.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Lafayette Tower Controller and taxiing aircraft pilot reported a runway incursion because the taxiing aircraft went over the hold line.
summary: A pilot taxiing Aircraft X on a closed runway due to construction crossed the hold-short line for Runway 22R while Aircraft Z was landing. The pilot attributed the deviation to non-standard markings, construction distractions, and confusion between holding short of 22L versus 22R, though ground control intervened to prevent a collision.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported the Supervisor was making incorrect computer system entries to combine and de-combine sectors causing confusion.
summary: An air traffic controller working R35 reported that a Front Line Manager's aggressive and experimental sector configuration changes caused airspace assignment errors and communication failures. The controller felt unsafe due to the manager's hostility and inability to resolve the technical issues, ultimately forcing a reversion to the MID configuration.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported ATC assigned a late missed approach heading that was opposite to the published turn direction. The crew was slow to react initially and ATC then assigned a turn reversal.
summary: During a missed approach in dense fog, the crew received conflicting turn instructions from Tower after the Flight Director failed, causing a 270-degree turn while accelerating. The Pilot Monitoring attributed the confusion to Tower's failure to provide amended missed approach instructions prior to the approach clearance.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being unable to pressurize the aircraft and returned to the departure airport where the cargo door was found to not be closed properly.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin pressurization failure during climb due to an improperly latched aft cargo door. They returned to the departure airport for a safe landing after mechanics confirmed two door latches were disengaged, though no emergency was declared and no injuries occurred.

synopsis: A CE-560XLS flight crew reported smoke and fumes on descent so the crew diverted to a nearby airport. Maintenance found a burned set of wires under the forward left galley carpeting and believe that to be the smoke's source. The First Officer commented about the aircraft emergency checklist complexity.
summary: The PIC and First Officer of a CE-560XLS encountered smoke and burning smells during an RNAV arrival at 12,000 ft, prompting an emergency descent interrupted by a TCAS RA to avoid a VFR aircraft. After executing the electrical fire checklist to stop the smoke, they landed, evacuated due to lingering odors, and mechanics later identified burned wires under the galley carpet as the cause.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported an APU auto shut down at the gate due to low oil quantity. The APU was deferred, but later, Maintenance determined that leaking oil likely caused fumes in the cabin on previous legs with a different crew.
summary: The flight crew discovered an APU oil leak causing cabin fumes on prior legs, which previous captains failed to report to maintenance. The leak allowed oil to re-enter the APU intake, resulting in flames upon restart and requiring the APU to be placed on the MEL.

synopsis: An air carrier pilot reported received conflicting and confusing ATC instructions on an arrival in a foreign country and had to respond to an RA for conflicting traffic.
summary: The flight crew and approach controller experienced a communication failure during the ILS 5R arrival at MMMX, causing confusion over waypoints and headings. This led to two TCAS RAs requiring immediate vertical speed corrections and a climb to 11,000 feet before the crew safely intercepted the localizer and landed.

synopsis: Maintenance personnel reported that the incorrect circuit breakers were pulled when deferring a Vacuum Waste Blower.
summary: A maintenance controller incorrectly instructed a technician to pull and collar the Vacuum Waste Controller circuit breaker during MEL 38-XX configuration, causing total lav failure and an aircraft return to ZZZ. The error resulted from misreading MEL steps that required the controller breaker to remain closed, which was later corrected to restore lav operation.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: M20 pilot reported making an unplanned landing, reporting pilot neglected to lower the landing gear.
summary: The pilot landed a Mooney 20 gear-up after rushing the checklist during a short practice flight. The incident resulted in propeller contact and a belly scrape, which the pilot attributed to haste and a missed transponder certification renewal.

synopsis: A Pitts flight instructor reported a runway excursion and ground loop when the student applied right rudder then right brake.
summary: During dual tailwheel instruction in a Pitts, the student inadvertently applied right rudder and brake after touchdown, causing a ground loop despite the instructor's attempt to assume control. The aircraft departed the runway at a 30-45 degree angle, resulting in left wing contact and a sheared tailwheel.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Light twin pilot reported encountering severe turbulence and windshear on downwind for the SLC ILS Runway 34L at 10000 feet in IMC. 2000 feet was lost and a terrain warning was received along with a master warning for fuel pressure before control was regained.
summary: The pilot flying an ILS approach to SLC encountered a severe downdraft in IMC that caused a 2,000-foot altitude loss, triggering terrain and fuel warnings. After recovering and regaining control, the crew completed a side-step landing on Runway 34R and reported the incident to SLC TRACON.

synopsis: A Flight Instructor reported his instrument student moved the fuel tank selector to the OFF position while attempting to change engine fuel sources. The Instructor determined the engine failure cause and restarted the engine.
summary: During a VOR-B practice approach, a student pilot inadvertently selected the fuel tank to off while task-saturated, causing engine failure due to fuel starvation. The instructor subsequently restored fuel flow, and the aircraft landed safely at the home airport.

synopsis: BE40 Captain reported a bird strike in the number 1 engine while on downwind at an uncontrolled airport. Landing on one engine was accomplished shortly after.
summary: The pilot reported a bird strike into the left engine while at 1500ft with flaps 20 degrees and 160kts IAS during the downwind entry at uncontrolled field ZZZ. Severe vibration from the strike necessitated shutting down the engine, but the aircraft landed safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported a rough running engine at 15,000 feet and elected to divert to a suitable airport. During descent it was suspected that the left magneto had failed.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced an engine roughness and subsequent left magneto failure in a piston aircraft at 15,000 feet, causing a diversion to ZZZ1. The pilot attributed the delayed checklist execution and initial circling outside gliding range to task saturation, interruptions, and a loss of emergency mindset.

synopsis: BE20 flight crew reported being unable to maintain heading or airspeed during a simulated engine failure in IMC while under FAA evaluation.
summary: During an FAA IPC evaluation in a King Air 250, an inspector simulated a right engine failure at 500 feet, but the crew failed to fully secure the engine, causing excessive drag and autopilot disengagement. The aircraft could not maintain heading, forcing a return to ZZZ for an ILS approach and a subsequent FAA meeting regarding cockpit resource management.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU Center Controller reported that a C90 TRACON Controller climbed an aircraft into the Center's airspace without coordination.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a trainee received a handoff for Aircraft X at 12,000 feet in the FARMM sector, which was outside the departure sector's assigned altitude range. The controller attributed the issue to C90 vectoring the departure into adjacent airspace without awareness of surrounding sector altitude limits.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZOA Center Controller reported an unsafe situation when an aircraft was switched over from NCT TRACON and the pilot took it upon himself to climb to avoid traffic at the same altitude.
summary: A solo controller in Sector 29 managed a conflict between a climbing departure and an aircraft on the SUTTR arrival at FL190 after a delayed check-in. The controller executed an immediate climb and turn to prevent loss of separation, resolving the situation before the aircraft entered the 3-mile ring.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZME Center Controller reported a radio problem that is ongoing and has not been corrected.
summary: An air traffic controller in the R41, 40 sector lost radio contact with Aircraft Y descending to 040 while managing Aircraft X's approach at SRB. The controller used Aircraft X to relay a climb clearance to 050 to maintain separation, attributing the communication failure to known poor low-altitude radio coverage in the area.

synopsis: C90 TRACON Controllers working a mid-shift without a Supervisor were unsure how to handle ELT reports.
summary: An air traffic controller received multiple reports of a strong ELT signal from aircraft near DPA during marginal VFR conditions. The controller and Controller in Charge lacked specific ELT procedures in their reference materials and no supervisor was present, forcing them to guess the correct coordination steps while awaiting dawn for potential search and rescue.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Tower Controller reported of a NMAC while working three combined positions, the radar being on the 60 mile range, and not being able to see traffic close in.
summary: An LCL controller managing a combined position in a TRACAB configuration issued a follow instruction that led to a 0.16-mile near miss between two aircraft in the pattern. The controller attributed the incident to staffing shortages, equipment limitations, and a facility culture of recklessness that prevented proper separation monitoring.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: MYF Tower Controllers reported a runway incursion citing that a lack of runway markings and minimal staffing attributed to the incursion.
summary: LC controllers observed Aircraft X turn onto the active runway while Aircraft Y was landing, requiring an immediate exit instruction. The reporter attributed the incursion to missing runway edge markings on the intersecting runway and reduced safety oversight due to combined GC and CIC positions caused by staffing shortages.

synopsis: SAN Tower Front Line Manager reported of duplicate aircraft identifications in the SAN and LAX Area. Someone was attempting to use a call sign, saw that it was being used, but dropped the data tag anyways.
summary: A San Diego Local controller reported that LAX Tower improperly dropped Aircraft X's position tag, causing a duplicate ID conflict and forcing a retag with a call sign already used by LAX. The controller attributed this to LAX's reckless practice of removing flight plans not belonging to their facility, which violates proper ATC etiquette.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ABQ Tower Controller reported of a TCAS RA event during an opposite direction operation. The departure did not turn as instructed leading to a loss of separation.
summary: The tower controller cleared Aircraft Y for an opposite-direction departure from Runway 21 while Aircraft X was on a visual approach to Runway 3. Aircraft Y's delayed departure roll caused Aircraft X to execute a TCAS resolution advisory, which the controller attributed to poor timing and failure to utilize an alternative runway.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B737 reported that while parked at the gate, the aircraft rolled forward and the entry door made contact with the jet bridge.
summary: While unoccupied at the gate, the aircraft rolled forward, causing door 1L to contact the jet bridge and sustain cosmetic damage to the interior seal and cover. Maintenance freed the door, placed the item on the MEL, and the flight departed after a delay.

synopsis: Ramp Agent reported an injury to another Ramp Agent caused by a runaway freight dolly being towed by a contract worker. The reporter believes that the Contractor does not maintain their equipment and that their employees are negligent.
summary: A contractor employee driving a tractor towing universal dollies in a warehouse caused the hitch to pop, allowing the dollies to roll and strike a worker unhooking a cargo can. The worker suffered life-threatening injuries requiring over a week in the ICU due to the contractor's disregard for safety protocols.

synopsis: CE560XLS flight crew reported omitting the step down fix UCEVE with a crossing altitude of 1700 feet during the RNAV 14 approach to STS. This resulted in a terrain warning and a go-around was initiated.
summary: The Captain and First Officer missed the UCEVE step-down fix during the RNAV 14 approach to STS, descending from 3300 feet to 700 feet. This triggered a terrain alert, forcing a missed approach and vectors for a new attempt.

synopsis: The Captain of a DHC-8 reported that during climb they were unable to retract the nose gear.
summary: The crew aborted an engine start due to a reported hydraulic leak, then experienced a gear unsafe indication after takeoff caused by an open alternate gear extension door left by maintenance. They returned to land safely and recommended updating preflight inspection procedures for post-maintenance delays.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain on approach to ELP received a windshear warning, executed the escape maneuver, and proceeded to their alternate.
summary: The pilot encountered a Red Windshear Warning on final approach to ELP Runway 26L despite tower reports of no current shear. Consequently, the crew executed the windshear procedure and diverted to their alternate airport for a normal landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew received a climb clearance to 30,000 feet. The crew received an ACARS message to contact ATC on a different frequency where the Controller stated they should not have been climbing.
summary: Pilots departing CLT on the ESTRR2 departure climbed to 30,000 feet after receiving clearance from Charlotte ATC. Atlanta Center later questioned the climb, claiming the pilots entered their airspace without handoff, though the crew maintained they followed instructions and attributed the confusion to unclear controller diction.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they received an EGPWS obstacle warning during a night VOR Runway 26L approach to ELP.
summary: The pilot-monitoring and flying partner descended below their assigned 6,900-foot crossing altitude at FEMOL while configuring the aircraft for a visual approach to El Paso. This loss of situational awareness, attributed to high workload and potential radio squelch issues, triggered an EGPWS obstacle warning before ATC instructed an immediate climb to 8,000 feet.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported the First Officer trimmed nose up during takeoff which caused a warning as trim exceeded the limit. The First Officer intended to lighten takeoff rotation effort, but was cautioned his action was poor technique.
summary: The First Officer trimmed the aircraft nose-up during the takeoff roll to reduce rotation force, moving the stabilizer out of the green band and triggering a configuration warning. The Captain aborted the takeoff at 120 kts, and after maintenance inspection confirmed no system failure, the crew departed later after counseling the First Officer on the dangers of this technique.

synopsis: Air carrier Relief Pilot reported that after takeoff they were unable to maintain departure procedures due to the limited database in the aircraft.
summary: A crew flying an aircraft with an outdated navigation database hand-built a departure from Mexico City, resulting in a three-mile course deviation due to the inability to program "fly-over" waypoints. The deviation was compounded by pilot confusion and communication breakdowns, leading to an ATC correction and a subsequent missed approach caused by database limitations.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reported a IDG 2 trip during approach. The Captain attempted to reset it, but used the IDG 1 switch causing the air driven generator to deploy.
summary: During a hand-flown base-to-final turn, the pilot monitoring mistakenly cycled the IDG 1 switch instead of IDG 2 after a GEN 2 OFF caution, causing a momentary power loss and Air Driven Generator deployment. The pilot corrected the switch error, and the aircraft landed safely despite high workload and visual acquisition difficulties.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A student pilot became confused about his position on final relative to other aircraft at SFB and was instructed to go-around when he got too close to other aircraft.
summary: A student pilot on the Jessup arrival at 1,500 ft was cleared to land on 9C but found another aircraft alongside him at the same altitude. The tower instructed a go-around, which the pilot executed before safely landing on 9R.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported being dispatched with number two pack deferred. On the second leg, in cruise at FL370, an ECAM AIR ENG 1 BLEED LEAK is received causing the number one bleed valve to close automatically. Once at 10,000 feet the bleed leak indication clears and the flight continues to destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced an engine bleed leak and cabin altitude rise at FL370, triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. The reporter attributes the severity of the event to the number 2 pack being on deferral, which prevented normal pressurization recovery.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported an unstabilized approach to CYYZ due to shifting winds.
summary: The flight crew experienced a sudden 90-degree wind shift from a 50-knot tailwind to a crosswind while descending for ILS RWY 05 in heavy rain. Relying on ATIS and ATC forecasts of improving conditions, they managed high airspeeds to stabilize and landed safely.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a fuel leak was discovered in flight and the crew elected to divert. Maintenance determined an aircraft fuel quantity indication anomaly was the cause.
summary: The crew encountered a left main tank fuel leak at FL330 caused by an open crossfeed valve, prompting a diversion and single-engine landing. Although no external leak was visually confirmed, the aircraft was grounded for maintenance after follow-on pilots observed similar fuel loss.

synopsis: Airbus A320 series flight crew experienced a terrain warning descending to 10,000 feet approximately 9 NM east of KICDO during the ILS 12 at BZN. The aircraft was climbed to 11,000 feet and ATC confirmed that 10,000 feet was the correct altitude.
summary: During descent to BZN in IMC, the crew received a GPWS 'TERRAIN' alert 9-10 miles east of KICDO while cleared to 10,000 feet. The pilot flying executed an escape maneuver to 11,000 feet, and the controller attributed the event to a recent Minimum Safe Altitude change before the crew completed the ILS approach.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that the FAF altitude for the VOR DME Runway 25 at MRLB is below 1000 feet AGL and will cause an unstabilized approach if the aircraft is not configured for landing prior to leaving 1300 MSL.
summary: The flight crew experienced an unstable visual approach to Runway 25 at MRLB due to an unusually low published final approach fix altitude of 1,100 feet MSL. The captain and first officer manually leveled off to avoid terrain, attributing the deviation to unfamiliarity with the airport and the approach's non-compliance with stabilized criteria.

synopsis: The Captain of an Embraer EMB-505 reported that during taxi they heard a loud bang, causing both engines to spool-up so they shut down the engines and turned off all electrical.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud bang and engine spool-up on the ground after engine start, caused by water intrusion shorting the air conditioning controller box. The crew immediately shut down the aircraft, noting a previous uncorrected leak report and expressing concern over the potential for catastrophic electrical failure if the event had occurred in flight.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a problem with a buzz-squeal on VHF1 transmissions from VHF3 covered transmissions from ATC.
summary: Pilots reported VHF1 buzz-squeal interference from VHF3 transmissions covering ATC instructions from 2000 AGL to the gate, forcing a re-transmit request for taxi instructions. The crew attributed the issue to a long-standing Honeywell radio problem affecting the fleet, experienced on frequencies 133.3, 121.85, and 131.97 in Denver.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A crew member in an MD-80 reported that takeoff roll seemed a little longer when he discovered #2 engine EPR was low.
summary: The pilot experienced an unstable EPR and cycling right engine heat valve light during takeoff roll in ZZZ, which resolved after adjusting throttles and cycling the heat switch. The reporter attributes the issue to an uncommanded engine heat valve malfunction and requests maintenance investigation.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they experienced a windshear alert on final to RJAA, executed a go-around, and diverted.
summary: The crew encountered wind shear during approach to RJAA runway 16R, triggering a missed approach and diversion to alternate ZZZZ due to fuel concerns. Despite declaring minimum fuel, ATC refused direct routing until an emergency was declared, resulting in a 16-hour flight ending with 12,900 lbs of fuel.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported they could not respond to a flight crew in a timely manner due to weather and excessive workload.
summary: A dispatcher reported a delayed response to Flight XXXX during arrival into ZZZ due to extreme workload, weather, and a lengthy system login process during shift turnover. The flight arrived safely, but the captain expressed concern over the communication lag caused by the dispatcher managing 20-25 aircraft simultaneously without additional support.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported being rushed by the Gate Agent and not being informed about Air Marshals and an escorted prisoner before boarding.
summary: During post-landing boarding, a gate agent failed to inform the flight deck or cabin crew about two armed individuals, two Air Marshals, and an escorted prisoner on board. The agent admitted this security oversight after boarding began, noting he had only notified the marshals.

synopsis: The pilot of a Diamond DV20 reported that while in climb he had a near miss with a Mooney that was not in radio communication.
summary: The pilot reported a near miss with a NORDO Mooney while climbing to 2000ft MSL for an ILS approach to ZZZ. The incident occurred because the other pilot failed to maintain a lookout or provide position reports, forcing the reporter to pitch down after an ADS-B alert to avoid a midair collision.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported he landed to the side of the grass runway 27U at X51.
summary: The pilot attempted a landing on turf runway 27U at X51 but was distracted by a ramp vehicle and bird activity, resulting in a go-around. Poor markings caused the pilot to land off the runway in rough grass, where the airport manager later stated the aircraft exceeded weight limits and type restrictions not listed in the AFD.

synopsis: C172 instructor returned to land immediately after takeoff due to a rough running engine. A cracked cylinder head was discovered as the cause.
summary: After takeoff, the pilot experienced rough engine operation and RPM loss due to a cracked cylinder. Unable to climb or maintain altitude, the pilot turned back below 1,000 feet but was too high for Runway XXR, forcing a landing on Runway XXL.

synopsis: PA44 pilot detected high engine oil pressure after takeoff and an immediate return was requested. An uneventful landing ensued.
summary: The pilot and instructor experienced high oil pressure in the right engine shortly after takeoff, prompting an immediate return to Runway XXL. They landed safely and returned to the departure airport due to safety concerns regarding the abnormal gauge indication.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 reported that being #3 on approach he made a left 360 for spacing prior to calling the tower for clearance.
summary: The pilot, on an IFR flight cleared for a visual approach as number 3 behind a VFR aircraft, initiated an uncoordinated left 360 due to perceived spacing issues. Tower rejected the maneuver, re-sequenced the aircraft further out, and later claimed sufficient space had been provided.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A twin engine pilot flying a coupled approach to MVY, recovered and landed at minimums after the autopilot was either inadvertently disconnected or failed.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR approach to MVY in rapidly deteriorating weather experienced a KFC200 flight director drift near decision height, possibly due to accidental autopilot disconnect. The pilot executed a missed approach but subsequently landed safely after the aircraft drifted left of centerline.

synopsis: A Cessna 182 pilot reported that while on a long final approach he observed a Cessna 172 turning base directly toward him on a collision course.
summary: The pilot aborted a final approach to Runway 5 to avoid a collision with a Cessna 172 descending from left downwind. The incident occurred because the tower, lacking radar, cleared multiple aircraft while the CFI failed to identify extended final traffic, resulting in conflicting landing positions.

synopsis: PA23 Pilot reported he descended below his assigned altitude while troubleshooting a gyro failure.
summary: The pilot, while being vectored for a visual approach, descended to 2,500 feet below the cleared 3,000 feet altitude. This occurred because the pilot was distracted by a gyro failure that disabled the HSI, RMI, Autopilot, and Flight Director.

synopsis: C182 pilot experienced what sounded like back fires during taxi at idle RPM and returned to the ramp for maintenance to check the aircraft. Maintenance determined the sound was normal but when takeoff was attempted a cylinder separated from the crankcase and tore through the cowl.
summary: The pilot experienced backfiring during taxi and takeoff in a horizontally opposed 6-cylinder aircraft. Upon applying full power, the first cylinder blew through the cowling and crankcase, likely due to a developing crack, forcing a runway shutdown with no injuries.

synopsis: Gulfstream IV Captain reported an NMAC during the Aspen LOC DME-E Approach with a Challenger 300 departing on the LINDZ 8 SID opposite direction.
summary: A pilot on an IMC LOC DME-E approach at Aspen Airport experienced a near mid-air collision with a climbing Challenger 300 on the LINDZ EIGHT departure. The reporter attributed the event to mistimed arrival release, the departing crew's delayed turn, and inadequate ATC monitoring, resulting in a TCAS resolution advisory and missed approach.

synopsis: PA-23-250 pilot reported he climbed through his ATC assigned altitude when his gyro CB popped.
summary: The pilot departed an aircraft and overshot a cleared altitude of 2,000 feet to 3,000 feet due to distraction from a gyro CB electrical smell and autopilot failure. Departure cleared the pilot to maintain 3,000 feet after the error was observed.

synopsis: Pilot reported while on an IFR flight plan he declined to descend into a cloud layer below due to icing concerns.
summary: The pilot experienced broken communications with a heavily tasked controller while being cleared to descend to 5,000 feet. The pilot cancelled IFR to remain VFR above clouds due to icing concerns, but later realized this worsened the controller's situation and should have descended first while reporting the comms issues.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a runway excursion occurred when the left brake failed on the landing roll.
summary: The pilot experienced a right brake failure during the third landing of a currency flight, caused by a hairline fracture in a brake line. The aircraft veered into the grass to stop safely, resulting in no damage to persons or property before the line was replaced.

synopsis: PA28R pilot reported a GPS failure with a subsequent penetration of a restricted area and an unauthorized landing at a military field.
summary: The pilot experienced a GPS malfunction during a VFR flight, leading to an inability to determine position or identify the airport. The pilot landed safely on Runway 15 at an unknown military base, realizing the error only after parking and speaking with police.

synopsis: C150 pilot reported a NMAC with another light aircraft in the pattern at EQY airport.
summary: A pilot approaching Runway 23 at Monroe executed a go-around after a Bonanza departed without radio response and appeared near the pilot's altitude on final. The pilot side-stepped right to a left upwind, completed a normal pattern, and landed safely.

synopsis: Stinson HW-75 pilot reported a ground nose-over resulted after a loss of directional control on the landing roll that could have been related to a new tailwheel.
summary: Following maintenance replacing the tailwheel on a Maule, the pilot experienced a nose-over during a landing test flight when the new ABI 3200 tailwheel froze at 90 degrees, causing the aircraft to dart left and exit the runway into snow. The incident resulted in damage to the propeller, cowling, and air box, with the pilot attributing the cause to either pilot error or a mechanical fault.

synopsis: CE-560XL Captain reported his First Officer made a decision to divert for an entry door problem without consulting the Captain.
summary: During cruise at FL390, a continuous door warning light appeared due to a suspected sensor connection issue, though no red lights were visible on the door. The SIC unilaterally diverted and landed without consulting the PIC, despite the crew's assessment that a safe landing at the original destination was feasible.

synopsis: DCA Tower controllers reported that they requested 4 miles in trail from Potomac TRACON for aircraft landing DCA. It was agreed by both facility Traffic Managers, but PCT gave DCA 2-3 miles.
summary: DCA Local and Ground controllers reported that PCT disregarded coordinated 4-mile final spacing restrictions during heavy departures, resulting in 2-3 mile arrival trails. This caused unsafe squeeze-plays, go-arounds, missed release times, and extensive gate holds due to taxiway congestion.

synopsis: ZDV Center Controller reported he was advised by an arrival to an uncontrolled airport that another aircraft had been given a departure clearance by another controller to departed opposite direction and too close to them.
summary: The controller released departing Aircraft Y at discretion while Aircraft X cancelled IFR near Runway 10. Aircraft Y departed too close to the approaching Aircraft X, causing the pilot to contact Center, highlighting a misunderstanding that VFR aircraft are not separated from IFR traffic in the terminal environment.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZDV Center Controller reported a pilot needed an immediate descent due to severe turbulence.
summary: Air Traffic Control cleared Aircraft X to descend after the pilot reported an inability to hold altitude due to severe turbulence near the Rockies. The pilot leveled at FL290, diverted to Denver for a damage inspection, and reported no injuries.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that the company's prescribed hand signals for marshaling aircraft into parking is inadequate for purposes of identifying the ramp lead-in line at night with a wet ramp. Captain suggested returning to a marshaling signal that had previously been used.
summary: Pilots reported that current marshalling signals fail to indicate the angle of parking lead-in lines at night or in wet conditions, causing confusion. They recommend using exaggerated arm movements pointing in the line's direction to improve safety and clarity during parking.

synopsis: Just prior to cruise level-off, B737 First Officer reported an aural cabin altitude warning horn along with the red warning light. Crew diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew diverted to Airport ZZZ after an uncontrollable cabin pressurization failure triggered a warning at 36,000 feet, forcing an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. The aircraft landed safely at maximum structural weight with no injuries, where mechanics began diagnosing the issue.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a turbulence jolt at cruise attitude that injured a Flight Attendant.
summary: During the HNL-ZZZ cruise at FL290, a flight attendant fell from her jumpseat due to sudden moderate turbulence while unstrapped and reaching for the interphone. She sustained bruises to her elbow and shoulder, and the crew arranged for medical personnel to meet the aircraft upon arrival in ZZZ.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported he noticed a trend where copilots are placing their hand against the back of the throttles, when the only hand there should be the Captain's.
summary: A Captain reported that Copilots on Boeing 777s incorrectly place hands on throttles during takeoff rolls, violating procedures. This causes distraction and risks finger injury or delayed aborts if the Captain must rapidly retract throttles.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the tendency of Denver Approach controllers to push pilots to accept late RNAV approach clearances.
summary: The pilot reported that Denver ATC pressured the crew to accept an RNAV arrival during the downwind leg at 11,000 feet, despite the crew's refusal due to briefing concerns. The crew subsequently flew a visual approach to an uneventful landing, highlighting a recurring issue where controllers push late RNAV clearances without understanding the associated safety risks.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported an asymmetrical spoiler deployment during descent. The crew reported there was no data available for a no-spoiler landing.
summary: The flying pilot experienced asymmetric spoiler deployment causing a rapid roll and autopilot disconnect during descent into ZZZ. After troubleshooting with Dispatch and confirming normal operation, the crew landed with spoilers disarmed, noting a lack of checklists and landing data for a no-spoiler condition.

synopsis: The flight crew of an Embraer ERJ-175 reported that they descended too rapidly when they received a EPGWS obstacle alert and a call from Tower to say they were too low.
summary: The pilot descended early during a visual approach, triggering a GPWS 'TERRAIN' caution and an ATC low altitude warning. The error resulted from misinterpreting the approach chart's 900 feet label as applying to 4 DME instead of 3 DME due to label proximity.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they descended before being cleared by ATC for a visual approach to MKK.
summary: The pilot and First Officer descended to 4,300 ft MSL for a visual approach to MKK without a valid clearance due to ambiguous controller instructions and pilot distraction. The controller ordered a climb to 5,000 ft MSL and vectored the aircraft to the MKK VOR before issuing a proper visual clearance.

synopsis: The First Officer of a B737 reported that when taxiing into a gate, vehicle traffic continually crossed in front of the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing to the gate, a bus and other vehicles crossed within 20-30 feet of the aircraft nose despite flashing landing lights. The pilot was forced to stop abruptly to avoid a collision after the ramp controller stated wing walkers were responsible for stopping traffic.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a tail strike due to a strong downdraft during landing.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer landed an aircraft at MTPP when a strong, unexpected downdraft at 30 feet caused a firm touchdown and bounce. The crew rejected a go-around due to insufficient energy, resulting in a tail strike attributed to the low-altitude wind shear.

synopsis: G450 flight crew reported lateral and vertical deviations occurred when approach mode was selected too early in the approach. Crew cited fatigue as a factor.
summary: Pilots on a Boeing aircraft approaching Panama City armed the approach mode too early, causing the autopilot to prematurely capture the localizer and deviate from the feeder route. The crew manually corrected the flight path and altitude, attributing the error to premature automation engagement and fatigue during a circadian low.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported that they connected the autopilot during climb and the aircraft pitched over and went into an uncommanded descent.
summary: The crew experienced uncommanded autopilot pitch deviations during climb and cruise, followed by de-ice boot failures and flight director loss after pulling the autopilot circuit breaker. They hand-flew the remainder of the flight, reporting a 700 ft altitude deviation to ATC before completing a normal landing.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported they had a medical emergency onboard, difficulty understanding the Medlink Doctor and the Doctors onboard complained about the poor quality of the stethoscope and blood pressure cuff.
summary: During a flight with a medical emergency, the crew managed a passenger's condition while communicating with MedLink and ATC. The First Officer incorrectly programmed a descent fix due to distraction, causing an altitude restriction error that was later corrected after the crew notified ATC.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate Captain reported being cleared to taxi eastbound on Taxiway K and hold short of Taxiway E after landing on Runway 27R. The crew did not see any E signs and held short of Runway 35 after crossing Taxiway E.
summary: The flight crew landed at PHL and mistakenly taxied past Taxiway E onto Runway 35 due to missing signage for Taxiways E and F. After realizing the error and being questioned by ground control, they were cleared to cross the runway and reached the ramp without further incident.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet pilot reported a taxiway incursion at FRG. Reporter stated taxiway G signage and markings at the ramp were difficult to detect.
summary: The flight crew taxiing from an FBO at FRG struggled to identify unmarked Taxiway G, mistaking a road for the taxiway. This confusion led to a runway incursion where the aircraft crossed the hold short line of Runway 19 by one to two feet.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported a takeoff from a runway with a runway visual range that was below minimums.
summary: A fatigued Captain and First Officer mistakenly departed with 800 RVR visibility after misreading takeoff minimums for the wrong runway due to fatigue and rushing. The flight proceeded normally despite the error, which the crew attributed to an accident chain involving fatigue and poor risk management.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported a rejected soft field takeoff when his student lost control during takeoff roll.
summary: During a soft-field takeoff in a Piper Archer, a student pilot failed to apply sufficient right rudder, causing the aircraft to swerve left. The flight instructor took control, reduced power to idle, and stopped the plane to prevent it from veering off the runway.

synopsis: After lift-off, float plane pilot reported encountering converging traffic that was on an instrument approach to a nearby airport. Pilot met with his home airport manager in order to develop procedures for ensuring future separation of traffic in similar situations.
summary: A floatplane pilot climbing into Class D airspace spotted converging IFR traffic that was not yet visible on Tower radar. The pilot maintained visual separation without evasive action, leading to a debrief on improving radar contact protocols for mixed VFR and IFR operations.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported incurring STS Runway 20 approach hold area after leaving the run up area. The reporter did not see the hold-short line protecting the Runway 20 approach path because of its distance from the Runway 14 entry taxiway.
summary: The pilot missed the A3 intersection while taxiing to Runway 14, inadvertently crossing the Runway 20 approach path due to confusing signage. Ground control advised a possible pilot deviation, but the tower later stated there was no safety issue as no traffic was present.

aircraft: Vans Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A VANS RV pilot reported that he detected what he thought was a failed engine cylinder and diverted to a nearby airport. On the ground, he determined the Number 4 cylinder exhaust pipe had severed completely.
summary: A pilot cruising at 6,500 feet experienced engine roughness and power loss due to a severed exhaust pipe on cylinder 4. While managing the situation and landing safely, the pilot briefly entered Delta airspace at 2,000 feet without contacting ATC due to high workload and anxiety.

synopsis: PA28 instructor, supervising a student solo from the ramp, reported calling the Tower on a handheld VHF to have his student go-around after the student is cleared to land on the shorter runway.
summary: A flight instructor on the ground intervened when a student solo pilot was cleared to land on an unfamiliar, short runway instead of the assigned one. The instructor transmitted a go-around request on the tower frequency, causing the student to abort the approach and land safely on the correct runway.

synopsis: LGA Tower Controller reported of an unsafe situation due to approach not separating two arrivals better.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at LGA Local Control issued a go-around to Aircraft Y due to dangerously tight spacing behind Aircraft X on an ILS approach to Runway 22. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to poor sequencing by N90 and the incorrect assumption that a Visual Approach clearance guaranteed safe separation.

synopsis: OGG Tower Controller reported confusion during a go-around and Approach Control attempting to sequence traffic back into the arrival flow.
summary: The Cab Coordinator and Local Controller at Maui Tower managed Aircraft X's go-around and VFR pattern while coordinating with HCF Approach regarding Aircraft Y and Z. Conflicting instructions and expectation bias caused a loss of separation, requiring the Local Controller to issue emergency altitude changes to avoid a collision between the two aircraft.

synopsis: MSP Tower Controller reported a conflict when clearing an aircraft while an arrival was within the Arrival Departure Window.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at Local Control North cleared a departure from Runway 30R while an aircraft was in the Arrival Departure Window for converging Runway 35. The controller recognized the procedural error but allowed the departure to continue, citing a lack of clear guidance and low traffic demand as contributing factors.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported that new checklist response procedures and policy are interfering with cockpit and radio communications.
summary: The pilot reported that a new cockpit call-out procedure and excessive briefings created distraction during climb out, causing three missed radio calls and subsequent instructions. The reporter attributed this to information overload obscuring critical details.

synopsis: B737 crew reported executing a missed approach due to 'Terrain' and 'Too Low-Flaps' aural warnings received on short final. Crew determined that the cause was that the wing flaps were in the Flaps 25 position instead of the required Flaps 30 position.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain encountered turbulence on an ILS approach to Runway 9 at San Diego, causing autopilot disengagement. A flap configuration error, where the handle was moved to 40 and blew back to 25, triggered warnings and necessitated a go-around before a safe landing.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported they continued the flight to their destination regardless of the thunderstorms in the area.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain ignored diversion requests and flew through severe thunderstorms, causing altitude deviations and a suspected lightning strike. Post-flight inspection initially missed damage, but maintenance later found a missing static wick and exit point damage attributed to the strike.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff at 100 kts when they discovered the stabilizer trim was not set properly.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 100 knots after the trim setting drifted from 8 up to 5 up, causing heavy yoke forces and a Master Warning. The pilot attributes the event to trim verification occurring too late and suggests moving the check to the Before Takeoff section.

synopsis: B767-300ER flight crew reported a hard landing resulted in a tail strike.
summary: The flight crew experienced difficulty contacting Tower before receiving a visual clearance. A hard landing occurred on final approach, resulting in an undetected tail strike that was later confirmed by an EICAS message during taxi.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported ATC alerted him to a speed restriction departing CLT that they had missed. The complex departure charts and the iPad interface contributed.
summary: The flight crew departed CLT on the BOBZY2 SID and inadvertently accelerated to 300 KIAS instead of the required 280 KIAS after 10,000 MSL. They missed the speed restriction note due to poor legibility of the multi-page chart on their iPad, though they immediately complied with Atlanta Center's correction.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after the left hydraulic system A quantity went to 10%.
summary: The pilot reported a master caution flicker and left hydraulic low pressure light at FL350 with System A quantity at 10%. After completing the QRH checklist and notifying ATC, the aircraft landed uneventfully.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported diverting after encountering a severe mountain wave over the Southern Rockies.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe clear-air turbulence and mountain waves at FL370 southwest of PUB, causing autopilot and autothrottle disengagement and uncommanded bank angles. Unable to obtain timely descent clearance due to frequency congestion, they descended to FL290, diverted to ZZZ, and landed safely with no injuries but several sick passengers.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported it took a long time to get the needed planned altitude from ATC to avoid an area of turbulence.
summary: The pilot reported that ATC issued a mandatory reroute over blocked airspace between PKE and DRK below FL280, ignoring known turbulence from FL270 to FL350. This forced extensive coordination to revert to the original route at FL250 to avoid severe turbulence indicators.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported not perceiving taxiway L7 beyond Runway 8L and turned further left onto Runway 8L. Airport chart depiction was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot, after landing on runway 8R, turned left onto runway 8L instead of right while taxiing on L7 due to a discrepancy between the Jeppesen chart and actual ground layout. Tower controllers observed the deviation, instructed the crew to exit at K6, and the pilot attributed the error to inaccurate charting.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported they overshot a cleared altitude and exceeded temperature limitations on an engine while they were distracted by a VNAV issue.
summary: The Captain hand-flew the aircraft after VNAV failed to engage during climb, leading to an autopilot mode conflict and a brief engine over-temperature event caused by delayed power reduction. The crew continued to the destination using minimal automation after failing to resolve the VNAV malfunction.

synopsis: SR20 flight instructor reported returning to departure airport after the Number 5 cylinder showed signs of overheating.
summary: During an instrument training climb at 450 feet, the instructor observed excessive EGT and CHT on engine #5, which quickly reached maximum temperature and caused vibration. The crew requested priority handling, landed safely on runway 18, and taxied to the ramp after engine temperatures normalized.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew member reported he had difficulty with poor visibility through the windshield in heavy rain during an approach. He reported he was concerned with his company's decision to not reapply rain repellent coating to the windshields.
summary: A pilot reported distorted depth perception and poor visibility during the landing phase in moderate to heavy rain due to a lack of rain repellent on the windshield. The reporter attributed this safety hazard to the company's failure to regularly reapply the hydrophobic coating.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced three separate TCAS RA events within two minutes during the AVSAR 1C Arrival to MMMX.
summary: Pilots on an arrival to MMMX received three descending RAs between 10,000 and 12,000 feet due to ATC vectors toward rising terrain and a non-compliant aircraft. The crew complied with all RAs to maintain terrain clearance, refused vectors toward the other aircraft, and landed safely after ATC confirmed the other flight made wrong turns.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that while accomplishing the preflight some rain repellant dripped on the First Officer's face and into his eye.
summary: A mechanic was exposed to rain repellent streaming from an aircraft nose during preflight, causing eye irritation after the inbound crew reported an uncommanded discharge on approach. The incident highlighted failures in crew notification, lack of immediate MSDS access from Maintenance Control, and discrepancies between the chemical name on the canister and operational data.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) Apprentice reported that when driving a vehicle around a Boeing 737, the vehicle made contact with the flap fairing.
summary: A ground driver operating a mule vehicle near an aircraft with flaps at 45 degrees was blinded by wing and ramp lights. The vehicle struck the flap fairing tip, causing damage due to poor visibility from the lighting conditions.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported that after checking the APU oil on a Boeing 737 he neglected to reinstall oil cap.
summary: A mechanic performing an APU oil check on the ground left the oil cap cover on a low-battery lift while distracted by a conversation with a Lead. Two days later, the missing cover was discovered, confirming the APU oil cap was left uninstalled on the aircraft.

synopsis: The pilot of a Diamond DV20 reported that while attempting to takeoff the aircraft suddenly sped up, the pilot lost control of the aircraft and it departed the runway.
summary: The pilot aborted a touch-and-go takeoff on Runway 22 after the aircraft suddenly accelerated and veered left despite full right rudder and left aileron input. The aircraft was stopped in adjacent grass with no damage to the runway or airframe, and was later towed for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: TBM-850 pilot experienced confusion during a visual approach due to a similar sounding call sign and executed a go-around after nearly landing gear up.
summary: The pilot of an aircraft approaching DAL for runway 31L initiated a go-around after receiving a confusing "cancel landing clearance" call, inadvertently retracting the landing gear. The crew executed a full go-around, landed safely on 31R, and attributed the incident to communication ambiguity caused by a similar call sign and the decision to abort the landing.

synopsis: TB 21 instructor with a licensed trainee reported a gear up landing with the instructor at the controls. This was the first flight in this type aircraft for the trainee and the instructor interpreted a gear warning horn as a faulty stall warning indication.
summary: A student pilot and CFI in a Professional Pilot Program landed gear-up after misinterpreting the gear horn as a stall warning during a control exchange on base. The incident resulted from the student's unfamiliarity with the aircraft's audio tones and the instructor's failure to complete the before-landing checklist.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Air taxi pilot reported experiencing whiteout conditions while VFR on approach to TRK. A passenger in the right seat panicked, distracting the pilot which lead to a stall and recovery during the IMC missed approach.
summary: A Part 135 pilot flying to TRK entered a white-out and accelerated stall while avoiding a missed approach aircraft, exacerbated by a distracting passenger. The pilot recovered, diverted, and landed safely, attributing the incident to premature VFR cancellation and passenger distraction.

synopsis: LGB Tower controllers discovered operational errors doing a routine review of ATC Operations. The Support Specialist states the Tower manager ordered him to not report the errors.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was on base to final for Helipad 2, violating LGB N7110.20 separation standards. The reporter filed a Mandatory Occurrence Report after the facility manager refused to do so, citing internal review findings as non-reportable.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU Center Controller reported that a C90 TRACON Controller advised the Center Controller that an aircraft wanted to divert. The pilot never wanted to divert and the reporting Controller advised that the TRACON Controller was not helpful nor honest.
summary: A C90 arrival controller vectored Aircraft X away from ORD and weather without informing the flight crew of a diversion plan, claiming the aircraft was already coordinating an alternate. The crew, unaware of the intent, was forced to divert after being flown 50–60 miles southwest with no ability to assess the storm.
