aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A ZAU Center Controller reported that sectors were not being staffed in accordance with guidelines.
summary: An observer reported that a Front Line Manager avoided assigning a Radar Approach Controller to a known complainer during complex weather in ZAU, instead directing a relieved controller to the position. The reporter concluded this prioritization of personal factors over operational needs created a safety event by delaying necessary staffing.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZBW Center Controller reported another Controller mistakenly transferred him an aircraft that was in conflict with his traffic.
summary: A ZNY controller accidentally handed off an aircraft at FL210 to a ZBW controller, creating a conflict with an EWR arrival at FL180 due to the aircraft being left on a heading. The ZBW controller resolved the conflict by amending the arrival's altitude, attributing the error to high workload and fatigue from a two-controller midnight shift.

synopsis: Front Line Manager reported that there were high winds causing drift of aircraft on departure. This lead to an unsafe situation when the faster aircraft departed behind the slower aircraft.
summary: A Front Line Manager reported that ZZZ Tower cleared two successive departures on the same heading in strong crosswinds, causing Aircraft X to drift right and merge with Aircraft Y. The departure controller corrected the conflict by turning Aircraft X left, noting that tower-assigned headings in such conditions create unsafe situations for departure sequencing.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported that the Local Controller did not tell the truth about a close call relating to an aircraft exiting a runway with an arrival landing the same runway.
summary: A pilot reported a runway incursion where an SR22 landed long and passed within 30–50 feet of a Cessna still rolling out after turning off midfield. The pilot later discovered the local controller had initially downplayed the event, though the SR22 pilot confirmed the close call.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported the gear failed to extend, so they had to use the manual extension procedure.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a landing gear extension failure during a visual approach at 2,000 feet. After a go-around and successful manual extension, they landed uneventfully and were towed from the runway.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported diverting for IDG and APU problems. They discovered that a month earlier another crew had a similar experience with the exact same outcome.
summary: The First Officer and Captain diverted a CRJ-200 from cruise due to an IDG 2 fault and subsequent APU oil temperature caution, which mechanics attributed to a failed IDG and low APU oil. On the second day, they added fuel to meet a minimum landing weight MEL restriction before completing the flight safely.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported a very high workload and management pressure interfered with his duties.
summary: A dispatcher delayed 14 flights due to severe weather and excessive workload after management failed to provide requested assistance. The Director subsequently lectured the dispatcher for violating coordination procedures, threatening disciplinary action while the dispatcher managed high call volumes and unsafe flight release loads.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported an airborne conflict with a corporate jet resulting in an RA on arrival into ONT.
summary: During descent to 15,000 ft, SoCal Approach advised the crew of VFR traffic at 16,500 ft. The crew followed RA guidance to level at 17,000 ft, allowing a business jet to pass 500 ft below, though the pilot felt the controller should have vectored one aircraft to avoid the conflict.

synopsis: A300 First Officer reported a rejected takeoff when the auto thrust tripped off at 80 knots.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 80 knots after the Auto Thrust System lever tripped. Maintenance found water in the courier compartment, likely from snow-covered cans, which may have caused the lever to trip.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported a loss of communication radios and weather radar due to precipitation static during cruise.
summary: During enroute cruise in IMC, the crew experienced simultaneous radio static and weather radar failures while deviating for weather. Unable to communicate with ATC or trust radar data, they squawked NO COMM, turned back to the departure airport, and relied on another aircraft to relay instructions.

synopsis: SR20 instructor with student reported a low power reading in cruise and elected to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: An instructor and student in a single-engine aircraft experienced abnormal engine noise and indications en route, prompting a diversion to the nearest airport after an unusual knock was felt. The crew reported unusual power and tachometer readings to Approach but did not declare an emergency while diverting with two souls on board.

synopsis: Two maintenance technicians reported that after installing an engine in a Eurocopter it was discovered they failed to install the bushings in the aft mount.
summary: Maintenance technicians installed a replacement engine on an EC135 but missed installing bushings in the aft mount due to outdated manuals and a late engine swap decision. The omission was discovered during engine packing, forcing the aircraft out of service for repairs before it was returned to service.

synopsis: An A320 Captain reported experiencing a failed engine anti-ice valve and returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The crew returned to ZZZ due to an inoperative engine anti-ice switch, performing an overweight landing after consulting maintenance and ATC. Following a ground repair to lock the valve open, the aircraft was refueled and dispatched to continue the flight.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reported ATC will not approve IFR flights to EYW via V3 due to 'traffic conflicts', requiring flight along the west coast of Florida over swamp and open water. The reporter believes this is not safe.
summary: A General Aviation pilot reported that Miami Center mandates unsafe IFR routes over the Okefenokee Swamp and open ocean for flights to EYW, rejecting safer alternatives due to alleged traffic conflicts. The pilot argues these mandatory routes over un-navigable terrain and water create unnecessary drowning risks, while safe overland paths via eastern Florida airports remain available.

synopsis: A PA-28 instructor reported his student's control and landing difficulties ended with a high flare and an early power reduction. Subsequently, the aircraft landed hard which resulted in a tail strike.
summary: An instructor and student pilot experienced a hard landing with a tail strike during a forward slip training maneuver in a single-engine aircraft. The student abruptly reduced power and pitched up while maintaining the slip, causing a stall and requiring the instructor to take control to prevent a worse outcome.

synopsis: A C210 pilot reported a 5 minute clearance void time led to announcing takeoff intentions on the CTAF and hearing a King Air pilot announce a go around on short final.
summary: The pilot departed on an instrument flight plan and incorrectly assumed a King Air on final approach was distant due to a five-minute void clearance. The pilot began takeoff, but the King Air called a go-around, forcing the pilot to abort the departure.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported advising the Captain to hold short at the first set of hold bars approaching Runway 8R on Taxiway M at MIA. After continuing across, the Tower informed the crew that they had crossed the hold line then cleared them for takeoff.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a runway incursion while taxiing to Runway 8R after a last-minute runway change caused task saturation. The crew held short of the incorrect hold short line due to the Captain's reliance on experience over the First Officer's concern, prompting a Tower correction.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small fixed wing pilot reported mistakenly following traffic towards the parallel runway, was advised of his error and executed a go around.
summary: A flight instructor flying a VFR approach to CNO mistakenly identified traffic on runway 26L while cleared for 26R. The pilot executed a go-around after tower correction, re-entered the pattern, and landed safely on 26R, attributing the error to focusing on the preceding aircraft rather than total situational awareness.

synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported that on takeoff from ZZZ when it was snowing he noticed a snow plow at the departure end of the runway.
summary: A pilot repositioning a critical patient at uncontrolled airport ZZZ encountered a county snow plow on the runway during low visibility and snow. The pilot aborted the takeoff roll, lifted off mid-field using soft field techniques, and cleared the plow, attributing the incident to poor plow lighting, lack of radio communication, and no active NOTAMs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Small fixed wing pilot flying VFR west of SAN at 1500 feet, entered SAN airspace without clearance on an incorrect track, conflicting with a B737.
summary: A pilot flying a VFR aircraft near San Diego received conflicting instructions from North Island Tower regarding a route change and handoff, leading to an inadvertent entry into Class B airspace. The pilot attributed the incident to a communication breakdown and failure to clarify ambiguous instructions before deviating from the standard Shoreline Route.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported an aircraft did not have the updated OAPM Arrival procedures for their destination.
summary: An OAPM aircraft lacked updated STARs, specifically DSNEE1 and DOOBY1, for the destination airport. The reporter attributed this to airlines not receiving updated information and requested that data distribution be ensured.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller working sectors with new arrival/departure procedures discovered an error in one of the routes.
summary: The reporter states that the BOACH JANNY route is interrupted by the HEC or LYNXX fixes according to OAPM. They request a Preferred Departure Arrival Route (PDAR) to resolve this airspace procedure issue.

synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported an aircraft was cleared via an OAPM STAR, but the aircraft had an extra fix in their database compared to the chart.
summary: A pilot reported a database mismatch while cleared on an OAPM routing with the SEAVU.LOVIN.KRAIN sequence. The chart lacked the LOVIN waypoint, which the pilot attributed to a potential spelling error, prompting a recommendation to update charts.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported aircraft climbing into their sector via new OAPM departure procedures were climbing to the wrong altitude.
summary: The pilot reported that an aircraft following OAPM procedures was cleared to climb to 23,000 feet via a SID but checked in climbing to 12,000 feet. The controller instructed the aircraft to continue climbing via the SID.

synopsis: BNA Departure Controller reported receiving departures from the Tower that were assigned incorrect headings.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a loss of separation between a departing aircraft and an arrival due to the departure accelerating unexpectedly during a high-traffic day. The controller attributed the incident to fatigue and chaos caused by excessive photo missions, military flights, and a flight check aircraft operating in opposite directions.

synopsis: ZLA Center Controller working airspace with new OAPM arrival and departure procedures reported an aircraft received by him had incorrect routings.
summary: A pilot reported that an RNAV aircraft landing at SBA received incorrect OAPM routing and an interim altitude of 14,000 feet instead of the required 15,000 feet. The reporter attributed this to new procedures and requested that the 14,000-foot restriction for Category Q aircraft be permanently deleted.

synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported working an aircraft that did not have new OAPM arrival procedures available on the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that Aircraft X was not loaded with new OAPM procedures. The reporter recommended updating the airplanes to include these procedures.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller working with new OAPM arrival procedures received an aircraft that did not have the new procedures available in their navigation database.
summary: The crew attempted to fly new OAPM procedures, but Aircraft X lacked the COMIX STAR onboard, preventing STAR execution. The reporter recommends updating the system to resolve this equipment deficiency.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported an aircraft using a new OAPM departure procedure checked on their frequency climbing to the wrong altitude.
summary: Aircraft X on the ORCKA 1 SID under the new OAPM route checked in climbing to 19,000 feet instead of the required 23,000 feet. The reporter requested a system update to reflect the proper altitudes.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: HUF Controller reported an airspace violation due to communication problems with another facility and the aircraft pilot.
summary: During a TRACAB operation, a developmental controller and pilot managed Aircraft X, which entered a hold instead of approaching due to autopilot error. The aircraft briefly entered IND airspace without coordination because IND Approach refused to answer the phone, but it was eventually re-cleared and landed safely.

synopsis: ZLA Center Controller received an aircraft on an OAPM departure from an adjacent sector at the wrong altitude.
summary: Aircraft X on a new OAPM route should have been at 23,000 feet. An adjacent controller reread the letter of agreement and realized their error.

synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported a departing aircraft was issued the wrong SID according to the new OAPM arrival/departure procedures implemented for their airspace.
summary: Aircraft X was issued and flew the POM9 SID instead of the required SNSHN1 SID due to an OAPM issue. The flight plan incorrectly showed the POM9 SID, resulting in the aircraft not flying the correct procedure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller received multiple aircraft from an adjacent Center on the wrong STAR.
summary: The reporter stated that aircraft were not issued the appropriate STAR and that ZOA should comply with the letter of agreement. No specific phase of flight, aircraft type, or outcome was described in the narrative.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being cleared initially to climb via the SLAPP1 to maintain FL210 then told to climb and maintain FL230 and the crossing restriction (JETHK of FL 190B) is removed. After a level off at 15,000 for traffic the crew is recleared to climb via, but the crossing restriction is not reentered.
summary: The flight crew departed BUR on the new SLAPP 1 RNAV SID and inadvertently climbed above the JETHK FL190 restriction after deleting it for an initial "climb and maintain" clearance. The error occurred when ATC later issued a "climb via" clearance, and the crew failed to reprogram the restriction before reaching the fix.

synopsis: B737 crew reported they hit a deice truck as they were being marshaled into the gate.
summary: The flight crew taxied into a gate where a ramp agent directed them toward an unattended de-ice truck parked parallel to the safety zone. The aircraft struck the truck, denting the left outer slat, due to the agent's conflicting instructions and obscured visual cues from glycol on the ramp.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported the First Officer dropping a water can on the center pedestal where is burst open and emptied. A short time later Transponder #1 and #2 NAV tuning head failed which then affected the First Officer's LNAV.
summary: Water spilled from a dropped can onto the center console during cruise, causing failures to the ATC transponder and VHF NAV 2. The crew switched to backup systems, managed the approach using the Captain's instruments, and landed safely with no further incidents.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the tiller would not turn the nose wheel. The tiller became operable after maintenance, but a flight 2 legs later the same anomaly occurred.
summary: The Captain experienced a frozen nose wheel steering tiller during taxi, which a mechanic temporarily fixed on the taxiway by cleaning a dirty bypass valve. The issue recurred two legs later, leading to a shutdown, tow, and permanent logbook entry after the mechanic confirmed the valve required thorough cleaning.

synopsis: EMB175 Captain reported diverting to the alternate airport after two missed approaches at the planned destination.
summary: The crew diverted to alternate ZZZ1 after two missed ILS approaches at ZZZ due to weather deteriorating to 0/0 visibility. Fuel entered the red range en route to the alternate, but the aircraft landed safely after notifying ATC.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported encountering moderate turbulence, precipitation, and static in the VHF radios during flight over eastern Pennsylvania.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe static and turbulence while navigating storms at 10,000 feet, leading to a misinterpreted ATC clearance and a self-deviation to avoid radar returns. Subsequent ATC vectors into the weather caused moderate turbulence, resulting in a 40-knot airspeed increase and a 300-foot altitude loss.

synopsis: A pilot reported chart confusion regarding the LNAV/VNAV BCT RNAV (GPS) Runway 5 and RNAV (GPS) Y Runway 23 approaches when local altimeter is unavailable. The charts appear to permit a PBI Airport altimeter to higher approach minimums.
summary: A pilot reported conflicting chart notes at BCT regarding Runways 5 and 23, where BARO VNAV is marked unauthorized with a PBI altimeter, yet LNAV/VNAV minimums are adjusted for its use. This ambiguity creates uncertainty on whether VNAV approaches can be flown with a PBI altimeter during increased activity under a presidential TFR.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported a flap malfunction on final approach.
summary: During a night approach in moderate turbulence, the crew executed a go-around due to a flap discrepancy and later received GPWS warnings on short final. The reporter attributes the "TOO LOW FLAPS" and "TERRAIN" alerts to misreading the non-normal checklist regarding flap inhibit, caused by fatigue, turbulence, and divided attention.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier on frequency with a company similar call sign was called incorrectly by ATC which confused everyone. Finally, with a frequency change, the crew descending to 14,000 was told their clearance was to 17,000, but that crew never heard 17,000.
summary: The pilot of Air carrier XXY reported a clearance error at FL190 where the controller issued 14,000 feet instead of 17,000 feet due to call sign confusion with Air carrier XZY. The controller acknowledged the mistake after the crew descended through 15,500 feet and instructed them to level at 14,000 feet.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported a nosewheel steering fault inflight. The flight landed with inoperative nosewheel steering.
summary: The flight crew encountered a WHEEL N/W STRG FAULT one hour into flight, requiring differential braking for steering and rollout. They landed on the longest runway, cleared it using differential braking, and were towed to the gate after an unknown equipment malfunction.

synopsis: B777 Crew reported ATC called for an intermediate level off during climb out from a foreign airport which may have been attributed to misunderstanding the clearance.
summary: The pilot and First Officer departed ZZZZ and were cleared to climb to FL230, but the controller later ordered a level-off at FL140. The pilot suspected a misunderstanding caused by language barriers, high traffic, and confusing their call sign with the altitude clearance.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported the Tower directed a go-around due to FOD on the runway, followed by a VFR pattern at 4800 feet causing a GPWS terrain warning.
summary: The crew at MSO received a go-around clearance for FOD and selected flaps 30 to follow traffic, triggering an EGPWS terrain warning requiring a 50-foot climb. The reporter attributed the event to high terrain, poor ATC go-around instructions, and unfamiliarity with the airport.

synopsis: SR20 instructor reported two cylinder head temperature indications climbed into the red, the engine began running rough and lost power, resulted in a return to the airport.
summary: During takeoff at 500 AGL, the Instructor Pilot experienced red CHTs on cylinders 5 and 6, engine roughness, and a 40% power loss. After ATC cleared a right turn and landing, the aircraft safely taxied to the ramp.

synopsis: PA-34 pilot reported poor braking action on landing and ran off the end of the runway.
summary: The pilot flew an RNAV approach in IMC with rime ice, landing on an unplowed, untreated runway with nil braking action after tower failed to report conditions. The aircraft overran the runway by ten feet, striking a light and damaging the props, though it was later taxied to the ramp.

synopsis: PA28R pilot reported becoming confused during a VFR flight to BUR and lined up on VNY. BUR Tower detected the error and issued a new heading and climb back to assigned altitude.
summary: A VFR pilot unfamiliar with Los Angeles airspace mistakenly lined up on Van Nuys instead of Burbank after ATC traffic avoidance instructions. The pilot failed to re-check heading, leading to a tower correction to climb and overfly Van Nuys before being cleared to land at Burbank.

synopsis: Cessna Caravan pilot reported failure to remove the tail stand before flight.
summary: The pilot discovered the tail stand was left installed after noticing reduced cruise speed and pitch oscillation during flight. The aircraft landed safely with no damage, and the pilot removed the stand on the ground, attributing the error to closing the cargo pod door prematurely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported hitting a taxiway sign while clearing the runway at DTO.
summary: The pilot, after landing on Runway 36, accelerated to reach a distant exit but was then instructed to turn right at the nearby A5 taxiway. Unable to stop in time due to excessive speed, the aircraft rolled off the pavement and struck the A5 sign, causing damage to the sign but not the aircraft.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: S56 TRACON Traffic Management Coordinator reported a decision to change runways was overridden by the Supervisor. The Final Controller reported a loss of separation on final due to the strong winds.
summary: A TRACON flow controller at SLC requested a south flow to avoid tailwinds exceeding pilot limits, but a supervisor overruled the decision and removed the controller from duty. Separately, the controller reported a loss of vertical separation between two descending aircraft due to an incorrect assumption that the trailing aircraft would not catch up.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported an aircraft checked in climbing to the wrong altitude.
summary: An aircraft was climbing via the ORCKA SID to 12,000 feet. The narrative reports this climb but provides no further details regarding the cause or outcome.

synopsis: BUR Local Controller reported a possible runway incursion due to the close proximity of a taxiway and Runway 8.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Aircraft X taxiing with its nosewheel five feet right of the terminal line, potentially encroaching on Runway 8 while Aircraft Y was landing. The controller could not contact Aircraft X, which was likely on ground ops frequency, though Aircraft Y exited the runway before any collision occurred.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Portland TRACON Controller reported a loss of separation due to an aircraft overshooting assigned altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined sectors during an arrival rush issued a corrective descent to Aircraft X after it climbed to 7700 ft instead of the assigned 7000 ft. The controller attributed the altitude deviation to pilot confusion over the departure procedure and sector combination, resulting in a separation of 1.8–2 miles laterally and 400–600 ft vertically.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: PRC Tower Controller reported an unsafe operation when an aircraft had to maneuver out of the way of another aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller on Local 2 issued traffic advisories between Aircraft Y on Runway 3R and Aircraft X on Runway 3L during heavy VFR traffic. Aircraft X maneuvered to avoid a conflict with Aircraft Y on the crosswind, attributed to poor tower visibility and lack of Local Assist staffing, though no NMAC was reported.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller received a handoff on an RNAV departure climbing to the wrong altitude.
summary: An aircraft climbing via the ORCKA SID stopped at 12,000 feet instead of continuing to 23,000 feet. The TRACON Supervisor subsequently issued a clearance for the aircraft to proceed direct to LAX via the ORCKA.

synopsis: ZJX Center Controller worked a small aircraft and issued a suggested heading around weather, but the aircraft experienced major downdrafts.
summary: An air traffic controller advised Aircraft X on a weather heading and cleared it direct to destination. The aircraft subsequently descended from 8,000 feet to 2,600 feet over two minutes, prompting the controller to request more advanced equipment for weather assistance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: SCT Developmental Controller reported a loss of separation with a LAX departure and an aircraft going around.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a new Metroplex airspace lost situational awareness during a conflict between a departing aircraft and a go-around. The controller attributed the separation uncertainty to distraction by new procedures and delayed pilot responses, resulting in excessive maneuvering and unconfirmed climb clearances.

synopsis: ZLA controllers reported an airborne conflict when a departure aircraft entered their airspace without proper handoff from SCT TRACON.
summary: Sector 13 and 14 controllers observed two LAX departures on the ORCKA1 SID auto-popping into Sector 14 without a point-out, creating a potential conflict with an arrival at TANDY. The controller instructed the arrival to maintain visual separation, attributing the unsafe situation to confusion caused by new airspace limits and departure procedures.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an elevator feel malfunction. Post flight maintenance inspection revealed a significant amount of water in the elevator feel pitot tubes on the vertical stabilizer.
summary: The Captain reported heavy elevator feel and minimal displacement during takeoff and climb due to water in the elevator feel pitot tubes. Despite the non-normal response, the aircraft remained fully controllable, allowing for a safe landing without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: ERJ-170 Dispatcher and First Officer reported that due to strong headwinds flight planned to divert, however, winds decreased and Crew proceeded to destination but landed with less than reserve fuel.
summary: A dispatcher identified insufficient fuel on Aircraft X due to stronger-than-planned 180-knot winds, but the relieving dispatcher failed to enforce a diversion despite the crew's "get there-itis." The flight landed with 1,400 lbs fuel after a two-hour delay, though the original dispatcher noted the handover lacked effective flight management.

synopsis: Embraer EMB-145 flight crew reported descending with excessive speed due to misinterpretation of the charted speed restriction.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer exceeded arrival speed restrictions during descent into ZZZ due to confusion over speed reduction points and reduced vigilance. ATC vectored the aircraft off the arrival to prevent loss of separation, after which the crew corrected the airspeed and resumed the approach.

synopsis: The Captain of an Embraer EMB-175 reported adding control input to the aircraft because the First Officer did not rollout on heading.
summary: During climb-out on vectors, the Pilot Flying zoned out while hand-flying and failed to roll out on the assigned heading, overshooting by 10-20 degrees. The Pilot Monitoring intervened by placing hands on the controls, prompting an immediate correction and preventing a potential conflict with traffic 500 feet above.

synopsis: A319 pilot reported VHF communications were interrupted by data packet bursts on short final at DEN.
summary: During a night visual approach to Denver (DEN) on final for 35R between 200 and 300 feet AGL, the crew heard three VHF data packet bursts on Comm 1 tuned to Tower 133.3. These bursts, consistent with ACARS, briefly blocked a non-intended transmission but caused no other radio anomalies.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported they misunderstood Departure Controller's altitude assignment due to new phraseology associated with new OAPM RNAV departures.
summary: The flight crew and Departure controller experienced a missed altitude restriction at KEGGS after the crew leveled at 12,000 feet following an ambiguous "Climb via SID" clearance. The crew attributed the late climb to incomplete phraseology that failed to specify a target altitude, resulting in crossing KEGGS at 12,300 feet instead of the required 13,000 to 19,000 feet.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported the flying First Officer mistakenly retracted the flaps instead of the speedbrakes on approach. Fatigue was cited as a factor.
summary: During a visual approach, the First Officer mistakenly retracted flaps to 0 instead of speed brakes, causing an overspeed from 180 to 210 knots. The Pilot Monitoring corrected the configuration, and the crew attributed the error to fatigue from a two-day trip.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported that with the autopilot engaged the aileron appeared to be out of trim. With the autopilot disengaged the ailerons were extremely heavy.
summary: During cruise, pilots experienced high aileron control pressure and autopilot trim cautions caused by an unsecured main landing gear bay panel rubbing against control cables. The panel, left loose by mechanics during a prior inspection, shifted in high-speed airflow, but the aircraft landed safely after the condition resolved.

synopsis: Cessna 172 instructor reported that during landing the student encountered a sharp crosswind causing damage to the wingtip and propeller.
summary: A student pilot landing on Runway 09 encountered a sharp 15-knot crosswind gust at 5 feet, causing the right wing to strike the runway. The pilot's attempt to prevent a flip resulted in the propeller striking the ground, breaking the right wingtip and bending the propeller.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported rejecting takeoff when the First Officer noticed the TOGA button had not been pushed.
summary: The pilot and first officer rejected a takeoff at 80 knots during a repo flight because the TOGA button was not pressed, resulting in missing "ROLL TO" annunciations. The crew aborted safely, corrected the flight mode annunciator settings, and completed the flight after acknowledging a failure to cross-check standard procedures.

synopsis: Phenom 300 First Officer reported climbing in response to UES Tower issuing a low altitude alert during a night visual approach.
summary: During a night visual approach into UES, the SIC selected a lower altitude with the autopilot engaged, triggering a low altitude warning at 800 feet AGL. The aircraft climbed 300 feet and continued safely, but the report cites a lack of crew coordination and failure to disengage the autopilot as the cause.

synopsis: Air taxi pilot reported that a VFR aircraft which had them in sight flew too close to them.
summary: A pilot cruising at 8,000 feet reported a near-miss with a Cessna Skylane climbing VFR to within 300 feet after ATC issued a climb clearance while the aircraft was too close. The pilot attributed the incident to the controller failing to maintain separation or issue a heading change, noting the traffic blended with background buildings.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported during climb the Master Caution light came on and a Speed Trim light on the overhead panel illuminated.
summary: Maintenance personnel disabled the autopilot stab trim switch during preflight on a Boeing 737 without notifying the flight crew. The crew subsequently experienced autopilot engagement failure and a speed trim light, forcing an overweight emergency return to the departure airport after the switch was identified as off.

synopsis: The First Officer of a CRJ-900 reported hearing a loud sound of air escaping from behind the flight deck door.
summary: During cruise at FL340, a loud airflow noise from the forward galley prompted the flight crew to descend and divert to ZZZ1 due to unknown causes and weight restrictions. The aircraft landed safely with normal systems, though a prior forward cargo door issue was suspected as a potential cause.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that during taxi they lost control of the aircraft due to de-icing fluid on the taxiway.
summary: The pilot experienced a temporary loss of nose wheel steering and brakes while taxiing on a deicing fluid-slicked taxiway, causing the aircraft to drift toward the edge. Reverse thrust was used to regain control, and subsequent maintenance inspection found no evidence of a taxi light strike.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported several unusual maneuvers the FMC commanded to comply with restrictions for the SNA DSNEE1 Arrival.
summary: B737 pilots reported issues on the DSNEE 1 arrival into SNA, including steep descents requiring full speed brakes and premature deceleration to 220 knots. SoCal Approach advised flying the published arrival and requested a safety report, though the crew noted no limits were exceeded.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported that while in flight they received a 'Wheel N/W steering fault', possibly caused by an open hydraulic service panel.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nose wheel steering fault en-route due to an unsecured hydraulic service panel left open since pushback. After cycling the anti-skid switch in flight, the fault recurred on landing, requiring rudder and differential braking to exit the runway before being towed to the gate.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported a windshear alert just prior to touchdown. They elected to land rather than execute the windshear recovery as required by SOP.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate turbulence and a reactive windshear warning at 100–125 feet AGL during a Flaps 3 approach. They elected to land rather than execute a missed approach due to low fuel reserves, later acknowledging this violated SOPs but was justified by the aircraft's energy state and position.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported the towbar broke free and the nose gear rolled over the towbar. The ground crew did not connect the steering bypass pin.
summary: The flight crew experienced a tow incident at ZZZ where the ground crew failed to communicate or install the steering bypass pin. The tow bar broke free from the nose gear, causing the aircraft to roll over it and stop with the gear resting on the bar.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported that ATC did not keep them on the published arrival.
summary: During the lateral portion of the STOCR arrival into CLT, the flight crew descended to FL210 at 320 knots while disregarding published altitudes. ATC subsequently requested a speed reduction to 250 knots and issued vectors for spacing after questioning if the crew was flying published speeds.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported the crew started the wrong engine during an air start procedure.
summary: The Captain accidentally commanded an air start of engine one instead of engine two, placing a ground supervisor in the hazard area. The supervisor evacuated safely, and the event was caused by the Captain's inattention and the First Officer's lack of experience with irregular starting procedures.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported several boisterous, non conforming passengers boarded their flight and were determined to be under the influence of marijuana but were removed after a gate return. After a layover between flights, the same passengers were boarded on a connecting flight at a different airport.
summary: Flight attendants removed three intoxicated women from a taxiing aircraft after they consumed edibles and violated safety rules, but the same women boarded the crew's second flight hours later. Despite the crew's safety concerns and request to decline, they were pressured to fly with the passengers, who were cleared by police at the departure airport.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported they did not disarm the cabin door and subsequently the slide fell out of its pack, but did not fully deploy. Distraction was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: A cabin crew member acting as lead attendant failed to fully disarm the aircraft door while distracted by a gate agent's knock during a rushed deplaning. The agent subsequently opened the door, causing the slide to partially deploy due to the incomplete disarmament and the attendant's lack of experience.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight Attendants reported they received a chime signal followed by a very quick landing at ECP at night with several of them not in their jump seats.
summary: Flight attendants reported a sudden, jarring landing at ECP without visual ground cues due to the airport's lack of surrounding development. The captain attributed the abrupt touchdown to a quicker-than-expected landing clearance after initial confusion about a potential go-around.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA instructor pilot reported he stopped short of runway 21R at PDK when cleared across by Tower to avoid another aircraft doing a touch and go.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing a landed aircraft at PDK, crossed runway 21R after clearance, assuming an arriving aircraft was stopping. The pilot stopped just short of the runway surface upon realizing the other aircraft was performing a touch-and-go, avoiding a collision.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported he picked up an IFR clearance in the air from ZLA which stated 'upon reaching one zero thousand, cleared to destination.' Pilot reported he climbed through a cloud layer to reach his cruise altitude and questioned the legality of this behavior.
summary: A pilot picking up an IFR clearance from ZLA while VFR below clouds entered IMC before reaching the "upon reaching 10,000" altitude restriction. The reporter noted this created a conflict between the clearance validity and the need to climb through clouds, suggesting controllers should explicitly allow climbing through IMC to the minimum vectoring altitude.

synopsis: The Captain of a Bombardier CRJ-700 reported that the First Officer was flying and was 3000 ft lower than assigned altitude.
summary: During the CAVLR Three arrival into Washington Dulles, the First Officer descended 3,000 feet below the assigned 22,000 feet at the initial fix after misreading the FMS while the Captain managed multiple tasks. The Captain regained altitude but continued the descent with no conflict, attributing the error to the First Officer's lack of mid-size aircraft experience and excessive workload.

synopsis: Aeronca Champion instructor pilot reported the engine began surging while at cruise. They were able to make a landing at a nearby airport.
summary: During a training cruise at 2,300 feet, a student pilot experienced an uncommanded engine power drop to 700 RPM, prompting the instructor to take control. The instructor maintained altitude by rapidly cycling the throttle to surge the engine, allowing a safe landing at ZZZ airport while first responders were alerted.

synopsis: Pilot of a PA-46 reported aborting his takeoff from a turf runway and hit an area of loose soil that collapsed the nose gear.
summary: The pilot aborted a takeoff from a turf runway at 55–60 knots. During deceleration, the aircraft entered loose soil, causing the nose gear to collapse and the aircraft to stop nose down on the cowling.

synopsis: C-172 pilot reported that while attempting to get into VFR conditions he climbed through clouds without an IFR rating or an IFR flight plan.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot departed ZZZ airport for ZZZ1 but returned due to obscured mountains. Pressed by deadlines, the pilot attempted a VFR climb through clouds, violating FARs due to poor climb performance judgment and human factors, before safely exiting the cloud layer.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot who had flight plan approval to operate in a special use airspace reported having their flight plan cancelled by ATC after stopping on the ground for a short period of time.
summary: A pilot conducting multiple traffic patterns at FME within the Washington SFRA had their flight plan prematurely closed by PCT TRACON after a 20-40 minute ground delay for student coaching. The controller closed the plan due to the transponder code disappearing, leaving the pilot operating without a current flight plan until another aircraft alerted them to contact ATC.

synopsis: A ZSU Center Controller reported they were forced to combine sectors against their wishes. The Controller assigned a climb rate to an aircraft but the aircraft did not comply with the instruction.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a combined sector in San Juan issued a descent clearance to Aircraft X at 29,000 feet to avoid conflicting traffic at 27,000 feet. Due to poor frequency coverage, the pilot could not hear the controller, requiring the Controller in Charge to coordinate with Santa Domingo Center to re-establish contact.

synopsis: Chicago Center Controller reported an aircraft was having mechanical problems, wanted to go to an alternate. Aircraft landed at intended airport with a damaged tire.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers vectored Aircraft X, experiencing elevator control issues and unable to maintain altitude, from the D-Track to ZZZ2. The pilot accepted an ILS approach to runway 4, descended through 8,000 and 3,000 MSL, and landed safely with a damaged tire.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A ZID Center controller cleared an aircraft for an approach than noticed it turn off course into higher terrain below their Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An IFR training pilot deviated south during a Localizer Runway 25 approach due to equipment issues, while the controller faced radio transmission failures. The controller used an alternate transmitter to instruct the pilot to climb to 6400 feet near terrain, allowing the aircraft to rejoin the localizer safely.

synopsis: B737NG Pilot reported the aircraft navigated off course on its own.
summary: The flight crew departed Runway 25R and climbed unrestricted to 19,000 feet but inadvertently switched to HDG mode instead of LNAV. ATC noted this was the fourth occurrence that night when they queried the crew about an early turn toward BOACH.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported they did not turn on the pressurization pack valves and consequently the aircraft did not pressurize.
summary: The flight crew of a 737 experienced abnormal pressurization and a rumbling noise during climb after inadvertently leaving pack switches off due to strobe glare and complacency. They returned to ZZZ for a precautionary landing after discovering the error and resetting the packs to auto.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported that the Jeppesen Electronic Flight Bag and the FMC database have different update times.
summary: Pilots departing LAX experienced confusion when their EFB JeppFD-Pro application automatically updated to the OSHNN7 SID while the FMC database remained valid for the OSHNN6 SID. Although the crew manually selected the correct charts to avoid an error, ATC questioned their departure, indicating other crews had likely flown the incorrect OSHNN7 procedure due to this database misalignment.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported that the 'climb via' verbiage used for climbing instructions is flawed.
summary: A 29,000-hour pilot reported that repeated FAA instructions on climb phraseology created a distraction during the climb phase. The pilot stated that the confusing variations forced a mental pause while managing aircraft configuration and navigation, posing an unnecessary threat due to flawed human factors.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported experiencing a possible false terrain warning while in the initial phase of approach in a mountainous terrain area in clear VMC night conditions. An escape maneuver was executed as a precaution.
summary: The flight crew received a GPWS "terrain, terrain, pull up" warning at 11,000 feet while being vectored for a visual approach to RWY 12 at BZN. They executed a terrain escape maneuver, but ATC stated no terrain issue existed and cleared them to descend to 7,000 feet for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported losing a portion of a nose gear door just after takeoff. Flight returned to the departure airport and landed normally.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud noise and vibration after gear retraction during takeoff, suspecting a nose gear door issue despite no warnings. They returned to the departure airport, where inspection revealed the follow-up door had separated from the aircraft.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported that extreme winds at LAS created unsafe landing conditions. The flight diverted to a nearby airport with more safe conditions and landed normally.
summary: The flying pilot diverted a flight to LAS to ZZZ due to severe wind shear and turbulence that caused an unstable approach and go-around. During the diversion, the pilot accidentally advanced throttles to MAX detent while overriding auto-throttles, resulting in a maintenance check before returning to LAS.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported multiple go-arounds due to wind shear alerts from ATC at DEN, he finally decided to land on runway 26 with a crosswind very close to limits.
summary: The flight crew executed three go-arounds at Denver due to wind shear and microburst alerts on Runway 16L, eventually landing on Runway 26 in 30-knot crosswinds after declaring low fuel. The pilot attributed the difficulty to inadequate dispatch support regarding alternate options and requested clearer guidance on wind shear decision-making and crosswind limitations.

synopsis: Citation 750 flight crew reported a pressurization malfunction and requested priority handling from ATC to their destination airport. While dealing with the malfunction they accidently landed at the wrong airport.
summary: The crew of a flight descending through 38,000 feet experienced a cabin altitude warning and subsequently landed at the wrong airport (ZZZ2) instead of ZZZ1. The pilot attributed the error to task saturation caused by the pressurization issue, multiple ATC instructions, and similar airport alignments.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported that they rejected takeoff due to a misconfigured flap position.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a "No Take Off - Flaps" warning during takeoff due to the MCDU flap setting not matching the selected Flaps 4 configuration. The incident was attributed to complacency and poor Crew Resource Management, requiring a runway exit and checklist re-verification before a successful departure.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a repair made to his aircraft by a non-mechanic. This repair was made by a ramp manager then an actual Mechanic came out shortly after to re-do the repair correctly.
summary: A Ramp Manager unauthorizedly concealed damaged insulation tubing in the Passenger Service Unit to expedite turnaround, delaying departure by 11 minutes until a mechanic properly secured it. The pilot attributed this safety violation to management pressure for on-time performance despite understaffing and lack of training.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a GPWS warning while on approach over terrain at night.
summary: Pilots inbound to AVL received a GPWS "TERRAIN, PULL-UP" warning 10 miles northwest of the airport during a visual approach to runway 17. The crew attributed the alert to a high descent rate near terrain and executed a climb before completing a stabilized landing.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a break away from the tow bar during push back, requiring the aircraft to be stopped abruptly when the tug driver called for the brakes to be set, with the aircraft in motion.
summary: During pushback, a faulty headset and unsecured tow bar caused the aircraft to roll backward unattached, prompting the pilot to brake aggressively. A flight attendant was injured, leading to a return to the gate for maintenance inspection before a safe departure.

synopsis: G280 Captain reported an issue with ATC in regards to understanding best forward speed.
summary: The pilot of a G280 descending in ZZZ maintained best forward speed while ATC requested 320 knots, causing a misunderstanding due to decreasing VMO limits. The controller asked for speed updates, but the pilot believes no separation was lost and plans to clarify ambiguous airspeed clearances in the future.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: M20 pilot reported encountering IMC conditions while flying VFR. He elected to divert to an enroute field and wait for the weather to pass before continuing to his destination.
summary: A VFR pilot flying at 3500 feet entered IFR conditions and climbed to 10,500 feet, but was informed by Center that "VFR on Top" is invalid and that the pilot was not IFR current. The pilot reversed course, landed at a nearby airport in VFR conditions, and later resumed the flight after the weather cleared.

synopsis: C-172 instructor pilot reported a failure in CTAF communication by another aircraft on short final when they reported taking active runway and crossing the hold line.
summary: A student pilot and instructor crossed the hold short line for Runway 21 at an uncontrolled airport after hearing no conflicting radio calls. They stopped immediately upon being notified by a Cessna on short final, which subsequently landed safely on the runway.

synopsis: Bonanza 35 pilot reported a runway excursion during takeoff roll.
summary: A solo pilot conducting a VFR takeoff in a single-engine aircraft veered sharply left after releasing excessive right rudder pressure, allowing P-factor to push the aircraft off the runway. The pilot aborted the takeoff, experienced a brief bounce and stall, and came to a stop in high grass with no injuries or smoke.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported being distracted by an unlatched cabin door and climbed into Class B airspace. This situation was exacerbated by an incorrect altimeter setting.
summary: A pilot flying a high-performance aircraft with an Aspen Evolution 1000 PFD entered Class Bravo airspace at 1500 MSL during departure due to an incorrect altimeter setting in the backup steam gauge. The deviation resulted from a split instrument scan and distractions caused by an unlatched passenger door and unfamiliarity with the aircraft.

synopsis: B737 fight crew and ATC reported a B737 requested an intersection takeoff, but when the crew began to increase taxi speed, ATC perceived it as the takeoff roll and commanded the crew to stop.
summary: A B737 crew misread charts and accelerated on closed Taxiway E instead of Runway XYL for an E4 departure after ATC cleared them for takeoff. The controller ordered the aircraft to stop before it could enter the barricaded area, preventing a runway incursion.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZDC Controller and the pilot involved reported that the aircraft lost both engines and landed successfully at a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X experienced a dual engine failure in IMC while descending to 13,000 feet north of Greensboro. After ATC vectored the aircraft to DAN, the pilot executed a safe landing with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Two Center Traffic Management Specialists and a Controller report the Command Center ignored requests for weather reroutes, causing numerous Center sectors to be dangerously overloaded with traffic deviating for weather.
summary: ZFW controllers and Command Center managed weather re-routes for eastbound and westbound traffic, but Command Center refused to publish structured routes for all affected aircraft. This caused unmanageable traffic volume and data block overlap in ZFW sectors, creating an unsafe situation the controller attributed to poor planning decisions made outside the facility.

synopsis: Chicago TRACON Instructor reported that an aircraft was turned off final, into a lower Minimum Vectoring Altitude area. Aircraft was then instructed to a different heading in order to exit the lower MVA area.
summary: During a training session, an instructor's trainee vectored Aircraft X into a 3300ft MVA while attempting to maintain sequence in 60kt winds. The instructor corrected the error by directing a climb, but the maneuver resulted in less than standard wake turbulence separation with the succeeding aircraft.

synopsis: Salt Lake Center Controllers reported problems associated with a refueling operation and air traffic close proximity to a Restricted Airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a refueling mission involving Aircraft X, Y, and Z near the Mountain Home Range Complex, where military flights entered airspace without clearances and violated RVSM requirements. The controller admitted to potential loss of separation between Aircraft X and Y due to complex coordination failures and an incomplete position relief briefing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a NMAC with a small aircraft while on descent to AUS on the WLEEE3 Arrival in Class E airspace.
summary: During descent into Austin, a crew flying an RNAV arrival encountered a small aircraft at 5200 ft while leveling at 5000 ft after an ATC clearance. The intruder passed close on the right without TCAS alerts or traffic advisories, prompting the crew to report the incident and recommend mandatory Mode C transponders in Class E airspace.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported that the ILS Critical Area hold sign for runway 13R at DAL was located in a position which caused confusion and a runway incursion.
summary: The pilot and First Officer crossed Runway 18 while taxiing to Runway 13R, mistakenly identifying the ILS critical area hold short sign as being for Runway 18. The pilot attributed the error to the sign's distance and noted frustration that these hold short areas are not depicted on the 10-9 chart.

synopsis: Crewmember of large turbojet reported a dispute with the Captain in regards to the correct arrival procedure into the destination airport.
summary: The First Officer discovered an unsafe STAR with a mountain-crossing discontinuity during approach, but the Captain verbally assaulted and ordered him out of the seat. An International Relief Officer intervened to confirm the error, allowing the First Officer to load the correct STAR and execute a safe descent after passing the TOD.

synopsis: A Boeing 737 flight crew reported experiencing a hard landing due to an insufficient flare technique at touchdown. As a result, several injuries were reported.
summary: During a First Officer's initial Boeing 737 landing in flaps 40, the pilot failed to flare due to tail strike concerns and misjudged height, causing a hard landing at 2.5 degrees pitch. While initial checks reported no issues, four flight attendants later reported neck injuries.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported clear air turbulence that resulted in a flight attendant injury.
summary: During climb at 19,000 ft MSL, clear air turbulence occurred, potentially injuring a flight attendant in the aft galley. The crew requested medical personnel, who met the aircraft upon arrival, while passengers deplaned normally.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported poor climb performance passing FL300 and discovered the right engine to be at idle thrust. Thrust lever movement had no effect on thrust and it was decided to shut the engine down and restart it, which was done successfully. After restart the engine functioned normally.
summary: During climb through FL300, the crew noticed the right engine fuel flow was low and unresponsive to throttle, with no EICAS alerts. They performed an inflight shutdown and restart via QRH checklists; the engine restarted normally, allowing the flight to continue to destination and land uneventfully.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported three windshear go-arounds during approaches to DEN Runway 16L. After declaring a low fuel alert, a successful landing was accomplished on Runway 26.
summary: The crew encountered multiple windshear alerts and microburst advisories during three failed approaches to Denver runway 16L, necessitating go-arounds. They subsequently declared low fuel and landed safely on runway 26 after switching runways due to gusty crosswinds exceeding limitations.

synopsis: The Captain of a Cessna business jet reported encountering mountain wave conditions followed by extreme turbulence. The result was a temporary loss of aircraft control, followed by a precautionary landing at a diversion airport.
summary: The pilot encountered extreme mountain wave turbulence while climbing through FL350 near the front range, causing the aircraft to become uncontrollable with airspeed exceeding Vmo. After disengaging the autopilot to reduce speed to Vturb, the crew regained control and diverted with ATC priority handling.

synopsis: Air carrier Airbus A321 Lead Technician reported that after finding damage to an A321 outboard flap fairing he misinterpreted the specifications for allowable damage.
summary: A fuel truck struck the right outboard flap fairing during ground fueling, causing honeycomb damage. Although initial manual review suggested the damage was allowable, damage professionals determined it exceeded limits, requiring fairing removal and release under a Configuration Deviation List.

synopsis: A commercial pilot instructing a UAS ground school class at 3G3 Airport (Wadsworth, OH) was confronted by an aircraft pilot who accused him of flying in Class D airspace. His UAS flew below CLE Class B and outside CAK Class C.
summary: Two Remote Pilots in Command demonstrated drones on a taxiway while a Cherokee PA-28 landed and cleared the runway. The fixed-wing pilot accused them of illegal operations in Class D airspace, but the drone pilots clarified they were operating legally under Part 107 in Class G airspace.

synopsis: Pilot of a Cessna 172 reported a brake failure resulting in a taxiway excursion.
summary: During taxi out from a regional airport, the pilot experienced a right brake failure on Taxiway Charlie, causing the aircraft to drift left onto the grass. The crew shut down the engine, and rescue trucks and a tow tug returned the aircraft to the maintenance hangar for repairs.

synopsis: BE90 Pilot reported an electrical failure after takeoff and returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a complete electrical failure during departure, causing landing gear and instrument malfunctions. After contacting Approach to return, the aircraft landed safely with gear down and was taxied to maintenance.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A C90 Controller and one of the two pilots involved reported an airborne conflict in C90 airspace.
summary: A C206 VFR pilot and a C525 IFR jet experienced a near miss near ZZZ while the C206 descended rapidly through 7,000 feet to avoid 90-knot headwinds. The controller attributed the incident to not anticipating the C206's fast descent rate, while the pilot cited extreme wind conditions as the cause.

synopsis: Jacksonville Controller reported confusion about aircraft RVSM compliance while the aircraft crew were waiting for a certificate.
summary: An air traffic controller in sector R33 noticed conflicting RVSM status remarks for Aircraft X en route to PNS, where the flight plan indicated capability but remarks cited pending paperwork. The controller reported the discrepancy to Quality Control, which investigated a potential pilot deviation, though the Operations Manager initially confirmed the aircraft was legal.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported a problem with the rudder trim which eventually resulted in the flight diverting to an enroute field.
summary: The flight crew experienced a 15-degree right yoke trim and inoperative right rudder trim at FL 390. After verifying circuit breakers and consulting Dispatch, they diverted due to discomfort continuing over water and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: A319 captain reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning while being vectored for an approach the Eugene Airport (KEUG). An escape maneuver was successfully performed.
summary: The flight crew received a GPWS terrain warning at 4,400 ft while being vectored by Cascade Approach for an ILS to runway 16R at EUG. They executed an escape maneuver to 6,000 ft, noting the highest terrain was 3,400 ft and that Approach reported similar incidents in the area.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a contradiction from standard operating procedures when asked to release the brakes prior to push clearance to facilitate use of a new style tug.
summary: Ground crew requested the flight crew release brakes to pull the aircraft onto a new hydraulic tug plate, violating the pilot's SOP to release brakes only after receiving clearance. The reporter noted this request, while logical for the equipment, conflicted with standard operating procedures.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a fuel distribution irregularity due to improper fueling procedures. After determining that center of gravity limits were satisfied, the aircraft was dispatched.
summary: The crew discovered all fuel was in the inner tanks with closed transfer valves after fueling on battery power, causing multiple load plan corrections and a departure delay. The Flight Manual did not address empty outer tanks, but fuel transferred to them within one hour after takeoff.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the SNA DSNEE 1 RNAV Optimized Profile Descent (OPD) altitude constraints between ROADE at 17,000-FL190 and PHIYA at or below 13,000 ft are beyond B737 descent capabilities.
summary: The B737 crew reported an impossible crossing restriction at ROADE on the DSNEE1 RNAV into SNA, causing repeated "TOO STEEP" FMC messages. SoCal Approach Control acknowledged the issue and granted latitude to deviate, as the required descent exceeds aircraft capabilities.

synopsis: A Gate Agent reported being asked to operate the jet bridge to the aircraft during severe lightning.
summary: Customer service representatives operating a jet bridge to an unchocked aircraft during severe lightning face safety risks. The reporter cites a past incident where three agents were injured by a lightning strike and warns that wind could move the aircraft, damaging both the bridge and the plane.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported shutting down the right engine after observing a right oil filter Status message.
summary: The crew of a 767 at FL320 encountered a persistent R Oil Filter EICAS message, prompting a descent to FL240 and a right engine shutdown per QRH procedures after consulting maintenance experts. The aircraft was rerouted and landed uneventfully at ZZZZ.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain unfamiliar with the CLT ramp reported a taxiway incursion incident. Ramp markings were cited as contributing factors.
summary: A pilot reported deviating from the ramp to Taxiway M at Charlotte (CLT) at night due to poor, damaged, or missing markings on wet surfaces. The pilot attributed the incident to inadequate maintenance of ground markings and lighting, recommending progressive taxi instructions and improved signage to prevent future errors.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reported a temporary loss of control due to severe turbulence.
summary: The crew encountered severe, undetectable turbulence at FL360, causing autopilot disconnection, stick shaker activation, and an uncommanded climb to FL375. The pilot manually controlled the aircraft, descended back to FL360, and advised ATC and dispatch to deviate from the forecasted moderate turbulence area.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported several go-arounds due to windshear warnings at DTW, then finally landed during a windshear caution alert on the third approach.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe windshear and turbulence during three approaches to DTW, executing two escape maneuvers and declaring minimum fuel. The final landing involved a flap overspeed event caused by an unexpected airspeed gain, which the pilot attributed to inadequate preflight weather assessment and the decision not to divert.

synopsis: A flight attendant reported that a passenger had a razor blade out.
summary: A passenger possessed a razor blade during taxi out. The crew secured the item and handed it to TSA upon landing, with the passenger remaining cooperative throughout the incident.

synopsis: B737-700 Flight Attendant reported that the new storage location for the emergency medical kit does not allow the kit to be accessed in flight due to conflict with the slide bustle when the door is closed.
summary: A flight attendant on a 737-700 reported being unable to retrieve the relocated First Aid Kit from compartment C-10 during flight due to interference from the slide bussel. The kit could only be removed after landing with the door open, an issue confirmed on other aircraft in the fleet.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant crew reported a strange odor on the aircraft during descent, all crew members affected and went to the hospital. Lead Flight Attendant recommended that they should also be trained to use portable oxygen during fume events.
summary: During descent, four flight attendants and the flight deck crew detected a strong, unusual odor, causing symptoms like chest pain, dizziness, and metallic taste. The entire crew was hospitalized post-landing for evaluation, where the reporter recorded elevated blood pressure and questioned carbon monoxide levels, attributing the incident to toxic fumes.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported a lack of communication from the cockpit during descent in severe turbulence.
summary: Cabin crew reported severe turbulence during approach to ZZZ airport, citing 41-mph gusts and violent aircraft movements without prior captain notification. The captain later dismissed the lack of communication, claiming announcements would not have changed the outcome, despite crew concerns over poor CRM and safety.

synopsis: Cabin crew reported strong fumes in the cabin after application of takeoff power, that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: During take-off, fumes entered the cabin, prompting cabin crew to notify the flight deck. The flight deck advised returning to the departure airport.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported a strong odor in the aircraft during boarding. When many passengers and cabin crew members began to feel ill, the Captain decided to have the passengers exit the aircraft.
summary: Cabin crew and passengers experienced fumes, headaches, and coughing during boarding, prompting the Captain to halt the process and deplane everyone. The incident was caused by a strong odor detected in the flight deck and cabin, with symptoms persisting for some crew members after re-entry.

synopsis: A330 flight attendants reported an aircraft evacuation at the gate due to heavy smoke in the passenger cabin.
summary: A flight attendant reported that despite mechanics warning against boarding, an agent boarded passengers on a defective aircraft, leading to an electrical fire and heavy smoke in the cabin. The crew evacuated passengers after the Captain initially ordered a stop, citing pressure to depart as the primary cause of the unsafe situation.

synopsis: The flight attendants of an Airbus A330 reported a musty sock odor in the cabin during takeoff and continued during flight. Many required medical attention.
summary: Flight attendants and the captain reported a strong musty odor in the cabin during takeoff that persisted to landing, causing crew nausea and headaches. Medical evaluation was delayed by over two hours due to ground handling failures, though blood tests eventually returned normal results.

synopsis: Four B757 flight attendants reported two fume events at the gate prior to push back. After the second event the flight attendants were taken to the hospital and the aircraft was taken out of service.
summary: Four flight attendants experienced two fume events on board an aircraft during preflight and boarding, causing severe symptoms like nausea and shaking. The crew was hospitalized for treatment, and passengers were deplaned after the captain attributed the incident to a ventilation and air conditioning system failure.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant and Captain reported smelling a strong burn-off or fuel smell during takeoff, then once again after landing.
summary: Flight attendants and passengers reported strong fume odors and irritation during takeoff and taxi-in, which the captain initially deemed safe to continue. Contract maintenance failed to duplicate the issue, but company maintenance later found a significant hole in the low-pressure duct.

synopsis: MD500 pilot reported a NMAC after taking off without contacting the control Tower.
summary: A new helicopter pilot departed without contacting the tower due to first-day pressure and excitement, resulting in a 300-foot vertical and 100-foot horizontal separation from an approaching landing helicopter. The pilot subsequently contacted the tower, received instructions to call upon landing, and acknowledged the error was caused by rushing and nervousness.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported entering 'KLINE' into the FMS instead of the correct spelling 'KLYNE.' The two fixes are in close proximity and the error was not initially apparent.
summary: The pilot en route to ROD entered "KLINE" instead of the cleared fix "KLYNE" in the FMS, causing an unintended left turn. After ATC queried the position, the crew corrected the entry to KLYNE, resulting in a right turn with no traffic conflict, prompting a recommendation to rename one of the similarly pronounced fixes.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reported engine roughness so the pilot turned back toward the departure airport, but the engine quit completely and an off airport landing was successfully accomplished.
summary: The pilot of a Piper Cherokee 6 experienced an engine shudder followed by a complete shutdown while en route north of ZZZ. After declaring an emergency, the pilot successfully executed a forced landing in an open field with no injuries to the pilot or passenger.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain reported being cleared to taxi via the northern route to Runway 24L, but did not hold short of Taxiway D as required by the standard taxi route description.
summary: The flight crew followed ground clearance to taxi via the northern route to Runway 24L but encountered a stationary Airbus A320 on Delta taxiway. A controller instructed them to hold, stating the northern route terminates at Sierra and Delta, a restriction not depicted on the airport diagram or included in the clearance.

synopsis: A Line Check Airman reported the flying pilot executed a rejected take off at rotation for no apparent reason resulting in stopping in the overrun and prompting an evacuation.
summary: A Check Airman Captain and a flying Captain conducted an OE training takeoff where the flying pilot aborted after V1 without announcing it, causing the aircraft to overrun the runway by 1,000 feet. The crew evacuated all passengers and crew safely despite VMC conditions and no reported windshear or airspeed fluctuations.

synopsis: A corporate pilot reported severe mountain wave activity and a brief moderate clear air turbulence encounter which disconnected the autopilot along with a 600 foot altitude loss.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate clear air turbulence and severe mountain wave activity while cruising at FL350 after an ATC vector, causing autopilot disconnect and a 600-foot altitude loss. The crew notified ATC, received a reroute offer, and recovered without injuries or further issues.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE-525 pilot reported diverting after observing a master warning and cabin altitude annunciator while climbing through 13,000 feet.
summary: During climb through 13,000 feet MSL, the crew observed a master warning and high cabin altitude, suspecting a door or seal issue despite normal indicators. The flight was diverted to another airport as continuing the planned route was deemed unsafe.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported insufficient action was taken by the Traffic Management Units to prevent sectors from being overloaded when forecast weather manifested.
summary: An air traffic controller reported an unprecedented volume of overflight aircraft in the ZFW sector due to weather forming in ZKC, with no Traffic Management Unit plan enacted. The controller attributed the excessive handoffs and operational chaos to the lack of a timely TMU response or established playbook for the forecasted weather.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported an aircraft violated Class C airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller tracked a Cessna that violated CMH Class C airspace for 12 minutes and crossed a departure corridor. Although the controller identified the aircraft via ADSB and requested contact, the pilot failed to respond, preventing safety education despite a similar violation occurring the previous week.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported severe turbulence encounter while on climbout from Denver.
summary: The flight crew encountered sudden severe turbulence at FL260 during climbout from DEN, causing autopilot disengagement and difficult control. No injuries were reported, and the crew decided to continue to the destination, landing without incident before logging the event for maintenance.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported an irate passenger began banging on the flight deck door while the aircraft was waiting for a gate.
summary: Pilots and cabin crew reported an irate passenger banging on the flight deck door while the aircraft waited on the ramp with one engine running. Law enforcement met the aircraft, questioned the passenger who claimed to be bipolar and off medication, and escorted him out of the secure area after a verbal warning.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported asking for clarification regarding visibility values while landing in SEQM. Flying First Officer was able to pick up the runway environment visually at 500 feet AGL and adjusted for a landing.
summary: The First Officer flew an ILS approach to Runway 36 at Quito where the approach controller failed to provide visibility values despite three requests. The crew received an RVR of 600 meters from the tower, corrected two sink rate calls during the final descent, and landed normally.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported an unstable approach as a result of gusty winds at the end of a divert from another airport also experiencing gusty winds.
summary: The crew diverted to PIT after two missed approaches at ZZZ due to winds exceeding 50 knots. Despite gusts up to 53 knots and an unstable approach at 500 feet, the Captain landed safely on Runway 28L to avoid fuel exhaustion, noting that ZZZ's 2-minute average wind reports may have obscured actual conditions.

synopsis: A B777 flight crew departed VHHH flying the OCEAN 2 RNAV. After ATC removed the 220 knot constraint the MCP speed select was changed but the FMC remained at 220 knots which prevented the aircraft from accelerating after flap retraction.
summary: During a heavy B777 departure from VHHH, the crew experienced multiple autopilot disconnects and autothrottle retardations caused by an unremoved 220-knot FMC speed restriction. The Flight Crew intervened to lower flaps and hand-fly the aircraft, preventing a stall while the Captain corrected the speed setting on the MCP.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported a severe turbulence event in oceanic airspace. Captain stated they experienced a 1,500 foot loss of altitude during the event.
summary: The crew encountered unforecast severe turbulence at FL360 while attempting to avoid moderate turbulence, causing loss of autopilot and autothrottle control. Stick shaker warnings occurred, and the aircraft gained 1,500 feet before the crew manually maintained control for three to four minutes.

synopsis: Motor glider pilot experienced a 'loose' rudder during a turn with the engine off and turned towards a near by airport. After landing the rudder separated from the aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying a G109B motor glider experienced a loose rudder during a turn while gliding on a ridge with the engine off. The pilot landed safely but suffered side-loading due to crosswind misalignment, causing the rudder to detach completely after the aircraft drifted into the grass.

synopsis: C177 pilot on pipeline patrol reported running out of fuel and landing on a gravel road.
summary: A pilot flying a pipeline patrol aircraft experienced an engine failure 15 miles from ZZZ due to higher-than-expected fuel consumption from improper mixture settings. The pilot safely executed an off-airport landing on a gravel road after the engine quit.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: BHM Tower Controller observed vehicles entering a taxiway without approval causing an aircraft to suddenly stop.
summary: Aircraft X, taxiing to the ramp after landing, was forced to stop when three trucks crossed Taxiway Alpha without ATC approval. Although a cautionary advisory was issued, the vehicles proceeded proactively, creating a conflict on the movement area.
