synopsis: A light transport aircraft Captain reported crop dusters at PRN that did not make radio reports and landed and departed in opposite directions.
summary: The crew of a VFR arrival at PRN experienced a runway incursion with an Air Tractor landing on the opposite runway while they were exiting. The reporter attributes the near-miss to the spraying aircraft's unpredictable low-level patterns and failure to make radio calls on CTAF.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on final to SEA Runway 16R in trail of a B737.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 737 while on final to ILS 16R in IMC, causing 15-degree wing rolls and requiring additional power. The aircraft flew above the glideslope with no further encounter, though the pilot noted a lack of ATC wake turbulence advisories.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot of a small aircraft departing an uncontrolled airport reported a near miss with a helicopter departing at the same time.
summary: During departure from EHR, a pilot encountered a non-broadcasting helicopter within 200 feet that did not appear on TCAS or respond to CTAF calls. The pilot executed a right turn and continued climbing to establish separation from the parallel-flying helicopter.

synopsis: DA-20 pilot reported landing in a field about 1 mile short of their destination due to engine failure.
summary: A pilot flying a local VFR flight to break in a new engine experienced a total engine failure on final approach due to forgetting to activate the fuel prime switch. The pilot executed a successful power-off landing short of the intended runway after realizing the error during post-flight review.

synopsis: CE-560XL flight crew reported altitude excursion while flying the RUUDY5 SID from TEB. Both reporters mention the Captain's misunderstanding of NACO charts as a contributing factor.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported that the Captain misread a government chart while flying the RUUDY5 departure from TEB, causing the aircraft to cross WENTZ at 2,000 feet instead of the required 1,500 feet. The deviation resulted from the Captain selecting heading mode instead of NAV mode and failing to observe the intermediate crossing restriction due to unfamiliarity with government charts.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: CMH TRACON Controller reported their NIDS (NAS Information Display System) routinely fails to depict current adverse weather conditions.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that while Aircraft X and Y descended into Dayton in extreme weather, the NAS Information Display System repeatedly lost critical data feeds. This equipment failure prevented timely transmission of weather, RVR, and windshear information to the pilots, creating ongoing safety issues.

synopsis: A Ground Controller reported detecting a pilot taxiing displayed signs of being inebriated. The Controller had airport operations and law enforcement meet the airplane.
summary: Ground and Local Controllers detected a pilot's slurred speech and incorrect runway requests while taxiing Aircraft X. Airport operations confirmed the pilot was intoxicated, leading to his arrest for DUI after he returned the aircraft to the hangar.

synopsis: A Controller reported observing an aircraft descend below its assigned crossing altitude and into an underlying sector.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a corporate jet violated Sector 22 by descending below the 24,000-foot "at or above" restriction at TERIA while executing the ZELKA1 STAR. The controller issued a maintain FL220 clearance and noted this was a recurring issue with business jets on this specific arrival.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Tower Local Controller reported not observing that an aircraft was landing on the wrong runway until it was over the landing threshold. The Controller issued go-around instructions which the pilot did not comply with.
summary: The Local Controller and pilot of aircraft X were involved at CCR during the approach and landing phase. The pilot, unfamiliar with the airport layout, mistakenly landed on inactive Runway 1L instead of cleared Runway 32R, prompting a go-around for a following aircraft due to ground vehicles on the wrong runway.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: SCT TRACON Controllers reported a Controller forgot to issue a coordinated heading to an aircraft so it turned on its filed route into confliction with other traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller forgot to issue a 140-degree heading to Aircraft Y at DARTS, causing it to turn left toward Aircraft X landing Runway 33 at BUR. The controller corrected the conflict by turning Aircraft X right and Aircraft Y south, though separation distance remains uncertain.

synopsis: SEA Local Controller reported an A321 climbed at a slower than normal and expected airspeed resulting in the subsequent departure overtaking the A321.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a separation issue between departing A321 Aircraft X and Aircraft Y when X failed to accelerate. The controller capped Y's altitude at 3000 feet despite a Mode C discrepancy and encountered unprofessional resistance from the departure controller during coordination.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ORD Local Controller reported issuing an aircraft a go-around was then issued nonstandard go-around instructions by the Departure Controller.
summary: An aircraft departure hit a coyote on Runway 9L, causing a closure and missed approaches for Aircraft X and Y. The controller shipped Aircraft Y to Departure before full coordination, later learning Aircraft X received a non-standard climb to 6,000 feet, highlighting a need for better ORD Tower and C90 communication.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the FO over-rotated after takeoff and got a momentary stick shaker before reducing pitch.
summary: The First Officer experienced an over-rotation and stick shaker activation during takeoff due to distraction and rushing. Later, the Captain nearly caused a stall by pitching toward the new dual-cue flight director display, mistaking it for legacy V-bars, requiring the First Officer to intervene.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing loss of the B hydraulic system.
summary: The crew experienced a total loss of B hydraulic fluid and pressure at cruise, prompting a divert and overweight landing. Mechanics later advised that the B electric pump should have been shut off immediately to prevent cavitation, raising concerns that continued operation could have caused an engine fire.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the parking brake would not release after it was set while holding short of the runway for takeoff. Passengers and crew were removed and Maintenance took over the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew held short of the runway when the parking brakes failed to release after clearance for takeoff. Maintenance could not disengage the brakes, requiring passengers to deplane on the taxiway before the crew secured a replacement aircraft and departed hours late.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported that the First Officer's O2 mask did not test properly.
summary: The Captain reported a faulty First Officer oxygen mask test switch during preflight, which mechanics eventually replaced but failed to secure properly. At FL380, the unsecured mask assembly detached from the panel, rendering the quick-don feature useless and creating a serious safety risk during a potential rapid decompression.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported that an anti-skid MEL issue was not able to be included in a takeoff performance data calculation which caused the crew to takeoff with incorrect data.
summary: The crew deferred the anti-skid system, requiring Max Thrust, but Dispatch failed to apply the MEL to the takeoff performance data due to ACARS limitations and lack of training. This caused a 90-minute delay and raised concerns that incorrect V-speeds were used for takeoff, though the flight to ZZZ was uneventful.

synopsis: EMB175 Captain reported he had to take control of the aircraft during climb out when the First Officer failed to level off for traffic above their altitude.
summary: The Captain intervened when the First Officer overshot the assigned 10,000-foot altitude to 10,200 feet while climbing. The reporter attributed the error to the First Officer's fixation on EGPWS RA commands and lack of high-performance aircraft experience.

synopsis: EMB175 Captain reported an autopilot disengagement and abrupt pitch up at FL350. Later, maintenance inspection revealed a disagreement with the elevator servo.
summary: During cruise at FL350, an elevator servo disagreement caused the autopilot to disengage and the aircraft to pitch up abruptly, triggering the stick shaker. The flight crew recovered immediately, sustaining minor injuries to one flight attendant, while maintenance identified the servo issue as the root cause.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported they received several EICAS messages related to the squat (Weight On Wheels) switch and diverted for an uneventful landing.
summary: The flight crew diverted from FL310 to ZZZ after multiple EICAS messages, including LG WOW SYS FAIL, triggered a QRH procedure. Although warnings cleared during descent, the crew landed with full flaps and emergency services on standby, reporting normal operation of steering, reversers, and spoilers.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported they landed past the first third of the runway due to a wind shift, power application and light aircraft but were able to turn off before the runway end.
summary: The pilot of a light MD-11 encountered landing turbulence and a 5-knot wind shift on short final, causing a high descent rate. Adding power to arrest the descent resulted in a long touchdown beyond the first third of the runway, though the aircraft exited safely.

synopsis: Beechjet Captain reported disconnecting the autopilot on descent when it leveled above the cleared altitude, and expressed frustration with flying different aircraft with different engines, checklists, QRH books, flows, SOPs, and limitations.
summary: Pilots flying an arrival in VNAV mode experienced an FMS altitude conflict that caused the aircraft to level at 5000 feet instead of the assigned 4000 feet. The crew manually descended to the correct altitude, attributing the event to conflicting ILS data and broader safety concerns regarding operating three different aircraft types without adequate company support.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525 flight crew reported a loss of pressurization and rapid descent. Pressurization was reestablished at 10,000 feet and continued to a landing at the original destination.
summary: Pilots flying at FL430 experienced a rapid cabin pressurization loss while descending to cross CABAB at FL360, triggering a rapid descent to 10,000 feet. The crew donned masks, followed ATC guidance, and continued to the destination with no injuries or aircraft damage after the system re-established normal pressure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported transitioning from the MSY RYTHM Arrival to the Runway 20 RNAV at 2,000 feet and were notified reentering Class B . The crew was not aware the aircraft was below Class B at 210 knots in IMC.
summary: The flight crew descended to 2000 feet at 210 knots on the RYTHM arrival into MSY while in IMC, resulting in a Class B airspace excursion. The pilot attributes the incident to an ATC clearance that placed the aircraft below the Class B floor at an excessive speed without warning.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported landing with the #2 engine at idle thrust, with no response to thrust lever input, due to a FADEC fault.
summary: During a visual approach descent, the crew received an ENG 2 FADEC CONTROL FAULT at 8,800 feet, rendering the right engine throttle unresponsive. The pilots hand-flew a single-engine landing after forgetting to arm the approach mode, resulting in a safe arrival with no further incidents.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported the Captain inadvertently turned off Inertial Reference system #1 while deploying the sun visor.
summary: During climb out, the Captain inadvertently switched off Inertial Reference 1 while adjusting his sun visor, causing a loss of EGPWS. The crew arrested the climb, requested FL280 to avoid RVSM airspace, and maintained an emergency descent plan while informing Dispatch.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported landing safely after receiving a trailing edge flap disagree warning.
summary: The crew experienced a trailing edge flap disagreement at flaps 20 during an ILS approach in IMC with rain and strong winds. They executed a go-around, but the flaps remained stuck, forcing a diversion due to deteriorating weather and less than one hour of fuel remaining.

synopsis: Fractional Jet crew reported descending below cleared altitude on approach to LWB when erroneously believed were cleared for a visual approach.
summary: The flight crew descended below 6,000 feet to 5,200 feet on approach to LWB, believing they had a visual clearance, but ATC clarified they had not been cleared and were below the MVA. The crew attributed the miscommunication to expectation bias and workload, though no terrain conflict occurred and the aircraft landed safely after receiving the proper clearance.

synopsis: Deadheading air carrier pilot reported the nose of the A320 lifted 4-5 feet off the ground at the gate during the unloading procedure when the forward bags were removed first.
summary: A deadheading pilot reported that an aircraft pitched nose-up during deplaning, with the main door striking the jet bridge, likely due to aft-heavy loading and gusty winds. The pilot coordinated with emergency services to remove aft cargo, allowing the nose to lower safely with no injuries reported.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported that a Flight Attendant advised of a passenger loading limitation affecting weight and balance which the Captain was not aware of and which was not noted on the takeoff performance data.
summary: The Captain reported that a Flight Attendant revealed an undocumented weight and balance restriction requiring empty seats, which was not on the flight release or takeoff performance data. The Captain attributed this to flawed Weight and Balance procedures that prevent Load Agents from noting restrictions, creating a regulatory compliance risk.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported noncompliance with an apparently intoxicated passenger.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a male passenger repeatedly moved from his assigned seat to an empty exit row and later the economy section, refusing to return despite multiple requests. The passenger eventually became aggressive, demanding crew names while appearing intoxicated, prompting the Purser to intervene and the crew to seek official assistance.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Flight Attendant reported a passenger in an emergency exit row was defiant and non-compliant when asked to stow his laptop and remove newspapers from the exit row floor beneath his feet.
summary: A flight attendant reported a high-mileage passenger in an exit row refused to stow a laptop, fasten a seatbelt, or remove a newspaper from the aisle during a pre-push compliance check. The crew member did not escalate the situation or remove the passenger despite the refusal to comply with federal regulations.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported an abusive and drunk passenger in flight. The passenger was escorted off the aircraft by security at the destination airport.
summary: A flight attendant reported that an intoxicated male passenger became verbally and physically abusive toward crew members during the cruise and arrival phases. The passenger was denied alcohol, threatened the crew, grabbed an arm, and was ultimately escorted off the aircraft by local police upon arrival.

synopsis: CFI reported that he observed his solo student failed to execute a go-around after a bounced landing resulting in the aircraft coming to a stop on a collapsed nose gear.
summary: A student pilot flying a Cessna 152 solo experienced a nose gear collapse during the landing flare after four bounces. The reporter attributes the incident to incorrect control inputs following the initial bounce instead of executing a go-around, leaving the aircraft resting on its nose and left wingtip.

synopsis: GA pilot reported electing to takeoff over an aircraft at the other end of the runway after initially rejecting the takeoff because of the conflict.
summary: The pilot at SOV aborted a takeoff on Runway 16 after another aircraft entered Runway 34, obscured by a berm. Despite having the right of way, the pilot impulsively took off over the other aircraft at 300 feet due to stress and embarrassment, later admitting this was unsafe.

synopsis: PA-30 pilot reported the landing gear collapsed during the landing roll even though the green light indicated gear down and locked.
summary: The pilot of a Piper PA-30 reported that the landing gear collapsed upon touchdown during a landing in mildly rough air, despite green gear down lights and visual confirmation. Post-landing inspection revealed that a portion of the airframe supporting the gear motor assembly appeared torn away.

synopsis: BE-350 Captain reported having CRM issues with a Captain-qualified First Officer.
summary: The Captain reported that while climbing through FL230, the First Officer (a company Captain) ignored the Captain's instruction to inform ATC they could not increase climb rate. The First Officer instead told the new controller they were climbing as fast as possible, causing the Captain to drop the issue to avoid a hostile flight deck environment.

synopsis: Decathlon pilot reported a propeller strike after aggressive application of brakes while taxiing.
summary: The pilot, taxiing a ferry flight, experienced a propeller strike after aggressively braking at a hold line due to distraction from prior tasks and unfamiliar braking characteristics. The tail rose unexpectedly, causing blade impact with no injuries or other aircraft damage.

synopsis: CE-560 Captain reported a contradicting clearance from New York TRACON while flying the TEB1 SID.
summary: The pilot reported that after departing TEB runway 24, New York TRACON issued an amended clearance to turn right and climb to 4,000 feet, overriding the TEB1 departure procedure. The controller subsequently criticized the crew for not following the SID, creating confusion as the new instructions contradicted the published procedure.

synopsis: C206 pilot reported that a pilot-qualified passenger's incessant input regarding traffic and other aspects of the flight caused undue interference and distraction.
summary: A pilot reported that a private pilot passenger distracted him during cruise and final approach, then interfered with engine controls on the runway roll-out by tapping the propeller control. The incident occurred because the pilot had omitted crew interference from the passenger briefing, leading to the passenger correcting a non-critical setting while the pilot was managing a gusty crosswind landing.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 pilot operating as an insurance professional reported the PIC drifted towards the parallel runway while departing. It was discovered the aircraft was in heading mode rather than VNAV.
summary: An insurance professional and a single-pilot owner-operator experienced a drift toward Runway XXR after takeoff due to the pilot's unfamiliarity with avionics and incorrect Heading mode selection. The professional took control to avoid a conflict with another aircraft, prompting a debrief on verifying system configurations and improving cockpit communication.

synopsis: ZKC Center Controller reported conducting a flight break up after aerial refueling according to previous procedures, but was advised of a procedural error due to a new interpretation of the FAA guidance.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a flight breakup for a tanker and three fighters at FL280 during an altitude reservation. The controller later received a procedural error notification for clearing the fighters directly instead of routing instructions through the flight lead, a requirement the controller disputes as adding unnecessary risk.

synopsis: ZNY Center Controller reported failing to coordinate an altitude revision due to entering the data into the incorrectly computer.
summary: An air traffic controller inadvertently used the 'MANUAL' button instead of 'NEGOTIATE' when coordinating a climb for Aircraft X from 39,000 to 40,000 feet with Santa Maria Center. This caused a discrepancy between the system and Santa Maria's records, though no loss of separation occurred, attributed to the controller confusing the procedure with frequent manual coordinations to Gander Center.

synopsis: B737 pilot reported similar sounding call sign on the same route could have caused confusion.
summary: Flight 1234 followed flight 3412 through similar airspace and was switched to the same frequencies four times due to confusingly similar call signs. Although no errors occurred, ATC controllers noted the situation was confusing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a NMAC after takeoff at BWI.
summary: The crew avoided a midair collision during climb out on the TERPZ 6 departure by aggressively banking and climbing after receiving a Resolution Advisory and a Tower turn instruction. The incident resulted from a communication breakdown between the Tower and Departure controllers regarding approaching traffic.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported being cleared to descend via the OLAAA 1 Arrival to LAX except with several altitude adjustments. After a runway change and a speed adjustment, two crossing restrictions were missed.
summary: Pilots descending into LAX on the OLAAA 1 Arrival experienced confusion over "descend via" clearances with SoCal Approach, leading to a runway change and FMC reprogramming. Distractions caused the crew to miss vertical path deviations, resulting in crossing MADOW at 8,500 ft and TOZEK at 7,200 ft instead of the required 8,000 ft and 6,000 ft.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a loss of fuel quantity indication at FL350 with the FMC showing decreasing fuel. Fearing a possible fuel leak the Captain elected to divert to a suitable alternate.
summary: The crew of a 737-Classic experienced erroneous fuel quantity indications and a rapid FMC fuel drop enroute at FL350, prompting a rapid descent and uneventful landing due to suspected fuel leak. The pilot attributed the incident to the aging fleet's multiple MELs on fuel pumps and gauges.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported an issue with unsuitable takeoff conditions at LAX due to excessive tailwinds.
summary: The crew aborted a takeoff on Runway 24L at LAX after discovering an 18-knot tailwind exceeded limits, despite Tower and ATIS reporting westerly flow. The Captain refused the clearance and vacated for Runway 6R, while Tower continued using tailwind runways, causing inbound aircraft to hold or consider diversions.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported stopping the taxi because an aircraft under tow began to drifted towards the taxiway.
summary: While taxiing on C line, a tow on B line cut across too closely, forcing the pilot to stop. The pilot reported that failing to stop would have caused a ground collision and aircraft damage between the two aircraft.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported getting low and slow during a night visual approach to Runway 33 at BUR. The Captain assumed control for the final approach and landing.
summary: The PF and CA flew a visual approach to RWY 33 at BUR without the RNAV Visual approach plate in their database. A terrain alert occurred during the base turn due to being inside the approach, prompting an autopilot disconnect and go-around thrust application before the CA stabilized the aircraft for a safe landing.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving excessive and contradictory clearances from ATC while descending into CLT on the STOCR 1 Arrival.
summary: The flight crew and controller experienced contradictory instructions and missing altitude clearances during descent via the STOCR 1 arrival. The aircraft descended too low for departing traffic, prompting a climb to 9,000 feet after both parties recognized the conflict.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported neglecting to set the parking brake after arriving at the gate due to fatigue and distraction.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an unintended aircraft rollback at Gate X after failing to visually confirm the parking brake was set during a non-standard engine cool-down procedure. Fatigue from a long duty day and distraction by the cool-down clock contributed to the error, which was stopped by the crew with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Maintenance Personnel reported a speed brake cable was not routed correctly during installation.
summary: A mechanic installed a new speed brake cable and initially inspected it without finding discrepancies, though the cable was later found routed over a pulley guard instead of under it. The error occurred because the cable is only visible via a mirror from the rear and appeared correctly routed while moving.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A medium transport flight crew reported a runway overran into the EMAS after landing.
summary: The First Officer and Captain landed an empty Part 91 aircraft on Runway XX but failed to decelerate sufficiently to exit at the normal turnoff. Despite maximum braking and thrust reversers, the aircraft rolled into the overrun area, sustaining minor damage from contact with the EMAS.

synopsis: Lancair IV pilot reported erroneous airspeed at FL270 due to pitot icing led the G3X autopilot to attempt to maintain airspeed by pitching down.
summary: A pilot flying a Garmin G3X-equipped aircraft at FL270 in IMC experienced pitot tube icing, causing false airspeed loss and an autopilot-induced dive. The pilot recovered by disconnecting the autopilot, applying pitot heat, and using emergency procedures to level the aircraft at 23,000 feet.

synopsis: Balloon pilot reported making contact with a power line on descent for landing. The power line was not seen by the pilot, but was observed by a passenger too late to avoid contact.
summary: A hot air balloon pilot descended for landing from 1,200 feet AGL and struck two power lines due to misjudging their visibility against the hillside. The fabric broke a line, causing the basket to rebound into wetlands with no injuries and minimal damage.

synopsis: An EMB-500 flight crew reported their Crew Alerting System (CAS) alerted GPS OUTAGE at which time the autopilot reverted to PITCH and ROLL. The crew misunderstood ATC and mistakenly began a descent to FL350 while dealing with the autopilot but TCAS alerted RA at which point they returned to FL350. Shortly thereafter, GPS returned to normal.
summary: During a descent to FL360, GPS failure and high workload caused the crew to mishear a traffic advisory as a descent clearance to FL350. The crew descended toward conflicting traffic, triggering a TCAS RA, before immediately climbing back to FL360 after spotting the aircraft.

synopsis: Falcon 20 Captain reported landing in light snow to discover nil braking action. The aircraft stopped past the end of the runway with no damage.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing in light snow, the aircraft experienced poor braking and ran off the runway end into grass due to snow on a thin layer of ice. No damage occurred, and no runway condition reports had been issued despite visible contamination.

synopsis: King Air 90 pilot reported an engine failure at FL220 and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot of a four-person aircraft experienced an explosion and sparks from the left engine at FL220, prompting a precautionary shutdown and diversion to ZZZ. After intercepting the localizer for runway XXL but going around due to being high, the crew landed safely on runway 33L.

synopsis: G-V flight crew reported the autopilot initiated an unwanted 300 foot descent from the selected altitude.
summary: The crew of a newly accepted Gulfstream aircraft experienced an inadvertent nose-down autopilot descent while level at 4,000 feet on vectors for Runway XXL. The aircraft lost 300 feet before the crew regained control and returned to 4,000 feet.

synopsis: M20 pilot reported a gear up landing due to distractions caused by gusty winds and lack of recent experience.
summary: An experienced pilot landed a Mooney M20 with the gear retracted after a local pattern flight with a passenger. The incident resulted from the pilot's distraction by wind correction and passenger conversation, which caused him to skip the landing checklist and miss the gear warning.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZNY Center controllers reported turning two aircraft, one climbing and one descending, into confliction due to incomplete coordination.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in Sector 75 and ZNY Sector 39 lost separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y due to uncoordinated headings and climb instructions during a frequency outage. Aircraft X climbed into Aircraft Y, triggering a TCAS climb alert for Aircraft Y before separation was re-established.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: SMO Tower Controller and inbound jet pilot reported an airborne conflict between a jet arrival and a helicopter transitioning the area when weather deteriorated.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a VOR-A approach clearance to Aircraft X, conflicting with the crew's briefed RNAV GPS approach, while simultaneously allowing VFR Aircraft Y to cross the final. Aircraft X executed a missed approach after receiving a TCAS Resolution Advisory due to reduced separation caused by the unexpected approach assignment and high ground speed.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: F11 TRACON Controller reported receiving numerous arrivals simultaneously which were deviating for weather. Two aircraft passed with less than required separation.
summary: An air traffic controller managed nine aircraft entering airspace with moderate to extreme weather, resulting in a loss of separation due to insufficient spacing from adjacent sectors. The controller used extreme vectors to maintain separation while attempting to align aircraft for final approach.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZMP Center Controller reported approving point-outs of three in trail aircraft and noticed the fastest aircraft was overtaking the slower aircraft. The aircraft had to be turned and climbed to a new altitude to maintain separation.
summary: ZDV controllers handed off three aircraft at 37,000 feet to ZKC, causing a separation conflict requiring a climb to 38,000 feet, an incorrect altitude for the flight direction. The reporter attributes this to ZDV controller incompetence and demands their decertification and center closure for retraining.

synopsis: B737NG First Officer reported experiencing windshear shortly after gear retraction. An EGPWS wind shear warning and an airspeed loss both occur as the Captain recovered using maximum thrust.
summary: The flight crew encountered windshear shortly after takeoff from Runway XXC at ZZZ during thunderstorms, causing a 15-knot airspeed loss and triggering an EGPWS warning. The Captain executed an escape maneuver using emergency thrust to recover performance, after which ATC ceased departures and the crew contacted maintenance regarding potential engine exceedances.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported airspeed degraded during their initial climb when the autopilot aggressively pitched up.
summary: During a B747 departure in gusty winds, the crew experienced rapid airspeed decay after engaging VNAV and reducing power. The autopilot disengaged at 2,500 feet with a pitch-up command, prompting manual nose-down input to recover from low-speed conditions.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a possible fuel leak at FL340 when EICAS indicated a fuel imbalance. The crew elected to divert to the nearest suitable airport and landed with a 4,000 pound split between the right tank and the left.
summary: The flight crew experienced a significant fuel imbalance and suspected leak in the right tank during cruise, triggering an EICAS message. They diverted to ZZZ1, landed safely with two engines, and maintenance confirmed fuel loss despite finding no visible leak or sensor fault.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ATC requested 250 KTS approaching KILDE, but after overshooting final, failed to slow and descend sufficiently so executed a go-around.
summary: The pilot executing an RNAV Y 30L approach to SJC overshot the final course due to a flight management system discontinuity error, resulting in a high-speed go-around. Fatigue, emotional stress, and low recent flight hours contributed to the initial configuration error and subsequent speed management issues before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported being struck by lightning on descent to ROA. Evidence of a bird strike was also noted after landing.
summary: During descent into ROA at 13,000 feet, the crew was struck by lightning and suffered a bird strike despite no forecast thunderstorms. The event caused temporary loss of windshield heat and the number one communication system, which was restored via switch reset and system transfer.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported executing a missed approach on the ORF ILS 5 approach due to gusty 30+ knot crosswinds. The crew flew a successful approach to IAD, which also presented gusty conditions. The autopilot had difficult tracking in the high crosswind.
summary: The crew hand-flew ILS approaches to ORF and IAD after the autopilot struggled to intercept the localizer in strong crosswinds. They executed a missed approach at ORF due to low visibility, diverted to IAD, and landed safely before canceling the flight.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a delay in gate arrival during a medical emergency due to ramp congestion and lack of personnel experience.
summary: The flight crew declared a medical emergency for a seizing passenger during arrival into ZZZ and received priority handling to land at XXL. Upon reaching the ramp, a 15-minute delay occurred due to an obstructing outbound flight, unavailable marshals, and an inexperienced jetbridge operator, which the pilot attributed to poor training and cost-cutting measures.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported encountering severe turbulence several times until descending to smoother conditions.
summary: Cabin crew and flight attendants encountered severe turbulence at FL290 and FL280 during a weather deviation, causing two flight attendant injuries. The reporter attributed the event to sleep inertia, lack of cockpit Wi-Fi preventing weather updates, and questionable dispatch decisions regarding the weather system.

synopsis: A330 flight crew reported receiving an ECAM alert ENG 1/ENG 2 FUEL FILTER clog after takeoff at about 700 feet resulting in a return to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The crew received dual engine fuel filter clog ECAM warnings at 700 feet after takeoff, prompting an immediate overweight landing at the departure airport. The aircraft was removed from service, but maintenance logs later showed no clear explanation for the warnings.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported not shutting down the right engine after gate arrival. The fuel lever appeared to be in the cutoff position, but was just shy and the engine continued to run after the crew departed.
summary: The First Officer and Captain failed to shut down the right engine after parking, leaving it running for approximately 10 minutes. The cause was reliance on thrust lever position without verifying EICAS gauges, compounded by noise masking, rushing to commute, and the First Officer's hesitation to speak up about abnormal walk-around observations.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported when the autothrust was turned OFF on final, number one engine rolled back to idle. One ENGINE ELECTRONIC CONTROL Computer had been MELed, but he was concerned not properly disconnected. The aircraft was removed from service.
summary: The pilot reported that during descent and short final, continuous ECAM warnings occurred, and Engine 1 rolled back to idle after auto-thrust was disengaged. The crew landed safely but contacted safety officials to address concerns regarding the aircraft's MEL compliance for subsequent flights.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported his student made a very hard landing after stalling the aircraft above the runway.
summary: A student pilot and instructor stalled an aircraft 30 feet above Runway XXR during landing due to a late base-to-final turn and poor alignment. The plane bounced, struck both wingtips and the tail on the runway, but stopped safely and was taxied to the hangar.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Skydiving pilot and TRACON Controller reported the skydiving aircraft entered Class B clearance without a clearance from ATC.
summary: A skydiving pilot entered Class B airspace without explicit clearance, relying on a Letter of Agreement, while a controller missed initial calls during a shift change. The controller later identified the unauthorized entry, noting a 4,000-foot vertical separation from a descending business jet that would have been a near midair collision had the jet been lower.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: P80 TRACON Controller reported an IFR arrival had to respond to a TCAS alert with a VFR parachute jump aircraft even though the Controller had attempted to vector the aircraft away.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller vectored Aircraft X left to avoid a spiraling climb by jump Aircraft Y, resulting in a TCAS Resolution Advisory with a closest point of 1.5 miles and 800 feet. The controller attributed the conflict to Aircraft Y's late call for flight following and recommended changing the Letter of Agreement to require earlier notification.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported he discovered the Stabilizer Trim not functioning during climb after takeoff. The QRH checklist was completed and flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a total stabilizer trim failure during climbout, rendering manual and autopilot trim inoperative. They executed the failure checklist, returned to the departure airport, and performed an overweight landing with flaps 15 using manual trim.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the paper weight and balance forms used on charter operations, believing that an iPad application would be much less error prone.
summary: The reporter, likely a flight crew member, states that paper weight and balance forms used in charter operations are prone to arithmetic errors due to crew distractions. They recommend replacing these forms with an EFB app to eliminate errors and email copies to Dispatch.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported during preflight an aircraft just returned from the hangar, ground personnel notified him about pitot covers not removed from the RUDDER FEEL DIFFERENTIAL PITOT tubes. The pilot stated he may never have seen them from his vantage point.
summary: During a ferry flight preflight, ramp personnel alerted the pilot to uncovered rudder feel differential pressure pitot probes on the aircraft. Although the covers were removed by maintenance, the pilot departed without a new logbook entry despite concerns that the existing release was invalid.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a low fuel situation on arrival to EWR.
summary: The flight crew encountered weather during descent into EWR and was denied a left deviation by NY Center due to traffic, causing a climb to 15,000 ft and a 68-mile delay. This resulted in a fuel critical situation, forcing the crew to declare low fuel to receive priority handling and land safely.

synopsis: Phenom 300 Captain reported a serious degradation of his ability to navigate due to suspected GPS jamming while descending into SLC. Captain received radar vectors from ATC to the airport, however, they experienced several RAs from an undetermined source during the approach.
summary: A Phenom crew descending into SLC encountered GPS jamming and multiple TCAS 'descend' RAs while on a visual approach. They complied with the RAs, maneuvered below 1200 AGL, and landed safely after the conflicting traffic diverged, though ATC reported no evidence of a conflict.

synopsis: Hawker 800 Captain reported misunderstanding a Canadian Controller's instruction to descend to FL240 and descend via NUBER2 arrival. The descent was continued after reaching FL240 without clearance to make the ROKTO crossing restriction.
summary: A pilot reported confusion during descent into CYYZ at FL260 after receiving a clearance to "Descend 240, Descend Via Arrival." The controller clarified that the phraseology only authorized descent to FL240 while complying with STAR restrictions, not a full descent via the arrival, prompting the pilot to request clearer instructions.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported a NMAC with a UAV while on approach to SLC.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a drone passed within 100 feet of the aircraft at 8,500 feet during the approach to SLC. The crew notified ATC, landed normally, and found no damage, attributing the incident to unauthorized drone operation.

synopsis: Contract Maintenance personnel and Air Carrier flight crew reported that a pry bar was left on the wing of a Boeing 737 after replacing the engine. A passenger noticed the tool on top of the wing as aircraft was holding for takeoff.
summary: A mechanic left a prybar on the wing after assisting with engine anti-ice ducting and fairing installation during a #2 engine change. The tool, which concealed an emergency exit pathway marking, was discovered by a passenger while the aircraft was taxiing to the runway.

synopsis: LR-35 Captain reported displeasure with the way his First Officer managed his duties during arrival. The result was a missed crossing restriction at a higher than cleared speed.
summary: During arrival into ZZZ, the First Officer incorrectly configured the GPS for an ILS approach instead of the planned visual approach to runway 31L, causing an unintended turn and descent rate reduction. The Pilot Flying manually corrected the flight path to meet the FL190 crossing restriction at 250 knots, attributing the incident to miscommunication, incomplete ATIS review, and distraction.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported inadvertent entry into SFO Class B airspace.
summary: A VFR pilot flying toward SJC airspace drifted up to the bottom of the SFO Class B shelf due to ridge lift. The pilot descended immediately to clear the shelf and noted that better altitude margin awareness or a route shift west would have prevented the proximity.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported a UAV operator stated he was interfering with his commercial business along a boardwalk.
summary: A helicopter pilot conducting a tour at 500 feet was contacted by an unidentified individual claiming to be a drone operator who alleged the pilot violated a 400-foot altitude limit. The pilot did not see the drone, and the individual refused to provide identification or cooperate with the airport or the pilot's employer.

synopsis: Tower Controllers reported allowing an opposite direction operation to occur with less than required separation. Training in the Tower was in progress at the time.
summary: The air traffic controller admitted a lack of focus caused a loss of separation between a military flight of four fighters departing Runway 27 and Aircraft Y on a practice ILS approach to Runway 9. The controller estimated the aircraft were approximately 2 miles apart at 3,000 feet while one descended and the other ascended.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Anchorage Center Controller reported an aircraft departed, they thought they were returning on their own to the departure airport, but actually kept flying and were discovered minutes later when the pilot questioned the Controller about a possible re-route.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly removed Aircraft X's flight plan after radar displayed a false landing due to equipment malfunction. The controller later restored the plan after the aircraft requested a reroute, noting that using full call signs would have prevented the coordination error.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ORD Local Controllers reported he allowed two aircraft to land on a runway unaware that a Supervisor had posted the runway as closed.
summary: Local Control and Controller in Charge managed a brake failure on Aircraft Y blocking Taxiway M, causing multiple go-arounds and back-taxiing. Due to unclear coordination, the Center Tower closed Runway 9L while three aircraft landed on it, though no incursions occurred.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported that climb gradients to DRSET should be published for Runways 13L and 13R on four SIDs at DAL.
summary: A pilot reported a climb gradient discrepancy on DAL SIDs where meeting the 4000 ft MSL restriction at DRSET requires 501 ft/NM, exceeding the published 500 ft/NM obstacle clearance. The reporter noted this challenges older or heavy aircraft, especially with reduced thrust, and requested updated chart data to clarify ATC requirements.

synopsis: The flight crew of a Boeing 737 reported that they found a crack in the MLG wheel well bulkhead.
summary: During preflight, the First Officer discovered a 10-inch crack in the left main wheel well forward bulkhead, leading maintenance to ground the aircraft for repairs. The pilot reported that this inspection area is not emphasized in the normal walk-around or AOM, despite the crack requiring immediate repair.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported ambiguity in procedures, AIM guidance, and ATC expectations during missed approaches that occur following a go-around from a visual approach clearance given subsequent to an instrument approach clearance.
summary: A pilot reported a procedural ambiguity regarding go-around actions after a visual approach clearance when tower communication is lost. The narrative cites conflicting guidance between the AIM, various flight manuals, and a past LAX incident where the tower supervisor advised flying the published missed approach procedure.

synopsis: B777-200 flight crew reported they queried Dispatch about a high fuel burn and were told the operating empty weight used to calculate fuel burn was more than 92,000 pounds light.
summary: The flight crew discovered excessive fuel burn of 6,000 lbs due to an incorrect Operating Empty Weight (OEW) entry, which was over 92,000 lbs lower than the normal 321,000 lbs. Load planning and Zero Fuel Weight were verified as correct, confirming the OEW error as the cause.

synopsis: Corporate Jet flight crew reported a runway incursion after landing at GGG due to construction and communication issues.
summary: The crew landed long at GGG in gusty winds and, confused by ground vehicles and delayed tower communications, taxied uncommanded across Runway 36 toward Runway 31. The tower classified this as a runway incursion and pilot deviation, forcing the crew to stop and wait for explicit taxi instructions.

synopsis: CL350 Captain reported that they continued takeoff after receiving a config warning on EICAS.
summary: The pilot flying experienced a recurring rudder trim warning during takeoff on a short runway with two passengers. Despite the trim being nearly centered, the warning returned during acceleration, prompting the pilot to continue the flight rather than abort, though they acknowledged this decision violated standard operating procedures.

synopsis: C560XL Captain reported multiple routing changes and advisories of GPS outages distracted them resulting in several clearance deviations.
summary: The pilot and an IOE First Officer flying into SLC missed a descent to 15,000 feet at FRNZY due to distraction from multiple ATC arrival changes and GPS outage discussions. They realized the error at 31,000 feet, executed a steep descent, and crossed the restriction late but safely.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a NMAC on arrival preceded a bounced landing and a go-around, followed by an unstabilized approach to another go-around.
summary: The Captain experienced a TCAS alert during a visual approach, leading to a high glidepath intercept and a landing bounce that required a go-around. A second approach was missed due to unstable airspeed, but the crew eventually landed safely after correcting a heading overshoot during the missed approach.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence at 10,000 ft 5 miles in trail of a B747 on arrival into MIA.
summary: During arrival above 10,000 ft, the crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding 747, causing significant rolling and autopilot disconnect. The pilot attributed the event to insufficient separation and lack of ATC warning, though no injuries occurred as cabin crew were seated.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 flight crew reported experiencing multiple system failures on descent, including autopilot/autothrottle disconnect, Captain's airspeed indicator error, and air conditioning/pressurization pack failure.
summary: The flight crew experienced Mach Trim failure, unreliable airspeed, and dual pack failures causing rapid depressurization during descent from FL310. They maintained control, exited RVSM airspace, and landed safely with no injuries while maintenance troubleshooting continues.

synopsis: Hawker 800 First Officer reported an altitude deviation occurred that arose from the difference in 'descend via' clearances between Canada and the United States.
summary: Toronto Center issued a "descend via" clearance to FL240 to a crew at FL260, causing confusion as the crew descended below the assigned altitude. The controller clarified that Canadian phraseology restricts descent to the specific assigned altitude, unlike US procedures, highlighting a need for verification.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported returning to departure airport after multiple nose gear related error messages. Ground Personnel reported the nose gear steering torque links were not connected.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple nose gear warnings on climbout due to disconnected torque links, suspecting they were not fully locked after pushback. The aircraft returned for a safe landing, where significant shuddering occurred below 80 knots before stopping for inspection.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported the co-pilot's seat came off the seat rail during an intentional spin training maneuver.
summary: During an intentional spin, the co-pilot seat detached from its rail, causing the Instructor Pilot to fall. The Pilot Under Instruction recovered the aircraft alone, and the crew landed safely without declaring an emergency, noting that utility-category aircraft might require reinforced seats.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attended reported an odd odor in the front of the cabin. Other flight attendents noticed odd physical effects from the odor and the aircraft ultimately returned to the gate.
summary: Flight attendants detected a strong odor and reported eye irritation and headaches during boarding, prompting the Captain to return the aircraft to the gate. Passengers were deplaned so maintenance could investigate the source of the smell.

synopsis: PA44 student pilot reported an NMAC in the vicinity of Niagara Falls after failing to fly the published photo pattern.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor in a training aircraft descended below the designated 3,500 ft altitude to avoid a head-on conflict while circling Niagara Falls counter-clockwise. The near-miss occurred due to misjudging the other aircraft's direction and failing to have the circling pattern ready, resulting in a 100 ft separation.

synopsis: CE-680 flight crew reported deviating from assigned altitude after receiving an RA.
summary: During a check airman observation flight, the crew encountered a TCAS RA warning while climbing to 2000' after a missed approach due to VFR traffic turning toward them. The crew descended to 1600' to resolve the conflict before climbing back to 2000' after ATC acknowledged the RA response.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a NMAC with an SR22. Evasive action was taken by the C182 pilot.
summary: During a climb from SQL, a C182R pilot misidentified an SR22 as conflicting traffic and requested a new vector from Norcal, inadvertently placing both aircraft on a collision course. The C182R's GDL-88 alert prompted immediate evasive action, avoiding a near collision estimated at 1,000 feet separation.

synopsis: A C172 student pilot reported unusual indications in the right fuel gauge and discovered after landing that the right fuel cap was missing. The student pilot concluded that it had not been secured adequately prior to flight.
summary: The pilot, fatigued from insufficient rest, performed a cursory preflight inspection and departed, later discovering the right fuel tank cap was missing during flight. This caused erratic fuel gauge readings and a rolling tendency, prompting a precautionary landing at ZZZ airport where the cap was replaced before the flight continued safely.

synopsis: Falcon 2000 Captain reported a NMAC with two light aircraft in the vicinity of PBI airport.
summary: During an instrument descent to PBI, the crew encountered two Cessna 172s in loose formation within clouds, triggering conflicting TCAS climb RAs. The crew executed an immediate climb and turn to avoid the VFR traffic, which ATC had not contacted and suspected was illegally operating in clouds.

synopsis: TBM850 pilot reported an engine failure at altitude, recovered power using the secondary power control lever and diverted to a safe landing.
summary: The pilot of a four-passenger IFR flight experienced an unresponsive primary torque/throttle control at Flight Level 240, causing an unintended descent and a false engine failure belief triggered by a gear down aural message. Power was restored by activating the secondary power control lever, allowing a safe landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: A center controller and flight crew reported an aircraft did not comply with a crossing restriction and descended into restricted airspace.
summary: A pilot reported that Aircraft X descended below the 28,000-foot restricted area due to an FMS malfunction that deleted speed and altitude restrictions on the ANJLL1 arrival. The crew manually corrected the 1,000-foot deviation after ATC intervention, attributing the incident to the FMS error and high workload.

synopsis: Boston Center Controller reported communication problems with Canada ATC during a Non-Automated hand off.
summary: An air traffic controller in sector 52/53 attempted four times to contact Canada Drummond for a point out of Aircraft X before issuing a manual right turn to heading 200. Drummond eventually accepted the transfer, but the controller noted that automated handoffs would eliminate the need for these manual phone calls.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Two Center Controllers reported working a busy sector with weather deviations and did not notice an aircraft overtaking another aircraft descending to the same altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined sectors experienced a conflict alert between two descending arrivals due to coordination errors regarding altitude assignments and routing. Although Sector 42 turned one aircraft to maintain separation, the event was reported as a potential NMAC and documented as an internal Mandatory Occurrence.

synopsis: SCT TRACON Controller reported that an aircraft went through the localizer and ended up in a higher Minimum Vectoring Altitude then was issued.
summary: A pilot on an ILS approach to SNA crossed the localizer and descended to 3,000 feet while in a 3,700-foot MVA after an insufficient intercept turn. The controller attributed the situation to the pilot's confusion and noted that current MVA restrictions prevent efficient approaches from both sides of the localizer.

synopsis: ZDV Controller reported receiving an aircraft below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller received Aircraft X at 110 feet below the 120 MIA during a handoff from ZAB, with MSAW failing to alert until the aircraft was halfway through the sector. The controller verified terrain clearance with the pilot and allowed the flight to continue without a climb, noting the need for better manual monitoring of low-altitude routes.

synopsis: ZDC Controller reported that an aircraft was issued one altitude, but descended below that altitude in a holding pattern.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a clearance for Aircraft X to descend via KORRY3 and cross BRAND at 11,000 feet, but the pilot descended to 10,000 feet before entering the RBV hold. The controller attributed the altitude discrepancy to a pilot misunderstanding of the clearance, though no separation loss or TCAS RA occurred.

synopsis: SoCal TRACON Feeder and Final Controllers reported a handoff that was not made correctly which resulted in an aircraft having to be resequenced due to not seeing traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined STADIUM/ZUMA sectors at LAX failed to hear a handoff request for Aircraft Y, resulting in a loss of separation with Aircraft Z during simultaneous ILS approaches. The controller attributed the incident to high workload, staffing shortages, excessive overtime, and uneven traffic flow that stretched downwind legs.

synopsis: SAT TRACON Controller reported of an unsafe issue when an aircraft on a visual approach was following traffic and became extended over another airport, and traffic around that airport.
summary: An air traffic controller on Approach West issued a traffic alert to Aircraft X during a visual approach when a transponder-equipped target converged rapidly at 4,500 feet. The pilot did not respond to the controller but followed a TCAS advisory, prompting the controller to recommend upgrading the airspace to Class B to prevent future catastrophic safety failures.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after experiencing loss of cabin pressure.
summary: During climb through FL210, the crew experienced a rapid depressurization event caused by an auto pressurization failure, indicated by warning lights and a rising cabin altitude. The crew donned oxygen masks, descended to 13,000 feet, and returned to the departure airport without deploying passenger oxygen masks, landing safely after a fire department inspection.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported concern about a possible track deviation when he had difficulty finding the identifier for Mateo while on approach to MMMX.
summary: The crew flying an arrival into MMMX received a last-minute clearance to intercept the Mateo radial, but could not locate the identifier on their primary STAR or approach charts. This caused significant distraction while searching for the buried identifier on a separate plate, creating an uncomfortable situation where they feared missing the assigned radial.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 First Officer reported noticing a smoky smell in the aircraft about the same time they received a status message for the L2 air compressor.
summary: During descent through 18,000 feet, the flight crew detected a burning smell and executed the smoke checklist, shutting off recirculation fans and power outlets. After requesting emergency vehicles as a precaution due to recurring odors on approach, the aircraft landed safely with no external smoke found by fire crews.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported a disruptive passenger who changed seats and then tried to extort some kind of compensation for causing disruption.
summary: Flight attendants managed a disruptive passenger who changed seats, demanded compensation, and threatened to film them to force removal. The reporter attributes this behavior to a lack of sanctions for recent security violations, creating a dangerous environment where passengers exploit the situation.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing a stabilizer trim problem.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a stabilizer trim runaway at 8,500 feet while flying with autopilot engaged. They executed memory items, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely on a wet runway despite missing the initial thrust reverser deployment.

synopsis: Dash-8 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after losing #1 pitot heat and #1 comm radio.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced multiple system failures, including pitot heat loss and pressurization issues caused by a maintenance error, during a climb in heavy rain. They diverted to an alternate airport, landed safely despite instrument failures, and reported fatigue and possible lightning damage, though inspections found no strike evidence.

synopsis: Flight crew reported an altitude deviation on a STAR into CYYZ and were informed in Canada a 'descend via' clearance only means speeds not the altitudes.
summary: Pilots on a new route encountered ambiguous "descend via" clearances during descent into Toronto due to conflicting ICAO phraseology interpretations between US and Canadian controllers. The crew queried the clearance to avoid violating altitude restrictions, highlighting a need for updated training on recent language changes.

synopsis: B777 Dispatcher believed the flight he assumed at the start of his shift may have been dispatched illegally with only 45 minutes of reserve fuel on a flight to VHHH.
summary: An air traffic controller questioned the legality of a VHHH flight's 45-minute special reserve fuel and Class 1 navigation interpretation over Russia. Although the flight landed safely, the controller reported confusion regarding the undocumented rule interpretation allowing position fixes every two hours instead of hourly.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported ordering evacuation of the aircraft due to a ground equipment fire.
summary: The flight crew and ground personnel responded to a fire on the right wing caused by a baggage cart being towed away from the aircraft. The incident resulted in smoke entering the cabin, leading to passenger deplaning, a maintenance inspection, and a subsequent aircraft and crew swap.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: First Officer reported that due to an unprofessional Captain disregarding the pilot monitoring instructions they encountered a near miss.
summary: The PIC ignored checklists, engaged in non-sterile cockpit behavior, and attempted to erase the CVR during a visual approach to the wrong airport. This distraction led to a TCAS RA requiring a climb to avoid a collision, after which the PIC instructed the reporter not to file an incident report.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported loss of GPS signal in the Moscow area that lasted for about 20 minutes.
summary: Pilots flying a jet south of Moscow experienced a 20-minute GPS outage causing RNP alerts and high inertial ANP. Enabling radio updating restored accuracy, though the system never displayed a "GPS Inop" message despite blank data lines.

synopsis: The Captain of a Boeing 777 reported that the #1 engine had an over temp and would not come up to speed as quick as the #2 engine, resulting in a rejected takeoff.
summary: The captain and maintenance personnel aborted a takeoff due to a left engine spool-up delay and configuration warning caused by a suspected fuel controller issue. The aircraft was grounded for inspection after the engine exhibited excessive temperature and fuel burn prior to departure.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported they diverted to an alternate after experiencing a fuel leak.
summary: The flight crew experienced a fuel leak and 4,000 lb imbalance enroute, triggering a diversion to the nearest suitable airport per the QRH. They landed safely after rejecting a dispatch request to divert to a further maintenance hub due to worsening imbalance risks.

synopsis: Ramp Service Employee reported striking a stair truck with the aircraft winglet while towing an aircraft to a remote parking spot.
summary: A ramp employee towing an aircraft to remote parking at dusk struck a left Scimitar wing with a stair truck due to misjudging distance. The reporter attributed the incident to staffing shortages, lack of a third wing walker, poor lighting, and the stair truck being improperly parked.

synopsis: A pilot conducting a visual approach reported reducing their airspeed below the speed assigned by ATC.
summary: The pilot reported gaining on traffic during a visual approach while maintaining an assigned 170 knots. To prevent a closure issue, the pilot voluntarily slowed to 150 knots early, maintaining 2.5 miles separation and completing a safe landing without incident.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet pilot reported receiving several revised clearances in a short amount of time from a very busy ZLC Center Controller due to GPS jamming occurring in the area.
summary: Pilots reported that Center issued four different arrival procedures in four minutes due to GPS jamming, causing task saturation and a missed crossing restriction. The crew required vectoring for descent after continuous FMS changes, though ATC claimed the situation was not a problem.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported that during landing with glideslope captured they received a GPWS warning and it continued after landing.
summary: The flight crew landed an aircraft on RWY 32 at PIT in moderate rain and icing conditions. The EGPWS triggered false alerts during approach and rollout, which maintenance attributed to ice accumulation on the radio altimeter antenna due to fluctuating temperatures.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported receiving an EGPWS warning while being vectored below the MSA by ATC on an approach to BNA in IMC.
summary: The Captain and First Officer received an EGPWS "Terrain Terrain" warning while being vectored by ATC to 2500 feet MSL in IMC conditions during an ILS 2R approach. The crew climbed to 4000 feet MSL, attributing the warning to the vectored altitude being too low for the varying terrain in that sector.

synopsis: Embraer ERJ-175 First Officer reported attempting to accomplish a crossbleed start with the operating engine at idle thrust.
summary: A First Officer attempted a normal engine start instead of a required cross-bleed start after the APU was shut down, causing high N2 temperature. The Captain corrected the issue by increasing power on Engine 1, allowing the start to complete normally without exceeding limits.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ERJ First Officer reported a 'moderate to severe' wake turbulence encounter at 14,000 ft on arrival into IAH 12 miles in trail of a B747.
summary: A crew descending via GESNR at 14,000 feet in Houston Approach encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B747, causing autopilot disconnect and a 30-degree roll. The Flight Attendant braced safely, and the crew attributed the incident to insufficient lateral separation or vectoring by ATC.

synopsis: Embraer EMB-175 First Officer reported a discrepancy on the main landing gear that maintenance felt was airworthy. Eventually the issue was addressed and the flight departed.
summary: During preflight, the First Officer and Captain identified an over-serviced left main landing gear shimmy damper with no indicator band visible. After the Maintenance Supervisor initially cleared the aircraft, the pilots refused to depart until mechanics drained fluid to restore the gauge to limits, resolving the safety conflict.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported being re-sequenced twice on arrival to Runway 25L at LAX due to missing a crossing restriction and not being cleared for the approach.
summary: The flight crew missed ATIS information regarding the active RNAV GPS 25L approach and failed to clean up the FMS before executing a change, causing an unintended ALT HOLD. This resulted in missing the SEAVU altitude restriction, requiring two 360-degree turns for re-sequencing before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Boeing 777 Captain reported dangerous goods on board were not properly documented for the flight.
summary: The flight crew reported that Dangerous Goods in position 1L were not properly documented as ADG for the flight to ZZZ. The reporter stated the goods were manifested to the ULD, but the ramp agent failed to manifest them to the flight.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported a passenger misconduct incident regarding the unauthorized use of premium seating. When the passengers were confronted, and told they would be charged for upgrading, they responded in a very threatening and abusive manner.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger and his wife occupied premium economy seats without payment, becoming aggressive and threatening when asked to move or pay. The attendant allowed them to remain to avoid escalation, citing fatigue and safety concerns, and alerted the gate agent upon landing who flagged the passenger for future flights.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported a passenger misconduct incident involving the unauthorized filming of the flight crew performing their duties.
summary: During meal service, a passenger requested the Purser, refused to stop filming crew, and interfered with duties. The Flight Attendant could not issue a formal warning due to missing misconduct sheets and called for clearer policies to handle such confrontations.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported the water in the aft galley was contaminated, had a dark yellow green color and smelled like anti-freeze/deicing fluid.
summary: Cabin crew reported dark yellow-green, foul-smelling water in the aft galley, suspecting contamination by anti-freeze or transmission fluid. The crew served this water to passengers, resulting in stomach issues for one crew member, and demanded immediate tank testing and accountability for the fill operation.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported that during some light turbulence the aircraft suddenly dropped injuring a Flight Attendant.
summary: Flight attendants serving in the aft galley were injured when the aircraft suddenly dropped in severe turbulence, lifting one crew member into the ceiling and slamming them to the floor. Five crew members and one passenger were on the floor, resulting in back pain for the reporter, who later failed to file a claim due to technical issues.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that a passenger detected a brown liquid on her tray table that irritated skin when contact was made.
summary: Flight attendants encountered a corrosive liquid on a first-class tray table during cruise, causing a burning sensation to one crew member. The crew contained the hazard using a Universal Precaution Kit, and Hazmat and maintenance crews inspected the area upon landing with no lasting injuries reported.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Maintenance Technician reported oil leaked from a generator that was recently replaced.
summary: A mechanic installing a new engine-driven generator on an EMB145 in rain suspected the O-ring was dislodged during difficult alignment of the spline and exhaust ducting. The mechanic reported no immediate oil leakage during the operational check but recommended longer leak checks and better weather protection to prevent future issues.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported not having the proper equipment to gain access to the upper rotating beacon on an Embrarer aircraft.
summary: Maintenance personnel attempted to repair a beacon light water leak on the aircraft fuselage using an unbalanced scissor lift on a wet surface. The reporter cited a lack of proper equipment and only one fall restraint harness as the cause of the unsafe working conditions.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported TRACON vectored him away from the initial approach fix at intended destination.
summary: During descent to PXE, ATC provided vectors conflicting with all three onboard NAV sources, placing the aircraft 15 miles south of the airport. The pilot ignored ATC's claim of being over Warner Robins Air Park, followed their own navigation to land safely at PXE.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an engine problem that resulted in a diversion to the nearest airport.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 172SP experienced sudden power loss and violent shaking at 6,000 feet due to Cylinder 3 showing zero CHT and EGT. After receiving vectors to ZZZ1, the pilot landed safely; mechanics later confirmed Cylinder 3 had zero compression and was ruined, though the specific cause remained unknown.

synopsis: B300 Captain reported a loss of pressurization at FL310, a descent to lower altitude and successful landing were made.
summary: During cruise at FL310, the pilot and Flight Observer experienced a pressurization failure causing cabin altitude to exceed 10,000 feet. They descended to 9,500 feet to avoid mask deployment, landed safely, and subsequent maintenance checks found no anomalies.

synopsis: UAV operator reported he may have operated within 5 miles of PHX airport at an altitude of 60 feet AGL.
summary: A pilot operating a drone at 60 ft AGL may have flown within the five-mile radius of PHX airport. The pilot realized after the flight that they potentially violated the five-mile rule for airports with operating control towers, despite avoiding Class B airspace.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported a partial gear extended landing following an apparent hydraulic system failure.
summary: A Cessna 210 pilot on approach diverted after a hydraulic hose failure prevented gear extension, leading to a gear-up landing. The aircraft skidded on its tail and left stabilizer, sustaining minor damage, while the pilot attributed the incident to cycling the gear handle after a hose separation.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a seating configuration that did not allow the emergency over wing exit to be opened. When contacted, the reporter stated the problem had been corrected.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a B737 with 148 seats has a three-seat row installed at a mid-cabin emergency exit, blocking window access due to locked upright seats. The reporter states this configuration violates Part 121.585, though the airline claims it is legal.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a long landing and runway excursion due to loss of control under heavy braking.
summary: During a landing practice session, the pilot floated on touchdown and applied brakes before the aircraft fully settled, causing a ground loop that exited the runway and struck a taxiway light. The pilot attributed the loss of control to premature braking, light aircraft weight, and calm winds resulting in high ground speed.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported the purser advised that there was a thick layer of light-gray smoke in passenger cabin and a strong hydraulic-like odor.
summary: Flight crew and cabin crew experienced smoke and fumes in the mid-aft cabin shortly after takeoff, likely triggered by gear retraction. The crew declared a PAN-PAN, returned safely to the departure airport, and diverted to another aircraft, resulting in a delay with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: PA-34 flight crew reported a training flight resulted in multiple diversions and minimum fuel condition due to weather conditions and inoperative runway lights.
summary: Pilots in a Seneca encountered strong crosswinds and failed runway lights during multiple ILS approaches to ZZZ, ZZZ1, and ZZZ2, exhausting their fuel reserves. After declaring minimum fuel, they successfully landed at ZZZ3 on the second ILS 2 attempt after initially missing the runway environment.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported that he penetrated Class B airspace when he encountered moderate to severe turbulence and updrafts at approximately 200 feet below the bottom of class B. He had contacted ATC attempting to get Class B clearance, but had been told to standby.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 34 inadvertently entered Class B airspace due to moderate to severe turbulence and updrafts causing an uncommanded climb to 5,800 feet MSL. The reporter attributed the incident to adverse weather, cockpit distractions, and a deviation from the planned left turn to avoid restricted airspace.

synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported an airborne conflict between enroute aircraft and aircraft in restricted airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X, Y, Z, and A near active restricted areas, creating a potential conflict between X and A due to poor climb performance and altitude constraints. The controller issued last-minute heading changes to avoid a collision, admitting uncertainty about maintaining standard separation or restricted area clearance.

synopsis: B737 Crew reported a NMAC on climbout from EWR.
summary: A pilot flying southeast of EWR at 6,000 ft received TCAS Resolution Advisories to descend due to a Cessna at 6,500 ft. After complying with the 'Descend' command and clearing the conflict, ATC instructed the Cessna to maintain 6,500 ft.

synopsis: A320 Flight Crew reported being notified later that the gear collapsed while parked at the gate.
summary: The crew landed an aircraft right of centerline during a heavy rain Cat I ILS approach with a 12-knot crosswind. Although the landing and taxi appeared normal, the landing gear collapsed later while parked at the gate, causing major damage.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported several tires were blown during landing rollout.
summary: The flight crew landed a 405,000-pound aircraft in gusty winds, experiencing a firm touchdown followed by a loud bang and smoke. Maintenance later confirmed four main gear tires blew, likely caused by wheels locking up during deceleration, requiring a tow to a remote stand.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported that they had an unaccounted passenger on board.
summary: The flight crew reported a weight and balance discrepancy of one passenger due to gate agents boarding an individual with a fraudulent ticket without scanning. The crew performed three weight and balance calculations as the Service Operations Center and customer service alternately removed and re-added the passenger.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported LAX and SCT Controllers would not change the runway landing direction even though the winds had been from the east all day and were exceeding the 10 knot tailwind limit for most aircraft.
