summary: A student pilot executing a solo go-around at ZZZ struck a runway light with the stabilator endcap due to gusty crosswinds. The aircraft was returned to service after a mechanic performed an undocumented repair, violating maintenance record-keeping requirements.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: An instructor reported that his student, flying a light sport aircraft, was stuck on a runway with the brakes locked. The student injured himself in an attempt to check the brakes.
summary: A student pilot on his fourth solo flight exited a running aircraft on the runway to inspect locked brakes, violating safety instructions. He was struck by the propeller on his hand but subsequently taxied to an FBO and sought medical assistance.

synopsis: A Cessna 414A pilot reported having an in-flight shutdown.
summary: The pilot experienced an in-flight failure of the right engine, secured it, and made a successful landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: G-550 First Officer reported receiving a low altitude alert from the Tower while on visual approach.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach to runway 6 requested a low altitude alert from the tower while approaching off the runway centerline. The pilot noted that maintaining an IFR approach path would have prevented the low altitude condition encountered in visual conditions.

synopsis: Air Traffic Controller reported a departure on a SID that did not make contact in a timely manner and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Air Carrier X departed opposite direction and entered a 3500-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude at 3000 feet due to delayed communication. The controller attributed the incident to a flawed procedure allowing departures below mountainous terrain and warned of potential higher altitude conflicts.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported executing a go-around after encountering wake turbulence on short final in trail of an E2 military aircraft.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft during landing on Runway XX, causing sudden lift loss and drift. The First Officer initiated a go-around, and the aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully after completing required checklists.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported an incident with a Captain acting strangely and making passengers uncomfortable.
summary: A flight attendant reported that the Captain caused a 90-minute ground delay with alarming fuel and weight announcements, then threatened to divert during flight to prioritize his meal over passenger service. The Captain's unprofessional behavior, refusal to communicate with the cabin crew, and termination of aircraft power with passengers onboard created an unsafe environment.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A single engine pilot reported approach control vectored a military aircraft over his aircraft which the pilot felt was unsafe.
summary: A pilot approaching Anchorage reported a loss of separation with a military aircraft during heavy weather and wind shear. The TRACON controller vectored the military jet inside the Final Approach Point on an ILS, forcing the pilot to take evasive action to avoid a collision.

synopsis: UAS pilot previously registered a toy UAS as per FAR 107, but the FAA website did not allow him to register a newly purchased Phantom 4 Pro. The UAS was flown then subsequently registered as a commercial UAS.
summary: A pilot with manned aircraft experience operated a Phantom 4 Pro drone in Class E airspace without realizing ATC authorization was required under Part 107. The reporter attributed the oversight to confusion regarding differing regulations for recreational UAS versus manned aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A twin engine pilot, reported an airborne traffic conflict while maneuvering to avoid a restricted area. While maneuvering, the pilot deviated from his assigned altitude, resulting in a resolution advisory (RA) in the other aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna in Class E VFR space turned 180 degrees to avoid restricted airspace, inadvertently climbing from 4,200 to 4,350 feet. This maneuver caused a near-miss with a King Air at 5,000 feet, triggering a TCAS RA for the King Air while both crews maintained visual contact.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported that turning onto incorrect taxiway due to confusing signage at TEB.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing for departure, mistakenly turned onto the wrong taxiway due to unclear signage and difficulty identifying the runway 19 threshold. The pilot realized the error before entering the runway, queried the controller, and was instructed to correct the path to complete the run-up and receive IFR release.

synopsis: ZNY Center Oceanic Controller reported they had less than required separation between two aircraft on crossing courses even though the ATOP tool did not identify a separation problem.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 89 experienced a conflict between Aircraft X and Aircraft Z at FL380 after the ATOP system failed to display the conflict during coordination. The controller resolved the situation by instructing a descent to FL370, attributing the near-miss to a potential ATOP system error.

synopsis: CHA TRACON Controller allowed an aircraft to enter a 6,000 foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude area at 5,000 feet.
summary: An IFR overflight aircraft exited airspace at 5,000 feet into a 6,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude (MVA). After Atlanta Center alerted the controller, the aircraft was instructed to climb to 6,000 feet for terrain and subsequently handed off.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: P80 Controller reported numerous unidentified VFR targets routinely fly in close proximity to the final approach course, and suggested that the airspace be evaluated for a redesign.
summary: An air traffic controller on the final approach position reported difficulty avoiding VFR aircraft circling below 5000 feet while vectoring IFR traffic. The controller stated that immediate action was sometimes required to prevent TCAS events and warned that a serious accident is likely without airspace reclassification.

synopsis: SAN Tower Controller reported sending an aircraft around, which then caused the controller to stop a departure below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude to maintain separation between the two aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a go-around to Aircraft X on final and held departing Aircraft Y at 1500 feet to prevent an overtake, inadvertently placing Y below the 1900-foot MVA. The controller attributed the incident to a delayed decision to turn Aircraft X earlier to establish a diverging course.

synopsis: SNA Tower Controller reported using a Pre Departure Clearance function in error which caused the aircraft to be below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an incorrect "climb via the SID except maintain 2000" clearance to Aircraft X due to a fat finger error. This caused the aircraft to depart below the minimum vectoring altitude, prompting a request to remove the erroneous option from the clearance delivery menu.

synopsis: SCT TRACON Controller reported an aircraft checked in on the frequency that had not been handed off by Center due to computer issues.
summary: An air traffic controller lost radar data for Aircraft X descending on the OLAAA ONE arrival to LAX due to a handoff automation failure between sectors. The controller manually regained control of the limited data block, preventing a potential loss of separation or collision with other traffic.

synopsis: NCT Controller and flight crew reported the pilots flew the SID incorrectly into confliction with a previous departure.
summary: Aircraft X and Y departed SJC on the SJC2 procedure, but X turned early due to missing SJC VOR DME signals and a distracting cabin pressurization issue. The controller vectored both aircraft to establish separation, attributing the deviation to confusing SIDs and poor tower coordination.

synopsis: Boeing 737 Captain reported that the stabilizer trim would not operate using the trim switches or the autopilot.
summary: During takeoff and climb, the First Officer and Pilot Flying experienced a total loss of electric trim, confirmed by a 'Stab out of Trim' light when the autopilot was engaged. They flew using manual trim until the Pilot Flying cycled the trim circuit breaker, which restored normal trim system operation.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported confusion with the flap setting on takeoff that led them to forget to retract the landing gear.
summary: The flight crew departed with flaps retracted and landing gear down, triggering airspeed alerts and airframe rumbling. The pilot attributed the flap discrepancy to an unexplained system failure and the gear exceedance to distraction, ultimately raising the gear at 250 knots after leveling at 3,000 feet.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported being dispatched with FWD GND EXH VAL on MEL. During climbout the aircraft did not pressurize and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew departed ZZZZ with an improperly documented equipment cooling deferral, later experiencing rapid depressurization at FL190 and an equipment overheat warning. They returned to ZZZZ after dumping and burning fuel to land below maximum weight, resolving the overheat by selecting standby and increasing speed.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported losing hydraulic fluid and finding the QRH procedure to be confusing.
summary: The flight crew managed a left hydraulic quantity leak at cruise by following QRH procedures, resulting in a safe landing with nose wheel steering. Post-landing, shutting down the right engine disabled the PTU, causing a loss of steering that required a tow, while the crew noted confusion regarding checklist terminology.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a procedural deviation while departing Washington National Airport (DCA) which resulted in the penetration of Prohibited Area P-56.
summary: The Pilot-in-Command of Aircraft X departed DCA but inadvertently penetrated P-56A airspace due to the First Officer's incorrect FMS and display configuration. The crew corrected the navigation settings mid-departure, and although queried by ATC, no law enforcement action was taken following the incident.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported a NMAC with a UAV climbing out of LGA.
summary: The pilot and a new hire IOE student encountered a drone near 1,000 feet shortly after takeoff from LGA Runway 4. Although the crew feared a strike, post-flight inspections found no damage, and the pilot attributed the close call to delayed drone advisories and focused instrument monitoring.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported that a malfunctioning Lateral Navigation mode caused a course deviation on departure and reversion to a raw data, hand-flown approach.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced repeated failures to arm lateral NAV mode during RNAV departure and LOC approach, causing a course deviation and autopilot reversion to ROL mode. The crew manually corrected the departure path and landed using raw data after the Captain could not rearm the approach mode.

synopsis: A Cessna 402 Captain reported fluctuating fuel flow and engine roughness during climbout. Though the engine recovered somewhat he elected to make a precautionary landing at the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer reported a temporary left engine fuel flow drop and RPM loss while climbing through 7,800 feet. The crew returned to ZZZ without declaring an emergency, and the flight landed safely after the engine stabilized.

synopsis: Cessna 402 Captain reported that a passenger noticed smoke coming from a circuit breaker panel. After confirming that an electrical problem did exist, the Captain elected to divert a suitable nearby airport.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew diverted to ZZZ after a passenger reported smoke from the left circuit breaker panel, which stopped upon isolating electrical systems. Fire crews found no active source but detected an electrical fire smell, leading the crew to suspect the heater or lightning strike detector.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a deviation for weather in oceanic airspace, after deviating a message was received from ATC that denied the deviation.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence at FL330 and deviated left off their lateral offset procedure to avoid weather after receiving a delayed response from SF Radio. Although ATC later stated they were unable to approve the left deviation due to traffic, the crew had already maneuvered and subsequently returned to course.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported that a B777 flight crew shut down the right engine due to loss of oil quantity and pressure and diverted without incident.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZ after low oil quantity and dropping pressure in the right engine prompted a shutdown. The aircraft landed safely with no further issues.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a terrain warning on a night visual approach to CHO runway 03.
summary: Pilots flying into CHO RWY 03 received an EGPWS terrain warning while descending to 2600 ft after ATC cleared a visual approach from 3000 ft. The crew executed a go-around, attributing the incident to ATC vectoring too low near an 1800 ft ridge without adequate terrain awareness.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer attributed a traffic conflict on approach to PHL to apparent controller inexperience.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach for Runway 35 at 3000 ft received conflicting ATC instructions that directed them toward a conflicting aircraft. The crew manually executed a tight right turn and climb to avoid a collision after the controller, described as inexperienced and behind the curve, failed to provide adequate separation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Business Jet flight crew reported that upon taking the runway at MTJ a GA pilot announced that he was going around. The crew reported that this was the first transmission from the GA Pilot.
summary: The flight crew departed Montrose Runway 31 after scanning and using TCAS, but a Cessna 172 pilot on short final executed a go-around, claiming the crew cut him off. The reporter attributes the incident to the Cessna pilot's failure to make position reports on CTAF, which prevented necessary coordination.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported a gate agent started to board a flight even though Maintenance had requested the aircraft not be boarded until a tire change was completed.
summary: A flight crew halted boarding after a gate agent prematurely authorized it while maintenance changed a tire on jacked aircraft. The reporter attributed the safety risk to poor communication and pressure to depart, noting that maintenance had explicitly warned against boarding due to potential jack failure.

synopsis: A321 Crew reported a problem reprogramming the FMGC after a missed approach.
summary: The flight crew experienced dual FMGC failures and autopilot issues during an ILS approach in adverse weather while near minimum fuel. After manually stabilizing the aircraft and resolving a minor flap exceedance, they successfully sequenced the systems and completed the landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported that Dispatchers were not advised by their company of missile launches which could have affected the safety of flights operating near the launch area.
summary: Dispatchers learned of North Korean missile launches from a company aircraft inquiry while managing flights to South Korea and Japan. The Chief Dispatcher revealed Corporate Security knew four hours prior but withheld the information, leaving Dispatch to speculate on the reason.

synopsis: A300 Flight Crew reported that an overloaded cargo container was discovered after block-in at destination.
summary: The Ramp Agent and offload crew discovered that a container in position 7R was loaded incorrectly shortly after block in. The container weighed 8,380 lbs, exceeding the 6,152 lb limit by 2,228 lbs due to incorrect weighing or recording.

synopsis: A319 Flight Crew reported a strong 'dirty sock' odor in the cabin before and during flight which resulted in hospitalization of a Flight Attendant.
summary: The flight crew detected a strong odor upon boarding and deferred the APU, but the smell returned during descent in rain, causing illness to the captain, first officer, and a flight attendant. The return flight was canceled, the flight attendant was hospitalized, and the crew was removed from duty due to the unresolved odor despite turning off both packs.

synopsis: Air carrier deadheading First Officer reported that flights were canceled due to tornadoes reported in the area.
summary: A deadheading crew member boarded an aircraft at ZZZ despite active tornado warnings, FAA closure notices, and suspended operations. The flight departed with special permission while the airport remained in a predicted tornado path, leaving the reporter to rely on seat belts and prayer for safety.

synopsis: A330 Captain reported after a stop short of the gate a chock was stuck. Captain reported using idle reverse to attempt to free chock, in violation of policy.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing to the gate, stopped due to inadequate jet bridge clearance and later attempted an unauthorized power back to free a stuck nose chock. This safety violation, caused by excessive focus on schedule over safety, required a tug to move the aircraft after the pilot's reverse thrust attempt failed.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported a Bleed Off Eng L EICAS message and an APU that was deferred. Pilot reported after consultation with dispatch, crew decided flight could legally continue into ETOPS airspace and proceed to destination.
summary: The flight crew received a 'Bleed Off Eng L' EICAS message while cruising with an inoperative APU, leaving only one bleed source. After consulting operations, maintenance, and legal regarding ETOPS legality and fuel reserves, they determined it was safe to continue the flight as filed.

synopsis: EMB-175 Crew reported the FMS failed to sequence on an RNAV approach which resulted in a missed approach and were vectored for an ILS approach.
summary: The PIC and SIC encountered an FMS load 27.1 sequencing failure during an IMC RNAV Z 12R approach to MSP, causing the aircraft to miss the final approach course with a frozen MFD and incorrect CDI deflection. They executed a missed approach, switched to ILS 12L, and landed safely, attributing the event to the FMS software issue.

synopsis: CE-750 Maintenance Technician reported a pressurization problem was not repaired correctly and an incorrect part was supplied for a thrust reverser lock-out panel.
summary: A mechanic at ZZZ repair station found Aircraft X pressurizing on the ground due to a stuck check valve and received an unfinished thrust reverser disable panel. The mechanic identified these as repeat issues caused by previous repairs lacking inspector signatures and refused to install the incorrect part until the MEL was removed.

synopsis: BE33 pilot experienced engine failure on final approach and landed in a field short of the runway. The aircraft was undamaged and the next day the engine started normally.
summary: The pilot of a Beechcraft Debonair experienced an engine failure on final approach after switching fuel selectors to the left main tank. The pilot executed an emergency landing in a grass field with no injuries or damage, later confirming the engine ran normally after refueling.

synopsis: PA-25 pilot reported fuel exhaustion and an off airport landing in an open field during glider tow operations.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure during glider towing due to misjudging fuel levels and departing with insufficient reserves. After releasing the glider, the pilot landed safely in an open field, refueled, and returned to the airport with no damage or injuries.

synopsis: C182RG instructor and CFI student reported the gear lever was raised while on the ground during a touch and go landing which resulted in a nose gear retraction and prop strike.
summary: A student pilot and instructor practicing short field landings in a C182RG retracted the landing gear while still on the ground during cleanup. The nose gear collapsed, causing the propeller and cowling to strike the runway, attributed to rushing procedures and lack of attentiveness.

synopsis: BD700 flight crew reported taking off without being released by ATC at an airport with a closed Tower.
summary: The pilot and a new co-pilot departed VFR without a clearance due to poor radio reception and poor CRM, causing confusion with ATC regarding flight status. The pilot attributed the decision to fatigue and homesickness, noting a potential conflict with an aircraft on final that was avoided by an immediate right turn.

synopsis: GA instructor pilot reported an incident of a near miss while rolling out on the runway after landing by a close following aircraft.
summary: A pilot landing at GSO on Runway 5R reported that another aircraft, instructed to go around, instead leveled off 100 feet above and landed while the pilot was still taxiing. The reporter attributed the incident to the other pilot's failure to execute the go-around and the tower's authorization of a landing despite the active runway occupancy.

synopsis: GA pilot reported being issued an assigned heading and received no further instructions from ATC until they asked for instructions 2 miles from the airport.
summary: The pilot reported a potential deviation during the approach phase after ATC lost primary radar contact and issued conflicting heading instructions. The supervisor later reviewed the tapes, confirmed the pilot was following initial instructions correctly, and stated the pilot was "clean" regarding the incident.

synopsis: PA28 IFR pilot sitting on the right seat flying at night in full IMC encountered Avionics Audio Panel Failure. Moments later the pilot encountered partial panel and the baggage door opened mid-flight resulting in a diversion to a nearby airport.
summary: A solo pilot flying a Piper Arrow IFR at night experienced audio panel failure, a faulty attitude indicator, and an open baggage door that caused temporary loss of control. The pilot disregarded ATC descent restrictions to land safely in zero visibility, acknowledging the decision to continue despite partial panel issues was a mistake.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported losing control of his aircraft in turbulence during climb after takeoff. Control was recovered at very low altitude over the departure airport and the aircraft maneuvered for a normal landing.
summary: During climb-out after takeoff in VFR conditions, the pilot encountered uncommanded right wing rise and altitude loss despite full aileron input. The pilot reduced power to level the wings, executed a low-altitude turn back to the runway, and landed safely, attributing the event to possible wind shear.

synopsis: A balloon pilot reported striking a power line that was not initially visible. He took evasive action, which snapped the power line, and was able to land safely.
summary: The pilot and observer landed a hot air balloon in a golf course parking lot after striking a power line hidden by a tree. Despite activating blast valves, suspension cables snagged the line briefly before it snapped, allowing a gentle landing.

synopsis: Captain reported receiving an incorrect altimeter setting from Approach Control and elected to remain on QNE for the visual approach. The Controller meant to say 981 HPA for QFE, but kept stating 2981 HPA.
summary: During the UMBEG arrival, a pilot and controller experienced an altimeter discrepancy when the second controller issued a QFE setting of 2981 HPA instead of the requested QNH. The crew reverted to the previous 1004 HPA setting to avoid a 500-foot error and landed safely, attributing the confusion to the controller's broken English and the unexpected unit change.

synopsis: A321 passenger reported the instructions on the door Emergency Exit Door and instruction card quite confusing, taking several minutes to determine the proper steps.
summary: A flight attendant asked a passenger to demonstrate opening an emergency exit door. The passenger could not open the door for several minutes because the door instructions were confusing and the seat pocket instructions were too small to read.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported a NMAC while entering the traffic pattern at JVW with another GA aircraft that turned crosswind.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X entered the left downwind at Raymond-Williams Airport without hearing the departing Aircraft Y, resulting in a reported 50-foot near miss. The pilot extended the downwind to clear the pattern before completing three subsequent takeoffs and landings with no further conflicts.

synopsis: CLT TRACON Controller reported an aircraft's Mode C quit working after it appeared it would not make a crossing restriction.
summary: Air Traffic Control observed Aircraft X reporting 12,000 feet while Mode C indicated 14,500 feet during a STAR arrival. The pilot attributed the discrepancy to a Mode C equipment failure, though the controller suspected a pilot deviation due to the 2,500-foot error before the transponder signal was lost.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew and the Dispatcher involved reported a nose tire tread separation at rotation and the steps taken to safely return the aircraft to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nose gear tire separation during takeoff rotation, causing significant shimmy and debris impact. They returned with gear extended, consulted the AOM for specific procedures, and landed safely with a damaged left nose tire after burning fuel.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported a Right Pack failure and loss of pressurization on climb out at 12,500 feet with subsequent return to departure airport after regaining control of pressurization.
summary: During climbout, a right pack light illuminated, prompting a descent to 10,000 feet where the cabin altitude warning activated despite the cabin remaining below that limit. The crew stabilized pressure and returned for an overweight landing after a child passenger reported nose and ear bleeding.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported Maintenance was unaware of the aircraft's periodic windshield rain repellent treatment.
summary: A First Officer reported that heavy rain obscured forward visibility on a newer model aircraft during landing, forcing a missed approach despite maximum wiper speed. The pilot noted that Maintenance Control was unaware of a required rain repellent re-application program, raising concerns about safety and operational efficiency.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced three separate TCAS events during a visual approach into MDW.
summary: Pilots flying an RNP Y 22L approach to MDW encountered multiple TCAS alerts due to conflicting VFR traffic, resulting in Resolution Advisories that forced altitude deviations and hand-flying. The crew landed safely but noted that mixing VFR general aviation with the instrument approach created significant workload and distraction.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported being vectored off the approach to avoid a light twin pilot that could not or would not comply with ATC instruction.
summary: The reporting pilot and a light twin aircraft were involved during an RNP approach where the twin failed to follow ATC heading and climb instructions. The controller diverted the twin to a VFR field, allowing the reporting crew to complete an uneventful landing after a temporary deviation.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported that he was concerned about the proper procedures for an MEL item that required other systems to operate normally.
summary: The Captain and Maintenance Control disputed MEL verification for engine start and limiter systems, leading to an unnecessary gate engine run after Maintenance suggested assuming systems worked. The Captain later determined this action violated Flight Operations Manual policies regarding MEL applicability and verification procedures.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported an NMAC with a weather balloon at FL400 over Virginia.
summary: During cruise at FL400, the flight crew spotted a white weather balloon with an instrument package passing within 100 to 200 feet of the right wing. The pilot reported the close call to Washington Center, noting that the lack of a transponder on the balloon prevented ATC from issuing a warning or vectoring to avoid the potential impact.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported not being aware of a dent on the aircraft, which was discovered by ground crew at the departure airport.
summary: A flight crew member discovered a minor dent aft of the L1 door after a supervisor provided an email from BNA operations that had not been logged or communicated to the crew. The reporter cited a safety breach because BNA operations failed to notify the flight crew or airline personnel before departure, delaying the maintenance inspection.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported being informed by their company after the event that they violated noise standards during arrival to OAK. The crew was not aware of the procedures and was following published arrival procedures and ATC vectors until cleared for the visual approach.
summary: The flight crew executed a visual approach to OAK Runway 30 following ATC vectors and altitude assignments, including a 3000-foot clearance. Three days later, the company notified them of a noise abatement violation on the base leg, which the crew attributed to a lack of accessible procedures and conflicting ATC instructions.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported descending below the MIA Runway 26R RNAV Approach profile. The autopilot did not capture the vertical path and the crew did not detect it until they were low causing a GPWS warning.
summary: The flight crew descended below the 1,500 ft minimum to 1,300 ft on the RNAV/GPS Rwy 26R approach due to distraction by weather. This triggered a ground proximity alert, but the crew corrected the altitude and safely landed after confirming obstacle clearance.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate Jet Captain reported a descent on vectors that was meant for another aircraft.
summary: During descent via vectors for RMN, the First Officer misidentified a blocked clearance for another aircraft as ours and read back a descent to 2000 feet. The controller corrected the error, instructed the crew to maintain 2000 feet, and attributed the incident to the crew's failure to follow standard altitude change confirmation procedures.

synopsis: Captain of a corporate turbojet reported issues with flying with contract pilots.
summary: The Flying Pilot and a contract Non-Flying Pilot missed a requested position report waypoint due to Crew Resource Management issues and tension. The NFP's defensive behavior, refusal to follow SOPs, and incorrect altitude entry contributed to the missed report, though the flight concluded safely.

synopsis: BE20 Pilot reported a NMAC on approach to landing when the aircraft was being overtaken by an L39 from behind. The pilot reported the second aircraft made a go-around.
summary: A King Air 200 pilot reported a near midair collision with an L-39 jet during the traffic pattern at an uncontrolled airport. The incident resulted from the jet's incorrect position reports and failure to identify the King Air, causing the jet to close in from behind and execute a go-around.

synopsis: SEA Tower Controller reported the TRACON could not accept an aircraft on a previously agreed to heading which placed the aircraft into confliction with parallel runway departure traffic.
summary: The tower controller reported that Departure controllers cancelled a 140-degree turn for Aircraft X, forcing it straight out and causing a TCAS RA with Aircraft Y due to unsafe proximity. The controller attributed the conflict to Departure's lack of coordination regarding protected airspace and failure to follow letter of agreement procedures for propeller aircraft.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Approach Controller reported issuing an altitude below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude, triggering a Low Altitude Alert.
summary: An air traffic controller inadvertently cleared Aircraft X to descend to 2000 feet instead of the intended 3000 feet due to a slip of the tongue and failure to verify the pilot's readback. The controller issued a visual approach clearance after the pilot reported the airport in sight, and the aircraft landed without incident.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported degraded weather at the destination and alternate required the crew to obtain a new alternate. Captain reported a runway change added to the mix and with no printer aboard the aircraft it made for a very busy scenario.
summary: The crew experienced FMC data saturation during a degraded weather arrival at ZZZ while managing multiple alternate plans and runway changes. The reporter attributes the resulting safety degradation to the lack of a flight deck printer, which hindered the transcription of critical performance data and weather requests.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported improperly reloading the FMC when given a new vector for the MCO ILS 18R which resulted in an overshoot and a missed approach initiated by ATC.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that late ATC vectors between HAMMY and TUFFE during an ILS approach to MCO Runway 18R caused a rushed FMS entry error. This resulted in an overshoot, aggressive autopilot corrections, and a go-around to re-intercept final outside HAMMY.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported a gate return for fuel and pressure from the ramp controller to proceed to the gate even though the Captain felt there was not adequate clearance.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing to a gate for refueling, a ramp controller pressured them to proceed despite the pilot's concerns about insufficient clearance from a blocking aircraft. The pilot refused to move without visual confirmation, citing the controller's unsafe instruction to ignore clearance doubts even with AccuPark available.

synopsis: B737 Crew reported being informed after a landing that aircraft blew a tire on take off. Crew was upset for not being advised prior to landing.
summary: The flight crew took off and blew the number 3 main tire due to FOD from a preceding aircraft but were not notified by maintenance or ATC. They landed normally, discovered the damage at the gate, and the aircraft was taken out of service, though the crew felt proper notification could have allowed for safer landing preparations.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported smoke in the cockpit during takeoff. Oxygen masks were donned and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer reported smoke in the cockpit shortly after V1, caused by maintenance applying excessive chemical compound to the engines. The crew executed an immediate return and visual landing, noting that poor communication protocols with the cabin crew created confusion during the event.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a dual air conditioning pack failure while climbing out and subsequent divert.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered severe weather and dual pack failures during climb, forcing a descent to 10,000 feet and a diversion to ZZZ after the cabin altitude warning activated. Post-landing, the crew discovered masks had deployed in the cabin, leading to an investigation and temporary removal from flying duties.

synopsis: Ramp Agent reported being injured between a pallet and a dolly when the Container Loader moved the pallet.
summary: A ground handler was pinned between a dolly and a freight pallet while lowering locks at the gate of Aircraft X. The container loader operator moved the pallet without seeing the handler, crushing their knees and causing injuries requiring hospitalization.

synopsis: C208 pilot reported a missed approach when the aircraft iced up on approach to the destination airport, was unable to climb above 4000 feet, requested a descent and returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot encountered severe icing during an IFR approach, causing rapid airspeed decay and climb failure despite de-ice systems. Due to radio coverage gaps, the pilot relayed an emergency request via another aircraft to descend to 1,000 feet, successfully breaking out of the ice layer and landing safely.

synopsis: Global Express Captain reported taking evasive action on ASE Taxiway A between Taxiways A4 and A5 because he perceived his wingtip near the windsock located 84 ft off the taxiway centerline.
summary: The flight crew experienced a near-midair collision with a windsock while taxiing a large aircraft on Taxiway A at ASE. The pilot corrected the path to clear the obstruction by a few feet and recommended operational warnings and infrastructure changes to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: C680A First Officer reported the aircraft landed with a left main gear disagree indication. Post flight maintenance sign off showed they cleaned cannon plugs.
summary: The pilot landed the aircraft believing the gear was down and locked after completing checklists. Maintenance reported cleaning a cannon plug, which the pilot attributed to the issue on the less than one-year-old aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported two flights reported passengers observed a missile launch that crossed the aircraft's route of flight. Dispatcher reported no information was provided until after the fact.
summary: Air traffic controllers and dispatchers managed a missile launch near Japan affecting Aircraft X and Y. Due to delayed corporate security information, controllers relied on internet reports and passenger alerts to establish diversion plans for flights crossing the affected area.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported that without paper checklists, the requirement to stow the EFB when the EFB mount is inoperative leaves no Normal Checklist available.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported that an inoperative EFB mount forces stowing the tablet during critical phases, making electronic checklists inaccessible. The reporter attributes this operational conflict to missing paper checklists and unavailable maintenance parts, requesting a return to paper procedures.

synopsis: A Piper PA31 Captain reported an aborted takeoff due to engine surging.
summary: The pilot and trainee aborted a PA-31 takeoff at 80 knots due to right engine surging. Despite normal engine gauges, the pilot took command, exited the runway, and returned to the ramp.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported a rear galley compartment opened during landing ejecting its contents. The latch had been properly locked. Maintenance indicated they had received numerous calls about the latches on this type of galley.
summary: During landing, a rear galley compartment on the aircraft popped open despite Flight Attendants confirming the latches were secured, ejecting soda cans into the aisle. A mechanic attributed the failure to known issues with either the bottom latch or the top hinge on this specific galley door type.

synopsis: Vans RV8 pilot reported that the engine failed during cruise flight.
summary: The pilot experienced increasing oil temperature, decreasing RPM, and a rough-running engine that froze during cruise. A successful dead stick landing was executed on a road with no injuries or damage, though EMS responded to the scene.

synopsis: DA-20 Instructor pilot reported that the brakes failed on one side causing the aircraft to veer off the runway striking a taxiway light cover.
summary: An instructor and student in a Diamond DA-20 experienced total right brake failure after landing, forcing a 180-degree turn on the runway. While taxiing, the aircraft veered left into the grass and struck a taxiway light because the mixture cutoff failed to stop the propeller in time.

synopsis: Aero Commander pilot reported requesting priority landing due to low fuel condition, and was unable to go-around when a Cessna was slow to turn final approach.
summary: A pilot with low fuel in an analog-gauge aircraft was cleared to land second behind a Cessna on final approach. Despite the pilot's refusal to go around due to fuel concerns, the Cessna executed a go-around, resulting in the pilot landing safely but being met by ground safety equipment.

synopsis: An Observer near Texas Tech University Medical Center (TA79) reported a new crane 120 ft high is lighted but its boom, over 100 ft long horizontally, is not lighted and presents a hazard for helicopters taking off and landing at the adjacent helipad.
summary: A pilot reported a new 120-foot crane with an unlit boom near the University Medical Center helipad in Lubbock, TX. The reporter warns that the unmarked boom poses a collision risk for helicopters operating at the pad day and night.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported the complete loss of electrical power due to a failed alternator, and elected to divert to a nearby suitable airport where a successful landing was accomplished.
summary: The pilot experienced a total alternator failure at 11,500 feet east of La Veta Pass, causing all avionics to go offline after lowering the gear. The aircraft diverted to Pueblo (PUB), where the pilot landed using a Stratus ADS-B unit and iPad while relying on tower light signals for traffic and clearance.

synopsis: PC-12 pilot reported the EFIS displays flashed and went blank on approach, normal operation was regained by resetting electrical system.
summary: During descent through heavy weather, the pilot experienced EFIS/GPS display failures at 13,000, 5,000, and 4,000 feet, forcing a hold and electrical reset before completing the approach. The crew replaced generator number 1 and plans a test flight to verify the aircraft is airworthy.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: ZLC Center Controller reported denying a routing request to BOI Approach Control due to weather and terrain. Approach called the Center Controller's Supervisor who approved the route.
summary: An air traffic controller rejected a BOI Approach request to route an aircraft through weather at 10,000 feet due to a Minimum IFR Altitude of 10,900 feet. A supervisor subsequently approved the unsafe clearance without the controller's knowledge, bypassing safety protocols before the controller was relieved.

synopsis: SNA Tower Controller reported being unable to provide required Class C airspace services due to a radar outage.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an ASR-9 radar failure caused intermittent target loss and inaccurate data tags during a final approach in Class Charlie airspace. This resulted in a late traffic call for an air carrier aircraft on a parallel runway, which the pilot found uncomfortably close.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported being uncertain of the taxi instructions from ground control, causing them to cross a hold short line of an active runway.
summary: The flight crew taxied across the hold short line for Runway 8L without explicit clearance while another carrier back-taxied and departed from that runway. The pilots attributed the incident to ATC rushing an opposite-direction departure in a congested environment, which led to confusing instructions and a lack of specific hold-short commands.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that after several flights the aircraft was found to have had a lockout pin installed in the wheel well.
summary: The Captain discovered logbook errors regarding thrust reverser deferrals at ZZZ and departed for ZZZ1, but later learned a lockout pin was found in the wheel well after several legs. The pilot attributed the oversight to unclear documentation and visibility of the pin, noting that maintenance procedures were not visibly confirmed by the flight crew.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported misinterpreting an altitude clearance on departure due to a communication error with ATC. The cleared altitude was confirmed with ATC and the flight proceeded uneventfully.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring missed a 5000-foot altitude cap issued by Ground Control during taxi at SFO due to construction distractions. After initially climbing via the SID, the crew identified the missed restriction from the First Officer's notes, and Departure Control issued a corrected clearance before the aircraft reached 5000 feet.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported unconsciously starting the APU while the unit was still being serviced by a Mechanic.
summary: During pre-pushback, the Captain started the APU while a mechanic was servicing it, misinterpreting a ramp agent's comment as clearance. The APU was immediately shut down after the error was realized, causing no injuries but highlighting a communication failure and expectation bias.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that the fuel system condition did not match the requirements in the fuel pump deferral.
summary: The flight crew refused to depart with 480 lbs of fuel in the center tank due to a deferred pump MEL requiring an empty tank. After maintenance initially claimed the fuel was unusable, the crew contacted dispatch and maintenance control to change the MEL, resolving the issue after a 1 hour 20 minute delay.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported executing a go-around after TRACON issued a low altitude alert on approach to CVG. The localizer was later found to be mistuned.
summary: During an ILS 9 approach to CVG, the crew missed the localizer due to an inadvertent frequency change from 111.9 to 110.9, causing a go-around at 2,400 feet. The pilot attributed the error to high task loading and confirmation bias, noting no FMC warnings appeared until after the missed approach.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a traffic conflict while on final approach at ONT. While complying with TCAS commands the flight became temporarily destabilized on the approach, but recovered and made an uneventful landing.
summary: A B737 crew on an ILS 26L approach to ONT received a TCAS RA to descend at 1500 AGL due to VFR traffic, conflicting with ATC's "no factor" assessment. The PF descended and turned to avoid the unseen traffic, resulting in an unstable approach below the glideslope before re-intercepting and landing normally.

synopsis: Falcon 900EX Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after the #3 engine failed in flight.
summary: During climb through FL360, the crew heard a bang and vibration before Engine #3 spooled down with zero N1 and high ITT. The crew executed the shutdown checklist, diverted to a nearby alternate with a long runway, and landed safely.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported a track deviation on arrival into MIA. Chart design and fatigue were cited as contributing.
summary: The fatigued flight crew mistakenly followed the Lost Comm Box procedure instead of the RNAV 26R arrival into MIA, deviating to waypoint HOXIL. Approach Control cleared them direct to NAYIB, and the flight landed uneventfully, with the error attributed to fatigue and a confusing chart presentation.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported a flap disagree in climb out and returned to the departure airport for a successful flaps 10 landing.
summary: After takeoff, the flight crew experienced a Flap Disagree warning indicating outboard flaps remained at 10 while inboards indicated up. The crew executed the QRH, consulted Operations, and landed safely with emergency trucks standing by, concluding the incident was an inherent aircraft risk.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported the point where the runways intersect at LGA is uneven. This causes a large jolt for aircraft taking off on Runway 13/31.
summary: The pilot reported significant bumps and impacts during takeoff from Runway 13 at LGA, specifically at a joint connection and while crossing Runway 4/22. The uneven surface caused jolts comparable to a hard landing, which the pilot believes may eventually damage landing gear or other aircraft components.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot of a turbojet reported issues with Tower managing aircraft separation at an airport with multiple closures of taxiways and one runway.
summary: The pilot back-taxied Runway 24R at BKL Airport while another aircraft was on short final, causing a go-around due to the pilot's obscured view from the aircraft's A-pillar. The controller apologized, sequenced the landing after the pilot cleared the runway, and no further action was taken regarding the incident.

synopsis: A Maintenance Inspector reported that the front engine mounts did not have washers installed.
summary: A line maintenance technician observed mechanics installing a new right engine but failed to verify washers on the forward mount bolts due to complacency. The technician noted that while aft bolts were correct, the front installation lacked washers because the team did not double-check after the initial successful installation.

synopsis: Flight crew of a corporate turboprop aircraft reported a near miss while on 3 mile final approach.
summary: During a visual approach, a Pilatus crew executed an evasive left turn to avoid a merging PA-28 Cherokee after Tower instructed the Cherokee to follow them. The near miss occurred because the Cherokee pilot mistakenly believed he was following a Cessna, while TCAS provided no warning.

synopsis: Single engine aircraft pilot reported operating in restricted airspace after his GPS signal was lost.
summary: The pilot flew through restricted airspace R3601A at 2500 MSL after failing to notice a lost GPS signal. A fighter jet intercepted the aircraft, prompting the pilot to depart northward to exit the restricted area.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot of a small aircraft on VFR descent to LHM reported a Near Mid-Air Collision (NMAC) with an unidentified twin-engine aircraft departing LHM.
summary: A VFR pilot descending to Lincoln Regional for Runway 15 encountered a climbing twin-engine aircraft while still on autopilot. The pilot made a minor control input but required no evasive action as the aircraft passed well clear.

synopsis: A corporate pilot reported the Ground Controller was overworked and lashed out at the pilot for multiple radio calls.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing at a construction-impacted airport, they were instructed to cross a closed runway and call Ground on an incorrect frequency. The overwhelmed Ground controller, managing multiple frequencies, failed to respond initially and later admonished the crew before issuing a taxi clearance.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported difficulty with new navigation equipment while on a RNAV approach and experiencing rapidly deteriorating visibility while on a VFR flight.
summary: The pilot encountered two issues while flying a Garmin 650-equipped aircraft into KTTD: first, inability to advance the GPS during an RNAV-A approach caused a deviation, resolved by canceling IFR due to high ceilings; second, sudden haze from forest fires degraded VFR to IFR conditions, requiring an emergency IFR clearance.

synopsis: UAV operator reported operating within the borders of Class E airspace.
summary: The Remote PIC operated a Mavic Pro UAV within Class E airspace at Philips AAF due to an incomplete airspace inspection and failure to verify others' incorrect Class G identification. No conflicts with other aircraft occurred during this violation.

synopsis: SCT Controller reported intentionally turning an aircraft below the MVA because the aircraft was over the ocean and not in unsafe proximity to terrain.
summary: An LAX Approach controller and trainee directed Aircraft X to climb through a 4,000-foot MVA over the ocean to avoid excessive flight miles, despite Arrival Controller denial. The reporter asserts the aircraft remained safe over water and recommends raising go-around climb limits to 5,000 feet to prevent future MVA violations.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Seattle Center Controller reported that an aircraft checked in after a previous loss of communication.
summary: An OJT Instructor on Sector 10 discovered an IFR aircraft had flown 122 miles without coordination after the pilot reported lost comms with ZLC. The controller cleared the aircraft to its destination and handed it off to approach, noting no flight plan existed in the system.

synopsis: ZSU Controller reported an aircraft initiated their go-around instructions from the approach end of the runway at TISX instead of the departure end which placed the aircraft below the MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller and a student pilot in Aircraft X experienced a terrain conflict during a practice ILS missed approach at TISX when the pilot climbed below the 2400-foot MVA. The controller issued a safety alert and instructed the pilot to maintain terrain clearance until reaching 2400 feet, after which the aircraft safely joined its route.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a go-around was executed due to a blurred vision through the windshield caused by heavy rain.
summary: The Captain and First Officer executed a go-around during final approach in heavy rain due to poor visibility through the forward windows. They subsequently landed uneventfully after conditions improved, attributing the decision to effective crew resource management and windshield blurring.

synopsis: CRJ900 Captain reported the FMC showed a climb vice a descent due to the designation of a climb waypoint on the SID even though the crew programmed a lower altitude.
summary: A CRJ-900 crew encountered an FMS error while descending from FL250 to meet a FL230 restriction at NUTZE on the BARMY3.NUTZE route. The system incorrectly commanded a climb because it treated the SID waypoint as a climb point, forcing manual intervention to avoid a potential altitude deviation.

synopsis: CRJ900 flight crew reported neglecting to stow the spoilers until shortly before landing.
summary: A fatigued crew conducting a night ILS approach to RWY 35 used flight spoilers to intercept the glideslope but failed to retract them due to high workload and missed callouts. The First Officer noticed the deployed spoilers at 100 feet AGL and retracted them before a safe landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported difficulty and stress in working with Guatemalan controllers. He was given a revised, unacceptable takeoff clearance by MGGT Tower and did not receive the winds for takeoff. Captain also stated the RNAV (RNP) Runway 20 Approach is allegedly flawed in its design. It consistently positions the aircraft low when on the glidepath at the decision altitude.
summary: A pilot reported that at MGGT, controllers issued conflicting clearances and failed to provide wind updates, resulting in a heavy takeoff with a suspected tailwind and sluggish rotation. Additionally, the pilot described the RNAV (RNP) approach to Runway 20 as geometrically flawed, causing aircraft to appear low over the runway threshold despite correct instrument indications.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported the autopilot and yaw dampener disconnected without other alerts. The rudder trim displaced full right until the First Officer centered the trim after a suspected trim switch malfunctioned.
summary: The pilot reported that at 15,000 feet, the autopilot and yaw damper disconnected with rudder trim pegged right, likely masked by turbulence. The crew maintained heading in a slip until the First Officer centered the trim, revealing a switch fault where trim continued traveling after release.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported making a forced landing short of the destination airport due to loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot executed a precautionary forced landing eight miles west of ZZZ during arrival due to engine sputter and power loss. Fuel contamination with unknown debris was suspected, but no injuries or damage occurred, allowing the pilot to purge the tanks, refill, and continue the flight.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported a Bravo airspace intrusion on departure from HAF due to an aircraft close to max gross weight and terrain considerations.
summary: The pilot took off from Runway 30 at HAF with full fuel, violating a noise restriction requiring a 500-foot climb before turning right toward hills. Distracted by checking airspace graphics, the pilot realized the turn was unsafe, contacted NorCal to activate the IFR plan, and received a squawk code and Bravo airspace intrusion warning.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported returning to the departure airport due to high cylinder head and oil temperature, possibly due to a significant temperature inversion.
summary: A pilot flying a C172 from Salinas (SNS) experienced severe engine overheating during a climb due to a temperature inversion and the aircraft's cooling limitations. The pilot executed a 180-degree turn, returned to SNS, and landed safely after the engine cooled, with post-flight inspection revealing no fire.

synopsis: TBM7 pilot reported an altitude deviation resulted from a pitot static system anomaly.
summary: During climb in IMC, the pilot experienced a static system failure misdiagnosed as a pitot issue, causing a false altitude gain to 8,000 feet. ATC vectored the aircraft to heading 360 to recover the assigned altitude after the pilot activated alternate static and cross-checked GPS.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Turboprop flight crew reported departing EYE VFR due to not being able to contact ATC for an IFR clearance. During departure the aircraft encountered opposing traffic requiring an evasive maneuver into Class C airspace.
summary: A departing VFR flight from EYE executed evasive action to avoid a light aircraft on the Runway 21 localizer after failing to establish ATC contact. The crew penetrated Class C airspace during the maneuver, but ATC later confirmed the conflict and validated the captain's decision.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported a NMAC with several jumpers near S33 at 12,500 feet that required evasive action.
summary: A pilot flying VFR at 12,500 feet near Madras Muni executed an aggressive left turn to avoid three unlit parachutists after Seattle Center cancelled flight following due to sector saturation. The reporter attributed the incident to ATC's inability to provide separation services and failure to advise of the jumpers, noting the lack of position lights made visual detection difficult.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZDC Center Controller reported an aircraft called them that was on an IFR flight plan outside of their airspace in another sector and with no radar data tag.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller handled an IFR aircraft with a missing flight plan that was 30–40 miles outside airspace and fluctuating near 17,300 feet. The controller issued a new code and a 20-degree turn before transferring the aircraft, attributing the issue to a failed flight plan handoff and a potential incorrect frequency switch by Approach.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ZID Center controller reported HTS Approach routinely does not accept handoffs or answer the landline.
summary: An air traffic controller attempted multiple handoffs to HTS Approach for Aircraft X two minutes from the boundary but received no answer. The controller issued a non-radar turn to 180 degrees after finally receiving a verbal "keep coming" approval from an out-of-breath controller who claimed the radar position was busy.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: S56 TRACON Controller reported a loss of separation due to a slower speed aircraft in front of a faster departure.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a Developmental Controller managed departures in the Lake and Gunnison sectors where Aircraft X failed to maintain assigned speed, causing separation with Aircraft Y to decrease to 2.6 miles. The Controller issued a turn to avoid terrain after Aircraft X missed crossing restrictions, noting that current departure procedures and reliance on visual separation created safety risks.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: LGB Tower Controller reported not detecting that an inbound aircraft had lined up to the departure end of the runway due to unreliable radar coverage.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a trainee pilot experienced a loss of radar contact on the new FUSION system while Aircraft X was inbound. The pilot flew toward the wrong runway, prompting the controller to issue a climb to 2000 feet and westbound heading to avoid conflict with an arriving air carrier.

synopsis: Center Air Traffic Controller reported two aircraft 'descending via' on crossing STARs were going to have less than required separation due to one aircraft not complying with its crossing restriction.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a single sector with 12 aircraft intervened when Aircraft X missed a 21,000-foot STAR restriction while Aircraft Y descended nearby. The controller attributed the unsafe 5.1-mile separation and frequent restriction misses to inadequate STAR crossing fix spacing, recommending a 3-mile southward shift to increase separation to 8 miles.

synopsis: A Departure Controller reported an A321 departing climbed at a much slower speed than a trailing B737 requiring them to vector the B737 away to maintain separation.
summary: An air traffic controller assigned 3,000 feet to an A321 (Aircraft Y) departing behind Aircraft X on the same SID to prevent loss of separation caused by the A321's rapid acceleration. The controller attributes the near-miss to Tower's failure to account for A321 performance and recommends increasing departure spacing to 4–5 miles.

synopsis: ZZZ Center Controller reported the shift Controller in Charge left the operation for 2 hours on a mid-shift.
summary: An air traffic controller reported being left alone with two bays of strips by their CIC for two hours during a shift with abnormal runway configurations and poor weather. The controller managed holding and a missed approach at ZZZZ, describing the lack of support as unsafe and calling for a facility culture change.

synopsis: ZOA Center controller reported that a sectors' workload has become unmanageable resulting in delays and aircraft conflicts due to the variety of traffic situations and equipment limitations.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 44 reported extreme complexity during a holiday weekend involving VFR and IFR aircraft, including a near-miss at 10,000 and 10,100 feet. The controller attributed the unsafe conditions to system limitations, such as a lack of proposal strips and a dedicated shout line to the tower, which hindered clearance issuance and coordination.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported refusing a trip due to severe weather conditions.
summary: The Captain of an EMB175 deferred departure from ZZZ due to crosswinds exceeding AOM limits and a tornado watch, but was initially removed by the Chief Pilot. The flight was subsequently cancelled after management agreed with the Captain's safety assessment.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew reported a loss of pressurization while climbing through 10,000 feet, accomplishing the relevant checklists, and safely returning to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a pressurization failure during climb after takeoff from EWR, causing cabin altitude to exceed 10,000 feet and requiring an immediate descent and return. The aircraft landed safely, but the crew determined the pressurization system was inoperative and swapped to another aircraft for the next leg.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported that the Captain initiated a low speed rejected takeoff when the Surface Movement Guidance System (SMGS) lights illuminated on the runway.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff on Runway 10L/DD after the Captain observed illuminated Runway Red Center Lights triggered by another aircraft crossing the hold short line. The crew completed checklists, parked for verification, and subsequently prepared for a successful departure.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported a flap malfunction and difficulty selecting which QRH flap configuration checklist to use.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a flap extension failure on a Boeing 737 during approach to PDX, resulting in a flaps-up landing after troubleshooting revealed trailing edge asymmetry. The crew managed the emergency with ARFF support, landing safely with high brake temperatures that required extended cooling before baggage handling could resume.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a return to the departure airport following a #1 Hydraulic Pump failure after takeoff.
summary: After takeoff, the Engine #1 Hydraulic Low Pressure light illuminated during gear retraction due to a left engine hydraulic pump failure. The crew followed QRH procedures and returned for a normal overweight landing before taxiing to the gate for logbook entries.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported misunderstanding Ramp Control's taxi instructions and taxied on an active taxiway without clearance from Ground Control.
summary: The flight crew at DTW inadvertently taxied onto active Taxiway K without clearance while proceeding to Spot 5 after pushback. The incident resulted from ambiguous ramp markings and charts that failed to clearly distinguish the boundary between the ramp area and the active movement area.

synopsis: CRJ200 Crew reported a problem with the ACARS that prevented the system from providing timely takeoff data and SELCAL aural alerts.
summary: The flight crew received a delayed SELCAL alert after takeoff indicating an ACARS flap setting change from 20 to 8, caused by a malfunctioning ACARS system that failed to provide aural warnings prior to departure. The crew attributed the unsafe situation to the system's inability to extinguish advisory messages and the burden of rerunning performance data.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported an altitude preselect anomaly led to an altitude overshoot on arrival into LGA.
summary: During cruise and approach to LGA, the crew experienced random altitude preselect jumps, causing the autopilot to overshoot the assigned 4,000 feet. The pilot attributed the incident to looking away from the Flight Mode Annunciator during altitude capture, requiring a manual descent correction.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported loss of left engine oil quantity in cruise. The crew elected to shut down the engine and divert.
summary: During cruise at 29,000 ft, the crew observed zero left engine oil quantity and dropping pressure, prompting a diversion and engine shutdown per QRH. Maintenance later confirmed the engine was completely out of oil, though the aircraft landed safely following standard procedures.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported departing an uncontrolled field prior to being released by ARTCC.
summary: The flight crew departed VFR after receiving a hold-for-release clearance but failed to contact ARTCC a second time to obtain the formal IFR release. They realized the omission at 3,000 MSL, confirmed the clearance with ARTCC while maintaining VMC, and proceeded uneventfully to their destination.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported the new LED landing lights do not provide the level of illumination found in the older incandescent bulbs.
summary: A pilot reported that retrofit LED landing lights provide insufficient intensity and illumination for night landings at Central American airports with substandard markings. The pilot attributed increased maintenance issues, such as cracked podding, to the difficulty of landing safely with these lights.

synopsis: B787 flight crew reported an anomaly with the navigation function of the FMC during an update of the winds on an oceanic route.
summary: The crew flying a random Atlantic route experienced an FMC anomaly where a waypoint dropped after a wind update, forcing the Captain to manually fly the track. The pilot attributed this to a known Boeing issue and recommended avoiding wind updates on Atlantic tracks until resolved.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that following two go-around maneuvers due to windshear, diverting to alternate in a low fuel condition.
summary: The Captain flew the aircraft, which encountered windshear alerts on two short final approaches, causing go-arounds and a diversion to an alternate airport. The crew declared minimum fuel and urgency due to the weather and holding delays but landed safely with approximately 12,200 pounds of fuel remaining.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain and Dispatcher reported that the company elected to not notify the crew of a seismic event in the area of the destination airport.
summary: A pilot reported that a dispatcher withheld real-time USGS seismic event information from the crew en route to ZZZ, fearing an unnecessary diversion. The pilot concluded that censoring this security data prevented the crew from evaluating potential risks and agreed that timely communication is essential for safety.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported database update issues while transiting through Brazilian airspace. Crew were cleared to waypoints not in the updated database.
summary: The crew departed ZZZ and switched to a new navigation database after dispatch confirmed new Brazilian airways. Enroute, ATC reported the filed route did not exist and attempted to clear the aircraft to missing waypoints until a clearance to the end of Brazilian airspace was issued.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a tow bar disconnect during pushback due to shear-pin failure as the push crew aligned the nose wheel. Captain questioned ground personnel training may have contributed to the event.
summary: The pilot reported multiple pushback incidents involving tow-bar misalignment and shear pin failures that caused the aircraft to lunge toward ground crew, narrowly avoiding injury. The reporter attributes these safety risks to inadequate ramp agent training, supervision, and a lack of procedures ensuring tow-bar alignment before disconnecting.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a lightning strike at FL180. The crew elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a lightning strike with a blinding flash and explosive concussion near 18,000 ft during the climb phase. Concerned about potential damage and terrain, they returned to the departure airport, completed relevant checklists, and executed a successful overweight landing with no defects found.

synopsis: CE-560 flight crew reported overshooting assigned altitude on descent due to inadvertent autopilot disconnect and distraction with iPads.
summary: Two experienced pilots descended below their cleared 12,000 ft altitude to 10,500 ft because the Pilot Flying's autopilot disconnected unnoticed while both crew members were distracted by iPads. The event was identified as a Crew Resource Management failure where neither pilot monitored the aircraft's altitude capture.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported declaring minimum fuel due to weather hold and windshear go-around.
summary: The crew diverted from VHHH due to wind shear and weather, facing ATC confusion and ramp closures at alternates ZZZ2 and ZZZ3. High workload and stress led to a minimum fuel declaration and a final approach in heavy rain, resulting in a landing with under 10,000 lbs of fuel.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reported on climb out with one air conditioning pack deferred, the other pack failed. Captain reported crew ran QRH procedure and used deferred pack to provide pressurization and cooling on return to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to ZZZ after Pack 1 failed during climb-out, leaving no pressurization. They utilized the MEL'd Pack 2 to maintain cabin altitude tolerances, resulting in high temperatures and a delay but a safe landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported the company is engaged in a policy of intimidating pilots into not using the company's fatigue policy.
summary: A pilot reported that the Company suspended a Captain for calling in fatigued, creating an intimidating environment that discourages crew from using the Fatigue Policy. The reporter stated this retaliation compromises safety by forcing pilots to risk their employment to report fatigue or other safety concerns.

synopsis: Piper PA28 flight instructor reported the engine lost power during climb, then regained power when turning crosswind for a parallel runway.
summary: During a student touch-and-go climb at 300 feet, the instructor experienced a partial power loss with RPM dropping to 1000, suspected to be carburetor-related. The pilot diverted to a parallel runway, requested priority without declaring an emergency, and landed safely with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: ASK 21 glider instructor pilot reported landing safely after noticing the left aileron had become partially disconnected from the control linkage apparently due to improper maintenance.
summary: A student pilot and instructor flew a club training glider during an aero tow when the left aileron partially disconnected due to improper assembly by students during maintenance. The instructor maintained control with limited inputs, executed a high crosswind entry, and landed safely after the aileron fully detached on rollout.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a go around was required on final approach when another GA aircraft turned base and caused an airborne conflict.
summary: A pilot flying VFR on final approach to Runway 17 at ZZZ executed a right turn to avoid a flight school aircraft turning base from downwind. The reporter attributes the conflict to the school owner's incorrect instruction that pattern traffic always has right-of-way, creating a risk of mid-air collision.

synopsis: Gulfstream III First Officer reported a dual engine flameout at night at cruise altitude with total loss of electrical power, restart was accomplished at 13,000 feet, no avionics and a divert field landing.
summary: The flight crew at FL450 experienced dual engine flameouts and total electrical loss due to turbulence. After restoring power briefly, they restarted engines below 13,000 feet without avionics and landed at the nearest airport.

synopsis: C150 Pilot reported a power loss during climb and successful landing at a divert field.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss at 5,200 feet MSL while in contact with TRACON flight following. After diverting to the nearest airport and landing safely, the engine restarted during taxi, allowing the aircraft to reach transient parking for inspection.

synopsis: SR20 instructor pilot reported demonstrating exceptionally deep stall characteristics to a fellow instructor.
summary: Two instructors practicing stalls in an SR20 observed the right wing stalling before the left, causing a 55-degree bank and 25-degree nose-low attitude. The reporter noted the aircraft remained fully controllable with no limitations exceeded, but submitted the report due to program concerns regarding these stall characteristics.

aircraft: Bell Helicopter Textron Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Bell Jet Ranger pilot reported losing communications with ATC, and inadvertently penetrating VIP TFR.
summary: A pilot flying a low-altitude relief mission within a VIP TFR lost radar and communications contact due to terrain masking. The pilot was later questioned by the Secret Service after ATC mistakenly identified a separate VFR aircraft penetrating the TFR as the missing relief flight.

synopsis: A pilot reported the Gansner Field (2O1) rotating beacon is non-operational at night.
summary: A pilot reported that the rotating beacon at Gansner Field, Quincy, CA, has been non-operational for three months due to a rickety tower and lack of funds for repairs. The pilot expressed concern that airport and county officials are not addressing this hazard in an area with few ground references.

synopsis: A320 rejected takeoff due to indications [loud bang, right yaw, number engine smoke, right engine fail EICAS] of engine fail. Aircraft Rescue & Firefighting [ARFF] confirm no active fire, escorted to gate.
summary: During takeoff acceleration, the crew aborted after a loud bang, right yaw, and ENG 2 FAIL ECAM message. Smoke was reported from Engine 2 by the flight deck and a following aircraft, but ARFF found no fire, leading to a one-engine taxi to the gate without evacuation.

synopsis: A PA28 instructor pilot reported that during climb they had a near miss with another PA28 that was on descent.
summary: An instructor and student pilot in a training aircraft experienced a close call with Aircraft Y while climbing and turning east after departure. The reporter attributed the conflict to ATC clearances that allowed both aircraft to approach dangerously close despite prior traffic advisories.

synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor reported that during climb the with engine throttle set at full power the aircraft was unable to climb and the engine power was decreasing.
summary: A student pilot and CFI experienced severe engine pulsing and power loss during the climb phase of a soft-field takeoff, resulting in a low-speed stall warning and an emergency landing on an adjacent runway. The aircraft returned to the ramp under its own power with continued roughness, though the specific mechanical cause was not identified in the report.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported on downwind at LOM being passed underneath by another GA aircraft that continued on to a landing that required a corrective maneuver for separation.
summary: The pilot reported that Aircraft Y ignored radio calls and cut them off on left downwind at LOM by flying below the standard 1500-foot pattern altitude. The reporter attributed the incident to Aircraft Y's deliberate low altitude and refusal to yield, forcing a corrective maneuver to avoid a collision.

synopsis: C177 pilot reported landing in a field after encountering IMC weather conditions in flight.
summary: The pilot departed, flew 50 miles east, and made an emergency landing in a field after visibility deteriorated into IMC conditions over a ravine.

synopsis: ZDC Center Controller and flight crew reported the aircraft turned early on an RNAV SID.
summary: Aircraft X pilots departed CLT on Runway 18C after a last-minute change from 18L, causing the FMS to drop the BATTA waypoint and trigger an early turn toward RDU on the BARMY3 SID. The controller corrected the course, and the pilots attributed the deviation to the runway change potentially deleting waypoints in the FMS.

synopsis: ZAB Developmental Controller reported issuing a departure clearance through the FSS which did not ensure terrain clearance.
