summary: The crew experienced a left engine failure with loud bang and yaw during takeoff at 872,000 pounds, causing N1 rollback and high EGT. They completed a fuel dump, resolved an autoland discrepancy with maintenance, and landed normally with no visible engine damage.

synopsis: Dash 8 First Officer reported a burning odor and a popped circuit breaker after installing an incorrect panel light bulb.
summary: During cruise at FL200, the First Officer installed an incorrect bulb in the co-pilot's ice detection lamp per the Captain's instruction, causing a burning odor, smoke, and a tripped circuit breaker. The crew subsequently returned to the departure station, descending to 9,000 feet and landing safely, though the reporter criticized the decision not to land at a nearer airport.

synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff due to the propeller autofeather failing to arm.
summary: The crew rejected a takeoff because the auto-feather system failed to arm. The pilot reported this aircraft has experienced daily auto-feather failures or rejected takeoffs for a month yet continues to be signed off for revenue service due to a management and maintenance issue.

synopsis: Dash 8-300 Captain reported rejected takeoff due propeller auto feather failure to arm.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff after the auto feather failed to arm during the normal scan, despite the aircraft having recent maintenance for the same issue. The flight was cancelled, the system was MELed, and the aircraft operated with weight restrictions to the next airport for repairs.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that it was very confusing trying to interpret the MEL book to safely plan out a flight with proper fuel loads and weight restrictions.
summary: A dispatcher initially misinterpreted an MEL regarding an AC PAC, failing to reduce the MTOW for required ECS shutdown. A pilot corrected the error before boarding, attributing the issue to unclear MEL instructions for dispatchers and a lack of specific procedural guidance.

synopsis: An Airbus flight crew reported the activation of the Runway Overrun Prevention System (ROPS) while landing at KORD. They were in compliance with all landing parameters and safely exited the runway after using moderate braking.
summary: During landing in Chicago, the Pilot Monitoring heard a Runway Overrun Prevention System (ROPS) alert seconds before touchdown due to forgetting the aircraft was equipped with it. The captain executed a normal landing with maximum braking and exited safely, though the crew realized they should have initiated a go-around.

synopsis: B747 Captain reported continuing to the destination after experiencing dual FMC failure. One FMC was successfully recovered.
summary: The flight crew experienced a dual FMC failure after radar service terminated in Class II airspace. After holding and completing the QRC without resetting circuit breakers, the right FMC recovered while the left remained failed, leading the crew to continue to the destination.

synopsis: An A320 First Officer reported that multiple traffic targets in the vicinity of Whiteman (WHP) caused TCAS alerts and necessitated maneuvering that prevented the A320 from achieving a stabilized approach by 1,000 feet AGL on the Visual Approach to Runway 15 at BUR. A go-around was performed and the aircraft subsequently landed uneventfully at BUR on runway 08.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS resolution advisory during the visual approach to BUR Runway 15, triggered by conflicting traffic while descending from 6,000 feet. The encounter prevented stabilization, forcing a go-around and a subsequent vector for Runway 8.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence departing EWR in trail of an A321/A320/A319 undifferentiated series aircraft.
summary: The First Officer, acting as pilot flying, encountered moderate wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A320 during a night departure from EWR Runway 22R. After reporting the turbulence to ATC and receiving a right turn and climb instruction, the crew exited the wake and continued the flight without incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported programming the wrong fix into the FMS due to similarly pronounced fixes YELLA and YELAH which are only 56 NM apart.
summary: The flight crew deviated from the intended route while climbing on the OSHNN8.NNAVY departure after entering the similarly spelled fix YELLA instead of YELAH in the FMS. The reporter attributed the error to a rushed clearance near the fix change and the existence of two phonetically identical waypoints with different spellings.

synopsis: CRJ Captain reported a ground conflict with a ground support truck that unexpectedly entered the taxiway.
summary: A ground support truck towing carts failed to stop at Taxiway B2 while the aircraft was taxiing on Taxiway Bravo, forcing the pilot to brake. The truck blocked the taxiway but moved after stopping, resulting in no damage to the aircraft or equipment.

synopsis: C172 student pilot reported a complete electrical system failure while entering the traffic pattern.
summary: A student pilot on a solo cross-country flight experienced a total avionics and communications failure while on downwind for Runway 15. The pilot diverted to land on another runway due to suspected fuel gauge errors and electrical issues, then taxied to parking under tower instructions via cell phone.

synopsis: Saab 340 First Officer reported returning to departure airport after the left engine failed shortly after takeoff.
summary: The First Officer reported that shortly after departure at 500 feet AGL, the left engine failed following an explosion, indicated by high turbine temperature and dropping torque. The crew secured the engine, performed single-engine procedures, and landed safely back at the departure airport within 15 minutes.

synopsis: HS125 Captain reported being alerted to an NMAC by a TCAS RA after shortly after departing the airport.
summary: The pilot and First Officer received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to descend while climbing to 6,000 feet after ATC issued a conflicting climb instruction. They descended to pass 500 feet below a Cessna 172, avoiding a potential collision that the pilot attributed to the controller's failure to address the traffic conflict.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an unusual attitude and unstabilized practice approach while circling to another runway.
summary: During a practice GPS approach, the pilot circled to another runway at minimums and inadvertently banked 40–50 degrees left due to shifting winds. Recognizing the unstable approach while over the runway numbers, the pilot executed a go-around.

synopsis: PA-60 Aerostar pilot reported several system malfunctions and a communication breakdown led to altitude and heading deviation prior to cancellation of IFR clearance.
summary: A pilot and co-pilot conducting a post-annual test flight experienced pressurization and radio failures, leading to confusion over IFR cancellation. The crew inadvertently violated ATC instructions by turning without clearance and nearly landed gear up due to distraction, though they eventually landed safely after a go-around.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported a loss of engine power shortly after takeoff and landing on the takeoff runway with the gear up.
summary: The pilot reported severe power degradation five seconds after takeoff, preventing the aircraft from climbing. The pilot executed a belly landing straight ahead on the runway center, stopping 200 feet from the departure end with no injuries.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported parachute operations in the vicinity of LMO put skydivers and aircraft in danger because of the zone's proximity to V220 and V85. Reporter also stated, regular CTAF communications may interfere with the 'jumpers away' call.
summary: A pilot reported encountering three open parachutes near the HYGEN intersection while flying a direct route to BDU from the north. The reporter attributes the hazard to parachute drop paths varying near active airways and instrument approach paths, compounded by unreliable CTAF communications and conflicting chart instructions.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported maneuvering to increase separation from traffic on approach to Runway 22 at PAH. He descended below the Terminal Area Altitude and received an obstacle warning on his portable GPS unit.
summary: The pilot, flying IFR then VFR to PAH, experienced a TCAS alert and obstacle warning while maneuvering for RWY 22 behind a jet and a GA aircraft. The pilot attributed the incident to failing to re-engage the autopilot, climb to the TAA, and load the approach procedure after switching runways.

synopsis: CL30 Captain reported an NMAC with a light aircraft in the vicinity of HAVEN intersection at 7000 ft.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that while level at 7,000 ft, Lansing Approach vectored them into a Cherokee 200 ft above, triggering a TCAS Resolution Advisory to descend 1,500 ft. The controller failed to answer traffic queries and defended the vector, though the crew noted the controller misstated the vertical separation and prioritized climbing the piston aircraft.

synopsis: Two air carrier Maintenance Technicians reported that during a heavy check on an Airbus 319 it was discovered that lower engine mount pins were missing.
summary: A mechanic reported that three lower engine mount pins were missing from an aft engine mount during a heavy maintenance engine build-up for a Quick Engine Change. The mechanic attributed the oversight to hangar distractions and construction activity, noting the mount was signed off without the pins installed.

synopsis: A319 Maintenance Technician reported finding a check valve was missing a through bolt on an engine that was slow to spool.
summary: A mechanic inspected a #2 engine exhibiting slow acceleration and vibration, discovering a missing through bolt on the 5th stage check valve. The bolt was reinstalled, a FADEC motoring check passed, and the aircraft returned to service.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a missed approach to Runway 8L at ATL due to strong tailwinds combined with ATC handling which led to the aircraft being too high for a stabilized approach.
summary: The flight crew executed a go-around on the STOWL 1 arrival into Atlanta due to strong, unanticipated tailwinds that prevented safe deceleration and descent. The pilot attributed the unsafe approach to ATC's failure to account for wind conditions, though a subsequent approach landed normally.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the aircraft automation had an erratic action with the autopilot trying to stay on path.
summary: During an arrival descent, the flight crew experienced erratic autopilot pitch and high airspeed due to suspected FMC Update 13 software inaccuracies, resulting in a 400-foot altitude deviation below FL300 at the ZZZZZ intersection. The crew later disengaged automation on final approach to hand-fly the RNAV Y Runway XXL approach after the system incorrectly indicated a low path.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported a loss of pressurization while at cruise altitude. An immediate descent was initiated and a successful diversion to a suitable airport was accomplished.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude increase to 13,000 ft, triggering warnings and requiring an immediate descent. Although cabin pressure stabilized below 10,000 ft during the descent, the crew diverted the aircraft and landed safely without assistance.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported construction at AVL has resulted in the actual taxiways in use not matching those depicted on the current Jeppesen airport diagram.
summary: The flight crew at AVL encountered a mismatch between the Jeppesen diagram and actual taxiways due to construction during low-visibility night taxi. They stopped to verify routing with Tower, rejected an intersection departure due to performance software limitations, and back-taxied to runway 35 for a safe departure.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported refusing an aircraft that had several flap/slat write ups and requested a test flight before a return to revenue service.
summary: The Captain refused a Boeing 737 due to recurring Flap/Slat Flight Control System failures causing high-speed emergency landings and brake overheating. He rejected the aircraft because Maintenance cleared it for revenue service without a required test flight to verify the FSEU replacement.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported multiple traffic conflicts while approaching the arrival airport IDA.
summary: The crew of an aircraft at 10,000 feet received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb after a second unidentified target abruptly turned into their path. The pilot disconnected the autopilot and climbed to 11,400 feet, resolving the conflict before descending for a visual approach and uneventful landing.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported discovering the transfer gearbox shroud for a CFM56 engine could be installed upside down and may have occurred on previous gearbox assemblies.
summary: A mechanic reported a potential installation error of the shroud on five GE C2 transfer gearboxes during check and repair, as the manual's 6 o'clock position requirement was unclear. The mechanic noted that standard pressure and backlash checks would not detect this discrepancy, recommending updated maintenance notes and logbook verification.

synopsis: C150 pilot reported landing at a closed airport due to lack of information on AWOS or NOTAMs of the closure.
summary: A pilot landed at ZZZ on a closed runway because the AWOS and phone were inoperative and a NOTAM was missed, despite seeing a yellow X. The pilot departed after realizing the error, attributing the incident to the lack of automated closure broadcasts and poor tenant notification.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Agricultural aircraft pilot reported striking ground equipment during a low level spray pass that caused minor damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot demonstrated a Thrush agricultural aircraft and struck a parked silage wagon with the left landing gear, propeller, and spray components during a low pass. The pilot attributed the collision to a false sense of invulnerability and poor planning after falling into a rhythm from previous successful passes.

synopsis: MEM Tower Supervisor reported problems associated with climb via and maintain clearances off of Memphis especially the ELVIS3 SID
summary: An air traffic controller reported that changing Memphis RNAV SIDs to mixed Climb Via and Maintain clearances increased workload and risk of incorrect clearances during takeoff and climb. Additionally, a 2-degree magnetic heading adjustment to the ELVIS SID without considering local procedures caused confusion and undue risk to the National Airspace System.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an improperly worded CPDLC reroute from ATC on an oceanic flight.
summary: Pilots flying at FL380 inadvertently turned direct to AMAKR after loading a CPDLC reroute that deleted waypoints 41N30 and FATMO. They manually corrected the course and queried SFO regarding the ambiguous clearance, which later included a direct instruction to AMAKR for traffic.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported shutting down the wrong engine on the taxiway. During the attempted engine restart, smoke was reported from the tailpipe.
summary: Pilots mistakenly shut down engine 1 instead of engine 2 during post-landing taxi, causing a power loss. A subsequent restart attempt produced excessive smoke, prompting a precautionary fire truck response and a decision to tow the aircraft to the gate with both engines shut down.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that there was miscommunication with foreign ATC regarding aircraft speed due to a language barrier.
summary: During departure from ZZZZ, the flight crew missed a 200-knot speed restriction due to the controller's unclear English and excessive chatter. The controller later became upset when the aircraft maintained 250 knots, as the speed instruction was lost in the initial clearance.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported difficulty extending the landing gear and flaps related to an improperly handled hydraulic pump deferral at an international station.
summary: The flight crew discovered maintenance failed to disable the HMG or pull circuit breakers for a hydraulic pump issue, causing a loud whine and delayed gear extension. After a go-around due to flap asymmetry and nose gear delay, the crew manually secured the system and landed safely with flaps 20.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported braking aggressively to avoid a collision with a truck on the DEN ramp.
summary: While taxiing to the gate, the Captain braked aggressively to avoid a high-speed truck approaching from the right. The truck skidded to a stop, nearly striking a wing walker.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after experiencing a loss of cabin pressure.
summary: During climb through FL300, the flight crew encountered a cabin altitude warning exceeding 10,000 ft. They descended to FL240, recovered cabin pressure using manual control, diverted to an alternate, and landed uneventfully after donning oxygen masks.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a greater than planned fuel burn on an international flight, likely due to erroneous weight and balance calculations, along with deviations for weather.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced excessive fuel burn during a flight to ZZZ, landing with 8,300 pounds instead of the planned 14,000. They attributed the high burn to a suspected weight and balance miscalculation caused by using standard passenger weights for a sports team carrying heavy equipment.

synopsis: Boeing 777 First Officer reported that a flight attendant sustained an injury as a result of a galley cart tipping over.
summary: During a cruise climb, a galley cart tipped over and struck a flight attendant's leg while the pilots were on break. The flight attendant sustained a swollen, painful leg but remained able to walk.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported that the aircraft has an operational ceiling of 41,000 ft, but the crew O2 mask is only certified to 40,000 ft.
summary: A pilot reported a discrepancy in the 737NG Flight Manual where crew oxygen masks are certified for 40,000 feet cabin altitude, while the aircraft operates up to 41,000 feet. The reporter warns that an explosive decompression at FL410 could render masks ineffective, leaving crews with only 15 seconds of useful consciousness.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported difficulty in executing an RNAV approach using aircraft systems automation which resulted in going below glideslope mid-approach at SDF.
summary: The First Officer and Captain flew an RNAV 35R approach in VFR conditions when the aircraft descended excessively toward the 909-foot Decision Altitude due to autopilot logic. The crew disengaged the autopilot, climbed to rejoin the glideslope, and completed a stable visual approach after triggering gear and altitude alerts.

synopsis: Bombardier Challenger Captain reported encountering severe turbulence that resulted in speed deviations and momentary altitude excursions.
summary: The pilot of a CL-350 encountered severe clear air turbulence and mountain waves at 45,000 feet southwest of LAR VOR, causing rapid bank, airspeed fluctuations, and a false stall warning. The pilot disengaged the autopilot, regained control, and descended to 43,000 feet where the passenger was checked and found to be okay.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV on approach to LAX.
summary: The pilot and first officer encountered a black and white striped drone at 1,300 feet MSL while on the ILS approach. They avoided the drone by 50 feet, notified the tower, and continued to land uneventfully.

synopsis: B747 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after it became clear the fuel system was compromised by improper maintenance at a foreign station.
summary: A local mechanic mistakenly safety-wired the number four fuel transfer valve open instead of closed during pre-flight maintenance, causing an uncontrollable fuel imbalance in cruise. The crew diverted, jettisoned fuel, and landed safely, avoiding a potential engine flameout that would have occurred had the flight continued further.

synopsis: Boeing 777 flight crew reported the aircraft struck the jet bridge while under automated parking guidance due to the improper placement of the jet bridge.
summary: During taxiing to the gate, a B777-200's left engine struck a jet bridge while using the Docking Guidance System. The incident occurred because the bridge was not fully stowed and ground crew failed to signal its proximity to the approaching aircraft.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus flight crew reported an engine failure during climb out. The flight crew returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an in-flight #2 engine failure at 4200 ft, characterized by a pop, vibration, and missing fan blades. They returned safely, landing without incident, and later discovered hot metal fragments on the runway caused by the engine disintegration.

synopsis: DA-42 flight instructor reported diverting to an alternate after an intentionally feathered prop would not unfeather.
summary: During a multi-engine stage check, the instructor and student diverted after failing to unfeather the left propeller due to a faulty accumulator. The reporter noted that required maintenance test flights were not performed after recent engine replacements, which likely would have identified the issue.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported encountering skydivers near DVO. The sectional and terminal charts do not indicate skydiving is present at DVO. A NOTAM was posted only 90 minutes before jump operations began and ATC, possibly unaware, gave no warning of the activity.
summary: A pilot flying over DVO at 2,400 feet encountered two parachutists after canceling flight following with NORCAL TRACON, which had not advised of the activity. The conflict occurred because the relevant NOTAM was issued only 90 minutes prior and lacked chart symbols, prompting the pilot to manually maneuver for separation.

synopsis: A Piper Super Cub pilot reported making two off field landings due to engine performance problems, possibly due to a fuel system anomaly.
summary: The pilot experienced engine vibration and power loss at 4,500 feet, forcing two safe off-field landings. Investigation revealed a missing left fuel tank cap, which caused fuel starvation despite the right tank containing eight gallons.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: P50 TRACON Controller reported not noticing a departure climbing through the altitude of an arrival until the pilot reported responding to a TCAS RA.
summary: An air traffic controller in the QUARTZ Arrival Sector missed a departure climbing on the RBN SID while managing arrivals on the PINNG and HYDRR routes. The controller instructed Aircraft X to comply with the STAR after the pilot reported responding to a Resolution Advisory caused by the non-procedure-separated departure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: P80 TRACON Controller reported a recurring issue with unidentified VFR aircraft transitioning through the PDX Runway 10 final approach corridor.
summary: An air traffic controller in the north radar sector delayed responding to a VFR aircraft departing Scappoose, allowing it to enter the PDX Runway 10 approach corridor behind an arriving jet. The controller issued traffic advisories, the VFR pilot reported visual contact, and no incident occurred, though the reporter cited systemic airspace conflicts as a future risk.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the aircraft became disconnected from the tow bar during push back, and the ramp crew was deficient in communication to the crew about the urgency of the situation.
summary: During pushback, the tow bar disconnected due to improper securing by ground crew, causing the aircraft to accelerate uncontrollably while the tug driver failed to communicate or signal an emergency. The flight crew applied brakes to stop the aircraft safely, preventing potential tail strike or collision, though ground crew refused to reconnect or explain the incident.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a NMAC with a UAV on approach to PDX.
summary: The First Officer reported a blue quadcopter drone passing within approximately 100 feet of the aircraft on final approach to PDX RWY 28R at 900 feet. No evasive maneuver was required, but the incident was reported to Portland Tower after passengers confirmed the sighting.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported dealing with a fuel leak from an overwing fuel cap requiring a return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew discovered a leaking right wing fuel cap seal during preflight on an ETOPS flight, which worsened after takeoff. They returned to the departure airport, dumped 17,000 lbs of fuel to avoid an overweight landing, and landed safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported that the rescheduled departure was pushed 2 hours later than the crew desk wanted to reduce earthquake induced stress and fatigue.
summary: Pilots experienced an earthquake during a layover in ZZZZ, causing their inbound flight to divert and forcing an overnight stay at a downtown hotel. Citing fatigue and potential safety threats, they used threat management to successfully request a later departure time from Operations.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported confusion due to reports that Kingston FIR was NOTAMed closed.
summary: The IRO, Captain, and FO encountered routing confusion over Kingston airspace due to a suspended ATS service NOTAM missing from their pre-flight paperwork. After being diverted to OTAMO by Barranquilla, they received a new clearance from Kingston to AVUTI once the controller clarified the situation.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported being sprayed with hydraulic fluid in the eyes while conducting the preflight. They were transported to the hospital for treatment.
summary: During preflight inspection, a crew member entered the right wheelwell and was sprayed with leaking hydraulic fluid, causing eye burns and disorientation. The individual was treated in a bathroom for 20 minutes before being transported by ambulance to a hospital, as no eye wash station was available and medical assistance was delayed.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported they had to go-around due to traffic still on the runway.
summary: The crew executed a go-around at 100 feet on approach to ORD 27L because the preceding aircraft delayed exiting the runway. After turning right to avoid departing traffic from 28R, the crew received vectors for a visual approach and landed without incident.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported making contact with a fire truck while being guided into the gate. Damage was not immediately evident, however the wingtip scimitar was found to be damaged.
summary: During taxi to the gate, the crew stopped after a wing walker signaled a fire truck was too close, despite initial guidance to proceed. Later, operations informed the crew that the aircraft's scimitar had contacted the truck, an event the pilots were unaware of until after the incident.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported the tow bar broke during pushback resulting in a delay until the aircraft could be inspected.
summary: During pushback, the tow bar broke, causing a 30-minute delay on the taxiway. The tow bar was removed and the aircraft inspected, after which the remainder of the flight was uneventful.

synopsis: ERJ-175 Captain reported that he assumed control of the aircraft during an unstable approach, and continued the approach instead of going around.
summary: The Captain took control during a visual LOC approach to runway 27L at ORD after the First Officer failed to descend past 2,200 ft due to an FPA mode selection error. The Captain stabilized the aircraft and completed a safe landing despite being initially fast and considering a go-around.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported a NMAC with a UAV shortly after takeoff from a hospital.
summary: A helicopter crew experienced a near midair collision with a small drone during initial climb from a hospital helipad to 2200 MSL. The drone passed 25–50 feet overhead at approximately 1350 MSL, leaving no time to react due to the drone's small size, lack of lights, and absence on radar or TCAS.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported that while hand flying the departure, the autotrim system continued to pitch the aircraft nose up. The flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During departure, the pilot reported improper autotrim causing an uncommanded nose-up pitch requiring manual sidestick pressure. The crew returned for an overweight landing without declaring an emergency, logging the flight control issue and 400-pound excess weight for maintenance.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reported that the ground crew asked them to abort engine start due to an incorrect tow bar attached.
summary: During pushback of a Q400, the tug driver requested an engine start abort because the wrong, undersized plate was attached to the tug. The crew successfully executed the abort checklist, and the tug was reconfigured before the pushback was completed.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 Maintenance Technician reported the nose gear pin can mistakenly be installed into the NLG drag brace hollow bolt rendering the gear unsafe for ground testing.
summary: A mechanic reported a safety risk on a new B787 during post-delivery modification where an unmarked NLG drag brace pivot link hole could allow incorrect pin placement. This error could cause gear collapse during ground testing, potentially damaging the aircraft and injuring personnel.

synopsis: G550 flight crew reported they overshot the 5,000 restriction at STREL departing SNA citing confusion with the 'climb via' clearance.
summary: During a noise abatement climb from SNA on the FINZZ1 departure, the crew climbed above the 5000 ft STREL restriction after receiving a clearance to 8000 ft. The reporter attributed the confusion to ambiguous ATC phrasing and high workload, though no conflict occurred.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi First Officer reported the ramp area at ACK is very congested, poorly marked, and uncontrolled.
summary: The pilot reported a dangerous ground situation at Nantucket Memorial Airport (ACK) during arrival and departure phases. The FBO-controlled ramp is congested, unmarked, and lacks ground guides or taxi lines, causing aircraft to park haphazardly with minimal clearance.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: GSO TRACON Controller reported the radar scope went blank for a few seconds.
summary: An air traffic controller lost radar display for two seconds while managing four aircraft within six miles during final approach, likely due to maintenance work. The controller switched to an adjacent scope to maintain separation, though the specific cause was attributed to a "no user" error.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: PIT Tower Controller reported that an aircraft taxied on a closed taxiway where there were no closure markings.
summary: A pilot training a developmental student landed Aircraft X on runway 32 and taxied to a hangar via a closed taxiway. Airport authority vehicles questioned the movement, highlighting a recurring lack of cones, markings, or barriers to indicate the closure despite repeated requests from air traffic.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: FWA TRACON Controller reported losing radar on an aircraft when it went over the radar site.
summary: An air traffic controller lost Aircraft X on radar near the QTZ site while it flew southwest at 8,000 feet into GUS airspace. The loss was attributed to a possible automation anomaly caused by the FWA radar outage and the aircraft passing over the QTZ cone of silence.

synopsis: The Pilot of a Boeing 737 reported that passengers were boarded prior to the flight crew arriving.
summary: The Captain reported that a Gate Agent boarded 175 passengers and closed the door without pilot monitoring or aircraft power, despite Flight Attendant objections. The crew delayed departure to complete preflight duties, citing the Agent's rush and misinterpretation of new procedures as safety risks.

synopsis: A B767 Captain reported that Maintenance repaired a hydraulic leak prior to departure, during cruise the hydraulic quantity started dropping.
summary: The crew experienced hydraulic leaks and antiskid failures in flight after a pre-departure repair, compounded by SATCOM loss. They landed safely on a long dry runway using reverse thrust to minimize braking, with post-landing inspections revealing no damage.

synopsis: Ramp Controller reported requiring guidance on the B737-900 since the aircraft requires a tail stand.
summary: A ramp agent, unaware a 737-900 required a tail stand due to staffing shortages, connected a jetway that subsequently dropped six inches, causing a passenger to fall. The incident occurred without a jetway alarm, and the passenger's identity remains unknown.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to EWR in trail of a B757.
summary: The crew on approach to EWR encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 757 while cleared for ILS 4L at 3,000 ft. The turbulence caused a sudden left roll, prompting a sidestep to runway 4L where they landed safely.

synopsis: The flight crew of a Boeing 737 reported that ATC cleared them 'Direct To' a way point without further instructions or clearances after they arrived at the way point.
summary: A flight crew on radar vectors for the RNAV GPS RWY 31 approach into LGA intercepted the final approach course after being cleared direct to CHALN IAP without explicit approach clearance. The incident resulted from an ambiguous clearance and frequency congestion, leading to a conflict with another aircraft and a subsequent corrective turn by ATC.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported the aircraft's autotrim malfunctioned during departure. The crew elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an uncommanded nose-up trim issue shortly after lift-off, requiring constant forward stick pressure to maintain trajectory. They returned to ZZZ for a stable, slightly overweight landing without declaring an emergency, citing the unknown risks of autopilot engagement and a night missed approach.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported their aircraft descended below an RNAV Arrival crossing restriction when a runway change was entered in the FMC.
summary: During descent on the BLUZZ1 arrival, the crew deviated below the 14,000-foot restriction at BLUZZ to 13,200 feet after loading a new approach in the FMS. The pilot attributed the altitude loss to changing the approach near a restriction while the autopilot failed to maintain the path despite speed brake deployment.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported encountering closed taxiways at CHO that were not included in NOTAMs for their arrival time.
summary: The flight crew landed at CHO and found Taxiways G and A blocked by sandbags and lights with no valid NOTAMs at the time. Airport Police removed the barricades, allowing the aircraft to reach the terminal safely after the crew contacted Dispatch.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reported during climb they received a 'CABIN PRESS' warning.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin pressure warning at FL230 during climb, resulting in a controlled descent to 10,000 ft due to pressurization failure. They completed unpressurized flight checklists and continued normally, though passengers were not informed of the incident until ground agents inquired.

synopsis: A Navigator of a military aircraft reported that due to a miscalculation of aircraft weight, they received an excessive amount of fuel from the tanker aircraft.
summary: During aerial refueling, an augmented crew discovered an incorrect basic aircraft weight entry in the performance computer, causing them to exceed the published gross weight limit by 20,000 pounds. After consulting engineers who confirmed no structural damage occurred, the crew declined a second refueling and completed the mission with a safe fuel margin.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a gear-up landing occurred due to distractions and the lack of gear warning horn.
summary: The pilot and safety pilot in a single-engine aircraft executed a no-flap landing at ZZZ, resulting in a gear-up touchdown due to distraction, checklist failure, and a malfunctioning gear warning horn. The pilot attributed the incident to a non-sterile cockpit, disrupted habits, and an unverified mechanic adjustment that prevented the horn from sounding at the correct power setting.

synopsis: TRACON Departure Controller reported becoming overloaded when a departure deviated from course and allowed another aircraft to fly below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined departure sectors experienced a loss of separation with a B737 due to an ambiguous RNAV departure and high workload, leading to a subsequent MVA violation with Aircraft Z. The controller attributed the incident to sector combination errors, poor scan management, and a failure of the low altitude alert system.

synopsis: PCT TRACON Controller reported assigning an operational error conducting a flight break up procedure even though they were in compliance with the 7110.65.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a flight breakup for two military fighters, instructing Aircraft Y to squawk a code and maintain 3000 feet once clear of formation. The controller argued that standard procedures were followed and requested clarification on 7110.65 phraseology regarding issuing instructions through a lead aircraft.

synopsis: Harrisburg Tower Developmental Controller reported releasing an aircraft without clearance to the correct Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller training on the LRP sector released an aircraft climbing to FL30 instead of the required FL40 due to a memory lapse regarding the 36 MVA. The controller immediately corrected the clearance after noticing the error, prompting a review of SOPs for airports with MVAs above FL30.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: FTW Tower controller reported a near mid air collision in the pattern when one pilot misunderstood the clearance.
summary: During a busy Local Control handover, Aircraft X and Aircraft Y experienced a near mid-air collision while Aircraft X extended upwind and Aircraft Y turned crosswind. The reporter attributes the incident to Aircraft Y misunderstanding a "wide right 270" instruction, likely flying a heading of 270 instead of performing the maneuver.

synopsis: Baltimore Local Controller reported approving an aircraft to cross a runway after the departing aircraft. Local then cleared an additional aircraft for takeoff before the aircraft had finished crossing downfield.
summary: A Local Controller approved a runway crossing for Aircraft Y while clearing Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway 28, causing a runway incursion risk. The controller canceled the takeoff after realizing the crossing, forcing Aircraft X to stop short of Taxiway Delta due to the controller's failure to use a memory aid.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Local Controller reported an inbound aircraft still on Approach Control frequency descended through the altitude of a VFR departure.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a traffic alert and right turn to departing Aircraft X at 2,000 feet to avoid descending VFR Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the conflict to Aircraft Y descending into the VFR traffic and recommended restricting descents until passing lower VFR aircraft.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: S46 TRACON Controller reported canceling a Visual Approach clearance to avoid VFR traffic that was not in communication with ATC.
summary: An air traffic controller, preoccupied with a non-responsive VFR aircraft, delayed issuing traffic to Aircraft X on a visual approach regarding a crossing VFR target at 1800 feet. The controller issued a climb and re-cleared the approach after Aircraft X likely responded to a TCAS resolution advisory, landing safely despite the controller's concern over unmonitored VFR traffic in the corridor.

synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft was late in reporting position and could not be contacted. The aircraft was eventually contacted and confirmed to be at a lower altitude due to an engine failure.
summary: An air traffic controller lost contact with Aircraft X, an HF-equipped flight descending to FL200 due to an engine failure, after it missed a position report upon entering the FIR. Oceanic control confirmed the aircraft's status and priority handling request, allowing it to continue to its destination.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light Transport flight crew reported a track deviation on the Cathedral 1 departure from KPSP attributed to fatigue and FMS departure confusion.
summary: The pilot flying, suffering from fatigue after a long international flight, incorrectly programmed a non-coded departure into the FMS, missing a required tear-drop maneuver to the EMRUD fix. This navigation error caused a deviation from the CATHEDRAL 1 departure, requiring ATC to issue a corrective left turn, though no traffic or terrain conflict occurred.

synopsis: B767 Check Airman reported an incorrect part installed on an emergency enter/exit window.
summary: A first officer discovered an incorrect retainer clip installed on the emergency exit window of a 767 freighter during preflight inspection. This error could lock out first responders, and the pilot suspects a fleet-wide issue with installing correct parts on this safety-sensitive system.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported that the Engine Alert Display showed several failures and the stick shaker remained on continuously.
summary: Pilots experienced multiple flight control and air data failures after passing FL190 due to a missing Captain's AOA vane. They executed the Airspeed Unreliable checklist, descended to FL270 to exit RVSM airspace, and completed an uneventful visual landing using backup pitch and power settings.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that while ATC asked them to descend and maintain altitude, TCAS told them to 'CLIMB' for traffic. TCAS and ATC were in disagreement.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer experienced a TCAS Resolution Advisory shortly after departure while climbing to 17,000 feet, conflicting with an ATC instruction to maintain 8,000 feet. The crew prioritized the TCAS RA over ATC clearance, avoiding a collision with traffic that passed 300 feet below them despite ATC reporting the other aircraft at 9,000 feet.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported being unable to obtain information for a diversion due to not having an ACARS unit for each pilot.
summary: Two pilots enroute faced a safety issue when a single ACARS unit prevented simultaneous access for dispatch coordination and weather data during a passenger medical event. This equipment limitation caused a delay in obtaining diversion information, though the flight continued to the destination without incident.

synopsis: Boeing 777 Captain reported communication problems and difficulty in understanding the foreign Controller while receiving a re-route.
summary: The crew in ZZZZ airspace deviated for thunderstorms but struggled to understand a foreign controller's fast, unclear reroute instructions on VHF and HF. They resolved the issue by using Satcom to relay dispatch messages and CPDLC queries, eventually receiving the new routing and assisting a following flight with the same communication difficulties.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an APU fire warning during deplaning.
summary: During deplaning, the APU faulted and triggered a fire warning, prompting the crew to discharge the extinguisher and evacuate passengers. The crew contacted ATC for fire equipment after the fire handle was pulled and the warning light remained illuminated.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported he was concerned that their Data Link departure change message does not have the same format as the predeparture clearance message.
summary: The pilot reported a safety compromise during departure when the Data Link Communication (DLC) differed from the filed and uploaded flight plans. The issue was caused by the DLC format not matching the Pre-Departure Clearance (PDC) and the inability to print the DLC.

synopsis: CL-300 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing multiple generator anomalies.
summary: During climb through FL260, the right generator tripped twice, and a subsequent APU start attempt failed when the left generator also tripped, causing an ESSENTIAL POWER ONLY situation. Resetting both generators per the red QRH restored the right generator, but the left generator remained offline.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported that during descent the aircraft would not respond to automated inputs to stay on profile.
summary: During arrival descent, the crew encountered late ATC clearances and VNAV anomalies where the aircraft remained high on profile despite correct Flight Mode Annunciators. The First Officer used speed brakes and switched to Flight Level Change with autothrottles off to manage advancing throttles and meet restrictions.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported recovering from an unusual attitude at 8,000 FT that resulted from a severe downdraft associated with convective activity.
summary: The crew encountered an unforecast thunderstorm downdraft below 10,000 feet while descending for an unexpected ILS 9 approach, causing the autopilot to fail and the aircraft to pitch down rapidly. The Captain recovered the unusual attitude and used speed brakes to manage airspeed exceeding 290 knots before resuming the arrival.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported that he descended below the Decision Altitude in IMC due to improper instrument equipment setup procedures.
summary: A pilot flying an ILS 17L approach at COS in IMC descended to 120 AGL due to suspected GNS 430 setup errors, likely failing to activate the ILS frequency or switch to VLOC mode. The incident resulted from not cross-checking navigation displays or verifying altitude against fixes, with no low altitude alerts received.

synopsis: RV-8 pilot reported a loss of control during taxi due to an unexpected jet blast encounter.
summary: While taxiing on Taxiway K after landing, the aircraft veered right and lifted its tail due to full-power jet blast from a twin-engine jet on the adjacent ramp. The pilot regained control using differential braking, narrowly avoiding departure from the taxiway.

synopsis: PA-28 Pilot on an IFR flight plan reported being issued opposite direction traffic in IMC, but the Controller took no action to separate the traffic.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight at 10,000 ft in IMC conditions reported a near-miss with a descending TBM after the controller failed to issue evasive instructions. The pilot executed a 45-degree turn to avoid a collision within 700 ft, attributing the incident to the controller's inaction despite both aircraft being unable to see each other.

aircraft: Gulfstream Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Gulfstream Captain reported they passed the Runway 28L hold short line on Taxiway A1 at HWD.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently crossed the hold short line for Runway 28L on taxiway A1 at HWD due to faded markings, an unusual location before the run-up area, sun glare, and distraction from nearby aircraft. The First Officer noticed the line but failed to call it out, prompting the crew to conduct additional CRM and SOP training.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a Near Mid Air Collision on downwind with an opposite direction SR22.
summary: The reporter, Number 3 in downwind, executed an abrupt left maneuver to avoid a head-on collision with a Cirrus SR22 flying the wrong downwind direction at the same altitude. The reporter stated the Cirrus pilot took no action and later blamed a student pilot on final for interrupting his IFR approach.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Thrush S2R pilot reported overflying a city at low altitude after becoming caught beneath an overcast layer.
summary: A pilot conducting crop dusting in VFR conditions encountered sudden IMC with less than 1 mile visibility and a 500 ft ceiling. The pilot maintained 100 ft AGL to follow a GPS track back to the departure airport, noting the forecast did not predict such conditions.

synopsis: RV12 pilot reported that after landing on Runway 32 at GAI, the taxiways were not available due to construction. He was forced to taxi onto the grass due to an aircraft on short final.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 32 had to taxi back due to closed exits, forcing a pull-off into grass to avoid a conflict with a following aircraft that executed a go-around. The reporter attributes the incident to poor construction planning that left no runway exits available, increasing collision risk.

synopsis: DA-40 instructor pilot reported a runway excursion due to a student's foot getting jammed on the rudder pedal.
summary: During a student pilot's third landing in a Diamond DA20, the aircraft veered left and exited the runway because the student's large foot became trapped between the instrument panel and the rudder pedal. This jammed the pedals, preventing proper braking and steering control until the instructor cut the engine and the plane stopped on the grass.

synopsis: A commercial UAV operator reported that a fixed wing aircraft descended and circled near their drone, interrupting a photo shoot.
summary: A UAS pilot conducting a photo mission below 200 feet encountered a manned aircraft that approached from the sun and circled the drone. The pilot suspected the aircraft was investigating the UAS's activity, which hindered operations, though no collision occurred as the aircraft departed quickly.

synopsis: A Tower Ground Controller and flight crew reported an aircraft missed a turn while taxiing and entered the runway approach safety area with an arriving aircraft on short final.
summary: A Ground Control controller managing heavy traffic with a disabled runway issued taxi instructions to Air Carrier A but failed to notice the aircraft missed a turn and crossed the runway approach safety area. The controller attributed the missed incursion to high workload caused by correcting multiple flight strip errors resulting from similar airline call signs.

synopsis: TPA TRACON Controller reported that an underlying tower did not protect for a point out and an airborne conflict occurred due to a release.
summary: The controller kept a PA28 VFR while vectoring it into Bravo airspace after a point-out to PIE Tower. PIE Tower subsequently launched an IFR Learjet on a conflicting heading, resulting in 2.1 miles separation because the tower failed to protect the point-out.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Center controller reported the vector for sequencing was insufficient and resulted in less than required separation.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between a BFL departure and an arrival at 13,000 feet due to an incorrect altitude clearance and premature vectoring. The controller attributed the error to increased sector complexity from new descent procedures, difficulty locating fixes, and URET display limitations.

synopsis: Boeing 737 Captain reported receiving a 'Terrain Caution' during initial approach.
summary: The pilot received a Terrain Caution at night during a visual approach while in Level Change and HDG Select modes. The alert was attributed to the descent rate, prompting a manual flight path adjustment to re-establish lateral and vertical paths before continuing the approach.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported complying with a RA to avoid a collision during a turn to base.
summary: The crew executed a Resolution Advisory during a right turn to base for runway 4R after the controller directed them into traffic they could not see. The pilot attributed the conflict to the controller turning the aircraft directly into the other traffic, resulting in a close call estimated near 500 feet.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported they were unnecessarily vectored off course and assigned a slow speed to allow other traffic to pass them.
summary: The flight crew reported that Minneapolis Center instructed a speed reduction to Mach .74 and a vector to sequence behind an aircraft at 38,000 feet, causing an 800-pound fuel overburn. The pilot believes this unnecessary maneuver compromised safety and was performed to accommodate another airline, noting a hostile controller response when questioned.

synopsis: Dash 8 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing #2 engine fire and subsequent shutdown in flight.
summary: The crew experienced a #2 engine oil pressure loss and fire at 9,000 feet, extinguishing it with two bottles and diverting safely. Post-flight inspection revealed heat damage and oil leakage, suggesting a ruptured oil line near a hot component as the probable cause.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light Jet Captain reported a GPWS Terrain warning after descending to a traffic pattern altitude based upon a mistaken airport elevation.
summary: The pilot descended below Traffic Pattern Altitude while on a visual approach to Runway 7 at CEU due to misreading the chart and calculating an incorrect altitude. This error triggered a GPWS warning, prompting a manual climb before the crew continued the approach without executing an escape maneuver.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot reported that they were unable to land on a highway intersection due to a tailwind and irregular landing zone.
summary: A helicopter pilot attempted a mountain landing without a wind check, encountering a tailwind that caused low rotor RPM and loss of tail rotor authority. The pilot aborted the approach, turned 180 degrees to regain control, and landed at an alternate site after the crew identified procedural failures and communication gaps.

synopsis: Widebody First Officer reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning when they flew an incorrect track departing VHHH.
summary: The First Officer reported that a late clearance change and poor flight deck communication led to the accidental deletion of the PORPA waypoint from the FMC. This caused a course deviation toward terrain shortly after takeoff, triggering a Ground Proximity Warning that required immediate manual correction.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported continuing to destination in VFR conditions after the main landing gear failed to retract after takeoff.
summary: The pilot flying and First Officer on a CRJ-200 experienced a landing gear malfunction after takeoff, resulting in a 'Gear Disagree' warning and main gear remaining down. They continued the flight at 200 KIAS with gear extended, landing safely without further incident.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 pilot reported that due to severe weather conditions he inadvertently flew into a TFR.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 10 encountered severe turbulence causing significant bank, yaw, and altitude loss while attempting to skirt a TFR. The pilot subsequently lost situational awareness and inadvertently entered the TFR due to not actively monitoring ForeFlight on an iPhone.

synopsis: Air Ambulance pilot reported experiencing a near mid-air collision with an opposite direction aircraft while setting up for landing at a hospital. Both aircraft took evasive action by banking right.
summary: An EC135 air ambulance descending for a hospital landing encountered a head-on conflict with an unannounced R44 in Class G airspace. The EC135 pilot executed a firm right turn and climb to avoid the collision after visually spotting the R44, which lacked a transponder and did not monitor CTAF.

synopsis: C177 pilot reported a NMAC with a turboprop aircraft in the vicinity of THA airport.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision at 5,500 feet with an aircraft turning north while the other pilot was not on the ATC frequency. The reporter executed an immediate descent and turn, passing 250 feet below the other aircraft, and attributed the incident to the other pilot's lack of radio contact and nonchalant attitude.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported they allowed an aircraft to depart a different runway than what was coordinated with the TRACON.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared an aircraft for takeoff in the opposite direction of the advertised runway due to expectation bias, calm winds, and a lack of visible runway indicators. The controller attributed the error to fatigue and poor visibility of the Information Display System-4, resolving to write pertinent data on flight strips to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew and TRACON Controller reported a NMAC with a non-transponder-equipped glider at 7000 FT on the arrival into ORD.
summary: During the FYTTE arrival into ORD at 7,000 feet, the crew executed evasive action to avoid a glider that appeared without TCAS alerts. The maneuver caused a brief stick shaker activation and a 400-foot altitude deviation before the aircraft returned to the assigned flight path and landed safely.

synopsis: Ground personnel reported of an air hose that came loose from an aircraft due to jet exhaust from another aircraft. The air hose wrapped around his ankle and pulled him down.
summary: A ground handler connecting an air hose to Aircraft X was pulled under the aircraft when a nearby 777-300 jet blast wrapped the hose around the handler's ankle. The handler escaped the hose after the 777-300 turned toward a parallel taxiway and jet blasted the gate area.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported executing a go-around at 200 AGL after encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B737 landing at STL.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B737 at 200 feet, causing aircraft roll and buffeting. The First Officer initiated a go-around due to an unstable approach, attributing the event to insufficient ATC spacing for wake dissipation.

synopsis: Embraer 505 Captain reported an in-flight failure of the integrated flight instrument system.
summary: During cruise, a GEA 1 failure caused multiple system outages including auto pressurization and left engine instruments. The pilot reported that the QRH lacked specific guidance, the flight training company provided no documentation, and simulator training did not accurately replicate the real-world failure scope.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported she wanted to reseat a passenger who was using a cane from the emergency exit row, but was overruled by customer service.
summary: A Flight Attendant reported that a limping passenger using a cane was allowed to remain in an emergency exit row despite failing to meet criteria. Customer service agents overrode crew safety concerns due to discrimination fears, withholding the passenger's admitted knee injury from the flight crew.

synopsis: A B737-900 Flight Attendant reported that the flight attendants experienced headaches and became cognitively foggy and fuzzy during flight. Shortly after the flight landed, reportedly, they were all administered oxygen and all exhibited elevated carbon monoxide levels in their blood.
summary: During the descent phase, flight attendants and a reporter experienced Carbon Monoxide poisoning symptoms, including headaches and cognitive fog, likely caused by a full trash cart in the galley. The crew requested an expedited landing, and all three were treated in the ER with oxygen after elevated CO levels were confirmed.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate aircraft flight crew reported lining up and beginning their takeoff roll on the right edge of the runway. They quickly realized their error, corrected to centerline, and continued the takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer misaligned with the right edge of Runway 1R at intersection Bravo due to missing lead-in lights and non-functioning centerline lights. They struck edge lights during the takeoff roll, corrected to the centerline, and completed the flight without incident or damage.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 Pilot reported a NMAC after takeoff while another aircraft was on final causing the other aircraft to go-around.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot back-taxied for departure on Runway 14 while a Cirrus pilot was on final approach during taxiway construction. The Cirrus pilot executed a go-around to the right after the Cessna began its takeoff roll, prompting the Cessna to side-step left to avoid conflict before both aircraft safely separated.

synopsis: BE20 Pilot reported wing damage after encountering a wind shear during the landing flare.
summary: The pilot experienced an abrupt drop and right roll during the flare on Runway 14 due to an extreme wind shear burst. This resulted in wing damage to the last 18 inches and tip, with ailerons found rough after landing.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported stopping just past the hold short lines when an aircraft was observed on short final.
summary: A pilot and student stopped on Runway XXL after a Piper Warrior on final approach was obscured by their wing. The student applied brakes just short of the pavement, preventing a runway incursion as the Warrior landed at 50 feet.

synopsis: Cessna 400 pilot reported entering Class A airspace without an IFR clearance then IFR conditions when issued a descent.
summary: The pilot, delivering a plane in mountainous terrain, entered clouds and icing after an aggressive ATC descent order, leading to a wrong frequency error and unauthorized descent. The pilot attributed the incident to poor judgment, hypoxia, and lack of instrument training, resolving to complete formal instrument certification.

synopsis: AUS Approach Controller reported an airborne conflict due to a VFR aircraft in the path of an IFR arrival on a descend via clearance.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a 500-foot vertical and 1.8-mile horizontal separation loss between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during descent on Radar East. The controller attributed the incident to GRK Approach handing off an overflight through an arrival drop box coinciding with the STAR, noting the Collision Alert failed to trigger.

synopsis: Center Controller reported being unable to contact a PA23 aircraft which flew below the MEA.
summary: A NORDO PA23 entered a 9000-foot MEA while level at 8000 feet despite the controller's blind transmissions and relay attempts. The reporter attributes the incident to the pilots' failure to monitor guard or contact ATC for 100 miles.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air Taxi pilot reported that after overshooting the LAN Runway 10R LOC, lined up for the wrong airport.
summary: The pilot reported a pilot deviation during an ILS 10R approach at LAN caused by a tight ATC vector, a temporary NAV flag, and misidentifying a nearby runway. The controller admitted this error occurs frequently, prompting the pilot to recommend procedure revisions and better pilot briefings regarding the adjacent airport.

synopsis: Cessna 172 flight instructor reported a near mid air collision with an ultralight aircraft.
summary: During a cross-country cruise at 2,500 feet MSL, a Cessna 172 instructor and student encountered an ultralight aircraft due to the instructor's distraction copying ATIS and potential visual obstructions. The instructor took control to pull up, achieving 150 feet of separation, while noting that sun glare and scanning techniques contributed to the late detection.

synopsis: A BE20 pilot reported that flight following advised him of an approaching aircraft so they took evasive action to avoid a mid-air collision.
summary: Aircraft X crew encountered a potential collision with Aircraft Y while flying a fire mission at 11,500 MSL outside a TFR. The pilot delayed evasive action to allow the air attack to hail the other aircraft and due to right-of-way rules, eventually climbing left after ATC advised the traffic was not in sight.

synopsis: A11 TRACON Controller reported losing communication with an aircraft which descended below the MVA before climbing and reestablishing communications. Later the aircraft requested to join up with a flight of aircraft and the Controller reported they (ATC) did not know the procedure for a flight join up.
summary: An air traffic controller issued low altitude alerts to Aircraft X after it descended below expected arrival altitudes due to a pilot error and missing map data. The controller later issued an incorrect altitude clearance and mishandled a fighter join-up due to stress, lack of training, and staffing shortages, though the aircraft eventually landed safely.

synopsis: ONT Tower Controller reported of an unsafe opposite direction operation.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers reported a communication failure regarding contra flow operations at ONT, where the departing crew failed to notify the SCT sector before shift change. Although Aircraft X departed Runway 8R safely with no loss of separation from arriving Aircraft Y, the incident highlighted the need to adjust contra flow timing and shift handover procedures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: ZSE Center Controller reported they allowed an aircraft to fly below the minimum IFR altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller misinterpreted a relief briefing, believing an aircraft was on an airway with 8,000-foot GPS altitudes instead of a point-to-point route. The controller subsequently climbed the aircraft from 8,000 to 9,000 feet after realizing it was below the 9,000-foot Minimum IFR Altitude.

synopsis: JCF TRACON Controller reported issues with a drone pilot and the possibility of flying a clearance that was supposed to be flown later.
summary: An air traffic controller issued Aircraft X an IFR clearance to BTY244044, but the pilot inadvertently followed a later filed flight plan, causing the aircraft to exit R-2508 airspace at FL500+. The controller issued boundary alerts and instructed an immediate south turn, which the pilot complied with after confirming the correct clearance.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of an MD80 on approach to ATL.
summary: The pilot reported experiencing wake turbulence while following an MD-80 on a visual approach at ATL, recovering and landing safely. Although the crew did not report the event due to busy radios, the pilot noted that reporting is required at RECAT airports and recommended increased spacing.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported managing a defective fire detection system on one engine after takeoff and the subsequent problems that occurred after the divert.
summary: The crew diverted from ZZZZ to ZZZZ2 due to intermittent left engine fire detection failures, but Dispatch refused release citing a NOTAM requiring an emergency declaration. The aircraft returned to ZZZZ, where lack of coordination with ground operations caused a duty day expiration and flight cancellation.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported a loss of cabin pressure due to a PACK 2 failure with PACK 1 on MEL.
summary: The crew experienced a PACK 2 overload at FL250 while PACK 1 was on MEL, causing rapid cabin pressurization. They requested priority descent to 10,000 ft, diverted to ZZZ, and landed safely.

synopsis: BE99 pilot reported losing the right engine shortly after takeoff resulting in a return to airport of departure. Upon landing the aircraft slid off the end of the runway.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine fire and oil pressure loss shortly after takeoff in rain, forcing a single-engine return. Due to low visibility and high approach, the aircraft overshot the runway, slid off the end into a field, and required an emergency evacuation.

synopsis: BE40 flight crew reported a NMAC while on short final to HND with an aircraft that turned base too early.
summary: The flight crew flying a visual approach to Henderson Runway 35L executed a go-around after an Aztec deviated from ATC instructions by turning into their path. The Aztec had been cleared for a left downwind on parallel Runway 35R but turned toward the crew's aircraft, prompting the crew to stop descent and reenter the traffic pattern.

synopsis: BE35 pilot on landing roll reported a ground conflict with opposite direction traffic on the takeoff roll at MLE.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 12 at MLE encountered an aircraft taking off from the opposite end at 500 feet. Despite radio warnings and light flashes, the other pilot did not respond until slowing down just before the landing aircraft exited, causing a near collision due to the takeoff pilot's failure to visually check the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they received an IFR departure which they thought was VFR which flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An Arrival Sector controller mistakenly believed an IFR aircraft departing Runway 10L was VFR due to expectation bias and a missing departure strip caused by a shared printer. The aircraft entered a 6,500-foot MVA at 4,700 feet without triggering a low altitude alert before being cleared on course.

synopsis: FAR Local Controller reported an operation involving a military UAV that was being conducted not in accordance with the LOA.
summary: An air traffic controller trainee managed UAVs and other traffic in the local pattern, but a conflict arose when the trainee allowed a UAV to turn base early due to unknown engine failure restrictions over populated areas. This forced a go-around that created a potential mid-air collision with another aircraft, highlighting the need for updated procedures regarding UAV limitations and lost-link behaviors.

synopsis: ANC Tower Controllers reported the Controller in Charge ordered them to allow aircraft to takeoff and land on a the LHD gravel runway that had a moose observed near it.
summary: The Controller in Charge (CIC) overruled the LHD controller's decision to divert two arrivals to ANC due to a moose on the LHD runway, insisting they land despite the hazard. The LHD controller refused, and both aircraft safely landed at ANC, though the reporter cited the CIC's poor supervisory judgment and contempt for staff as a safety concern.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A Center Controller reported their sectors are being overloaded with complex traffic and Traffic Management Units are not doing anything to affect the flow.
summary: An air traffic controller reported unsafe conditions during severe weather when the Traffic Management Unit failed to prevent sector overloads. The controller stated that excessive aircraft concentrations and a lack of information distribution to pilots created an impossible workload that threatened safety.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Center Oceanic Controller reported proper procedures and equipment requirements were not implemented during a planned radar and radio outage period.
summary: Air traffic controllers in Sectors 62, 63, and 58 faced a 10-minute radar and frequency outage caused by satellite alignment issues during high traffic volume. Although separation was maintained after a controller warned of a conflict at 37,000 feet, the incident resulted from SOP violations, lack of strip coordination, and insufficient backup equipment.

synopsis: A Departure Controller reported an aircraft departed on the wrong heading and was below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller in departure sectors observed a Cirrus turning east toward terrain after the pilot failed to read back a tower heading. The controller issued low altitude alerts and additional turns to ensure terrain clearance, noting the pilot eventually confirmed visual contact with the ground.

synopsis: A Ground Controller observed the Local Controller clear aircraft for intersection takeoffs with less than required Wake Turbulence separation.
summary: A Ground Controller reported that Local Controllers repeatedly cleared small aircraft for intersection takeoffs without required 3-minute wake turbulence holds after larger aircraft departed from points 1,200 feet further down the runway. The reporter attributes this to controllers ignoring FAAH 7110.65 rules to prioritize efficiency, despite the regulation mandating holds based on the preceding aircraft's departure point.

synopsis: Boeing 737 flight crew reported a significant airframe vibration right after takeoff. Suspecting a blown tire, the crew reduced the gross weight of the aircraft and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced severe vibration on takeoff and landing caused by a shredded number 2 main landing gear tire. After burning fuel and preparing for an emergency landing, the aircraft stopped safely with no fire or significant damage and was towed to the gate.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported receiving conflicting clearances from ATC, which resulted in confliction with other departing traffic.
summary: The pilot reported a potential conflict with an Embraer during climb after TCAS was MELed and a "Climb Via" clearance was active. The crew maintained the SID despite Tower instructions to avoid turning inside the traffic, noting that ATC later claimed the paths were diverging while the aircraft were actually converging.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported executing a go-around after receiving a GPWS terrain warning on a visual approach to MFR.
summary: The crew accepted a visual approach to MFR at night in hilly terrain, descended below the 5300 ft minimum safe altitude, and triggered terrain warnings. They executed a go-around, requested vectors for an ILS approach, and landed safely after realizing ATC did not intervene during their low descent.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV shortly after takeoff from PHL.
summary: The pilot reported a drone encounter during the departure climb on runway 27L after initially mistaking it for a bird. The crew maintained a safe distance of approximately 200 feet from the black drone at 600 feet AGL and notified ATC, allowing the flight to continue without incident.

synopsis: CL350 Captain reported rejecting the takeoff after experiencing directional control issues following a main gear tire failure.
summary: Pilots aborted a CL-350 takeoff due to sudden yaw and left wing drop caused by a suspected brake or tire malfunction. Post-flight inspection revealed an overheated left gear assembly and a deflated, detached #2 tire, leading to a return to the ramp.

synopsis: EMB 505 flight crew reported an overheat warning for both ducts without a published procedure in the QRH to addressed the situation.
summary: The crew experienced dual air conditioning duct overtemperature warnings while leveling at FL360, causing extreme cockpit heat. They suspected a Ram Air Mixing Valve error, landed safely, and extinguished the warnings by closing bleed valves during descent.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported the company Dispatcher planned the flight through an area of potential volcanic ash.
summary: The crew identified active volcanic ash NOTAMs on their planned route, but Dispatch initially denied the risk. After the Captain and Chief Pilot rejected the original flight plan, the aircraft was re-routed north of the activity, departing with only moderate turbulence.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an NMAC with a VFR aircraft in the vicinity of PSP.
summary: The crew received a CLIMB RA while approaching CEKMA on the RNAV Visual 31L due to a VFR aircraft spiraling below. The VFR pilot was unaware of proximity to PSP airport, but the aircraft passed 300 feet below after ATC ordered a heading change.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported descending below charted altitude on approach to BTV citing fatigue as a contributing factor.
summary: The fatigued pilot descended below the 5400-foot crossing restriction at NIDUQ while on vectors to the RNAV GPS Z Rwy 33 approach at BTV. The crew received a visual clearance after the violation was noted and landed safely, attributing the error to fatigue and selecting vectors instead of an Initial Approach Fix.

synopsis: A319 pilot reported that they did not hold short of Taxiway F while taxiing to Runway 25R at LAX.
summary: The pilot reported a taxi clearance discrepancy at LAX while taxiing to Runway 25R, where the tower controller stated they were not cleared to cross Taxiway Foxtrot. The flight continued normally, though the pilot noted the chart's description location was unclear for unfamiliar operators.

synopsis: CE560XL Captain reported executing a go-around when the approach became unstabilized following confusion in the cockpit as to the ATC clearance.
summary: During an ILS approach into BJC in IMC, the flight crew missed ATC vectors due to a non-essential anti-ice discussion that violated sterile cockpit procedures. This communication breakdown caused an unstable approach and a missed localizer, requiring ATC to cancel the clearance and re-vector the aircraft for a safe landing.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported landing with partial trailing edge flaps following a TE FLAP DISAGREE message.
summary: The flight crew encountered a TE FLAP DISAGREE while vectored for the ILS, leading to a failed alternate flap extension and an emergency declaration. The Captain landed safely with full reverse thrust, and brake temperatures remained below 4 during taxi.

synopsis: CL-300 flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert while distracted by a gear warning horn associated with an air-ground disagreement.
summary: The flight crew descended below 6000 ft on the RNAV 29 approach when a false radio altimeter reading triggered a gear warning. They continued the approach despite being outside radar coverage and too low, later realizing they should have leveled off to troubleshoot the issue.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported climbing in response to a GPWS terrain warning on a night visual approach to SJC.
summary: During a visual approach to SJC 30L, the crew received GPWS terrain advisories at 4000 and 3800 ft MSL after the Captain selected FLCH descent mode.
