The Captain disconnected the autopilot to climb to 4100 ft, attributing the event to the descent rate, while the PM noted a failure to verify the Captain's terrain awareness.

synopsis: Captain of a Part 121 turbojet reported difficulties interfacing via CPDLC with ATC.
summary: While operating on NAT X, the flight crew received three CPDLC messages from Reykjavik Centre within one minute, but the FMC prompt displayed only two. The crew discovered the missed squawk instruction only after manually checking the ATC log page, highlighting a potential safety failure in the message display system.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported two flight attendants were injured by an abrupt stop to avoid a runway incursion.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a near runway incursion while taxiing a jet, stopping just after the hold short bar of closed Runway 4R due to the Captain misidentifying a taxiway. The sudden stop injured two flight attendants, and the Captain attributed the event to his own navigation error and delayed reaction to the First Officer's warning.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after the sole remaining air conditioning/pressurization pack failed in flight.
summary: The crew of an aircraft with two existing MELs experienced a Bleed 2 Overpressure during initial climb, causing loss of Pack 2 and pressurization. After failed QRH crossbleed attempts, the crew diverted to the nearest suitable airport due to the aircraft's history of this fault.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported encountered severe turbulence causing the airspeed to fluctuate below the desired airspeed.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate to severe turbulence while en route at FL 380 managing an RTA speed of 0.778M following a Generator 2 OFF alert. Turbulence caused airspeed to drop 5 knots below the bottom limit, requiring max thrust to recover and a heading change to avoid weather.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported observing a UAV during climbout from PHL.
summary: During climb out from Philadelphia International through 4,500 feet, the pilot observed a large, four-bladed unmanned aerial vehicle several hundred feet below and west of the aircraft. No evasive action was required, and the pilot later reported the sighting to authorities, estimating the drone was stationary and possibly 500 feet below.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported observing Ramp personnel towing an aircraft without a brake rider and no ability to address tractor problems.
summary: Ramp personnel towing an aircraft to the maintenance base ignored Tower instructions to hold due to tug trouble, creating a risk of the unchalked aircraft rolling back and striking the reporter's aircraft. The tow continued after the tug was deemed operational, though the reporter noted the danger of moving aircraft without brake riders or chocks.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA flight instructor reported becoming distracted with a student pilot, missed a two mile check in report and landed without a clearance.
summary: A flight instructor and student landed a private aircraft without clearance at night after the instructor missed a 2-mile report while managing an unprepared student. The instructor accepted responsibility for the missed call and landing without clearance but also criticized the tower controller for failing to monitor their position in clear VFR conditions.

synopsis: GA pilot reported becoming disoriented and unable to locate the departure airport, concerned about fuel exhaustion, landed unannounced at a nearby Class D airport.
summary: A solo pilot became lost during a training flight, drifted south, and entered Class Delta airspace without charts or radio frequencies. Fearing fuel starvation, the pilot landed at ZZZ Airport without tower clearance, later apologizing and receiving permission to taxi and depart after contacting the tower by phone.

synopsis: A contracted drone operator reported he was alerted by the drone's sensors that he may have penetrated Class E airspace. He immediately terminated his video photography and exited the area.
summary: A drone operator flying a DJI Mavic Pro near Kearney Regional Airport inadvertently entered Class E airspace due to map resolution limitations. The operator landed the drone safely at 60 feet AGL, reporting no risk of collision or impact on other aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Designated Pilot Examiner reported that while on final approach to a non-towered airport, another aircraft lined up on the departure end of the runway.
summary: During an FAA instrument check ride GPS 17 approach, the applicant landed on Runway 17 while a large aircraft entered Runway 35. The instructor radioed the intruder to exit immediately, and the aircraft returned behind the hold short line, allowing the landing to complete without incident.

synopsis: C170 pilot reported a runway excursion during landing due to gusty winds.
summary: The pilot of a C170 with recurring electrical issues aborted a landing on Runway XXR due to a sudden crosswind gust, then departed the runway into grass after a second approach due to a locked tail wheel and insufficient rudder authority. The aircraft came to rest safely with no injuries or damage, classified as a non-incident.

synopsis: Pilot instructor of privately owned military type trainer reported a near miss with another military aircraft.
summary: During takeoff roll on Runway 14, the pilot of military trainer Aircraft X observed military Aircraft Y at 300 feet AGL without a CTAF position report. The pilot executed an evasive maneuver behind Aircraft Y to avoid wake turbulence and obstructions, then resumed navigation and notified Eglin Approach of the conflict.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: TOA Tower Controller and GA pilot reported an aircraft possibly landed with an opposite direction traffic rolling on the runway.
summary: A pilot and a newly certified controller experienced a runway change and radio congestion, leading to a missed go-around instruction and a perceived pilot deviation. The pilot landed safely after the preceding aircraft cleared, attributing the misunderstanding to high workload and differing visual perspectives.

synopsis: ZUA Center Controller reported controllers use incorrect procedures to determine IFR cancellations of aircraft flying into uncontrolled airports.
summary: Guam ARTCC controllers incorrectly instructed Aircraft X to cancel IFR with GSN ATCT while on a visual approach to uncontrolled TNI. This unofficial practice caused a 30-minute delay in closing the flight plan due to unverified ground reports and a lack of training for uncontrolled airport operations.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the loss of multiple hydraulic systems.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced sequential failures of the B and A system engine hydraulic pumps, resulting in total loss of System B and reduced System A quantity. Following QRH procedures and early flap/gear extension, the aircraft landed safely on Runway XX using only the A system electric pump.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported FMC route data was missing two fixes on their assigned departure SKYL8 from OAK.
summary: The flight crew reported missing PORTE and OSI fixes on the LEGS page for the SKYLINE 7 Departure from Runway 30, despite ATC confirming they should be included. The crew manually entered the fixes and proceeded without issue, suspecting an error in the database, Jeppesen plate, or ATC instructions.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported an ATC low altitude alert due to an altitude deviation on arrival into ONT. Fatigue and workload were cited as contributing factors.
summary: During a visual approach to ONT, the First Officer descended below the assigned 8000 ft without announcing the change, prompting ATC to order a climb to 7700 ft. The pilots attributed the altitude awareness breakdown to fatigue, expectation bias from repeated ATC visual approach mentions, and a failure to verify autoflight changes.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a ground conflict with a company B737 on the ramp at DEN.
summary: The pilot reported a near collision while taxiing at Denver after ramp tower failed to warn of a company B737 crossing within 100 feet behind them. The pilot had to brake hard and reverse thrust to avoid the aircraft, which was not mentioned in the initial clearance despite being a significant hazard.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the transition from the asphalt taxiway to the concrete gate at one of the companies Jetbridge pads at EWR has a very large lip to overcome.
summary: A pilot reported that a 1 to 1.5-inch pavement lip at Gate 10-7 in EWR prevented the aircraft from cresting onto concrete while taxiing with engines running. Due to the tight maneuvering area and excessive lip height, the crew could not break away and required a tug to complete parking.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported that while on final another aircraft was given takeoff clearance on the same runway, causing them to go-around.
summary: The flight crew executed a go-around after an A380 received takeoff clearance but delayed rolling, causing insufficient separation on final. During the climb, they passed 400 feet below a Cessna 172 before landing safely, attributing the incident to tight ATC intervals and the A380's runway delay.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported on descent into FSD the ZMP frequency 128.0 had a loud side-tone that was almost deafening and made communication with the Center difficult.
summary: During descent into FSD, the pilot experienced deafening audio interference on MSP Center frequency 128.0, making communications difficult and dangerous. MSP Center acknowledged the known frequency problem and instructed the pilot to file a report.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported while on a vector to ZSPD ILS 17R, the crew did not get a response from approach so they switched to the Tower frequency on the approach plate (124.35) and did not get a response either. Captain reported approach gave the crew a different Tower frequency than what was listed on the approach plate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a radio communication failure while being vectored for the ILS to runway 17R at 4,900 feet. They reestablished contact via emergency frequency 121.5 after failing to reach Approach or Tower on published frequencies, suspecting a frequency discrepancy caused the initial silence.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp employee reported that the company Hazardous Material Screener identified undeclared hazardous materials during preflight inspection.
summary: A screener discovered undeclared lithium and flammable liquids during the screening of a shipment. The narrative does not specify the aircraft, phase of flight, or further outcome.

synopsis: CRJ900 Captain reported a nose wheel steering failure shortly after takeoff.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, the aircraft experienced a Nose Wheel Steering failure while the First Officer was flying. The crew completed the QRH, notified ATC and passengers, and the First Officer executed a safe landing with no damage or injuries.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an NMAC with a light aircraft in the vicinity of BIS airport.
summary: The flight crew of a jet on final approach to Runway 13 at BIS executed a go-around after a NORDO single-engine aircraft entered controlled airspace without clearance and headed directly toward them. The pilot aggressively maneuvered to avoid a collision, lost visual contact, and subsequently landed safely.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported a Crew Chief may have falsified documents by signing off items that were not accomplished due to time pressure.
summary: A mechanic reported that the Crew Chief instructed him to defer a worn lavatory door hinge and a drain mast issue due to manpower shortages, then falsified maintenance records by signing off on these unrepaired items. The mechanic attributed the falsification to pressure from a Supervisor who threatened to ground the aircraft if the discrepancies were not resolved.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a safety of flight issue due to excessive control instructions by the Final Approach Controller.
summary: The flight crew reported that air traffic controllers repeatedly denied requests for lower altitudes and slower speeds to maintain high arrival rates, forcing the aircraft to stabilize only after permission was finally granted. The pilot stated this practice compromises safety and warned of a potential accident despite repeated reports to supervisors.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported an engine flamed out during cruise due to possible fuel issue.
summary: The First Officer observed flickering fuel flow and zero outer tank indications while flying, leading to a right engine flameout. The crew diverted and landed uneventfully after receiving ATC vectors, noting no fuel leak and that inner tanks remained functional.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an incorrectly set altimeter led to a near mid air collision.
summary: A pilot flying direct at 7,700 feet MSL experienced a near mid-air collision with a Cessna due to an incorrect barometric pressure setting of 30.18 instead of 30.11. The pilot acknowledged that failing to adjust for a weather front caused the aircraft to fly physically higher than the controller's assigned altitude.

synopsis: DV20 flight instructor reported incorrectly filing an IFR flight plan in a VFR only aircraft.
summary: A Diamond DA20 pilot filed an IFR flight plan for training in a VFR-only aircraft and encountered clouds during climb. The controller rejected the request, instructed the pilot to contact ATC post-flight, and the pilot acknowledged the error of filing IFR in a non-IFR certified aircraft.

synopsis: Piper PA-28 instructor reported they were on an extended downwind when another small airplane cut under them nearly causing a midair collision.
summary: A pilot and student in the pattern observed an aircraft pass within 100 feet below them after it entered on extended base without radio calls. The intruder landed shortly after a DC-3, which was still on the runway with approximately 2,500 feet separation, then departed west without a departure call.

synopsis: M20 pilot reported flying into IMC conditions while trying to fly beneath a low overcast layer.
summary: The pilot flew VFR into deteriorating weather near EDC, entering IMC without a clearance due to get-there-itis and delayed decision-making. After climbing to 2,800 ft to clear terrain, the pilot obtained a popup clearance and completed the RNAV 13 approach safely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Banner towing pilot reported adjusting flight course to remain clear of ambiguous ATC warning of possible TFR penetration.
summary: The pilot disputed a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) with ZZZ Tower, citing FAA rules requiring stadium seating of 30,000 or more. The pilot deviated south to comply with the controller despite GPS showing minimal TFR penetration, while the TFR's validity remains debated among the FAA, TRACON, and sports teams.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Piper J5 pilot reported losing control of the aircraft after hand propping the engine.
summary: During hand propping, the engine started and dragged the pilot around before he fell to avoid the circling aircraft. The left main landing gear ran over his shoulder, causing a dislocation, and the plane eventually stopped after striking a lift.

synopsis: C152 student pilot reported an NMAC with another small aircraft in the traffic pattern at a non-towered airport.
summary: A student and instructor practicing touch-and-go landings on Runway X encountered Aircraft Y departing southwest while climbing through the downwind leg perpendicular to their path. The aircraft passed within a few hundred feet, and subsequent attempts to contact it on CTAF were unsuccessful.

synopsis: Bonanza 35 pilot reported experiencing enroute icing and ATC transmissions that resulted in an overspeed while descending to clear the ice. A subsequent altitude excursion related to the pilot's misunderstanding of the altitude clearance.
summary: The pilot encountered unexpected icing while penetrating clouds at 11,000 feet, prompting a rapid descent to 5,000 feet to escape the weather. During the descent, the pilot oversped the aircraft due to delayed power reduction while responding to ATC queries, but recovered and landed safely after clarifying altitude clearances.

synopsis: Diamond DA40 pilot reported encountering severe turbulence while traversing a mountain pass. He and all the passengers hit their heads on the ceiling when the seatbelts became ineffective.
summary: A pilot and three passengers in a Diamond aircraft encountered severe turbulence and a violent altitude drop while passing a mountain pass, causing head strikes and broken seatbelts. The pilot attributed the injuries to ineffective seatbelt latching and modified the course to avoid mountains for the remainder of the flight.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna pilot reported he accidentally descended while trying to retrieve his chart off the aircraft floor. ATC issued an altitude alert.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 340 or 210 north of Denver Centennial encountered moderate turbulence at 8000 ft, causing a 1000 ft descent to 7000 ft while distracted by scanning for traffic and retrieving items. The controller issued an altitude alert after the deviation, prompting the pilot to correct the altitude and remain vigilant in congested airspace.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ACT TRACON Controller reported leaving their position to attend to the flight strip printer and heard the conflict alert sound at his position. When they returned, they observed one of their aircraft in close proximity to an unidentified target.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a clearance to Aircraft X climbing to 3,000 feet but missed a conflict alert with unidentified Aircraft Y while retrieving strips. Although the aircraft separated naturally, the controller failed to properly radar identify Aircraft Y or issue a "radar contact" call during the scramble to establish separation.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they had to cancel an aircraft's approach clearance and subsequently the aircraft responded to an RA for an unidentified VFR aircraft flying through the final approach course.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Aircraft X on an ILS approach canceled the clearance due to a non-compliant VFR aircraft climbing nearby. The pilot subsequently initiated an uninstructed climb, likely due to a TCAS resolution advisory, before landing safely, prompting the controller to call for mandatory VFR communication in that airspace.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported that ATC gave them descent clearance and the aircraft failed to descend using automation.
summary: The Captain and a new-hire First Officer failed to descend from FL380 to FL340 because the autopilot remained in V/S mode despite their belief it was in VNAV Path. The Captain attributed the error to task saturation caused by the First Officer's language translation delays and inadequate monitoring of the flight mode.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that new FMC software may have been responsible for the aircraft slowing excessively when ALT INT was selected to initiate a cruise descent.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the crew initiated a descent with new FMC software, but the aircraft unexpectedly decelerated to 0.63 Mach after the First Officer pressed ALT INT. The reporter suspects the software incorrectly reset the cruise altitude to the final constraint, causing an unsafe low-speed condition that required manual intervention.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a Flight Attendant was slightly injured when the Captain came to an abrupt stop to avoid a collision with a fuel truck on the ramp at SFO.
summary: During taxi to Runway 1R, a fuel truck failed to yield, causing the Captain to brake to avoid a collision. A flight attendant struck her shoulder against the galley but declined medical attention and continued the flight.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported that the aircraft descended below GS intercept altitude, EICAS message indicated a glideslope problem, the autopilot was disconnected, and a stabilized approach was completed manually. After landing, an IRS EICAS message was received.
summary: PHNL pilots experienced an autopilot disconnect and fluctuating ILS indications during an ILS 08L approach, causing an unintended descent below the glideslope to 2300-2400 feet. The crew manually leveled the aircraft, completed the landing, and attributed the event to degraded automation performance requiring enhanced monitoring.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that with the Lower Multi-Function Display Unit deferred, all engine instruments were displayed except for hydraulic quantity and pressure on the Upper Display Unit.
summary: The flight crew operated an aircraft with an MEL placard for an inoperative lower Multi Function Display Unit but discovered during cruise that hydraulic quantity and pressure indications were missing. They suspect an unaddressed system display failure or software issue, as the MEL only covered engine indications, and reported the discrepancy to maintenance upon arrival.

synopsis: MD-11 First Officer reported observing a momentary engine fire warning just prior to landing. The landing was completed normally, however during taxi the engine fire warning resumed and the engine was secured.
summary: The crew experienced a momentary fuel handle flicker at 500 AGL, followed by a Level 3 Engine 1 fire warning on the taxiway. Despite normal engine parameters and no visual fire, they discharged both fire bottles before fire trucks confirmed no fire, allowing a safe taxi to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported responding to a GPWS terrain alert on a night visual approach to MFR.
summary: During a night visual approach to MFR, the Captain descended too aggressively below published altitudes, triggering an EGPWS terrain alert near SERTE. The crew executed an escape maneuver, leveled off at 8,200 ft, and subsequently landed safely on runway 32.

synopsis: The Captain of a Bombardier CRJ reported that the Flight Management System put out erroneous information.
summary: The flight crew reported an FMS flickering issue and a subsequent failure to generate a Green Send command for passenger weights during pre-takeoff programming. Upon arrival, the FMS displayed an incorrect VRef speed of 125 knots instead of the expected 140 knots, prompting the crew to manually use the correct speed.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported that after takeoff the landing gear would not retract.
summary: The flight crew received gear disagree and nose door open warnings after takeoff, prompting a return to the departure airport. After burning fuel and declaring an emergency, they landed safely with the gear down and locked, then deferred the retraction issue to continue the revenue flight.

synopsis: CRJ flight crew reported a General Aviation aircraft turned early, resulting in a TCAS RA and subsequent go-around.
summary: The Captain hand-flew a visual approach to runway 24 when a Beechcraft, mistakenly following a Citation instead of the RJ, turned base and final on a collision course. A TCAS "Don't Descend" RA prompted a go-around, allowing the crew to return for a safe landing.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Flight Attendant and flight crew reported that pre-landing notice was not heard in the cabin and the service cart was not stowed when the landing gear was deployed.
summary: A new flight attendant in the aft cabin did not hear the landing chime or receive a phone call when gear deployed, leaving a beverage cart unsecured. The crew attributed this to a missed communication during an expedited turnaround, though the pilot maintained all checklists and SOPs were completed.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Flight Attendant reported an APU fire due to excess fuel just before pushback that resulted in all passengers exiting the aircraft.
summary: During pushback preparation, the APU failed twice, causing a total power loss and excessive fuel smoke that ground crew mistook for fire. The cabin crew evacuated all passengers, but after the captain explained the situation, most reboarded and the flight departed as scheduled.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported sighting a drone over the Griffith Park Observatory while operating at 600 AGL. The pilot altered his climb to avoid the drone.
summary: A helicopter pilot filming near Griffith Park Observatory encountered a drone operating above 500 AGL, forcing the pilot to maneuver below the observatory and abort a climb at 600 AGL. The pilot attributes the conflict to private drone operators failing to respect helicopter airspace and regulations.

synopsis: A Cessna 421 pilot reported penetrating Class B airspace due to weather and unable to maneuver within the airspace.
summary: A pilot descending VFR through Weber Canyon for OGD landing encountered turbulence that prevented descent below the cleared 7,700 feet limit. Unable to turn due to terrain, the pilot briefly penetrated the Class B airspace shelf to safely exit the canyon and was subsequently cleared for landing.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported the pilot flying the aircraft landed long and fast resulting in a excursion from the runway end and damage to the aircraft.
summary: During a BFR in a student-piloted aircraft, the pilot flew a high-speed approach in gusty winds, resulting in a long float and runway excursion into a ditch. The reporter attributed the loss of braking to a wind gust lifting the right wing and cited obstacles preventing a go-around, causing nosewheel, propeller, and wing tip damage with no injuries.

synopsis: Lancair pilot reported receiving an IFR clearance via VORs and airways when they were prepared to fly the published STAR. They were issued a VOR Approach which required a steep turn to the IAF which the pilot felt was in violation of ATC procedures.
summary: A pilot reported that SoCal Approach used outdated, verbally dictated clearances instead of published STARs, causing unnecessary workload. The controller issued an unwarned 110-degree turn contrary to FAAH 7110.65, resulting in a serious overshoot of the final approach course.

synopsis: PA34-200T pilot reported an altitude excursion in cruise when the electric trim malfunctioned.
summary: The pilot experienced an uncommanded climb and trim system failure while descending from 7100 to 7000 MSL, where electric and manual trim inputs initially failed. The issue resolved after cycling the electric trim power off, allowing manual correction, and the pilot suspected a temporary trim motor lockup.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Tower Controllers and a landing pilot reported another aircraft ignored instructions to cancel takeoff clearance and departed over the landing aircraft still on the runway.
summary: An ATC controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while Aircraft Y was still rolling out on Runway 14 at SRQ. Despite repeated cancellation instructions, Aircraft X departed and climbed over Aircraft Y, which the controller attributed to the pilot ignoring instructions or radio issues.

synopsis: P80 TRACON Controller cancelled an arrival's STAR and vectored the aircraft to avoid an unidentified VFR aircraft flying through the final approach course.
summary: An air traffic controller diverted a B737 on the STAR to avoid an unidentified VFR primary target in the approach corridor. The VFR aircraft turned toward the B737, forcing a high base leg near noise limits, though the pilot eventually spotted the traffic with no collision.

synopsis: Denver Approach Controller and four pilots reported that an aircraft went through assigned final course causing an airborne conflict with two other aircrafts.
summary: Aircraft X, cleared for an RNAV approach to Runway 35R, mistakenly entered Runway 34R into their FMC and flew a westerly heading, conflicting with Aircraft Y on final for Runway 35L. This error forced Aircraft Y to execute a rapid TCAS descent to avoid collision while controllers re-vectoring Aircraft X.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: HUF Local Controller reported an unsafe situation due to the D-Brite being expanded to 60 miles for use by the Radar Controller.
summary: An under-staffed Air Traffic Controller at Local/Ground Control lost visual contact with Aircraft Y due to an unusable D-Brite display and cloud cover. The controller subsequently transposed call signs for Aircraft X and Z, causing a delay in issuing a corrective turn and resulting in a close proximity situation between Aircraft X and Z during a go-around.

synopsis: B737 Max flight crew reported that an Auto Shutdown of the Number Two engine on engine start was probably due to the First Officer activating the Isolation switch and the Pack switch during the start.
summary: The First Officer prematurely isolated the bleed air and turned on the right pack during a Boeing MAX engine start, causing an incomplete start and auto shutdown of engine 2. The crew aborted the start, returned to the gate, and attributed the incident to rushing the unfamiliar start procedure.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported ATC repeatedly assigned instructions to incorrect aircraft due to similar call signs.
summary: SoCal ATC repeatedly confused flight XXYX with flight XXXX during the ROKKR 1 arrival, potentially issuing a 7,000 FT descent clearance intended for the other aircraft. Controllers urgently ordered XXYX to stop descending at 10,100 FT before providing vectors for traffic and resuming the approach.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported being unable to load some data into the FMC which was caused by the cruising altitude being below the minimum crossing altitude of one of the arrival fixes.
summary: The pilot reported that performance weight and balance data failed to load into the FMC because the filed cruise altitude of FL220 was below the STAR's minimum crossing restriction of FL240 at ZZZZZ. Deleting this altitude restriction allowed the data to load, revealing a system limitation where conflicting altitude restrictions prevent data loading.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the debate between safety and efficiency during international departures where speeds in the climb below 10000 feet are unrestricted.
summary: A pilot reported a potential conflict between the Flight Operations Manual and FAR 121.11 regarding high-speed climbs below 10,000 feet on a Boeing 787. The reporter argues that accelerating to cruise speeds after flap retraction increases safety risks for minimal fuel savings compared to standard 250-knot procedures.

synopsis: A regional jet flight crew and flight attendant reported a partial slide deployment due to miscommunication between flight attendants and ground personnel at a foreign airport.
summary: During post-landing shutdown, the Main Passenger door partially opened with the slide deploying because a ground employee opened it from outside while a flight attendant was disarming it inside. The crew deplaned passengers via the Forward Service door, and the aircraft was terminated for the night due to this miscommunication.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported returning to the departure airport after experiencing smoke in the cockpit probably related to failure of symbol generator #1.
summary: During an RNAV departure at 4,000 feet, the crew experienced a total loss of flight displays and autopilot, suspected to be a Symbol Generator #1 failure. An electrical burning smell and smoke subsequently filled the cockpit, prompting the crew to return to the departure airport.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported that the aircraft was shut down, on multiple occasions, prior to deplaning all the passengers.
summary: Cabin crew reported that flight deck shutdowns during passenger deplaning on 737s left them unable to use the interphone or PA, forcing reliance on a megaphone. The reporter stated this created an unsafe communication gap and a health hazard due to rapid cabin temperature rises for remaining passengers.

synopsis: Learjet 35 flight crew reported a dual tire failure during takeoff resulting in reduced braking capability during the rejected takeoff which caused the aircraft to depart the end of the runway.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 120 knots after two left-side tires blew, causing brake failure and a runway excursion into grass. A subsequent right gear fire was extinguished by the first officer, and all occupants evacuated safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Beechcraft 99 pilot reported taking off with the crew hatch not fully secured, and that the hatch subsequently departed that aircraft.
summary: The pilot departed with an unsecured crew hatch that tore open shortly after takeoff due to wind noise. The aircraft returned to the departure airport for inspection without damage, though the pilot admitted to deviating from ATC clearance before obtaining permission.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an airborne conflict with an acrobatic aircraft while on a cross country flight.
summary: A VFR Cessna 172-R pilot encountered a faster, uncommunicative aircraft conducting erratic maneuvers near ZZZ, requiring three evasive turns to avoid a collision. The reporter attributes the close calls to the other pilot's reckless flying, lack of ATC contact, and disregard for safety despite having TCAS and ADS-B.

synopsis: Glasair pilot reported an NMAC with a spinning aircraft that descended rapidly through his altitude.
summary: While cruising at 6,500 feet, the pilot observed a Turbo Porter in a fully-developed spin passing within approximately 240 feet. The reporter attributed the near-collision to the other pilot's unsafe practice of spinning to minimize descent time, which prevented effective see-and-avoid.

synopsis: A Piper Arrow pilot reported experiencing strong exhaust fumes while flying with an instructor. The flight was safely terminated, however, post flight, the pilot exhibited symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning.
summary: A student pilot and flight instructor experienced carbon monoxide poisoning during touch-and-go training when a tiny exhaust leak in the heating shroud allowed fumes into the cabin. The student required hospitalization after testing positive for 2% carbon monoxide in their blood.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 3 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: HCF TRACON controllers reported that a Special Operation aircraft was allowed to fly at an altitude below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X, on a special TMU-approved route, flew below the 12,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude despite climb instructions. The pilot refused to climb due to flight plan constraints, and the controller was advised by a supervisor not to issue a safety alert, resulting in an unsafe altitude violation.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: SAN Tower Controller reported a NORDO aircraft on the runway caused confusion in the cab and the subsequent arrival to go-around.
summary: An ATC controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while Aircraft Y was on final, but CIC distracted the controller by transmitting on the active frequency. This distraction caused a delayed response to Aircraft X's runway incursion, triggering an ASDE alarm and forcing Aircraft Y to go around without proper coordination.

synopsis: NorCal TRACON Controller reported that an aircraft descended below assigned altitude causing a loss of separation with a heavy aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft Y away from Aircraft X's wake turbulence during descent into SFO and SJC. Confusion arose when Aircraft X descended below its 12,000-foot restriction due to unclear MEA altitudes on the BRIXX arrival, prompting a request to remove those altitudes.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported that ground personnel prematurely removed ground power and chocks prior to pushback.
summary: The flight crew and ramp agent were involved during pre-push when the agent used non-standard signals to disconnect power and remove chocks, causing the aircraft to roll three to four feet backward. The tug stopped the movement without injury or damage, though the forward door was blocked until the aircraft was towed forward.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported that the crew oxygen system failed to test properly. Maintenance found the valve on the oxygen bottle was not fully open.
summary: The pilot discovered the oxygen pressure gauge dropped to 100 PSI during preflight testing, suspecting the bottle valve was off. Maintenance confirmed the valve was closed, turned it on, and issued a release, though the pilot noted the aircraft likely flew from ZZZ1 to ZZZ with the oxygen system inoperative.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the crew oxygen system pressure dropped excessively when testing. Later, Maintenance found the oxygen valve not fully open.
summary: The captain and first officer observed abnormal oxygen pressure drops during preflight and cruise but continued the flight. Maintenance later found the valve not fully open, a fault the crew missed because normal oxygen flow masked the indication anomaly.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a takeoff with the wrong flap setting.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a flap setting discrepancy during the before takeoff checklist for Runway 09L, where flaps were set to 1 instead of the required 5. The Captain attributed the error to poor communication with the pushback crew and a failure to cross-check the FMC, flap handle, and indicator, though the takeoff continued safely.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reported a significant fuel spill while fueling was in progress at the gate. The aircraft was safely evacuated and the spill was addressed by ground personnel.
summary: During boarding at ZZZ, a fuel truck overfilled the right tank while the left tank remained empty, causing a 250-gallon spill and a 3,000-pound imbalance. The crew evacuated passengers and grounded the aircraft due to suspected single-point refueling system failure and an inability to stop fuel flow from the truck.

synopsis: Citation X Captain reported loss of all nav capability except standby compass shortly after takeoff. Captain suspects anomaly was related to improper nav database software load.
summary: The pilot reported a dual IRS failure immediately after takeoff in a Citation X, suspecting maintenance loaded the wrong navigation database. With no cockpit warnings, the crew navigated visually using only the standby compass to complete the short VMC flight without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported that during approach the flaps became stuck at 20 degrees.
summary: The crew experienced a flap system failure at 1,500 feet during approach to Runway 36R after fuel concerns arose from a long taxi and STAR change. Despite flaps sticking at 20 degrees, they landed safely with increased speed and notified maintenance of the malfunction.

synopsis: PC-12 flight crew reported the rudder trim failed to the far right position and could not be moved. They successfully diverted.
summary: The crew experienced a stuck rudder trim and false autopilot/yaw damper failure messages during initial climb, requiring aileron slips to maintain heading. They diverted to an alternate airport and executed a safe flaps 15 landing after troubleshooting confirmed the issue could not be fixed airborne.

synopsis: A330 flight crew reported a TCAS RA and NMAC with a PA42 on the HYPER7 STAR to IAD.
summary: While descending on the HYPER7 STAR to YYANG, the crew received a TCAS TA and RA from a PA42 twin turboprop approaching from 1 to 2 o'clock. The pilot followed the RA, but the intruder passed 100 feet below the cockpit; ATC did not acknowledge the near miss and cleared the crew to descend to 3000 feet for the ILS 19L.

synopsis: CL605 First Officer reported due to weather and turbulence he was slow to level at their assigned altitude resulting in an altitude excursion.
summary: The pilot and non-flying pilot overshot FL270 to FL272 while climbing in turbulence after switching to vertical speed mode too close to the level-off altitude. The pilot manually leveled the aircraft, triggering a TCAS traffic alert, and attributed the incident to autopilot limitations and their own operational errors.

synopsis: A Hawker 4000 Captain reported a yaw damper system failure and a rudder fault with associated autopilot disconnect and instability inflight while overwater at FL400. The crew regained control, reversed course, and returned to the departure airport.
summary: During cruise at FL400 in oceanic airspace, a yaw damper failure caused longitudinal instability, prompting the crew to execute a contingency maneuver and descend to FL280. The aircraft became controllable at the lower altitude and landed safely at ZZZ with partial flaps.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DCA Tower Controller reported airport roads off the end of two runways are distractions and confusing for pilots and controllers when airport vehicles use the roads.
summary: Local Control cleared Aircraft X for departure after confirming the runway was clear, though an Airport Authority vehicle was simultaneously in the adjacent Run Up Block. The pilot questioned the vehicle's presence, revealing a safety gap where vehicles cross near the runway without ATC authorization or communication.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZDV Center Controllers reported the trainee failed to take appropriate action to resolve a traffic conflict.
summary: A radar trainee and a new controller lost standard separation between Aircraft X and Y at 26,000 feet due to conflicting instructions, frequency static, and a misinterpreted turn. The incident occurred in a combined sector with high complexity, including a diverting aircraft and photo mission, leading to a loss of separation that required immediate descent and turn corrections.

synopsis: DAY Controller reported a drone pilot operated a drone in violation of their Authorization Request.
summary: Local Control reported an uncoordinated drone operation in direct conflict with pattern traffic, where the pilot violated a 75-foot waiver by intending to climb to 300 feet. The Air Traffic Manager failed to notify controllers or enforce restrictions, creating an unsafe situation for departing aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they had to vector an aircraft to its destination below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude because of instrument failure.
summary: An Approach Controller vectored Aircraft X for an ILS approach at 8,000 feet before the pilot reported gyro instrument failure and ground contact. The controller issued a climb to 3,000 feet, but the pilot requested a descent below the 2,600-foot MVA, leading to a coordinated landing clearance after erratic maneuvers in IMC.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Center Controller recieved a handoff from the TRACON of an aircraft below their Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: A Radar Assist reported a Minimum IFR Altitude violation when a TRACON handoff aircraft entered the sector at 7,000 feet instead of the required 8,000 feet. High traffic complexity and complacency regarding frequent false MSAW alerts delayed the climb clearance until the violation occurred at the airspace boundary.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported a Controller had to jump around on the catwalk to get the attention of a fire truck for an inbound emergency aircraft.
summary: Aircraft X reported an electrical issue and requested priority handling while returning to land. The controller struggled to alert the fire department due to outdated procedures and a lack of a Letter of Agreement, though the aircraft landed safely without requiring rescue.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: NCT TRACON Controllers reported distractions caused a go-around aircraft at OAK to enter an area below the MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller missed a go-around check for Aircraft X at Oakland while managing military fighters on the wrong beacon code. The aircraft entered a 2400 ft MVA before the controller issued a turn and climb, prompting a recommendation to issue 3000 ft clearances for future go-arounds.

synopsis: IND TRACON Controller reported that a trainee ignored their instructions, resulting in aircraft on conflicting headings.
summary: A Departure Control supervisor and trainee managed a C172 and a Lear Jet departing from adjacent airports into the same airspace without coordination. The supervisor intervened to issue traffic avoidance headings and altitude restrictions after the trainee's initial routing created a potential conflict in marginal VFR weather.

synopsis: A Tower Controller reported an aircraft initiated a go-around due to a TCAS/RA it received for parallel runway traffic that it had in sight.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued missed approach instructions to Aircraft X after it reported a TCAS Resolution Advisory while paired with Aircraft Y. Investigation revealed Aircraft Y did not receive an RA, leading the controller to speculate on asymmetric TCAS modes but noting a lack of full understanding regarding the system's behavior.

synopsis: A Trainee Controller reported an aircraft he thought was descending to 11000 feet continued descending through 11000 feet into opposite direction traffic at 10000 feet.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a Learjet descending from 11,000 to 9,000 feet into a head-on conflict with a Citation at 10,000 feet on the MOLLY4 arrival. The controller's instructor intervened by issuing an expedited descent to 9,000 feet to avoid the collision, attributing the risk to reliance on pilot-reported altitudes.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported they received several warnings 'Air Systems' and 'A/I Duct', shut down the Number 2 engine, and returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb at 31,000 feet, the crew encountered air system and anti-ice alerts, prompting a diversion to ZZZ for fuel dumping. A subsequent dump valve disagreement caused a minor fuel spill on the taxiway when the crew manually operated the fuel system to offload tail fuel.

synopsis: The Captain of a Bombardier Global reported that during approach using parallel runways they received an RA.
summary: A pilot conducting a visual approach to RWY 30L at ZZZ1 experienced a TCAS RA when a parallel 737 on RWY 30R initiated a go-around at 600 ft AGL due to a perceived conflict. The pilot landed without following the TCAS command, and subsequent investigation concluded the aircraft never crossed paths, attributing the event to the other crew's decision to go around.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being cleared to cross a runway at FAT where a GA aircraft was on very short final. The Captain elected to hold short of the runway.
summary: The Captain and First Officer landed on RWY 29R at FAT and held short of RWY 29L after spotting a GA aircraft on final while crossing via exit B10. No conflict occurred because the crew and ATC reacted quickly, though the crew noted they did not hear a landing clearance for the GA aircraft.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that a main landing gear wheel departed during turnout to taxiway after their landing rollout.
summary: During taxi after landing in heavy rain, the crew felt a thump and later learned the right outboard main landing gear tire had separated and rolled into a pond. Maintenance suspected locked brakes caused the failure, though the crew reported no abnormal indications prior to the separation.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a control problem during climbout and a successful return to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced heavy flight controls and excessive trim requirements during climb and approach, prompting an overweight return to ZZZ. Post-landing, the crew reported feeling unsupported by the Operations Manager and gate agents before being assigned to deadhead back.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an incorrectly programmed hold at DEALE Intersection which led to an RA with another airliner.
summary: The crew erroneously programmed a hold west instead of east of DEALE, leading to a collision course with a 737. ATC issued immediate avoidance vectors, and a TCAS RA prompted a climb to 11,000 feet to resolve the conflict before the flight continued safely.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported the stick shaker activated while encountering wake turbulence on approach to ATL in trail of a B777.
summary: During the CHOPI arrival into Atlanta, a crew flying 10 miles behind a Boeing 777 entered wake turbulence while slowing from 210 to 180 knots. The turbulence caused a stick shaker activation and autopilot disconnect, though the crew reported the aircraft remained in a safe state without an aerodynamic stall.

synopsis: BE58 pilot was concerned his assigned departure heading was toward high terrain while he was in an area where ATC did not have radar contact.
summary: The pilot of a high-performance piston twin departing PRC runway 21L deviated from a cleared heading of 200 due to rising terrain and lack of radar contact until 9,000 feet. The pilot assumed a 360-degree turn was intended, turned left without notifying ATC, and later received vectors after establishing radar contact.

synopsis: B777-200 Captain reported the filed route took the flight through an area on the chart labeled a 'No Fly Area'.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 777-200 discovered their filed route crossed a charted "No Fly Area" while preparing depressurization procedures near high terrain. They deviated around the area and weather, noting that flight planning software allowed the filing and that the manual iPad-based procedure required excessive attention.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on descent to LAX in trail of an A380. They stated 'perhaps more separation is necessary' behind super jumbo aircraft.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A380 while descending through 32,500 feet en route to LAX, causing significant roll and dislodging service items that injured a flight attendant. The crew requested increased separation from the super-heavy aircraft, and although the landing was uneventful, the report suggests current wake turbulence criteria may be insufficient.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that a combination of poor lighting, construction, and lack of signage made it extremely difficult to discern the correct path into the ramp.
summary: The flight crew at SFO experienced confusion while taxiing to the gate at night due to conflicting EFB chart data, poor lighting, and lack of signage. They inadvertently entered the wrong ramp line but stopped to verify their position against pavement markings before safely reaching the gate without conflict.

synopsis: Captain reported problems with JeppPro software on the electronic flight bag.
summary: A pilot reported that on two landings at EWR, the JeppPro EFB taxi chart defaulted to a blank AMM mode during rollout, requiring manual intervention. The pilot identified this as a safety threat due to inadequate information, disorientation, and the need to manipulate the device at a critical flight phase.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported autopilot unable to maintain correct track in NAV Mode due to right wing spoilers being permanently slightly deployed.
summary: During arrival, the crew lost course tracking due to suspected right-wing spoiler malfunction, causing a hard right bank on final. Retracting flaps temporarily fixed the issue, leading to a discontinued approach and subsequent maintenance discovery of stuck spoilers.

synopsis: Embraer 175 Captain reported night visual approaches unsafe with current aircraft equipment, company training and procedures.
summary: A Captain and First Officer conducting Operating Experience at night in Albuquerque executed two go-arounds on visual approaches to Runway 26 due to poor runway visibility and unstable profiles. They eventually landed safely on Runway 21 after correcting a high and overshooting approach, attributing the difficulty to challenging night visual conditions and a lack of RNP guidance.

synopsis: The Captain of a Bombardier DHC-8 reported that after engine start the cockpit started filling up with smoke.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced rapid smoke filling the flight deck after starting engine 2 on a ferry flight of an aircraft with prior fire damage. The crew evacuated, suspecting residual oil in the bleed system was atomized when bleeds were activated too soon, though the company attributed it to procedural timing.

synopsis: B737 crew successfully rejects takeoff below eighty knots when smoke enters cockpit through First Officer's glare shield vents.
summary: During takeoff, smoke from the First Officer's glare shield vent prompted the Captain to reject the takeoff below 80 knots. The fumes dissipated immediately upon idle thrust, and after confirming no cabin smoke, the crew returned to the gate.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported encountering significant wake turbulence on approach to CLT 4.5 miles in trail of a B757. Reporter expressed concern at the reduced separation standards in trail of B757 aircraft.
summary: A pilot approaching runway 18R encountered significant wake turbulence from a preceding B757, causing temporary loss of control. The pilot attributed the incident to ATC vectoring the aircraft too close behind the B757, requesting a return to the previously required 5-mile spacing.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported experiencing an ENG FAIL light during takeoff roll resulting in a high-speed rejected takeoff.
summary: During takeoff roll at 120 KIAS, an ENG FAIL light illuminated, prompting the Captain to execute a rejected takeoff. Crews reported hearing an engine rollback, but after maintenance checks and trans-loading, the flight continued to the destination.

synopsis: B787 Flight Attendant reported an issue with fasten seat belt sign usage with a particular crew.
summary: A flight attendant discussed with the captain and purser the captain's practice of keeping the Fasten Seat Belt sign on for the entire flight to ensure a quiet environment. The attendant cited FAR 121.311 violations and reduced turbulence awareness, prompting the captain to agree to reevaluate his approach.

synopsis: Maintenance reported they installed an incorrect bearing on an MD-11 nose gear wheel assembly.
summary: A mechanic installed incorrect bearing part number M224749 instead of the correct part number 68462 in the inboard wheel half serial number aug92-0739.

synopsis: A student pilot reported that another aircraft entered the non-towered runway without notice, causing a go around, then performed an early turn, resulting in an airborne conflict.
summary: A pilot on final approach for a solo landing executed a go-around when a Bonanza entered the runway for takeoff without proper coordination. The Bonanza subsequently cleared the airport, allowing the pilot to complete the landing without incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported poor communication with ATC and unfamiliarity with the area led to an airspace violation.
summary: The pilot descended east of SDL without a confirmed Class B clearance, causing a conflict with Phoenix ATC. The pilot attributed the error to unfamiliarity with the aircraft and area, admitting fault for failing to verify clearance before initiating descent.

synopsis: PA-24 Comanche pilot reported a landing gear collapse upon landing for unknown reasons.
summary: The pilot of a Comanche on final approach landed with the gear collapsed, causing the aircraft to skid on its belly and block the runway. Although the pilot believed the gear was down and tower personnel confirmed it, the collapse closed the airport for two hours.

synopsis: A Gulfstream Captain reported that reloading the FMC after a runway change, using the same SID, some of the waypoints dropped out.
summary: The flight crew experienced an FMS error after a last-minute runway change, which dropped the SID transition and caused them to miss two fixes. Although they deviated from the SID and received a direct clearance to the departure fix, no traffic or airspace incursions occurred.

synopsis: A Gulfstream First Officer reported they received a Traffic Advisory on base leg and a Resolution Advisory during final approach.
summary: The reporting crew on a visual approach to RWY 03R received a climb RA for a P-51 below but refused to climb as the P-51 overtook them from above. The reporter attributes the incident to the P-51 pilot's failure to follow ATC instructions, while noting the tower provided adequate guidance and the flight landed safely.

synopsis: PA44 flight instructor reported a near-mid-air-collision on after takeoff due to a lack of attention to preceding traffic separation.
summary: A PA-44 instructor and student lost sight of a Cessna they were cleared to follow during a short-field takeoff training flight. The instructor attributed the resulting 50-foot near miss to focusing on internal training rather than maintaining external visual traffic separation.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reported entering an usual attitude due to loss of reliable attitude indicator information.
summary: The pilot experienced an abrupt unusual attitude and attitude indicator failure while intercepting the localizer in IFR conditions. The approach was aborted, and Air Traffic Control vectored the aircraft to ZZZ1 for a safe landing after the pilot regained level flight using ground contact.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot of a turboprop aircraft reported diverting to an alternate airport after the other pilot became incapacitated.
summary: The Pilot Flying became incapacitated by vomiting and unconsciousness at FL250 due to undiagnosed atrial fibrillation. The Pilot Not Flying disengaged the autopilot, managed an emergency descent to a nearby non-towered airport, and landed safely while a passenger assisted the sick crew member.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft Flight Instructor reported entering IMC while ferrying an aircraft on a VFR flight.
summary: A fatigued pilot ferrying an aircraft with inoperative transponder, turn-and-slip, and Nav radio encountered deteriorating weather and scud running after 10 hours of flight. The pilot declared PAN PAN, received ground-based navigation assistance from Cheyenne Approach due to lack of radar, and safely landed at 200–300 feet AGL.

synopsis: Cessna 510 pilot reported an airborne conflict on departure.
summary: A pilot climbing VFR after takeoff received a TCAS resolution advisory while descending to 3500 feet due to ATC instructions, forcing a hard right bank to avoid converging traffic. The pilot attributed the near-miss to poor radar coverage below 3000 feet, ATC assigning a descent into oncoming traffic, and communication gaps caused by the controller managing two frequencies.

synopsis: A ground observer reported noticing a UAV was operating near the stage at a concert event.
summary: The reporter observed an unmanned UAS hovering at 250 AGL near a concert stage and pyrotechnic display. The pilot deemed the operation unsafe and noted it should have been prohibited under the established security TFR.

synopsis: FFZ Tower Controller reported overlooking a potential conflict between an arriving and departing aircraft until they were almost converging.
summary: The controller reported a near mid-air collision between Aircraft X on left traffic for RWY 22L and departing Aircraft Y. The controller admitted failing to recognize the conflict sooner, resulting in Aircraft X passing approximately 400 feet above Aircraft Y, which reported an NMAC.

synopsis: SLC Tower Controller reported runway and taxiway closures increased their workload causing them to have to issue an arriving aircraft go-around instructions.
summary: A local controller managing departures and arrivals during runway and taxiway closures crossed two aircraft at H10, realizing insufficient spacing for a takeoff clearance. The controller canceled the departure and instructed an arriving aircraft to go around due to the conflict.

synopsis: NCT Departure Control Coordinator reported a departure contacted the TRACON on the wrong frequency and neither the trainee or the Supervisor observing the trainee noticed the wrong aircraft had called them.
summary: A TRACON Coordinator reported that Aircraft X departed on the wrong frequency and was initially ignored by a trainee Departure Controller, creating a conflict with overflight Aircraft Y at 9,500 feet. The incident was resolved when the trainee eventually contacted Aircraft X, but the reporter attributed the near-miss to the trainee's incompetence and the supervisor's lack of proficiency.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZOA Center Controller reported the adjacent TRACON sectors took point outs on aircraft that were head on into confliction instead of taking communication and control of the two aircraft.
summary: A head-on conflict occurred between Aircraft Y climbing to 19,000 feet and Aircraft X descending via the RAZRR STAR due to TRACON removing Y from radar before issuing separation. TRACON later issued a panic 130-degree vector to avoid a near miss, while the supervisor blamed the Center for not climbing Y, ignoring that TRACON failed to maintain control.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a disparity between the Jeppesen 10-9, 10-9B, and the actual signage in the area of k, K-3, M, and L Taxiways from Runway 27R to Spot 9 at PHL.
summary: The pilot reported a discrepancy between airport signage and the 10-9 chart while taxiing from runway 27R to Spot 9. Signage indicated taxiway K-3, which was not shown on the chart, and the 10-9 and 10-9B charts displayed conflicting taxiway configurations in that area.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported that takeoff performance data limits the pilots options for a safe Rejected Takeoff.
summary: A 737-800 pilot at Chicago Midway rejected a dispatcher-approved takeoff plan with only 270 feet of stopping margin due to safety concerns regarding shifting winds and heavy aircraft weight. The pilot argued that software restrictions preventing the use of "bleeds OFF" to increase margin were unsafe, despite the Chief Pilot confirming the positive margin was legal.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that after landing, they were still taxiing on the runway when another aircraft was given clearance for takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that heavy rain obscured taxiway markings during rollout, causing a delay in exiting the runway while ATC cleared another aircraft for takeoff. The pilot alerted ATC and the departing flight, resulting in the cancellation of the takeoff and instructions for the other aircraft to taxi down the runway to an exit.

synopsis: Embraer Captain reported not following proper parking procedure for shutting down the engines which placed ramp employees in a hazardous situation.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X turned off the beacon while the #2 engine was running, causing a ground crew member to nearly be sucked into the engine while placing a cone. The pilot reported the incident to the chief pilot after the employee informed them of the near-miss.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported an issue with the FMS which did not comply with altitude restrictions during an ILS approach.
summary: A pilot reported that a Honeywell MCDU-equipped aircraft ignored the 3,600 FT crossing restriction at HUNDA during two LAX runway 25L arrivals. The aircraft crossed at 3,550 FT and 3,540 FT while in DES/NAV mode with APPR pressed, capturing the glide slope prematurely.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported issues with scheduling of all night flights which result in fatigued pilots.
summary: A pilot reported that fatiguing schedules involving legs and sits prior to red-eye flights and frequent schedule changes remain an issue despite being legal. The reporter asserts that these practices violate the intent of Part 117 and recommends specific rest periods to mitigate human factors risks.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reported that the seatbelt/harness for the second observer seat did not release properly, and that Maintenance initially failed to accurately document the repair.
summary: The crew discovered a defective quick-release harness on the left observer seat while hooked to a tow tug with two engines running. The flight returned to the gate to replace the incorrect part and resolve a misleading maintenance logbook entry before departing.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 First Officer reported engine surging which resulted in an engine failure and landing at planned arrival station.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine compressor stall followed by complete failure during climb, causing an EGT spike and fire bottle discharge failure. They landed safely at ZZZ, where maintenance found metal shavings in the tailpipe of an engine changed eight days prior.

synopsis: PA28 pilots reported that during landing rollout, a deer walked in front of the aircraft and was struck by the propeller.
summary: An instructor and student in a Piper PA28-161 Warrior struck a 75-pound buck with the idling propeller during a night landing rollout at approximately 3 mph. The impact stopped the engine, but a preliminary inspection revealed no visible damage to the propeller, cowling, or nose gear, and no injuries occurred.

synopsis: Citabria pilot reported a gust of wind during landing caused the aircraft ground loop.
summary: The pilot reported that during a wheel landing in gusty winds, the aircraft drifted right, failed to climb adequately on a missed approach, and drifted left. Despite full control inputs to correct the drift and touch down midfield, the aircraft ground looped.

synopsis: MEM Tower Local Controller reported they had to issue last minute instructions to separate an arriving aircraft which initiated a go-around just as a departure was airborne.
summary: An air traffic controller managed simultaneous approaches and a departure involving Aircraft X, Y, and Z. Aircraft X initiated an unannounced go-around while Aircraft Y was airborne, prompting the controller to issue conflict avoidance instructions and later attribute the event to suboptimal use of the Arrival Departure Window procedure.

synopsis: HCF TRACON Trainee Controller reported a military helicopter did not comply with its missed approach instructions which placed it into conflict with another departure.
summary: An ATC controller and pilot of Aircraft X experienced a conflict during a practice VOR-A missed approach at MKK when the pilot misinterpreted revised outbound instructions and turned back toward the VORTAC. This deviation required immediate corrective headings and altitude changes to maintain separation from departing Aircraft Y, attributed to pilot misunderstanding and a complex missed approach procedure.

synopsis: B777-300 Captain reported an anomaly with the automatic announcement system.
summary: Pilots and flight attendants on a Boeing 777-300 reported that the automated takeoff announcement was not heard in all cabin areas. The crew questioned whether relying solely on this automated message creates a communication hazard compared to manual announcements or backup procedures.

synopsis: Air carrier Load Planner reported confusion and nonstandard procedures being used by ramp employees while loading cargo.
summary: A load planner reported that a ZZZ operations agent incorrectly requested loading two heavy mail carts into Pit 4 of an A319, unaware the pit is smaller than on an A320. The planner corrected the agent to split the loads, warning that such misunderstandings and potential net modifications create balance hazards and safety risks.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: B737 Captain reported that one of the Company Tailored Jeppesen charts for Runway 31L at PSP erroneously indicates that there are VASI lights to the left of the runway which may lead to Taxiway C being mistaken as a runway.
summary: The First Officer lined up on Taxiway C instead of Runway 31L at PSP due to a Jeppesen chart error stating VASIs were on the left. The Captain corrected the alignment at a safe altitude, noting the chart incorrectly listed VASIs instead of the actual PAPIs located on the right.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reported being informed by ATC that they were off course. They informed the crew that there was reported GPS signal jamming in the area.
summary: The flight crew experienced a reported deviation while flying the HUULL 1 STAR into LAX due to GPS signal jamming, which ATC initially disputed. Although the crew verified their FMS data was correct, ATC later confirmed the jamming but suggested possible aircraft equipment malfunction as an alternative cause.

synopsis: BE55 pilot reported damage to the propeller blades and landing gear door due to runway contact after takeoff due to an unexpected nose down trim condition.
summary: The pilot and an avionics technician conducted a post-maintenance flight to verify a replaced autopilot roll servo. Due to preflight complacency regarding trim verification, the aircraft settled after takeoff, causing propeller and gear door damage when the pilot inadvertently retracted the gear while correcting the out-of-trim condition.

synopsis: SR20 flight instructor reported the flight school chief instructor demonstrated excessive aircraft flight control input and did not report unnecessary stress that was placed upon the airframe.
summary: During a training flight in a Cirrus SR20, the chief pilot entered an incipient spin while demonstrating a falling leaf to the new hire instructor. The event resulted from the chief pilot's drastic control inputs, reaching 164 degrees roll and -10,000 FPM vertical speed, before recovery was achieved.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Center Controller reported that an aircraft declaring Minimum Fuel departed his assigned altitude without notification resulting in a conflict with another aircraft.
summary: An ATC trainee and supervisor managed Aircraft Y's fuel shortage diversion at FL270 above Aircraft X at FL250. Separation was lost when Aircraft Y descended to FL262 without clearance, resulting in a 300-foot vertical proximity, which the controller attributed to the pilot's failure to report altitude changes.

synopsis: Captain reported procedural issues with the FMS on the 737-MAX in reference to descent capabilities.
summary: During 737-MAX training, pilots found that pressing the ALT INTV button unexpectedly updated the FMC cruise altitude from the MCP, contrary to the Fault Reporting Manual. This caused the aircraft to fail descending on new clearances until ALT INTV was pressed again, creating a potential altitude violation hazard.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported difficulty in interpreting displays of the FMS which resulted in an altitude deviation during the approach.
summary: Two pilots flying a LOC 9R approach into ORD mistakenly used FMS waypoint distance instead of ILS DME for step-down fixes due to task saturation from a late runway change. They descended below 4,000 feet before realizing the error, climbing back to 4,000 feet while remaining above the minimum safe altitude.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported that a new bridge near EWR has sequencing white strobe lights that could be mistaken for Runway End Identifier Lights.
summary: A pilot reported that sequenced strobing lights on the new Goethals Bridge towers could be mistaken for REILs during an approach to Newark Airport in an east wind. The reporter suggests changing the lights to random flashers and posting a warning to prevent crews from mistakenly heading for the bridge.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported experiencing a malfunctioning nose gear air/ground sensor which resulted in several configuration warning messages. After completing all troubleshooting checklists and consulting with maintenance personnel, a successful landing was accomplished.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent configuration warnings on approach due to a faulty nose gear air/ground sensor, prompting a go-around and priority landing. A post-flight inspection identified a severed rivet on the sensor plate as the cause, though the reporter criticized the unavailability of a Subject Matter Expert during the event.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Business jet flight crew reported difficulty catching altitude restriction departing HOU on the PDC print out.
summary: The flight crew departed HOU on the WYLSN5 and initially set 16,000 feet based on a PDC, but ATC corrected the clearance to 5,000 feet. The crew attributed the error to missing the altitude restriction in the PDC notes due to rushing, though no navigation deviation was confirmed.

synopsis: Flight crew of a large turbojet aircraft reported a ramp fire occurred before departure on a cargo pallet before it was loaded into the cargo hold.
summary: A flight attendant smelled smoke during a pre-flight walk-around, prompting an evacuation after an agent reported fire on the ramp. The crew exited to find fire trucks extinguishing a smoldering cargo pallet, with the reporter believing the fire originated on the ground rather than the loader.

synopsis: Legacy 600 Captain reported they had to go-around because the aircraft landing ahead of them was still on the runway.
summary: The pilot reported that while on a visual approach to runway 34 at HPN, a Cirrus ahead stalled its engine after being instructed to remain on the runway. The pilot executed a go-around and landed safely, attributing the incident to ATC rushing to close the facility and issuing conflicting clearances.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525 Captain reported a track deviation during climb from SLC when they were distracted by turbulence or a wake vortex encounter.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence while climbing out of SLC on the LEETZ 6 departure, causing autopilot disengagement and a deviation that missed the PPIGG fix. ATC issued a heading to rejoin the departure, and the crew later admitted they failed to report the turbulence or deviation due to being preoccupied with controlling the aircraft.

synopsis: BE55 pilot reported experiencing a collapsed nose gear upon landing.
summary: The pilot executed a missed approach and landing on Runway YY in rain, experiencing a bounce and balloon during the flare. Despite normal landing speed, the nose wheel collapsed upon the second touchdown, prompting an immediate evacuation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA flight instructor reported that K90 TRACON was concerned about his flight lesson near a nuclear power plant.
summary: A flight instructor and student operating a training aircraft over Plymouth Bay northwest of a nuclear power plant were contacted by the FAA after being tracked by Boston TRACON due to the facility's radar outage. The instructor reported no pilot deviation action was taken but recommended clarifying ambiguous NOTAM restrictions regarding proximity to nuclear facilities.

synopsis: ZDV Center Controller reported receiving a NORDO aircraft that wasn't in radar coverage below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller received a non-radar IFR handoff of Aircraft X at 6000 ft with no radio contact. The controller issued a blind climb clearance to 8000 ft for the MVA and subsequently observed the aircraft climbing from 6200 ft as it entered the 7000 ft MVA area.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: BJC Tower Controller reported that an aircraft on visual approach was concerned that an aircraft in a VFR corridor was too close.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a conflict between Aircraft X on a visual approach and uncommunicating VFR Aircraft Y near the final at 7300 ft. The incident, which prompted a Mandatory Occurrence Report, highlighted safety concerns regarding VFR aircraft operating in corridors without ATC communication.

synopsis: PBI TRACON Controller and a GA pilot reported miscommunication, which resulted in the aircraft descending below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller trainee vectored Aircraft X below the 2,500 ft MVA while the instructor failed to intervene. Separately, a pilot in IMC misunderstood a controller's clearance, descended below 3,000 ft, and violated the IFR environment after losing visual contact.

synopsis: ZNY Center Controller reported they were required to work more than 10 hours which is a violation of work rules.
summary: A crew member reported that a Supervisor altered their sign-out time to hide a shift exceeding 10 hours. The reporter requested proper shift management and accurate payment for the actual hours worked.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on short final at PHX in trail of a B757.
summary: PHX Approach and Tower controllers vectored the crew to a short final with aggressive overtake clearances, causing a tight S-turn and wake turbulence encounter behind a preceding B757. The pilot reported the situation was unsafe due to ATC instructions but allowed the First Officer to continue, resulting in a close landing just as the runway cleared.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a near midair collision while on final approach, and going around on the second approach, both due to lack of traffic separation from ATC.
summary: During approach to Runway 08 at 1,500 ft, the crew executed two go-arounds due to a Twin Otter and a VFR aircraft maneuvering into their path. The pilot attributed the unsafe situation to TJSJ Tower's failure to manage traffic, noting the Twin Otter turned and climbed directly toward them.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported smoke emanating from the First Officer's side external to the flight deck possibly from the external power connection. The crew and passengers evacuated.
summary: The flight crew observed smoke near the First Officer's window at the gate, likely caused by the ground power chord. They evacuated passengers, shut off ground power, and removed the aircraft from service while passengers continued on another flight.

synopsis: Embraer First Officer reported encountering severe turbulence while on descent into ORD.
summary: During an RNAV arrival into Chicago at 14,000ft, severe turbulence caused violent rolls that disengaged the autopilot, prompting a right offset to avoid a 737 wake.
