No injuries occurred, but maintenance found a broken Captain's side piano hinge rod, and the Captain grounded himself for a wrist injury.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported a minor track deviation occurred when they encountered wake turbulence on approach into PHL in trail of an A320.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding A320 while on the ILS 27R approach to PHL at 3,000 ft, causing the autopilot to disengage. The pilot manually recovered the aircraft and accepted a reduced speed of 160 kts from ATC, attributing the event to insufficient separation provided by controllers.

synopsis: Captain of a Widebody Transport reported having issues with ANC ATC in both communications and clearances.
summary: The flight crew reported confusion during departure after the ANC controller issued complex intercept clearances and multiple frequency changes that were difficult to program. The crew suspected the controller may have mistaken them for a different flight that had rejected takeoff due to an engine thrust issue.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported performing an evacuation of the aircraft at the gate during boarding when the cabin filled with smoke from an external fire in the vicinity of the aft cargo compartment.
summary: Four crew members witnessed a fire under the aft cargo door that burned it black and filled the aircraft with acidulous, electric-smelling fumes, forcing an evacuation. The crew documented evidence contradicting the loader fire theory and faced uncertainty regarding ferrying the damaged aircraft and crew rest.

synopsis: ERJ-175 pilot reported distraction and poor performance from the company tablet EFB on short final.
summary: During short final in an E175, the Pilot Monitoring became distracted while struggling to zoom on a Microsoft Surface EFB due to poor mounting, portrait orientation, and unresponsive touch gestures in turbulence. The pilot turned off the device to complete the landing and cited the hardware's unsuitability for the cockpit environment as the cause of the distraction.

synopsis: ERJ145 Captain reported experiencing smoke and fumes, both in the cockpit and cabin. A successful diversion to a suitable nearby airport was accomplished.
summary: The flight crew experienced smoke and an electrical smell in the flight deck and cabin during cruise at FL250, prompting a diversion. Maintenance attributed the incident to Pack 2 failing while the aircraft was already operating with Pack 1 on an MEL, resulting in no injuries.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported receiving a low altitude warning while approaching the SAV area.
summary: The pilot reported receiving conflicting ATC descent and climb instructions near SAV while avoiding an aerobatic aircraft and terrain. The crew climbed to 2,500 feet to avoid antennas detected on the MFD before continuing a visual approach to runway 10.

synopsis: Airbus pilot reported a loss of cabin pressure due to loss of the one remaining pack.
summary: The crew dispatched with one pack inoperative, and the second pack failed at FL330. They descended to FL100 to stabilize pressurization, reinstated the pack, and continued at FL220 with no further issues.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reported ASOS was broadcasting inaccurate weather.
summary: The flight crew encountered inaccurate ASOS fog reports while approaching ZZZ, observing 10 SM visibility instead. Unable to contact Center due to a ground communication outage, they landed safely, noting the weather sensor requires repair or relocation.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the Airport Moving Map (AMM) on the Jeppesen FD-Pro cannot be turned off by the flight crew. Zooming out on the AMM taxi chart causes taxiway names to disappear resulting in increased workload and heads-down iPad work during after landing taxi.
summary: A pilot reported that the Jeppesen FD-Pro's Airport Moving Map automatically activates after landing and cannot be disabled. This causes safety concerns at large airports because zooming out hides taxiway names, forcing unsafe heads-down iPad manipulation to switch charts for situational awareness.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Light transport flight crew reported landing at the wrong airport.
summary: The flight crew descended for an ILS 5 approach to KBPK but landed at the wrong airport, KFLP, due to loss of situational awareness. Despite glideslope warnings and visual discrepancies, the pilots disregarded cues and continued the approach to an uneventful landing at Marion County Regional Airport.

synopsis: UAV operator reported unauthorized operation of a drone in close proximity to a moving freight train.
summary: An experienced hobby drone operator flew a racing drone near, under, and inside a moving freight train for three minutes. The incident occurred due to the operator's unawareness of strict rules regarding railroad property, though the drone landed safely with no other jeopardy.

synopsis: BE300 flight crew reported an A380 pilot communicated to Ground Control of a near collision on the taxiway.
summary: A turbo-prop pilot taxiing at LAX reported a near miss with an A380 on taxiway S while turning from T1, despite receiving no hold instructions from Ground South. The A380 crew reported the incident to Ground North, who assigned a Tower Manager to investigate, though the turbo-prop crew maintained they had ample clearance.

synopsis: PA44 flight instructor reported losing control while taxiing and striking a taxi light due to a distraction.
summary: The pilot lost control while taxiing and struck a taxi light due to divided attention caused by a fogging windshield. No injuries occurred, and the pilot recommends stopping taxi operations until the windshield clears.

synopsis: Flight crew Falcon 900 reported a failure of cabin pressurization and commenced an emergency descent and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: Pilots on a flight at FL410 experienced weak cabin pressurization and a cabin warning, prompting a priority descent and diversion. Maintenance later identified a disconnected flex tube at the forward water separator as the cause of the bleed air loss.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported aggressive aborted takeoff when alerted by ATC, as another aircraft taxied onto the runway.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff on Runway 24 at Chicago Executive after the Tower controller stopped them to avoid a collision with Aircraft Y crossing from Taxiway Echo. The near-miss was caused by Aircraft Y entering the runway, potentially due to faded markings at a known hot spot, though the specific taxi clearance remains unknown.

synopsis: C172 pilots reported they did not recall an instruction to contact the Tower until already having entered the Tower's airspace.
summary: A safety pilot reported that a student pilot practicing an ILS approach under VFR failed to contact the tower before landing, resulting in an airspace violation. The reporter attributed the incident to the student's inexperience and poor cockpit organization, noting uncertainty over whether Approach issued the frequency change instruction.

synopsis: Stearman pilot reported loss of control during engine run up resulting in a propeller ground strike.
summary: During a static engine run-up, the aircraft tail rose while the pilot held full up elevator, causing the propeller to impact the ground. The aircraft came to rest upright vertically on the propeller hub.

synopsis: A pilot and Center Controller reported a communication problem with an altitude clearance and descended below the minimum IFR altitude.
summary: A Radar Controller and pilot experienced a descent clearance misunderstanding where the pilot read back 11,000 feet instead of the issued 14,000 feet, causing the aircraft to descend below the Minimum IFR Altitude. The controller issued a low altitude alert and climb instruction after the pilot failed to verify the clearance, attributing the error to unclear radio communications.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported that they smelled smoke in the aircraft, which dissipated after a while.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew smelled smoke during climbout, prompting a return to the airfield after ATC reported similar incidents. The crew determined the smoke was environmental, but running the checklist locked the overboard exhaust valve open, requiring a lower altitude until maintenance confirmed higher flight was safe.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported iPad Jeppesen FD Pro taxi chart defaults to small scale, difficult to read, moving map on landing resulting in a dangerous situation.
summary: A pilot reported that the Jepp FD Pro iPad app automatically displayed an unreadable, small taxi chart upon landing rollout. This caused a dangerous distraction during runway exit, as the pilot could not easily enlarge the map to identify taxiway clearances while managing flight controls.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported incorrect baggage counts which led to issues with weight and balance.
summary: The pilot reported a significant baggage weight discrepancy between the Cargo Load Report and actual load, causing suspected center of gravity issues during takeoff and landing. The pilot believes the aircraft was out of the CG window for landing and reported the error to the Chief Pilots to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: BE58 pilot reported that after landing an engine shutdown, and while attempting to restart, the engine caught fire.
summary: The pilot experienced engine roughness and a subsequent right engine fire on taxi after leaning mixtures too lean for landing due to newly installed fuel pumps. The fire occurred during a memory-based restart attempt that deviated from the Pilot's Operating Handbook, but was extinguished by cutting the mixture to idle cutoff.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: HOU Tower Controller and flight crew reported the Controller cleared them to cross a runway at the same time a departure was beginning its takeoff roll.
summary: A Tower controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was crossing the runway due to expectation bias, causing an ASDE-X alert. The pilot of Aircraft X entered the runway despite believing it was clear, but Aircraft Y rotated and overflew them safely.

synopsis: ZAU Center Controller reported the Radar Controller did not follow proper procedures to ensure required non radar separation criteria were met for the receiving facility.
summary: A Radar Assist controller reported that a Radar Controller improperly cleared Aircraft X and Y to deviate direct to fixes before terminating radar, failing to establish required Oceanic Non-Radar separation. The reporter attributed this error to inadequate training on airspace transition requirements and a lack of understanding regarding radar termination responsibilities.

synopsis: ZMP Center Controller reported an adjacent Center controller handed off two aircraft that were converging inside their airspace.
summary: A radar controller at ZDV managed a potential loss of separation between eastbound Aircraft X and northeast-bound Aircraft Y at 37,000 ft by turning Y 15 degrees left. Northwest winds aided the maneuver, allowing Y to pass 6.5 miles behind X while avoiding conflict with nearby Aircraft Z.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported they did not comply with an ATC assigned speed.
summary: The flight crew, descending on downwind to 7,000 feet, slowed to 185 knots to manage flap limits and PRM approach concerns. ATC scolded them for non-compliance with the 210-knot speed clearance, though a subsequent FAA representative confirmed the controller understood the situation.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported that they got an 'OBSTACLE, PULL UP' alert when they turned base early.
summary: The First Officer and Captain flew a visual approach to runway 19R, triggering a GPWS "OBSTACLE, PULL UP" alert due to deviating from the required 3,500-foot altitude and turning too early near the Tower. The crew immediately executed the avoidance maneuver, intercepted the final approach, and landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: An Embraer-145 First Officer reported that the nose gear would not retract after takeoff. The crew opted to return to the departure airport and discovered that the nose gear pin was still installed.
summary: The flight crew detected a nose gear pin left in the wheel well during takeoff, causing the gear to remain down despite normal hydraulic indications. After leveling at 5,000 feet, burning fuel, and following QRH procedures, they landed safely, revealing the pin was hidden by a short red flag and missed during the preflight walk-around.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported responding to an RA while on final approach to 28C at PIT due to opposite direction VFR traffic also under ATC control.
summary: During descent from 5,000' to 4,000', the crew received TCAS RAs due to a VFR aircraft crossing 500' below. The pilots manually adjusted vertical speed to comply with the RAs, climbed to 4,100', and attributed the conflict to ATC allowing insufficient separation between the jet and the small aircraft.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported a track deviation occurred departing DFW airport.
summary: The crew experienced an EFIS COMP MON caution and wake turbulence during departure from DFW Runway 18L, causing a left drift despite autopilot engagement. ATC provided vectors and a frequency change after detecting the deviation, but navigation performance normalized en route to RBBIT.

synopsis: B777-300 First Officer preparing to depart on an international flight reported the fueler alerted them to a potential fuel upload issue that was traced to malfunctioning fuel quantity indicators. The flight would have departed 25,000 lbs short of cleared fuel had the issue not been caught on the ground.
summary: During preflight, the flight crew and fueler discovered the B777's fuel gauges erroneously indicated a full load while the aircraft was actually over 25,000 lbs short. Maintenance rebooted the Fuel Indication System to correct the readings, preventing a potential fuel exhaustion incident that would have required a diversion.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported that a SID crossing restriction was missed while hand-flying the aircraft due to distractions and not following the flight director.
summary: The First Officer hand-flew a departure, overshooting the 11,000-foot TARRK restriction by 700 feet due to distraction from fuel and pressurization checks and misinterpreting flight director pitch cues. The crew descended to comply with the restriction after ATC notification, attributing the error to lost situational awareness and recommending earlier autopilot engagement for complex SIDs.

synopsis: M20 flight instructor reported exiting a taxiway into the grass when the student failed to properly apply the brakes in an aircraft that has only 1 set of brake pedals.
summary: A flight instructor and student exited the taxiway into grass during taxi after the student failed to stop the aircraft by mistaking a high ledge for the brakes. The instructor shut down the engine to stop the aircraft, resulting in no damage to the occupants, aircraft, or ground equipment.

synopsis: LR31A Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport after a precautionary shutdown of the left engine following a low oil pressure indication.
summary: The crew experienced fluctuating left engine oil pressure that dropped below 25 psi, triggering an annunciator light during climb. They performed an in-flight shutdown, diverted to an alternate airport, and landed safely; maintenance later found a damaged aneroid in the oil pressure relief valve.

synopsis: RV-7 pilot reported that he took off from the opposite runway than was assigned because of weather and other distractions.
summary: The pilot unintentionally departed runway 9R instead of the cleared 27L from intersection C due to weather fixation and misinterpreting ATIS information regarding closed runways. No traffic conflict occurred as the pilot immediately coordinated with ATC while airborne, attributing the error to a flawed mental plan and quicker-than-expected clearance.

synopsis: AL3 pilot reported diverting to an alternate airport after noticing a fuel leak in flight.
summary: During cruise, the pilot detected a fuel smell and observed a leak from the right tank at the wing root. The pilot diverted to the nearest airport, shut off the electrical system for safety, and landed without incident.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reported a near miss with a UAV.
summary: The pilot and copilot observed a drone flying 100 feet from the aircraft at 12,000 feet during cruise. Jacksonville Center was advised of the situation.

synopsis: ATC Center controller reported vectoring several aircraft for sequencing to an airport unnecessarily due to faulty instructions from the Traffic Management Unit.
summary: An air traffic controller in a high sector feeding ATL reported that Traffic Management Unit (TMU) reshuffling caused unnecessary vectors for six to eight aircraft. The controller stated that sudden metering time changes increased workload, fuel burn, and safety risks due to poor coordination before the list was altered.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported a runway incursion after instructing an aircraft to standby.
summary: An air traffic controller working a combined local position missed a student pilot's incorrect readback of "line up and wait" after being told to "standby," causing the student to enter the runway while another aircraft was on final. The controller attributed the runway incursion to fatigue, multitasking, and complacency, resulting in the second aircraft executing a go-around.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported an altitude deviation on arrival into BOS.
summary: The flight crew of a 757-300 on the JFUND 2 arrival into BOS descended below 7,000 feet prior to SPYSD after an FMC path recalculation during an approach change. The pilot attributed the low altitude to the temporary loss of the vertical path while manually maintaining a one-mile right offset.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported an anomaly with charting hold patterns in the ORD area. Some patterns are published on the second page and crews are not guided to look for the patterns there by zooming out on their EFB's.
summary: A pilot on the WATSN3 arrival into ORD could not locate a published holding pattern at MKITA due to confusing chart placement in inset boxes. The crew requested vectors, and another aircraft reported the same issue, highlighting the lack of clear notes directing pilots to the inset patterns.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported being uncomfortable with the procedure in place at PHF airport that allows military aircraft to be vectored over arrivals at low altitudes.
summary: A commercial crew on ILS 7 approach to PHF encountered an E2 Hawkeye overflying their final approach path at 300–500 feet AGL without prior notification. The pilot reported the unsafe proximity to ATC and the Chief Pilot, recommending that overflying aircraft avoid passing arriving airliners or provide advance crew advisories.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a close encounter with a 'fixed wing drone' at 4000 ft while on left downwind to Runway 22 at LGA.
summary: During an approach to LGA Runway 22 at 4,000 ft, the First Officer observed a fixed-wing drone pass within 30 feet of the aircraft. The crew reported the man-made object to ATC, and the flight continued without physical contact or incident.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported finding the outboard speed brakes deployed during post-flight inspection.
summary: Pilots on an arrival approach experienced intermittent gear warnings due to an MEL-disabled GPWS and landed with speed brakes inadvertently deployed. The crew attributed the error to system logic faults and distraction from the gear horn, noting the aircraft had a prior unresolved logbook entry for the same issue.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reported a close encounter with a UAV at 4000 feet on the downwind leg for Runway 27R at ORD.
summary: The pilot and First Officer encountered a suspected drone while executing the FYTTE4 RNAV STAR to ORD at 4,000 feet MSL between VULCN and HIMGO. The object passed closely on the right without requiring evasive action, attributed to reckless UAV operation near arrival traffic.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported having a reaction to fumes coming from a passenger carry-on bag, and questioned the safety of relocating the bag to the checked baggage compartment of the aircraft.
summary: Cabin crew reported a strong odor during boarding that caused severe physical symptoms, which was traced to a passenger's carry-on bag. The bag was moved to the cargo hold without identification, leading the crew to withdraw from duty and seek medical evaluation for an allergic reaction to an unknown irritant.

synopsis: GA pilot reported flying at the wrong altitude during a flight flown in the vicinity of the Statue of Liberty. He recommended the NYC TAC VFR Planning Chart be modified to include the FAA altitude restrictions listed on the NY Class B Airspace Hudson River Exclusion SFRA.
summary: A pilot conducting a local operation in the New York SFRA flew at 1200 MSL while orbiting the Statue of Liberty, exceeding the 1000-foot limit for such maneuvers. The pilot realized post-flight that the NYC TAC VFR Planning Chart lacked clarity on altitude requirements for local versus transient operations.

synopsis: ATC Center Controller reported supervisory personnel ordered the controllers to split a sector in the middle of a busy traffic period.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that management forced a sector split during high traffic without coordination, removing a Radar Assist and later reassigning the controller to a busy sector while an unready replacement took over. This chaotic execution caused frequency errors and unresolved conflicts, which the controller attributed to poor management accountability and a failure to prioritize safety over administrative targets.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported receiving a terrain warning after descending 200 feet low on a night approach to RNO in an area of rising terrain.
summary: The pilot descended 200 feet below the glide path during a night visual approach after disconnecting the autopilot, triggering a single 'Caution Terrain' alert due to rising terrain. The crew continued the approach and landed, though the pilot acknowledged failing to execute a required go-around upon receiving the caution.

synopsis: Airbus 320 flight crew reported a NMAC during descent, and descending to comply with an TCAS RA.
summary: While being vectored for a visual approach to runway 11 at 2000 MSL, the crew received a TCAS descent resolution advisory due to a Cessna 172 at 1800 MSL. The pilots disconnected the autopilot and descended to 1400 MSL, passing 300 feet below the traffic before climbing back to 1800 MSL and completing a normal landing.

synopsis: Boeing 777 flight crew reported after selecting 'Econ Cruise;' the Flight Management Computer blanked and recomputed the ETA and fuel, followed by the autopilot commencing an uncommanded right turn.
summary: The captain and first officer experienced an uncommanded right turn during cruise after selecting Economy speed near a waypoint, causing the FMC to blank and recompute. The crew manually corrected the deviation of less than 2 nm, suspecting the FMC update violated a bulletin warning against lateral or vertical changes within 4 nm of a waypoint.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported his aircraft as well as others on approach to ORD received TCAS RAs for traffic which was not reported by ATC.
summary: The flight crew executed a TCAS avoidance maneuver during descent near 9,000 feet after receiving a Resolution Advisory. The controller failed to warn descending aircraft of the conflict, stating the threat was at 8,500 feet, while other aircraft also performed maneuvers on the approach frequency.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that as they started a descent, as per ATC instructions, then received a TCAS alert of traffic below.
summary: During the BENKY4 arrival at 9000 FT, the crew held altitude after a TCAS TA indicated traffic at 8500 FT, despite an ATC clearance to descend to 8000 FT. A single-engine Cessna passed 500 FT below, triggering a TCAS RA, which ATC later attributed to a station aircraft maneuvering in the area.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported dual FMS, Flight Director, and autopilot failures during the initial climb.
summary: During climb from 11,000 ft, dual FMC and Flight Director failures occurred while the First Officer was flying. The crew returned to ZZZ, received ILS vectors, and landed uneventfully using ROSE mode after losing autopilots.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported mistakenly taking off with flaps set at two instead of the computed requirement of flaps four.
summary: The flight crew missed the required Flaps 4 setting during the after-start checklist, selecting Flaps 2 instead due to rushing and habit. Although the aircraft rotated safely, the crew noticed abnormal speed indications after takeoff and confirmed the incorrect flap configuration via the takeoff data page.

synopsis: A pilot reported, twice, recently they were on a departure and had to take evasive action to avoid adjacent airport traffic that ATC did not advise them about.
summary: A pilot departing under IFR clearance to 11,000 feet maneuvered right to avoid a descending single-engine aircraft at 2,000 feet after ATC failed to issue traffic alerts. The pilot attributed the near collision to a lack of radar at the tower and insufficient traffic monitoring by Center.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported that a log book entry may have been signed as accomplished when the work was not done.
summary: A pilot reported that maintenance personnel falsified aircraft records by signing off a forward lav door hinge repair that was never performed, likely due to supervisory pressure. The discrepancy was discovered when the pilot compared original logbook photos with altered entries showing a completed lubrication and permanent repair.

synopsis: A Socata Pilot reported that when he entered into an uncontrolled airport traffic pattern he did not have the correct frequency dialed into the radio causing a near miss.
summary: A pilot on final approach for a full stop landing on runway 19 encountered an aircraft taking off in the opposite direction due to dialing the incorrect CTAF frequency. Both pilots maneuvered to avoid a collision, passing approximately 100 feet vertically and 300 feet horizontally apart with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain reported on departure from AVQ they were given an immediate turn for parachute activity at MZJ on check in with U90 Controller. This was not listed in NOTAMS or mentioned when the pilot called to obtain a departure frequency and squawk code.
summary: A flight instructor departing Marana VFR received unexpected vectors from Tucson Approach for parachute activity at Pinal Airpark (MZJ) despite no NOTAMs in their briefing. The pilot attributed the conflict to uncoordinated jump operations near a busy nontowered airport and recommended evaluating the safety of the MZJ jump zone.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported an electrical failure and loss of radio and transponder on a flight through Class Bravo airspace. He elected to divert to a nontowered airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a total radio and transponder failure while approaching ZZZ1 airspace at 3,500 feet. After setting transponder code 7600 with no response, the pilot descended to 1,500 feet, contacted the tower via cell phone, and landed at ZZZ2 for repairs.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported a NMAC with a drone while on a visual approach to CMA at 4000 ft.
summary: A VFR pilot approaching CMA at 4,000 feet reported a near miss with a small, unidentified orange object while turning for Runway 26. The pilot suspected the object was a drone but did not notify ATC due to workload, noting no traffic advisory was issued.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: NCT TRACON Controller reported an aircraft turned early on the SJC2 SID and into confliction with a previous departure.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X on the SJC2 departure turned early inside an established southeast-bound track, requiring a vector to heading 100 and a descent to 4,000 feet to maintain separation. The controller attributed the error to pilot confusion with complex procedures and criticized SJC Tower for releasing aircraft without ensuring deconfliction prior to frequency transfer.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Center Controllers reported the Traffic Management Unit failed to take any action during a period of known weather obstructions causing their sectors and workload to be unmanageable.
summary: An air traffic controller at MSP reported that uncoordinated weather deviations and a lack of Traffic Management Unit planning forced trainees to manage two inbound streams without support. The controller recommended that the Command Center must provide a plan rather than leaving sectors to handle the situation alone.

synopsis: A Tower and TRACON Controller reported an aircraft on a visual approach climbed unexpectedly which put it into confliction with departing traffic.
summary: Aircraft X climbed from 2,500 to 3,000 feet after being cleared for a visual approach, creating a 1,000-foot and 3-mile separation loss with Aircraft Y at 3,500 feet. The controller attributed the event to the pilot's error or autopilot malfunction, noting the pilot incorrectly believed climbing was permitted on a visual approach.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a confusing depiction on the JAX airport diagram. The west ramp taxi line ends at the normal left edge marking for Taxiway J.
summary: A pilot taxiing from Gate to Runway 26 via ramp, H, B, and C encountered a discontinuous taxi line south of the ARP between Papa and Juliet. The pilot noted the gap was visible in daylight but requested JAX Airport paint a continuous line to prevent issues during restricted visibility or night operations.

synopsis: Large Transport Captain reported the signage and some of the taxiways at SFO did not match the Jeppesen chart.
summary: Pilots reported a discrepancy between the SFO 10-9 airport diagram and actual taxiway signage during taxi operations. The charted taxiway 'B1' was signed as 'Q', and 'Q1' was unmarked, prompting a request to verify that diagram labels match physical signs.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported encountering multiple bird strikes shortly after takeoff from SFO resulting in spurious flight instrument indications. After dumping fuel, a return to the departure airport was safely accomplished.
summary: The flight crew struck a flock of geese at 800 feet after takeoff, causing airspeed discrepancies, windshear alerts, and flight director failures. The crew executed the unreliable airspeed checklist, dumped fuel to reduce weight, and returned safely to SFO.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported after landing on Runway 9 at MYNN, they exited at Taxiway B and crossed the hold line for Runway 14 while trying to determine if they were clear of Runway 9.
summary: The Captain reported that while taxiing a large jet on Taxiway Bravo at Nassau after landing on Runway 9, the crew overshot the hold short line for Runway 14 due to the lines being only 50 feet apart. The aircraft stopped before entering the active runway, but the pilot identified the short taxiway and nonstandard markings as a safety hazard requiring chart updates.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported taking corrective action after the Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System was triggered due to a non-standard departure.
summary: The pilot departed MMGL on a non-standard heading due to military activity, triggering a single EGPWS terrain warning above 7,000 ft. The crew disengaged autopilot and increased climb rate, attributing the alert to a delayed turn by Departure Control that kept the aircraft near high terrain longer than the published procedure would have.

synopsis: A 747-400 flight crew reported a failure of the #1 engine during climb out. The engine was secured and a heavyweight landing was successfully accomplished at the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced an engine #1 surge and yaw near ZZZZZ Intersection at 3000 feet, leveling off at 6000 feet to complete checklists. They landed overweight to save fuel, but post-flight inspection revealed melted tire fuse plugs and deflated tires following a brake temperature warning.

synopsis: A Boeing 777-200 Captain reported receiving a RAAS (Runway Awareness and Advisory System) alert for short runway takeoff.
summary: The pilot performed a 180-degree turn on a 148-foot wide runway for takeoff after receiving back-taxi instructions, triggering a short runway RAAS alert. The crew later identified that the taxi chart failed to depict the turnaround and the runway was too narrow for the maneuver, which the pilot admitted should have prompted an inquiry to ATC.

synopsis: A Widebody Transport First Officer reported that during a back-taxi on the takeoff runway it was not clear where to make the 180 turn.
summary: The crew back-taxied and turned 180 on the runway due to closures, triggering a 'Short Runway' warning near 80 knots because Jeppesen charts obscured a pre-threshold taxi circle. They continued the takeoff, citing unclear chart details and language barriers with controllers as contributing factors.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning on a visual approach at dusk to AVL airport.
summary: The pilot flying received a ground proximity warning while intercepting the ILS localizer from the south at UMUXE during a visual approach to Asheville Runway 35. The crew leveled off immediately, and the reporter attributed the warning to a rushed descent and insufficient briefing of the approach plate.

synopsis: A Boeing 737 Captain and a Dispatcher reported that it was discovered after takeoff that the weight manifest included 2000 pounds of cargo that was not loaded.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X departing ZZZ received a post-takeoff weight manifest showing a 2,018 lb decrease due to mail listed but not loaded. Dispatch noted the error, though it remains unknown if the change affected the aircraft's center of gravity or trim settings.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported several crew memebers experienced headaches and nausea from a rotten egg/sulphurous smell on the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew and a flight attendant experienced a suspected fume event with sulphur smells and symptoms like headaches during climbout and cruise while circumnavigating weather. After landing, EMTs found two crew members had high blood pressure, leading the pilots and one flight attendant to decline further duty.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported that a self-induced FMC position error was the likely cause of a false GPWS Terrain Warning and track deviation after takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a false terrain warning and navigation discrepancy during takeoff due to an incorrect FMC position update caused by operator error. The crew identified degraded IRS status, requested radar vectors from ATC, and continued the flight tracking VORs.

synopsis: Maintenance reported that 'unserviceable' tags were removed from several tow bars and, the tow bars were put back into service without being repaired.
summary: A mechanic discovered an E-190 tow bar and two others in the hangar and at the gate incorrectly fitted with AN bolts instead of shear pins. Although tagged out, the tags were removed without repairs due to vendor understaffing, language barriers, and lack of parts, creating a risk of aircraft damage or injury.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain reported a deviation on the HAYEZ FIVE departure from VNY due to the First Officer reprogramming the SID and manually deleting two fixes necessary for the departure.
summary: During an IFR departure from VNY, the first officer manually deleted two upcoming fixes from the FMS while the pilot flying monitored the Garmin 750, causing a missed turn. The controller issued vectors after the error, and the crew attributed the incident to the first officer's confusion over duplicate fixes and a breakdown in communication.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 pilot reported that while flying downwind for landing an RV8 pilot flew into the pattern without communicating his position or intentions causing a near miss.
summary: The pilot and student in Aircraft X nearly collided with Aircraft Y on the downwind leg for Runway 36 at ZZZ. The incident occurred because Aircraft Y entered the pattern without prior calls and turned less than 100 feet below and left of Aircraft X, requiring the pilot to take control to maintain separation.

synopsis: PA-28 Student Pilot reported a NMAC with a Beechcraft in the vicinity of a non-towered airport.
summary: A student pilot and instructor experienced a near mid-air collision with a Beechcraft during the landing phase, with less than 100 feet of vertical clearance. The instructor took evasive action after a radio warning, and the other pilot was identified as negligent but reportedly protected due to their official status.

synopsis: Corporate Jet First Officer reported while taxiing out at PBI a GA aircraft flew over their aircraft that had departed from the short parallel runway.
summary: While taxiing at PBI, the crew observed an aircraft taking off from a parallel runway and passing over them at less than 100 feet. The pilot attributed the near-miss to compromised tower-ground coordination and the airport's layout, where a short runway departs over active taxiways.

synopsis: A Cessna 182 Pilot and a Cessna 152 Pilot reported a near miss on final approach due to ATC miscommunication.
summary: Two Cessna pilots experienced a near-midair conflict on final approach to Runway XXR when Tower lost track of sequencing due to confusion between two separate tower frequencies for parallel runways. The lead pilot diverted left while the second pilot executed a go-around after Tower instructed them to climb, resolving the incident without damage.

synopsis: CE650 Captain reported a loss of all pitot-static instruments during cruise.
summary: The crew experienced a slow degradation of both pitot static systems during cruise over the ocean, causing autopilot anomalies. They descended out of RVSM altitudes using pitch, power, and an iPad with Stratus S2, regaining instrument functionality near FL220 before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: LJ31 flight crew reported encountering clear air turbulence and loss of aircraft control at FL450 with an altitude loss of 800 feet.
summary: During cruise at 45,000 feet, the aircraft encountered clear air turbulence causing uncontrollable pitch, roll, and an 800-foot altitude loss. The crew regained control at 44,200 feet, notified ATC, and descended to 41,000 feet with no damage or passengers on board.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported diverting due to System A hydraulic failure.
summary: The crew experienced a System A hydraulic leak caused by a bird strike in the nose wheel well, leading to a nose gear extension failure and low fluid levels. They diverted to ZZZ, manually extended the gear, and landed safely with fire services standing by.

synopsis: The flight crew of a Boeing 737 reported that during push-back an adjacent aircraft was also being pushed-back and the winglets may have touched.
summary: The flight crew and ground operations personnel experienced a near-mid-air winglet contact during pushback due to a runway change, obscured visibility, and non-standard marshalling signals. Although initial reports indicated a touch, subsequent inspections confirmed no damage occurred on either aircraft.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that inoperative stall warning systems noted during preflight were due to disconnected stick shaker cannon plugs.
summary: Pilots discovered both stall warning systems failed to test during preflight, causing a one-hour delay. Maintenance found the cannon plugs disconnected from both stick shakers, a condition that disabled the warning system until the plugs were reconnected and tested normally.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported the automated system was down and the manual weight and balance provided was 14,000 pounds less than the actual weight.
summary: The flight crew and an agent manually entered weight and balance data after a system lockout, but the agent incorrectly placed non-standard passenger values. This error caused the aircraft to be approximately 14,000 pounds heavier than calculated, resulting in dangerously low landing speeds that were corrected mid-flight.

synopsis: Air carrier flight Crew reported a track deviation due to confusion with the departure clearance delivery format.
summary: Pilots departing Melbourne on Runway 16 misinterpreted a clearance for the Bison 5 departure as the Dosel 9 SID due to phrasing and accent issues. This confusion caused crews to fly the wrong procedure, resulting in pilot deviations and a controller issuing a corrective heading after passing the ALBAK waypoint.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported they began to taxi before the tow bar was disconnected.
summary: The flight crew attempted to taxi with the tug still attached after failing to receive confirmation of disconnection from the single tug driver. The resulting shudder caused an immediate stop, a nose gear inspection, and a return to the gate before the flight continued.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported sighting 2 UAVs while conducting an approach at LGA. The event was reported to ATC, however no evasive action was taken.
summary: The crew encountered two drones 500–1,000 feet below and half a mile right while approaching Runway 22 at La Guardia near GREKO. They maintained visual contact, required no evasive action, and reported the incident to ATC after landing.

synopsis: B767 Flight Attendant reported having a conversation with the Captain regarding the use of the fasten seatbelt sign throughout the entire flight.
summary: A flight attendant discussed seat belt sign usage with the captain during a preflight briefing, warning that leaving it on continuously removes advanced turbulence warnings and violates FAR 121.311. The captain initially resisted but agreed to cycle the sign as needed during the flight, acknowledging the safety risks.

synopsis: B767 Flight Attendant reported concern with other flight attendants lack of knowledge of the flight deck emergency call function on the interphone.
summary: The pilot briefed six flight attendants on using the aircraft's B777-style interphone to place emergency calls by dialing 4 instead of pressing an Alert button. Only one attendant knew the procedure, prompting a request for a demonstration and a recommendation to add this task to future recurrent training modules.

aircraft: Commander Prop Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MWH Tower Controller in Charge reported he observed the Local Controllers using an unsafe procedure for arriving aircraft to intersecting runways.
summary: The Tower Radar Controller observed Local 1 and Local 2 controllers simultaneously authorizing unrestricted landings on Runway 4 and Runway 32R without coordinating control of the midfield intersection. The reporter identified this as a safety issue where two controllers owned the same runway portion, creating a risk of conflict due to unclear transfer of intersection authority.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: CRQ Tower Controller reported an aircraft they cleared for takeoff was at the opposite end of the runway then they thought it was with traffic opposite direction on short final.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a departure clearance to Aircraft X while distracted by extreme heat and five extra personnel in the tower cab. The pilot reported being on Runway 06 instead of the cleared Runway 24, requiring a cancellation and exit, which the controller attributed to the unsafe working conditions.

synopsis: PWM TRACON Controller reported he observed a NMAC reported by an aircraft with an unidentified VFR target during a partial radar outage.
summary: A flight data specialist reported that high workload and degraded radar performance in multimode likely prevented a controller from issuing a traffic advisory, leading a regional jet to maneuver to avoid a VFR aircraft. The incident was attributed to poor communication regarding equipment status, which increased controller workload and reduced situational awareness.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported a main gear tire shredded on takeoff.
summary: The crew discovered a shredded number 2 main gear tire on departure from ZZZ after ATC notification during cruise. They returned to ZZZ1, landed safely with minimal braking, and deplaned passengers via airstairs after CFR inspection confirmed no fire or excessive heat.

synopsis: B757 Gate Agent reported the aircraft made contact with the jetway when the aircraft was marshalled to the incorrect parking line by the ground crew.
summary: A ground handler reported a Boeing 757 misparked on a 777-300 line, causing the second door to pass the Jetway. Although the handler and flight crew initially believed no contact occurred, a Customer Service supervisor later confirmed the aircraft had struck the Jetway.

synopsis: ERJ-175 Captain reported the aircraft was ferried after having been painted. Days later, panels were found painted shut.
summary: The captain and first officer accepted an aircraft for flight to ZZZ after maintenance and maintenance control deemed painted-over seals airworthy, despite the crew's concerns. Four days later, another flight discovered hydraulic panels painted shut, likely because wet paint dried before the crew could verify panel operation.

synopsis: CE-680A flight crew reported overshooting an altitude restriction departing TEB when they were distracted by a wake turbulence encounter.
summary: The pilot experienced a wake turbulence upset below 1500 MSL while departing TEB on the RUUDY6 departure, triggering a Traffic Advisory and dislodging their headset. Although the pilot feared a door was ajar, the aircraft was later found sound, and ATC noted the crew had not read the departure clearance.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported encountering convective activity with an altitude gain of 300 feet at level off and communication issues between the crew members.
summary: During cruise at FL350, the crew encountered moderate turbulence while climbing to FL370 to avoid weather, causing the First Officer to disconnect automation without a callout and resulting in a 300-foot altitude overshoot. No injuries occurred, but the pilot reported the incident to emphasize the need for automation callouts and earlier weather avoidance clearances.

synopsis: C402 pilot reported a fire in the overhead electrical panel that extinguished on final approach to a divert field.
summary: The First Officer experienced an electrical fire in the overhead panel while at 5,000 ft on downwind after activating the Captain's light switch. The crew declared an emergency, diverted, and evacuated the aircraft after the fire self-extinguished on final approach.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported an aborted takeoff due to an airspeed anomaly. After Maintenance addressed the issue, a subsequent takeoff was successful, however the problem returned once airborne and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer experienced airspeed indicator failure during two takeoff attempts due to pitot tube debris, which maintenance cleared using an unapproved method. The aircraft returned to the gate after airborne airspeed disagreement and system lockouts, prompting the reporter to criticize the maintenance organization's lackadaisical handling of the critical fault.

synopsis: Learjet 35 Captain reported they lost all hydraulic pressure on initial descent.
summary: The flight crew experienced a total loss of hydraulic pressure on short final, triggering a go-around and diversion to ZZZ. They restored pressure using the auxiliary pump to land safely, later discovering a hydraulic leak in the right main gear-well.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported the aileron control lacked feel and resistance.
summary: The flight crew detected a lack of resistance in both ailerons during a pre-flight check. After resetting ELAC 1 and 2 failed to resolve the issue, maintenance found worn rods below the joysticks, leading to the aircraft being grounded as unairworthy.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported that a caterer attempted to open the galley service door prior to being cleared to do so.
summary: A caterer returned to the forward right door and attempted to open it without waiting for the "All clear" signal. A Flight Attendant disarmed the door, preventing a slide deployment caused by the caterer's failure to follow procedures.

synopsis: B747 Captain reported they had a rapid loss of a large amount of fuel within a 30 minute period.
summary: The flight crew experienced a sudden fuel imbalance between Main Tanks 1 and 4 shortly before top of descent, suspecting an insidious leak in Tank 1. They managed the situation by monitoring fuel and closing cross-feed valves, landing safely but with 5.7 tons below planned arrival fuel.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reported that they descended early for the FAF and received an EGPWS terrain alert.
summary: The pilot and first officer flying a night visual approach into AVL received an EGPWS terrain alert after descending to FAF altitude too early due to the pilot misinterpreting the approach chart. They disconnected the autopilot, climbed until the alert ceased, and continued the approach with terrain and the airport in sight.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a near mid air collision with another Cessna in the vicinity of U14.
summary: A pilot descending through 11,500 ft to 9,500 ft near Nephi Airport encountered a Cessna at the same altitude due to a continuous radio transmission blocking CTAF communications. The pilot executed an aggressive right turn to avoid a near mid-air collision, resulting in approximately 500 ft horizontal and 50 ft vertical separation.

synopsis: A Beach Bonanza pilot reported that he lost situational awareness when he entered a cloud.
summary: The pilot lost situational awareness and directional control while entering a cloud on a 320 heading, inadvertently turning westbound. Poor instrument technique and emotional distraction caused the pilot to ignore ATC vectors and fly direct to an intersection until queried.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Skydiving pilot and TRACON Controller reported an aircraft was permitted to fly through the skydiving operation active jump zone.
summary: A skydiver reported an unexpected airliner climbing through the drop zone at 13,500 feet during final approach, noting ATC provided no alert. Separately, a controller described a VFR aircraft nearly colliding with a commuter jet due to high workload and insufficient staffing to open a relief sector.

synopsis: Cessna 182 pilot reported a sudden loss of engine power immediately after takeoff. He landed straight ahead on the departure runway and taxied uneventfully to the ramp.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna experienced an uncommanded power reduction at 20 ft AGL during takeoff at ZZZ. The pilot landed straight ahead, exited the runway, and taxied to maintenance under engine power for inspection.

synopsis: A pilot reported the Approach Controller became agitated when the pilot asked why a change in altitude was necessary during cruise.
summary: The pilot flying a general aviation aircraft encountered a conflict with Greer Approach controllers regarding a descent clearance to 9,000 feet. The controller became irate when questioned, claimed absolute authority, and the pilot eventually complied after repeated demands while asserting the right to question clearances.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported that while on final a Cessna 172 turned base to final below him.
summary: During landing practice, a Cessna 172 approached the reporter on base and turned final below their altitude. The reporter exited the pattern to the right to avoid conflict, citing a lack of communication as the primary cause.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported that when he put the gear down he did not get green down light. The gear collapsed on landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear malfunction during a VFR ferry flight due to undetected low hydraulic fluid caused by a stained sight gauge. Despite emergency extension attempts, the gear failed upon landing in a crosswind, causing the aircraft to slide off the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A Tower Controller reported they observed an unidentified aircraft not in communication joined short final to their airport than broke off their approach and departed the airspace.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers noticed Aircraft X squawking 1200 entering Class Charlie airspace and attempting a wrong airport approach. The pilot ignored light gun signals, went around, and landed at the correct airport (FIN) where he ran out of fuel due to confusion.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported vectoring an aircraft off their approach to avoid unidentified VFR traffic lost required spacing with the arriving in trail traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller instructed Aircraft X to climb to 4,500 feet to avoid VFR traffic, causing it to cross the path of trailing Aircraft Y at 5,000 feet. The controller noted that Aircraft X may have penetrated Niles airspace during recovery and admitted a better option was to turn north and climb.

synopsis: A Tower Local Controller reported an aircraft initiating a go-around was in confliction with a helicopter transitioning the airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a single runway with a closed north side faced a conflict when a jet executed a go-around while a helicopter transitioned at 1,500 feet. The controller deconflicted the jet by stopping its climb at 1,100 feet and recommended prohibiting VFR helicopter transitions near runways to prevent unsafe mixing with jets.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported simultaneous, multiple communication and navigation equipment failures. The flight was able to continue to the destination airport where it was discovered that a liquid spill had caused the failures.
summary: The flight crew experienced simultaneous failures of both transponders, VHF NAV switches, and the number 2 COMM shortly after liftoff. Maintenance later discovered liquid spillage on the center pedestal as the cause, though the crew reported no prior spill.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the aircraft rolled onto the towbar trapping it under the nose wheels when the Captain released the brakes before notifying the Tug Driver after the pushback.
summary: The Captain released the parking brake during a pushback hold at the top of the alley, causing the aircraft to roll forward and crush the towbar under the nose gear. The incident occurred because the Guide Agent prematurely released the towbar lock while the Tug Driver was not ready, a failure the Captain attributed to incomplete communication.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported missing a crossing restriction on climbout from LAX citing VNAV performance and a wake turbulence encounter as contributing.
summary: The pilot missed a 13,000-foot climb restriction at KEGGS while in VNAV ECON climb due to prioritizing 320 KIAS over altitude and encountering wake turbulence from a preceding B777. After disconnecting the autopilot and reducing speed to 280 KIAS, the aircraft recovered to meet the next restriction at COOPP.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer expressed concern that luggage with a built-in Lithium-Ion battery should not be loaded with checked baggage.
summary: A cabin crew member stopped a ramp agent from loading a suitcase with a hidden lithium-ion battery into the cargo hold during preflight. The item was moved to the cabin after the passenger failed to remove the battery per IATA regulations, preventing a potential safety hazard.

synopsis: The Captain of an Embraer 175 reported going around after receiving a GPWS warning to pull-up during initial approach.
summary: The flight crew conducting a visual approach to Runway XXR in Day VFR conditions received a GPWS 'Pull Up' warning, likely triggered by cell towers on a nearby mountain. They executed an escape maneuver, leveled off at 8000 ft, and successfully completed a second approach after logging the thrust lever event.

synopsis: Bombardier CRJ flight crew reported that during climb the plane began to make small unusual movements the right engine instrument gauges (N1, ITT, N2) all disappeared and were replaced by yellow dashes.
summary: The crew experienced a right engine FADEC failure at FL245, causing instrument loss and an oil warning before the engine relit. They returned to the airport for a normal landing, attributing the event to a faulty FADEC and suggesting maintenance should not dispatch with dual FADEC faults.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported that contract ramp personnel are not properly trained regarding aircraft handling procedures.
summary: The flight crew reported that untrained ground personnel at a startup station used improper phraseology, pushed the aircraft the wrong direction three times, and failed to display the pin or verify clearance before walking away. This lack of training and ambiguous communication created a hazardous environment where the crew could not confirm the area was clear before taxiing.

synopsis: PC-12 pilot reported an airborne conflict with a light aircraft shortly after takeoff from BJC.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss during IFR departure from BJC 12L when an inbound Mooney crossed their flight path less than 1 nm from the runway. The pilot attributed the minimal separation to potential tower positional awareness issues or the inbound aircraft heading to the wrong runway, noting a 30-60 second delay would have prevented the conflict.

synopsis: A single engine Cessna pilot reported the loss of engine power due to fuel crossfeed mismanagement. While descending to accomplish a landing, he successfully reconfigured the fuel system, restarted the engine, and continued on to his destination.
summary: The pilot forgot to switch fuel tanks on a 4.3-hour flight, causing the left tank to run dry and the engine to lose power at 4.0 hours. After losing 2,500 feet, the pilot switched to the right tank, restarted the engine, and continued to the destination.

synopsis: Cessna 210 pilot reported task saturation, losing situational awareness, deviating from course, and asking for assistance after the Controller asked why he had made a turn. The Controller provided assistance and the flight then proceeded normally.
summary: A single-pilot IFR flight in an aircraft with a Garmin 480 and Aspen PFD lost situational awareness while transitioning from GPS to VOR navigation near Penn Cove. Task saturation caused the pilot to program the wrong course and heading, requiring ATC intervention to correct the deviation and complete the flight safely.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported continuing to fly the aircraft following a practice soft field takeoff that resulted in some damage related to ground contact.
summary: A student pilot and instructor conducting a soft field takeoff in a single-engine aircraft with a passenger and full tanks experienced a high pitch attitude, runway excursion, and wingtip strike due to excessive back pressure and CG shift. They continued flying multiple legs unaware of the damage until a post-flight inspection revealed the tail skid plate drag and wingtip impact.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported that procedures for an ECAM 'NAV LS TUNING DISAGREE' warning could not be found in the QRH. Captain questioned what other ECAM warnings are not covered in the QRH.
summary: The crew discovered the Captain's STBY NAV switch was on after hangar departure, leading to a deferred CAT 2 inoperative message and an in-flight 'NAV LS TUNING DISAGREE' ECAM. Cycling both STBY NAV switches cleared the warnings, revealing the aircraft incorrectly retained the standby mode despite the switch appearing normal.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported an encounter with light wake turbulence on arrival into LAX in trail of a heavy aircraft.
summary: The crew experienced a light wake turbulence encounter from a preceding heavy aircraft during arrival at LAX. The event caused a single roll of 15 degrees or less.

synopsis: Air carrier personnel reported a small child almost fell through the gap between the jet bridge and the aircraft.
summary: During deplaning, a toddler almost fell through an 8'x12' floor opening on the aircraft's right outboard side. The reporter attributes the hazard to a modified bumper at the bridge connection point.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported landing safely after shutting down the left engine following a low oil pressure message and high ITT.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a left engine oil pressure warning and high ITT at 11,000 feet while descending in icing and turbulence. The crew executed an intentional engine shutdown, descended to 4,000 feet to avoid weather, and landed safely on one engine with fire trucks standing by.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported refusing to accept an aircraft after experiencing autoflight display anomalies that had occurred at least twice in the recent past.
summary: The Captain reported intermittent blanking of flight instruments and fuel displays during climb and descent due to a suspected Display Electronics Unit (DEU) fault. Despite maintenance replacing and resetting the DEU with normal test results, the Captain refused the aircraft for the next leg because the recurring issue remained unresolved.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported he was unable to clear the runway as the left brake had locked up during landing roll.
summary: A flight instructor landed a training aircraft in strong crosswinds and discovered a left brake failure while attempting to vacate the runway. The pilot used the elevator as an air brake to stop on a taxiway edge, causing a 15-minute runway closure until the aircraft was manually pushed clear.

synopsis: Phantom Pro 4 UAV Operator reported a collision with a tree during climb.
summary: The pilot flew a DJI Inspire drone into a tree due to misjudging proximity to the obstacle. The incident resulted in damage to the onboard camera and a rotor blade.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported continuing flight to the destination after experiencing shudder during flap extension where no damage was found. Upon landing after the subsequent flight they found that the left flap extend/retract rod had failed.
summary: The flight crew experienced repeated shudders and a loud bang from the left wing during flap extension and retraction on two flights, with no CAS messages or control issues. Post-landing inspection revealed a snapped left flap center extension/retraction rod, resulting in the aircraft being grounded.

synopsis: SR22 Pilot initiated a climb prior to receiving ATC approval in an attempt to avoid icing conditions.
summary: The pilot, flying an aircraft not approved for known icing at 10,000 ft, encountered moderate rime ice after delaying anti-icing activation while awaiting ATC clearance. The reporter attributed the incident to ATC's failure to acknowledge the emergency and their confrontational responses to requests for an immediate altitude change.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA flight instructor reported another aircraft entered the runway without CTAF announcement, causing a ground conflict.
summary: The pilot cancelled IFR and entered the visual pattern for Runway 3R7, but another aircraft holding short of Runway 26 entered for takeoff without a radio call. The pilot executed a go-around to the right while the other aircraft continued its takeoff, and the pilot subsequently landed after re-entering the pattern.

synopsis: CL30 First Officer reported that an emergency gear extension procedure was used due to a hydraulic pump failure. Landing and taxi were uneventful.
summary: During an ILS approach to ZZZ, the crew experienced a left hydraulic system failure causing a gear unsafe indication and initiated a go-around. After successfully extending the gear via the emergency checklist, they completed a normal landing with full nose-wheel steering despite the left hydraulic reservoir showing zero quantity.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: SRQ Tower Controller reported they cleared an aircraft for takeoff while an aircraft was landing on an intersecting runway.
summary: The controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff from Runway 04 while Aircraft Y was landing on Runway 14, causing Y to stop short of the intersection. The controller attributed the incident to distraction and failure to issue land and hold short instructions, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported his vectors for traffic were too late and insufficient to avoid a NMAC between their aircraft and an unidentified VFR track.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a near-midair conflict between IFR Aircraft X descending to 3000 feet and VFR Aircraft Y climbing through 2500 feet. The controller attributed the close call at 3600 feet to delayed vectoring instructions, slow turn compliance, and a failure to prioritize altitude separation over lateral vectors.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported a neigboring Center Sector allowed an aircraft to fly through a corner of their airspace without coordination and then observed the same Sector handoff two aircraft on converging headings at the same altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X climbed into their sector without a pointout, followed by a handoff of two aircraft at 35,000 feet that crossed with only 5.1 miles separation. The controller attributed the close proximity to the adjacent sector's lack of coordination and the climbing aircraft's speed increase upon leveling.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported he misidentified an aircraft when the plane did not use their call sign when responding to instructions.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft Y for a descent while mistakenly believing Aircraft X was requesting a diversion due to omitted callsigns. The controller later realized Aircraft X had read back the clearance, attributing the confusion to high workload and emergency stress.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported the Approach Control descended an aircraft to a different altitude than what was coordinated which placed the aircraft below the Minimum Safe Altitude.
summary: A controller reported that Approach ATC disregarded coordinated 5000-foot instructions and assigned a Cessna 185 to 4100 feet, causing the NORDO aircraft to fly below the 4800-foot MSA for 10 minutes. Canadian ATC eventually relayed a climb instruction to restore safe altitude after Approach failed to coordinate the change.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported they overshot final approach course at LAX when the autopilot failed to capture the localizer. Wake turbulence was also cited as contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence while capturing the Localizer for LAX 24L at 2,200 feet, causing the autopilot to fail to align. The First Officer manually disengaged the autopilot and banked 30 degrees to avoid the 25R approach area, resulting in a safe landing and a subsequent Pilot Deviation inquiry.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported that when returning to the gate at SAN to remove a pitot cover, they encountered difficulty finding Delta Taxiway in the fog due to lack of signage and a lead-in line when coming off Runway 27.
summary: The crew returned to the gate after an aircraft behind reported a streamer, caused by a missed left elevator feel pitot cover despite MRD records. During the foggy return taxi, the pilot misjudged a 140-degree turn at intersection D due to poor visibility and lack of signage, requiring Airport Operations assistance to complete the maneuver.

synopsis: Air Carrier Crew reported a NMAC on approach to SFO runway 28L with an airliner on visual approach to runway 28R.
summary: The flight crew, cleared to intercept 28L final, experienced a TCAS RA due to a 737 on 28R that was not visually acquired until the conflict resolved. The crew initiated a go-around after the vertical separation decreased to 100 feet, attributing the safe outcome to the TCAS alert.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported they failed to make a crossing restriction on arrival into SFO. Fatigue and distraction from a wake turbulence encounter were cited as contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew descended via DYAMD3 to RWY 28R but failed to verify FMC legs due to fatigue, resulting in an incorrect altitude constraint at FLOWZ. NORCAL queried the descent, leading to radar vectors to correct the altitude, though the crew could not identify the exact cause of the error.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported a rejected takeoff due to no airspeed indication, after failing to ensure the pitot covers were removed during preflight.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff due to no airspeed indication caused by installed pitot covers, which he noticed but failed to have removed before completing the preflight. The pilot attributed the error to distraction during a maintenance discussion and noted that RTO braking did not engage during the low-speed rejection.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that his company attempted to have them fly to an airport which was in close proximity to the ash cloud of an active volcano in violation of the Flight Operations Manual.
summary: Dispatch instructed the crew to fly to ZZZZ1 at night despite volcanic ash and company policy violations. The crew delayed departure for over 12 hours on the second night to verify management's intent to ignore safety rules regarding the ash cloud.

synopsis: A Boeing 767 Captain reported that they returned to the gate because the Right Hand side did not have duct pressure, which started a chain of events prior to takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple delays and system failures, including over-fueling, pack pressure loss, and an APU failure, before manually landing right of centerline due to fatigue and wind. The pilot attributed the manual landing decision to unexpected lateral drift and noted that operational stress from repeated aircraft defects contributed to the challenging environment.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence departing DTW in trail of an A321.
summary: During initial climb, the pilot experienced a hard right roll exceeding 30 degrees bank caused by wake turbulence from a preceding A321. After leveling the wings and maintaining maximum climb, ATC issued a right turn to exit the route, after which no further roll issues occurred.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a rejected takeoff after hearing the Tower Controller broadcast STOP STOP STOP without a call sign.
summary: The flight crew aborted a low-speed takeoff on Runway 27 at CVG after hearing an unaddressed "STOP" announcement from Tower. The crew cleared the runway and received approval to depart from operations control, attributing the abort to the ambiguous ATC instruction rather than a call sign confusion.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported a heading problem with the AHRS system on climb out after a night departure.
summary: Pilots departing LGA Runway 13 experienced AHRS heading indicator malfunctions and EFIS COMP MON cautions during climbout when switching from DG to MAG mode. The crew relied on standby compasses and ATC headings until leveling off, allowing them to realign the system and resume normal navigation.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported miscommunication resulting in several Flight Attendants still standing during takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported that three flight attendants stood during takeoff despite an automated cabin announcement, citing conflicting excuses including poor time management and intentional policy violation. The pilot concluded the crew's actions intentionally violated safety protocols and risked injury.

synopsis: CRJ900 First Officer reported a rejected takeoff due to incorrect flap setting.
summary: The crew performed a rejected takeoff at 50 kts due to an aural flap misconfiguration warning. After exiting the runway and resetting flaps from position 1 to 8, maintenance was called, and the flight continued 15 minutes later.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported missing the proper taxi route to runway 19 at DCA due to signage and darkness.
summary: The crew missed Taxiway Kilo while taxiing on Runway 15 at night due to unclear markings and chart discrepancies. A startled Captain attempted a sharp turn, nearly striking edge lights, but the aircraft was safely maneuvered back onto the runway with no damage.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Regional Jet Captain reported responding to a TCAS RA climb command while descending into ORD when a Citation climbing VFR triggered the conflict alert.
summary: During the WATSN 3 arrival into ORD, a crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory while a Citation climbed through their 12,000' altitude under visual separation. The crew climbed to 12,900' per TCAS instructions because the Citation's heading made relative motion difficult to judge, despite ATC stating the Citation had clearance to climb.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they flew the wrong PHX SID due to confusion between the name of the SID and the name of a fix utilized in other PHX SIDs.
summary: The pilot programmed the wrong SID during cockpit preparation after being distracted by a passenger issue. The error was identified shortly after takeoff, and the pilot attributed the mistake to a SID title sharing a fix name with another procedure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain questioned the safety of implementing Wake Turbulence Recategorization separation standards at JFK and other major airports.
summary: The Pilot in Command departed behind a Boeing 767 on Runway 31L after the Controller provided 3.5 miles of separation, conflicting with the company manual's 5-mile requirement. The Controller later cited FAA Order 7110.659 as the authority for the reduced separation, prompting the pilot to request an operating manual update.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Crew reported lining up with the wrong runway at a nearby airport at night.
summary: The flight crew descended for a visual approach to Bethel (BET) but mistakenly identified Kwethluk (KWT) runway lights due to high intensity and lack of parallel/cross lights. They executed a go-around, acquired the correct airport, and landed safely, attributing the error to misidentified pilot-controlled lighting.

synopsis: CL30 Captain reported both generators disconnected when the APU was started on final approach which caused the electrical system to go to essential power. Captain reported a reset of both generators and landed in normal configuration.
summary: The flight crew experienced a dual generator disconnect and dark cockpit during APU start on approach in IMC conditions. The cause was attributed to starting the APU too late, but the crew recovered power by resetting generators and landed safely.

synopsis: An Airbus A300 First Officer reported the failure of the right main landing gear to extend normally. An alternate method was employed and a successful landing was accomplished.
summary: During an ILS approach, the right main gear failed to extend and lock, triggering ECAM warnings. The crew executed the gravity extension procedure, landed with open gear doors, and taxied clear using differential braking before being towed to parking.

synopsis: Line Technician reported a B737 returned to the gate due to a pitot static cover not being removed prior to departure.
summary: The aircraft returned to the gate after another pilot spotted a vertical stabilizer pitot static cover. The cover was missed during a foggy walk-around because its dark grey side faced out, making it difficult to see after a wet wash.

synopsis: LNC4 Pilot reported rapid loss of cabin pressure at FL250 resulting in a diversion to a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot experienced rapid cabin pressure loss at FL250, initiating an emergency descent to FL100. After a mechanic inspection at ZZZ confirmed the aircraft was airworthy, the flight continued to the original destination at FL110 without further issues.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported propeller damage due to contact with a runway end light while taxiing onto Runway 33 at PGA. Pilot suggested better signage and markings would be appropriate to avoid future occurrences.
summary: A pilot taxiing a wooden propeller aircraft onto Runway 33 struck raised runway end lights while attempting to use the full runway length. The collision destroyed the propeller because the lights extended into the runway and were obscured by the cowling, and the pilot misinterpreted the chevron markings.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported a near-mid-air-collision in the pattern when another pilot did not follow tower instructions.
summary: The reporter's aircraft encountered a Cessna (Aircraft Y) at traffic pattern altitude while turning downwind after a touch-and-go. The reporter descended to avoid the Cessna, which was flying toward them after departing Runway XX, attributing the conflict to the Cessna pilot's misunderstanding of instructions or lack of situational awareness.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported a near-mid-air-collision after receiving a clearance to land.
summary: The pilot descended from 2,500 feet after being cleared to land but was instructed by ATC to maintain altitude due to traffic. Upon seeing an aircraft on a collision course, the pilot executed an emergency descent, which the controller criticized for lacking prior clearance despite the immediate safety threat.

synopsis: General aviation flight instructor reported an airspace violation following an unexpected spin induced by the student pilot.
summary: During a practice stall with a student, the student's incorrect inputs caused a left spin recovered at 800 feet AGL. Low visibility, rain, and the startle factor led to a momentary situational awareness lapse, resulting in an inadvertent entry into Class C airspace before the instructor directed an immediate exit.
