summary: A pilot reported that the JeppFD-Pro software design blocks critical SID altitude information, such as on the TERPZ 6 at BWI, with a movable display tool. The pilot stated this poor interface design risks missing critical data and requires a redesign to prevent information obstruction.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported returning to departure airport after experiencing a bird strike at 800 feet AGL on initial climb.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud bang and burnt smell at 800 feet AGL during climb, suspecting a bird strike. They returned for a normal landing, and post-flight inspection confirmed a bird strike on the number 1 engine with no apparent damage.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported observing a fuel quantity indication anomaly during descent.
summary: During descent, pilots received a fuel quantity alert and declared an emergency, noting an apparent 3,000-pound loss that later reduced to 2,000 pounds by shutdown. The #2 tank was approximately 1,400–1,600 pounds lower than #1, though the crew could not determine the cause during the idle descent.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported noting a dent under the main cabin door on walkaround. During flight a louder than normal cabin noise levels led Maintenance to discover, post flight, that the dented area had underlying structural damage.
summary: During preflight, the crew found a significant dent with a sticker and hydraulic residue, which maintenance later confirmed caused structural damage, grounding the aircraft. In-flight cabin noise prompted the inspection, revealing the dent sticker program is inadequate for tracking airframe damage progression.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported noticing a potential for a navigation error involving two fixes with similar spelling - PRYMD and PYRMD - while preparing for departure from MEM.
summary: The flight crew identified a potential routing error during departure while resolving an FMS discontinuity, caused by the similar spelling of waypoints PRYMD and PYRMD. The oversight was caught by following company procedures, prompting a recommendation to rename one waypoint to prevent future conflicts.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing stabilizer trim anomalies.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer experienced repeated Stab and Mach Trim disconnections and a violent nose-down drop after takeoff due to a known aircraft issue. They returned to the departure airport, landed safely, and recommended functional test flights before returning such aircraft to service.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported being pushed back with only 1 wing walker which nearly led to a collision with another aircraft.
summary: At TYS, a pushback crew with only one wing walker nearly collided with Aircraft Y due to poor situational awareness and staffing shortages. The tug driver stopped abruptly and became upset, but no contact occurred; the reporter attributes the near-miss to the crew prioritizing on-time departure over safety procedures.

synopsis: A Bonanza pilot and a Piper PA28 flight instructor reported that misunderstanding of ATC instructions caused a NMAC.
summary: A Bonanza pilot on a visual approach to Runway XXR experienced a near-miss with a training Cherokee that crossed 700 feet below. The incident resulted from the Cherokee instructor misinterpreting ATC instructions to follow the Bonanza and failing to monitor radio traffic, compounded by the controller's delayed conflict alert.

synopsis: A balloon pilot reported having to land on a residential street due to inability to safely continue to an open area.
summary: A pilot with over 40 years of experience made a street landing in a residential area due to calm weather preventing travel to an open dirt field. A homeowner complained about the landing, prompting the crew to pack the balloon quickly and promise not to return.

synopsis: C441 pilot reported a TRACON Controller in training issued several turns in the wrong direction, which had to be corrected by an instructor. The incorrect vectors caused a traffic conflict.
summary: A pilot flying in IMC received conflicting left and right turn vectors from two controllers, including a trainee, causing a traffic alert. The pilot disengaged the autopilot to manually steepen the turn and avoid conflict, later learning the errors resulted from a trainee operating in busy airspace.

synopsis: B737 Captain and First Officer reported exceeding a speed restriction on departure after reconfiguring their EFB display and inadvertently hiding the published airspeed restriction from view.
summary: The flight crew exceeded the 250-knot restriction above 10,000 ft while flying the LADYJ 2 RNAV departure from LAX in VNAV. The deviation resulted from pilot distraction, an expanded EFB view hiding the restriction, and failure to manually program the speed limit.

synopsis: B737 flight crew and dispatch reported that during taxi the number 2 engine failed, but after restart all indications were normal until descent when the engine surged/stalled several times.
summary: Pilots experienced a number 2 engine rollback during taxi and later compressor stalls during descent, attributing the initial event to cold, windy conditions and insufficient warmup time. After consulting Maintenance and Dispatch, they continued the flight, managed the in-flight stalls per the QRH, and landed safely without shutting down the engine.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a new TRACON procedure that resulted in increased fuel burn and minimum fuel status on multiple flights.
summary: Pilots flying into IAH encountered a new TRACON policy requiring 30 nm downwind legs for all arrivals, resulting in an estimated 2,500 lbs of extra fuel burn. This caused the aircraft to arrive at minimum fuel for two landings while operating 8 to 17 nm behind the required interval.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Flight Crew reported that they returned to departure airport after suffering ill effects from fumes emanating from the Left Pack after takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a strong burning oil smell and fumes from the left air conditioning pack during climb, causing headaches and disorientation for the flight deck and cabin crew. The crew donned oxygen masks, declared an emergency, and returned to the departure airport for medical evaluation after the fumes impaired their alertness.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported they initiated a go-around below 1,000 feet due to severe weather and a windshear warning.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate turbulence, icing, and a windshear warning below 1000 ft AGL during a night ILS approach, prompting a go-around. Task saturation and failure to select a vertical guidance mode prevented autopilot engagement, causing an altitude deviation before the crew recovered automation and successfully landed on a second attempt.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported executing a missed approach after encountering windshear on short final at SEA.
summary: The crew encountered a windshear warning on short final to SEA 16L while flying an ILS approach in gusty conditions. The First Officer hesitated briefly before executing the escape maneuver, resulting in a successful go-around and subsequent landing without altitude loss.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported that they had turbulence during approach then they got a windshear warning and had to go-around.
summary: The crew encountered a windshear warning at 500 feet AGL during a night approach in moderate turbulence and icing, triggering a go-around and climb to 5000 feet. After resolving task saturation and communication issues, they successfully completed a second approach and landing by manually overriding auto-throttles to maintain airspeed.

synopsis: Boeing 737 Crew reported a dual NAV/Display failure while on approach. They executed a missed approach and recovered the failed NAV systems using the QRH while preparing for their second approach.
summary: The First Officer flying an arrival into SJC experienced dual PFD display source messages, followed by Flight Director failure and ND data loss on final approach. These failures caused an autopilot downgrade to Control Wheel Steering and an overshoot, necessitating a go-around before a normal landing was completed.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported returning to the gate after experiencing a total loss of electrical power during taxi out.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced dual generator failure during taxi after the Captain cleared an initial ECAM while single-engine taxiing. The aircraft returned to the gate following a total electrical power loss, with the Captain attributing the delay in identifying the malfunction to the single-engine taxi decision and workload.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing loss of cabin pressure related to single pack operation and a forward equipment overheat anomaly.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a FWD Equip OVHT message followed by a Cabin Altitude Master Warning. After failed attempts to control cabin altitude, they executed an expedited descent and landed safely, noting the cooling checklist should address single pack operations.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported receiving a TCAS RA descend command towards traffic during an ATC directed go-around.
summary: The crew executed a go-around at TUS after ATC issued an unclear command regarding traffic, later receiving a conflicting TCAS RA while visually tracking a helicopter. The pilot ignored the RA to maintain visual separation, attributing the incident to runway construction and conflicting procedures with a neighboring military base.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported that a gust from a nearby thunderstorm caused a right roll during the landing flare, which resulted in a wingtip contacting the runway.
summary: The flight crew encountered unforecast thunderstorms and shifting winds during the final approach and flare of a routine flight. A sustained gust induced a right roll, causing the right wingtip to contact the runway surface just before touchdown.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported a momentary stick shaker due to turbulence descending from FL360 to FL340.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence in an embedded storm at FL380 despite clear weather radar, causing airspeed loss and a brief stick shaker activation. They descended to FL340 with increased power to recover, attributing the event to undetected convective activity and a lack of prior reports.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported that due to an A/C pack deferral and a Bleed Duct warning, the aircraft lost all pressurization.
summary: The flight crew experienced a depressurization at FL270 due to a deferred right pack and a left bleed duct warning, forcing an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. While oxygen masks deployed, one row failed to deploy properly, and the crew noted smoke and heat from the generators upon landing.

synopsis: PA-31 Captain reported shutting down the left engine in cruise at 7,000 feet due to low oil pressure and high oil temperature.
summary: The pilot reported losing power on the left engine while enroute at 7,000 feet due to low oil pressure and high temperature. The engine was shut down, and the aircraft landed safely at ZZZ where maintenance observed oil leaking from the cowl flap.

synopsis: A flight instructor reported that his student, on an initial solo flight, lost control upon landing his Cessna 152. The aircraft exited the runway surface, collapsing the nose gear and damaging the propeller.
summary: A student pilot soloing a local flight lost directional control on final approach due to improper wind correction, causing the aircraft to veer into grass. The nose wheel collapsed and the propeller struck the ground, but the student remained uninjured.

synopsis: C421 pilot reported the right engine was shut down in cruise at FL210 due to oil loss and a diversion was completed without incident.
summary: The pilot reported an oil leak from the right engine's top vent while cruising at FL210. The pilot immediately shut down and feathered the right engine, diverted, and landed without incident.

synopsis: GEG Radar Approach controllers reported their sector vectored an aircraft below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at the Handoff position allowed a tanker aircraft to enter a 5500-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude while at 5000 feet due to distraction and lack of briefing. The controller issued a climb to 6000 feet but noted the Minimum Safe Altitude Warning system failed to alarm during the incident.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew reported that during descent they received a 'MAIN BATT LOW' EICAS message that eventually disappeared.
summary: During descent below FL180, the flight crew detected a cooking odor and received battery-related EICAS messages without associated electronic checklists. Assuming the issues were spurious due to workload and lack of guidance, they completed an uneventful approach and landing before debriefing maintenance at the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier Gate Agent reported concern about the safety of gate-checking luggage that has internal lithium ion batteries.
summary: A cabin crew member reported a safety concern regarding 'AWAY' carry-on bags containing non-removable lithium-ion batteries. The reporter questioned if checking these bags when overhead bins are full poses a risk and suggested restricting them to the cabin.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported complying with a TCAS RA on climb out from SEA RWY 16C after following traffic departing from RWY 16L.
summary: The pilot reported that while taking off from SEA runway 16C behind an early-turning departure, the aircraft triggered an immediate "reduce vertical speed" RA at 1400 feet MSL without a prior TA. The pilot manually complied, the conflict cleared within seconds, and the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported they were dispatched with pneumatic bleed Number 1 deferred inoperative and decided to return to departure airport after experiencing loss of pneumatic bleed Number 2.
summary: The Captain returned to the departure airport after a BLEED 2 FAIL warning occurred at FL220 while Bleed 1 was already deferred. The decision was driven by compounding factors including a closed crossbleed valve, previous Bleed 2 issues that day, and the inability to use the APU above 15,000 feet.

synopsis: Cessna Citation pilot reported the illumination of a cabin door seal warning light, followed by a loss of cabin pressure warning came on during cruise. A descent was executed, and a successful diversion a suitable airport was accomplished.
summary: The pilot reported a door seal light at 40,000 feet, triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet after a loud sound indicated pressure loss. A mechanic found frozen condensation from prior rain caused the seal malfunction; after draining the water, the flight continued.

synopsis: Falcon 2000 pilot reported encountering wake turbulence 5 miles in trail of an A320 on approach into SAN.
summary: During descent via LYNDI FOUR into SAN, the crew encountered two wake upsets from an A320, causing a 35-degree bank. After ATC confirmed a 5-mile separation, the crew adjusted VNAV to fly above the published path to avoid further wake turbulence.

synopsis: MSP Tower Controller reported they observed conflicting traffic of an aircraft executing a go around and a converging runway departure.
summary: A controller observed a B757 go-around and a departing CRJ on converging runways during high wind gusts with the wind shear system inoperative. The aircraft maneuvered to avoid a collision with approximately 0.4 miles lateral and 100 feet vertical separation before entering clouds, attributed to complex operations and staffing issues.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate after confirming a fuel leak from the left engine.
summary: The flight crew encountered a fuel leak and imbalance during cruise, confirmed by a CDU message and visual inspection of the left engine. They diverted to a nearby alternate, coordinated with ATC and dispatch, and executed an uneventful overweight landing.

synopsis: A Boeing 767 flight crew reported the loss of a primary hydraulic system. A diversion to the most suitable airport was successfully accomplished.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid center hydraulic leak enroute, triggering C HYD QNT and C HYD SYS PRESS messages. They diverted to reduce landing weight, landed safely with alternate gear extension, and discovered a left main landing gear fire caused by a failed high-pressure O-ring.

synopsis: EMB-170 First Officer reported a Flight Attendant was injured during a wake turbulence encounter 8 miles in trail of a B777 on arrival into LAX.
summary: During the HLYWD1 arrival to LAX, the crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding Boeing 777, causing a 30-degree roll and injuring one flight attendant. ATC provided step-down altitudes and a runway change to avoid further wake, while the captain managed the injury and crew scheduling.

synopsis: Cessna 402 pilot reported diverting due to the loss of rudder control during cruise.
summary: During cruise, the pilot reported the right rudder pedal jammed full forward, eliminating right rudder authority while the aircraft remained straight and level. The crew diverted to ZZZ1, landed safely, but the aircraft could not taxi and required towing to the ramp after passenger evacuation.

synopsis: EMB-190 Captain reported that due to a Pack deferred and Bleed Overpressure they lost de-icing capability.
summary: The crew encountered a Bleed 2 overpressure caution on takeoff with Pack 2 off per MEL, requiring Engine 2 idle and loss of wing anti-icing. They continued to ZZZ above icing conditions and landed safely on 27R after completing single-engine checklists.

synopsis: Four air carrier Maintenance Technicians reported that when pushing a CRJ-200 out of the hangar they lost control and the aircraft made contact with another aircraft.
summary: A tug driver and wing walker pushed an aircraft out of a hangar when the ramp incline caused the wing walker to lose visibility. The right outboard flap struck the lower fuselage and lodged into the nose gear of another aircraft during the turn.

synopsis: Westwind Captain diverted to a nearby alternate after an inflight shutdown of the right engine. This was due to a loss of oil pressure later traced to failure to replace the oil cap.
summary: The flight crew shut down the right engine in flight due to low oil pressure caused by an unsecured oil cap. The engine seized during the ILS approach to an alternate airport, but the crew landed safely without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported observing another aircraft takeoff opposite direction during rollout at non towered airport.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair collision at N47 while landing on runway 26, where an unidentified aircraft took off downwind from runway 8 without stopping or looking. The intruder passed 150 feet horizontally and 35 feet vertically above the landing aircraft due to sun glare and lack of CTAF communication, resulting in no injuries or damage.

synopsis: IAI Westwind First Officer reported that the Number Two engine was shut down due to loss of oil pressure and a diversion was accomplished without incident.
summary: The crew diverted and landed the aircraft after Number Two engine oil pressure dropped below minimum, causing the Captain to shut down the engine. During descent between 14,000 and 70,000 feet, high N2 windmilling caused strong vibrations.

synopsis: BE36 Pilot reported that on a night landing currency flight at a towered airport, he landed on the wrong runway.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine aircraft at night landed on the wrong runway after accepting an unusual ATC request to stay east of Runway 01. The error resulted from limited visual cues, unfamiliarity with the short runway, and failure to use instruments for situational awareness.

synopsis: A pilot reported the Center in Mexico would not hand him off to the Center in the United States so they had to contact the Center on their own and checked in while already in U.S airspace.
summary: The pilot reported a flight plan error at MMCU where a VFR plan was initially filed instead of IFR, and later experienced a radar handoff failure between Monterrey and Albuquerque Centers near the US border due to poor radio coverage. Despite Monterrey's reluctance to facilitate the transfer, the crew established contact with Albuquerque, completed the flight, and landed without incident.

synopsis: CE680 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival into MCO 6 miles in trail of an A321.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence at 6,500 feet while being vectored for a visual approach to runway 36L at MCO, trailing an A321. They slowed their descent and flew one dot above the ILS glideslope to avoid further wake, resulting in no additional encounters.

synopsis: DEN Tower Controller, D01 TRACON Controller, and a flight crew reported a NMAC between aircraft departing on parallel runways.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Aircraft X on a 150 heading and Aircraft Y on a SID from parallel runways, causing their paths to merge due to a misjudgment of separation. The controller issued emergency turns to resolve the conflict, resulting in Aircraft Y's pilot declaring a near miss and a third aircraft being held at 7000 feet.

synopsis: PHX Tower Controller reported an aircraft departed on a closed runway.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway 7L, but the pilot diverted attention to another aircraft and mistakenly entered the closed, unlit Runway 7R. The controller attempted to cancel the departure, but the pilot switched frequencies and departed safely from the wrong runway.

synopsis: Tower Controllers reported they had less than required separation criteria for an Opposite Direction Operation.
summary: The Tower CIC changed the active runway to 17, but new controllers mistakenly launched a Global Express from Runway 35 while a Beech Bonanza was on visual approach to Runway 17. This created an opposite direction operations conflict, requiring the Bonanza to be vectored for a Runway 35 approach.

synopsis: B777 Flight Crew reported that an unexpected autoland due to a change in weather, resulted in a shorter approach and insufficient time for Flight Attendants to secure carts, one of which struck a passenger.
summary: During a CAT II autoland with autobrakes 4, a passenger claimed a galley cart struck his head upon landing. The Captain met the upset passenger in the galley near door 2L after the flight, where the passenger demanded to speak about the landing despite the crew having performed standard cabin alerts at 10,600 feet.

synopsis: ERJ-175 First Officer and Flight Attendant reported evacuating the aircraft after haze filled the cabin following engine pack troubleshooting.
summary: Flight crew and maintenance personnel experienced strong fumes and smoke in the cabin during ground engine runs on an aircraft with a suspected BLEED 2 fault. The odor returned upon starting the #2 engine, leading to multiple evacuations, terminal evacuation, and medical treatment for potential smoke inhalation.

synopsis: Cessna Caravan pilot reported TKS fumes in the cockpit inhibiting the use of the cabin heater unless the oxygen mask is used.
summary: The pilot reported TKS alcohol fumes entering the cockpit via the bleed air system while using cabin heat during climb in icing conditions. The pilot mitigated exposure by turning off cabin heat and using supplemental oxygen, concluding that no effective prevention exists for this scenario.

synopsis: The First Officer of an A321 reported that during climb the aircraft experienced a violent shudder followed by an ENG STALL ECAM message.
summary: During climb through FL200, the crew experienced an ENG 2 STALL and EGT OVERLIMIT, leading to Engine 2 failure. The Captain executed the ENGINE 2 FAIL procedure, diverted back to the departure airport, and landed safely before shutting down the affected engine.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported they were issued go-around instructions due to an aircraft on the runway.
summary: A pilot on short final at SNA reported that the tower cleared an air carrier to line up and wait, causing a conflict. The controller subsequently ordered the landing aircraft to go around after realizing the error, highlighting a chronic issue with runway clearance procedures at this airport.

synopsis: A Boeing 777 First Officer reported that electronic checklist is not accurate regarding the Smoke, Fire and Fumes Checklist.
summary: A pilot reported that the Boeing 777 onboard electronic checklist fails to reference critical cabin fire procedures found in a separate QRH bulletin. This discrepancy increases workload during emergencies and prevents the checklist from resolving the fire, potentially leading to a negative outcome.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported that they felt rushed and pressured when ATC gave them vectors very close to the final approach course.
summary: The flight crew received aggressive vectors from ATC during an RNAV approach in weather, resulting in a low altitude deviation due to unverified VNAV selection. The crew corrected the descent after breaking out, attributing the incident to rushed vectors and a failure to crosscheck aircraft automation.

synopsis: An Embraer 145 Flight Crew reported that they received a 'Terrain-Terrain Pull up, Pull up' warning during climb while following ATC instructions.
summary: The pilot reported a GPWS terrain warning at 5,000 feet during departure, prompting an escape maneuver to 6,000 feet. The cause remains uncertain, with the pilot suspecting either a radio altimeter malfunction or actual terrain despite the charted MORA being 3,500 feet.

synopsis: AS-350 Pilot reported that failure to remove the tail rotor block resulted in insufficient right pedal on initial hover and a return to the ground.
summary: The pilot and two medical crewmembers failed to remove a tail rotor block during preflight checks. Upon starting the helicopter and hovering, they noted insufficient right pedal control and landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: ATR42 Captain reported that on descent for landing, the right engine flamed out with 900 pounds of fuel indicated in the right tank. Tank was subsequently found to be empty.
summary: The pilot reported that after a maintenance fueling error caused an initial imbalance, a right engine flame-out occurred during descent due to a feeder jet pump malfunction. Although the Fuel Quantity Indicator showed 900 LBS, maintenance found no fuel in the right tank, forcing a single-engine landing.

synopsis: A320 Flight Crew reported severe turbulence after clipping a benign looking cloud.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence while penetrating a visually smooth cloud at FL330, causing an uncommanded climb to 34,300 ft and a 40-degree bank. The pilot manually regained control after the autopilot was disengaged, resulting in no injuries or exceeded limitations despite the unexpected weather deviation.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reported a hard landing, resulting from insufficient flare, caused the inertia escape reels to dislodge from their housings.
summary: The First Officer executed a hard landing during an ILS approach due to insufficient flare, causing the aircraft to bounce. The Captain took control to recover the landing without a go-around, citing low altitude and good runway position as reasons to avoid a potentially worse outcome.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus flight crew reported that after landing one of the Thrust Reversers would not stow.
summary: The First Officer landed in a moderate crosswind, but the No. 2 Thrust Reverser failed to stow, causing the Auto Throttles lever to trip and damaging the engine cowl skin. The reporter attributed the damage to a jammed outer portion of the reverser that buckled the skin while the inner portion attempted to stow.

synopsis: ERJ-175 Captain reported that passengers deplaned via air stairs in front of a running engine.
summary: The Captain reported that while Engine 1 ran to power the parked aircraft, ramp agents positioned air stairs 15 feet in front of the live engine and allowed passengers to deplane. The Captain immediately shut down the engine, noting the Ramp Supervisor admitted agents should not have signaled the Flight Attendant to open the door while the engine was running.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported landing on a runway that was shorter than company operating parameters after lining up with the wrong runway at DCA.
summary: The nonflying pilot on River Visual 19 entered DCA in the FMS fix page and selected the NDB instead of the VOR, causing a high descent and missed Runway 19. The crew accepted a clearance for Runway 22 but later realized the 5,000-foot runway was too short for a safe landing.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported a significant fuel leak after takeoff.
summary: During climb after takeoff, the instructor detected a fuel smell and observed a significant leak from the left fuel tank cap, which was tightly secured. The instructor notified ATC and requested a visual approach back to the departure airport.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported concern with SOP adherence during pushback.
summary: During pushback, the tug driver stopped the aircraft off the yellow line and disconnected the tow bar without clearance, causing the aircraft to move. The pilot attributed this safety incident to inadequate training and oversight of the pushback crew regarding proper positioning and clearance procedures.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported a high speed rejected takeoff due to an engine fail alert light.
summary: The crew executed a high-speed rejected takeoff at 145 knots due to a flickering red ENGINE FAIL alert, stopping with a 1,600-foot margin. Subsequent inspection revealed a destroyed #1 engine turbine compressor, likely from FOD, and a damaged #5 main tire.

synopsis: Airbus 320 Maintenance Technician reported that external power cord malfunctioned.
summary: A pilot troubleshooting window anti-ice messages observed smoke and a small flame at the external power connection after rebooting the aircraft. The pilot disconnected the worn gate power cable, extinguishing the fire, and engineering attributed the incident to the damaged cable.

aircraft: Bell Helicopter Textron Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported a NMAC with a helicopter attempting to land on the same hospital helipad from which he was lifting off.
summary: During hover checks at a hospital pad, a medical transport helicopter nearly collided with another helicopter landing overhead. The paramedic spotted the intruder's searchlight and warned the pilot, preventing a strike caused by the other aircraft's failure to monitor the common frequency and the pad's limited size.

synopsis: Pilot reported departing from a closed runway contrary to issued ATC instructions.
summary: The pilot, fatigued from a night shift, departed Phoenix on a closed runway 7R instead of the cleared 7L due to lost situational awareness and fixation. The aircraft was airborne before the pilot noticed the closed runway markings, prompting ATC to order a turn and report for potential violations.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 pilot reported an experimental aircraft was landing in the opposite direction.
summary: A student pilot in a Skyhawk departed Runway 16 while a yellow experimental aircraft landed on Runway 34, causing a near mid-air collision. The reporter attributed the incident to the experimental pilot repeatedly using the wrong runway and traffic pattern despite multiple corrections from other pilots.

synopsis: J3 Cub pilot reported that a ground loop and runway excursion resulted after landing with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot lost directional control during landing rollout on a 1800ft strip due to a quartering tailwind and improper stall technique, causing the aircraft to sink into a drainage channel. The pilot attributed the incident to insufficient tail wheel contact and inadequate standard brakes, though no reportable damage or prop strike occurred.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot reported a disagreement between them an ATC about the departure instructions.
summary: The pilot took off from a taxiway southeast into the wind after receiving a clearance that conflicted with landing traffic, causing the controller to express frustration and issue an alert. The pilot climbed to 700 feet west of the runway to avoid buildings, concluding that accepting a takeoff clearance toward landing traffic was inadvisable.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reported an NMAC with a Beechcraft Baron in the vicinity of 4R5.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair collision with a Beechcraft Baron during descent to 4R5, where the Baron crossed 200 feet ahead and 50 feet below at 2,500 feet. The pilot executed a left turn to increase separation, but radio contact remained unsuccessful despite the Baron likely having just departed Runway 22.

synopsis: A320 Captain and the NCT Controller reported on an airborne conflict that occurred when the A320 departed OAK and a C182 flew into his departure path.
summary: An A320 on the CNDEL 3 RNAV departure from OAK received a TCAS "climb" resolution advisory due to a C182 circling VFR at 4,500 ft entering its flight path. The controller instructed the A320 to turn heading 180 to avoid the conflict after the C182 failed to maintain visual separation.

synopsis: CL30 First Officer reported returning to departure airport after the left engine failed shortly after takeoff. During return to the airport the engine was successfully restarted.
summary: The Second in Command reported severe left engine vibration and surging at 1200 ft AGL during initial climb, triggering flameout and exceedance messages. Retarding the thrust lever stopped the vibration and allowed the engine to relight, enabling a safe return and landing on Runway XX.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: K90 TRACON Controller reported an unidentified VFR aircraft was a NMAC with a VFR aircraft the Controller was working.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic advisories to Aircraft X regarding opposite-direction VFR traffic at 800 feet, but the pilot climbed to 1,500 feet and sighted the traffic at that altitude. The controller attributed the conflict to unverified altitudes and admitted they should have issued proactive vectors to de-conflict the situation.

synopsis: B737 pilot expressed concern about the design of the single-engine go-around procedures at RNO.
summary: A pilot reported that Reno Special Operations 10-7B guidance to level off at 6200ft MSL during a single-engine missed approach places aircraft dangerously close to a 6274ft peak near fix ZAKBI. The pilot recommends revising the procedure to level off at 6800ft MSL to ensure adequate terrain clearance.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a loss of cabin pressure while at cruise altitude. After conducting an emergency descent, cabin pressurization was stabilized, and a return to the departure airport was successfully accomplished.
summary: The flight crew experienced an altitude warning and horn at FL400, prompting an emergency descent with oxygen masks. After regaining cabin control at 22,000 feet, they descended to 14,000 feet for terrain clearance and returned to the departure airport for a normal landing.

synopsis: EMB-175 reported encountering severe turbulence in the vicinity of FCA VOR at FL320.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence while descending from FL330 to FL310 near Kalispell, MT, causing violent shaking and instrument fluctuations. After climbing to FL350, conditions improved to light chop with no injuries or aircraft damage reported, though a post-flight maintenance inspection was required.

synopsis: Bombardier Dash 8 flight crew reported shutting down the APU and discharging the fire bottle after noticing an excessive electrical load on the APU and smoke reported to be coming from the tail area.
summary: After engine start, the crew discovered a welded APU contactor causing high load and smoke, prompting immediate deplaning. With wheelchair passengers still aboard, the captain discharged the APU fire bottle as a precaution before fire services inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: Champion 7FC pilot reported directional control difficulties during landing roll led to a nose-over event.
summary: During a touch-and-go landing, the aircraft veered right, then left after brake corrections. Tapping the right brake caused it to lock, resulting in the aircraft pitching onto its nose.

synopsis: BE55 pilot reported diverting to an alternate airport for a planned gear up landing when the landing gear failed to extend.
summary: During approach, the pilot reported the landing gear would not extend despite multiple attempts and manual extension procedures. The aircraft diverted to a larger airport for a successful gear-up landing with no fire or injuries.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported pushback brake release procedure SOP deviations are becoming more common.
summary: A pilot reported that ground crew requested brake release without pushback clearance at San Francisco and other stations. The pilot advised them to standby, noting this violation of standard operating procedures is becoming a frequent trend.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported executing a go-around following a wake turbulence encounter and a firm touchdown in gusty wind conditions.
summary: A new Captain flying an MD-11 to EWR overcorrected aileron during a crosswind ILS approach, causing a firm landing and triggering a First Officer-initiated go-around. The First Officer subsequently took control for a safe landing on the second attempt after observing the Captain's instability and procedural errors.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV on approach to CLT.
summary: A pilot reported a drone passing within 5 to 10 feet of the wingtip during a visual approach to runway 23 at CLT at 3,000 feet. The incident caused ATC to suspend runway 23 approaches for three following aircraft and dispatch a police helicopter to locate the drone.

synopsis: C150 pilot reported an off field landing due to loss of engine power. After refueling, the following flight experienced radio problems that resulted in landing without a clearance.
summary: The sole pilot of a Cessna 150 experienced an engine failure attributed to carburetor icing and low fuel during a cross-country flight, forcing a safe highway landing. Later, while en route to ZZZ, two-way radio failure and fuel concerns led to a landing at ZZZ1, where ATC alleged a pilot deviation despite the pilot's safety-focused actions.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported a NMAC during a training flight near MKY.
summary: During a training flight at 2,000 ft southwest of MKY, the pilot spotted a Cessna on a head-on collision course. Both pilots executed evasive maneuvers, with the reporter descending right and the other ascending, resulting in no accident.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: EUG Controllers reported unknowingly accepting a handoff on an aircraft which was 1,000 feet below the Minimum Enroute Altitude until it was pointed out by the Supervisor.
summary: EUG Approach accepted Aircraft X from ZSE at 5,000 feet, below the 6,000-foot MEA on V287, and issued a climb after the aircraft passed a 5,300-foot MVA. The pilot requested and received a VFR On Top clearance at 5,000 feet, prompting a recommendation to revise the LOA to enforce MEA compliance prior to handoff.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported not recieving any instructions or briefing about a new radar site and a significant radar software system upgrade including new separation standards prior to its implementation.
summary: An air traffic controller reported being assigned to a position with new radar coverage and separation minima without prior knowledge. The supervisor, managing a shift with minimum staffing, instructed the controller to read the required changes on the position to relieve an overworked colleague.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported a serious unruly passenger incident while at cruise altitude. The individual was subdued, and the flight continued to the destination airport, where law enforcement personnel were waiting.
summary: The flight crew managed an escalating disruptive passenger incident during descent that required restraint by cabin crew, a Federal Flight Deck Officer, and a law enforcement officer. The aircraft landed normally with priority taxi to the gate where authorities removed the passenger for a mental evaluation, with no injuries reported to the crew.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported that a male passenger had groped a flight attendant. A decision was made to divert and have the passenger removed by law enforcement authorities.
summary: The captain diverted to Phoenix after a passenger groped a flight attendant during cruise. The aircraft landed uneventfully, and the passenger was removed by ground authorities, though the captain noted he failed to explicitly declare priority handling with ATC.

synopsis: A Boeing 757 captain reported an electrical odor smell evident in the cockpit and cabin. The flight completed a successful diversion to a suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew detected an electrical smoke smell at cruise, prompting an emergency descent and overweight landing at ZZZ. Maintenance identified a tripped circuit breaker for an equipment cooling fan, which showed smoke and soot on the rotor vanes.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp employee reported the push back crew for a B737-800 was subjected to jet blast from another B737-800 when the two aircraft were directed to adjacent ramp spots. Reporter suggested Ramp Control should give more consideration to ramp safety when they assign ramp spots for push back and tow bar disconnect operations.
summary: ATC instructed a B737-800 to push to spot X while another B737-800 pushed to spot YY directly ahead at ZZZ Airport. The first aircraft's push crew was exposed to jet blast during tow bar disconnection, which the reporter deemed unsafe and a misuse of spots intended for wide-body aircraft.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A regional jet pilot reported experiencing multiple physical symptoms resulting in an inability to continue the flight. A diversion to a suitable airport to seek medical help was accomplished.
summary: A fatigued First Officer with cold symptoms experienced fever, rapid heart rate, and shallow breathing at 38,000 feet, initially suspecting hypoxia. The crew diverted to the nearest airport after medical evaluation confirmed a 103-degree fever from a cold virus, safely terminating the flight.

synopsis: Embraer 175 Captain reported returning to the gate after receiving 'ENG REF ECS DISAG' caution message when preparing for takeoff.
summary: The flight crew received an 'ENG REF ECS DISAG' caution during taxi due to a PACK 1 FCV1 fault caused by maintenance failing to pull circuit breakers for a disabled ram air system. Mechanics corrected the breaker configuration at the gate, resolving the issue but causing a two-hour departure delay.

synopsis: Embraer 175 Captain reported receiving electrical shocks through a headset while in contact with a charging iPad.
summary: A pilot reported receiving electrical shocks through a TSO-approved headset while charging an iPad in the cockpit of various Embraer aircraft during all flight phases. The pilot attributes the issue to a grounding design failure between the phone jack and electrical outlets, noting the shock occurs regardless of charger type or seat position.

synopsis: A Boeing 747-400 captain reported observing #1 Engine Overheat and Fire Warning lights shortly after takeoff. The appropriate emergency checklists were completed, and a return to the departure airport was successfully accomplished.
summary: Pilots reported an Engine 1 overheat and fire warning shortly after takeoff following a maintenance delay. They executed emergency procedures, returned to the airport, and landed safely; fire crews inspected the engine and found no fire, clearing the aircraft for maintenance.

synopsis: A Boeing 777-200 Captain reported the sudden failure of the right engine while at cruise altitude. After all appropriate emergency checklists were completed a successful diversion to a suitable airport was accomplished.
summary: The Captain and an IOE trainee experienced a sudden right engine failure and fire warning shortly after returning to the cockpit. The crew diverted to ZZZ due to adverse weather, executed a safe landing with ARFF support, and deplaned passengers without incident.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported the quick donning oxygen mask 'came apart' when it was removed from the storage compartment for use in cruise flight. Mask was replaced with an observer's mask and flight continued.
summary: During cruise, the Captain found the quick-donning oxygen mask broken with a detached hose and microphone, rendering it useless. The Captain replaced it with the Second Observer's mask, reported the failure to maintenance, and suggested the damage resulted from repeated forced stowing.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported that reliance on backup automation with a mis-tuned localizer resulted in a course deviation and traffic conflict.
summary: During a visual approach in VMC, the pilot tuned the wrong ILS frequency due to task saturation and a rushed runway change, causing the autopilot to fail to capture the localizer. The crew received a traffic alert and tower instruction to turn, but manually corrected the course and completed the approach safely after disconnecting automation.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported a runway excursion during landing due to poor crosswind technique.
summary: The pilot executed a non-stabilized approach to Runway 29, landing with high speed, misconfigured flaps, and incorrect crosswind compensation. The aircraft veered off the left edge onto the grass, but the pilot successfully recovered and returned to Taxiway Echo without an accident.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported multiple sets of power lines near BDR are set with wire markers placed on one of the wires. That wire and its markers are actually at a lower elevation than the other unmarked wires nearby.
summary: Pilots operating near Sikorsky Memorial Airport (BDR) reported a navigation hazard where Tana Wire Markers on lower powerlines mislead crews into ignoring higher, unmarked wires crossing the Housatonic River. This confusion creates a collision risk for helicopter and fixed-wing traffic photographing nearby construction.

synopsis: PC 12 flight crew reported being unable to make the turnoff that ATC was planning, resulting in cancellation of takeoff clearance for a B737 in position on the crossing runway.
summary: The pilot reported a potential runway incursion during landing rollout on Runway 08 while crossing Runway 15 after accepting an unexecutable taxi clearance. The incident caused a B737 to cancel its takeoff, attributed to the pilot's delayed refusal of the clearance and the controller's premature issuance of a takeoff clearance.

synopsis: An Approach Controller and air carrier flight crew reported a near mid air collision due to poor ATC coordination on a departure from a satellite airport.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a stale release for a departing aircraft to climb to 3,000 feet, causing it to conflict with a large transport on a visual approach at 3,600 feet. The transport crew executed a TCAS climb resolution advisory, passing 200 feet above the departing aircraft, which the controller attributed to the expired coordination and high arrival volume.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Tower Controller reported the Ground Controller allowed an aircraft to enter a runway at the same time another aircraft was landing.
summary: A trainee Local Controller cleared Aircraft X to cross a runway while Aircraft Y was landing on an intersecting runway. The trainer intervened to stop Aircraft X, which had already entered the runway, forcing it to turn 180 degrees and hold short after Aircraft Y touched down.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported altitude deviation due to distraction from flying duties during arrival.
summary: During descent into DFW on the BRDJE3 arrival, the crew missed the TUSLE crossing restriction due to distraction while troubleshooting an FCU 1 fault and sending a Maintenance Report Message. The aircraft descended 8,000 feet below the required altitude before the crew leveled at 17,000 feet and received ATC clearance to rejoin the arrival.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported being out of contact for ten minutes in Fukuoka airspace due to a late hand off from Manila ATC and an error in ATC frequency information in the Jepp-Pro application.
summary: The flight crew lost CPDLC and HF contact with Manila Control while transitioning to Fukuoka FIR, resulting in a 10-minute delay contacting the correct NAHA Control. The pilot attributed the incident to outdated Jeppesen charts and a failure by Manila to properly hand off communications to NAHA.

synopsis: A First Officer reported the flight crew deviated from the assigned SID.
summary: During Aircraft X's takeoff, flight deck distractions from ground crew and maintenance caused the crew to incorrectly program the BMRNG transition instead of the 123 heading. The aircraft turned toward the 340 radial prematurely, requiring ATC to vector it back to the correct SJC VOR fix.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported that during taxi and shutting down Number 1 engine, started the APU and was unable to establish electrical power.
summary: The First Officer reported multiple electrical failures and cabin pressurization issues after landing while taxiing to the gate. The aircraft failed to shut down normally, requiring maintenance to perform an electrical reset, which the pilot believes is insufficient to address the recurring root cause.

synopsis: CL-350 flight crew reported that the autopilot was flying a holding pattern in an irregular pattern when it got an error message and blacked out.
summary: The pilot reported that while entering a hold at ZZZ VOR due to heavy traffic, the FMS blanked and the autopilot subsequently flew half-bank turns without PFD indication. ATC vectored the aircraft to rejoin the arrival, and the flight landed safely, though the cause of the FMS timeout and autopilot anomaly remained unexplained.

synopsis: The Captain of an EMB-505 reported that they flew the pattern at between 500 and 800 AGL when they got a GPWS warning.
summary: Two pilots flying a visual approach in VMC entered the pattern at 500–800 AGL instead of 1500 AGL due to fatigue, a truncated briefing, and an incorrect altitude alerter setting. The crew received a gear GPWS warning, landed long, and attributed the incident to fatigue-induced poor judgment and situational awareness.

synopsis: EMB-505 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence 10 miles in trail of an A350 at FL425.
summary: Pilots climbing from FL410 to FL430 encountered wake turbulence from an A350 at FL428, causing abrupt rolls requiring autopilot disengagement. The reporter attributed the incident to insufficient 10-mile separation and a lack of ATC notification regarding the heavy aircraft ahead.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported that they started and continued takeoff roll without the use of flight directors and autothrust.
summary: The Captain and First Officer conducted a takeoff without flight directors or autothrust, likely due to pre-takeoff selection errors, resulting in an improper V1 call. Although the aircraft rotated safely, the crew acknowledged poor communication, situational awareness, and automation management during the incident.

synopsis: Boeing 777-200 flight crew reported that during cruise they had an engine rollback and fire indication and proceeded to divert uneventfully to an appropriate alternate.
summary: The flight crew managed an engine rollback with high EGT and fire indication by executing memory items and diverting 15 NM left. They descended to FL200, landed safely overweight, and were towed for inspection after extinguishing the fire via the Fuel Control switch.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain reported while on RAJEE SID, ATC issued numerous amendments to published procedure using non-standard, or nonspecific phraseology. This, along with new Visual Jeppesen SID altitude depictions contributed to altitude deviation.
summary: The flight crew overshot 7,000 feet during climb on the ONT SID after receiving conflicting ATC clearances. The pilot attributed the deviation to confusing Jeppesen altitude depictions and inconsistent phraseology, noting that increased automation workload and traffic density contribute to such errors.

synopsis: An Embraer ERJ-175 flight crew reported difficulty controlling the thrust of the #2 engine. Using appropriate emergency checklists, the engine was secured, and the flight successfully diverted to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew encountered an uncontrollable number 2 engine with high N1 and a LIM indication while enroute at FL340. They shut down the engine, diverted, and landed safely, noting that FUEL LO LEVEL warnings appeared during fuel balancing despite adequate fuel.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported all four cabin crew members experienced physical symptoms after exposure to fumes on the aircraft before departure.
summary: Cabin crew and pilots aborted a preflight departure due to a strong odor later identified as an APU oil leak. The aircraft was taken out of service, and crew members reported ongoing symptoms including brain fog and chest tightness from the toxic fume exposure.

synopsis: A Cessna 172 Pilot reported that when the airplane was taxied and the brakes were equally applied, the airplane pulled to the left.
summary: During a C172 dual checkout taxi, the aircraft veered left and exited the taxiway due to suspected air bubbles in the brake lines, despite equal brake pressure. The pilot and instructor stopped in the grass without damage, and a mechanic later added hydraulic fluid after noting prior intermittent right brake issues.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported that on approach there appeared a pole with a red light mounted atop it, ahead of the left wing.
summary: A pilot on a night approach to Runway 26 at DXR nearly struck a lighted pole and treetops while slowing behind another aircraft. The pilot climbed to a safe altitude and attributed the incident to unfamiliarity with the terrain and a lack of visual approach slope indicators.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reported some wing damage resulted when he lost directional control on landing roll and struck a landing light.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft in gusty winds and low sun, failing to correct a bounce which caused the plane to porpoise and veer into grass. The right flap struck a runway light, causing a dent, primarily due to incorrect control inputs during the bounce.

synopsis: C208B Captain reported rejecting the takeoff shortly after liftoff when he experienced a loss of power related to a leaking o-ring in the fuel manifold.
summary: The pilot experienced a sudden power loss during takeoff due to a punctured o-ring in the fuel manifold installed after recent nozzle replacement. The crew safely aborted the flight, landed on the remaining runway, and taxied back for maintenance.

synopsis: Air Traffic Controller reported that he advised an MD-88 crew to descend to clear opposing traffic. MD-88 crew complied despite receiving a TCAS RA to climb.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X and Y on opposite courses with 500 feet vertical separation. When Aircraft X reported an RA climb, the controller advised against it, preventing the climb and noting the TCAS resolution was startling.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported ATC issued a traffic alert to descend while TCAS was commanding a climb with traffic observed above.
summary: During arrival into FLL, the crew encountered a VFR twin at 7,400 feet while descending to 6,000 feet. The pilot ignored a TCAS climb Resolution Advisory to avoid climbing into the traffic, instead increasing descent and turning away after visually spotting the aircraft, noting that simultaneous ATC instructions caused confusion.

synopsis: A Boeing 777 flight crew reported that after landing ATC reported to the crew that smoke was coming from the landing gear.
summary: The pilot flying applied manual brakes during a visual approach in gusty winds, resulting in several blown tires and reported smoke. Although no high brake temperatures were indicated, the aircraft could not be towed, requiring passengers to deplane via air stairs.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported that the quality of air in the cabin caused the cabin crew and some passengers to become light headed and ill. The ozone converter was reportedly a contributing factor in the event.
summary: Cabin crew and passengers experienced dizziness at FL320, prompting a divert to ZZZZ for an overweight landing. The flight crew attributed the symptoms to a possible high ozone concentration, as no fumes were detected and the aircraft systems remained nominal.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence 10 miles in trail of an MD11.
summary: The crew of an aircraft descending to FL290 behind an MD11 encountered wake turbulence at 10 miles separation, causing a 45-degree roll. The pilot attributed the event to poor ATC traffic management and light winds, noting that both the controller and the MD11 pilot initially dismissed the report.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: A Small Transport Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV operating in Boston Class B airspace without ATC knowledge.
summary: During climbout at 2,700 feet near Boston, the pilot encountered a 2-foot black drone within a few hundred feet. The pilot reported the incident to Boston Departure, and the subsequent controller requested further details.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the PAPI depiction on the Jeppesen 12-5 Chart for the PHL RNAV (GPS) Runway 27L approach, dated 22 Jun 2017, is shown on the incorrect side of the runway.
summary: The flight crew executing an RNAV GPS approach to Runway 27L found the PAPI located on the left side, contrary to the Jeppesen chart showing it on the right. After confirming alignment with the correct runway via ATC, the crew attributed the discrepancy to an inaccurate chart and recommended a reprint.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported entering an uncharted and poorly lighted island area while taxiing at SAT airport.
summary: The flight crew taxied into a new, uncharted island at the intersection of taxiways D and G at SAT due to missing blue lights and an outdated 10-9 diagram. They shut down engines and were towed clear by a tug with no damage to the aircraft or ground equipment.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported receiving two GPWS terrain warnings on a day visual approach.
summary: During a visual approach, the Pilot Flying maintained a high descent rate while the Pilot Monitoring was configuring the aircraft, triggering two GPWS terrain warnings. Despite the alerts and a low altitude alert from Tower, the crew confirmed visual contact with the terrain and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: CE-560 flight crew reported losing directional control on landing roll after a main gear tire failed.
summary: The crew experienced sluggish rotation and vibration on takeoff, followed by a right main gear tire failure and sparks at touchdown, causing the aircraft to veer off the runway. The pilots suspect Foreign Object Debris damage at departure caused the tire to deflate en route, resulting in an evacuation.

synopsis: Maintenance reported that while servicing the engine oil on a Boeing 787, it sounded like someone attempted to start the engine.
summary: During a post-arrival walkaround, a pilot observed the left engine cranking while a mechanic serviced it on a stand and a refueller was attached. Despite the pilot's urgent commands to shut down the engine, the flight crew responded that the engine was secured and fuel was off, leaving the engine motoring.

synopsis: PA28R pilot reported a NMAC in the pattern at LHM airport.
summary: A PA28R pilot flying touch-and-goes at Lincoln (LHM) crossed in front of a Cessna on final due to fixation on departure and failure to announce intentions. The pilot acknowledged the intrusion, apologized, and re-entered the pattern after the Cessna pilot notified him of the error.

synopsis: An American Champion Decathlon pilot reported inadvertently entering a spin condition while performing aerobatic maneuvers. A successful spin recovery was accomplished.
summary: During an aerobatic instructional flight in a Decathlon, the instructor inadvertently entered an inverted spin at the top of a half Cuban 8 due to uncoordinated rolling and increased stall speed. The aircraft was recovered at 700 ft AGL using the Meigs-Bueller method after the stall horn sounded during the maneuver entry.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence shortly after takeoff in trail of a B757.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 6 behind a B757 and encountered wake turbulence at 50 ft, requiring a sidestep to the upwind side. The reporter attributed the event to an immediate takeoff behind the 757 and recommended that Tower ensure proper separation.

synopsis: Ground reporter stated that simultaneous push-backs from a terminal in IAH is a safety hazard due to jet blast from airplanes in front of one another.
summary: Multiple Boeing 737s experienced jet blast exposure during ramp pushback operations. Aircraft Y, Z, and A crews were subjected to jet blast from adjacent aircraft while maneuvering between spots and taxiing, as described by the reporter.

synopsis: Ramp personnel reported that 3 pallets were missing from an offload causing a large weight discrepancy.
summary: Ramp personnel discovered three missing pallets during offload, creating a 28,016-pound weight discrepancy and a potential nose-heavy condition. Although the manifest was corrected to remain legal, the error could have resulted in a safety of flight issue.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported that while in cruise they experienced a faint acrid smell that smelled like a possible electrical fire.
summary: During cruise at FL350, the flight crew and cabin crew detected strong fumes and a BLOWER FAULT, prompting a diversion to ZZZ. The aircraft landed overweight due to an unadjusted fuel calculation, though no evacuation was required and passengers deplaned at the gate.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported that they taxied in on the wrong line and the winglet made contact with ground equipment.
summary: Ground crew guided a CRJ-900 on the wrong taxi line at the gate, causing the left winglet to strike ground equipment. The reporter attributed the incident to a lack of stop signals from wing walkers and inadequate training or situational awareness among ground personnel.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported being targeted by a laser while performing an approach to LAX Airport. This event resulted in a momentary loss of situational awareness and injury to his left eye.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to KLAX 25L were targeted by a green laser from the San Gabriel River area, causing momentary loss of situational awareness as they shielded their eyes. The aircraft landed safely after the crew notified Los Angeles Tower, though the pilot experienced eye watering and a headache.

synopsis: B777 pilot reported the failure of an engine while in oceanic airspace. All appropriate checklists and procedures were followed, and the flight successfully diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During a crew change, the flight crew experienced a right engine failure and fire warning, executing memory items to extinguish the fire. The aircraft diverted to ZZZ, landed overweight, and was towed to parking after the First Officer reported no visible abnormalities.

synopsis: A Metroliner Captain reported losing control of the aircraft at the start of the takeoff roll, due to an asymmetrical thrust condition, which resulted in damage to the aircraft.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot reported significant right engine torque lag causing the aircraft to veer right and depart the runway. Despite using differential power, steering, and brakes, the pilot struck a runway light and bent a left propeller tip while avoiding a taxiway sign.

synopsis: Cessna 750 flight crew reported that when they received clearance from ATC to hold over a fix, the FMC directed the autopilot to turn in the opposite direction.
summary: Pilots entered a holding pattern west of ZZZ VOR at FL390 with incorrect right turns due to relying on the FMS database without verifying the published left-turn procedure on charts. ATC provided corrective radar vectors, and the crew proceeded to destination uneventfully after acknowledging their failure to confirm hold details or query ATC.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported that Federal Air Marshals were allowed to board prior to the crew boarding.
summary: A flight attendant reported a passenger boarded an aircraft at the gate before the minimum crew arrived, violating FAR 121.391. The reporter attributed the breach to boarding pressure and a security lapse where the passenger bypassed screening while waiting on the jet bridge.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Cessna Citation flight crew reported they had an engine roll back to cut off during descent.
summary: During an IFR descent from 34,000 to 31,000 feet, the right engine rolled back to cut off. The crew followed the manufacturer's checklist to successfully restart the engine, and the flight continued to the destination while maintenance assesses the issue.

synopsis: A Check Airman in a Cessna 172 reported that when as they started to cross a runway, a helicopter flew at low level in front of them causing a NMAC.
summary: The flight crew received a ground clearance to cross Runway XY on taxiway B2 while a helicopter was cleared to depart northbound on the same runway. A near collision occurred when the helicopter passed in front of the aircraft, caused by the tower controller failing to realize the aircraft was taxiing.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported smelling fumes in the aft galley causing two flight attendants to become ill.
summary: Two flight attendants in the aft galley suffered fume exposure symptoms, leading the captain to divert the aircraft. Mechanics later replaced the right fuel pump, while three passengers reported smelling fumes but declined medical attention.

synopsis: ORD Tower Controller reported a CRJ-200 encountered wake turbulence 2.7 miles in trail of a B757 on approach to Runway 10C.
summary: A CRJ-200 pilot reported moderate to severe wake turbulence while following a B757 at 2.72 miles on approach to runway 10C in 100/09 winds. Both aircraft landed safely, but the pilot questioned the safety of current wake turbulence reclassification rules and requested an investigation into minimum separation distances.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that during climb the autopilot pitched over to regain airspeed.
summary: During climbout to FL390, the First Officer looked away from instruments while the Captain managed a speed decay near FL370 caused by VNAV pitch-down behavior. The Captain lowered the nose to recover airspeed, resulting in minimal altitude loss and a flashing MCP 'A' indication before resuming the climb.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported the FMC directed the aircraft's autopilot to turn in the wrong direction.
summary: A foreign carrier crew reported a potential FMGC database anomaly during a night IMC departure from ZZZ airport in mountainous terrain. The flight director commanded an unsafe left turn at 800 feet AGL, but the First Officer recognized the error and corrected the course, preventing a potential terrain collision.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported that while dealing with communication issues they neglected to complete the landing checklist and received an aural alert 'TOO LOW, FLAPS'.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer experienced a total loss of transmit capability and intercom audio during a visual approach to 3,000 feet. While troubleshooting, the PF neglected to set flaps to 5, triggering a "TOO LOW, FLAPS" alert at 700 feet, but the crew continued and landed safely before communications restored.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported difficulty identifying the proper taxi exit entrance during roll out on the active runway due to insufficient markings.
summary: The Captain reported that during a night landing on Runway 11, poor taxiway lighting and missing lead-in lines prevented locating exit P, causing the crew to taxi short of Runway 22L. This resulted in a go-around for traffic and a subsequent investigation into a potential pilot deviation after a go-around warning was activated.

synopsis: A BE-400 Captain reported that during preflight checks they were unable to open the engine fuel valve because the engine was fire bottle discharged.
summary: The Pilot-in-Command and First Officer discovered discharged fire bottles during pre-flight due to the First Officer inadvertently activating the fire protection system switch. This error grounded the aircraft, which the reporter attributes to the First Officer failing to follow the checklist and the Captain's divided attention caused by limited ground crew.

synopsis: Large Turbojet flight crew reported a taxiway excursion at LFPG resulting in damage to two main wheels.
summary: The flight crew departed Paris via a non-standard exit due to de-icing and, while turning from taxiway MD2 to D without specific routing instructions, felt a jog and received a tire pressure warning. The aircraft stopped with both tires 8 and 11 showing 1 psi, prompting a return to the ramp.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a cabin scenario with overpowering fumes in the cabin after engine start of a turbojet.
summary: Cabin crew and passengers experienced severe symptoms during pushback due to a strong "dirty sock" odor indicating a fume event. The aircraft returned to the gate for deplaning, and the reporting flight attendant was hospitalized for abnormal cardiac testing and tremors.

synopsis: Piper 32R pilot reported that during climb all electrical power was lost.
summary: The pilot experienced an alternator failure during initial climb from ZZZ, leading to total electrical loss. After coordinating with ATC to activate runway lights and using a smartphone for navigation, the pilot manually extended the gear and landed safely at ZZZ.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reported a NMAC with a UAV at 7500 ft in the vicinity of TRL airport.
summary: A pilot departing GPM reported a drone encounter while climbing to 7500 feet southwest of Terrell (TRL). The pilot initially mistook the drone for a bird but identified it by four red lights, estimating the separation was within 500 feet.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot reported taxiing onto the runway after receiving hold short instructions from the tower.
summary: The pilot taxied onto Runway 24 without clearance after holding short for landing traffic on Runway 14. The pilot entered the runway anticipating a takeoff clearance despite having no other traffic on Runway 24.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported returning to departure airport after the complete right side pneumatic system was determined to be inoperative.
summary: During takeoff, the crew received bleed leak warnings and reported debris falling from the aircraft, likely caused by a pneumatic system failure or runway FOD. The flight returned to the departure airport for a normal landing after consulting maintenance and ATC.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that Jeppesen RNAV Arrival charts for MMUN do not include the additional waypoints after the transition points.
summary: Pilots flying into MMUN encountered incomplete RNAV arrival data in their Jeppesen EFB, missing waypoints for the BUBUN 1B STAR. They resolved the issue by loading the EPNEL1B STAR to verify a clearance point on the 30R final, recommending that STAR charts include all RNAV points to prevent confusion.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported that he did not have rudder authority when he used the rudder standby system.
summary: The Captain discovered a standby rudder failure during preflight on an aircraft swap, where the light illuminated but no rudder authority existed. Maintenance replaced the overhead module with no success, resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service.

synopsis: B757-200 Captain reported that when they attempted to exit the runway he was unable to rotate the nose wheel because the tiller wheel jammed.
summary: The Captain, flying a visual approach, stopped partially on the runway after a loose sunglass case jammed the tiller wheel during a rapid deceleration for an early exit. Tower cleared a following aircraft for a go-around while the crew secured the obstruction and resumed taxiing without further assistance.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported that during climb one of the engines failed.
summary: The flight crew experienced an engine number 2 failure following a compressor stall at 16,300 feet during climb. They returned to the airport, executed an RNAV approach due to ILS outages, and landed safely with the aircraft taxiing to the gate under its own power.

synopsis: Widebody Transport flight crew reported an anomaly with the runway lighting at the Aguadilla, Puerto Rico (TJBQ) airport. The lighting problem was a result of backup electrical power issues due to a recent hurricane.
summary: The flight crew landed an aircraft at TJBQ on a non-tower RNAV RW08 approach after the tower closed early and runway lights failed due to generator fuel depletion. Although construction lights and reflectors caused confusion about lighting status, the crew safely landed and taxied using aircraft lights under clear moonlit conditions.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer on approach to IND in trail of a heavy reported speed dropped 10 kts which triggered the stick shaker in a possible wake vortex encounter.
summary: The crew experienced a stick shaker activation while on approach to IND runway 23L following a heavy aircraft in gusty winds. The pilot attributed the airspeed loss to poor judgment in wake turbulence avoidance and continued the landing in VMC conditions.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported that on a B757-300, when the inlet cowl is removed, there isn't anyplace to secure the fan cowl hold open rod.
summary: A mechanic reported an unsafe condition during inlet cowl removal where the Maintenance Manual requires both fan cowl hold open rods, but the forward rod must be disengaged. This conflict risks personal injury and aircraft damage due to undue stress on the cowling, prompting a proposal for a temporary support bracket.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported that an aircraft departed with an entry door handle out of alignment.
summary: A maintenance technician reported an out-of-alignment aft entry door via tablet, but a supervisor and crew chief ignored the Procedures Manual and refused to recall the aircraft. The aircraft departed with the potential safety hazard, as management dismissed the tablet alert and instructed staff to ignore safety protocols to ensure departure.

synopsis: A C172 pilot reported becoming confused and disoriented after takeoff, due to a sudden and unexpected turbulence encounter. The resulting heading and altitude deviation generated both an obstacle and sink rate warning.
summary: During departure in gusty winds, turbulence caused a TAWS alert and a radio frequency error, leading the pilot to turn past the assigned heading. The pilot attributed the near-loss of separation to reverse sensing on the NAV2 radio and a casual attitude toward the obstacle departure procedure.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported a NMAC with a UAV on approach to I19.
summary: During descent for landing at I19 at 2500 ft MSL, a pilot observed a stationary hobby drone at 1 o'clock and banked left to avoid it. The pilot reported the drone operator's activity as dangerous, noting it could have caused severe damage or loss of life without timely maneuvering.

synopsis: Certified Professional Controller, CPC, at Denver TRACON (Pueblo Sector), reported a recurring automation failure between D01 (PUB Sector), and Springs departure, COS. Automation handoffs received, do not transfer necessary aircraft data to provide required service. Further interfacility automated handoffs to Denver ARTCC, ZDV, do not display and transfer correct data.
summary: An air traffic controller at the Pueblo sector accepted a handoff for Aircraft X, which the pilot and Colorado Springs confirmed was IFR at 10,000 feet, but the automation displayed it as VFR with no flight plan data. The controller had to manually reset the flight plan to resolve the automation failure, which caused a "Local Flight plan" error during the handoff to Denver Center.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported a Local Controller vectored an aircraft that was below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: A trainee Controller in Charge transferred Aircraft X to Radar without coordination after the pilot reported inability to maintain VFR, placing the aircraft on a collision course with an obstacle. The Radar controller intervened by issuing an emergency turn and climb to avoid the hazard, attributing the incident to the trainee's inexperience and premature certification for staffing needs.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: S46 TRACON Controller reported that SEA Tower routinely launches successive departures with minimum separation regardless of aircraft performance differences.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined departure sectors allowed a speed overtake between a turboprop and a faster jet due to tunnel vision from a simultaneous pilot deviation elsewhere. The controller attributed the near-loss to unsafe Letter of Agreement procedures permitting only 3 miles separation for dissimilar aircraft, forcing complex speed restrictions and vectors to maintain safety.

synopsis: PCT TRACON Controller reported receiving an aircraft from Tower at 2000 feet, in an area with a 2100 foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Aircraft X departed DCA northbound behind Aircraft Y while delayed communications prevented a visual separation strip transfer.
