synopsis: First Officer reported after receiving alerts from ATC, flight crew, and the EPGWS to 'Go Around', the Captain continued the landing.
summary: A resting crew member and First Officer Y observed a visual approach into Almaty where the Captain ignored three go-around calls despite rain obscuring the runway and multiple aural alerts. The aircraft landed with a rapid descent after the Captain refused to execute a go-around, disregarding the Flight Operations Manual policy that any crew member can mandate one.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the right wing engine pods were scraped during a gusty crosswind landing.
summary: The pilot reported that a sudden wind gust at touchdown exceeded aileron authority, forcing full control inputs to prevent a wingtip strike. This resulted in engine pods 3 and 4 scraping the runway, prompting a recommendation to delay flights in similar conditions.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported programming the incorrect SID in the FMC.
summary: The flight crew departed Venice with an incorrect SID (ROKIB 6S instead of cleared 6X) due to unfamiliarity, fatigue, and disrupted checklist flows. ATC queried the deviation, and the crew corrected the heading without separation issues.

synopsis: A300 First Officer reported the landing gear would not retract due to a sensor issue.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear retraction failure and subsequent loss of autopilot and auto-throttles shortly after takeoff. They returned for an uneventful ILS approach and landing, attributing the issues to a sensor problem.

synopsis: Cessna Citation pilot reported receiving a Ground Proximity Warning while conducting a Visual Approach.
summary: During a night visual approach at 5,000 feet, the crew received GPWS terrain and pull-up alerts despite having the runway and terrain in sight. The pilot attributed the false alarm to the rate of descent, complied with the warning, and completed a normal landing with no unsafe situation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported excessive vectoring from ATC caused a critical fuel situation.
summary: The flight crew declared minimum fuel during extensive vectoring to Miami after ATC added 300 miles and ordered a diversion to Fort Lauderdale following the crew's refusal to fly into a storm cell. The captain advised ATC of the critical fuel situation to land in Miami, resulting in a safe arrival with more fuel than the original plan predicted.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported fuel fumes/odor in the aft cabin resulted in a direct approach and landing at the planned destination.
summary: During cruise at 22,000 ft, flight attendants reported a strong fuel odor causing nausea, prompting the crew to execute odor checklists and divert for a precautionary landing. Post-landing inspections confirmed a major fuel leak penetrating the air conditioning system, leading to immediate passenger deplaning.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a lightning strike while flying 80 miles away from an area of dissipating thunderstorms.
summary: The flight crew encountered a lightning discharge while climbing from TPA through an outflow area despite radar showing no nearby cells. The aircraft was grounded for over 24 hours with 17 defects after the crew declined an ATC-denied reroute request to avoid the weather.

synopsis: B-767 flight crew reported a brake fire had been extinguished after gate arrival.
summary: After a normal landing and shutdown, a brake fire ignited on the left main gear truck, likely caused by recent brake maintenance and hot brakes. The flight crew was not notified until they observed smoke and extinguishing chemicals, resulting in a 1.5-hour delay while the fire department secured the aircraft.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ Captain reported a low altitude alert from ATC while on approach to MSP.
summary: The Pilot Flying descended below the glideslope during a visual approach due to ATC clearance changes and workload, while the Pilot Monitoring arrested the descent at 1000 ft AGL. The unstabilized approach was continued after an ATC low altitude alert, resulting in a safe landing despite configuration errors and automation issues.

synopsis: First Officer reported problems with nose wheel steering and gear disagree lights after take off.
summary: The flight crew experienced nose gear vibration, a gear disagree warning, and steering inoperative messages after takeoff due to four failed gear sensors. They returned to the origin airport for a precautionary landing with fire services standing by, using rudder and differential thrust to exit the runway before maintenance grounded the aircraft.

synopsis: Flight crew reported entering holding with the wrong direction of turns and did not notice their airspeed reducing to near stall speed.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the crew improperly entered a hold at fix ZZZ due to rushing FMS setup, causing an unintended turn and thrust reduction that degraded airspeed to within 8 knots of a high-altitude stall. The pilot monitoring failed to notice the speed loss while managing the hold entry, though power was increased before a stall occurred.

synopsis: B737 Flight Crew reported issues with the FMC fuel burn computations.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced erratic FMS fuel predictions and waypoint times caused by managed speed mode using Cost Index. Switching to hard-coded speeds in the VNAV pages immediately resolved the computer errors, allowing the flight to continue normally.

synopsis: Beech 1900 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing an unusual vibration that may have been related to an earlier wake turbulence encounter.
summary: After departing SDF, the pilot and First Officer encountered suspected wake turbulence at 3,000ft, causing violent vibration and oscillation. They returned for a precautionary landing to allow maintenance inspection due to concerns of potential aircraft damage or malfunction.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 First Officer reported a flight control malfunction with the ailerons.
summary: During climb out at 3,000 feet, the Captain reported abnormal aileron force, which the First Officer confirmed as double normal. Despite no system faults, the crew diverted and landed uneventfully after notifying ATC and dispatch.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported breaking off the approach to MCO when a wake turbulence encounter contributed to a track deviation during localizer intercept.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft on a 90-degree base leg to ILS 17L at MCO encountered severe wake turbulence while descending at 210 KIAS. The turbulence caused an autopilot disconnect and localizer overshoot, requiring a 360-degree turn to re-establish the approach.

synopsis: Flight crew reported encountering severe turbulence and a downdraft causing excursion from assigned altitude.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain encountered moderate turbulence and a downdraft at FL360 near ORM, causing an uncommanded descent to 35,250 feet and rapid airspeed increase. The pilot disconnected the autopilot to manually regain control, and the aircraft returned to FL360 without exceeding airframe limits.

synopsis: EMB-145XR pilot reported that a 'Pitch Trim' EICAS warning has appeared during several flights on the same aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a recurring main pitch trim EICAS warning on an aircraft with a known history of this malfunction. Despite maintenance inspections and QRH procedures, the issue persisted during climb, forcing a return to the gate and prompting a call for a ferry flight to a maintenance base.

synopsis: PA28 instructor reported three traffic conflicts requiring evasive action.
summary: During initial descent to KAPA after a training flight, the pilot and student received two TCAS alerts from a southbound aircraft that turned northwest. The pilot executed an aggressive evasive maneuver that nearly violated Denver Class B airspace, though ATC later confirmed no violation occurred.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reported while on a VOR-A non-precision approach, specifying intentions to execute the missed approach, being cleared by ATC to land on a specific runway.
summary: During an IFR VOR A practice approach, the crew flew a low approach and executed a missed approach at minimums after Tower cleared them for Runway 19 but stated no landing was intended. The crew was reprimanded for not circling to Runway 19, though they maintained the ambiguous clearance and approach design did not require a landing.

synopsis: Citabria pilot reported a wind gust resulting in a ground loop during landing rollout.
summary: The pilot landed a Citabria at ZZZ and ground looped while rolling out at 15 knots after a gust of wind caught the aircraft near vacant lots. The plane tipped onto its left side causing minor damage, but there were no injuries or property damage.

synopsis: A Helicopter pilot landing on private property reported their downwash blew a chair over which hit a bystander.
summary: Pilots landing a heavy helicopter at a private facility chose a northeast approach to avoid tailwinds and obstacles. Downwash from the landing blew lawn furniture, striking a bystander in the knee, though the crew was unaware of the minor injury until after departure.

synopsis: Large transport aircraft Captain reported missing a crossing restriction.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Pilot Flying in a cruise aircraft missed a FL270 crossing restriction at TULEG due to overconfidence in VNAV and failure to monitor the descent path. The crew descended late, could not contact ATC due to frequency congestion, and leveled at FL270 after passing the fix.

synopsis: BE9L pilot reported landing on a runway marked closed, but no NOTAM.
summary: The King Air crew diverted to ZZZ due to weather, landing safely after avoiding unmarked runway Xs caused by an overlooked NOTAM. The airport manager apologized for the oversight, removed the debris, and issued a corrective NOTAM before the crew departed.

synopsis: C152 student pilot reported a NMAC and runway incursion by opposite direction departing aircraft.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 30 via CTAF encountered a Turbo Mooney taking off from Runway 12 without communication. The uncontacted Mooney passed approximately 50 feet above and ahead of the departing aircraft during rotation.

synopsis: AS350 Pilot reported starting a descent too early and passing within less than 300 feet of a ridge.
summary: The pilot unintentionally descended below 300 feet AGL while leaving a 1000-foot cruise to reach a planned 1500-foot cruise in mountainous terrain. Radar altimeter indications confirmed the aircraft passed just above 200 feet AGL over a ridge before climbing to 2000 feet AGL.

synopsis: Tecnam P2006T instructor reported traffic making nonstandard traffic pattern entry, resulted in a NMAC.
summary: A training flight with two students on upwind/crosswind legs avoided a mid-air collision when an unreported aircraft crossed their path 30 feet away. The hazard resulted from the intruder failing to report position, entering downwind incorrectly, and not seeing the training aircraft.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported landing in strong crosswinds resulted in a loss of control and runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot soloing a cross-country flight encountered strong crosswinds at ZZZ1, causing a runway excursion on the third landing attempt. The aircraft skidded off the left side of the runway into dirt and onto a taxiway, resulting in minor propeller gauge damage but no injuries.

synopsis: A R44 Pilot reported an encounter with a UAV just before liftoff.
summary: A helicopter pilot encountered a small drone hovering near the rotor system during landing and takeoff at a wedding venue due to a friend operating it without prior coordination. The pilot resolved the conflict with hand signals and executed a max performance takeoff, noting that better ground communication could have prevented the near-mid-air collision.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna pilot reported heading and altitude deviations on an ILS approach due to cockpit distraction.
summary: The pilot hand-flying an ILS approach in IMC lost situational awareness due to loud radio noise, causing localizer and glideslope deviations. After declaring an early missed approach, the pilot landed safely despite Tower concerns regarding the premature call and nearby mountains.

synopsis: Grumman AA-5 pilot reported a loss of control and runway excursion.
summary: The pilot rejected a landing after a hard bounce caused the aircraft to turn right into the grass. A go-around was performed, and post-landing inspection revealed the right wheel fairing broke off, prompting a runway inspection request.

synopsis: Beechcraft pilot reported a near midair collision during initial climb.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision during climb-out at 2,000 feet while denied flight following by Approach. The pilot executed a steep climbing right turn to avoid another aircraft on a collision path, noting Approach failed to warn the other pilot or resolve the conflict.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna instructor pilot reported becoming confused while conducting an instrument approach.
summary: During an IFR training flight in IMC, the instructor and student inadvertently flew a VOR-A approach to Oceanside (KOKB) instead of the cleared Palomar (KCRQ) approach. The error occurred because the student handled communications while the instructor flew, leading to a missed clearance detail and a subsequent missed approach.

synopsis: RV9A pilot reported encountering wake turbulence from a B737 while transiting a MSP arrival area.
summary: A pilot in cruise at 2,700 ft below MSP Class Bravo encountered wake turbulence from a landing 737, resulting in a 2.6G vertical jolt. The pilot attributed the event to being unable to climb due to airspace restrictions and the high volume of landing traffic.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reported encountering thunderstorms enroute that were not displayed in a timely manner on his XM weather datalink.
summary: A pilot flying VFR encountered rapidly building thunderstorms while approaching GREGS intersection, experiencing a 350-foot altitude deviation due to thermal activity despite clear datalink weather. The pilot attributed the situation to delayed XM updates and controller workload, noting that earlier approval for a direct route to TKI would have avoided the congested storm area.

synopsis: ZMA Controller reported confusion relating whether two aircraft could self-separate from each other.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported confusion during Hurricane Hunter operations involving Aircraft X and Y in overlapping non-radar airspace. The incident highlighted training gaps regarding self-separation rules and unclear procedures for protecting arrival airspace, resulting in conflicting instructions and restricted flight paths.

synopsis: NorCal TRACON Controller reported an unsafe situation with a departure off of Livermore airport.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a Low Altitude Alert to Aircraft X departing LVK after the pilot descended from 3,800 to 2,200 feet in response to a Resolution Advisory. The controller attributed the incident to limited radar coverage in the valley and recommended expanding the departure Delta to 4,000 feet.

synopsis: Montgomery Tower Controller reported a runway conflict after clearing an aircraft for takeoff while another aircraft was on short final.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was landing on the same runway during touch-and-go operations. The controller attributed the near-miss to a tower window post obscuring the view and complacency due to low traffic, despite knowing Aircraft X had inoperative Mode C.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported exceeding 250 knots in order to remain separated from an aircraft conducting an approach to a parallel runway.
summary: During an RNAV Z arrival to SJC, the crew executed an abrupt descent and turn to avoid a converging heavy aircraft after ATC assigned visual separation. The pilot hand-flew the aircraft, exceeding 250 knots below 10,000 feet, and completed a visual approach landing ahead of the other aircraft.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported failing to make a crossing restriction on the RNP-Z Runway 20R approach to SNA.
summary: Pilots flying an RNP-Z approach to SNA Runway 20R noticed the aircraft failed to descend automatically after crossing KLEVR at 5000 feet. The Pilot Flying manually selected Vertical Speed to regain the profile, then accepted a visual approach clearance from ATC and landed safely.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported overshooting an altitude restriction on the RNAV (RNP) Z approach to DEN Runway 16R. Lack of mode awareness was cited as contributing.
summary: The pilot descended below the assigned 11,000 feet while managing an RNAV approach to Denver and visual traffic separation. The deviation of approximately 260 feet occurred because the pilot failed to reset the MCP altitude after switching to Vertical Speed mode due to distraction.

synopsis: B737 pilot reported a significant discrepancy between the Captain's and First Officer's airspeed and altitude indications, possibly due to ice contamination in the pitot-static system.
summary: During cruise, a Captain and First Officer experienced altitude and airspeed disagreements caused by suspected ice in the Captain's pitot-static system. After descending to warmer temperatures, instruments normalized, allowing a safe manual landing without auto-throttles.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported safety concern with the current ATC procedures regarding 'Descend Via' clearances without transition, approach or runway information.
summary: Pilots reported recurring issues during IAH arrivals where frequent reroutes and conflicting "Descend Via" clearances caused FMC programming delays and altitude warning confusion. The reporter attributes these safety risks to ATC assigning unclear transitions and standard procedures that force crews to ignore altitude warnings due to varying fleet software limitations.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported declaring minimum fuel with ATC after incurring delay vectors due to unanticipated weather conditions at the destination.
summary: The Captain and crew experienced significant approach delays at 25PD due to unexpected thunderstorms and runway changes, leading to confusion over orbit instructions. With fuel critically low, they declared Minimum Fuel, refused further delays, and were vectored directly to land safely on Runway 17R.

synopsis: Ground Crew reported a near strike with a B787 during pushback due to a communication breakdown with ATC.
summary: The tower failed to alert the pilot of a 787 on the taxiway before issuing a pushback clearance. This resulted in a near ground miss with the 787, which was taxiing at least 30 mph.

synopsis: CRJ Captain reported diverting due to abnormal flight controls.
summary: The pilot reported abnormally heavy flight controls requiring 2–3 times normal input during climb out of GSP, despite normal hydraulic indications and no cautions. The crew diverted to ZZZ due to the abnormal control feel, as the QRH provided no solution, though the landing remained routine.

synopsis: Regional Jet flight crew reported applying water to hot brakes in order to cool the brakes prior to takeoff.
summary: The Pilot in Command and First Officer cooled a hot brake with water after ATC cleared them to open the passenger door on the movement area. They took off without contacting Maintenance Control, though the reporter noted the brake temperature normalized and no undesired aircraft state occurred.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported deviating into restricted airspace without clearance due to severe weather.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that the Captain deviated into Chinese airspace without clearance to avoid severe weather while Taipei coordinated with Chinese ATC. After Chinese ATC rejected the deviation, the crew advised ATC of the situation and returned to Taiwan airspace five minutes later once the weather cleared.

synopsis: Airbus flight crew reported smelling residual fumes from an APU oil leak repair upon entering the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that a First Officer detected residual fumes from an APU oil leak, prompting a crew assessment before flight. The reporter recommends better particle sniffers, protective equipment for mechanics, and improved fume evaluation procedures to ensure safety.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported refusing the flight due to unresolved multiple write-ups.
summary: A standby flight attendant refused to work Flight X after the Captain reported unresolved left wing fuel tank maintenance issues and multiple write-ups. The crew member contacted the Operations Center base manager due to safety concerns, was removed from the flight, and the aircraft was subsequently taken out of service.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported several HAZMAT shipping errors.
summary: A ground employee reported multiple shipping documentation errors, including incorrect Airway Bills, mismatched piece counts, and improper hazardous goods labeling. The reporter attributed these mistakes to personal distractions caused by recent family deaths and home break-ins.

synopsis: Kitfox pilot reported minor damage after a forced landing following a low altitude power loss related to vapor lock.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss due to vapor lock during takeoff from a gravel bar, forcing an immediate landing. Excessive braking caused the Kitfox to flip, resulting in a broken propeller and wing tear, but the pilot was uninjured and repaired the aircraft for flight the next day.

synopsis: Private pilot reported almost hitting a skydiver during descent.
summary: A pilot descending in Class B airspace toward HHR at 2,000 feet MSL executed an evasive left turn to avoid a person in a harness and helmet. The pilot reported the near-miss to SoCal Approach and Hawthorne Tower, noting the object was unidentified but likely a parachutist or para-plane.

synopsis: A Cessna 206 pilot reported experiencing engine roughness while feeding from the left fuel tank, which subsequently was found to be missing a fuel cap.
summary: The pilot experienced partial engine power loss during descent due to fuel starvation caused by a missing left fuel cap. After declaring an emergency and landing safely, the missing cap was recovered, the tank refilled, and the flight resumed after confirming normal engine operation.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported descending below minimums on an instrument approach.
summary: The pilot attempted an RNAV 29 approach to Tracy (TKC) in broken clouds and initially executed a missed approach. Driven by "get-there-itis" and advanced avionics, the pilot descended below the MDA to 290 ft AGL, visually acquired the runway, and landed safely.

synopsis: Cessna 210 pilot reported a temporary loss of engine power due to improper fuel tank management.
summary: The pilot conducting post-maintenance engine tests forgot to switch fuel tanks while descending to 3,500 feet, causing an engine stoppage east of ZZZ1. After troubleshooting and switching tanks, the engine recovered, allowing a safe landing with adequate fuel remaining.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Tower Controller In Charge reported not realizing an aircraft was on a IFR clearance and observed the Local Controller use improper procedures resulting in the aircraft being below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: The Tower Controller in Charge and Local Controller issued a go-around and left traffic pattern clearance to an IFR aircraft on a GPS/RNAV approach, inadvertently directing it below the 2,900-foot MVA. The controller attributed the error to failing to verify the aircraft's IFR status or offer a missed approach procedure before assigning the low-altitude turn.

synopsis: NorCal TRACON Controller reported vectoring an aircraft below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: The controller managed Aircraft X, Y, and Z during approaches to SJC Runway 12R and 12L. Aircraft X failed to intercept the ILS due to equipment issues, forcing the controller to cancel Aircraft Y's approach and issue a 4,000-foot MVA to maintain separation.

synopsis: Fairbanks Controller reported having a flight of aircraft below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude and waiting until it went into an area of higher terrain. Reporter also stated the flight additionally descended below another MVA and reported doing so.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing mixed VFR/IFR fighter traffic experienced radar data entry failures while decombining sectors. Aircraft X descended below the assigned 060 altitude into lower Minimum Vectoring Altitudes, prompting the controller to issue a new 040 clearance without issuing a safety alert due to high workload.

synopsis: A Boeing 777 pilot reported an electrical system anomaly that was successfully managed despite ambiguous Flight Manual and MEL guidance.
summary: During climb out, the crew experienced a right generator and IDG failure, disconnecting the unit and starting the APU. Although the MEL required APU use for the flight, the crew, Dispatch, and Maintenance Control agreed via conference call that the APU was not required, citing vague checklist wording regarding "if available."

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported an intoxicated passenger, whose erratic behavior in flight resulted in the flight diverting to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: Pilots and flight attendants boarded an aircraft with a passenger cleared by police and a supervisor despite initial intoxication concerns. The passenger later became unruly, threatened suicide, and required restraint, forcing an emergency diversion to ZZZ where authorities removed him.

synopsis: ERJ First Officer reported receiving a Ground Proximity Warning while conducting a visual approach with the terrain in sight.
summary: The crew received a GPWS terrain warning while descending for approach into ZZZ due to a ridge. The Captain manually climbed to clear the terrain before resuming descent, noting they should have maintained Minimum Safe Altitude until crossing the ridge.

synopsis: Bombardier Challenger 650 flight crew reported a failure of the horizontal stabilizer trim.
summary: While cruising at 4,000 feet and 250 knots, the pilot encountered stab trim and Mach trim amber CAS messages and lost stabilizer trim control. The aircraft was diverted and landed with reduced flaps, requiring a minimum speed of 150 knots to maintain elevator pitch control.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported being notified on arrival of a HAZMAT violation.
summary: A ramp agent at ZZZ informed the flight crew after arrival that a bag containing an attached lithium-ion battery was unloaded from the main cargo bay. The pilot reported this as a fire hazard caused by the failure to remove the battery or gate-check the device, noting the crew was not notified prior to flight.

synopsis: Boeing 757 flight crew reported a false 'L Eng Shutdown' warning message during the takeoff roll, resulting in a high-speed rejected takeoff, and a return to the gate.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 120–130 knots due to a false left engine shutdown EICAS alert, though the engine remained running. Subsequent brake binding prevented taxiing, requiring ARFF inspection and maintenance to push the aircraft free before towing it to the gate for uneventful deplaning.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that after landing both engines were unresponsive to throttle input.
summary: After landing, the flight crew experienced unresponsive engines stuck at 20.2% N1 with illuminated reverser and engine control lights. Maintenance later identified a bad Engine Accessory Unit (EAU) causing six thrust reverser stow faults, though engine control was regained after manually selecting EECS to ALTN.

synopsis: PA44 pilot reported continuing in unsafe weather conditions following several suggestions to the instructor pilot.
summary: A student pilot and instructor encountered severe turbulence while attempting to beat an approaching storm during a training flight. The student reported that continuing the landing without diverting or requesting an instrument approach was unsafe due to the risk of microbursts and downdrafts.

synopsis: Denver TRACON Controller reported airspace issues relating to weather and improper procedure.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a Traffic Management Coordinator ordered them to manage aircraft deviating into DR4 airspace despite safety memos prohibiting non-standard operations. This resulted in the controller losing situational awareness, with some aircraft exceeding 17,000 feet and one arriving without a proper point-out or data block.

synopsis: Center Controller reported airspace violations due to another sector approving point outs in which they should not have approved.
summary: A radar controller and a trainee in Sector 10/11 inadvertently approved their own automated point-out for Aircraft X climbing to FL410, causing the aircraft to enter Sector 8/9 airspace without receiving sector approval. The incident occurred because the system's data block indicator did not distinguish between approvals made by the initiating versus the receiving sector.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a track deviation occurred on the RNAV (RNP) Z Approach to 20R in SNA when the First Officer failed to close a discontinuity.
summary: The crew flying an OHSEA 1 arrival into SNA experienced an FMC discontinuity error at KLEVR while attempting an RNAV (RNP) Z 20R approach due to a NOTAMed ILS. This caused an LNAV disconnect and track divergence, prompting the controller to vector them for a visual approach to runway 20R.

synopsis: B737NG First Officer reported a track deviation occurred following a last minute clearance change to the RNAV (RNP) Y Approach to Runway 8R in IAH.
summary: The pilot flying an NNCEE 1 arrival switched from ILS 8R to RNAV (RNP) Y RWY 9 but failed to execute the HOWLN transition turn. ATC noted the aircraft was off course and cleared the crew for a visual approach to RWY 9.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: First Officer reported a passengers' cell phone became lost in cabin on inbound flight creating a potential fire hazard. Maintenance ultimately retrieved prior to departure.
summary: The Captain and a crew member refused to depart on an ETOPS segment after maintenance planned to defer retrieving a lost passenger cellphone lodged behind a cabin panel. Citing the risk of an unmanageable Li-ion battery fire during the long overwater flight, they insisted maintenance locate and remove the device before departure.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ Captain reported erroneous GPWS Terrain Warning.
summary: Pilots flying an ILS Runway 05 approach into OAJ received a GPWS terrain warning at 2100 MSL while established on course. They assessed the alert as erroneous due to Day VMC conditions and no visible obstacles, landing safely before advising maintenance.

synopsis: ERJ145 captain reported reaching a critical fuel state due to deteriorating weather conditions at the destination airport, and subsequent difficulty finding a suitable alternate.
summary: The Captain and a trainee First Officer diverted to alternate ZZZ3 after a missed approach at ZZZ left them below BINGO fuel. The Captain attributed the situation to an uncooperative dispatcher who refused fuel calculations, despite the Captain's admission of omitting current fuel data in requests.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported that an ECAM message appeared 'F/CTL Flaps Lock' during climb.
summary: The pilot reported a "F/CTL Flaps Lock" ECAM during climb from ZZZ, causing an overspeed and requiring a return to land safely. Maintenance later found severe flap track wear and missing parts, attributing the unairworthy condition to previous faults being cleared by computer resets without physical inspection.

synopsis: A Cessna 402 pilot reported an oil system pressure anomaly during climb out, which resulted in an air return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced steadily decreasing right engine oil pressure during climb out. They cancelled IFR, returned to the departure airport for a landing, and notified maintenance.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported poor taxi line markings and lack of lighting in an area where multiple runways converge.
summary: The flight crew taxiing for departure on Runway 08R nearly entered Runway 12 due to poor taxi line markings and a lack of lead-in or REIL lights in the dark. Although they eventually reached the correct runway after ATC intervention, the incident highlighted the risk of following the left line where it splits toward the wrong runway.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported descending for an approach prior to receiving clearance and then being vectored below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude by ATC.
summary: The flight crew and ATC were involved during a visual approach to Boise 28R where haze and sun glare prevented traffic sighting. ATC issued a turn to heading 190 before the aircraft reached the 6500 ft minimum vectoring altitude, causing an altitude deviation alert.

synopsis: A Pilot reported several instances of VFR Flight plans being dropped from the system when filed electronically in Alaska
summary: A pilot reported that VFR flight plans filed electronically via Foreflight and [Company] were deleted before reaching Alaska FSS, despite receiving confirmation. This system incompatibility leaves pilots falsely believing their flight plans are active, creating a risk of missing aircraft with no alerting service.

synopsis: Experimental Aircraft pilot reported engine roughness and unexplained power loss.
summary: The pilot experienced unexplained power loss and roughness during a brief flight above the airport, prompting a power-off landing. The cause remains uncertain, with possibilities including inaccurate fuel measurements, bad fuel computer data, or debris, though the engine ran normally during the taxi back.

synopsis: C172 Student and Instructor reported a NMAC airborne conflict in the traffic pattern.
summary: A student pilot and evaluator were cleared for Runway 12C but were later told by the tower to go around for Runway 12R due to a conflicting aircraft. The reporter attributes the incident to the tower controller's error in believing they had issued a 12R clearance, a conclusion later confirmed by the tower manager after reviewing recordings.

synopsis: Oakland Oceanic Controller reported a loss of separation between two aircraft.
summary: An ATC controller reported that Aircraft X climbed from FL230 to FL400 without IFR clearance, causing a potential loss of separation with Aircraft Y at FL370. The conflict occurred due to communication failures preventing the issuance of a lower altitude restriction before Aircraft X reached FL400.

synopsis: Tracon Controllers reported a Frontline Manager not taking control of a situation, due to staffing and the Frontline Managers lack of training.
summary: An air traffic controller at ZZZ TRACON failed to separate a medical emergency diversion (Aircraft X) from Aircraft Y on parallel runways, resulting in a side-by-side approach. The reporter attributes this error to the controller's inaction and the supervisor's lack of terminal radar training and certification, which prevented timely intervention.

synopsis: Two Tower Controllers reported a P180 failed to change frequencies, which resulted in maintaining an altitude which triggered a low altitude alert.
summary: Local Control West cleared Aircraft X for takeoff from Runway 1L, but the pilot requested a return, then changed course to continue outbound on heading 300. The aircraft triggered a low altitude alert and flew at 2600 MSL within 300 feet of 2300 MSL obstructions northwest of the airport.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported departing with a tailwind component that exceeded limits, citing time pressure and rapidly changing weather conditions as contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew of an A330 departed Newark during gusty winds and a shifting gust front, taking off with a reported 22-knot tailwind component exceeding the 15-knot limit. The crew attributed the performance exceedance to high task loading and a failure to recalculate takeoff data after the wind direction shifted from crosswind to tailwind.

synopsis: BE-400 First Officer reported being advised of fuel spilling from the right wing.
summary: During preflight, line crew reported fuel spilling from the right wing. The pilot stopped the spill by cycling the fuel transfer switch, and maintenance suspected a low battery prevented the valve from closing.

synopsis: A321 pilot reported that the transponder was deferred due to a missing digit.
summary: Pilots departed with an inoperative transponder display digit under an MEL, filing for FL280 to avoid RVSM airspace after obtaining ATC approval. The reporter questioned regulatory compliance and noted a lack of guidance on transponder modes or emergency code procedures during the flight.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported a track deviation occurred following a late clearance change to the RNAV (RNP) Z Approach to Runway 34R at DEN.
summary: The flight crew, while on the FRNCH3 arrival, failed to verify FMC sequencing after switching to the RNAV (RNP) Z RWY 34R approach, causing the AFDS to miss the MCMUL RF turn and track to KALME. The pilot manually re-established the course, and the aircraft was cleared for a visual approach to land safely on Runway 34R.

synopsis: A gate agent reported that due to wet conditions the agent's hands slipped and the loading bridge started to fall towards the aircraft.
summary: A ramp agent injured their back while lowering a passenger loading bridge in rain when malfunctioning springs caused the bridge to drop. The agent manually stopped the bridge from striking the aircraft, completed the task, and was subsequently placed on On the Job Injury status.

synopsis: An air carrier First Officer reported that artificial departure times showed a pilot to be legal for a trip when in fact the pilot was not legal.
summary: An A320 First Officer on reserve was assigned a flight by Crew Scheduling using inaccurate computer-generated sign-in times that ignored his two-hour drive time. Although the pilot reported the assignment was illegal due to Reserve Duty Period limits, the flight was cancelled by the Captain after the pilot arrived at the airport.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported that the new procedure as to when to use the landing checklist has increased the workload during approach.
summary: A Line Check Airmen reported that moving the landing checklist call to after final flaps at 1200–1000 feet causes missed checklists due to high workload from landing clearances and pending missed approach altitude settings. The change was implemented to assist non-Electronic Check List users but conflicts with standard approach procedures.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported that the new procedure as to when to use the Landing Checklist has increased the workload during approach.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring on a B737 approach at 700ft discovered the landing checklist was incomplete, with speed brakes un-armed and ignition off. The crew corrected the configuration before 500ft, but the pilot attributed the error to new procedures causing excessive workload and distraction during the approach.

synopsis: Widebody transport Captain reported that they were instructed to go-around due to base under attack.
summary: A four-pilot crew with a mechanic and loadmaster diverted from a war zone airport during an Initial Operating Experience flight after a base attack forced a go-around. Subsequent diversions to alternate airports were complicated by security threats, lack of handler support, and duty time limits, leading the crew to press on to a final destination to avoid resting in a high-threat environment.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that CLT has an inaccurate taxiway signage and diagram.
summary: The flight crew landed at CLT and experienced confusion due to an inaccurate taxi diagram showing Echo 13 on the wrong side of November taxiway. This chart error caused a delay in contacting ramp control after entering the ramp area, though the aircraft eventually reached the gate safely.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after takeoff due to a Fuel Channel Fail EICAS messages and being unable to maintain normal fuel balance.
summary: The flight crew experienced a fuel crossfeed failure shortly after takeoff, causing rapid fuel imbalance and requiring an immediate return to the departure airport. They executed the QRH checklist, used slips to manage the imbalance, and landed safely with significant aileron trim required due to the fuel system failure.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported she was injured in turbulence while performing duties.
summary: A flight attendant serving beverages on a flight to LGA was injured when unexpected severe turbulence caused the aircraft to drop approximately 200 feet. The attendant struck the ceiling, was wedged between seats, and filed an On the Job Injury report after landing.

synopsis: B737 Maintenance Technician reported that the flight crew ignored the safety requirement while maintenance was working on the aircraft.
summary: While maintenance personnel jacked the aircraft to replace nose landing gear tires, the flight crew entered the flight deck and attempted to use the MCDU despite a "Do Not Operate" safety tag. The crew's refusal to leave endangered ground staff and the aircraft, though the plane was eventually released after a supervisor intervened.

synopsis: B757 Maintenance Controller reported that the maintenance procedures were ambiguous whether to require a test or confirmation flight.
summary: A mechanic reported conflicting maintenance documentation regarding flight requirements after replacing all four pitot probes during a C Check. The contradiction between the Job Instruction Card and an Engineering document caused confusion over whether a Group II Test Flight or Group I Operational Confirmation was required, leading to incorrect log entries.

synopsis: A Mooney Pilot reported that a Helicopter did a hover taxi less that 50 feet behind his aircraft.
summary: A pilot reported that while their aircraft was parked on the ramp, a turbine helicopter hover taxied and landed less than 50 feet away, causing full flight control surface deflection for 45 seconds. The pilot attributed this unsafe situation to the ground controller's failure to enforce safe distances and the helicopter pilot's irresponsibility.

synopsis: An EMB500 Pilot reported that upon landing and applying the brakes it seemed like nothing happened.
summary: The pilot of a Phenom 100 overran a wet runway at an uncontrolled field after experiencing a perceived brake failure and activating emergency brakes. While the pilot believed the brakes were inoperative, investigators concluded the event resulted from pilot error following an anti-skid loss that required manual braking.

synopsis: Gyroplane pilot reported a NMAC with a light aircraft in the pattern at X26 airport.
summary: A pilot conducting a proficiency check in a Gyroplane on short final at Sebastian Municipal encountered a Cherokee attempting to overtake on the right in a right-hand traffic pattern. Both pilots took evasive action to avoid a collision when the aircraft came within 100 feet of each other.

synopsis: Pilatus PC-12 Captain reported a failure of the landing gear to retract normally, necessitating an alternate extension method and return to the departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer experienced a HYDR caution and unsecured landing gear shortly after takeoff from ZZZ. They successfully extended the gear using the emergency handle, returned to ZZZ with priority handling, and landed safely with all three green lights.

synopsis: GA pilot reported aircraft contacted a power line during descent into airport at night.
summary: The pilot struck a power line at 150 feet AGL while descending to ZZZ because runway lights failed to activate and no NOTAM existed. The pilot executed a go-around, confirmed the aircraft was flyable, and landed safely, attributing the incident to the dark airport and excessive confidence in situational awareness.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported the pilot side window departed the aircraft in flight when the side door was opened for skydive operations.
summary: During a skydiving mission in a C182, the pilot's side window departed the airframe after the passenger door was opened at altitude. The reporter attributes the failure to rapid pressure differential or airflow snapping the hinges, noting the window likely landed in a forested area.

synopsis: DA40 pilot reported the rear passenger departed the aircraft in flight after reaching back to latch it and grabbing the wrong lever.
summary: The pilot reported that the rear passenger door flew off at 75 knots and 1,500 feet AGL because it was closed but not latched. The pilot accidentally grabbed the wrong lever while attempting to secure the latch, but the aircraft returned safely.

synopsis: J3 pilot reported executing a safe and damage-free forced landing after the engine failed in flight.
summary: The pilot of a J3C-65 experienced a loud bang and rough engine operation during cruise, followed by a complete engine failure on approach. The pilot executed a safe forced landing with no damage to the aircraft or property, though no emergency radio calls were made.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the revised approach had been loaded into the FMC prior to the activation date.
summary: The flight crew discovered a discrepancy between Jeppesen charts and the FMC arrival due to an early database update before descent. They verified their position using chart distances after the TWONA fix, resulting in an uneventful arrival despite the waypoint changes.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported that the Electronic Log Book is cluttered with Carry Forward items, causing critical items to be missed.
summary: A pilot reported that conflicting definitions of long-term maintenance items between the Flight Manual and Maintenance caused years-old defects to clutter the Electronic Log Book's short-term section. The reporter attributed this safety risk to unresolved IT programming issues and a lack of operational control over software development priorities.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported an oil filter message after engine start that cleared, then a second oil filter message at top of descent.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right engine oil filter EICAS warning at FL330, requiring engine shutdown per the QRH. They completed a single-engine approach and landing safely, arriving 25 minutes late with no severe damage or vibrations reported.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported the left engine performed at a degraded rate during descent and landing.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported left engine thrust degradation and erratic response near Top of Descent, which stabilized after the crew executed the Engine Indication Fluctuation checklist to disable EECs. The aircraft completed a normal landing with partial left engine power without notifying ATC.

synopsis: B757 Captain expressed concern with ATC procedures during approach to SFO that limited the options for runway separation during landing or a safe go-around should one become necessary.
summary: The pilot reported a tight separation during a visual approach to SFO RWY 28R when a B747 received takeoff clearance while the flight was below 1000 feet AGL. The pilot adjusted configuration and planned a low-altitude breakout turn due to unsafe separation and the controller's unprofessional response.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported that the push-back crew did not follow the SOP and disconnected the tow bar while the brakes were released.
summary: During pushback, the pilot refused to release brakes to assist ground crew with a stuck tow bar but agreed to do so only if the tug remained connected. The ground crew allegedly lied about the connection, disconnected the tow bar without permission after the pilot released brakes, violating standard operating procedures.

synopsis: CRJ Flight Crew reported that during climb the pilot flying spun the thumb wheel too fast causing the rate of climb to become too high.
summary: During 200 differences training, a First Officer flying the departure incorrectly adjusted the vertical speed selector, causing an unintended descent and acceleration to 240 knots. The Check Airman took control, corrected the flight path, and recovered the aircraft after losing approximately 300 feet.

synopsis: CRJ Captain reported that a false terrain warning sounded during descent.
summary: The flight crew received a terrain warning at 2,500 feet while descending for an RNAV approach in IMC, prompting a climb to 4,000 feet. ATC confirmed no terrain existed, and the crew landed safely after deferring the GPWS, concluding the warning was erroneous.

synopsis: EMB-140 flight crew reported responding to a TCAS Resolution Advisory during climb triggered by a military fighter.
summary: The flight crew received a Traffic Alert and Resolution Advisory during initial climb after takeoff due to a USAF T-38 entering an overhead break maneuver. The pilot stopped the climb to avoid the conflict, attributing the incident to ATC issuing takeoff clearance while airborne traffic was not well clear.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported becoming distracted with a confusing clearance then noticing the autopilot disconnected due to low airspeed.
summary: The pilot spent excessive time troubleshooting a non-existent FMS fix for the ILS approach, causing distraction from flight monitoring. This led to an autopilot disengagement, low airspeed, and altitude loss, requiring manual intervention to recover before ATC vectored the aircraft back to the approach.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported issues with the electrical system in cruise resulted in a diversion.
summary: Pilots reported multiple system failures and electrical arcing at cruise altitude 370, including hydraulic pump, anti-ice, air pack, and display unit faults. Following ECAM procedures and ATC notification, the aircraft was diverted.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported observing a Center of Gravity warning after takeoff.
summary: During climb through FL 320, the flight crew received an Excess Aft CG warning and transferred 1,500 pounds of fuel to the center tank using Trim TK Mode. The aircraft leveled at FL 340 with normal CG and pitch trim, and the remainder of the flight was uneventful.

synopsis: ERJ-135 First Officer reported receiving a 'LG/LEVER DISAGREE' message on descent due to an apparent nose landing gear down lock issue.
summary: The flight crew aborted a visual approach at ZZZ due to a nose gear disagreement warning and red indication at 5,000 feet. After a low pass confirmed the gear was not fully locked, the captain executed a smooth gear-up landing on runway XXL, which resulted in no collapse but required maintenance to address the unsecured nose gear.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported problems with emergency row passengers and a Customer Service Representative not moving the people out of the emergency row.
summary: A flight attendant reported that two passengers in exit row seats could not demonstrate understanding of evacuation procedures, yet a supervisor approved them to remain. The crew was concerned about safety, but the supervisor closed the door and departed before the issue was resolved.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported a loss of engine power led to an off field landing.
summary: A pilot cruising at 6,000 feet experienced engine failure due to fuel flow issues and lost vacuum instruments while descending below 3,100 feet. Unable to see landmarks through clouds or restart the engine, the pilot attempted a forced landing in darkness and struck a tree before impacting the ground.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported an inaccurate METAR prevented continuing to the airport VFR when the weather was IFR and getting worse.
summary: A helicopter PIC flying VFR encountered inadvertent IMC near TTN due to rapidly lowering ceilings that contradicted reported METARs. The crew diverted to PHL Approach for an IFR clearance and executed an ILS approach, breaking out at 800 feet.

synopsis: PA-28 flight instructor reported the pilot in training lost control during landing, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot and instructor landed a light aircraft in gusting 30-knot winds that shifted from left to right crosswind, preventing the right wheel from touching down. The aircraft drifted left off the runway into the grass, causing no injuries or damage but requiring ATC to close the runway for removal.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported becoming disoriented and committing several airspace violations.
summary: A fatigued pilot planning a westbound flight from Phoenix to the LA Basin misidentified VOR frequencies, causing a deviation through restricted areas, MOAs, and the ADIZ into Mexican airspace. After radar contact near MCAS Yuma, the pilot returned to US airspace without penalty, attributing the incident to fatigue and "Get-There-Itis."

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi First Officer reported a communication breakdown with the Captain while avoiding airborne traffic.
summary: During climb out of 7,000 feet, the non-flying pilot warned the pilot flying about traffic at 8,500 feet, but the pilot flying refused to stop the turn due to a CRM breakdown. The aircraft continued climbing toward the traffic, which was only 1,500 feet above and 0.5 miles away, without any avoidance action.

synopsis: GA pilot reported performing an instrument approach in a VFR-only aircraft.
summary: The ATP-rated pilot flew a non-IFR certified aircraft into ZZZ under deteriorating weather, executing an RNAV (GPS) XX approach despite the aircraft's limitations. The pilot identified the primary cause as the decision to continue based on a forecast that did not materialize, resulting in an unauthorized instrument approach.

synopsis: An experimental aircraft pilot reported that the aircraft ground-looped during takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot reported a ground loop incident. No specific aircraft, phase of flight, cause, or outcome details were provided in the narrative.

synopsis: Miami TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict with an arrival into Fort Lauderdale and a VFR just below the Class Bravo.
summary: Miami Approach stopped Aircraft X's descent at 3,500 feet and altered its base turn to avoid a VFR aircraft climbing through 2,700 feet near the Runway 9 ILS. The controller attributed this dangerous conflict to inadequate Bravo airspace design allowing VFR traffic to fly one foot below arrival glideslopes.

synopsis: Miami TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict with a VFR aircraft and an air carrier inbound to Fort Lauderdale.
summary: Approach held Aircraft X above a rapidly descending VFR aircraft transitioning around the Bravo at FLL, causing an unstable approach. The pilot attributed this unsafe situation to inadequate Class C airspace protections that allow VFR traffic to cross parallel finals without ATC advisories.

synopsis: Atlanta Center Controller reported an unsafe situation relating to traffic, weather, and Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: Air Traffic Control issued a visual approach to Aircraft X, which subsequently executed a go-around due to wind shear. To avoid heavy precipitation, the controller vectored Aircraft X below the Minimum IFR Altitude, prioritizing weather avoidance over terrain clearance.

synopsis: Miami TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict with a general aviation aircraft and an air carrier inbound to Fort Lauderdale.
summary: A Final Controller maneuvered Aircraft X inbound to FLL RWY 10L to avoid a fast-moving experimental VFR aircraft descending into the sector. The reporter attributes the conflict to inadequate Class C airspace protection that allows VFR traffic to cross final approaches without ATC advisories.

synopsis: Miami TRACON Controller reported a problem with VFR aircraft flying too close to final and requesting an airspace change.
summary: An air traffic controller observed an experimental VFR aircraft rapidly descending through both final approach paths at FLL, forcing a deviation of an IFR aircraft. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to inadequate Class C airspace protections that allow VFR traffic to cross finals without ATC advisories.

synopsis: MIA TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict and a request to change the Miami Class Bravo.
summary: A VFR aircraft climbed under Miami's Class Bravo airspace and tracked 1 foot below the glideslope near the 10-mile fix, forcing a controller to tighten a feeder final turn for safety. The pilot attributed this unsafe situation to inadequate Bravo airspace design that allows VFR traffic to fly directly beneath heavy arrival paths.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Miami TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict due to a VFR aircraft climbing into the FLL final.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a VFR aircraft climbing under FLL finals forced an inbound IFR aircraft to stop its descent, resulting in a high, unstable, and unsafe approach. The controller attributed this hazard to inadequate Class C airspace protections allowing VFR traffic to cross final approach paths without ATC advisories.

synopsis: Pilot reported confusion between what they did and what the Controller expected them to do on an RNAV arrival.
summary: The flight crew encountered conflicting instructions during the ZPLYN 3 arrival into DEN after canceling the approach clearance. The controller requested a heading vector while the crew remained on the LNAV track, highlighting a need for simple altitude and heading guidance when FMC reprogramming is no longer feasible.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported confusion with an ATC ground clearance and possible Controller personality related problems.
summary: After landing, the crew received a taxi clearance to XX1, XX2, and XX3, which they read back without correction. The controller later claimed the crew and another flight had confused each other's calls, though the reporter suspects the controller was the confused party as no traffic conflicts occurred.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported difficulties with weather and ATC communications resulting in a diversion.
summary: The crew climbed to VMC below FL055 after a missed approach but could not contact KZAK or SFO via CPDLC, HF, or SATCOM despite 30+ attempts. They declared PAN, PAN, PAN to reach SFO, observed another flight on TCAS above FL245, and received clearance after a 5–10 minute delay.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a failure of the flaps system after takeoff.
summary: During takeoff, the crew encountered a flap malfunction and QRH table of contents errors, causing confusion before returning to ZZZ. After a high-speed landing following an ATC vectoring issue, maintenance confirmed the flap failure, and the crew was grounded for the day due to stress.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Boeing 787 Captain reported concern about being unable to schedule a trip until several weeks after initial training.
summary: A recently qualified 787 Captain reported an 18-day gap between Initial Operating Experience and their first solo flight. The pilot stated that scheduling delays prevented an earlier trip and expressed concern that this break negatively impacts safety.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported encountering moderate wake turbulence while on descent 15 miles in trail of an A330.
summary: During enroute descent from FL280 to FL200 on HYPER7, the crew encountered moderate wake turbulence from an A330 Heavy 15 miles ahead. The uncoordinated pitch, yaw, and roll movements caused passengers and flight attendants to tumble, but no injuries occurred.

synopsis: Storekeeper reported additional HAZMAT training is required for storeroom personnel.
summary: Storekeepers at ZZZ reported that West side Tool Crib Attendants frequently misidentify parts and falsely declare shipments as non-hazardous. The reporter attributes this risk of undeclared hazardous materials to a lack of training or due diligence by the Attendants.

synopsis: CRJ First Officer reported observing a pneumatic duct overheat warning while in flight.
summary: The crew experienced multiple system warnings, including L AOA heat, L Static heat, and L 10th Duct red alerts, causing a delayed departure and an unscheduled landing at ZZZ. The flight landed safely at flaps 20 after the crew followed QRH procedures to manage the uncorrected duct warning.

synopsis: CRJ First Officer reported that the aircraft never pressurized. Upon roll out an additional engine red oil press low light came on.
summary: The flight crew encountered a cabin altitude warning due to unknown pressurization failure during climb, descending to 4,000 feet for an ILS landing. A subsequent false right engine oil pressure warning caused by a transducer fault led to an engine shutdown, but the aircraft taxied to the gate safely.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported an in flight engine shut-down due to low oil pressure during arrival.
summary: During an RNAV arrival, low oil pressure in engine #2 prompted a shutdown and priority landing. The aircraft landed safely on one engine and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: Embraer 505 Captain reported excessive vibration from the nose landing gear until gear retraction.
summary: The pilot reported strong nose gear vibration on takeoff, which ceased after gear retraction. The pilot refused to fly the aircraft because maintenance only replaced the nose wheel assembly for excessive spin without performing the requested structural vibration checks or gear cycles.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported EICAS messages appeared showing a 'R ENG HI STAGE' followed by 'L ENG HI STAGE'.
summary: The crew experienced dual engine high stage indications at FL320, causing a loss of pressurization and an urgent descent to 10,000 feet. They landed, shut down both engines due to suspected maintenance issues, and were towed to the gate after a tug malfunction.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported a heading deviation after takeoff due to three runway changes during taxi and the failure to input the latest change into the FMC.
summary: The flight crew experienced task saturation due to three runway changes during taxi at ZZZ, leading to an incorrect runway entry in the flight management system. This caused the Flight Director to command a left turn after takeoff instead of the required right turn, which the pilots corrected after discovering the error while airborne.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported heading and glide path deviation due to a cruise ship in the flight path for landing.
summary: The crew encountered an unstable approach during an RNAV arrival in IMC due to a tall ship blocking the flight path and unexpected aircraft acceleration. The Captain manually maneuvered to avoid the vessel, corrected airspeed and descent rate deviations, and executed a safe landing after clearing the obstruction.

synopsis: B787 First Officer reported receiving notification after takeoff of an overweight condition for an intersection departure.
summary: The flight crew received an ATC message two minutes after takeoff claiming they were 1,500 pounds overweight for the intersection departure. The pilot attributed this to a 6,200-pound fuel system reporting error and criticized the communication during a sterile cockpit phase.

synopsis: A321 pilot reported a loss of 400 feet of altitude due to autopilot failure, weather, and turbulence.
summary: Pilots in cruise at FL350 encountered moderate turbulence from unknown weather, causing airspeed fluctuations and a 400-foot altitude loss despite autopilot engagement. ATC queried the deviation but confirmed no separation conflict after the crew filed a PIREP and recovered to assigned altitude.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported inadvertently entering into the FMS values that resulted in a crossing restriction not made.
summary: The pilot deleted mandatory altitude restrictions at NADEE and KNIGT waypoints while descending via the SNKPT2 RNAV arrival, causing the aircraft to level off at 9,300 feet. The error was corrected by switching to vertical speed mode and receiving a new clearance that removed the missed KNIGT altitude constraint.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CE-560XL Captain reported on approach a right main gear unsafe indication was present.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right main gear light failure at the FAF, prompting a go-around and emergency gear extension procedures. After successfully blowing down the gear and confirming visual indication, they landed safely, evacuated passengers, and towed the aircraft for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: CE-560XL First Officer reported difficulties in extending the landing gear.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right main gear light failure after lowering gear at the FAF. They successfully deployed the gear using the emergency blow-down procedure, landed safely, and evacuated passengers before towing the aircraft for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: CL604 flight crew reported that mistakes loading the approach appropriately in the FMS resulted in lining up on the right localizer even though their FMS was displaying the left.
summary: A flight crew and air traffic controllers experienced a runway misalignment during an RNAV arrival due to non-standard descent clearances and FMS input errors. The crew lined up on the wrong localizer despite FMS display discrepancies, resulting in a go-around and a subsequent safety review.

synopsis: An E170 First Officer reported that there was an inset on the approach plate which included another IAF (initial approach fix) that was missed.
summary: Flight crew descending on the ZEEKK arrival into IAH missed CLSIK and GRUNG fixes due to a non-intuitive Jeppesen chart inset while flying direct to SILLS. ATC advised the error but allowed the landing without incident, attributing the issue to chart design and crew misunderstanding.

synopsis: LA-4 A/B Buccaneer single pilot executing an instrument approach reported that Tower received a low altitude alert warning.
summary: The pilot, experienced in IFR but unfamiliar with this aircraft's ILS, received a low altitude alert from the Tower Controller during an ILS approach to ZZZ in IMC. The alert was caused by the pilot's lack of familiarity with the specific ILS characteristics of the aircraft, which was subsequently corrected.

synopsis: CJ2 and PA28 pilots reported runway incursion resulting in both aircraft taking evasive action.
summary: A Cessna CJ2 pilot on an IFR departure from Runway XX rotated early to avoid a PA28 crossing at high speed without radio calls. The crossing pilot claimed radio failure, while the departing pilot attributed the near-collision to the other aircraft's failure to monitor CTAF or announce its position.

synopsis: ROC Tower Controller and a CRJ-700 flight crew reported problems with the XEROX6 departure which caused an airborne conflict.
summary: A tower trainee cleared two aircraft for takeoff on Runway 4, resulting in a loss of IFR radar separation when Aircraft X deviated from the XEROX6 departure by failing to turn left. Separation was restored through tower-applied visual separation and subsequent radar vectors after the trainee switched Aircraft Y to Departure Control prematurely.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported possibly striking birds after takeoff.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a potential bird strike during takeoff, causing a low oil quantity indication on the left engine. The crew returned for an overweight landing; inspections found no damage, resulting only in a deferred oil indicator and oil service.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported loss of communication with ATC prior to landing.
summary: The crew experienced radio communication failures with BOS Center and PVD Approach while intercepting the LOC for KENTE. They continued the approach using CTAF, landed uneventfully, and relayed their flight plan closure via another aircraft.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported that the First Officer's flight instruments started to malfunction and disagreed with the Captain's side causing a return to their departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced multiple system failures and erroneous FO indications during climbout at 1,500 feet, attributed to a faulty FO Air Data Computer. The crew transferred control to the Captain, completed checklists, and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported that after setting up the cockpit prior to flight, someone came in the cockpit and undid the set-up configuration.
summary: Ground crew connected power and shut down the APU, inadvertently turning off IRS, fuel pumps, battery, emergency lights, and window heat while the flight crew was away. This unauthorized reconfiguration created a safety hazard by leaving the aircraft in an undesirable state for the next flight.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported he is often dispatched with inoperative Wifi which thus restricts the Company's internet based severe weather avoidance tool.
summary: A pilot reported that inoperative WiFi systems on two recent flights prevented access to the WSI weather application during severe convective weather. The pilot argued that this deficiency hindered real-time storm avoidance and increased risk, urging that active WiFi be required for such conditions.

synopsis: Ground personnel reported that due to hand held radios being unuseable, normal work assignments were not being accomplished.
summary: Ramp agents refused to move an aircraft due to a one-hour handheld radio outage, citing safety concerns regarding emergency communication and past incidents. The morning supervisor questioned their refusal after the night supervisor initially instructed them to hold off on the move.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew reported landing without clearance following a wake turbulence encounter. Fatigue was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew landed at LAX on runway 25L without obtaining tower clearance due to fatigue and distraction from wake turbulence avoidance. Approach Control failed to instruct a frequency change, and the crew forgot to switch to Tower, resulting in an unauthorized landing that was later corrected by Tower.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported that the Pilot Reconciliation Report can be accessed electronically.
summary: The pilot reported that relying on electronic Pilot Reconciliation Reports (PRR) via iPad at the gate is unsafe due to poor signal, battery drain, and cockpit workload during pushback. The reporter argues that the paper form must remain to ensure reliable security reconciliation between ground and flight crews.

synopsis: A330 Captain reported a track deviation occurred on a trans-Pacific flight after the CPDLC clearance was not loaded properly.
summary: The pilot of an LAX to ZZZZ flight deviated from a CPDLC clearance during climb after mistakenly deleting revised waypoints while assuming a duplicate uplink. The error occurred because the pilot deleted the new route segment instead of the old one, leading to a controller verification request.

synopsis: B737-800 pilot reported that they had to stop the taxi to avoid a collision with another aircraft being pushed back from an adjacent gate.
summary: The pilot reported a near collision during taxi after another aircraft pushed off a nearby gate and overlapped their wingtip clearance. The crew stopped to avoid impact, contacted Airport Operations to request ramp video preservation, and proceeded without further incident.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported that first flight of the day the Number 2 engine was slow to spool.
summary: The First Officer rejected a rolling takeoff on an Airbus with CFM engines due to abnormal right engine acceleration at 50% N1. The Captain later confirmed normal acceleration during a second attempt with brakes held, allowing a successful departure.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a passenger complained of an injury following wake turbulence during landing.
summary: During landing at LAX Runway 24R, the crew experienced a firm touchdown after entering wake turbulence at 40 ft AGL. A male passenger reported an injury, though the pilot considered the event routine and did not log it or deploy oxygen masks.

synopsis: Embraer ERJ Captain reported that a passenger deplaned and wanted to leave the luggage on the aircraft.
summary: The Captain of a ZZZ to ZZZ1 flight removed a passenger's checked bag after the passenger exhibited erratic behavior and deplaned without a confirmed name. Despite Operations pressure to depart, the Captain exercised authority to remove the bag due to safety concerns regarding the passenger's inconsistent story and unknown identity.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported cleared on to runway by ATC, while traffic on final was mistakenly aligned to same runway.
summary: The crew held short of Runway XX while Aircraft Z was cleared to land on Runway XY but aligned with Runway XX. After the crew crossed the hold short line to comply with a line-up clearance, they alerted Tower, prompting a go-around for Aircraft Z with an uneventful outcome.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported not getting the ILS receiver to tune either via auto-tune or manually during an ILS PRM approach.
summary: Pilots on a post-maintenance delivery flight to ATL could not tune the ILS 08L receiver, which remained frozen in PARK. They completed a visual approach using LNAV/VNAV, deviating left to avoid the NTZ, and landed uneventfully after confirming the ILS failure with ATC.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported a clearance misunderstanding which resulted in an altitude overshoot during arrival into ATL.
summary: The flight crew, operating with an inoperative TCAS, could not conduct a PRM approach into Atlanta, leading to modified clearances and an ATC miscommunication that required a climb from 8,000 to 11,000 feet. Later, moderate wake turbulence caused a 40-degree bank upset, while the crew noted the MEL failed to warn that TCAS is required for PRM approaches.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported losing electrical power and squawking wrong code of 7500.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical failure and avionics flickering enroute from ZZZ, causing intermittent and then total radio loss. After mistakenly squawking 7500 instead of 7600, the crew returned to ZZZ and landed uneventfully using an iPad app for navigation.

synopsis: C150 instructor reported a NMAC while distracted with a fire report.
summary: An instructor and student pilot in a training aircraft experienced a near mid-air collision with a C172 while investigating a fire. The incident occurred because the instructor fixated on the ground, failing to scan for traffic until the opposing aircraft was within 100 meters.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported temporarily losing control of aircraft in turbulence while executing approach into airport.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR approach to ISP encountered sudden, undetected windshear at 2,000 feet that caused a 70-degree bank and 800-foot altitude loss. The crew recovered, completed a visual landing below the glideslope, and reported no aircraft damage despite the lack of weather warnings.

synopsis: C172S Instructor Pilot reported loss of rudder pedal steering during taxi resulting in a taxiway excursion.
summary: A pilot and student experienced a loss of left rudder and brake response while taxiing a training aircraft, causing it to coast off the taxiway into grass. The aircraft was returned to the ramp with sluggish control, and maintenance was notified to inspect the system for damage.

synopsis: Tractor driver reported the tug began to lurch and bounce when the brakes were applied.
summary: During pushback of Aircraft X, a Supertug lurched and bounced violently when brakes were applied, causing the nose gear to rotate 30 degrees. A hydraulic leak and sensor failure prevented cradle opening, leading to the tractor's removal for maintenance due to unaddressed lurching risks.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported ramp personnel gave them the 'clear to taxi signal' with other persons under the aircraft.
summary: The pilot received a 'clear to taxi' signal from ground crew while the aircraft was still connected to the tug and personnel were under the nose. The reporter attributed this error to the ground crew member's lack of understanding of proper pushback procedures.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported the tow bar pin sheared during pushback due to the tug suddenly stopping.
summary: During pushback at ZZZ, a tug stopped abruptly to avoid an airport operations vehicle, causing a bump that sheared the nose gear pin. Maintenance inspected the gear and found no damage, with no injuries reported.

synopsis: EMB-140 First Officer reported flying through final approach course due to non-activation approach mode. After third attempt, PF became re-oriented and executed approach.
summary: The Captain (PF) and First Officer (PM) flew an RNAV XXL approach where the PF failed to activate the approach in the FMS and selected NAV mode prematurely, causing two missed intercepts. ATC vectored the aircraft for a third attempt, which succeeded after the crew requested a direct clearance to a fix to ensure proper FMS sequencing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported discrepancy between Antiskid MEL crew procedures and QRH crew procedure during approach.
summary: The flight crew encountered a confusing MEL regarding an inoperative anti-skid system, which caused an unexpected "speed brake do not arm" light during approach configuration. They executed a go-around to consult the QRH, landed safely with manual speed brake deployment, and recommended clearer MEL language to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: EMB-190 flight crew reported a bleed valve condition which compromised cabin pressurization, necessitating a descent to a lower altitude.
summary: The crew of an aircraft dispatched with Bleed 1 inoperative experienced a Bleed 2 failure at FL200 caused by anti-ice activation, resulting in pressurization loss. They descended to 10,000 feet per ATC clearance, followed the QRH, and completed the flight with no further issues.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported that the OAKES2 STAR will take you below class B airspace if flown at the lower altitude limits.
