summary: During a training approach, a student pilot flew high and fast, prompting the instructor to take control and force a landing to avoid trees during a potential go-around. The aircraft overran the runway into mud but stopped with no injuries or damage to the plane or occupants.

synopsis: PA46 pilot reported a nose landing gear issue after takeoff was the result of a distracted preflight that led to departing with the tow bar attached.
summary: The pilot of a PA46T Piper Meridian took off with a tow bar still attached due to a changed preflight procedure on an icy apron. The bar was dislodged after a low flyby and gear extension at an alternate airport, resulting in only a small dent to the aircraft belly.

synopsis: Tower controllers reported a runway incursion with a departure and a vehicle.
summary: An OJT instructor and trainee cleared Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway XXL while a maintenance truck was still on the runway due to a degraded scan during a discussion about a theoretical APREQ. The truck exited the runway before the aircraft began its takeoff roll, resulting in no collision.

synopsis: Boston Center Controller reported an unsafe operation relating to an opposite direction operation, and being distracted by the government shutdown.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent vector to Aircraft X for a ZUL LOA altitude during an opposite direction departure from YOW but failed to monitor the aircraft due to distraction from government shutdown stress and a busy traffic scenario. The controller noted that increased staffing and reduced stress would have prevented the loss of situational awareness.

synopsis: Huntsville TRACON Controller reported a loss of separation due to one aircraft not hearing the climb clearance. Reporter also stated position should be split, and was worried about money during the government shutdown.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X climbed to 10,000 feet on a conflicting heading with Aircraft Y after hearing the wrong frequency, delaying its climb clearance. The controller issued a 180-degree turn to Aircraft X to increase separation, noting that financial stress and high traffic volume may have contributed to the delayed conflict detection.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported a missed crossing restriction due to a communication breakdown or charting error.
summary: The flight crew on a BANND 2 arrival into OAK descended via clearance but were instructed to maintain 7000 FT after crossing KEENR at 8000 FT. The controller attributed the amended clearance to an incorrect chart altitude, despite no NOTAMs or operational notes being available to the crew.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning when vectored off the charted course approaching TUS.
summary: During the ZONNA1 arrival, ATC vectors to 265° while descending to 10,000 ft placed the aircraft near terrain without triggering visual warnings until a GPWS alert occurred. The crew executed a climb to 10,300 ft after ATC dismissed their altitude concerns, eventually clearing the mountain and landing on Runway 11L.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported a track deviation occurred on the RNAV (RNP) Z Approach to Runway 17R in DEN, following a late clearance change.
summary: The crew flying an RNAV approach into Denver experienced a navigation anomaly where the FMS failed to turn at the STAAM fix after capturing QWIKE, proceeding instead to an arrival waypoint. ATC issued multiple repeated instructions to correct the deviation, and the crew attributed the event to the un-modifiable active waypoint, late clearance, and communication issues.

synopsis: EMB-505 Captain reported a nose wheel steering issue during taxi due to the failure to reconnect the nose gear torque links during preflight.
summary: The pilot and SIC missed a disconnected nose wheel torque link during a rushed preflight inspection due to high workload and FBO delays. After noticing steering issues while taxiing, they stopped, shut down an engine, and had the gear reconnected by a tug before resuming the flight.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported an autopilot issue resulted in an altitude deviation while on the BOOVE 4 STAR to DFW airport.
summary: During the BOOVE 4 STAR into DFW at 11,000 MSL, simultaneous AP TRIM IS NU and LWD warnings caused an uncommanded descent to 10,600 MSL. The crew disengaged the autopilot, manually recovered the altitude, and attributed the event to a mechanical autopilot failure requiring maintenance attention.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Corporate aircraft Pilot reported confusing lighting on top of airport structures.
summary: A pilot approaching Runway 36 at OXC mistook a windsock light and DME shed light for a VASI while the PAPI was NOTAM'd out. The crew landed safely but noted the layout could cause a loss of vertical situational awareness during the airport's construction.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a flap asymmetry problem when a flap cable failed during go-around.
summary: A student pilot and instructor experienced a left flap jam during a go-around at ZZZ after the flap cable snapped while attempting retraction. The crew managed the resulting asymmetry with increased aileron and rudder inputs, landing safely on Runway XX without emergency assistance.

synopsis: C177 pilot reported a loss of control during landing after encountering a significant crosswind.
summary: The pilot landed in a 70-degree crosswind gust, causing the aircraft to yaw left and the nose fairing to scrape the runway for 50 feet before control was regained. The pilot reported no structural damage but noted the runway condition was worse than reported and admitted a lack of mental preparation for an immediate go-around.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported discovering burn marks on the cowl during post flight inspection due to improper maintenance work on the engine.
summary: The pilot discovered a damaged engine cowling and a hanging igniter on Aircraft X after a phase inspection, which Maintenance attributed to a potential internal combustion. The aircraft was grounded at ZZZ2, and the crew swapped to another aircraft to continue the route.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot reported a loss of engine power due to a non-standard fuel system and lack of system knowledge.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced an engine flameout in an experimental Glasair due to an undocumented fuel system that drew from a small header tank instead of the main tank. The engine restarted after activating transfer pumps, revealing that incorrect information and lack of system knowledge caused the header tank to run dry.

synopsis: B777 Flight Attendant reported being injured when the aircraft encountered unexpected turbulence and there were not enough jump seats in the aft galley for Flight Attendants to occupy.
summary: Six flight attendants in the aft galley of a full aircraft were injured during severe clear air turbulence while setting up breakfast service. One attendant, lacking a jumpseat, was thrown around, and the reporter sustained bruised ribs and a thigh injury as carts and debris fell.

synopsis: Oakland Oceanic Controller reported an airborne conflict when an aircraft descended to a non turbulent altitude through the protected airspace of another aircraft.
summary: The controller reported that Aircraft X descended without clearance from FL360 to FL300 due to turbulence, causing a loss of separation with Aircraft Y at FL350. The pilot subsequently declared PAN, deviated 15nm off route, and was instructed to maintain FL300 while the sector was split to manage the workload.

synopsis: B737 MAX flight crew reported departing with a maintenance item that should have been addressed before departure. Unfamiliarity with the MAX reportedly played a part in the incident.
summary: Pilots on a Boeing MAX flight observed an illuminated MAINT light during preflight and landing, initially dismissing it due to inexperience. The light's behavior indicated a non-dispatchable fault, which the crew realized only after landing, attributing the error to their lack of familiarity with the aircraft.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Boeing 787 flight crew reported pilot approach procedural errors coupled with late ATC final vector heading resulted in speed and altitude deviations.
summary: During an approach to ZZZ, the First Officer's stress and incorrect throttle management caused an airspeed decay and stick shaker activation while configured with flaps 20 and speedbrakes extended. The Captain recovered the aircraft after an altitude excursion, disengaged the autopilot, and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the STAR altitudes and intercept altitude from MORAM STAR to ILS 07, does not allow FMC to successfully and safely execute the modified route.
summary: Flight ZZZ-MSLP crew encountered high altitude issues on arrival due to FMC inability to execute a modified STAR. They reverted to manual heading and level changes, notified ATC, and completed a stable visual approach after intercepting ILS 07.

synopsis: B757 FO reported returning to departure airport after experiencing fuel boost pump issues.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X experienced a recurrent center right fuel pump failure during climb, triggering an EICAS message at 16,000 feet. Due to insufficient main tank fuel for ETOPS requirements, they returned to ZZZ for an approved overweight landing on Runway XXR.

synopsis: Tug driver reported a ground conflict during pushback with an aircraft taxiing at a high rate of speed.
summary: During pushback, the pilot braked to avoid a collision with another aircraft taxiing at high speed. The incident occurred after the pilot was instructed to wait for a towed aircraft before proceeding into the Y.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported company personnel did not follow FAR and company policy by not advising the Dispatcher of a potential aircraft issue prior to takeoff.
summary: A ramp tower at ZZZ failed to notify Dispatch or the Manager of Dispatch Operations about a potentially sheared pushback pin, violating regulations and company policy. Consequently, the aircraft departed with an unaddressed safety issue, preventing the crew from returning to the gate for landing gear inspection.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a GPWS obstacle warning on approach to ISP airport.
summary: The pilot conducting a visual approach to Islap misread the chart and missed a tower obstacle, triggering a GPWS warning at 1,000 feet. After a delayed go-around and an altitude deviation to 2,700 feet, the crew completed a second landing in moderate turbulence, attributing the incident to poor judgment and inadequate chart study.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew reported moderate turbulence that caused injury to two passengers that ignored the 'fasten seatbelt' signs.
summary: During climb through 12,000 feet after a direct routing from ZZZZ, moderate turbulence injured two unbelted passengers despite the seatbelt sign being on. A doctor on board and EMTs at the destination examined the passengers, who sustained bruising and a head bump but were cleared of serious injury.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported multiple bird strikes on departure led to a diversion.
summary: The crew experienced multiple bird strikes to the windshield and right wing slat at 800 feet AGL during climb-out from GEG RWY 3 in 800 RVR. They diverted to a VFR alternate for maintenance inspection, which revealed no major damage, allowing the flight to reach its original destination safely.

synopsis: B787-8 First Officer reported an unstable approach due to late descent clearance from ATC and tailwinds on final approach.
summary: The Pilot Flying on a Boeing 737-800 visual approach was vectored high and fast by ATC, leading to premature speed brake retraction due to an EICAS caution and flap retraction from exceeding limits. Despite a preceding aircraft going around for tailwinds, the crew landed safely after recognizing the configuration errors and wind conditions.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported recurring issue of not receiving required Hazmat documentation for Lithium Ion battery shipment.
summary: The Captain of a flight departing VHHH refused to carry a cargo load containing lithium batteries after failing to obtain details on packaging or inert status. The pilot cited a lack of guidance in company manuals regarding lithium batteries in the cargo hold as the reason for the refusal.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported sliding off pavement while attempting to exit the runway.
summary: During arrival in low visibility, the crew exited the runway and turned left as instructed, but the nose wheel became unresponsive, causing the aircraft to slip off the runway. No injuries or apparent damage were reported, and passengers were safely deplaned.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported a track deviation occurred on arrival into IAH when they got a last minute change in runway assignment but the new arrival was not correctly loaded in the FMS.
summary: The crew approached IAH on the ZEEKK2 arrival but switched to GESNR1 due to a runway change. The FMS inadvertently reverted to ZEEKK2, causing the aircraft to be off course and below altitude at ZEEKK, requiring ATC vectors.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the First Officer inadvertently activated the wrong switch during de-icing procedures and deployed the oxygen masks.
summary: The First Officer inadvertently deployed passenger oxygen masks while turning off the broadband switch in a dark cockpit due to the switch's proximity to the oxygen control. While all passenger masks deployed, forward galley and right aft galley masks failed to deploy, potentially hindering flight attendants during an actual depressurization.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported a glideslope warning on final approach and continued using the VASI.
summary: The crew experienced glideslope fluctuations and autopilot disconnection during an ILS approach to ZZZZ due to amber EICAS and FMA warnings. They continued visually to a normal landing after maintaining altitude and selecting flaps 30.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported a heavy left wing which was determined to be caused by a fuel imbalance.
summary: The pilot reported a 5,200-pound fuel imbalance during flight caused by a fueling error, despite the #1 fuel gauge being on the MEL. This resulted in a heavy left wing requiring right aileron input, necessitating manual fuel procedures without cross-feeding for the entire flight.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported confusion when ATC requested speed above 200 knots when below the Class Bravo airspace.
summary: Pilots and a controller disagreed on maintaining speed below 200 knots while descending below Class B airspace under IFR. The controller requested higher speed due to no traffic, causing confusion over the waiver authority, which led to post-flight discussions with the Duty Officer and ATC Supervisor.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported ramp load personnel neglected to notify Dispatcher of Hazmat [dry ice] loaded in cargo compartment.
summary: A ramp agent failed to advise the dispatcher of dry ice loaded in the forward belly of a B777. The reporter suggests adding a trigger in the Flight Progress Strips or workbench to alert dispatchers when dry ice is loaded in the aircraft's lower holds.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported being informed by the tower that right engine was smoking during takeoff.
summary: The crew reported a right engine smoke advisory after takeoff, but visual checks by a flight attendant and another aircraft confirmed no smoke. The flight landed uneventfully, and mechanics attributed the false alarm to an overfilled oil system.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported difficulty plotting company-provided areas of turbulence when the aircraft WiFi is unavailable.
summary: Flight crews reported that WSI turbulence guidance often contains inaccurate fixes, such as 160NNE HEKAB, which cannot be quickly determined. Without available WiFi to display Flight Plan Guidance on iPads, crews must contact Dispatchers to locate turbulence areas, causing unnecessary delays.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported requesting a new arrival clearance to MMCU airport after the Controller issued an RNP approach that the aircraft was not equipped to execute.
summary: During descent into CUU, the crew and controller experienced a clearance conflict when the controller issued a direct VOR clearance instead of the requested VORDME2 approach. The controller likely assumed RNP capability or intended an unsafe visual approach due to terrain, but eventually granted the correct clearance after the crew refused the direct routing.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported receiving a 'Pitot 2 Inop' EICAS message after pushback during engine start procedures.
summary: The flight crew received a Pitot 2 inop EICAS message during the single engine after start checklist following engine start. Maintenance Control advised returning to the gate to obtain a new aircraft, citing an ongoing issue.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported no required Hazmat documents provided to flight crew regarding electric scooter in cargo compartment.
summary: The First Officer discovered ground crew manually removing a 100-150 lb electric scooter from the cargo hold during the post-flight walk-around. The reporter attributes the incident to a lack of weight verification procedures and requests new forms to notify the PIC of such items.

synopsis: C402 Captain reported an engine failure in cruise.
summary: During cruise, the pilot experienced a right engine failure characterized by two shudders before the engine stopped. The pilot completed the Engine Failure in Flight flow, secured the engine, and landed safely at the destination airport with fire trucks present.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported pre-departure ATC communication difficulties almost led to a track deviation departing TNCM.
summary: The flight crew at TNCM accepted a revised clearance with an incorrect route due to a rapid readback and frequency saturation caused by an overworked controller. Although the crew trapped the error and corrected the route after takeoff, the incident involved significant stress from performance limitations, passenger bumping, and poor communication.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported a track deviation occurred on the arrival into DTW, due in part to fatigue and distractions.
summary: The flight crew departed for Detroit with the wrong arrival programmed in the FMS due to a clearance change and fatigue from a multi-day trip. They corrected the navigation error after ATC issued a fix on the correct arrival, attributing the oversight to similar arrival fixes and distraction from a denied boarding incident.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported takeoff with an unknown nose gear pin resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: A pilot discovered a fourth gear pin installed in the nose gear after takeoff on an aircraft recently returned from maintenance. The flight returned for an uneventful landing, the pin was removed, and the flight resumed, with the cause attributed to the use of an unmarked pin.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported the flight crew was replaced for fatigue following a stressful in-flight issue, but the flight attendants were not.
summary: A flight attendant reported a yellow emergency due to inoperative landing flaps, resulting in a safe landing with excellent crew resource management. Post-incident, pilots were relieved and sent to a hotel, while flight attendants were required to continue working, raising concerns about crew fatigue and safety protocols.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft instructor pilot reported the G1000 system malfunctioned during missed approach training resulting in a CFTT event.
summary: During the second RNAV 9 approach into RNM, the crew activated a missed approach but the G1000 failed to sequence, causing the aircraft to descend below MVA. The incident resulted from over-reliance on the coupled autopilot and delayed manual navigation while troubleshooting.

synopsis: GA flight instructor reported a conflict occurred during a simulated engine failure landing at a non-towered airport.
summary: A CFI and student in a Cessna 172 at ZZZ airport executed a simulated engine failure go-around to avoid an aircraft taking off from Runway XY without radio communication. The reporter attributed the near-miss to the other pilot's lack of transmission and admitted to flying with an expired medical certificate.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported a conflict with a helicopter while taxiing in the ramp area at FFZ airport.
summary: A pilot taxiing on Taxiway B experienced two close calls with a helicopter landing nearby due to a canopy sun-shield blocking the view. The reporter attributes the risk to operating on different frequencies, which prevented hearing the helicopter's landing clearance while monitoring Ground.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi First Officer reported inadvertently exiting the runway into a non-movement area rather than a taxiway.
summary: The crew landed at FTW in low visibility and mistakenly turned onto an unmarked closed area instead of taxiway C4, causing a runway incursion when ATC cleared another aircraft for takeoff. The pilot attributed the incident to poor signage, lack of runway edge lights, and ATC clearing the second aircraft without confirming the runway was clear.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported taxi guide lines associated with gate alignment were difficult to see when the ramp was wet and suggested reflective paint be used to increase visibility.
summary: A pilot reported that J-lines are often difficult to see at night on wet ramps, especially at unexpected angles or during turns without accurate marshaller guidance. The reporter suggested using reflective paint on these lines to increase visibility and reduce hazard.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported concerns that the company policy of hand-flown Cat III approaches is not as safe as autoland.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported a risky hand-flown Cat III landing in 600 RVR after a long duty day, exacerbated by a hotel evacuation alarm. The pilot attributed the safety risk to the lack of autoland usage despite available equipment and recommended reserving 600 RVR landings for autoland to reduce workload and improve safety.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported the snowy runway conditions on takeoff did not match the reported conditions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Boeing 737-800 departed Runway 5L after dispatch dismissed concerns about unplowed taxiways and a 75-foot plowed runway. During takeoff, the crew discovered the runway was 100% snow-covered beyond the initial plowed section, contradicting the reported 3/3/3 braking conditions.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported failing to comply with a crossing restriction that has been modified by ATC on the KORRY 4 arrival into LGA.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring on a flight arriving at LGA failed to change an FMC altitude restriction from "at or above" to "at" while loading speed constraints. This clerical oversight caused them to approach RIDGY at FL370 instead of FL270, requiring a late descent after ATC queried their ability to comply.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a flap retraction problem during takeoff, but elected to continue to the destination airport due to weather conditions at departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a trailing edge flap disagreement after takeoff from ZZZ due to a tripped P6-2-A-12 circuit breaker. They diverted to ZZZ1, completed the asymmetry checklist, and executed a safe landing with flaps 5.

synopsis: Pilot reported a go-around due to tailwind limitations and after landing at OAK airport, called Tower to question where the wind indicators were on the airport. Tower personnel did not know the answer.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X executed two go-arounds on Runway 30 at Oakland due to excessive tailwinds near the threshold, despite Tower reporting winds within limits. The reporter attributes the discrepancy to wind data not representing touchdown zone conditions and successfully landed on Runway 12.

synopsis: B737NG First Officer reported a NMAC with a warbird while on final approach.
summary: During an RNAV (RNP) Runway 31 approach, the crew executed a climbing TCAS RA after a warbird entered their airspace, resulting in a conflict resolution within 40 seconds. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the warbird flying into the approach end of the runway despite Tower awareness of its presence.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported trailing edge flaps failed to extend, crew executed a go-around and landed with flaps 15 using the manual extension system.
summary: During a visual approach, the flight crew encountered a trailing edge flap failure at 5 miles from the runway, limiting extension to 8 degrees. After executing a missed approach and manually extending flaps via the Alternate Flaps Extension System, the crew landed safely with flaps 15 on an ILS approach.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported concerns about accepting an aircraft with the fuel quantity totalizer deferred inoperative, because there is no easy way to identify a fuel leak in that scenario.
summary: The crew reported that dispatching a Boeing 757 with an inoperative fuel quantity totalizer under the MEL creates an unsafe condition. Without forward EICAS gauges or leak warnings, pilots must manually calculate fuel overhead, a process the reporter deems unrealistic and prone to failure.

synopsis: Flight Crew Member concerned about the process in place to inspect and maintain cockpit windows by an Air Carrier.
summary: A pilot reported that a Boeing 757 was initially cleared for dispatch by a gate mechanic despite cockpit window delamination, which was later identified as moisture-induced. The aircraft was subsequently taken out of service after a mechanic with Inspection Authority ordered a detailed inspection, highlighting gaps in maintenance procedures for detecting structural window defects.

synopsis: B737NG Captain reported miscommunication between himself and SFO Ramp Control.
summary: A flight crew taxiing at SFO received a conflicting clearance from Ramp Control to hold "on" Taxiway Bravo 4 instead of "short of" it. Despite clarifying the instruction, the crew turned onto Bravo 4, causing a stop command and a near-miss with a passing 787 before being cleared to continue.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported operating a flight with a missing fuselage panel after failing to notice the discrepancy during pre-flight.
summary: The pilot conducting the preflight inspection for a ferry flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1 failed to detect a missing panel on the aircraft's underside. The crew was notified of the missing panel days after the flight, despite the pilot believing the inspection was thorough.

synopsis: B737-900 flight crew reported diverting following two missed approaches and then calling in fatigued due to the long stressful flight.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ1 due to minimum fuel after two go-arounds caused by loss of separation and a preceding aircraft sliding off a slush-covered runway. Citing extreme fatigue and degraded performance from the difficult flight, the crew elected to layover rather than continue duty.

synopsis: Ground employee reported the belt loading systems become slippery from de-icing operations creating a safety hazard for ramp personnel.
summary: A ramp team leader reported that de-icing fluid at Gate XX made belt loaders slippery, creating a safety hazard. The reporter confirmed the issue, noting a lack of grip on both the belt and the side grip strips while inspecting the equipment.

synopsis: Air carrier Ground personnel reported unload audit verified Hazmat transport violation whereas revised load indicated in compliance.
summary: Ramp personnel initially loaded a flight with a dangerous goods error, causing a departure in noncompliance status. A subsequent typo correction to bag counts revised the load record to show compliance, raising concerns of potential regulatory violations for falsifying records.

synopsis: Ground employee reported a B767 was towed into the gate with a tug not rated for the aircraft type.
summary: A team leader used an improperly rated tug to tow an inbound B767 to the gate while a supervisor observed. The reporter identified the tug as rated only for B757 aircraft, deeming the operation an unsafe act.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp worker reported the use of a non-standard fueling nozzle could lead to introduction of the incorrect fuel to ground equipment.
summary: A mechanic reported that a non-standard green diesel nozzle connected to a gas pump at the terminal fuel farm creates a risk of misfueling. This color confusion could cause unsuspecting employees to damage gas-powered equipment, such as air start carts or pushback tractors, resulting in substantial costs.

synopsis: Ground employee reported over-usage of ear buds during warehouse and ground operations, posing a safety hazard.
summary: A warehouse employee reported that co-workers frequently use phones and earbuds while walking or operating electric equipment in the Airport Operations Area. The reporter stated this distraction creates a safety hazard that could result in serious injury or death from vehicle collisions, despite previous management briefings.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain reported terrain warning during approach to ASE airport.
summary: During a visual approach to ASE, the crew received GPWS warnings while descending over high terrain after being vectored off standard procedures for separation. The aircraft climbed to clear the terrain, then continued a stable approach and landed safely, with the pilot attributing the event to non-standard routing in unique terrain.

synopsis: EMB-145XR pilot reported the cabin altitude was abnormally high. Pilot executed a rapid descent.
summary: During descent from FL360, the crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude rise and hypoxia due to an incorrect CPCS panel setting of 8,000 FT instead of 800 FT. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 FT with no injuries, and maintenance replaced the faulty control panel.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported no published procedure for pushback from gate.
summary: The pilot pushed back from a Miami gate using JEP CO procedures, believing "Miami Gates" was authorized to issue clearance. Tower later clarified that Ground must authorize pushbacks, noting the JEP CO page was misleading for that specific spot.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert from ATC on approach to Runway 9R PHL after descending on a false glideslope.
summary: The flight crew descended below the FAF altitude on a visual approach to Runway 9R after capturing a false glideslope while expediting descent. ATC issued a low altitude alert, prompting the First Officer to climb back to 1,800 feet before the Captain hand-flew the aircraft to complete a stable landing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reported experiencing a CFTT incident while on a visual approach to ELP airport.
summary: The pilot flying a visual approach to El Paso (ELP) Runway 8R leveled off between 7,500 and 8,000 feet due to terrain concerns, triggering obstacle proximity and climb avoidance aural warnings. After remaining level until clear of the obstruction, the crew established a stabilized approach and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: B737-700 Flight Attendant reported confusing location of the aircraft cabin emergency exit lights.
summary: Cabin crew reported that misleading ceiling exit placards on this aircraft could cause passenger harm during an emergency. The safety briefing and cards fail to warn that the row 18 placard does not lead to over-wing exits, contradicting instructions to follow overhead signs.

synopsis: C152 pilot reported an engine malfunction after takeoff resulted in an immediate return to the departure airport.
summary: A two-person crew experienced significant engine power loss at 200 feet after takeoff from Runway XXR and was cleared to land on Runway YYR. They avoided a conflicting aircraft on the runway, resulting in a late touchdown, hard braking, and a flat tire, with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: HS125 Captain reported erroneous airspeed and altitude indications led to a return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced multiple instrument failures, including yaw damper, autopilot, and conflicting altimeter readings, shortly after takeoff from ZZZ. They returned for a precautionary landing with emergency services standing by but required no assistance after taxiing.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dulles Tower Controller reported being advised an aircraft with snow and ice covering aircraft surfaces was in line ready to depart.
summary: Local Control advised an Embraer pilot that snow and ice covered the aircraft's leading edges and tail despite a claim of prior de-icing. The controller removed the aircraft from the departure lineup to return for de-icing, preventing a potentially disastrous takeoff.

synopsis: ZMP Center Controller reported an unsafe procedure that was resolved, but was not what the center controller wanted, which would have led to an operational error.
summary: An air traffic controller managing arrivals into MCI from FL240 detected a large overtake between two aircraft 4,000–5,000 feet below their airspace. The controller resolved the conflict by adjusting speeds and altitudes, but criticized the procedure as unsafe due to excessive coordination with other sectors and missed critical safety information.

synopsis: SFO Tower Controller reported simultaneous go-arounds, one associated with a loss of communication.
summary: An air traffic controller managed arrivals for Aircraft X and Y during complex wind conditions, but lost radio contact with Aircraft X. Both aircraft executed go-arounds; Aircraft Y was too high and fast, while Aircraft X's cause was unclear, though the controller maintained separation and transferred both to departure.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported the terrain height for a mountain near MMPR is incorrect on aircraft display due to a software error.
summary: A pilot reported that the aircraft navigation database incorrectly listed terrain elevation at MMPR as 4,300 feet instead of the actual 4,642 feet MSL near PVR 360/14. This discrepancy compromises the backup safety system during arrivals and departures, as crews relying on the database would not know to maintain altitudes above 4,700 feet.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported receiving a GPWS alert on a visual approach to Runway 8R at ELP.
summary: The flight crew conducted a visual approach to Runway 8R at ELP after Runway 4/22 closed, failing to fully brief the recommended RNAV arrival offset. They received a GPWS 'Caution Obstacle' warning and a Tower verbal caution while crossing a ridge but verified terrain visually and completed an uneventful landing.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew and Dispatcher reported the right engine was inadvertently shut down when a clipboard was dropped onto the right engine control switch.
summary: During en route flight, a pilot dropped a clipboard that struck the right engine fuel control switch to CUTOFF, causing an engine shutdown. The crew executed engine-out procedures, descended to FL310, and successfully restarted the engine by returning the switch to RUN before continuing to ZZZZ without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported a new First Officer had difficulty complying with procedures and clearances in reaction to an RA and subsequent go-around.
summary: During a Boeing OE approach, the Captain failed to set TCAS to TA, triggering an RA at 1,000 feet MSL that the student First Officer ignored. The Captain took control, executed a go-around, and corrected a subsequent shallow descent at 2,500 feet MSL after Tower intervention.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported diverting to an alternate airport due to nose landing gear retraction issues following takeoff in snowy and slushy conditions.
summary: The flight crew experienced a gear disagree warning after takeoff from ZZZ due to snow and ice lodged in the nose gear assembly. They diverted to ZZZ1 for an overweight landing after successfully retracting the gear using alternate pump procedures.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported a pressurization overheat and passenger oxygen system issue during cruise.
summary: The pilot reported high 10th stage manifold pressure and low pack temperatures after takeoff, followed by a right pack HI TEMP caution at FL350. This caused a descent to 10,000 feet due to cabin altitude warnings, resulting in a landing at ZZZ where some passenger oxygen masks failed to deploy.

synopsis: Flight Crew and Maintenance Technician reported fuel quantity indication problem led to incorrect accomplishment of the Minimum Equipment List Procedure.
summary: A contract mechanic at ZZZ incorrectly collared four fuel quantity circuit breakers without installing the required jumper harness per MEL 28-6, leaving the flight crew with no fuel quantity indications. The crew departed with this defect, relying on manual fuel calculations, after the mechanic failed to reinstate the breakers as mandated by the maintenance manual.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ADS-B OUT EICAS alert and loss of GPS due to jamming.
summary: The crew experienced an ADS-B OUT L EICAS alert and loss of GPS information caused by jamming. No specific aircraft type, flight phase, or further outcome was described in the narrative.

synopsis: Beech 1900 Captain reported not recognizing during takeoff roll that the decreasing runway visibility would not permit a return to the field if necessary.
summary: The pilot received takeoff clearance at ZZZ but was advised of a sudden RVR drop to 2,100 after releasing brakes, rendering the only return approach below minima. The pilot continued the departure, noting that while an abort was physically possible, the late timing and potential tower staffing issues prevented a timely decision to stop.

synopsis: Two air carrier Flight Attendants reported communication breakdown with Operations Agent regarding transport of battery powered 'Segway'.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger boarded with an unverified battery-powered mobility device, which the Operations Agent sent to cargo without confirming the battery type. The crew departed unsure of the battery specifications, raising concerns about a potential safety violation regarding the device's transport in the cargo hold.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported non-retractable lavatory doors could pose a safety hazard in emergency situations, or injure people standing too close when opened.
summary: A passenger fainted in the aisle between non-retractable aft lav doors, blocking lav occupants and preventing galley crew from accessing medical equipment. The Purser resolved the immediate issue, though the reporter notes these doors have historically caused injuries and blocked the galley.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendants reported the cabin crew was pressured to work the flight following a stressful medical event in the airport terminal involving another crew member.
summary: Crew members reported fatigue and stress after a Captain suffered a medical emergency in a terminal bathroom, yet supervisors pressured them to fly their scheduled red-eye departure. The reporter felt bullied into flying while unfit, eventually falling asleep on the jumpseat during the flight.

synopsis: Maintenance technicians reported aircraft cleaners had used plastic bags as pitot tube covers for a wash which melted during an engine run.
summary: Mechanics ran engines for oil service on an aircraft undergoing a dry wash, melting plastic bags used to cover pitot tubes. The incident occurred because personnel ignored warning signs and circuit breakers, resulting in the replacement of all four contaminated pitot tubes.

synopsis: Experimental tailwheel aircraft pilots reported a loss of control during landing resulted in a slow speed ground loop and runway excursion.
summary: A pilot with a tailwheel endorsement landed a Sport Cub on Runway XXL but lost directional control during rollout at 25 mph due to ineffective differential braking and applying techniques from a heavier Cessna 180. The aircraft ground looped into the grass without damage, and the pilot attributed the incident to the Sport Cub's lighter weight reducing braking effectiveness at low speeds.

aircraft: Beechcraft / Beech Aircraft Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: BE-99 pilot reported a track heading deviation after an evasive maneuver to avoid a flock of birds near BTG VOR.
summary: A pilot flying at 11,000 feet on V23 deviated 30 degrees left to avoid migrating geese, inadvertently leaving the cleared route. After ATC notification, the pilot returned to V23, and the remainder of the flight was uneventful.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported noticing a small flame above the nose wheel after several unsuccessful attempts to start the carburetor equipped aircraft.
summary: The pilot attempted multiple starts on a carburetor-equipped aircraft before a small flame and smoke appeared near the nose wheel, which were extinguished. The incident was attributed to excessive priming needs and human factors, specifically external pressure from a club leader that caused the pilot to continue attempting starts instead of securing the aircraft.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported being dispatched into known icing conditions with an inoperative wing anti-ice system.
summary: The flight crew encountered dual wing anti-ice failures and heavy ice accumulation during an RNAV approach in known icing conditions, forcing a go-around and hold. After executing the ice dispersal procedure, they landed safely at flaps 20, attributing the issue to a deferred anti-ice valve limiting bleed air to a single source.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported continuing the approach to PHL after receiving a false GPWS terrain warning in VMC conditions.
summary: During arrival into PHL at 4,000 MSL, the crew received two false GPWS Terrain warnings while in level flight over 2,500 feet above obstacles. The pilots silenced the alerts in good VMC but noted the risk of complacency if the issue remains unresolved for future IMC or night operations.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported responding to a GPWS terrain alert on approach into CRW that may have been a false warning.
summary: The flight crew received a GPWS terrain alert while IMC on the RNAV (GPS) Y 23 approach to CRW after passing ENIVY. They executed an escape maneuver, were vectored by ATC for a new attempt, and landed safely with no further warnings.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet Captain reported an unstabilized approach into VNY airport due to windshear resulting in a missed approach and Terrain Warning.
summary: The pilot encountered windshear during an ILS 16R approach into VNY, triggering a go-around and subsequent EGPWS terrain warnings at 2,000 ft MSL. The crew climbed to 2,980 ft for clearance and landed safely, though the pilot noted they should have informed ATC of the need to exceed the assigned altitude.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported lateral trim problems during a post maintenance check flight. Post flight inspection revealed a missing wing panel.
summary: During a post-heavy maintenance test flight, the crew experienced left aileron and rudder trim requirements plus vibration caused by a missing right wing panel. The panel, which detached during takeoff due to improper reattachment, was found on the runway after the crew returned to land safely.

synopsis: B767-300ER First Officer reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing the loss of the Center Hydraulic System.
summary: A relief pilot assisted the Captain after a rapid loss of Center Hydraulic System fluid forced a diversion. The crew lowered gear at FL200, followed QRH procedures, and executed a soft overweight landing in VFR conditions before passengers deplaned safely.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported communication breakdown between flight crew resulted in procedural errors on final approach.
summary: The crew briefed for Runway 9R but was assigned Runway 10; the Pilot Monitoring failed to update the FMS, causing the aircraft to intercept the wrong ILS. Fatigue and rushing led to the error, requiring ATC vectors to re-sequence the approach before a visual landing.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported losing control of the aircraft after encountering black ice on a taxiway.
summary: During taxi to the run-up pad, the flight crew lost directional control on black ice despite good braking action reports, causing the aircraft to skid uncontrollably onto snow. Although inspections confirmed no damage, the crew elected to be towed out due to the slippery ramp gradient before continuing the flight.

synopsis: SA-227 Captain reported a fuel imbalance during flight led to discovery of a fuel leak after landing.
summary: The pilot noticed a right fuel imbalance on ILS approach to ZZZ, which was identified on the ground as a substantial leak caused by a loose quick drain plug. The spill was contained, and the aircraft was grounded for part replacement.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported Maintenance Technician did not appropriately communicate and evaluate the door slide issue identified by the crew.
summary: A flight attendant reported a loose L1 door slide-bustle stowage hook to the Captain and maintenance, but the mechanic dismissed the safety concern without repair. The reporter described the mechanic's argumentative and disrespectful behavior as damaging to the safety culture and discouraging future reporting.

synopsis: E-145 First Officer reported a track deviation occurred when the FMS route was improperly loaded.
summary: During the en route phase of a routine flight, the First Officer input an outdated stored flight plan into the FMS due to complacency and poor crew resource management. Air Traffic Control detected the deviation, prompting a correction, while the Captain failed to cross-check the flight plan against current paperwork.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot and Air Traffic Controller reported confusion in regard to instrument operations near BORTY waypoint.
summary: A pilot flying IFR VFR-on-top and a Fort Worth controller experienced confusion regarding Minimum IFR Altitudes while approaching KINK. The pilot landed without an approach clearance after the controller incorrectly required a climb to 5,500 feet, highlighting unresolved regulatory ambiguity on altitude requirements for uncontrolled airports.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported a hard landing and loss of control resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot experienced a hard landing and runway excursion on Runway XX after ATC delayed landing clearance due to priority handling for another aircraft. The aircraft bounced, veered right upon asymmetric touchdown, and rolled off the runway after the pilot over-corrected with the rudder.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported rushing to clear the runway of vehicles for landing traffic while training.
summary: A trainee controller failed to check radar while updating the IDS-4, allowing an arrival to reach 6-mile final with snow removal vehicles on Runway 21. The supervisor permitted this dangerous situation to develop for training purposes, though the trainee noted the team should have intervened to ensure safety.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported no response from a military aircraft until using guard frequency. Flight was then switched to UHF and turned before entering a higher MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X for an ILS approach to RWY32 at ZZZ, issuing a descent to 4000 feet east of the localizer to avoid military traffic. Communication was lost on VHF as the aircraft approached a 5900-foot MVA, but the pilot responded on guard frequency and executed the turn at 4500 feet before switching to UHF.

synopsis: ZNY Controller reported an airborne conflict which was avoided by climbing an aircraft into another sectors airspace without a correct point-out. Reporter stated fatigue issues related to the government shutdown.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential conflict between Aircraft X climbing to 17,000 feet and a Mode C intruder while working overtime. The controller attributed the near-merge to fatigue and management pressure, noting that an airspace violation into Sector 56 was necessary to avoid the collision after Liberty South transferred the aircraft without resolving the conflict.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a fuel leak was suspected due to abnormal fuel burn and a strong fuel smell after landing, but no fuel leak was detected.
summary: The Captain and First Officer suspected a wing fuel leak during cruise due to unexplained fuel loss, but no streaming was observed. Upon landing, a strong fuel smell prompted an immediate evacuation to the terminal while Maintenance inspected the aircraft, which was subsequently cleared for passengers to retrieve belongings.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported being high on a crossing restriction on the RNAV Z Runway 12R approach into SJC after receiving a late ATC clearance.
summary: The flight crew received a late RNAV Z 12R clearance during descent into SJC, leaving them high and unable to meet ATC speed and altitude requests. They deployed all drag devices to comply but acknowledged they should have declared unable to meet the conflicting constraints.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported communication breakdown between flight crew members on approach to landing.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported that the Captain ignored speed and configuration SOPs during an RNAV arrival and visual approach, leading to a go-around. The Captain's inefficient execution and lack of automation knowledge caused task saturation, resulting in a frequency setting error by the PM before landing clearance was received.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported passenger no easy access information to determine procedures for Lithium powered devices.
summary: The Captain and First Officer at ZZZ focused on deicing for cold soak fuel frost while a flight attendant reported a passenger's lithium battery device was loaded into the cargo bin. The crew later confirmed the device contained lithium batteries, raising concerns that an item requiring cabin carriage was improperly stowed in the hold.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported concerns with takeoff data settings being too low.
summary: Pilots reported that performance software set takeoff power too low (83.4% N1) for a deiced, IFR night departure, causing a sluggish climb until full power was applied at 1,000 feet. They attributed the issue to the software's inability to account for adverse weather conditions, resulting in insufficient power margins.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew reported accidental right engine shutdown in cruise with a successful restart and continuation to destination.
summary: A Relief Officer accidentally dropped a clipboard onto the right fuel cutoff switch, shutting down the engine during cruise. The crew executed engine failure procedures, restarted the engine, and coordinated with ATC and Dispatch to safely return to course and continue to the destination.

synopsis: Super Tug Driver reported being advised of ground conflict with parked aircraft after tow completion.
summary: A tug driver and observer moved a 787 from a gate after receiving clearance to the North Spot. The 787's wingtip struck the horizontal stabilizer of an adjacent aircraft because the driver was not alerted to the proximity until after the contact occurred.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported losing situational awareness during taxi resulting in taxiway excursion.
summary: The Captain, while taxiing after crossing XXR, misidentified outer edge lights as taxiway edge lights due to an optical illusion and struck two lights with the left main tires. The aircraft returned to the ramp for inspection, and the remainder of the flight was normal.

synopsis: CE680 Captain reported loss of aircraft control due to severe turbulence during cruise.
summary: The crew encountered severe mountain wave turbulence at 36,000 feet during arrival into ZZZ, causing an uncontrolled descent of 4,000 feet per minute. Despite deploying speed brakes and fighting the controls, they lost 4,000 feet of altitude before regaining control.

synopsis: EMB175 flight crew reported the aircraft rollback shortly after parking at the gate.
summary: The Pilot in Command and First Officer experienced an aircraft rollback at the gate after engine shutdown rendered manual rudder pedal brakes ineffective due to hydraulic pressure loss. The aircraft was towed forward by ramp personnel with no damage reported, as the parking brake was not set immediately upon stopping.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reported a communication breakdown between flight crew and deicing ground crew resulted in an unsafe situation.
summary: During taxi after remote de-icing at ZZZZ, the crew attempted to move the aircraft but it remained stationary due to a forgotten chock. A ground crew member reconnected to the intercom to scream "chocks," prompting the pilots to reduce thrust to idle before the chock was removed and taxi resumed without damage.

synopsis: MD83 Captain reported communication breakdown between flight crew resulted in a misdiagnoses of a flight control issue and a hard landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a stabilizer trim malfunction during final approach, resulting in heavy controls and a hard landing. The pilot attributed the incident to ambiguous trim instructions and a mechanical failure that prevented nose-up trim, though the system functioned normally after landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an EICAS warning illumination on takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot aborted two takeoff attempts due to an illuminated left engine cowl anti-ice amber light at 90% and 85% N1. The reporter attributed the second abort to an unsafe decision to perform a static run-up to verify the fault rather than returning to the gate immediately.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported NIL braking action and traction at the deicing pad.
summary: The crew experienced nil braking and steering on an icy deicing pad lane, causing the aircraft to slide toward ground equipment. The Captain stopped the aircraft using reverse thrust and full tiller input within 3-5 seconds, avoiding any collision despite poor surface conditions and limited buffer space.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Design Engineer reported that nonconservative structural margin analysis/calculations were used on aircraft fuel tanks and fuel system components.
summary: A company engineer reported that a non-conservative margin of safety calculation using maximum principal stress was applied to aircraft components at the ZZZ location. This method incorrectly predicted safety for ductile metals under compressive stress, whereas the Tresca criterion correctly indicated potential failure.

synopsis: SF50 Pilot reported erroneous terrain alert on departure due to improperly configured portable EFB resulting in altitude clearance deviation.
summary: The pilot experienced false terrain alerts during climb and descent caused by a Bluetooth-connected Garmin Pilot EFB, not the aircraft systems. This distraction led to an altitude deviation and delayed radio contact, though the pilot maintained control and landed safely after identifying the portable device as the source.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a communication breakdown with a Designated Pilot Examiner resulted in an unstabilized approach to landing.
summary: A student pilot and DPE conducting a check ride at a busy airport landed far down the runway after the DPE overruled the student's request for a go-around due to high altitude. The student attributed the unsafe landing to deferring to the examiner's authority rather than exercising the right to go around.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a runway excursion due to loss of directional control during landing roll.
summary: The pilot reported that upon landing on runway 010, the aircraft veered left, struck a landing light, and became stuck in mud. The pilot attributed the incident to possible error in landing speed and judgment, resulting in damage to two wheel pants.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: RSW TRACON Controller reported NMAC with an airliner and a VFR aircraft due in part to being distracted.
summary: An East radar controller issued a traffic alert to Aircraft X after realizing it conflicted with VFR traffic near LBV at 10,300 feet. The VFR aircraft turned back into Aircraft X's path, causing a near mid-air collision, which the controller attributed to distraction and premature descent clearance.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Palm Springs Tower Controller reported an unsafe approach due to weather and possible piloting issues.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers and a pilot of Aircraft X experienced a near-miss during a VOR-B approach to RWY 31L at PSP in deteriorating weather. The pilot descended below minimums, flew the pattern in the wrong direction, and executed a chaotic missed approach after hitting a cloud bank, prompting controllers to ban future VOR-B attempts.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZNY Center Controller reported an airspace violation due to external distractions.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an incorrect crossing clearance of FL230 instead of FL250 to Aircraft X, causing an airspace violation with Sector Z. The controller attributed the error to stress and fatigue resulting from personal financial concerns during a government shutdown.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller without an Assist reported an unidentified VFR aircraft climbed into traffic on a final approach course and another aircraft deviated from their course into a higher Minimum Vectoring Altitude Area.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Aircraft X and Y at ZZZ encountered a VFR conflict and a non-compliant aircraft descending below 5,600 ft MVA. The controller issued climb instructions and alerts but could not obtain assistance from colleagues, resulting in high workload and uncertainty regarding separation standards.

synopsis: SFO Ground Controller reported a pilot was confused by the departure clearance received via CPDLC.
summary: A Ground Control controller observed confusion between Clearance Delivery and Aircraft X regarding a CPDLC upload for the TRUKN2 SID with SYRAH transition. The pilot subsequently filed a direct to SYRAH, a deviation the controller attributes to recurring CPDLC upload issues requiring standardization.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Traffic Management Coordinator reported that an unqualified Supervisor working several positions created significant traffic problems.
summary: An untrained Supervisor combined the Arrival Coordinator and Supervisor positions, overwhelming the Arrival Controller with excessive traffic and ignoring a scheduled runway inspection. This caused aircraft to be vectored outside airspace, pulled from final approach, or sent around, creating a chaotic and unsafe situation.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported Lithium Ion powered mobility device was improperly transported on aircraft.
summary: During boarding, an A Flight Attendant flagged a passenger mobility device suspected to be a hoverboard, which an Ops Agent then tagged and loaded as checked baggage. Post-landing, the crew realized the device likely contained lithium-ion batteries that should have been stowed in the cabin or prohibited, highlighting a need for flight deck verification.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported missing a change in the clearance due to not following the SOP.
summary: The First Officer failed to print a CPDLC oceanic clearance, causing the crew to miss a waypoint change from N4950W to N4850W while at 34,000 feet. Gander Radio detected the error and issued a re-route, which the crew corrected before reaching the waypoint, resulting in no deviation.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported a trailing edge flap disagree problem.
summary: During an ILS descent, a 757/767 crew initiated a go-around after a TE FLAP DISAGREE warning, inadvertently climbing to 3500 feet before leveling off. The aircraft landed safely with flaps 20, and the pilot attributed the altitude deviation to not selecting ALT HLD immediately, noting this flap issue occurs fleet-wide.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported an EGPWS terrain warning during return to departure airport after a nose gear malfunction.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport after hearing a loud clanking noise from the nose gear and receiving intermittent gear-in-transit EICAS indications. While being vectored at 5,200 feet near towers, the crew executed a GPWS escape maneuver following a terrain alert before landing safely.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Citation Captain reported momentary loss of control from a wake turbulence encounter descending through FL210 inbound to ISM.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence while descending through FL210 on the CWRLD4 arrival, causing an uncommanded 70-degree roll and autopilot disconnect. Suspecting wake turbulence from a nearby heavy aircraft due to potential inadequate ATC spacing, the crew recovered control within five seconds and continued to the destination with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported an airborne conflict during climb due to a communication breakdown with ATC.
summary: The flight crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory during climbout from TEB after ATC issued an erroneous clearance to FL400, likely intended for another aircraft with a similar callsign. The crew manually descended 500 fpm to avoid a head-on conflict with Aircraft Y at FL350, attributing the error to ATC oversight and crew fatigue.

synopsis: Embraer 175 Captain reported confusion between LAX Controllers on runway clearance, possibly due to government shutdown and the additional stress on ATC.
summary: The First Officer flew an early morning arrival into LAX while the Captain managed radios. After Approach Control changed the arrival and cleared the crew for ILS 24R, a subsequent controller initially claimed they were lined up for the wrong runway before confirming the 24R clearance, resulting in a safe landing.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported a wake turbulence encounter descending into DFW in trail of a B787 resulted in a track deviation.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Boeing 787 while intercepting the ILS/LOC 17L at 8-10 miles from the final approach fix, causing a left deviation. They offset to recover the course and executed a safe landing, noting the need for increased vigilance when following heavy aircraft.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported IAS anomalies, probably due to pitot static icing.
summary: The crew experienced unreliable airspeed and autopilot disengagement during descent due to pitot static icing caused by heavy rain and debris. They executed the Airspeed Unreliable checklist and landed uneventfully after indications normalized at 2,000 feet.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported a taxiway incursion at EWR airport.
summary: The crew of an aircraft taxiing at night in poor visibility and icing crossed Runway 11/29 in error due to confusing Ramp instructions and split radio communications. After stopping to confirm their position and re-establishing a single frequency, Ground provided corrected clearance, allowing the aircraft to reach the gate without further incident.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported ATC irregularities on approach to SKBO, including clearance below MVA and an airborne conflict.
summary: The flight crew experienced a potential NMAC with Aircraft Y near AMVES due to ATC confusion over clearances and call signs, requiring a right turn to avoid traffic. Later, ATC instructed a climb above Minimum Vectoring Altitude despite the crew's terrain awareness, though the flight landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported receiving an ECAM for low fluid level in the Yellow hydraulic system.
summary: The flight crew managed a Yellow hydraulic low-level warning at FL350 by following ECAM procedures and landing safely with reduced braking capability. Post-flight inspection revealed a significant hydraulic fluid leak on the aircraft belly, though the system pressure remained normal until engine shutdown.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported descending to a lower altitude and diverting to a nearby alternate airport due to loss of cabin pressure.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a rapid cabin depressurization at FL370 due to an auto pressurization mode failure. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 feet, diverted to a nearby alternate, and landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported diverting to a second alternate after two go-arounds at the original destination and the primary alternate being closed.
summary: The Captain took control from the First Officer during a gusty approach to ZZZZ, executing two go-arounds due to windshear warnings. After communication failures with the alternate ZZZZ1, the crew diverted to ZZZZ2 with low fuel, landing with 1,100 lbs remaining despite a laser sighting and ground handling issues.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported icing conditions resulted in Captain's airspeed indicator errors.
summary: The crew encountered icing and unreliable airspeed on approach, causing a discrepancy between indicated and actual speed while ATC repeatedly requested slower speeds. They transferred controls to the First Officer's side to verify instruments and completed the landing, though the pilot noted ATC should have cancelled the approach to allow time for troubleshooting.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported a Traffic Resolution Advisory during climb from LGB due to VFR traffic.
summary: During departure from LGB, the crew received a TCAS Monitor Vertical Speed RA while level at 3,000 feet with a VFR aircraft 500 feet above. The crew complied by holding altitude until the conflict cleared, after which they received a new climb clearance and continued the flight without further incident.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported a glideslope anomaly on the ILS to Runway 30 at MIA apparently caused by B747 aircraft holding on the taxiway in the vicinity of the end of the runway.
summary: A crew flying an ILS approach to Runway 30 in Miami experienced glideslope interference from two 747s holding short of the runway. The reporter attributed the anomaly to the large aircraft and warned that engaged autopilots could have caused a dangerous dive.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported an NMAC with a light aircraft on approach to TPA.
summary: While vectored for a visual approach to Runway 19R at TPA, the crew received TCAS RAs due to a Piper climbing beneath them at 3000 ft. The Captain executed a climb, causing a brief flap overspeed, while ATC distractions complicated the response before the crew aborted the approach.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported diverting to an alternate airport to avoid icing conditions after receiving an engine bleed air caution message.
summary: During climb out, the flight crew received an engine bleed air caution and diverted to an alternate after determining no suitable airports existed to avoid icing. The aircraft landed normally, but the recurring issue suggests the previous maintenance replacement failed to resolve the root cause.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported going around after ATC advised off course, even though there was no off course indication.
summary: The crew on an ILS 10 approach reported centered localizer indications despite ATC stating they were off course, prompting a PRM breakout. The reporter attributed the discrepancy to a 55-knot crosswind affecting multiple aircraft, and the crew successfully completed the approach on the second attempt.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff when they received a 'Takeoff Config' alert message at 100 KTS for trim.
summary: During a ferry flight takeoff roll, the crew rejected the takeoff at 100 knots after a "Trim" master warning appeared. The pilots suspect the stabilizer trim moved unintentionally, possibly due to accidental switch contact, though no trim clacker was heard during the roll.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported diverting to an alternate airport after detecting signs of a fuel leak.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring detected a fuel imbalance and confirmed a leak in the Number 1 tank during cruise, leading to an engine shutdown per the QRH. The crew landed safely but failed to rebalance fuel after the shutdown, resulting in a significant imbalance at the gate due to a human factors error.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a runway excursion while exiting the runway in poor weather with runway condition erroneously reported to them as 6-dry.
summary: During an IOE landing on Runway XXR, the Captain lost brake and tiller control while taxiing to the runway end, causing the aircraft to slide into the grass. The First Officer attributed the incident to unreported icing conditions at the intersection despite a reported Runway Condition Code of 6, resulting in no injuries.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported a loss of cabin pressure descending through FL240.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at 23,000–24,000 feet due to a mechanical issue, likely an aft service door leak, and descended to 10,000 feet. While manually adjusting pressurization during descent, they inadvertently over-pressurized the cabin, but the aircraft landed safely with only minor passenger discomfort.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported concerns about the legality of duty time and number of legs flown with an augmented crew.
summary: The flight crew discovered missing cargo bins at ZZZ, requiring two unplanned return legs to ZZZ1 that the crew believes violated FAR 117.17(d) segment limits and potentially exceeded duty time. The crew also suspects inaccurate weight and balance data due to the removed bins.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported concern with the fuel planned for the flight to MMMX and requested an increase.
summary: The pilot and dispatcher discussed fuel planning for a night Airbus flight to MMMX, where the pilot felt the initial load was insufficient for the challenging terrain and approach. The pilot requested and received additional fuel plus a precautionary alternate, and the flight subsequently operated uneventfully.

synopsis: Air Carrier ramp agent reported contacting an aircraft on the adjacent gate with a fuel truck due to icy conditions.
summary: A fuel truck driver struck the left wingtip of a parked aircraft while backing out of a gate. The collision occurred because icy ramp conditions and iced-over truck mirrors caused the vehicle to slide despite the driver applying brakes.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Fractional flight crew reported encountering severe turbulence at FL230 over the Sierra Nevada Mountains.
summary: Pilots flying a RAZRR4 arrival into SJC at FL250 encountered severe turbulence south of STSHH, causing a 200-foot altitude loss, autopilot failure, and temporary loss of control. They diverted west to the San Joaquin Valley where turbulence subsided, recommending avoidance of this mountain-adjacent arrival during inclement weather.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported that the crew O2 level was found low during pre-flight by the next crew on the aircraft.
summary: Maintenance discovered low crew oxygen and a closed valve after arrival, despite a pre-flight bleed test showing no abnormalities. The pilot suggests monitoring oxygen levels in flight and verifying maintenance procedures, as the aircraft was incorrectly stamped approved for return to service.

synopsis: B757 flight crew and Dispatcher reported errors in the flight release software when calculating for a deferred fuel pump.
summary: A pilot reported that a dispatcher incorrectly calculated Fuel Over Destination and minimum takeoff fuel on the flight release for a ZZZ trip with a deferred left aft fuel pump. The errors, likely caused by software or human input, resulted in inaccurate fuel figures despite the aircraft carrying the required MEL penalty fuel.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported Flaps Fail Caution Message on approach and diverting to an airport with a longer runway.
summary: During approach to RWY XX at ZZZ, the crew experienced a FLAPS FAIL caution at 2,500 feet with flaps in the 0-degree position. They diverted to ZZZ1, landed safely with flaps zero, and reported the root cause as unknown.

synopsis: A330 flight attendants reported passengers informed crew of flames shooting out of engine exhaust on start. Cabin fumes became prevalent in passenger cabin.
summary: Cabin crew reported flames and smoke from the left engine and smoke from the right engine while taxiing during the safety demo. Maintenance inspected the aircraft, which had experienced fume issues the previous day.

synopsis: Air carrier Safety Analyst reported Hazmat material was found to be improperly packaged for transport.
summary: Warehouse personnel improperly loaded cargo containing dry ice. The cargo was called to the gate to be repacked for transport.

synopsis: CL35 Captain reported receiving master warning indication of fire in both engines, with aural warning of 'left engine fire', on final approach. Pilot not flying shut down the left engine in response, and post flight inspection revealed no sign of fire.
summary: During a hand-flown ILS approach in a CL35, a false dual engine fire warning triggered the crew to discharge the left fire bottle and evacuate passengers. Investigation confirmed a known detection system malfunction caused the alarm, resulting in no actual fire, damage, or injuries.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported accepting takeoff clearance from the Tower while another aircraft was still on the runway.
summary: The pilot reported a close encounter during takeoff on Runway 35L at DWH when another aircraft failed to clear the runway despite Tower clearance. The pilot queried Tower, was directed to proceed, and observed the obstruction while accelerating.

synopsis: Hot air balloon pilot reported a change in the wind direction and velocity required a new landing spot. After being unable to contact ATC for clearance, the only option was to enter and land with Class D airspace.
summary: A pilot flying a hot air balloon with six passengers and a student encountered sudden wind shear, forcing a deviation into Class D airspace without radio contact due to a dead battery. The crew safely landed in a distant field after failing to reach the tower, resulting in a pilot deviation attributed to the equipment failure.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported executing an immediate approach and landing following the appearance of smoke from the avionics equipment.
summary: The pilot reported smoke from avionics during the downwind leg and declared an electrical fire. After confirming separation from traffic on final, the pilot turned off avionics and landed safely with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: C414 Captain reported left engine control problems that led to a single engine approach and landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a stuck throttle on the left engine during an IFR glideslope approach. After canceling IFR to feather the engine, the pilot executed a safe single-engine landing in VMC, noting the scenario would be more challenging in IMC.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported Quality Assurance staff suggested a pilot initiated go-around due to preceding traffic was an ATC Operational Error.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a pilot initiated an unexpected go-around before the threshold during an overtake, causing an ASDE data investigation for a potential runway separation loss. The controller argued the event was not a safety failure since separation would have been met had the pilot landed, criticizing investigators for prioritizing data over visual observations.

synopsis: Tower Ground Controller reported incorrect coordination with Local Control that an aircraft on an IFR flight plan was a VFR flight due to being distracted by the government shutdown.
summary: The controller issued a takeoff clearance to Aircraft Y without an IFR release due to a mistaken belief the flight was VFR. This error occurred because the controller was distracted by personal financial concerns, requiring subsequent coordination to provide visual separation from an IFR arrival.

synopsis: MIA Approach Controller reported releasing departures from different airports on converging headings into a confliction due to fatigue and stress over a government shutdown.
summary: An air traffic controller at MIA TRACON issued conflicting headings to Aircraft X and Aircraft Y, causing a slight loss of vertical separation. The controller attributed the error to impaired focus and anxiety resulting from unpaid wages during a government shutdown.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported an aircraft misunderstood their traffic information, possibly due to poor radio coverage, and climbed above their assigned altitude into confliction with converging traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X and Y during climb, where a garbled clearance and readback error caused Aircraft X to request FL380 instead of maintaining FL280. The controller attributed the incident to potential fatigue, staffing shortages, and poor radio frequency quality, though no altitude deviation was observed.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported taking handoffs on two aircraft they did not recognize were converging at the same altitude due to stress from the government shutdown.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between Aircraft X and Y at 11,000 ft due to delayed conflict recognition and ineffective coordination with other sectors. The controller attributed the error to stress from a government shutdown, ultimately turning Aircraft Y right to avoid a collision after TRACON descended Aircraft X to 10,000 ft.

synopsis: A Center Controller working a combined sector reported that they were distracted by a conversation with the Supervisor over pay issues and made a late point out to the adjacent facility.
