summary: The PNF reported an unintentional landing at the wrong airport (ZZZ) instead of ZZZ1 during a visual approach in snowy conditions. The crew failed to identify the correct runway due to obscured numbers and snow cover, requiring a back-taxi and repositioning flight after being alerted by CTAF.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported on landing, an NMAC with opposite direction NORDO aircraft.
summary: A pilot and student on final approach to Runway 21 at FVX nearly collided with a homebuilt aircraft executing a power-off 180 to Runway 03. The experimental aircraft descended rapidly and overshot final, missing the landing aircraft by 100 feet horizontally, likely due to the pilot lacking a radio.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported loss of aircraft control on landing possibly due to ice, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot slid off the left side of the runway during landing, likely due to an icy patch, and came to rest in snow. The aircraft was towed out by the FBO with no damage to the airplane or airport property.

synopsis: M20J pilot reported the electric switch did not activate the flap motor during flap retraction. After landing the flaps operated normally.
summary: During a routine ILS practice approach, the pilot encountered a flap retraction failure where the electric switch did not activate the motor. The flaps unexpectedly retracted during the landing roll-out and functioned normally on subsequent tests, prompting the pilot to ground the aircraft for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: B777 Flight Attendant in-charge reported an inflight turbulence encounter that injured flight attendants and passengers.
summary: A flight attendant reported encountering unexpected turbulence while serving breads, causing three crew members to be injured and two passengers to sustain minor injuries. Although the seatbelt sign was on, the passengers refused paramedic assistance after the incident.

synopsis: ZOA Controller reported identifying an aircraft, but not realizing it was below the MIA until the MSAW went off.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a 12,000-foot clearance to an aircraft, triggering a Minimum Safe Altitude Warning (MSAW) alert immediately after identification. The controller amended the clearance to climb direct to 13,000 feet, attributing the error to relying on memory instead of checking Minimum IFR Altitude boxes beforehand.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported receiving an Aircraft Release with an excess amount of fuel on landing at an airport with a forecast of rain.
summary: The flight crew of an -800 aircraft questioned Dispatch regarding excessive tankered fuel for a Nashville arrival with potential rain. The Dispatcher dismissed the safety concern with arrogance, refusing to acknowledge the abnormal fuel load despite the crew's valid operational concerns.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported diverting after encountering a flap issue during the approach. The flight crew later determined they did not apply the correct checklist.
summary: During an ILS approach to ZZZ, the crew encountered a flap malfunction where the handle moved to 30 but the flaps remained at 25, prompting a missed approach. Diverting to ZZZ2 due to ATC interruptions and icing, the crew initially overlooked the applicable Trailing Edge Flaps Disagree checklist but eventually landed uneventfully using conservative flap 15 data.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported receiving a GPWS terrain warning as they descended below a crossing altitude while in VFR conditions.
summary: During a visual approach to PSP, the crew received a terrain warning while descending below the 2,900-foot crossing altitude at JISOP due to an unexpected VNAV loss. The Captain leveled off at 2,700 feet, cleared the terrain, and completed the landing without incident.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported engine malfunction on start-up as well as a conflict with station management during the gate return.
summary: The Captain of a 737 Max experienced an Engine 1 fault during startup at ZZZ, requiring a gate return with only Engine 2 running. After the Operations Manager initially refused parking assistance, a marshaller eventually arrived to guide the aircraft safely to the gate.

synopsis: 767 Captain reported runway edge signage at EGLL airport is not ICAO standard. During daylight hours taxiways are difficult to identify.
summary: A pilot reported difficulty identifying runway exit N9E at Heathrow during daytime due to a lack of ICAO-standard signage and confusing barricades on a closed taxiway. The pilot noted that without clear markings, distinguishing the open exit from closed taxiways while decelerating at high speed was hazardous.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported multiple malfunctions with both air conditioning packs and diverting.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 757 experienced multiple air conditioning pack failures and a rapid cabin altitude rise to 9,000 feet during cruise at FL370. The First Officer restored pressurization by isolating the bleed system, allowing the crew to divert and land safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: Tractor driver reported failing to communicate with the pilot due to lack of training when the aircraft disconnected from the tractor during pushback.
summary: A ground crew member reported that the aircraft disconnected from the pushback tractor five seconds into the push while loading late freight. The crew member continued driving to maintain headset communication, but the aircraft eventually rolled back onto the tractor due to a lack of training on proper emergency verbiage.

synopsis: Ramp agent reported a slip and fall hazard on stairs.
summary: Ground agents reported that glycol sprayed on can loaders made yellow metal stairs slippery, creating a slip and fall hazard. Consequently, agents avoided the stairs and rode the platform instead, which the reporter identified as an additional hazard.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported an aircraft was over burning fuel and required priority handling on arrival.
summary: The pilot inherited a flight overburning fuel and initially diverted to ZZZZ2, but the crew later found insufficient fuel to reach it. They declared a PAN PAN, returned to ZZZZ, and landed with 8,600 lbs of fuel remaining.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Ramp agent reported that an extremely loud warning signal in the tug being used for a push made it diffucult to hear Ground Control's instructions.
summary: Two ground crew members towing a 787 with a super tug experienced an "Over steer" alarm that was too loud to hear ATC instructions, causing them to misinterpret taxi directions and go the wrong way. The crew reported this unsafe condition to a lead mechanic, who agreed to investigate the alarm volume.

synopsis: Air Taxi Captain reported a departure fix was not programed in the FMS for the SID, a communication issue with the ATC controller and possibly flying an incorrect altitude.
summary: The pilot departed a VNY 16R in light rain and discovered the 1.5 DME fix was missing from the flight plan, causing an autopilot level-off error. The pilot manually leveled at 1750 feet while SoCal Departure issued an unprofessional low altitude alert during a heated exchange with another aircraft.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported an engine failure on initial climb resulted in an engine restart and return to departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a right yaw and idle N1 on the right engine during initial climb after takeoff on Runway XXL. After restarting the engine and burning fuel in a hold, Dispatch advised returning to ZZZ due to the aircraft being overweight.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a door handle anomaly resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to ZZZ after a Flight Attendant reported the left aft cabin door handle was unsecured, causing it to flutter during climb. The aircraft landed overweight with a firm touchdown, and maintenance later confirmed the improperly stowed handle was the sole cause of the diversion.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that after landing, a major access panel beneath the aircraft was found open. Damage found to composite fairing aft of access panel.
summary: Ground crew discovered an open access panel behind the right main landing gear during post-flight inspection of a new aircraft after normal flight and landing. The panel's support rod damaged the composite fairing, causing the aircraft to be taken out of service, though the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported delays in receiving departure clearance after the aircraft was deiced.
summary: The flight crew deiced at MSP, then faced a runway closure for plowing while holding short of Runway 30L. They diverted to an unplowed taxiway to reach Runway 30R, departing within their holdover time, though the pilot criticized the delay as a safety risk.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported failure to comply with an AD, in part because of poor communication on the issue from the company.
summary: The pilot of a CRJ-200 encountered unclear guidance regarding a flap Airworthiness Directive after a previous FLAPS FAIL caution. Due to poor company communication, the pilot had to independently research and perform required flight crew checks to ensure compliance before operating the flight.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported receiving an EGPWS terrain alert departing DCA that may have been a false alert.
summary: Pilots on a wet runway takeoff from DCA Runway 1 received conflicting EGPWS terrain alerts at 350–400 feet while on the REBLL4 departure. They executed a max thrust escape maneuver but suspect the alert was a false indication caused by a dual radio altimeter failure or wind drift, as other instruments showed positive clearance.

synopsis: E175 flight crew reported jet blast from another aircraft on the takeoff roll caused loss of the flight director vertical and lateral modes.
summary: The flight crew experienced EICAS FD mode loss messages during takeoff on Runway 22L at ORD due to jet blast from a heavy aircraft departing Runway 28R. After canceling the messages past 100 knots, they continued the takeoff and reselected modes airborne, with the remainder of the flight uneventful.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported ground service personnel attempted to open the galley door when it was still armed shortly after arrival, and explained they could not see the flag through the window because of sun glare.
summary: A Flight Attendant stopped Catering from opening an armed door upon arrival, preventing slide deployment. The Catering crew claimed they could not see the armed flag due to sunlight glare, but the door was successfully disarmed and opened safely.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Reporter stated a Boeing aircraft's engine borescope inspection was signed off as 'no findings' when inspection photo clearly showed cracks.
summary: A maintenance planner identified cracks in a borescope image previously signed off as clear, prompting a recommendation to remove the engine upon landing at ZZZ. Due to a lack of spare parts at ZZZ, the aircraft was ferried back to ZZZ1 where the engine was replaced and sent for repair.

synopsis: C172 pilot and safety pilot reported the trim system was sticky inflight. After landing the system made an audible sound and became stuck.
summary: A safety pilot and student pilot in a C172 experienced sticky elevator trim during descent, climb, and approach between ZZZ and ZZZ1, requiring increased back-pressure. The issue was caused by the trim cable catching internally, preventing the tab from moving aft, leading to the aircraft being grounded for maintenance with no injuries.

synopsis: Falcon 50 Captain reported a near mid-air collision with a light aircraft after departing OPF.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS Resolution Advisory during climb in Class B airspace near MIA, requiring an immediate descent to avoid a Beech Bonanza. The aircraft descended from 7300 feet while turning right to 360 degrees, allowing the intruder to pass overhead without further ATC coordination.

synopsis: Pilots reported an NMAC in the pattern at MYF.
summary: The pilot reported two incidents at MYF: a near mid-air collision caused by ambiguous landing instructions during heavy traffic, and a runway alignment error due to incorrect GPS programming. The pilot lost 250 feet avoiding another aircraft and later corrected a wrong runway approach after realizing the navigation error.

synopsis: Airline Cargo Agent reported being advised by TSA of paint spray can in checked luggage.
summary: TSA notified the airline of a paint spray can found in a checked bag. No aircraft, flight phase, or specific outcome was described in the report.

synopsis: PA 28R-201 instructor reported a complete throttle failure, and dead-sticking the aircraft to a safe landing.
summary: An instructor and student experienced a stuck throttle lever during a training flight, causing high manifold pressure despite throttle retardation. They safely landed the aircraft by following emergency procedures to slow down with gear, flaps, and propeller settings before shutting down the engine.

synopsis: ATC Tower CIC, Developmental;and FLM reported issues that took place during a skill check.
summary: A controller conducting a skills check on Local Control cleared a VFR aircraft to land behind another without explicit visual separation instructions, while a CIC repeatedly interrupted the session to question the clearance. The FLM dismissed the concerns, though the aircraft maintained safe separation of 500 feet vertically and 2 nautical miles laterally.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported that a Supervisor did not act in a timely manner when the weather changed.
summary: Local Control and the Supervisor failed to timely update the ATIS for Aircraft X as visibility dropped to 3/4SM, despite Local Control's warnings. The Supervisor attributed the delay to ASOS recognition, but the reporter cited a lack of safety culture and repeated management failure to correct inaccurate weather information.

synopsis: Chicago Center Controller reported confusing terminology being used related to turbulence severity.
summary: An Arrival Coordinator reported that C90 controllers relayed non-standard turbulence terms like "Severe Chop" from pilots on the WATSN STAR, who allegedly avoided using "Severe turbulence" to prevent grounding. The reporter warned this imprecise communication creates safety risks and urged strict adherence to official terminology for turbulence reports.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported rejecting takeoff after receiving a wind shear warning.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff on Runway 8R after a windshear warning occurred at 80 knots while the preceding aircraft was airborne. The aircraft stopped safely on Taxiway Delta, was deemed safe to return to the gate, and the crew was subsequently deadheaded to ZZZ.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported returning to the gate because the EEC switches were in the alternate position.
summary: The flight crew discovered EEC switches were in ALTN mode during the Before Start checklist due to scratched plastic covers obscuring the switch position. They executed the QRH, consulted maintenance, and returned to the gate after confirming the switches were left out of position prior to towing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported reaching clearance limit on the PCIFC 2 arrival to LGB airport without runway transition or further clearance.
summary: The flight crew descended via the PCIFC 2 RNAV Arrival but leveled at 9,000 feet at STYFF due to a missing runway transition and radio contact loss. Approach mistakenly believed they were on the ROOBY 3 arrival before issuing a heading and altitude to resolve the confusion.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported diverting due to a cockpit window air leak.
summary: The flight crew diverted from ZZZ to ZZZ1 during climb due to a loud pressure leak from the First Officer's R2 window caused by an unapproved, flimsy condensation tube. Maintenance confirmed the non-rigid hose interfered with the window seal, necessitating an aircraft swap to complete the flight.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the Captain's Pitch Limit Indicator came into view during cruise and a descent was initiated before the full clearance was received from ATC.
summary: The Captain experienced a false Pitch Limit Indicator on his ADI while cruising at FL400, causing an unplanned descent to FL360 and minor altitude deviations due to delayed ATC clearances. Maintenance identified the cause as a malfunction in the #1 Stall Management Yaw Damper, and the flight resumed normally after switching to the B autopilot.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 First Officer reported Crew Resource Management issues with a 787 Line Check Airman.
summary: A pilot reported safety concerns during a 787 trip with a Check Airman involving fuel planning, weather deviation clearances, and auto-throttle usage. The Check Airman refused extra fuel, initially denied wide weather avoidance, and insisted on keeping auto-throttles engaged during a visual approach, which the pilot argued degraded manual flying skills and safety.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported not documenting an aircraft equipment problem in the maintenance log.
summary: The crew failed to log an inoperative AP 2 during taxi and takeoff due to expectation bias and fatigue, mistaking it for a known Pack 2 deferral. Maintenance Control later identified the issue as an FMGC 2 failure after the second engine start.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported exceeding 250 knots below 10,000 feet due to severe turbulence.
summary: During approach to ZZZ, the crew encountered severe turbulence below 10,000 feet that prevented maintaining speeds under 250 knots despite corrective actions. The aircraft was grounded for inspection after exiting the turbulence at 5,000 feet and landing safely.

synopsis: EMB-140 Captain reported being unable to meet the given speed restrictions on approach. Aircraft encountered icing conditions, went around and diverted to another airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate to severe icing on non-protected surfaces and pilot windows while on the ILS XR final approach at 2000 feet. Unable to comply with further ATC speed reductions due to ice accretion, they executed a go-around, declared minimum fuel, and diverted to ZZZ1.

synopsis: EMB140 Captain reported Dispatch failed to provide assistance with weather and flight support requests.
summary: The pilot reported a flight to ZZZ1 with inoperative localizers where low ceilings and visibility caused departure delays and communication issues with Dispatch. Despite Dispatch dismissing concerns about the takeoff alternate and approach minimums, the crew successfully landed after coordinating directly with the tower.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported receiving a Bleed Overtemp Warning while in icing conditions.
summary: The flight crew encountered icing and dual bleed overtemp warnings at 13,000 feet MSL while departing LEX in a winter storm. They climbed to FL330 to exit the ice, reset the bleed valve, and completed the flight without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: Citation First Officer reported a hydraulic problem after takeoff and a rolling and pitching anomaly when extending the flaps.
summary: The flight crew diverted a climbing aircraft after receiving hydraulic pressure and volume low warnings. During landing configuration, asymmetric spoiler deployment caused an abrupt roll and pitch when flaps were extended, but the crew regained control, landed safely, and noted a need for QRH updates regarding this hazard.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a heading deviation due to significant fatigue.
summary: A fatigued pilot not flying on a red-eye flight to ZZZ misinterpreted a heading clearance during the ILS approach, causing a discrepancy with the pilot flying. The reporter attributes the confusion and degraded situational awareness to severe fatigue resulting from organizational pressure to extend duty time.

synopsis: Embraer E175 Captain reported a dual bleed failure resulting in a diversion and an overweight landing.
summary: The flight crew of an Embraer 175 experienced a BLEED 1 failure at FL240 while operating with BLEED 2 INOP, forcing an emergency descent and overweight landing at ZZZZ1. The pilot attributed the failure to both packs pressurizing the operative bleed valve, citing a need to update MEL procedures to turn off the associated pack when a bleed is inoperative.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported a communication problem while dealing with a circuit breaker that popped in-flight causing an increased workload.
summary: During cruise at FL370, a popped circuit breaker triggered an ECAM message, prompting the crew to seek maintenance advice regarding potential icing. Unable to establish voice contact with Dispatch or Maintenance due to communication failures, the crew descended normally without diverting, though the incident highlighted critical connectivity issues.

synopsis: A330 First Officer reported moderate turbulence resulted in a speed reduction before making the request with ATC.
summary: Pilots flying westbound on NAT D at FL390 reduced speed from Mach .82 to .80 due to moderate turbulence and notified Gander via CPDLC after the change. ATC acknowledged but later advised that speed change requests should be made prior to execution.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a communication error during pushback that resulted in a broken tow bar and a delay.
summary: During pushback, the tug driver moved the aircraft with brakes set after a miscommunication regarding the need for additional distance, causing the tow bar to break. The incident resulted in a 20-minute delay for repairs but no aircraft damage, attributed to nonstandard procedures and unclear communication protocols.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported ground conflict during taxi with another taxiing aircraft.
summary: The pilot and First Officer nearly collided with Aircraft Y on an unplowed taxiway during snowy conditions while following another aircraft to runway 22L. The First Officer spotted the conflict while the pilot was distracted by skidding and ATC congestion, allowing them to stop just feet away.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported poor communication with Flight Attendant relating to a Flight Attendant's injury.
summary: During descent into ZZZ, a flight attendant injured his head by striking a metal tray table while standing from the jump seat. The crew member sustained a minor bruise and headache but declined medical assistance and remained fit to work the return leg.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported aircraft sliding on an ice and snow covered taxiway.
summary: The crew reported sliding on a snow-covered taxiway at GRR while attempting to stop short of Echo to yield to a CRJ. The incident was caused by slick conditions and unfamiliarity with the taxiway location, though ATC resolved the situation by having the CRJ yield.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported departing without knowledge the release was to an alternate destination instead of the planned destination.
summary: The flight crew departed Seattle for ZZZ beyond the required time due to winter weather delays and miscommunication with Dispatch regarding runway closure limits. Although the flight plan dropped from the system, Tower cleared the aircraft for takeoff, resulting in a departure that likely required an alternate destination.

synopsis: Airliner 99 First Officer reported a ground strike by the number one propeller into an unforeseen snow bank while taxiing.
summary: The pilot exited Runway 16R at night in rain and struck an unreported 6–10 inch snowbank on a high-speed taxiway, causing two bent propeller blades on the left engine. The incident resulted from inadequate snow removal and missing NOTAMs regarding snowbanks at runway exits.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a late change from the RNAV (GPS) Rwy 3 approach to Hilton Head to the VOR-A circling approach, with an MDA very close to the reported ceiling, due to a reported loss of GPS signal.
summary: The flight crew operating into HXD switched from an RNAV to a VOR-A circle-to-land approach due to ATC-reported GPS unreliability. High workload caused them to overlook company SOPs requiring a 1,000 ft. ceiling, resulting in an approach flown at the lower published 800 ft. MDA.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported feeling pressure to accomplish a beverage service even though the flight crew knew there was turbulence ahead.
summary: During a flight to LAS, cabin crew performed a beverage service against the Captain's initial advice and company policy due to peer pressure. Strong turbulence during descent caused galley items to fly, soaking the reporter and creating a dangerous situation where injuries could have occurred.

synopsis: Aircraft Maintenance Technician reported being pressured by his Supervisor not to write-up discrepancies found during aircraft inspection.
summary: A mechanic performing an anti-ice duct inspection on Aircraft X's Number 1 engine reported that the Shift Supervisor pressured them to withhold documented discrepancies to protect the station's reputation. The mechanic stated this interference prioritized reputation over safety and disrupted the required concentration for the inspection.

synopsis: Maintenance technicians were directed to conduct weather radar test inside hanger and within 50 feet of flammable liquids.
summary: A mechanic refused to perform a weather radar test on an aircraft in a hangar near flammable drums due to AMM warnings against operating within 50 feet of fuel hazards. Management authorized the task, claiming the manual does not explicitly prohibit operation near such materials.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported some NOTAMs for inoperative airport systems preclude use as an alternate airport while others do not.
summary: A pilot reported that excessive NOTAMs at MCI unnecessarily restrict alternate status and instrument approaches by citing inoperative VORs, despite modern aircraft having GPS and RNAV capabilities. The reporter noted a lack of standardization, as other airports allow RNAV substitution for these inoperative components.

synopsis: General aviation pilot reported a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot landed a Piper on Runway YY at dusk after switching from Runway XX due to a departing aircraft. Rushing to clear the runway, the pilot turned left too soon, veered into a muddy field, and sustained propeller and engine damage.

synopsis: Eclipse 550 Captain reported autopilot disengage issues during final approach.
summary: The pilot experienced an autopilot disconnect failure at 1,500 AGL during an ILS approach to Runway XX at ZZZ. Pressing the 'ALL INTERRUPT' button disengaged the Flight Director, causing a rough transition, but the pilot corrected the aircraft and landed safely.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air Taxi Captain reported a ramp excursion due to confusing Marshaller instructions and taxiway markings.
summary: The pilot taxied a passenger aircraft in darkness and rain, circling a fuel island due to confusing lighted wand signals and a yellow line mistaken for a taxiway centerline. The right main gear exited the asphalt into grass, requiring engine shutdown and deplaning, which the pilot attributed to poor layout familiarity and inadequate markings.

synopsis: GA pilot reported entering a spin while practicing stalls in an unfamiliar aircraft, which had unexpected stall characteristics.
summary: A student pilot and CFI in a Grumman AA5A entered an inadvertent spin during a power-off stall checkout due to the pilot's aileron input, fixation on the turn coordinator, and sleep deprivation. The CFI recovered the aircraft at 2,100 feet after a 900-foot descent, preventing a ground impact.

synopsis: A Corporate pilot reported they were questioned by FAA Investigators about their company operation.
summary: FAA investigators interviewed the pilot and crew after a full duty day at a customs facility regarding charter operations. A subsequent ramp check occurred, but the pilot noted investigators failed to photograph credentials and recommended future questioning include legal counsel and occur before duty ends.

aircraft: Cessna Single Turboprop Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported a separation issue relate to wake turbulence separation and reclassification of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a C208 for an ILS approach to Runway 7L after verifying 7 miles of lateral spacing behind a Boeing on Runway 7R. The Tower Supervisor subsequently broke out the C208 due to a disagreement over the radar-measured separation, which the controller maintained was safe and compliant.

synopsis: ZSE Center Controller reported an airspace violation when he climbed into airspace not owned by the sector he was working. Reporter also stated this was due to fatigue and thinking about the government shutdown.
summary: An air traffic controller assigned Aircraft X to climb to FL410 instead of the required FL230 during a hand-off from low to high altitude sectors. The controller attributed this error to fatigue, lack of recent low-altitude sector experience, and distractions from coaching a trainee and personal stress.

synopsis: A pilot reported the aircraft slid off an icy runway while taxiing after landing.
summary: The Captain landed an aircraft in wet conditions with reported good braking action but slid uncontrollably onto the runway overrun area while turning onto a taxiway at the runway end. The incident occurred after the Tower instructed the crew to bypass a closer taxiway, despite no prior reports of poor braking conditions.

synopsis: B737 NG flight crew reported departing illegally due to weather.
summary: The flight crew departed with 18 minutes of deicing allowance time remaining, unaware that ATIS had updated to report three types of freezing precipitation. The pilot later realized the takeoff was illegal because they failed to check the updated ATIS before departure, despite ATC not advising of the change.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported experiencing an engine fire after takeoff resulting in an air return to the departure airport.
summary: During takeoff, the right engine EGT peaked and triggered fire warnings, prompting the crew to pull the fire handle and land. Post-landing smoke from the right engine required ARFF inspection and towing to the gate.

synopsis: 757 Captain reported the jetbridge is set to stop too far from the door leaving a large gap that could cause injury to a boarding passenger especially young children.
summary: The pilot reported a 10-inch gap between the aircraft and jetway during gate operations, posing a fall hazard for children. The First Officer had a mechanic reposition the bridge, attributing the gap to overly sensitive bumper sensors that halted movement to prevent aircraft damage.

synopsis: B767-400 flight crew reported a recirculation fan failure in the flight deck resulting in smoke and fumes event.
summary: Pilots on a Boeing 767-400 experienced dual recirculation fan failures at FL300, followed by smoke and an electrical smell from the right fan 90 minutes later. After shutting off the right fan, the smoke ceased, allowing a normal landing, though the First Officer later developed tracheal bronchitis from smoke inhalation.

synopsis: B777 Captain and First Officer reported a problem with the aircraft, checked with Maintenance, departed but when airborne after more discussion decided they should have stayed on the ground to have the problem looked into more.
summary: The flight crew departed with an MEL for a left bleed sensor, misinterpreting a subsequent bleed pressure caution as normal. Maintenance Control later identified a High Pressure Shutoff Valve trip, advised an in-flight reset, and the crew successfully restored normal bleed operation for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported a track deviation occurred on the DRLLR RNAV STAR into IAH, following a late change in the arrival.
summary: The crew accepted a last-minute RNAV Y Runway 26R approach while on DRLLR 5, but the First Officer overcompensated during a manual turn after crossing SKLER, causing a course deviation. ATC issued a breakaway instruction and vectors for a climb to 7,000 feet before revectoring the aircraft for an uneventful ILS 26R landing.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported after a temporary loss of nose wheel steering company operations requested that the crew taxi back to the gate without a tow.
summary: During taxi-out, the crew lost nose wheel steering, causing the aircraft to drift toward another gate. Despite Operations suggesting a reset, the pilots refused to taxi due to repeated failures and safety concerns, resulting in a one-hour delay before a tug towed the aircraft back to the gate.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported incorrect MEL assigned resulting in abnormal operational pneumatic configuration.
summary: The flight crew departed with an amber ENG BLEED L message and an incorrect MEL 362 for a bleed pressure sensor. Maintenance Control later confirmed the issue required MEL 361, and a bleed switch reset restored left engine bleed air, allowing the flight to land safely.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported navigating to the wrong fix due to similar sounding fixes (GOATZ and COAZT) on the same RNAV STAR.
summary: The flight crew operating into ONT descended early and crossed COAZT at 16,000 feet instead of the cleared GOATZ due to similar fix names causing miscommunication. ATC issued a new clearance to POXKU, and the crew attributed the deviation to the difficulty in distinguishing the two similarly named waypoints.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported experiencing an Air Data Computer malfuntion while on a international flight.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple airspeed and flight control EICAS messages at FL300 due to a suspected right-side ADC/pitot static failure. They diverted to ZZZZ, landed safely with a tailwind and no automation, and attributed the resolution to effective crew coordination and checklist execution.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reported an NMAC with a departure from an intersecting runway during a go around, and miscommunication with ATC.
summary: During a visual approach go-around, the crew contacted Departure instead of Tower due to radar confusion, receiving climb instructions that conflicted with a nearby E175. The pilots ignored the climb and TCAS RA to level off, avoiding a collision, and attributed the event to communication breakdowns and radar misidentification.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported operating a delayed flight with passengers even though the Dispatch Release indicated the flight was to be operated as a ferry flight.
summary: A First Officer and Captain operating a revenue flight from ZZZ to ZZZ3 with 14 passengers discovered the Dispatch Release incorrectly stated "Operated under 14 CFR Part 91." The crew attributed the oversight to rushing during pre-flight checks, while noting a broader communication breakdown between operations and the flight team regarding the flight's status.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported aircraft flap speed exceedance during Missed Approach maneuver while experiencing wind shear.
summary: The crew of a heavy aircraft encountered severe wind shear and tailwinds during an ILS 34 approach at ZZZ, causing speed excursions and control difficulties. They executed a go-around, attempted a second approach to Runway 22, and ultimately diverted to the origin airport due to unsafe conditions.

synopsis: Citation Captain reported a hydraulic problem during initial climb forcing them to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a dual hydraulic failure at FL290, causing uncommanded rolls during flap extension and requiring an emergency landing at ZZZ2. Post-flight inspection revealed fluid leaks and extended right wing spoilers, prompting the captain to recommend QRH revisions regarding spoiler control and landing distance multipliers.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported landing aircraft with incorrect configuration due to multiple intermittent EICAS warning messages.
summary: The flight crew encountered intermittent anti-ice warnings and a left engine vibration spike during approach in icing conditions. While managing these alerts, they inadvertently landed with flaps 30 because they failed to complete the landing configuration.

synopsis: C402C Captain reported a left engine surge requiring a return to departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced left engine surges, yaw, and fuel flow discrepancies during climb and descent, prompting a precautionary return to ZZZ. Maintenance later attributed the abnormality to likely fuel contamination, resulting in the aircraft being grounded and the pilot relieved of duty.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported clearance heading deviation after changes were made on the CDU on approach.
summary: The flight crew on a ZZZZZ arrival missed a required turn at ZZZZZ1 after changing the ILS approach in the CDU, causing the AFDS to remain in LNAV with incorrect active waypoints. The pilot attributed the navigation error to the distraction of making CDU changes while approaching a turn, which reduced monitoring capability.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported Tower issued a clearance to a fix and Departure Control did not know about it.
summary: The flight crew received a direct clearance to FEZTR from Tower but was told by Departure they were off course after a late handoff at 6,000 ft. The crew attributed the confusion to poor coordination between controllers and admitted they should have clarified the non-standard clearance earlier.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported turning on the incorrect taxiway, then ATC issued another clearance which included taxiing on a closed portion of a taxiway.
summary: The pilot made a wrong turn after landing on 12R and was subsequently cleared by Ground ATC to taxi via a closed taxiway. The pilot attributed the error to outdated ATIS information, lack of closure markings, and conflicting instructions between ATC and NOTAMs.

synopsis: Pilot reported ATC issues relating to separation of traffic on the ground and in the air during departure from DCA.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X at DCA reported a runway incursion risk when cleared for takeoff on Runway 1 while a Regional Jet was still crossing the intersection. The pilot delayed departure until the crossing traffic cleared, then safely took off but criticized ATC for issuing the clearance prematurely and for insufficient separation in IMC conditions.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported experiencing pressurization problems on departure due to improper pressurization panel setup.
summary: The Captain and First Officer misinterpreted MEL procedures for a pressurization defect during pre-flight, setting the manual altitude to 6,000 feet instead of the destination elevation. This caused an excess cabin altitude warning at 9,000 feet, requiring manual pressurization control to stabilize the cabin before continuing the flight.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported experiencing an engine fire during taxi for takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine fire during taxi after pushback, caused by significant oil leakage, with no cockpit indications. After securing the engine and confirming the fire was extinguished by ARFF, the crew refused a maintenance request to run the engine at the gate due to safety concerns.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported observing snow accumulation on the flaps after de-icing. Returned to gate for second de-icing.
summary: The Pilot in Command discovered one inch of snow on the flaps after a pre-takeoff cabin check, caused by a new procedure requiring flaps up during deicing. The flight returned to the gate for a second deicing with flaps down to ensure clean control surfaces before departure.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported climbing above the assigned departure altitude into a confliction with crossing traffic.
summary: The Captain and First Officer set an incorrect 10,000-foot altitude in the MCP due to distractions and the Relief First Officer's absence during clearance delivery. This error caused a TCAS RA and a climb to 3,800 feet with only 400 feet vertical separation from traffic before the crew descended to the correct 3,000 feet.

synopsis: CRJ900 flight crew reported taking evasive action on a visual approach to avoid traffic deviating off course on the parallel runway.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to runway 12L at Minneapolis received a traffic caution and RA while intercepting the localizer near another aircraft on runway 12R. The crew manually turned left to avoid conflict, complied with the RA, and completed a safe landing, attributing the event to early ATC clearance that reduced lateral separation.

synopsis: Air taxi pilot reported strong up and down drafts prevented the heavy aircraft from climbing as expected in a mountainous area.
summary: The pilot encountered stronger-than-expected downdrafts and turbulence during climbout from RNO, causing the aircraft to sink below 13,000 feet MSL and prompting ATC to declare an emergency. Despite utilizing max power, the pilot continued to the Sacramento Valley to avoid landing risks from low-level wind shear, eventually maintaining 14,500 feet.

synopsis: Two air carrier flight attendants reported injuries from a hard landing due to wind shear.
summary: During landing, wind shear caused a rejected approach, resulting in a hard bounce and immediate go-around. The violent impact injured a jumpseater and all four flight attendants with back, neck, and chest pain, requiring clinic visits and ending the crew's trip.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported lack of oxygen and a feeling of hypoxia and that the pilot advised that they, 'shouldn't be experiencing these symptoms.'
summary: During final descent into ZZZ, a cabin pressure loss caused by an overheated air conditioning pack led to hypoxia symptoms in all seven crew members. The flight deck failed to inform the cabin crew immediately, delaying oxygen use and causing concern over communication and the aircraft's continued service despite repeated pressurization issues.

synopsis: Mechanic reported that lack of proper equipment may lead to a major fuel spill when obtaining the fuel sample for the pre-flight fuel freeze test.
summary: A mechanic suffered a minor fuel spill on their clothing while sampling uplifted fuel because the fuel truck and sample hose lacked flow control valves. The reporter recommends suspending fuel freeze tests until trucks are refitted with on/off valves to prevent major spills.

synopsis: C150 student pilot and the non-participating flight instructor reported a communication breakdown resulted in a runway incursion.
summary: A student pilot and instructor were confused by an ATC clearance to maintain 600 feet for a restricted low approach during a touch-and-go, causing the student to initially ignore the instruction. ATC resolved the situation by holding the inspection truck short of the runway, preventing an incident.

synopsis: Air ambulance pilot reported a near midair collision with a crop duster near Paris, Texas.
summary: During a patient transfer return at 2,000 feet MSL, the pilot and nurse spotted a crop duster less than 1/8 mile away and executed a hard right turn to avoid a collision within 50 yards. The crop duster maintained its course, TCAS showed no traffic, and the flight continued to base without further issues.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported several heading deviations while maneuvering for landing.
summary: A PPL pilot flying a G1000-equipped Archer III mistakenly configured for Runway 34 and then entered a downwind for Runway 16 while cleared for Runway 9. Air Traffic Control intercepted both errors, issuing a go-around and a heading correction to prevent a runway incursion.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported descending prior to crossing restriction on approach.
summary: The flight crew descended to 4,000 feet early on an ILS 28C approach to O'Hare due to a mistaken belief they were above the glideslope. They crossed waypoint RZUKO at 4,000 feet instead of the cleared 5,000 feet but intercepted the glideslope and landed normally with no traffic conflicts.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being below crossing restriction while reprogramming FMS.
summary: During a Boeing 900 descent on the SILCN4 arrival to SJC, the crew descended approximately 1,000 feet below the published FL200 restriction at the SILCN fix. The deviation resulted from confusion caused by multiple ATC speed changes, turbulence, and FMC input difficulties while the Captain managed vertical speed manually.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported experiencing a pressurization problem during climb.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude increase to 11,300 ft while climbing through FL250, triggering ECAM warnings and requiring a descent to 17,000 ft. After confirming normal pressurization at 19,000 ft, they continued to the destination without diverting.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a rejected takeoff due to asymmetric engine thrust.
summary: During takeoff, the Captain rejected the roll after the aircraft pulled left due to the right engine producing TOGA power while both thrust levers were set to FLX. The RTO caused brake temperatures to reach 325 degrees, but after cooling and normal maintenance tests, the crew completed a successful TOGA takeoff.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew reported a confusing clearance revision via CPDLC led to a track deviation.
summary: The flight crew misprogrammed a CPDLC reroute clearance due to military activity, executing a direct to TERYY before the required N20E160 waypoint. The error occurred because the conditional instruction was separated from the main clearance text, causing the crew to overlook the specific activation point.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that a Ramp Agent loaded a bag into the forward cargo compartment while the aircraft's engines were running.
summary: During pushback with both engines running, a ground crew member loaded a bag into the forward cargo compartment without notifying the flight deck. The pilot reported this unsafe act by a new employee could have resulted in a fatality and immediately contacted airport operations.

synopsis: B737 pilot reported sighting a drone while on the VEECK arrival into O'Hare airport at 11,000 feet.
summary: A pilot on an aircraft arriving at ORD at 11,000 ft observed a black multi-rotor unmanned aircraft pass within 1,000 ft of the left wing. The Captain, occupied with ATC instructions, did not see the object, and the crew reported the encounter to ATC without initially classifying it as a NMAC.

synopsis: Tractor driver reported the tug spun out while towing aircraft in windy and rainy conditions.
summary: A ramp agent and partner moved an aircraft with a super tug in high winds and rain. While turning from Bravo 1 onto a taxiway per Ground instructions, the tug slid and its nose gear rotated 180 degrees, prompting a safety report to Ground and the supervisor.

synopsis: B767-300 First Officer reported scraping the tail skid on landing after encountering wake turbulence from a B777 taking off on the parallel runway.
summary: During a visual landing at MIA Runway 8L, the crew scraped the tail skid due to an abnormal pitch-up caused by suspected wake turbulence from a simultaneous B777 takeoff on Runway 8R. Maintenance inspected the aircraft, and it was returned to service without delay.

synopsis: Tractor driver reported losing control of the tug while towing across an icy ramp.
summary: Ground crew towing an aircraft from the gate to the North Ramp struck a sheet of ice while descending from high to low elevation. The attempt to correct the turn caused the tug to jackknife on the iced surface.

synopsis: Ramp worker reported gate agents were approaching the aircraft before it was secured, making for a dangerous situation.
summary: Pilots reported that while taxiing to the gate, a Customer Service Agent raised the jet bridge and ramp staff opened pits before the aircraft was chocked or stopped. The crew notified dispatch and supervisors, causing ground personnel to withdraw equipment, preventing a potential accident caused by negligence.

synopsis: Airline ground personnel reported Hazmat loading error with no method to prevent aircraft from taking off.
summary: Ramp personnel finalized Aircraft X's departure with only 7 bags instead of the required 15 to secure hazmat, violating FAA regulations. The crew's simultaneous weight request and number 1 takeoff status prevented intervention, resulting in the aircraft departing with improperly secured dangerous goods.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported receiving a terrain warning while on approach at night.
summary: Fatigued pilots on a visual approach to runway 17 at AVL descended too early from 6,000 feet, triggering a terrain warning. The crew immediately climbed back to 6,000 feet, re-established the approach, and landed safely after attributing the error to insufficient rest.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported encountering severe turbulence and deviating from assigned altitude, along with a Traffic Advisory on another aircraft.
summary: During cruise at FL 230, the flight crew encountered severe turbulence causing altitude and airspeed fluctuations, resulting in a Traffic Advisory and a Resolution Advisory for a flight below. The crew reported to ATC and received clearance for a lower altitude.

synopsis: ERJ-175 Captain reported exceeding assigned altitude while troubleshooting aircraft malfunctions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an altitude deviation through 5000 feet during takeoff due to distraction from multiple FMA failures and a BLEED 2 OVERPRESSURE caution. The crew corrected the deviation after the First Officer followed stuck TOGA pitch guidance while the Captain troubleshooted, subsequently restoring all systems.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported imputing wrong waypoint into flight management system. Crew realized mistake and continued as instructed by ATC.
summary: The Captain entered "HAVAN" instead of "HEVAN" in the FMS for a flight to ZZZ1, causing an incorrect right turn. ATC and the crew detected the deviation, corrected the course, and the Captain reported the ground-entry error to the INDY Field Office upon landing.

synopsis: CL-300 Captain reported receiving multiple indications of hydraulic system failure on approach.
summary: The crew experienced low hydraulic pressure, grinding noise, and vibration during gear extension and flap selection, forcing a go-around and emergency landing. The aircraft required towing off the runway due to the left-side hydraulic failure and lack of safe gear indication.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain reported severe turbulence encounter resulting in momentary loss of control.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence at FL200 and 13,000 feet while approaching ZZZ, causing brief loss of control and airspeed deviations. They descended to 17,000 feet after notifying ATC, confirmed passenger safety, and landed without further incident.

synopsis: ERJ-145 flight crew reported encountering severe turbulence, and momentary loss of control.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence at 35,000 feet during climb, causing autopilot disengagement, speed exceedance, and an uncontrolled dive. The Captain recovered the aircraft at 33,000 feet with no injuries, attributing the safe outcome to preventive actions like slowing the aircraft and securing the cabin.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported right pack overheat followed by cabin altitude warning in flight.
summary: During cruise at FL390, a right pack overheat triggered an emergency descent to 10,000 feet, causing a maximum cabin altitude of 12,000 feet and hypoxic symptoms for flight attendants. The crew suspects the right pack failure and left pack inability to maintain pressure caused the event, noting this was the third occurrence on this aircraft.

synopsis: First Officer reported a right engine oil bypass message, which led to shutting down the engine and landing with only one operational engine.
summary: The flight crew received a Right Engine Oil Bypass message on the upper Display Unit during approach to runway XXL. They performed the engine shutdown checklist, executed a single-engine landing with ARFF response, and taxied to the gate without further incident.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported encountering severe weather/turbulence while being vectored for landing.
summary: The pilot flying encountered severe turbulence, windshear, and heavy rain while being vectored for approach at CLT at 4,000 feet, causing airspeed to surge to 300 knots and bank angles to exceed 45 degrees. The crew diverted to ZZZ for fuel after finding that onboard weather radar and WSI failed to depict the hazard, though a post-flight inspection revealed no damage.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported misreading the ATIS and selected the incorrect approach.
summary: The flight crew prepared for the wrong ILS approach at ZZZ after mistakenly retrieving the departure ATIS instead of the arrival ATIS. Although ATC cleared them for the correct ILS Y approach, the pilots initially failed to identify the localizer until the Pilot Monitoring tuned the correct frequency, resolving the issue without loss of separation.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported pitch control problems after takeoff due to a trim switch failure.
summary: During initial climb, a faulty First Officer trim switch locked out the Captain's trim and prevented autopilot engagement, causing nose-up trim issues. The crew returned to ZZZ for a safe landing after maintenance confirmed the switch failure on the ground.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported wing tip contact with parked aircraft due to improper ground crew marshalling.
summary: Pilots and ramp crew at ZZZ airport experienced a winglet strike while taxiing behind a parked aircraft in blowing snow. The collision occurred because marshaling personnel failed to stop the aircraft despite the lead ramp crew's warnings, resulting in a sheared winglet and subsequent taxi to a different parking spot.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported missing an altitude restriction on arrival into IAH, citing a late runway change as contributing.
summary: The pilot reported a late runway switch to 27 with conflicting NOTAMs and a confusing visual clearance with crossing restrictions during arrival. The pilot attributed the incident to poor ATC briefings and ATIS information, noting they accepted the clearance but caught the errors late.

synopsis: Corporate pilot reported ATC cancelled the approach clearance without any further instructions so the pilot cancelled IFR, but was then advised should not have descended.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR RNAV approach to KSEF in IMC had the approach cancelled by Center due to a restricted area conflict, leaving the aircraft at 2000 feet without a heading. After being instructed to switch to a visual approach, the pilot descended without explicit clearance to avoid clouds and landed safely, though the controller later claimed the IFR clearance remained active.

synopsis: King Air 90 pilot reported encountering severe turbulence and controllability problems associated with the turbulence.
summary: The aircraft encountered severe turbulence causing pitch, altitude, and airspeed variations to exceed controllable limits for a short duration. Conditions abated within 2 miles, and the subsequent approach and landing at APA were uneventful.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported intermittent electrical failure and return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a total electrical failure during climb out from ZZZ. Intermittent power restoration allowed contact with Approach and Tower for return and landing clearances, resulting in a recovery with no traffic conflicts.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported a go around and off-field landing due to flaps being stuck full down.
summary: An instructor and student encountered windshear and stuck flaps during a soft-field training approach at ZZZ airport, causing an inability to climb. The instructor executed a forced landing in a nearby cornfield, attributing the flap failure to an electrical issue likely caused by wear and tear.

synopsis: Air taxi helicopter pilot reported flying a leg without a legal Risk Analysis confirmation.
summary: A standby pilot and medical crew prepared for a flight after mistakenly believing the pilot's Risk Analysis (RA) was submitted. The pilot later discovered the RA was saved as a draft, not submitted, causing a delay until it was corrected after landing.

synopsis: Airline employee reported Hazmat not properly secured for transport.
summary: Staff discovered two collars were not fixed while emptying a container containing DG goods (ICE 9). The narrative does not specify the aircraft, phase of flight, or further outcome.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate Jet flight crew reported high snowbanks at MSP made observing other ground traffic and following ATC's taxi instructions difficult. Other taxiing aircraft were in very close proximity.
summary: The pilot reported a close call while taxiing a small aircraft at KMSP where snowbanks obstructed the view of three Boeing 737s on Taxiway Whiskey. The pilot attributed the 25-foot wingtip-to-nose clearance to the snowbanks preventing timely visual detection, noting that no hold-short instructions were issued by ATC.

synopsis: Salt Lake Center Controller reported that Big Sky Approach will not accept handoffs in a timely manner, causing the center to turn aircraft to avoid and airspace incursion.
summary: The controller turned Aircraft X 90 degrees left during descent on the SADYL3 arrival to avoid terrain after Big Sky Approach delayed the handoff. The aircraft penetrated Big Sky airspace because one minute was insufficient for the turn, prompting the controller to initiate turns two minutes from the boundary in the future.

synopsis: JFK Tower Controller reported emergency vehicles on the runway were not in communication with ATC and not visible on ASDE.
summary: Aircraft Y executed a go-around on ILS 22R due to five to six unresponsive trucks on the runway that were not detected by the malfunctioning ASDE-X. The incident was caused by the trucks' lack of communication with ATC and the system's failure to display them, which the reporter attributes to equipment issues and insufficient driver training.

synopsis: ZJX Center Controller reported receiving a handoff and communications from an overlying sector of an aircraft that was in direct conflict with another aircraft in the overlying sector.
summary: Air Traffic Controller X issued an immediate right turn and expedited descent to Aircraft X at 28,000 feet to avoid a conflict with Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the near-miss to suppressed Conflict Alerts and poor performance by the supervisor and the controller in the sector above.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an aircraft on a heading to intercept an approach descended early and below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a low altitude alert to Aircraft X during a GPS approach at MFR after the crew initially denied terrain visibility. The crew climbed to the minimum vectoring altitude of 8700 feet, confirmed terrain in sight, and were re-cleared for the approach.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Boston TRACON Controller reported an aircraft on unexpected, uncoordinated arrival routing.
summary: An aircraft arrived on an uncoordinated direct routing instead of the planned ZBW16/A90 LOA because the ERAM system failed to generate a new flight plan strip after an amendment. The reporter recommends verifying ERAM automation performance and ensuring future compliance with LOA or verbal coordination.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Orlando Executive Controller reported an unsafe situation when a departure turned towards an arrival causing a Resolution Advisory for the arriving aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft Y deviated from a cleared 055 heading to 090 after takeoff, creating a conflict with Aircraft X on final approach. Aircraft X responded to a Resolution Advisory by climbing to 1,400 feet MSL before descending to land.

synopsis: Atlanta TRACON Controller reported an aircraft entered an area with a higher Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to display the Minimum Vectoring Altitude map when Aircraft X entered the sector at 3,000 feet, triggering a low altitude alert as the aircraft descended below the 3,400-foot MVA. The controller immediately climbed the aircraft to 3,400 feet and attributed the incident to turning off the MVA map earlier and not reactivating it.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Traffic Management Coordinator reported an Operations Manager assign a non certified Supervisor to work a sector during an aircraft emergency event.
summary: A TMC reported that during an emergency involving Aircraft X's autopilot failure, an Operations Manager replaced a competent controller with an uncertified Supervisor. The reporter stated this caused initial chaos and questioned the decision to remove an experienced controller from the position.

synopsis: Two Center Controllers reported an aircraft responded to an RA for traffic as well as encountered moderate turbulence causing injuries to some of the flight crew.
summary: An air traffic controller took over a sector where Aircraft X and Y experienced a TCAS resolution, causing Aircraft X to enter an unstabilized descent with an improperly configured engine. Upon leveling at 24,000 feet, Aircraft X encountered moderate turbulence, resulting in two crew injuries, which the controller attributed to the high airspeed from the TCAS-induced descent profile.

synopsis: B-737 First Officer reported descending below glideslope intercept altitude during vector to final.
summary: The pilot inadvertently set the altitude alerter to 1500 feet instead of adjusting the heading bug while descending on base leg, causing an unintended descent to 2100 feet. The pilot recognized the error, disengaged the autopilot, and climbed back to 2800 feet after receiving a low altitude alert from ATC.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an unstable approach when circling to land.
summary: The crew, operating a delayed flight into Burbank, accepted an ATC vector for an ILS 8 circle to Runway 15 but encountered high speed, tailwinds, and turbulence. Despite multiple GPWS warnings, the Pilot Flying continued the approach and landed, later reporting that a go-around was necessary due to the unstable conditions.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the cost index was set too low by Dispatch, so the aircraft could not meet the published speeds on the arrival.
summary: Pilots reported that a Dispatch-set Cost Index of 20 caused FMC "UNABLE 280 KTS" errors during the pre-flight weight and balance data load for arrivals with 280-knot STAR restrictions. The crew identified this conflict between fuel-saving programming and published speed limits as a safety issue that forces manual VNAV corrections and increases the risk of pilot deviations.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being given an instruction that would violate a FAR regarding speeds below a LAX Class Bravo airspace.
summary: A B737 crew descending via the OHSEA 1 arrival to SNA reported that ATC issued a direct routing and descent rate conflicting with FAR 91.117 speed limits in LAX Class B airspace. The crew noted that approach database speed constraints of 210 knots also violated the 200-knot restriction, requiring manual intervention to remain compliant.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported the aircraft slide forward with the parking brake set at the gate due to ramp conditions.
summary: The Captain reported that after setting the parking brake at the gate, the aircraft slid approximately 3 feet forward on an icy ramp due to residual engine thrust during shutdown. The movement ceased once the engines were shut down.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported undocumented Hazmat cargo loaded on aircraft with no flight crew notification.
summary: The First Officer and Captain identified three unlabeled cryogenic medical containers on the ramp during pre-flight, despite ACARS and paperwork indicating no dangerous goods. Operations confirmed the error and removed the cargo before departure, preventing an unauthorized hazardous materials load.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported ATC told them they took off after their clearance void time.
summary: The pilot departed EUG without Tower communications, receiving a Center clearance void if not off by 05:57 UTC. Although ATC called stating the clearance was void, the pilot noted the aircraft clock still read 05:57 at liftoff, raising questions about whether the void time applies at the start or end of the minute.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported company policy change that created an unsafe condition in the cabin and crew rest area.
summary: A Line Check Airman reported that removing a flight attendant from the B767's B-zone galley created an unsafe condition during cruise. This change leaves pilots vulnerable to passenger conflict while using restrooms or the crew rest facility at seat 7D due to a lack of immediate cabin crew support.

synopsis: Airline Ground Personnel reported Hazmat cargo listed for air transport without proper cargo documentation.
summary: The cargo warehouse loaded a lithium battery and another item onto the aircraft without a booking. No specific aircraft, phase of flight, or outcome was described in the narrative.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported a lateral course deviation after their FMS dropped off line.
summary: Pilots reported that FMS #2 dropped offline during cruise, causing loss of lateral mode and flight plan data. They attributed the recurring issue to a recent software update requiring manual entry of landing airport, OAT, and altimeter settings.

synopsis: C402 Captain reported returning to the departure airport due to a malfunctioning turn coordinator.
summary: The First Officer noticed an unstable turn coordinator giving incorrect indications while en route to ZZZ1 in VMC. The crew returned to ZZZ to avoid low visibility at the destination, obtained an ATC clearance, and subsequently cancelled the flight.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the First Officer became ill during cruise.
summary: During cruise, the First Officer lost consciousness for 30-60 seconds while the Captain was flying. The Captain diverted attention to get a Flight Attendant, advised ATC, and landed, where the First Officer was met by first responders and taken to a hospital.

synopsis: ERJ-190 flight crew reported a Flight Attendant was slightly injured climbing out of LGA as a result of a wake turbulence encounter with a B777.
summary: During climb through 17,000 feet, the flight crew encountered strong wake turbulence from a B777 reported 13 miles away by ATC, despite no TCAS or visual contact. The event caused a flight attendant knee injury, which the reporter attributed to poor ATC separation and insufficient traffic advisories during high workload.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported hazardous liquid spill in cargo pit from passenger checked bag.
summary: A hazardous liquid spilled in the forward cargo hold after the TSA failed to detect a bag containing the liquid in laundry detergent containers within checked baggage.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported their aircraft being struck by another aircraft while sitting still on the ramp.
summary: A Company 737 taxiing behind a stationary, deicing 737 at ZZZ contacted the parked aircraft's right winglet with its left winglet. The collision went unnoticed by the parked crew due to 28-knot winds masking the impact, though maintenance confirmed visible damage and cleared the aircraft to be tugged back to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported FAR 117 violations due to a change in Company policies.
summary: A pilot reported that SBGR management's excessive padding of crew transportation times forces pilots to arrive 40 minutes early, conflicting with FAR 117 rest and duty time calculations. The pilot concluded this practice is legally non-compliant and requested separate pilot transportation with reasonable pickup times.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported an L Engine Fuel Filter EICAS message that was intermittent during a flight which made them return to departure airport.
summary: The monitoring pilot and First Officer experienced a left engine fuel filter EICAS message and increased vibration during climb and descent. They returned safely to ZZZZ due to suspected fuel contamination, attributing the event to a system malfunction.

synopsis: A Regional Carrier Pilot reported they did not know their destination had an operating Control Tower until checking in on the UNICOM frequency.
summary: The flight crew arrived at MYAM unaware of its new Class D status due to missing NOTAMs and outdated charts. Center canceled their IFR flight plan, and they landed after Tower contact, noting uncoordinated IFR departures and reduced ARFF capabilities.

synopsis: First Officer reported not knowing the airport had an operational Control Tower until Tower Controller called the crew on CTAF and advised them of the correct frequency to be on.
summary: The pilot canceled IFR at 5,000 feet and landed VFR after discovering the tower was operational despite missing NOTAMs. The incident resulted from a lack of communication between the company and ATC, compounded by previous pilots failing to report the changes.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported receiving conflicting instructions from a TCAS/RA Alert for traffic above them that was not a factor.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS Resolution Advisory during climb to 9,000 feet after ATC advised of descending traffic. The crew attributed the event to outdated TCAS logic failing to account for modern aircraft climb rates, causing unnecessary altitude deviations and delayed ATC notification.

synopsis: B737-900 Captain reported GPWS callout made while on downwind vector.
summary: The pilot reported a 2500-foot GPWS callout while being vectored on the downwind leg of the BRAUN Arrival for runway 13R. This occurred before an approach clearance had been issued.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported the Captain's side windshield cracked in flight.
summary: The Captain reported a forward windshield shattering at FL370, causing limited visibility and necessitating a return to ZZZ. Despite Approach initially assigning Runway XY, the crew insisted on Runway XXL for gate access and landed safely.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported on final approach (LOC capture) the autothrottle system experienced a malfunction which resulted in an uncommand climb and acceleration.
summary: The relief pilot reported an uncommanded climb and acceleration during an ILS approach in auto-flight mode, prompting autopilot and autothrottle disconnection. ATC vectored the aircraft for a second approach, which was completed normally after the auto-flight malfunction was logged as a maintenance discrepancy.

synopsis: Embraer 175 flight crew reported experiencing intermittent GPS signal reception while taxiing for takeoff at LAX.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent 'ASD-B NOT AVAIL' EICAS messages and GPS signal loss during push-back and taxi at LAX, likely caused by nearby GPS jamming tests. After moving to a different taxiway location and amending their clearance to the non-GPS VTU8 departure, the signal stabilized, allowing for a normal takeoff and flight.

synopsis: EMB-505 First Officer reported a brake system failure, leading to a diversion and 2 blown tires.
summary: The SIC reported a Brake Fail CAS message during cruise, leading to a diversion where the Captain landed using emergency brakes, causing both tires to blow out. The crew executed an evacuation checklist and secured the aircraft, though the SIC noted missed briefing opportunities and premature door opening.

synopsis: G450 First Officer reported encountering green laser during approach to landing at MIA.
summary: The pilot reported a green laser strike on the left side of the aircraft affecting their left eye. The incident was reported to Tower, and the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: EMB-505 First Officer reported unable to pressurize aircraft after takeoff, forcing flight to divert. Pilot also indicated that the QRH was of little help.
summary: The crew ignored BLEED 1 and 2 OFF advisory messages during preflight and takeoff, resulting in a Phenom failing to pressurize and inhibiting the anti-ice system. They diverted to ZZZ, flying unpressurized at 6,000 feet, attributing the failure to inadequate manual guidance and system logic not opening the PRSOVs.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ flight crew reported deviating from BOOVE4 SID clearance while inputting new clearance from ATC.
summary: Pilots flying from ZZZ to DFW overshot the EGADS intersection by three miles after a last-minute arrival change from BOOVE4 to SOCKK3 caused a 30-second delay in programming. The crew attributed the deviation to the controller's late clearance and traffic saturation, noting they should have requested vectors and altitude instead.

synopsis: SA227 Captain reported an inverter failure on final approach causing them to deviate from the localizer on the ILS.
summary: During an ILS approach, a First Officer and Captain experienced an Inverter #1 failure that flagged both attitude indicators and caused the aircraft to drift off the localizer. The crew switched to Inverter #2, corrected the course, and landed safely, though the reporter noted this was the fourth such failure in a month.

synopsis: SR20 flight instructor reported high cylinder head temperatures on takeoff resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced severe engine surging and redlined Cylinder Head Temperatures on cylinders 2 and 3 at 500 feet AGL during takeoff, prompting a precautionary landing. After temperatures spiked again while taxiing, the pilot shut down the aircraft on Taxiway Uniform and had it towed to the ramp.

synopsis: SR20 flight instructor reported malfunctioning fuel flow indication resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced fuel flow and power indication discrepancies during initial climbout, prompting a return to the departure airport. Due to the aircraft's weight exceeding landing limitations, the pilot executed a soft field landing and reported the issue to maintenance.

synopsis: First officer reported incorrect wording on Jeppsen chart departure.
summary: A pilot reported that Reno 9 departure instructions for Runways 16L/16R incorrectly required climbing on both heading 164 and the IRNO Localizer south course simultaneously. The reporter stated this wording is impossible to fly, noting that instructions for Runways 25 and 34L/R do not contain this error.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported they were on a night visual approach and received a GPWS terrain warning. The crew did not execute a missed approach/go-around.
summary: During a night visual approach to PIT Runway 28L, the First Officer and Captain descended below glidepath after receiving a vector inside the FAF, triggering a "Caution Obstacle" warning. The crew leveled and corrected the flight path without executing a go-around, though the Captain later noted a go-around was required by procedure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported inability to communicate with Dispatch during a diversion.
summary: The crew encountered windshear on final approach to KLAS, triggering a go-around and subsequent diversion due to frequency congestion and communication failures. After declaring Minimum Fuel, they landed safely at alternate airport ZZZ1 with 4,300 pounds of fuel.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a track deviation occurred on the HAWKZ 7 arrival into SEA when the aircraft dropped out of LNAV into HDG SEL.
summary: During the HAWKZ 7 arrival into SEA, the crew switched from RNAV Z to ILS 16R and unexpectedly lost LNAV mode, causing a slight eastward deviation. The Pilot Monitoring delayed noticing the mode change until a direct to BREVE was entered to re-engage LNAV before landing.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported poor ATC communication when flying in Manila airspace.
summary: Pilots of Flight X and Y experienced severe HF and VHF communication failures and delayed CPDLC connectivity while transiting Manila airspace at night. The lack of backup frequencies or clear listening watch instructions created an unsafe situation until CPDLC connected, leaving crews without reliable contact for hundreds of miles.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff at approximately 100 kts after the loss of the right AC bus resulted in several systems failures.
summary: The Captain aborted takeoff due to a blank EICAS screen and missing Engine 2 data, but the RTO auto-brakes failed to engage because of a right AC bus electrical failure. The crew manually deployed speed brakes, shut down Engine 2, and taxied to the gate where maintenance confirmed brake temperatures were normal.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported due to company policy, the Flight Attendant staffing has decreased resulting in the forward portion of the cabin understaffed during cruise flight. The Captain states this is a security issue for the flight deck and forward passenger cabin.
summary: A pilot reported that reduced flight attendant staffing left the front galley unattended during cruise to ZZZ, delaying communication and raising cockpit security concerns. The crew expressed low morale due to staffing cuts and noted the Purser took a break without notifying the cockpit or designating a replacement.

synopsis: Ground employee reported Hazmat cargo improperly configured as well as incorrectly classified for air transport.
summary: A ground handler reported that a diesel air compressor booked on Aircraft X to ZZZ1 contained residual fuel despite documentation stating it was drained. The handler concluded the item should have been classified as Class 9, UN3530, Internal Combustion Engine.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported being advised of a turbulence encounter in cruise with injuries to the flight attendants.
summary: An air traffic controller received an ACARS report from a flight on the ZZZZZ4 arrival experiencing sudden severe turbulence between FL220 and FL210, causing two flight attendants to be injured while moving to their seats.
