summary: A maintenance reviewer questioned why Aircraft X was not scheduled for a Program Modification evaluation, noting that while Engineering Order X was deemed inapplicable, retired orders Y and Z may have incorrectly influenced the selection criteria. The aircraft requires evaluation to match other units modified at station ZZZ, as its OTS history shows the inspection was never completed.

synopsis: Maintenance staff report that required inspections were not accomplished following high wind event.
summary: A mechanic reported that a B737 moved from its parked position at ZZZ Airport due to 78 mph wind gusts, turning the nose gear 90 degrees with torque links attached. Management allegedly skipped required conditional inspections to avoid schedule delays, despite manuals mandating checks for any aircraft movement regardless of wind speed.

synopsis: Former air carrier pilot reported concern with the lack of attention being paid to Angle of Attack and Airspeed systems issues following the recent B737 Max accidents.
summary: The pilot questioned why AOA and airspeed system failures occurred in both MAX 8 accidents, noting MCAS involvement. They highlighted the lack of stick shaker reports in 737NG aircraft and emphasized that these systems are not linked except via computer outputs.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot reported a brake failure during brake conditioning taxi operations resulted in a taxiway excursion, smoke and fire from the brake assembly.
summary: The pilot reported that during post-inspection brake conditioning on the runway, the right brake pedal failed, causing the aircraft to veer off Taxiway Alpha and catch fire. The pilot attributed the total loss to a ruptured plastic brake line igniting spilled fluid on hot pads and recommended replacing it with a metal line.

synopsis: Aeronca pilot reported a loss of control after landing that resulted in a runway excursion and minor damage from contacting runway light.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing a taildragger on Runway XXR, the aircraft departed the right edge after the right wing lifted, rolling across grass and likely striking a runway light. Minor scratches were found on the left main landing gear strut, and the pilot attributed the incident to a lack of recent taildragger experience.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported that a student pilot had a runway excursion during solo cross country flight.
summary: A student pilot experienced a runway excursion during a solo cross-country landing, likely caused by a crosswind crab angle and potential distraction from low fuel warnings. The aircraft left the runway, damaged a light, and the instructor attributed the loss of control to the student's crosswind handling and stress.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported a loss of lift while practicing a short field takeoff.
summary: The pilot conducted a short-field takeoff from an intersection without a proper briefing, retracting flaps at 59 knots while only 100 feet AGL. This caused a loss of lift and stall warning at 50 knots, requiring a pitch-down correction that resulted in a 25-foot altitude loss due to procedural deviations and inattention.

synopsis: GA pilot on an IFR flight plan reported experiencing complete electrical failure and descended to VFR conditions into Class B airspace to return to the departure airport.
summary: A pilot experienced total electrical failure during an IFR flight, forcing a VFR climb and descent while using a cell phone to relay intentions. The aircraft landed safely after emergency gear deployment, though the supervisor noted the pilot should have landed at the closest airport due to unmonitored altitude in Class B airspace.

synopsis: ZDV Center Controller reported an altitude violation when an aircraft under ATC Control entered an area below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing high traffic volume failed to climb Aircraft X to 160 MIA before it reached the minimum, resulting in the aircraft entering the MIA at 128 feet. The controller attributed the incident to terrain avoidance requirements and plans to modify visual approach procedures for TEX airport.

synopsis: Ground Controller reported an runway incursion because of a bad read back.
summary: A trainee Ground Controller issued a poor crossing clearance to Aircraft X, which incorrectly read back hold short instructions and entered Runway XXL while Aircraft Y was on final. The controller diverted Aircraft Y, but Aircraft X crossed the runway before stopping, prompting a recommendation for a safety logic system to prevent future incursions.

synopsis: ZZZ Tower Controller and air carrier Flight Crew reported a near mid-air collision during go-around with a departing aircraft on the same runway.
summary: Pilots on a go-around for Runway 22L encountered a departing aircraft at 1000' AGL after being cleared to fly runway heading. The close proximity occurred because the departing aircraft began its roll during the go-around, resulting in a TCAS traffic alert but no resolution advisory due to low altitude.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a bird strike after takeoff and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud bang, vibration, and gear fault shortly after rotation on an XXL departure due to a bird strike involving nine ducks. Inspection revealed significant damage to engine number 1 fan blades and ground proximity switches, though the aircraft landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Load Personnel reported Hazmat was loaded in wrong pit.
summary: Ramp personnel identified hazardous goods in the PIT4 nesting system and advised moving the cargo to PIT5 or PIT6.

synopsis: Maintenance Control reported an aircraft experienced a fuel leak causing fuel quantity to drop below flight plan limit.
summary: During engine start and taxi, the aircraft experienced a #1 engine fuel leak spilling 300 gallons, which stopped at takeoff but resulted in a 2300lb overburn. The crew was not informed of the leak by ground personnel or dispatch until after landing, despite ARFF waiting at the destination.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported requesting Maintenance and paramedics after gate arrival due to strong fumes in the cabin and experiencing health issues.
summary: Cabin crew and the First Officer experienced fumes and illness during descent and at the gate in ZZZ, while the Captain remained unaffected. The odor, possibly from an air conditioning pack, caused medical symptoms requiring paramedic attention, though the source remained unsubstantiated.

synopsis: Captain reported severe pitch-up after flap extension and conducted no-flap landing.
summary: During a maintenance test flight, the crew experienced severe pitch-up and trim failure upon selecting flaps, requiring a no-flap landing. The incident was attributed to unresolved maintenance issues and a lack of scheduled functional testing following previous engine and gear failures.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported galley lighting configuration may cause overheat condition near light fixtures.
summary: A flight attendant reported that AFT galley light surfaces were extremely warm during cruise after hours of operation. The crew noted the heat was concerning for potential hazards like melting plastics or burns and requested an investigation into the lighting system's cause and mitigation.

synopsis: EMB-175 Flight Attendant reported burning smell in cabin shortly after takeoff.
summary: A flight attendant reported the L2 door arming lever was stuck, which maintenance temporarily fixed before takeoff. During climb, a strong burning smell filled the cabin and the captain announced a return to ZZZ due to landing gear stuck down, resulting in a safe landing.

synopsis: EMB-190 Flight Attendant reported fume event had incapacitated them during initial climb.
summary: During climbout, a flight attendant and other crew members inhaled strong fumes, causing incapacitation and respiratory distress. The reporter identified the cause as toxic Tricresyl Phosphate from engine oil and stated the event required donning portable oxygen.

synopsis: Safety representative reported directing cargo staff to correctly load a DG container which was insufficiently secured.
summary: A cargo inspector discovered a shifted flammable DG container resting on netting during a pre-loading inspection. The inspector notified cargo and ramp staff to secure the load before loading, warning that the shift indicated insufficient restraint for turbulence.

synopsis: PA28 flight instructor reported a near midair collision on downwind leg for landing.
summary: During a training flight's touch-and-go sequence, a student pilot and instructor in a Cessna Archer narrowly avoided a mid-air collision with a Bonanza that turned early without visual contact. The instructor executed an immediate descent to avoid the Bonanza, which had lost sight of the Archer and failed to notify the tower.

synopsis: ZDV ARTCC Controller reported being unable to communicate with aircraft due to faulty transmitters during mid-shift while working combined sectors.
summary: An air traffic controller working combined sectors experienced a loss of separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y due to degraded radio transmitter range and static. The controller issued multiple turn instructions that Aircraft Y did not hear, resulting in reduced separation that was ultimately managed via a traffic call without compromising safety.

synopsis: Syracuse TRACON Controller reported a UAV that was below the MVA that had to be climbed and an air carrier aircraft that busted their altitude clearance.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a UAV and escort aircraft issued a climb to 3,000 feet after the UAV entered a 2,700-foot minimum safe altitude while level at 2,000 feet. The controller attributed the incident to distraction from resolving a VFR snow squall conflict and a position relief briefing.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported an ATC communications breakdown on arrival into DEN resulting in a heading deviation.
summary: The flight crew, initially cleared for Runway 34R, reprogrammed for Runway 35L after ATC offered it. A clearance for visual 34R was issued due to clipped radio transmissions, but the crew clarified the error, received the correct visual 35L clearance, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported receiving Dispatch notification during cruise of Hazmat [Dry Ice] loaded on aircraft without providing NOTOC [Notice to Captain] prior to departure.
summary: The flight crew was notified via ACARS after takeoff that dry ice was in cargo pit 2, despite no prior documentation on DG forms, final weights, or service forms. The reporter stated the quantity was under 4 lbs, no animals were present, and no issues resulted from the incident.

synopsis: Ramp personnel reported aircraft departed with dry ice packs erroneously loaded in forward compartment.
summary: A ramp agent and lead ramp loaded dry ice quick packs in the forward compartment of an A320 after being incorrectly cleared. The aircraft departed and became airborne before operations could recall it, resulting in the flight proceeding to ZZZ1 with the hazardous material onboard.

synopsis: Ramp personnel reported the discovery of a Dry Ice Pack that had been erroneously loaded on an aircraft after the flight had departed.
summary: Ramp staff erroneously loaded dry ice into pit 2 instead of the forward pit after the aircraft dispatched. Operations failed to contact the aircraft before it took off, leaving the hazardous material onboard during flight.

synopsis: EMB-145 First officer reported an altitude deviation occurred on arrival into IAH when they descended below charted altitude on the ZEEKK2 RNAV arrival.
summary: The crew experienced vertical deviation while descending on the ZEEKK2 arrival to Runway 26L after the Captain selected 3,000 feet instead of transition altitudes. The reporter attributed the event to premature altitude selection and recommended better communication between pilots.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Boeing Captain reported the need for additional training on new checklist procedures.
summary: Pilots reported that the new B737 normal checklist was distributed with minimal training, causing confusion and standardization issues. The reporter attributes these problems to a lack of specific instruction and recommends a two-day training period with qualified check airmen before full implementation.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus pilot reported on challenges regarding the company's new checklists.
summary: Pilots reported that new Airbus checklist changes, intended to streamline training, removed critical verification steps for fuel, takeoff data, and status messages. The reporter argues these modifications increase the risk of runway incursions and missed critical items by forcing the Captain to look down during taxi and eliminating previous safety stopgaps.

synopsis: A320 Flight Attendant reported fumes in the cabin. Captain requested Maintenance and paramedics on landing.
summary: A flight attendant reported smelling fumes 25 minutes before landing, resulting in symptoms like dizziness and cognitive dysfunction for the crew. The aircraft had eight prior odor incidents and recent pack/APU replacements, though no one required hospitalization.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Light Transport aircraft flight crew reported receiving a Low Altitude Warning during approach for landing at CHA airport.
summary: The pilot, while vectored for a visual approach to Runway XX, intercepted the ILS localizer and glide slope before receiving a low altitude warning from the Tower. The pilot stopped the descent and subsequently resumed the approach.

synopsis: GA pilot reported during taxi to parking landing gear collapsed damaging wing and outboard aileron bracket.
summary: During taxi to parking, the left main gear of a Yak aircraft collapsed, striking the wing tip and outboard aileron bracket. The crew used the pneumatic system to lock the gear down, allowing the aircraft to be towed to the hangar without further issue.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reported a runway excursion after landing.
summary: An instructor and student pilot overshot Taxiway G during a hard landing rollout due to excessive speed and delayed turning. The instructor regained control, stopped in the grass without damage or injury, and the aircraft was later towed back to the FBO.

synopsis: Flight crew reports conflicts with helicopter arrivals and departures during aircraft taxi in airport ramp area.
summary: A fixed-wing pilot taxiing on the ZZZ south ramp was startled by an air-taxiing tour helicopter approaching from the right within 70-80 feet. The helicopter crossed the taxiway ahead of the aircraft, forcing an emergency stop due to a lack of Ground Control advisories regarding the helicopter's proximity.

synopsis: Atlanta TRACON Controllers reported that a departing aircraft advised someone was putting yellow X's on the runway as they departed.
summary: Aircraft X, cleared for a practice approach to Runway 06A, reported yellow X's on the runway during a low approach. The pilot and facility were unaware of a NOTAM closing Runway 13/31, which was issued without direct notification to the air traffic control facility.

synopsis: ZDC Controller reported an aircraft was below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
summary: An OJTI cleared Aircraft X for IFR departure from RWI while the trainee controller assigned the code. The pilot climbed slowly from 2,500 feet through a 3,200-foot MIA caused by an antenna, but the OJTI observed the aircraft remained one mile north of the obstruction and was not in danger.

synopsis: ZMP Controller reported Denver Center handed them off two aircraft that were on conflicting courses.
summary: Denver Center descended Aircraft X to 35,000 feet, creating a conflict with Aircraft Y that required Minneapolis Center to issue turn clearances. Separation was achieved only after pilots' personal conversations blocked initial clearances, though the reporter attributes the loss of separation to Denver Center's failure to ensure safe spacing.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a Flap Disagree on approach, used Alternate Flap extension and landed without incident.
summary: The First Officer flew an ILS approach to Runway XXR when flaps stuck at 5 despite a lever setting of 15. After a go-around and executing the Alternate Flap Extension checklist, the crew landed safely with flaps 15 and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a close encounter with a UAV while in descent for landing at EWR.
summary: During descent into EWR at 6,000 feet, the crew observed a 2-3 foot drone passing 300 feet right and 300-500 feet below the aircraft. The pilots reported the encounter to ATC, but no other aircraft confirmed the sighting, and the flight continued without further incident.

synopsis: A-300 Captain experienced a failure of the MCP backlighting and recommended that the MEL be modified to allow for day-time flight only when this malfunction is deferred.
summary: The Captain and First Officer deferred an inoperative Mode Control Panel (MCP) backlight on an A300, finding it impossible to see controls without overhead lights. This created excessive workload during departure and arrival, leading the pilot to recommend restricting the deferral to day operations only due to safety risks.

synopsis: B767-200 flight crew reported that during cruise, they received a Leading Edge Slat Asymmetry message. Flight crew diverted and landed without incident.
summary: A four-pilot crew en route from ZZZ to ZZZZ diverted to ZZZ after a Leading Edge Slat Asymmetry EICAS message appeared during cruise. Despite normal aircraft handling, the crew coordinated with Company to divert, followed checklists, and landed uneventfully at the maintenance facility.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported observing an engine vibration indication, resulting in a diversion to an alternate airport.
summary: The crew experienced engine #2 N1 vibration exceeding 7.0 at FL270, prompting autothrust disconnection and idle thrust. They diverted to an alternate airport for the remainder of the flight.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus captain reported the need for more training on newly-implemented procedures.
summary: A crew member reported that new triggers and flows procedures lack adequate training and clear guidance, creating a safety risk. The reporter attributes this to an attempt to force an Airbus operating syllabus into a Boeing environment, warning that this mismatch could lead to an accident.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus Captain reported missing assigned level off due to distraction and confusion with new procedures and checklists.
summary: The flight crew missed a 9,000 FT level-off during approach due to distraction from new, untrained checklists and flows. This resulted in a traffic conflict with an aircraft at 8,000 FT, requiring a climb back to 9,000 FT and a post-flight report to ATC.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported difficulties with Maintenance providing clarification in Aircraft Maintenance Log and wording on Minimum Equipment List.
summary: The Captain refused to depart due to conflicting MEL requirements regarding the forward cargo heat system and ECAM indications, citing maintenance's inability to provide clear written confirmation. After a 2.5-hour delay involving multiple mechanics and operations staff, a final AML entry confirmed the amber indication was compliant, allowing the flight to proceed.

synopsis: MD11 Captain reported the aircraft failed to capture the glideslope during approach to landing. Flight crew recovered and landed uneventfully.
summary: During the final approach of a light 385,000-lb aircraft, the crew descended 300 feet below the glide slope while distracted by checklists after failing to capture the glide slope from above. They corrected the deviation and captured the glide slope by 2,400 MSL, completing a safe landing without ATC intervention.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported experiencing a critical conflict during takeoff with an aircraft cleared to cross the runway.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a departing aircraft heard Tower clear another aircraft to cross runway 22R near V1 but continued takeoff as the other aircraft did not move. The pilot attributed the near-miss to unclear clearance procedures and potential controller distraction from four news helicopters, noting the outcome was safe but the situation was critical.

synopsis: EMB-170 pilot reported not crossing a specified intersection at the correct altitude due to a speed reduction by ATC while on the CLIPR2 RNAV arrival into DCA.
summary: The flight crew on a CLIPR2 RNAV arrival into DCA crossed the CLIPR waypoint at 13,000 ft instead of the amended 12,000 ft clearance due to reduced descent rates required to meet a new speed restriction. The pilot noted that using speed brakes or notifying ATC of the inability to comply would have been more proactive.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported burning electric fumes in forward cabin.
summary: A flight attendant reported a burning electric smell in the forward galley during boarding and flight, causing respiratory irritation and headaches for the cabin crew. The crew completed their duties using oxygen and masks, suspecting faulty coffee pot wiring, but were met by excessive ground support upon arrival.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Technician reported proper engine inspections were not accomplished following FOD (Foreign Object Damage) event.
summary: Maintenance personnel failed to comply with AMM procedures for FOD inspection and engine boroscopy on fan blades with documented tears and missing material. Consequently, the fan blades were found unserviceable in accordance with AMM 72-21-00-210-009-A.

synopsis: GA Pilot reported smoke accompanied by strong exhaust fumes in the cockpit during initial climb.
summary: The pilot reported smoke in the cockpit during climb after departing ZZZ1 due to a cracked exhaust pipe that allowed fumes into the engine compartment. The pilot diverted to ZZZ for a safe landing where firefighters confirmed the exhaust failure, resulting in no injuries despite an emergency declared on the pilot's behalf.

synopsis: C172 Pilot flying in airspace controlled by a Temporary Tower staffed with military personnel reported a near mid-air collision with a helicopter.
summary: During a training mission in the TAC ring at 2,600 ft, the pilot's aircraft and an Army Blackhawk helicopter lost separation to under 1,000 ft. The pilot executed an immediate left turn to avoid a collision, noting the helicopter appeared to take no evasive action despite the pilot having the right of way.

synopsis: ZLA ARTCC Front Line Manager reported that an aircraft was given a heading which took it towards high terrain, and also reported that the FLM was unaware of the incident until a week later.
summary: An ATCT controller and Front Line Manager delayed reporting a departure safety issue involving Aircraft X turning toward high terrain from Runway 3 at VCV. The reporter criticized the week-long delay and punitive handling, noting the event was not reported promptly as required by just culture principles.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: NEW Tower Controller reported that due to transmission ambiguity an aircraft lined up for the incorrect runway, causing a potential runway incursion, and go-around.
summary: The Controller In Charge corrected Local Control's erroneous traffic call regarding runway 18L to 36L for Aircraft X. Despite the correction, Aircraft X lined up for the wrong runway and executed a go-around after another aircraft was placed on the runway.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported an NMAC that was attributed to procedures that were not clear to the reporter relating to a TFR and go-around procedures.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that an unbriefed TFR for an aerial demonstration team encroached on their airspace, forcing Aircraft X to execute a go-around with a near-midair collision risk. The incident occurred because the active TFR was missing from NOTAMs and controllers received no procedural briefing, leaving them to manage operations without guidance.

synopsis: ZOB Center Controller reported an aircraft was 400 feet below the MIA and wasn't sure if he did anything wrong by leaving the aircraft at that altitude.
summary: The radar controller in the MGW sector allowed Aircraft X to fly 400 feet below the MIA for 2-3 miles while en-route at 3,000 feet. Despite two confirmations from CKB approach, the controller questioned the decision and concluded they should have climbed the aircraft to 3,400 feet for safety.

synopsis: B757-200 Captain reported dirty sock odor for 7-8 minutes after takeoff.
summary: During takeoff and the first 7-8 minutes of flight, the crew detected a dirty sock odor that later dissipated. All systems remained normal, and Maintenance was met to complete a fumes form after the crew recorded the incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A320 Captain reported a GPWS terrain warning on approach while in VFR conditions.
summary: The crew received a terrain warning at 6,000 feet while descending on the KEDIX 1B RNAV approach near MUVBA. The pilot believes the charted 5,500-foot minimum altitude is too low due to a mountain directly below, posing a risk for future arrivals at MMPR.

synopsis: Airline ground personnel reported a discrepancy between electronic load report and Ramp Service Manual regarding dry ice cargo pit loading locations.
summary: A lead loader moved a dry ice package to Pit 4, but the flight could not close out on the scanner because the pilot lacked an electronic Dangerous Goods notice. The aircraft returned to the gate to relocate the load to Pit 6 before continuing as planned.

synopsis: Flight crew reported they had ground conflict with another airplane during taxi to runway.
summary: During taxi to Runway XXR, the crew aggressively braked to avoid a collision with a CRJ that failed to yield at an intersection. The reporter attributed the event to the Ground Controller's failure to issue yield instructions and the distraction caused by a new checklist.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported communication breakdown between flight crew and Dispatch/Ground Personnel regarding battery powered mobility device transport configuration.
summary: The flight crew and ramp agents delayed departure while loading a 480-lb mobility device with conflicting battery policies. The Captain departed with the battery installed and unsecured due to reliance on an outdated manual, later discovering the Flight Operations Manual required battery removal and proper packaging.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew encountered brake overheat following long slow taxi to gate after landing.
summary: The pilot reported that a long, slow taxi behind a B747-800 caused excessive low-speed braking, resulting in a Level 2 Brake Overheat alert on wheels 4 and 7. Wheel 4 emitted fire, requiring extinguishment by maintenance and cooling by Crash Fire Rescue before the aircraft reached the gate.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported an airborne conflict with a UAV on initial approach to BED.
summary: A pilot reported a near midair collision with a drone while at 1,800 feet on a right base for Runway 23 at BED. The drone was approximately 1,750 feet high and within 1,000 feet horizontally, prompting an IDENT transmission and a report to Tower before a successful landing.

synopsis: Aircraft Maintenance Technician reported that Maintenance Control did not notify him that deferred system circuit breakers were reset by flight crew.
summary: A cabin crew member discovered the Captain had closed TV system circuit breakers per Maintenance Control instructions, reversing an MEL deferral while the crew member was inspecting the system during boarding. This unauthorized reversal created a safety hazard and left the aircraft MEL non-compliant without mechanic notification or verification.

synopsis: Air carrier ground personnel reported Hazmat transport violations on arrival shipment.
summary: Cabin crew reported receiving an unsecured Dangerous Goods package in the cargo bay that was under 80% full and lacked straps. The item bore a DG tag but contained no specific DG remarks.

synopsis: DA50-900EX Captain reported GPS 1 and GPS 2 both failed at the same time then returned to service and then again failed and again returned to service.
summary: The pilot reported simultaneous failures of GPS 1 and GPS 2 for two one-minute intervals while cruising at FL380 after departing UUWW. Although dual IRS maintained navigation, the actual cause remains unknown, though the pilot suspects receiver interference.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported the Tower allowed a VFR aircraft to climb into confliction with traffic TRACON was vectoring on downwind.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a 0.12-mile separation incident between Aircraft X at 3,000 feet and a VFR departure squawking 1200 climbing through 2,500 feet near APF. The controller attributed the event and three prior similar incidents to APF Tower's failure to provide separation and a lack of safety culture regarding VFR aircraft.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported an aircraft which they had not been notified had an engine out, refused their go around instruction for a false ASDE alert.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a go-around instruction to a single-engine aircraft on visual approach after an ASDE taxiway alert, but the pilot declined and landed safely. The controller attributed the incident to poor communication, a failure to declare an emergency, and overly sensitive ASDE tolerances for non-straight-in approaches.

synopsis: BJC Tower Controller reported an aircraft making evasive actions due to a VFR aircraft trying to shoot the gap between the Class D and Class B airspace.
summary: Local Control observed a VFR aircraft (Aircraft X) transiting between Class D and Class B airspace, conflicting with an inbound IFR aircraft (Aircraft Y) at BJC. Aircraft Y executed evasive action to avoid the conflict before landing normally, prompting a recommendation to encourage VFR pilots to seek radar advisories or avoid arrival paths.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZSE ARTCC Controller reported that an aircraft had a problem wanted to return to departure area and that ATC could not provide the approach information the aircraft needed at the time to assist the aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an aircraft en route from SEA at FL250 with an avionics issue received no effective assistance due to poor inter-facility communication. The lack of direct supervisor coordination and unclear approach information prevented the controller from providing priority handling or specific runway details to the distressed aircraft.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported the adjacent Center handed them off two aircraft on converging courses.
summary: ZMP controllers alerted ZDV that Aircraft X and Y were losing separation due to a 100-knot speed differential. ZDV controllers initially refused to issue control instructions, causing a delay that resulted in the aircraft passing 7 miles apart at the same altitude with over 110 knots difference.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Embraer regional jet Captain reported a track deviation occurred on arrival into IAH, wake turbulence was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The crew flying a DRLLR5 arrival into IAH encountered wake turbulence near DOMNO, triggering a 'Lateral Mode Off' message. The resulting off-course deviation required ATC vectors after the pilots manually corrected the turn using Touch Control Steering.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported various anomalies with the FMS.
summary: Pilots on a Boeing 767 cruise at FL370 and descent to 11,000 feet experienced uncommanded FMS thrust changes and transient autopilot/stab trim cautions triggered by speedbrake deployment. The crew manually corrected the thrust mode and continued the flight, attributing the software glitches to potential FMC issues requiring updates.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported failure of airspeed and altimeter instruments on climbout.
summary: During climb-out, the Captain experienced airspeed and altimeter failures with an oral warning. The crew followed QRH procedures, diverted to a VMC airport, and landed uneventfully after EEC Alt annunciators illuminated during descent.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported Inertial Reference System failure and flight manual did not state all effects of failure on aircraft systems.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced an autopilot disconnect and blank screens due to a Left IRS fault on the second trip, requiring a QRH procedure that lacked critical system impact details. The reporter noted that missing information regarding unavailable autopilot, auto-brakes, and flight director guidance could lead to flawed decision-making, unlike procedures from other airlines.

synopsis: B737 flight crew and ground personnel reported Main Landing Gear caught fire at gate after taxi-in.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X at ZZZ discovered a right main landing gear brake fire after parking, caused by a flat tire. The Captain ordered an evacuation, which was completed without incident, while emergency personnel extinguished the fire.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported NMAC on departure from LAX.
summary: During the LADYJ4 departure from LAX, the flight crew received a TCAS RA while vertically separated by only 500 feet from a VFR corporate jet. The First Officer manually descended 500 feet to avoid the conflict, which the reporter attributed to inadequate ATC separation.

synopsis: Saab 340 First Officer reported finding areas of possible corrosion on the airplane rudder near the trim tab during preflight inspection. Aircraft was removed from service and repaired.
summary: A pilot detected possible corrosion on rudder assemblies during preflight of a Saab 340 and reported it to Maintenance. The pilot considers this a general defect affecting the fleet that could lead to airworthiness issues if hidden corrosion on aging airframes is not found and removed.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported being notified by Ramp Agent that a gate-checked bag was transported with a Lithium Ion battery attached.
summary: A ramp agent discovered a gate-checked smart bag with an installed lithium battery after deplaning and corrected the passenger. The pilot reported that flight crew cannot supervise ground handling and recommended retraining ground operations to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an unreliable airspeed indication resulted in an over speed condition.
summary: During an enroute descent in light rain, the crew experienced an unreliable airspeed event where two indicators dropped to 230 kts while the standby showed 350 kts, causing autothrottles to command max thrust. The crew suspects pitot tube icing or water blockage caused the erroneous low-speed indications and subsequent overspeed warning before indications normalized.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence from preceding B777 approaching DFW.
summary: The flight crew experienced a sudden 35-degree left roll and 150-foot altitude loss at FL250 while following a descending B777 on the SEEVR4 arrival. The pilot disconnected the autopilot to recover, suspecting wake turbulence from the preceding aircraft's descent path.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported ground personnel notified Captain of a passenger's bag that ignited, because of undeclared Hazmat in a suitcase.
summary: During preflight boarding, a forward cargo fire warning sounded caused by an undeclared e-cigarette and batteries shorting in a passenger's bag. The Captain ordered immediate evacuation, ground crews extinguished the fire, and the aircraft was grounded for investigation while the crew coordinated with emergency services and dispatch.

synopsis: B747-400 Captain reported a fuel imbalance and fuel totalizer indication issue resulting in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew encountered a Fuel Imbal 2-3 EICAS message and a dropping totalizer level enroute, suspecting a fuel system issue. They diverted to ZZZ to allow mechanics to troubleshoot, holding to reduce weight before landing safely.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported Captain notified cabin crew of fumes in the cockpit.
summary: During departure below 1,000 feet, the Captain detected a strong oil smell in the cockpit while cabin crew reported none. Upon landing at ZZZ1, the odor entered the main cabin, prompting Fire Marshall intervention and full deplaning.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported not being given necessary information to work at unfamiliar airport not staffed with regular company maintenance.
summary: A field trip mechanic dispatched to ZZZ for Aircraft X maintenance could not determine taxi or run-up authorization due to a lack of local procedures, frequencies, and maps provided by the company. The incident highlighted that the company failed to equip mechanics with necessary airport-specific information for unfamiliar stations.

synopsis: UAV operator reported loss of control link and subsequent loss of UAV control. UAV was not recovered and assumed crashed in a forested area.
summary: The UAS operator lost telemetry and control link due to a ground station laptop power failure and high winds, causing the aircraft to drift out of range and crash in a forested area. The pilot in command did not contact ATC due to incomplete emergency procedure knowledge, and the aircraft remains unrecovered.

synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported a near miss while landing with traffic executing a late go-around to an intersecting runway.
summary: The pilot, approaching ZZZ airport, landed behind a bird-strike report and faced a conflict with two aircraft on intersecting runways cleared to land simultaneously. After the other pilots went around, the pilot aggressively braked to stop before the intersection but crossed it with only 100 feet lateral separation from a Cirrus, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: UAV operator reported failure to obtain an FAA waiver before operating within FTY Class D airspace.
summary: A Part 107 drone pilot operating a DJI Inspire 1 for a roof inspection received airspace warnings at a 2-foot hover in FTY Class D airspace. The pilot landed immediately after realizing the B4UFly app provided insufficient guidance and identified the need to file a waiver via FAADroneZone.faa.gov.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot on landing rollout at a non-towered airport reported an aircraft landing in the opposite direction on the same runway.
summary: A VFR pilot approaching ZZZ experienced a near-midair conflict with a tailwheel Cessna on short final for Runway XY while executing a touch-and-go on Runway XX. The pilot attributed the incident to the Cessna's failure to respond to CTAF calls despite the pilot making all required position announcements.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported cotter pin was found missing during pre-flight after 300 hour maintenance inspection was completed.
summary: A pilot discovered a missing cotter pin on the right pitch control linkage during preflight after a 300-hour inspection. The pilot admitted flying the aircraft between the inspection and discovery, potentially operating it with the pin missing.

synopsis: UAV operator reported violation of a TFR.
summary: A commercial airline pilot operating a DJI Inspire 2 drone inadvertently flew into a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) during a 10-minute VLOS flight under 400 feet. The incident occurred because the pilot forgot about the TFR after a last-minute location change, though no collision or injury resulted.

synopsis: A taildragger pilot reported loss of control during landing resulting in a prop strike and wingtip striking the ground.
summary: An ATP-rated pilot flying a Pitts tailwheel aircraft at ZZZ experienced a ground loop after touchdown when a sudden wind shear created a tailwind, causing the right wing to lift despite full aileron input. The aircraft struck the ground on its wingtip and nose, resulting in fuel leakage that was mitigated by draining the tanks before the aircraft was towed to a hangar.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot reported a runway excursion upon landing.
summary: During Phase I testing of an experimental gyroplane, the pilot requested a full-stop landing due to redline engine coolant temperatures. The aircraft veered off the runway on rollout because of pilot inattention and improper directional control, leading to grounding for cooling modifications and additional pilot training.

synopsis: Beechjet 400 First Officer reported a track deviation occurred departing CLE after encountering wake turbulence from preceding EMB-170.
summary: The crew of a departing aircraft at CLE encountered significant wake turbulence from a preceding E170 while climbing through 2,500 feet on the CAVVS2 SID. The event caused a 25-degree roll and course deviation, attributed to light winds keeping wake along the shared initial path of the two SIDs despite legal spacing.

synopsis: BE-200 First Officer reported loss of pressurization inflight.
summary: The pilot reported that while climbing to FL220, switching the cabin mode controller to manual warm caused a total loss of bleed air and a rapid cabin altitude rise to over 8,000 feet. The crew donned oxygen masks, descended to 10,000 feet, and diverted to ZZZ without attempting to re-pressurize the aircraft.

synopsis: Balloon pilot reported changing weather conditions resulted in a loss of control and contact with object while landing.
summary: The pilot and passengers successfully landed a hot air balloon in a residential area after wind pushed it between houses, where it snagged on a Direct TV antenna. After freeing the balloon, it drifted two to three miles and landed near a high school with no injuries.

synopsis: A330 Flight Attendant reported notifying the Captain of burning smell in the cabin during pushback for departure.
summary: Cabin crew and the Captain experienced a strong chemical burning smell and haze during pushback on an aircraft with prior APU and battery issues. The Captain halted pushback, returned to the gate, and ordered an emergency deplaning, resulting in crew members suffering eye and throat irritation.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a communication breakdown with ATC led to a near midair collision at a non-towered airport.
summary: A pilot conducting a practice RNAV 15 approach at PYM experienced a traffic conflict with an aircraft passing overhead due to a misunderstanding with Boston Approach regarding flight plan closure and CTAF frequency transfer. The pilot attributed the incident to not being advised to switch to CTAF before the FAF, resulting in a lack of traffic awareness during the final approach.

synopsis: PA-18 flight crew reported a loss of control and runway excursion due to lack of experience and misuse of the heel brakes.
summary: A pilot with a recent tailwheel endorsement veered off the runway during a stop-and-go practice landing while transitioning to brakes at 5–8 MPH. Excessive left rudder input caused the aircraft to roll into the grass, resulting in no damage but highlighting a need for further ground handling instruction.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they vectored an aircraft into an area below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller misread a Minimum Vectoring Altitude (MVA) map while vectoring an IFR aircraft over the ocean, descending it to 2,300 feet instead of the required 2,600 feet. This error triggered a low altitude alarm, though the aircraft safely exited the lower MVA area after the controller recognized the mistake.

synopsis: ROA TRACON Trainee Controller and an instructor pilot reported the pilot was assigned 4,000 feet which is below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: During an instructional flight, Approach controllers and a pilot experienced a low altitude alert when the aircraft descended below the 4,900-foot MVA after conflicting traffic was cleared. The pilot reported receiving conflicting altitude clearances from two sectors, resulting in a potential pilot deviation investigation.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported Washington Center appears to be consistently changing the crossing altitude at RIDGY on the KORRY 4 arrival into LGA and would like to see the chart changed to reflect that.
summary: A pilot flying the KORRY 4 arrival into LGA received a clearance to cross RIDGY at FL 270, conflicting with the published "at or above" restriction. The FMS initially prevented descent due to this discrepancy, requiring manual correction, and the pilot recommended updating the STAR to match ATC expectations.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported engine anomaly on climbout resulting in shutdown and return to departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that during takeoff, Engine 1 EPR remained abnormally high and unresponsive to thrust lever changes, causing yaw and rising EGT/N1. Following an ECAM fuel warning, the crew shut down Engine 1, coordinated with ATC, and returned safely to the gate with no evacuation required.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the Company supplied electric cord and adapter damaged the crew iPads when used for in-flight charging.
summary: During cruise at FL350, a pilot plugged an iPad into a new company-supplied USB adapter, causing a short circuit that emitted a burning smell and destroyed the pilot's iPad and the First Officer's power cord. The crew unplugged the faulty adapter, confirmed no outlet damage, and continued the flight using paper charts.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported poor lighting of the aircraft center console.
summary: A pilot reported that the Boeing 737 stabilizer trim cutout switches are inadequately illuminated, creating a risk during night upsets or MCAS events. The reporter identified this as a design flaw where crews might inadvertently cut engine switches instead of trim switches due to similar two-part actions and poor visibility.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported a track heading deviation due to similar sounding fix names BEERI and BERYS.
summary: The flight crew and Toronto Center experienced a clearance confusion between nearby intersections BERYS and BERRI due to similar phonetic spellings over VHF radio. The crew believed they were cleared to BERYS, but the controller intended BERRI, which was the original clearance.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported an engine compressor stall after takeoff that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud explosion, shudder, and flash from the right engine at 1,000 feet during a shallow left turn, suspecting a violent compressor stall despite normal engine indications. They returned to ZZZ for an overweight landing after jettisoning fuel, with post-flight inspections revealing no visible abnormalities.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported being notified by Load Planning that flight crew was not provided required Hazmat transport documents prior to departure.
summary: Load Planning contacted the flight crew en route to report undocumented dry ice in Pit 2, estimating less than 4 pounds. The crew was advised of the incident and recommended to file a report.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported following an inoperative glide slope and receiving a low altitude alert from Tower.
summary: Pilots on a red-eye flight missed an out-of-service glide slope buried in the ATIS, causing a low descent during a visual approach. The crew and Tower Controller corrected the descent to 2,000 feet, attributing the error to fatigue and lack of verbal warnings about inoperative equipment.

synopsis: MD-83 flight crew reported a high speed rejected takeoff.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 100 knots during the takeoff roll after the left engine EGT and fuel flow indicators began flashing. No other abnormal indications were observed.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported a communication breakdown between flight crew and Dispatch regarding transport of Hazmat material on ferry flight.
summary: The crew ferried an A321 with four empty portable oxygen bottles in the cargo, relying on Dispatch and Maintenance advice that no waiver was needed. After a medical diversion to ZZZ1, they returned to ZZZ unaware of the cargo contents due to a lack of ground support and documentation at the unserviced airport.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported a track deviation occurred on the LDORA STAR into DEN, citing lack of FMS synchronization as contributing.
summary: During arrival on the LDORA STAR, the flight crew overshot the course after changing the runway in FMS 1, which failed to sync with FMS 2. The deviation was caused by an undetected equipment sync error, compounded by high speed and a preconceived assumption that maintenance had properly configured the dual FMS system.

synopsis: EMB-135 flight crew reported a GPWS event during approach to OAK airport.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X received a GPWS and gear warning while descending from 3,200 to 3,000 feet during an ILS 12 approach to OAK. The crew climbed back to 3,200 feet to avoid terrain conflict, advised ATC, and resumed the descent once clear.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported opening UPK (Universal Precaution Kit) to clean up and dispose of human waste in the biohazard bag.
summary: Cabin crew managed a passenger in seat XXD who vomited due to turbulence during flight. They contacted the Captain to open the Universal Precaution Kit, which was used to clean the area and dispose of waste in a biohazard bag.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported fumes smell in the passenger cabin and experienced slight health issues.
summary: A flight attendant detected a strong, unpleasant odor after door closure and the safety demonstration, causing a slight headache. The crew checked overhead bins for spills but found nothing, leaving the source of the smell unidentified.

synopsis: C172 student pilot and flight instructor reported a loss of aircraft control and runway excursion by the student during solo landing and subsequent takeoff.
summary: A student pilot soloing a Cessna veered off Runway XXL onto a dirt apron during both landing and takeoff due to changing crosswinds gusting to 17 knots. The pilot lost directional control twice but sustained no damage to the aircraft or runway lights.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Aerial survey pilot not follow procedure and landed gear up.
summary: A student pilot and CFI landed an aircraft with gear up after the CFI pulled the gear warning circuit breaker for survey work and failed to reset it. The crew missed the warning and an external go-around call, resulting in a runway slide with no injuries.

synopsis: Gulfstream IV pilot reported receiving a GPWS warning and a warning from Tower during a missed approach.
summary: During a GIV instrument approach, the non-flying pilot called for a missed approach when the runway was not seen. The flying pilot failed to execute the procedure correctly, triggering terrain warnings and a Tower alert, leading to a diversion to ZZZ1.

synopsis: Citation 560XL Captain reported a GPWS event at the end of a long duty day.
summary: Pilots repositioning an aircraft between two uncontrolled airfields in deteriorating weather received a terrain alert after descending too low. The pilot flying initiated a short climb before completing the landing checklist and landing without incident.

synopsis: Glider pilot reported an NMAC with a military aircraft.
summary: A glider pilot reported a mid-air conflict while flying near a ridge when an inverted F-18E/F emerged 150–200 feet above the ridge with an energy vector aimed at the glider. The F-18 relaxed its pull and passed overhead and behind the glider at approximately 200 feet.

synopsis: GA turboprop pilot reported NMAC with traffic that was unreported by a 'busy' ATC Controller at RHV.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 31L at RHV experienced a close call with an aircraft passing below after a right turn. The pilot attributed the incident to potential uncoordinated traffic entry, drifting departure, or misidentified traffic alerts due to high traffic volume.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician failed to install cotter pin on throttle control resulting in engine shutdown in flight.
summary: A mechanic omitted a cotter pin during engine installation, causing the throttle control nut and bolt to loosen and fall off in flight, which locked engine speed at 2100 RPM. The pilot executed a power-off landing using mixture to shut down the engine, resulting in an undamaged aircraft.

synopsis: ZTL Center Controller reported a route conflict problem that he had never seen before to twice in one session.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in ZTL and ZME sectors managed a conflict between three aircraft converging at 11,000 feet near the DIODE fix. The event occurred because Aircraft X was routed non-routinely over DIODE without adequate coordination, forcing the controller to hold Aircraft Y at 15,000 feet and turn Aircraft X to ensure separation.

synopsis: Indianapolis Center Controller reported several concerns occurring during a session, which resulted in an airspace deviation.
summary: An air traffic controller working combined low-altitude sectors without a D-side due to staffing shortages violated CKB Approach airspace while managing a VFR photo aircraft. The controller attributed the error to high traffic complexity, frequency interference, and the lack of a dedicated tracker to handle coordination.

synopsis: Ramp Load Agent reported Hazmat cargo improperly configured for air transport.
summary: The ramp lead planned the flight with dangerous goods and one bag in pit 1, but finalized the load with no bags to secure the dangerous goods in that pit.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: EMB First Officer reported a track deviation occurred on arrival into IAH when a wake encounter caused an autopilot lateral mode trip off.
summary: During an IAH arrival descent through 10,000 feet, unexpected wake turbulence caused the lateral autopilot mode to disengage, resulting in an overflight of the turn. The crew manually steepened the bank to recapture the course and subsequently informed ATC of the deviation.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported an unusual odor during engine start.
summary: During the first engine start, the Captain and First Officer aborted due to an unusual odor and prior maintenance write-ups. The Captain reported light-headedness and was replaced by a reserve pilot, while the First Officer determined they were fit to fly the replacement aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported concerns with LGA ATC phraseology and expectations, which were apparently non-compliant with AIM procedures.
summary: The Captain of an aircraft landing at LGA stopped on Taxiway P after clearing Runway 31 because no further taxi clearance was issued. Ground Control scolded the pilot for stopping at a hotspot, but the Captain cited AIM and 7110.65 to justify holding until instructed, attributing the conflict to poor controller coordination and non-standard expectations.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported that an FAA Maintenance Inspector photographed the pilots' credentials with his personal mobile phone.
summary: An FAA Maintenance Inspector photographed the crew's credentials with a personal phone while jumpseating on a routine flight. The pilot reported operational security and privacy concerns to the inspector and subsequently filed a report with the union.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported ZMA ARTCC assigned routing in violation of FARs even after repeatedly asking ATC if the route was legal.
summary: Pilots departing MYEF queried ZMA Center controllers multiple times about a 50-mile restriction after receiving a direct routing to VENDS. Although controllers initially confirmed compliance, a subsequent controller provided a west heading to maintain the restriction and admitted ZMA had been issuing problematic routes in the Bahamas region.

synopsis: PA-28 student pilot reported a loss of control on landing that resulted in a runway excursion and contact with a taxiway sign and a parked aircraft.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control during the landing roll of a solo training flight, causing the aircraft to skid off the runway and strike a taxiway sign and another aircraft's propeller. No injuries occurred, and the pilot plans additional training and a pre-solo check before flying solo again.

synopsis: Corporate pilot reported the PAPI for Runway 30 at HTS airport has been providing incorrect glidepath depiction.
summary: A pilot reported that the Runway 30 PAPI at Huntington, WV, provided incorrect glide path indications due to the second light being out of adjustment. The reporter attributed the misalignment to the light likely being struck by a tractor during recent mowing.

synopsis: Piper Aztec (PA27) pilot reported a NMAC with previously reported traffic by ATC.
summary: A survey pilot at 4,800 feet reported a near-midair collision with a Cirrus aircraft that passed 50–200 feet below after the Cirrus pilot executed a sharp right turn. The reporter attributed the incident to the Cirrus's inaccurate transponder altitude and delayed ATC traffic advisories.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported confusion regarding a new note the FAA has attached to the RNAV approach at POF.
summary: A pilot reported confusion regarding an ambiguous January 2019 note on the RNAV (GPS) 18 Approach at Poplar Bluff Municipal restricting straight-in and circling operations at night due to a tree encroachment. The pilot attributed the issue to poor coordination between the FAA and airport management, noting that Memphis Center was unaware of the restriction.

synopsis: DFW Tower Controller reported a runway incursion with two arrivals on the same runway.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X and Y to land on Runway 17C and exit at taxiway M6, but M6 was found coned off. The controller sent Aircraft Y around after the airport authority admitted they forgot to notify ATC of the closure.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported burning plastic smell during climb in passenger cabin resulting in a return to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew reported a strong burning plastic odor during the approach to ZZZ, prompting expedited vectors and a fire department sweep upon landing. No fire was found, but the crew experienced throat discomfort from the fumes, which were strongest in the flight deck.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that they mistakenly used takeoff numbers for a runway which they did not use for takeoff, they were overweight for the runway at that flap and power setting they used.
summary: The Captain and First Officer at KFAT experienced a long takeoff roll on Runway 29L after the First Officer entered Runway 29R performance data into the CDU. The error occurred because the crew failed to verify the correct runway numbers, resulting in an overweight departure for the active runway's conditions.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported no formal training on new procedures before introduction, insufficient explanation of differences between triggers, flows, procedures, and policy compliance.
summary: Pilots failed to comply with new company procedures due to a lack of formal training and insufficient explanation of changes. The reporter attributes the near-zero compliance rate to pilots forcing old procedures and recommends revising or abandoning the new regimen.

synopsis: B737 Maintenance Technician reported that incorrect parts were installed on passenger emergency exit slide packs.
summary: A mechanic in the slide shop installed Goodrich O-rings and company-supplied yellow electrical tape on Air Cruiser slides that were later found to have incorrect effectivity. The reporter attributed the error to a lack of effectivity verification by buyers and recommended better communication regarding manufacturer changes.

synopsis: Learjet 55 flight crew reported a track deviation occurred following a wake turbulence encounter in trail of a B737-800 departing LAX.
summary: The pilot reported that wake turbulence from a preceding B737-800 on the ORCKA2 departure caused loss of control and a subsequent pilot deviation. The pilot attributed the missed KLIPR turn to controller distraction during a recorded inquiry about the event while the crew was still recovering.

synopsis: Military pilot reported an airborne conflict with opposite direction UAV.
summary: A DOD pilot flying Aircraft X lost 700 feet of vertical separation from Aircraft Y while descending to FL190. The deviation resulted from divided attention during weather discussions and the lack of autopilot altitude hold, despite a clearance to descend.

synopsis: CMH TRACON Controller reported staffing issues at the facility.
summary: Two air traffic controllers worked a full night shift without breaks due to minimal staffing after a colleague called in sick. The reporter states this caused fatigue and stress, increasing risk to the National Airspace System.

synopsis: ZBW Center Controller reported an airspace violation that may have been either human or equipment failure.
summary: An air traffic controller reported retaining track control of Aircraft X descending via JFUND2 STAR into Approach airspace, likely because signing in with new settings cancelled a previous handoff. The controller attributed the oversight to fatigue and noted the auto-handoff function failed to activate as expected.

synopsis: ZOB Center Controller reported problems associated with similar call signs.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly cleared Aircraft Y direct SLT and Aircraft Z to FL340 while Aircraft X held its heading, causing a separation conflict. The controller resolved the situation by descending Aircraft Y to FL320 and assigning new headings, attributing the error to similar-sounding call signs.

synopsis: B737 NG Captain reported failure to make a crossing restriction on the ZPYLN3 RNAV arrival into DEN following a late runway change.
summary: Pilots flying an RNAV arrival for Runway 17R were cleared to Runway 16L with a speed restriction of 280 KTS. A slow FMC update caused the aircraft to cross JPAGE at 17,900 feet instead of the required 15,000–17,000 feet, but the controller accepted the deviation.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported the current use of the Electronic Logbook (ELB) makes it difficult to look back at the aircraft's history, therefore the current process compromises safety.
summary: A pilot reported that the Electronic Log Book displayed irrelevant cabin entries, obscuring critical maintenance history for an aircraft experiencing unwanted fuel transfer. The pilot concluded the system's broken filtering logic and removed web access compromised safety by preventing timely review of essential maintenance data.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 Captain reported pungent burning odor on flight deck accompanied by health issues. Flight crew executed a divert.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ due to a sudden burning odor and eye irritation on the flight deck and in the cabin. After jettisoning fuel to reduce weight, the aircraft landed safely on Runway XX with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: GA pilot reported experiencing a nose tire failure on landing rollout causing the aircraft to depart the runway surface.
summary: The pilot reported that during a visual approach to RWY XX, the aircraft touched down with the stall horn sounding and veered left. Upon applying rudder, the plane made an uncontrolled sharp right turn, exited the runway, and sustained damage to the left main gear, nose gear, and propeller with no injuries.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported an airborne conflict with a UAV on final approach to ROA.
summary: During final approach to Runway 6 at ROA, a safety pilot spotted a drone at 200 feet AGL and 2 o'clock. The crew initiated a minor evasive turn, resulting in a 1,500-foot separation before landing and notifying Roanoke Tower.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: General Aviation pilot reported a near miss with an opposite direction aircraft when attempting to land.
summary: A VFR pilot landing at JNX on RWY 21 nearly collided with another aircraft on RWY 3 after missing a frequency change notice buried at the end of the AWOS report. Both pilots avoided a crash by veering right, though the reporter noted the other pilot had not heard his calls due to the frequency discrepancy.

synopsis: C172 pilots reported loosing rudder control and brakes during taxi.
summary: Two pilots taxiing a leisure aircraft lost directional control when the left brake failed, causing the plane to veer into a ditch and grass. The impact bent the right horizontal stabilizer and main gear, an outcome attributed to an unaddressed prior brake pressure issue.

aircraft: Diamond Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: General aviation pilot reported a near miss with an opposite direction aircraft when attempting to take off.
summary: A flight instructor and student on a Cessna accelerating for an intersection takeoff from Runway 03 at JNX nearly collided with a Cessna landing on Runway 21. The near-miss occurred because the landing pilot used the outdated CTAF frequency and was unaware of the runway change, forcing both aircraft to stop on the runway.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported sudden onset of toxic acrid fumes in the cabin resulting in health issues.
summary: Cabin crew and pilots experienced a sudden toxic fume event during the landing and taxi phases, causing burning sensations, nausea, and dizziness. The haze persisted until the forward door opened, sickening two flight attendants and the flight deck crew, with symptoms lasting until the next morning.

synopsis: ZKC Center controllers reported an aircraft had icing problems, and what ensued to get the aircraft into VFR conditions.
summary: An ATC controller managed Aircraft X, which reported deicing failure and icing at FL270, by issuing a descent to FL240 while maintaining separation from Aircraft Y at FL260. The pilot later diverted to CGI, recovered radio contact, and entered VFR conditions without loss of separation or further incident.

synopsis: Livermore Tower Controller reported a runway incursion.
summary: The log controller failed to notice Aircraft X crossing hold short lines on RWY 25R while Aircraft Y was on short final, due to tower visibility limitations and divided attention during heavy traffic. Although Aircraft X stopped clear of the runway before Aircraft Y crossed the threshold, the controller admitted to missing the incursion until other controllers verified the line crossing.

synopsis: Chicago Center Traffic Management Controller reported a problem with a rocket launch waver.
summary: An Operations Manager requested a rocket launch waiver without meeting the required one-hour facility notice, prompting the reporter to alert affected areas. The reporter noted the operation should not have been approved due to this late notice and recommended stricter adherence to coordination agreements.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported a failure of their nosewheel on takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nosewheel tire blowout during takeoff from ZZZ, causing vibration and a loud bang. They elected to keep the gear down, burned fuel in a holding pattern, and performed an uneventful overweight landing back at ZZZ, where maintenance confirmed right nose tire damage.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported experiencing an acrid fumes smell in the passenger cabin at the completion of passenger boarding.
summary: The Captain and First Officer evacuated passengers at the gate due to a strong acrid smell caused by a likely burned-out recirculation fan. After turning off the APU and packs, maintenance diagnosed the issue, and the flight was completed on a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported fuel odor in cabin and resulting passenger illness.
summary: During climbout from ZZZ, the crew diverted to ZZZ1 after flight attendants reported a fuel odor and a sick passenger. Maintenance later confirmed a fuel leak from the center tank, though the overweight landing was uneventful and no leaks were visible on the taxiway.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported a flap overspeed occurred on approach into ORD when they encountered either wake turbulence or unstable air.
summary: During an ILS PRM approach to ORD 10C, the crew encountered unstable air causing an airspeed excursion approximately 10 knots above the Flaps 3 limit for 2–3 seconds. The pilots deployed landing gear to manage speed, landed uneventfully, and Maintenance confirmed the overspeed was within limits.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Air carrier Captain reported a ground conflict with another aircraft after the other aircraft made a wrong turn.
summary: A pilot taxiing at ORD reported a near-collision with another company aircraft that ignored ATC instructions to cross behind them and instead turned nose-to-nose onto Taxiway A13. The other aircraft passed within 10-12 feet after the pilot stopped, an incident attributed to the second crew's disregard for safety and failure to follow clearances.

synopsis: B747 First Officer reported Hazmat cargo improperly loaded. Hazmat shipment not loaded in accordance to Hazmat loading procedures.
summary: The First Officer discovered inaccessible Class 1.4c HAZMAT on the main deck during a pre-departure check because full pallets blocked the walkway. The Load Master and Captain coordinated with the company to relocate the cargo, correct the NOTOC, and depart 52 minutes late.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 pilot reported both primary airspeed indicators were temporarily incorrect.
summary: During a cruise descent in IMC, the crew experienced conflicting airspeed indications and an overspeed warning caused by suspected moisture obstruction in both primary pitot tubes. The First Officer and Captain stabilized the aircraft after the standby indicator showed 350 kts while primaries read 230 kts, prompting a maintenance report upon landing.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported a track deviation occurred on the BOSSS2 RNAV arrival into DEN when the FMC was improperly programmed following a late runway change.
summary: The flight crew descended through FL180 on the BOSSS2 arrival at DEN when an FMC alert triggered an unintended turn and descent for ILS 35R instead of the assigned 35L. The crew corrected the deviation after realizing the FMS still held the previous approach, a mistake attributed to rushing new checklist flows during a last-minute runway change.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported being confused by ATC and not knowing what altitude they should be going to While on the ANTHM 3 RNAV arrival to BWI airport.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring experienced confusion during descent at BWI due to conflicting ATC clearances for the ANTHM 3 arrival. This resulted in an unintended descent below the planned path and a missed 11,000-foot crossing restriction at ROKTT, requiring a new clearance to maintain 10,000 feet.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported confusion attributed to not understanding ATC clearance, and ATC altitude changes from the procedure while on the ANTHM 3 RNAV arrival to BWI airport.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring experienced confusion during descent at BWI due to conflicting ATC clearances for the ANTHM 3 arrival. This resulted in an unintended descent below the planned path and a missed 11,000-foot crossing restriction at ROKTT, requiring a new clearance to maintain 10,000 feet.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot monitoring reported confusion attributed to not understanding ATC clearance, and ATC altitude changes from the procedure while on the ANTHM3 landing Runway 10 at BWI.
summary: During a descent via ANTHM3 at BWI, the flight crew inadvertently descended to 10,300 feet after the Pilot Flying reset the altitude selector to 4,000 and engaged managed descent. The error resulted from conflicting interpretations of an ATC clearance, high workload, and distraction, requiring a climb back to 11,000 before a revised clearance to maintain 10,000.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported being notified a Flight Attendant had experienced a fumes event.
summary: A flight attendant experienced a fume event. The narrative does not specify the aircraft, phase of flight, cause, or outcome.

synopsis: Corporate aircraft flight crew reported exceeding 200 knots during departure below SJC Class B airspace.
summary: The flight crew flying the TECKY3 RNAV departure from SJC exceeded the 200-knot speed limit under the SFO Class B airspace after turning past the STCLR waypoint. The crew attributed the error to missing a chart note regarding the Class B restriction and focused instead on the 230-knot limit at STCLR.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported hazmat was incorrectly loaded, ramp personnel corrected the error.
summary: Ramp personnel loaded an accessible dangerous goods package incorrectly, preventing the First Officer from seeing the label. The issue was quickly remedied due to a lack of attention to detail.

synopsis: A corporate pilot reported exceeding 200 knots below Class B airspace.
summary: Pilots departing SJC on an RNAV departure accelerated to 250 knots while below SFO Class B airspace. The controller alerted them to the violation, prompting a speed reduction to 200 knots, which the crew attributed to a confusing clearance and failure to review overlying airspace.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported a ground conflict with another aircraft on the ramp during pushback.
summary: The flight crew received pushback clearance in ZZZ, but ground crew stopped the push when Aircraft Y taxied closely behind. The reporter attributed the incident to either Ramp Controller inattention or the pilot of Aircraft Y misunderstanding their taxi clearance.

synopsis: EMB-140 Captain reported burning smell fumes during climb and cruise. Flight crew executed a return to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced an engine burning smell during takeoff and cruise, requiring a return to ZZZ and subsequent maintenance assistance. Scheduling then assigned an adjusted showtime that violated rest requirements, causing fatigue despite the crew's safety concerns regarding the stressful event.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Taxi Captain reported a taxiway incursion at SJC citing signage and lighting issues as contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew taxied at night from a San Jose FBO to Runway 30L but stopped on Taxiway V after realizing they had missed a required right turn due to confusing dual Taxiway G designations. The pilot attributed the near incursion to misleading signage and a clearance that omitted the necessary turn onto Taxiway V.

synopsis: EMB190 Captain reported uncommanded rudder deflection in cruise flight resulting in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple uncommanded rudder deflections at FL300, causing a cross-controlled state that required disconnecting the autopilot and diverting. They managed the situation by slowing to 250 knots and limiting bank angles, resulting in a safe landing with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported persistent fumes resulting in health issues. After precautionary air return, flight crew was diagnosed with low grade carbon monoxide poisoning.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced jet exhaust fumes and carbon monoxide poisoning symptoms during taxi, climb, and landing due to an unknown source, despite an MEL requiring the APU to run. The aircraft returned to the departure airport, where medical evaluation confirmed low-grade carbon monoxide poisoning for the crew.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported fumes in the cabin which resulted in adverse health issues to the reporter and a passenger.
summary: A cabin crew member reported severe symptoms from a strong pesticide odor on a ZZZ flight, causing near-fainting and requiring cockpit oxygen. The crew member later assisted a passenger who fainted in the aisle and was removed by paramedics upon arrival.

synopsis: Captain reported sighting an object (either a drone or balloon) close by his aircraft while flying at 15,500 feet.
summary: Pilots flying level at 15,500 feet and 220 knots observed an unidentified black object with a red payload pass above the right wing with 10 feet of clearance. The object, possibly a drone or balloon maintaining altitude, was reported to ATC.

synopsis: A flight instructor and a student reported a near miss at a non-towered airport.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a high-wing training aircraft nearly collided with an agricultural aircraft on final approach at an uncontrolled airport. The near miss occurred because the student's position blocked the view of the base leg, and a faint radio warning was ignored before the crop duster passed overhead.

synopsis: First Officer reported receiving a GPWS warning when repositioning the aircraft in poor weather.
summary: Pilots on a repositioning flight between two non-controlled fields inadvertently descended due to high workload while configuring for arrival in deteriorating weather. The terrain alert warning system prompted the pilot flying to arrest the descent, resulting in a normal landing.

synopsis: Captain reported a ground conflict with an aircraft taking off in the opposite direction during their takeoff roll.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X aborted takeoff on Runway 24 at 40 knots after discovering another aircraft attempting a takeoff in the opposite direction on Runway 6. The incident occurred due to a lack of CTAF communication, resulting in a runway incursion that was resolved by both crews stopping and taxiing off.

synopsis: A Cessna pilot reported losing radio communications with ATC but was able to contact the Tower on their cell phone for an approach clearance.
summary: A pilot flying IFR in IMC lost radio contact with Approach and Tower while both radios failed. The pilot used a cell phone to obtain a landing clearance, squawked 7600, and successfully flew the ILS approach after re-establishing radio contact upon breaking out of clouds.

synopsis: SR20 Flight Instructor reported a tail strike that occurred on takeoff.
summary: A student pilot and instructor practicing soft field takeoffs experienced a tail strike during a control transfer caused by distraction from crosswind issues and traffic. The incident also involved failure to retract flaps per checklist, leading the instructor to take a two-day safety stand-down.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Controller reported a pilot requested an immediate landing from ATC when the aircraft door flew off and the pilot's finger was severed.
