This created a dangerous situation where an eastbound arrival and a westbound overflight at 9,000 feet came within 6 miles at over 600 knots closing speed.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Center Controller In Charge reported an unacceptable workload was placed on the facility which resulted in controllers being unable to practice social distancing at the facility.
summary: The Controller In Charge reported that sectors XX and YY became overloaded with red alerts due to excessive rerouting and spacing restrictions without assistance from adjacent facilities or the Traffic Management Unit. This saturation forced a sector shutdown and created unsafe conditions, including a violation of social distancing protocols, which the reporter attributed to reckless management decisions.

synopsis: Center Controller and an air carrier First Officer reported an airborne conflict that resulted in an RA and a minimal altitude deviation. The Controller advised caution when climbing and descending aircraft during the COVID-19 pandemic because aircraft performance is not always as expected due to lighter-than-normal loads.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a First Officer reported a Resolution Advisory between two transports near FL300 caused by complex rerouted traffic and potential Mode-C errors. The pilot deviated to avoid conflict, but the autopilot subsequently captured FL303 instead of the assigned FL300, requiring manual correction.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Center Controller reported increased workload and complexity related to COVID-19 airspace closings.
summary: An air traffic controller managed high traffic volume during COVID-19 airspace closures while handling a non-RVSM aircraft at FL360 requesting a direct to ZZZ. The controller maintained separation with assistance from a second controller but noted the extreme complexity and recommended developing preplanned contingency strategies.

synopsis: Center Controller reported clearing an aircraft to an altitude that was not in his sector, citing an unusual configuration due to special COVID-19 social distancing procedures.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a combined sector configuration due to COVID-19 cleared Aircraft X to climb from FL340 to FL360 without coordinating with the upper sector. The controller realized the altitude was outside their sector boundaries during the handoff, attributing the error to an assumption that the unusual configuration included the upper airspace.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a Control Tower that was ATC Zero, leading to a disruption in communications.
summary: The pilot reported that ZZZ Tower evacuated due to Coronavirus concerns, disrupting ATC service while aircraft were airborne. The reporter stated this protocol poses an unacceptable risk and recommended dispatching flights with suitable alternates until the crisis is contained.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew received a momentary EGPWS terrain warning while turning base on a nighttime visual approach. The flight continued to a safe landing. The crew noted that distraction due to the COVID-19 pandemic, its impact on the company, and family concerns contributed to the event.
summary: During a night visual approach to Runway XX in ZZZ, the crew executed a go-around due to dim runway lights and an unstable approach. A momentary EGPWS terrain warning occurred during the subsequent downwind climb, attributed by the crew to mental distractions from personal and pandemic-related stressors.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported initiating a pushback before receiving required Hazmat documents.
summary: The flight crew released brakes before receiving the final dangerous goods notification during pre-preflight pushback. Although the aircraft did not move, the crew debated whether brake release constituted a push, but the flight continued to destination without issue.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a lack of personal protection equipment and improper cleaning and sanitizing of the dispatchers' office.
summary: A pilot reported unsanitary cleaning conditions at the Operations Center during midnight shifts, citing a lack of disinfectant wipes and a single hand sanitizer. The reporter observed a building attendant using the same rag to clean monitors, desks, and floors, which they believe fails to impede virus spread.

synopsis: Ramp agent reported non-standard operation and safety issue with regard to starting an aircraft engine at the gate.
summary: A ramp agent reported that a pilot and mechanic started Aircraft X's engines at the gate without notifying ground staff, violating safety procedures. The pilot claimed he received clearance from Ramp Tower, but the agent noted a lack of formal training and communication regarding engine starts at this station.

synopsis: CRJ700 First Officer reported that an FMS malfunction resulted in an altitude and course deviation.
summary: During the GIBBZ3 arrival, the crew reported a faulty autopilot that descended below the assigned 6,000 ft level due to wake turbulence and a faulty FMS that briefly blacked out, causing a loss of lateral guidance. The Captain and First Officer decided to file maintenance reports for both equipment failures after ATC vectored them back onto the arrival.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported deviating from charted course on departure in part because the aircraft was climbing quicker than normal due to a very low passenger count as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer departed a lightly loaded aircraft on the ZZZZZ 5 Departure, where an abrupt 15-degree pitch caused a missed ZZZ VOR 159-degree radial intercept. This deviation triggered a low altitude alert from ATC due to terrain, requiring a manual correction to rejoin the procedure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported departing with a passenger count discrepancy resulting in a weight and balance issue.
summary: The pilot and first officer of Aircraft X departed ZZZ with performance data based on an incorrect passenger count of 11 instead of the expected XX. After the first officer discovered the discrepancy in-flight, the crew recalculated landing parameters for the heavier weight and landed safely.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that during boarding they noted a child passenger had COVID-19 like symptoms, but at the time did not know what the correct protocol was to address the situation.
summary: During boarding, the Captain consulted Medlink regarding a coughing lap child, resulting in the child and parents being removed. After confirming no company policy existed and receiving Medlink's advice that risk was negligible, the crew operated and completed the flight.

synopsis: E175 Captain reported that a wake turbulence encounter on final approach resulted in a go-around.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence at 100 feet above the runway, causing instability. They executed a safe go-around.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported the standard taxi chart at PHX airport needs reformatting to conform with other airport standard taxi charts.
summary: Pilots taxiing at PHX for Runway 25R stopped short of Taxiway Delta due to contradictory Jeppesen instructions. The Tower Controller confirmed the error, noting 100 previous aircraft made the same mistake, and requested clarification of the poorly written standard taxi procedures.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported executing an uneventful emergency air return due to number 2 engine failure during climb.
summary: During climb to FL220, the First Officer reported a loud thump and severe damage to Engine 2, causing rapid EGT rise and RPM rollback. The crew executed the severe damage checklist, dumped 107,000 pounds of fuel, and performed an auto-land at ZZZZ; maintenance later found melted metal in the exhaust cone, though the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported experiencing a track heading deviation while on the ROLLN2 arrival to CLT. Captain stated similar sounding fix names BETYL and DEVYL contributed to the event.
summary: The flight crew and approach controller experienced confusion during descent into CLE due to frequent instruction changes and uncorrected readbacks of conflicting fixes. This led to a clearance for approach while off-course in IMC, requiring a climb and vector to rejoin the ILS before a safe landing.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported issues with a Center being ATC Zero and having to divert to obtain more fuel to reach their destination airport.
summary: The flight crew diverted from ZZZ1 to ZZZ2 for fuel after ATC rerouted them around closed ZZZ3 airspace. Descending to FL230 and adding 150 miles increased fuel burn, forcing an unplanned stop at ZZZ4 despite initial fuel planning.

synopsis: C-172 Single Pilot reported a go-around on landing due momentary loss of directional control . The right main landing gear struck a runway edge light in the process of the go-around.
summary: A Pilot Under Instruction lost directional control on final approach to Runway XXC due to wind and left-turning tendencies, striking a runway edge light during a late go-around. The incident caused damage to the right gear strut, with the pilot attributing the event to windshear and delayed decision-making.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported lack of disinfectant wipes and cleaning agents on the round trip flight.
summary: Cabin crew reported a lack of disinfectant wipes and cleaning supplies on a round-trip flight between ZZZ and ZZZ1. Cleaners arrived with only a vacuum and garbage bags, failing to clean bathrooms or refill tissue boxes.

synopsis: UAV pilot reported a Class B airspace violation.
summary: A pilot flew a drone for claim inspection without checking airspace, relying on manufacturer geographical fencing. The company's UAS department discovered the violation, prompting the pilot to commit to pre-flight airspace checks and obtaining LAANC or CoA authorization for future flights in controlled airspace.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Student Pilot reported an NMAC event in landing pattern during base turn to final.
summary: While flying base to land on Runway 29, the pilot reported a Baron flying behind cut diagonally in front. The pilot circled for one to two minutes until the Baron cleared the runway, then rejoined the pattern and landed normally.

synopsis: Instructor of a C-152 Single Pilot trainee reported that the trainee had a runway excursion including striking a landing light during their landing rollout.
summary: A student pilot soloing in a traffic pattern at ZZZ lost directional control on landing due to ineffective rudder use, causing a runway excursion where the left main wheel struck a light. The student recovered the aircraft to a stop with no injuries or substantial damage and later taxied to the ramp.

synopsis: BL-17 Pilot reported engine failure on first flight after purchase resulting in a forced landing.
summary: The pilot of a Bellanca Super King experienced an engine failure and nose gear collapse during a VFR flight after a mechanic installed a fuel metering unit and used experimental lubrication on cables. The throttle became stiff, the engine quit and surged without control, forcing a landing in a muddy field with no injuries.

synopsis: Corporate Jet Captain reported a taxiway incursion at PIT airport. The crew taxied onto to Taxiway N2 versus N as cleared. Captain cited poor taxiway signage/labeling as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot taxied onto a no-civilian aircraft zone at PIT after following poorly labeled lines while complying with an ATC clearance to taxi to the FBO via Taxiway November. The reporter attributed the incident to inadequate signage, lack of planning foresight, and ATC issuing instructions assuming familiarity with the area.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported engine failure which resulted in a safe forced landing.
summary: During a biennial flight review, the pilot experienced a total engine power loss at 1,500 feet AGL. The pilot safely executed a forced landing on a paved county road.

synopsis: PA-28 Pilot reported a NMAC event in landing traffic pattern with an unidentified twin aircraft in class D airspace.
summary: The pilot inbound for Runway XX at ZZZ observed an unidentified piston twin aircraft above and to the left while descending to 8,000 feet MSL. The pilot executed evasive action because the intruder appeared to be operating within Class D airspace without communicating with the Tower, though the pilot landed uneventfully.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a critical ground conflict while taking runway for departure with aircraft on final approach.
summary: A VFR pilot departing Runway 26 at VUO stopped just beyond the hold short line after spotting a Cessna on short final that had not been seen earlier. The Cessna pilot initiated a go-around, and the reporter attributed the event to not hearing the other aircraft's position reports.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported encountering wake turbulence from an opposite direction B787 in SEA airspace.
summary: During a visual approach to PAE, a southbound aircraft encountered wake turbulence from a northbound B787 climbing three miles ahead. The encounter caused an uncommanded 40-45 degree left roll, which the pilots recovered from, noting the wake drifted unexpectedly far despite south-to-north winds.

synopsis: Center Controller reported that under-staffing due to COVID-19 has resulted in numerous aircraft reroutes.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that ZZZ airspace was restricted to "As Needed" staffing due to Coronavirus, forcing aircraft to reroute around a 360 NM diameter. A proposal to use the ATOP system for non-radar operations at FL320 and above was rejected by the union, causing unnecessary flight inconveniences.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew and an enroute Controller reported an airborne conflict occurred when the flight crew took a descent clearance intended for another aircraft. Controller suggested that increased workload associated with COVID-19 procedures contributed to the event.
summary: Pilots descended from FL390 after mishearing a clearance intended for another aircraft due to frequency congestion. A TCAS traffic alert prompted a reduced descent rate, and ATC subsequently corrected the error and issued a new clearance to FL370.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported having an aircraft pressurization problem thinking it was an equipment problem but the Packs were not turned on.
summary: During climbout from ZZZ, the Captain and First Officer experienced a cabin altitude warning at 13,300 feet caused by both engine bleed air valves being left off. The crew attributed the missed switch positions to fatigue after a long duty day, but they successfully leveled off, corrected the configuration, and resumed the climb without oxygen mask deployment.

synopsis: First Officer reported issues relating to NOTAMS and towers closing for COVID-19 cleaning.
summary: A flight crew discovered a destination tower closure via FD Pro after Dispatch and NOTAM packets failed to list it, causing confusion with ground operations. The crew adapted by using alternative frequencies, while another airline's captain argued with a ramp controller over the same missing NOTAM instructions.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ORD taxiway Bravo line should be repainted.
summary: The pilot and first officer could not see the yellow Bravo taxi line while taxiing in snow and wet conditions. They stopped to locate the line, noting the faded markings as a safety hazard requiring repainting.

synopsis: Ground employee reported the employee bus carries more than 10 passengers and 6 feet social distancing separation is impossible.
summary: Employees reported that limiting bus occupancy to contain COVID-19 failed to meet CDC guidelines of 10 people or 6 feet separation. The reporter stated that the current measures fall short of these standards, making social distancing impossible.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots reported routing and fuel problems associated with a ARTCC airspace closure.
summary: The flight crew departed ZZZ1 for ZZZ3 but deviated from the updated route after ZZZ4 because they missed a dispatch change caused by ZZZ7 Center closure. ATC queried the deviation, allowing the crew to correct the flight path via ZZZ5 and continue safely to the destination.

synopsis: Captain failed to verify that the release was properly electronically signed prior to departure.
summary: The Captain failed to electronically sign the flight plan release before departure while using iPads to bypass the ramp office for COVID-19 compliance. The error resulted from a break in normal habit patterns combined with multiple distractions and interruptions during the briefing process.

synopsis: First Officer reported concerns with having to ride a bus full of crammed passengers from the gate to the aircraft increasing their risk of being exposed to Coronavirus.
summary: Cabin crew on Flight ABC from ZZZZ were forced to ride a packed bus with passengers to a remote gate. The reporter stated this increased Coronavirus exposure risk and requested dedicated crew transport separated from passengers.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger sprayed Lysol on and around his seat.
summary: A passenger sprayed Lysol aerosol in First Class, creating a strong odor that violated crew breathing space. The Captain deferred action until landing, noting the item is a prohibited dangerous good that the passenger had carried on board despite TSA screening.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported not following procedures during the disarming of doors after the arrival and stated distraction and anxiety about COVID-19 contributed to the event.
summary: A flight attendant reported that the R1 door warning strap remained armed after the L1 door was opened during a medical emergency. The reporter attributed the oversight to the D Flight Attendant's gloves blocking the view while disarming the girtbar, a situation exacerbated by fatigue and coronavirus anxiety.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported witnessing the aircraft's cleaning crew did not follow Covid-19 procedures and only sanitized the galley counter tops.
summary: Cabin crew reported that cleaners on Aircraft X failed to wipe tray tables and armrests during a two-hour turn, cleaning only countertops. The crew was advised by Union Stewards to report this deviation from pandemic cleaning instructions briefed to technicians.

synopsis: GA pilot training at night experienced a ramp excursion at LEE airport. Poor lighting was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: During a night flight training session, the pilot and co-pilot taxied an aircraft into a ditch on a poorly lit ramp while searching for a self-serve fuel pump. The reporter attributed the incident to insufficient airport lighting and a lack of visible markers warning of the ditch.

synopsis: Vans RV-8A pilot reported loss of directional control on the landing roll when left rudder travel was impeded by a cabin heat cable bracket.
summary: The pilot of an amateur-built aircraft in Phase 1 testing departed the runway right after landing in 8-knot crosswinds, damaging a distance marker. The pilot attributed the loss of directional control to a cabin heat cable bracket interfering with the left brake pedal when rudder pedals were set to maximum length.

synopsis: Center Controller reported unusual traffic flows due to COVID-19 and its effect on the normal workload.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X violated closed Sector X airspace while descending to 110 to avoid coronavirus restrictions. The controller attributed the violation to ZZZ Approach's inability to provide lower altitudes and a flawed descent procedure.

synopsis: Pilot reported concerns with carrying passengers who were COVID-19 positive.
summary: A crew member reported a potential FOM violation regarding the transport of passengers with Coronavirus without prior screening. The reporter stated that operating without a screening procedure disregards the manual's policy against transporting passengers with contagious diseases.

synopsis: EMB-140 fight crew reported flying an unstable approach which resulted an EGPWS and ATC low altitude alert.
summary: Pilots on an ILS 04 approach to LGA descended too rapidly to avoid being high, preventing glide slope capture and triggering glide slope warnings and a low altitude alert. They disconnected the autopilot, leveled off, and landed visually after breaking out of clouds, though they noted a go-around should have been executed.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported an EGPWS alert during approach to ONT airport.
summary: A pilot flying an aircraft in IMC received an EGPWS Terrain Pull Up alert while descending to 4500 ft toward the TAKOE fix at ONT. The pilot speculates a 3300 ft tower on a hill caused the alert and recommends SOCAL assign higher altitudes in that area despite charts indicating 4500 ft was adequate.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported pushing back without required Hazmat documentation.
summary: The Captain pushed back without the Final Dangerous Goods Summary due to distraction from early push crew and agent readiness calls. The missing document was requested from Load Planning and received before taxiing, as the Captain had failed to consult his personal checklist.

synopsis: Ramp agent reported working too close to others and not having sufficient antiseptic wipes.
summary: Crew members reported insufficient antiseptic wipes for work areas and ready rooms, with only two provided for equipment. Additionally, product sort procedures grouped staff together rather than spreading them out, creating a high risk of virus transmission.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a TCAS RA related to an abnormally high climb rate associated with very lightly loaded aircraft because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS Resolution Advisory during an RNAV arrival at 11,000 feet caused by another aircraft climbing rapidly to 10,000 feet. The crew executed a climb to clear the conflict, attributing the event to the other pilot's excessive climb rate rather than a loss of separation.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported they were notified by a Flight Attendant of a dirty sock" smell in the rear of the cabin prior to gate pushback resulting in a maintenance delay, and eventual flight cancelation."
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced strong cabin fumes from an APU oil leak before engine start, requiring passenger deplaning and a remote engine run-up. The First Officer refused to fly due to safety concerns regarding the fumes and the Captain's exposure, resulting in the crew being reassigned to a later flight.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported prior to flight departure, a required alternate airport was NOTAMed unavailable due to COVID-19.
summary: A dispatcher planned an ETOPS flight with ZZZZ as an alternate despite a NOTAM prohibiting its use due to COVID-19. The flight departed 10 minutes late after the dispatcher halted departure to correct the alternate to ZZZ following conflicting tower advice.

synopsis: Pilot and Controllers reported an altitude overshoot that caused an airborne conflict.
summary: A pilot and air traffic controller were involved when Aircraft X received a TCAS Resolution Advisory while climbing to FL200 near Lake X due to high climb rates. The controller attributed the event to failing to issue traffic advisories and combining altitude and routing clearances, though the pilot disputed the assigned altitude.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a fumes event during boarding and also during descent at destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced a fume event on Aircraft X during descent at 3,000 ft, boarding, and again through FL 210. Despite Maintenance deactivating Pack 1 and the APU, the odor persisted with Pack 2 and engine bleeds operating.

synopsis: Flight Attendant stated preoccupation with COVID-19 concerns resulted in forgetting to bring the EFB to work.
summary: A cabin crew member left their apron containing an EFB on a previous aircraft while heading to an overnight layover. The error occurred because changing service procedures disrupted their routine, and they did not retrieve the apron since they were not serving on the upcoming flight.

synopsis: A320 flight attendants reported ill passenger vomited on two FAs who took preventative measures on their persons as well as requested passenger medical evaluation at destination.
summary: Cabin crew managed a passenger who vomited between aft lavatories due to shortness of breath, resulting in light exposure to two flight attendants. The crew switched jumpseats to avoid contamination, cleaned the area, and paramedics evaluated the passenger upon landing before releasing her.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that the kit on the aircraft did not have required sanitation supplies or masks. In addition, these supplies are not being replenished in between flights.
summary: Flight attendants reported missing disinfectant, masks, and sanitation wipes on an aircraft at ZZZ, forcing them to break into kits and delay departure while waiting for supplies. The crew noted this was a recurring issue at ZZZ and ZZZ1, expressing concern over potential health risks due to the lack of required sanitation items.

synopsis: FCM Tower Controller reported one aircraft lined up for the wrong runway twice causing one airborne conflict. Controller also stated the controllers cannot determine which runway aircraft are lined up for due to Tower placement.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Aircraft X repeatedly lined up for Runway 10R instead of the cleared Runway 10L, causing Aircraft Y to execute a low go-around near an apartment complex. The controller attributed the incident to the Tower's inability to visually verify aircraft runway alignment, necessitating a new facility.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported problems associated with required training and social distancing.
summary: A pilot reported that the airline conducted simulator training events during a national health crisis, violating social distancing guidelines and government edicts. The reporter argued that these non-essential gatherings in small classrooms and simulators created unnecessary infection risks for pilots that could be mitigated by delaying training.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported the company training center and simulators could benefit from more sanitation and cleaning supplies for staff and trainees in order to support a safe training environment. The crew member suggested that the company pursue FAA approval to extend training events deadlines in order to have time to deep clean the training facility.
summary: A flight training center operator reported inadequate sanitation supplies and lack of quarantine measures for pilots entering simulators during the COVID-19 crisis. The reporter suggested extending training deadlines to allow for facility deep cleaning and restocking to prevent virus transmission among staff.

synopsis: Ramp employee expressed concern about Coronavirus related company procedures.
summary: Cabin crew reported a lack of proper sanitary equipment, receiving only two wipes for tractor work areas, while management discussed consolidating piers to place personnel closer together.

synopsis: Load Planner expressed concern about Coronavirus related company procedures that resulted in personnel being seated too close to one another.
summary: Load planners and a Lead complained about insufficient social distancing at assigned desks during a shift with reduced flight schedules. After loud complaints, the Lead moved the reporter to a desk across the aisle, providing adequate separation.

synopsis: Ground employee reported concern over his employer's Coronavirus related procedures.
summary: A ground crew member reported a lack of antiseptic supplies for cleaning work areas and equipment. The reporter also noted that consolidating staff in the product sort area prevents adherence to social distancing guidelines.

synopsis: EMB-505 Captain reported severe turbulence during approach resulting in momentary loss of aircraft control.
summary: The pilot reported a suspected severe turbulence encounter during enroute descent and final approach into Aspen, Colorado. This resulted in several moments of momentary loss of aircraft control in the bank attitude, though no excessive bank attitude aural warning was triggered.

synopsis: E175 Captain reported distractions related to turbulence resulted in a track deviation and a missed approach.
summary: During a radar vector to Runway 19C, the pilot deployed speed brakes to maintain 170 kts and encountered turbulence, mistakenly fearing a system failure. The crew subsequently deviated from the assigned heading, requested a climb to 3,000 ft to re-intercept the localizer, and post-flight inspection confirmed no defects.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an aborted takeoff because the tow bar was still attached.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff after hearing a loud metallic sound and feeling a bump caused by the propeller striking a tow bar left attached to the nose wheel. The incident resulted in damaged propeller tips and the tow bar, which the pilot retrieved after shutting down and taxiing back to the ramp.

synopsis: PA-21 Student Single Pilot reported a go around, including a ground strike, to a final landing with a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot overcorrected during landing on Runway XX, struck a runway edge light while attempting a go-around, and punctured the left fuel tank. The pilot subsequently landed again, overcorrected a second time, and veered off the runway onto the grass.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported landing from an unstabilized approach to DEN.
summary: The crew configured flaps 40 early to intercept the glideslope while monitoring wake turbulence from Aircraft Y. The Pilot Monitoring failed to crosscheck altitude when flaps were retracted to 30 at 402 ft AGL, resulting in a missed go-around opportunity.

synopsis: Ground personnel reported that persons exposed to COVID-19 were allowed to continue to work.
summary: Management notified employees of exposure to a coworker who tested positive for COVID-19 but allowed them to continue working without quarantine. One exposed employee worked, developed symptoms two days later, and potentially spread the virus.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an erroneous frequency change that resulted in a track heading deviation.
summary: The Captain, acting as Pilot Monitoring during an approach in low-traffic conditions, prematurely switched to Tower frequency and missed ATC vectors. This caused the aircraft to overshoot the turn to final, requiring a steep correction before stabilizing for a safe landing.

synopsis: Captain reported taxiing off the hard surface into the dirt, and cited poor lighting and markings at SGU airport as contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew entered a dirt non-movement area after pushback while turning onto a parallel taxiway. The deviation went unnoticed due to missing ground markings, absent edge lights, and poor overall ramp lighting.

synopsis: FBO Flight Supervisor for flight school reported Airport Operations Official notified the Duty Officer of a Critical Ground encounter of an FBO SR-20 with air carrier during taxi.
summary: The Flight Supervisor reported that the PIC of Aircraft X taxied under the wing of Aircraft Y during pushback after receiving a Tower clearance to taxi both aircraft to the ramp. The PIC believed there was sufficient clearance despite the abnormal path, and video evidence confirmed the incident.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew reported pushing back from the gate without required Hazmat documents.
summary: The crew realized during pushback that the aircraft lacked required dangerous goods paperwork. This documentation error occurred before departure, necessitating a halt to the pushback procedure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported the company provided face masks do not fit the reporter's face, causing fogging of glasses.
summary: A pilot declined a medical transport flight due to company-provided PPE failing fit tests and fogging glasses, creating a safety of flight issue. Dispatch refused to pay the pilot for not flying, despite management's failure to supply approved 3M 1860 masks.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported that the First Officer found an elevator hinge cover plate installed backwards, resulting in aircraft damage and a cancelled flight.
summary: The First Officer discovered a damaged or reversed elevator hinge cover during a pre-flight walk-around, resulting in a flight cancellation. The reporter, noting this is the third occurrence in two months, requested a safety bulletin and fleet-wide inspection to address the issue.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported issues with COVID-19 screening procedures after a flight.
summary: Cabin crew at ZZZ reported unsafe health screening practices during deplaning, where screeners failed to maintain social distancing and reused a single disinfectant wipe for multiple infrared thermometer cleanings. The crew attributed these issues to inadequate screener training, which they believe endangered their health by spreading germs.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the ATC Tower changed hours of operation and was closed due to COVID-19, resulting in a takeoff before curfew ended.
summary: The flight crew departed ZZZ to ZZZ1 from a closed tower environment after receiving clearance from TRACON. They realized post-departure that they took off several minutes before the ZZZ 10-7 page restriction prohibiting departures between XP:00 and XB:00.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airline Dispatcher reported disparities between current volcanic ash activity in the airport vicinity and active SIGMET utilized for airline operations.
summary: Dispatch and Aircraft X crew reported volcanic ash near MEX airport while WSI issued SIGMETs just outside the field, conflicting with crew observations and VAAC forecasts. Dispatch noted WSI failed to update TAFs or place SIGMETs over the airport despite ash being within 10nm, creating a disparity in weather products.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that during climbout, the aircraft rate of climb exceeded the pressurization system rate of climb resulting in a warning message. The crew reported an extremely light passenger and cargo load due to the COVID-19 pandemic contributed to the event.
summary: The Captain and First Officer received a differential pressure warning while climbing above FL320 with four passengers due to an excessive climb rate exceeding pressurization limits. They followed QRH procedures to control the pressure manually for the remainder of the flight, noting the aircraft remained under control with no negative consequences.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported an unstable approach and being unaware of flying approach well below charted altitude.
summary: During a reposition flight to CWA in low IFR, the Captain entered an incorrect altimeter setting (30.32 instead of 29.32), causing an uncommanded descent below 3,000 ft. The First Officer identified the error, prompting a climb to the assigned altitude; the crew continued the unstable approach and landed safely without a GPWS alert.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that a crewmember had possibly been exposed to COVID-19. For social distancing purposes, Flight Attendant sat in a cabin seat for takeoff and landing.
summary: A flight attendant informed the pilot of potential COVID-19 exposure and symptoms before the flight. The pilot sat in a separate jumpseat to maintain social distance during takeoff and landing to protect themselves and their family.

synopsis: C340-A pilot reported the aircraft difficult to control and a possible airspace violation, during a test flight, after it was released from maintenance.
summary: The pilot conducted a post-inspection test flight where the aircraft crabbed right after takeoff due to the main rudder trim being set to full right deflection, likely moved during maintenance. After centering the trim, the pilot regained control and landed safely, noting a separate right engine power issue.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported Runway 10C/28C is closed at PIT, but not marked with lighted X symbols.
summary: A pilot reported that upon landing at Pittsburgh International Airport, Runway 10C/28C was closed without lighted X's and contained parked aircraft due to ramp space shortages. The reporter attributed this hazardous situation to unused construction areas and suggested utilizing that space to prevent potential airfield accidents.

synopsis: BD700 Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV while on approach.
summary: During descent on a long downwind for ILS Runway 04R, both pilots observed a drone passing the left wing at the same altitude. The drone was located 100 to 200 feet from the aircraft.

synopsis: Navion pilot reported an engine failure and subsequent off field landing.
summary: The sole pilot experienced a complete loss of engine power during descent, forcing an off-airport landing that damaged the right wing leading edge on a stop sign. The cause remains unknown despite normal preflight checks, no fuel contamination, and 20 gallons of usable fuel remaining.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported a NMAC with a UAV.
summary: A pilot flying over Lewiston, Maine, observed a black, drone-like object pass the right wingtip, raising concern of a tail strike. The pilot subsequently advised a departing Skylane pilot on CTAF of the possible drone, which the departing pilot acknowledged.

synopsis: Cessna 172 Single Pilot reported an NMAC event during cruise over shoreline.
summary: A C-172 pilot cruising at 500 ft reported a near collision with a descending US Coast Guard helicopter approaching from the right. The pilot executed a right turn and descent to avoid the aircraft, which also turned right before continuing its descent to the beach.

synopsis: Aviat Pitts S2A Single Pilot reported a prop strike during taxi practice.
summary: The pilot taxiing a Pitts at high speed experienced an unsecured canopy opening during a simulated takeoff. While reaching for the canopy, the pilot inadvertently pushed the elevator forward, causing the tail to strike the propeller and the aircraft to rest nose down.

synopsis: Pilot was concerned why a site was temporarily closed for cleaning and what caused the closure.
summary: The reporter, an employee, expressed concern over the company's lack of communication regarding the temporary closure of facility ZZZ for deep cleaning due to multiple COVID-19 positive cases. The reporter stated the company failed to follow established protocols by not notifying potentially exposed staff or disclosing the specific trigger for the closure.

synopsis: Pilot reported a re-occurring issue of multiple ATC locations issuing takeoff clearances while preceding departure is still on takeoff roll.
summary: Concerned company pilots reported that ZZZ air traffic controllers issued takeoff clearances while preceding aircraft were still on the runway during takeoff roll. The pilots requested that this unsafe practice be shared with safety groups to prevent potential loss of life as airspace congestion increases.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp agent reported being uncomfortable with a company procedure requiring wearing shared headsets amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: Cabin crew reported that wing walkers and pushback drivers were required to use shared, unsanitized headsets during ground operations, creating a contamination risk during the pandemic. The crew argued this practice was unsafe due to a lack of cleaning supplies and the availability of personal hearing protection.

synopsis: Air carrier ramp agent expressed concern about wearing headsets that might be contaminated with coronavirus.
summary: A ground agent reported discomfort with supervisor-mandated use of wing walker headsets at a line station during the COVID-19 pandemic due to infection risks from contaminated equipment. The agent suggested using hand signals instead to avoid unnecessary exposure while noting that wipes only remove 65% of germs.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots reported departing without clearance in what they thought was an uncontrolled airport resulting in runway incursion and airspace violations.
summary: The crew of a flight from ZZZZ to ZZZ departed Runway Y after the Tower closed due to staffing issues, leaving them unable to contact Ground, Tower, or Departure. They coordinated with an inbound aircraft and self-broadcast before taking off, later being informed by ZZZZ Center of an unauthorized departure report.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported overshooting a charted altitude during a go-around. The Captain stated the very low aircraft weight associated with the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in an abnormally high climb rate.
summary: The pilot encountered severe turbulence and a 45-degree roll on final approach in a lightly loaded aircraft, triggering a go-around. Due to the high climb rate from low weight and TOGA power, the crew overshot the assigned 3,000-foot altitude by 700 feet before leveling off and completing a second successful landing.

synopsis: Flight crew member reported the company was sending crews out during pandemic without proper safety equipment.
summary: Pilots reported that the airline is sending crews on multi-day trips without N95 masks, disinfectants, or social distancing measures, violating SAFO 20003. The reporter attributes this to supply chain issues and management inaction, warning that accepting this unnecessary risk could lead to preventable deaths.

synopsis: Flight crew member reported the bag containing protective gear for COVID-19 was not boarded on the aircraft, and that the on duty in-flight Supervisor directed the crew to depart without the bag.
summary: Cabin crew reported that essential PPE was missing during boarding, causing a delay before departure. Although the Captain refused to close doors without the items, the Inflight Supervisor initially ordered the flight to proceed without them until the bag arrived six minutes later.

synopsis: Reporter was concerned that there weren't safety masks or respirators available for use.
summary: Cabin crew reported a lack of safety masks, respirators, and cleaning products at their station due to stock being sent elsewhere. The reporter noted that while health and safety items were unavailable, the group strictly enforced vest and seatbelt infractions.

synopsis: AA5B Tiger Single Pilot reported momentary loss of control during landing resulting in a prop and wing strike.
summary: The pilot experienced a hard landing in a crab with a prop and wingtip strike due to a right crosswind gust and possible wind shear at 5 feet AGL. The pilot recovered directional control, continued the landing, and taxied to the ramp, later concluding that a go-around would have been safer given the damage.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported landing without clearance due to fatigue and lack of recent flying assignments due to COVID-19-related decrease in flights.
summary: The crew landed without a clearance after the Pilot Not Flying mistakenly dialed the wrong tower frequency while the Pilot Flying focused on hand-flying. The reporter attributed the error to low recent flight time, fatigue, and distraction during the pre-landing checklist.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that due to weight and balance needs, the Operations Agent directed passengers on a nearly empty flight to sit close together, violating social distancing requirements. The Captain suggested that weight and balance be reworked to allow appropriate spacing between passengers.
summary: Passengers on a mostly empty flight were forced into close contact because the Operations Agent prioritized weight and balance over social distancing. The reporter states that better distribution of passengers, bags, and cargo would have allowed appropriate spacing.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported an NMAC event while under control of Approach Control during approach with a departing helicopter.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss with a helicopter at 2,500 feet while approaching EVV, triggered by a descent RA after ATC announced traffic at the same altitude. The pilot attributed the conflict to an incorrect assumption about the helicopter's climb and delayed ATC traffic advisories.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendants reported they failed to properly disarm doors prior to cross checking.
summary: A fatigued and distracted flight attendant failed to disarm the forward cabin entry door before opening it, causing the slide casing to separate from the door. The slide did not deploy, maintenance removed it, and passengers deplaned safely after the crew identified the error.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that another Flight Attendant refused to occupy the appropriate jumpseat due to social distancing concerns.
summary: A flight attendant refused to occupy the forward jump seat for takeoff and landing, citing social distancing due to Coronavirus despite the seat being functional. The pilot reported this refusal violated policy and placed passengers in potential danger during an evacuation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC event during a VFR flight under Approach Control routing.
summary: A pilot approaching Orlando under Approach control deviated from a heading instruction to avoid traffic passing 175 feet above. The pilot reported the altitude deviation, received a frequency handover, and landed safely, concluding that the pilot-in-command remains solely responsible for safety.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A pilot ferrying an aircraft reported a rejected takeoff due to abnormal engine indications from not removing the cowling inlet plugs.
summary: Two fatigued pilots rejected takeoff in Aircraft X with amphibious floats after abnormal engine indications caused by cowling inlet plugs left in place. The plugs warped the inertial separator, jamming its bypass door and restricting airflow, which would have likely caused an in-flight engine failure had the takeoff continued.

synopsis: Aventura AVII pilot reported forgetting to use the landing checklist to prevent the gear up landing.
summary: The pilot of an Aventura amphibious aircraft landed gear-up on the runway after expediting the pattern and failing to use the landing checklist. The fiberglass hull skidded, causing minimal damage, and the pilot manually deployed the gear to taxi off after verifying no runway damage or FOD.

synopsis: Single Pilot reported an uneventful forced landing at parking lot due to fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot departed ZZZ with 11 gallons of fuel, but the engine quit at 2,000 ft due to a leak from an open gascolator petcock left by a partner during pre-flight calibration. The pilot landed safely in a parking lot with no injuries or damage after the fuel level dropped precipitously.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported a NMAC event during a two plane formation flight as second aircraft with an unidentified helicopter that flew between the two aircraft.
summary: A pilot in a formation flight under an ADS-B waiver in Class B airspace lost 200 feet while executing a right turn to avoid a helicopter that passed between the formation. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the helicopter's failure to visually detect the trailing aircraft, noting that neither formation aircraft had ADS-B In capability.

synopsis: GA Pilot reported landing on a closed runway at LUD airport, noting that the runway was not marked with an X and the closure was not on the AWOS.
summary: A pilot inadvertently landed on closed Runway 35 at Decatur Airport during a local recreational flight. The reporter noted the runway lacked closure markings, AWOS advisories, or CTAF responses, with no maintenance personnel present.

synopsis: BTV TRACON Controller reported issuing a climb to an aircraft, the aircraft didn't climb as well as the Controller thought it would and ended up in a lower MVA.
summary: Air traffic controllers vectored an aircraft climbing for a visual approach, but the slow climb rate caused the aircraft to enter a higher Minimum Vectoring Altitude at a lower altitude. The controller attributed the error to mistakenly applying a departure rule.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that a fumes event during climb resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced a strong burning smell during climb and again on climbout from ZZZ, suspecting an oven or air duct source. They diverted back to ZZZ, landed safely without donning oxygen masks, and received an all-clear after first responders inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: Ground employee reported problems associated with sharing headsets.
summary: Ground personnel and a supervisor discussed mandatory wireless headset usage during pushback operations. The crew reported that the headsets hindered communication, situational awareness, and cleaning, while the supervisor admitted unfamiliarity with the equipment and ended the discussion.

synopsis: A-300F flight crew reported a hard landing/tailstrike by First Officer during first flight of OE. Captain executed a go-around to an uneventful landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a hard landing and tail strike during an IOE training approach to high-elevation airport ZZZ. The First Officer's abrupt control input caused a bounce, prompting the Captain to initiate a go-around; maintenance confirmed no structural damage but noted tail skid contact.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: First Officer reported becoming task saturated due to ATC clearance modification resulting in altitude excursion and momentary EGPWS Alert. Fight completed an uneventful landing.
summary: The Captain and Pilot Monitoring descended to 3,000 ft instead of 3,400 ft during an ILS 32 approach to ITH due to FMS cross-fill errors and task saturation. This misinterpretation of the approach plate caused a brief Landing Gear GPWS warning before a normal landing was completed.

synopsis: B737 pilot crew reported a NMAC with a large UAV.
summary: During climb out from MIA, the Captain reported a refrigerator-sized, blue and silver object passing below the aircraft near 10,000 ft. The object, which lacked wings or propellers, was described to Miami Center as possibly stationary or moving across the flight path, but the flight continued to destination without incident.

synopsis: Maintenance technician reported that an incorrectly labeled package resulted in a Hazmat shipping violation.
summary: A mechanic packed a portable fire extinguisher into a box for shipment on a flight after failing to identify it as Hazmat on the pick slip or by its location outside the designated stockroom section. The error occurred because the slip lacked a Hazmat remark and the part was not retrieved from the special Hazmat section.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported an uneventful emergency descent & diversion due to a loss of pressurization during cruise.
summary: The flight crew experienced a pressurization issue with thumping sounds and a slow cabin climb at FL410, triggering an emergency descent and oxygen mask deployment after the cabin altitude exceeded 9,000 feet. The aircraft stabilized below 9,000 feet at FL230, allowing the crew to stop the descent at FL210 and divert safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain report a NMAC with a UAV.
summary: During the RNAV arrival into TPA at 5,000 ft, the crew sighted a black, man-made drone near the shoreline. The object swept past the left wingtip, prompting the pilot to identify it as a personal drone likely filming the beach, though no flight path changes were deemed necessary.

synopsis: A-319 First Officer reported right cockpit windshield cracked during initial approach.
summary: The First Officer reported that on approach to ZZZ at 7,000 feet, the windshield cracked with an exploding sound, blocking visibility. As the non-flying pilot, the Captain continued the approach and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: B737 pilot crew reported the IRU's would not align, resulting in a rejected takeoff.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain vacated Runway 15R at BWI due to inaccurate displays and missing Flight Director guidance caused by intermittent GPS signals at the gate. After taxiing to the runway, GPS signals stabilized, allowing the crew to proceed with takeoff.

synopsis: Flight Attendant did not want to sit in the appropriate jumpseat for takeoff/landing for social distancing concerns. A Supervisor was contacted and the Flight Attendant was given the option to move to a different jumpseat or to be pulled from the flight. The Flight Attendant moved to another jumpseat.
summary: A flight attendant refused to occupy the jumpseat for takeoff and landing due to social distancing concerns, prompting the other flight attendant to involve the pilot and a supervisor. The crew was instructed that FAA rules require jumpseat occupancy, and the reporter agreed to comply with the policy.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that the aircraft did not have adequate cleaning/sanitizing supplies on board and the aircraft did not appear to have been properly cleaned.
summary: Cabin crew on Flight ABC reported insufficient cleaning supplies and a filthy aircraft condition prior to departure, hindering their ability to sanitize galleys and lavatories. Although some supplies were received at ZZZ1, the crew had to improvise cleaning methods, resulting in passenger complaints and concerns about health safety during the pandemic.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported there were no masks on the plane for flight attendant use and was concerned that the gloves and alcohol-free hand sanitizer were not adequate as personal protective equipment.
summary: Flight attendants on a 10-hour flight from ZZZZ to ZZZ reported working without masks, while cleaners in full hazmat suits removed trash upon landing. The crew expressed concern over the lack of protective equipment for themselves compared to the cleaners and requested safety improvements.

synopsis: Deadheading pilot reported that passengers in the back of the aircraft were told to move to seats at the front of the aircraft to accommodate a zone count, which required abandoning social distancing and sanitizing new seats.
summary: A deadheading crew member was forced to move from the rear to row 2 for a weight and balance count, compromising social distancing. The reporter states this procedure endangered their safety and recommends exempting crew from such moves immediately.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported number engine low N2 during takeoff roll and subsequent crew response to an uneventful takeoff.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain experienced a right engine thrust failure during takeoff on a light-weight aircraft. Despite an initial rejected takeoff call after V1, the crew continued the flight, contacted Maintenance Control, and completed the trip without further incident.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the aircraft had a bounced landing resulting in a go-around. The crew cited the handling and performance characteristics of the lightly loaded aircraft as a contributing factor.
summary: During a CAT III approach in a light aircraft, the First Officer added excessive power at 20 feet to arrest a high sink rate, causing a bounced landing and a go-around. The Captain attributed the incident to the aircraft's light weight and the First Officer's unexpected power application instead of relying on the flare cue.

synopsis: Technician reported disagreement over procedures for releasing an aircraft for service after an extended maintenance event with an open logbook item.
summary: A maintenance technician reported that base managers instructed staff to release Aircraft X as airworthy while Pitot probe covers remained installed and open maintenance entries were carried forward. The reporter stated this practice violates CFR 121.709 because the aircraft was declared airworthy despite being in an unairworthy configuration.

synopsis: GA pilot had difficulty finding a flight instructor during the COVID-19 pandemic to conduct a flight review.
summary: The pilot discovered post-flight that they had flown out of currency, exceeding the 24-month biennial flight review requirement. They suspended operations until securing an instructor for the review, attributing the error to a lack of personal calendar reminders and poor planning during the winter season.

synopsis: P2006 Tecnam Flight Instructor reported a nose gear collapse on normal landing with no previous indication of a problem.
summary: A student pilot and instructor landed an aircraft at ZZZ when the nose gear collapsed immediately upon runway contact, triggering gear warning lights. The reporter attributes the incident to a mechanical failure, noting the landing was not hard and no preventative action was possible.

synopsis: C206 pilot reported smoke and a loss of oil on takeoff that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after liftoff, Aircraft X began trailing smoke and oil following a recent oil change. The aircraft landed safely, but inspection revealed the engine had lost all oil, which was dripping from the cowl and covering the fuselage.

synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC while attempting to land at uncontrolled airport.
summary: The pilot of a local aircraft experienced a close call with Aircraft Y at a non-towered airport while on the downwind leg. The incident occurred because Aircraft Y failed to make standard position calls, prompting the pilot to extend the downwind leg to allow Aircraft Y to land ahead.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported a recurring failure of cockpit door locking mechanism and the incorrect door locking procedures.
summary: The pilot reported that the flight deck door failed to latch mechanically despite indicating lights being off during the before-start phase. The pilot attributed this recurring safety issue to inadequate procedures that rely solely on electrical indicators rather than requiring a physical check to verify the door is secure.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer expressed concern about the erosion of skills and knowledge while awaiting OE and consolidation flights. A restrictive flight schedule due to the COVID-19 pandemic was cited as contributing.
summary: A pilot reported that COVID-19 schedule restrictions delayed Initial Operating Experience flights for over a month, preventing the execution of planned training. The pilot expressed concern that these delays, compounded by Line Check Airman availability issues, are causing a loss of proficiency and skill retention.

synopsis: Ground personnel reported a discrepancy in HAZMAT cargo in the company load planning software.
summary: A cargo handler identified a software flaw causing a single AWB charter shipment to be incorrectly flagged as Hazmat, requiring a HOFF. Management resolved the issue by contacting the help desk, allowing the 56,928 lb shipment to depart as one unit.

synopsis: B747-400 flight crew reported continuing to use an autopilot after it had previously triggered an EICAS warning resulting in altitude and heading clearance deviations.
summary: During a descent to 3000 ft for a visual approach, the right autopilot failed to follow Flight Director guidance, causing an uncommanded pitch-down and acceleration toward flap overspeed limits. The crew disconnected the autopilot, recovered the aircraft at approximately 2300 ft, and completed the landing after logging the malfunction.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported having difficulty clarifying the company's current policy on the use of shared jumpseats and social distancing. The Flight Attendant occupied a passenger seat during takeoff and landing, rather than the assigned jumpseat. After the flight, the Flight Attendant found that jumpseat policy changes had not been put in place.
summary: A flight attendant sat in a passenger seat instead of a shared jumpseat during takeoff and landing after a lead flight attendant incorrectly stated the jumpseat was inoperative. The crew member later discovered this policy change had not been approved by the FAA, prompting a request for expedited review of shared jumpseat rules.

synopsis: Technician reported not installing a main wheel brake hydraulic line after troubleshooting a dragging brake and replacing the brake assembly.
summary: Aircraft Maintenance Technicians repairing a dragging brake on Aircraft X were diverted to fix a PSEU fault on another aircraft before returning to replace a grinding brake on Aircraft X. The reporter later discovered a brake hydraulic line was missing after three flight legs, attributing the error to high stress from overlapping maintenance tasks.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported a collision with an object while taxing aircraft for maintenance. The rush to ground planes due to the COVID-19 pandemic was referenced as a contributing factor.
summary: The right-seat pilot reported that while rushing to taxi an aircraft from a cramped ramp to a hangar for pandemic-related inspections, a last-minute ground clearance change forced a tight turn. This maneuver caused the right winglet to impact an object near the taxiway due to limited ramp information and frequent task reassignments.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported deviating from the departure clearance due to a malfunctioning HSI and compass.
summary: The pilot departed RWY 17 under IFR and entered IMC, inadvertently turning right due to suspected disorientation and HSI precession. After ATC provided no assistance and used abusive language, the pilot corrected the heading using ForeFlight, which revealed the compass was temporarily impaired before recovering.

aircraft: Navion Aircraft Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Navion Single Pilot reported entering icing conditions causing altitude and airspeed loss resulting in a stall. Pilot landed with ATC assistance.
summary: The pilot of a Navion encountered icing and a pitot heater failure during a repositioning flight, leading to unreliable airspeed and a power-on stall near the service ceiling. The pilot recovered by descending to lower altitudes with ATC assistance, attributing the incident to a poor decision to fly into suspect icing without PIREPS or an FIKI-equipped aircraft.

synopsis: EMB-505 Single Pilot reported flight control malfunction on takeoff resulting loss of pitch control, resulting in a return to departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced strong flight control resistance and pitch difficulty during takeoff, suspecting a flight control or trim malfunction. After an AP TRIM warning appeared, the pilot disabled the autopilot, returned to the airport, and landed safely.

synopsis: P-180 flight crew reported two blown tires on landing rollout due to a jammed left rudder pedal.
summary: The Pilot in Command and Second in Command landed an aircraft where a water bottle lodged between the left rudder and side wall, causing control issues and a runway excursion. The PIC recovered the bottle while the SIC took control, resulting in locked brakes, blown main tires, and a safe tow off the runway with no injuries.

synopsis: PA-28A Single Pilot reported a runway excursion on landing rollout due to a nosewheel first landing.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft at ZZZ on Runway XX with full flaps and 75 kts indicated airspeed. Upon touchdown, the nose wheel collapsed and the fork brace bent, causing the aircraft to veer right off the runway into grass before being taxied to the ramp.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported hearing multiple loud pops on takeoff and was informed that a nose wheel assembly was left on the runway.
summary: The crew heard a pop while taxiing, continued to takeoff, and were informed by Tower of a left nose tire left on the taxiway at 700 feet. They landed safely with no damage noted and were towed back to parking.

synopsis: First Officer reported that on takeoff, a nose wheel assembly departed the aircraft, requiring an emergency landing at destination airport.
summary: The crew lost a nose tire while taxiing to Runway XX but continued the takeoff after Tower notification. They diverted to ZZZ1 for a safe landing and tow, noting the missing gear symbol on the CONFIG page only after becoming airborne.

synopsis: A300 First Officer reported a hot brake that had to be soaked by the fire department upon gate arrival.
summary: After landing at ZZZ, the crew received a hot brake warning on wheel #8 while taxiing, prompting a stop short of the gate as temperatures exceeded 500 degrees. Maintenance identified a loose hydraulic brake line on the previously repaired wheel, requiring fire rescue to cool the gear.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a similar callsign issue and cancellations attributed in part to COVID-19 pandemic related work environment.
summary: Dispatchers for Flight ABC and a late inbound Flight ABC failed to identify a callsign conflict caused by similar flight numbers and disrupted workflows due to COVID-19 restrictions. ATC assigned a new callsign to Flight ABC to resolve the issue, which the dispatchers acknowledged and accepted.

synopsis: Captain reported refusing aircraft after multiple attempts to troubleshoot and repair a recurring engine fuel leak were unsuccessful and procedures were not adhered to.
summary: The Captain reported that a right engine fuel leak on Aircraft X was misdiagnosed and improperly repaired in ZZZ1 by sliding metal sleeves over saturated, torn fuel lines without inspector sign-off. Subsequent inspection in ZZZ revealed the hidden damage, leading the Captain to ground the aircraft as unsafe due to the fraudulent maintenance history.

synopsis: PA-28R pilot reported a ground strike with an unattended vehicle parked on the taxiway.
summary: A pilot with 180 hours taxiing a small aircraft at ZZZ airport collided with a white pickup truck parked on the taxiway. The truck, which lacked warning lights or NOTAMs, caused the left wingtip to rip off after the pilot failed to see the vehicle despite following standard taxi procedures.

synopsis: Pilot reported misinterpreting MEL and applied the incorrect MEL after failures of the Attitude Indicator on the Primary Flight Display.
summary: The pilot reported a Chelton PFD/MFD attitude indicator failure during a patient transport flight, causing erroneous bank readings and continuous warnings. The pilot delayed logging the defect in the MEL due to misinterpretation and concerns about company reaction, ferrying the aircraft for repairs the next day.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported the flight crew decided not to write up a minor in-flight equipment malfunction as a discrepancy, which might not be deferrable. The decision was due, in part, to the crew's uncertainty around recent changes in COVID-19 screening procedures at the destination airport.
summary: The flight crew deferred reporting an intermittent Captain's MCP autopilot light malfunction after departure from ZZZZ to ZZZZ1 due to COVID-19 security concerns at the destination. The reporter noted the crew should have consulted the Dispatch Deviations Guide or contacted maintenance, as the issue likely qualified for deferral.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported diverting due to a Cargo Fire EICAS Master Warning.
summary: The flight crew experienced false forward and aft cargo fire warnings at FL 360, likely caused by cargo loaded to the ceiling, and diverted to ZZZ. Maintenance confirmed the overloading caused the erroneous indication, while the crew noted ATC lacked company contact information.

synopsis: Technician reported being told the aircraft was 'okay' to board, but received no documentation stating the aircraft was properly sanitized.
summary: A mechanic on Aircraft X was instructed by a supervisor to remove a quarantine sticker and board without documentation confirming the required wait time or deep cleaning. The reporter stated this lack of records put employees at risk of contracting COVID-19.

synopsis: Flight Attendant expressed concern that attending a scheduled recurrent training class with a group of flight attendants could increase the risk of spreading the COVID-19 virus to other crew members and passengers.
summary: A flight attendant reported attending a crowded recurrent training session during a pandemic, violating government social distancing advisements. The crew member described the gathering as irresponsible and dangerous, fearing it would spread COVID-19 to fellow crew, passengers, and family members.

synopsis: Center Controller reported holding several aircraft due to weather at intended airport, interacting with TMU, lining aircraft up 20 MIT, then after the first three aircraft the Controller was told to hold remaining aircraft. Controller reported that due to the COVID-19 pandemic he did not call for D- Side help because of social distancing concerns.
summary: An air traffic controller managing ZZZ arrivals during weather delays faced confusion from rapidly changing Traffic Management Unit plans and sector communication gaps. The controller missed point-outs and struggled with sequencing, but Area 3 assistance prevented loss of separation despite the unusual operational conditions.

synopsis: Center Controller reported management was not following COVID-19 related facility policy for social distancing.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an Operations Manager violated social distancing protocols by roaming the control room and forcing a Facility Line Manager to open sectors based on staffing rather than traffic needs. The controller stated these actions contradicted agency and CDC guidance intended to minimize workforce exposure to COVID-19.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported conducting an unstable approach to a landing into an unfamiliar airport. The crew cited flying frequency as the main cause attributed to a reduction of flights during the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: A reserve Captain and a new First Officer with less than 100 hours flew an RNAV approach to ZZZ Runway XX in IMC. Poor ATC vectors and crew rustiness caused a high descent, but the First Officer disconnected the autopilot and added drag to salvage the approach for a safe landing.

synopsis: ERJ145 Captain reported the parked aircraft began rolling on the ramp and the First Officer put the brakes on and the parking brake causing an abrupt stop injuring a Flight Attendant.
summary: During engine start on a hardstand without a tug, the Captain failed to re-engage the parking brake, causing the aircraft to move. The First Officer abruptly applied brakes and the parking brake, injuring a Flight Attendant with whiplash due to the sudden stop.

synopsis: Captain reported wing anti ice failure in cruise, requiring a descent to exit icing conditions.
summary: Flight ZZZ-ZZZ1 crew received a wing A/I fail warning in moderate ice. They advised ATC and descended to 9000 ft to exit the ice conditions.

synopsis: Flight crew reported executing an evasive maneuver in compliance of GPWS Terrain Alert during approach due to altitude excursion.
summary: The Pilot Flying descended below the cleared 13,000 feet to 10,100 feet during the RNAV 05 approach, triggering a GPWS terrain caution at 11,700 feet. The crew immediately climbed back to 13,000 feet and completed the landing safely, attributing the error to fatigue and a premature altitude selection.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported pitch trim system failure on final, requiring a go around.
summary: The flight crew experienced a pitch trim asymmetry alert and autopilot disconnect at 3,000 feet on final approach to MSP. They discontinued the approach, unsuccessfully reset a circuit breaker, and landed safely after a Chief Pilot debrief advised against resetting breakers for flight control issues.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported breaking the tow bar during tow in after lack of communication lead to hard braking.
summary: The flight crew approached Gate XX believing it was a standard gate, but maintenance began towing the MD-11 toward a building using the incorrect 767 mark. The crew applied brakes to avoid a collision after the tow bar broke, resulting in an AML entry for inspection due to the lack of tow-in notification and maintenance error.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that due to aircraft weight and balance considerations, passengers were required to sit close together in specific rows. The crew member expressed concern that this was not conducive to health and social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that an Operations Agent seated 19 passengers in rows 4 through 10 due to weight and balance constraints. The reporter stated this arrangement compromised social distancing and questioned if utilizing zones 1 and 2 would have been safer during the pandemic.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported they are not being provided with adequate cleaning supplies and sanitizers during the COVID-19 pandemic. Flight Attendant also expressed concern with the flight being overstaffed for no reason.
summary: Cabin crew reported concerns regarding jumpseat assignments, excessive staffing, and a lack of hand sanitizer. The reporter stated that safety policies are being compromised by comfort preferences and unnecessary reserve staffing, which increases the number of personnel waiting in the airport.

synopsis: Technicians reported misreading an ECO, resulting in non compliance with established procedures.
summary: Two mechanics performed an Engineering Change Order on Aircraft X, incorrectly disconnecting ELAC wires because the effectivity page was located at the end of the document and overlooked. The aircraft was subsequently taken out of service after the error was discovered the following day.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported an IFR departure did not use the published departure procedure and was below the Minimum Enroute Altitude.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X below 8,000 feet in a 110 MEA area requested terrain avoidance vectors. The controller could not legally vector at that altitude, advised a west heading, and eventually cleared the aircraft direct to destination above 11,000 feet.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported aircraft began rolling after tow bar was disconnected after push back.
summary: During pushback in ZZZ, the aircraft rolled forward approximately 10 feet after the crew believed the parking brake was set. The roll occurred because the brake light was not verified, but the Captain stopped the movement immediately with no damage or injuries reported.

synopsis: E175 F/O reported the FMC was not performing properly in VNAV and was a factor in their failure to meet charted crossing restrictions on arrival into destination .
summary: The crew experienced vertical deviations and altitude constraint warnings while descending to SJC in PTH mode on an RNP AR approach. The pilot attributed the issue to the Baro VNAV system computing a flight path angle that did not meet the 7,000 ft constraint at JILAN, potentially jeopardizing operations specifications.

synopsis: SR-20 Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC during initial approach with an unreported aircraft.
summary: A pilot and student flying IFR to ZZZ reported a near miss with a VFR Bonanza while being vectored for the RNAV 31 approach. The aircraft crossed within 50 meters at the same altitude without prior traffic advisories, prompting the crew to maneuver away and suspect ATC workload issues.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having to ferry a flight for storage due the COVID-19 pandemic without correct maintenance release documentation.
summary: Pilots attempted a Part 91 maintenance ferry flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1 but departed without a proper maintenance release or ferry document in the logbook. Maintenance and Dispatch provided incorrect guidance and an unverified digital image, resulting in an improper departure that was later corrected by Flight Operations.

synopsis: B747 Captain reported a compressor stall on takeoff power application, causing a rejected takeoff and a return to gate for maintenance.
summary: The Pilot Flying rejected takeoff twice on Runway XX due to loud bangs and a left veer, suspecting a compressor stall on Engine 1 following a recent change. Despite normal engine indications and no visible damage, the crew returned to the gate for maintenance inspection after the second event involved a bright flash.

synopsis: Flight Attendant opted to practice social distancing by sitting in a First Class passenger seat instead of the assigned jumpseat next to another Flight Attendant who was coughing.
summary: A flight attendant sat in a First Class seat instead of the assigned jumpseat during takeoff and landing due to concerns about another crew member's health. The reporter requested that the FAA and company consider modifying flight attendant seating positions to allow for social distancing during the pandemic.

synopsis: Two flight attendants reported being notified that another Flight Attendant on the same flight had possible exposure to COVID-19 and as a result occupied a different jumpseat in order to maintain social distancing from cabin crew.
summary: A flight attendant occupied the right jumpseat during takeoff and landing to maintain social distancing after a previous crew member tested positive for COVID-19. The pilot reported this deviation from standard seating and suggested seeking FAA approval for alternative jumpseat assignments.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger violated COVID-19 social distancing rules when approaching the galley mid-flight to ask for a beverage.
summary: A passenger violated social distancing protocols in the aft galley to request a beer. The flight attendant discontinued all onboard service to prevent crew members from being exposed to illness.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported Gate Agent opened main entry door despite given crossed arms sign and warning strap across window because of a pressurization warning light illuminated at the doors.
summary: A flight attendant at ZZZ reported that a ground agent cracked the aircraft door open while the crew was rearming due to a flashing pressure light. The agent claimed to see a thumbs-up signal despite the attendant giving an "X" signal and a red banner being visible, causing a four-minute delay before the Captain authorized door opening.

synopsis: M20 pilot reported diverting due to an alternator failure.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew experienced an overvoltage indication followed by a pop and smoke from the right glare shield. They advised ATC, shed non-essential loads, pulled the alternator circuit breaker, and landed safely on battery power with normal systems.

aircraft: Beechcraft Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
