The controller cleared the visual approach after the pilot declared the airport in sight, noting earlier communication could have prevented the alert.

synopsis: Center Controller reported a conflict between a firefighter aircraft in a fire TFR area and a small aircraft near the TFR.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a high-performance jet exiting a firefighting TFR and rapidly climbing to within 100 feet of a small VFR aircraft near the boundary. The controller issued a traffic alert after the jet, which was not on radar, nearly collided with the small aircraft that was receiving flight following.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer could not locate the Obstacle Takeoff Notes for 3 departure procedures from SEA.
summary: A pilot reported that Jeppesen SID pages for KSEA reference missing Takeoff Obstacle Notes pages with incorrect numbering. The pilot requested an amendment to the notes or provision of the correct Jeppesen pages to resolve the discrepancy.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported mis-communication issues with ramp crew during pushback.
summary: During pushback, the flight crew attempted to taxi after resolving a nosewheel steering issue, but a ground crew member connected a tug under the nose without establishing eye contact or verifying with the cockpit. The crew stopped the aircraft upon visual confirmation of the tug, highlighting a failure in ground-to-flight deck communication and visibility protocols.

synopsis: A pilot reported diverting due to an oil leak in one engine.
summary: The pilot diverted the aircraft due to a right engine oil leak causing pressure to drop from 30 to 12 psi, despite an initial zero quantity indication. Maintenance advised following procedures, but the pilot landed safely before mandatory shutdown was required over the Rockies.

synopsis: Pilot reported ATC instructing them to hold short of a runway due to a small aircraft landing on another runway. Pilot advised ATC unable to LAHSO but did so.
summary: The flight crew rejected a LAHSO clearance to hold short Runway 4L after landing on Runway 8L, citing prior notification to Approach. They manually braked to a stop just past Taxiway E, leaving approximately 1,000 feet of separation from Aircraft Y, which had sidestepped to Runway 4L.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported an unstable approach and requesting a 360 turn on final from Approach. Reporter cited lack of flying and distractions during the approach as contributing factors.
summary: Two pilots on a non-revenue flight into ZZZ violated sterile cockpit rules during a visual approach to Runway XL, causing the aircraft to become high and fast. The crew executed an approved 360-degree turn to re-establish a stable approach and landed safely, attributing the incident to distraction and complacency.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported possible GPS jamming resulted in loss of GPS and ADS-B.
summary: The flight crew experienced a GPS and ADS-B failure between UNEDA and NOKID, causing ANP to spike to 15.6 and loss of RNP capability. The crew suspects active GPS jamming or a system logic error, but the aircraft landed safely in Anchorage after signals normalized.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported aborting a takeoff roll when the tiller was accidentally bumped, causing the steering to disengage.
summary: The Captain, recently upgraded and feeling rusty, accidentally bumped the tiller while taking controls during takeoff acceleration, triggering a Steering Inop Master Caution. This caused an aborted takeoff; the crew reengaged steering to exit the runway but failed to call maintenance before deciding to continue the flight.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert from AUS Tower on approach to Runway 35R.
summary: The Pilot Flying descended below the published 2500 ft minimum for fix SSHOE after incorrectly setting 2100 ft in the FCU, prompting a Tower alert and Captain intervention. Subsequent wind shear reports triggered a go-around with a momentary flap over-speed warning, though maintenance found no mechanical fault.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that deferred maintenance items were not properly documented due to multiple distractions in the flight deck, including international COVID-19 screening protocols.
summary: Flight crew failed to transfer two Deferred Maintenance Items and log maintenance stickers at ZZZZ1 due to distractions from local quarantine authorities and mechanics removing the logbook. The crew realized the errors upon securing the aircraft at ZZZZ and attributed the oversight to external interruptions disrupting standard post-flight duties.

synopsis: Technician reported that policies and procedures are not consistent and difficult to follow during inspections of aircraft in short term storage.
summary: A mechanic reported inconsistencies between the All Fleets Maintenance Manual (AFMM) and fleet-specific manuals while performing pitot cover checks on Aircraft X. The mechanic noted the AFMM lacks FAA approval for logbook sign-offs and conflicts with approved disinfection procedures, urging regulatory clarification on its use.

synopsis: Technicians reported aircraft engine found damaged during shipping.
summary: During engine shipping, the engine shifted within its cradle and fell, causing damage. The reporter attributes this to vague preparation instructions lacking specific hardware diagrams and requiring multiple personnel for tasks assigned to a single signatory.

synopsis: GA pilot experienced a runway excursion while performing a rejected takeoff. Pilot reported confusion between the pilot and Tower Controller about whether the take-off clearance had been canceled.
summary: The pilot rejected a takeoff on Runway 06R due to difficult control in a tailwheel aircraft, causing a runway excursion. The pilot attributed the incident to an unacknowledged clearance cancellation and aggressive controller behavior, noting no visual stop signals were given.

synopsis: C182 Pilot reported a near mid air collision while on approach, which caused the other aircraft to take evasive action.
summary: A pilot flying a high-wing single-engine Cessna VFR at 2,900 ft MSL reported a near mid-air collision with an opposing aircraft that turned sharply left within 500 ft. The event occurred while the pilot was tuning radios for landing at ZZZ, and the other pilot appeared to turn to avoid the reporter's aircraft.

synopsis: Single pilot reported a NMAC with opposite direction landing traffic.
summary: The pilot executing a landing on Runway XX encountered a BT-13A landing in the opposite direction 300 feet ahead at 10 feet altitude. The pilot performed a go-around while the BT-13A pilot, who had not made radio calls, dove to the runway, bent his landing gear, and skidded on one wheel.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported calling on radio for traffic and attempting to depart in a 2 minute window, when an aircraft on final requested pilot to hold position, but ultimately had to go-around.
summary: The pilot departed Runway XX during a 2-minute IFR release window, cutting off an aircraft on short final that initiated a go-around. The incident resulted from the pilot's urgency to beat the void time and lack of confirmed traffic position, despite having limited recent flight experience.

synopsis: GA pilot reported inadvertently leaving the transponder code set from the previous flight. The pilot was accustomed to getting a code from the Tower, however the Tower had closed early due to COVID-19 hours and the pilot did not check the transponder.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft with an ADS-B transponder set to a previous flight's code instead of XXXX after departing ZZZ without flight following due to tower closure. The error resulted from habitually expecting a code at ZZZ and unfamiliarity with the new transponder, leading to an incomplete preflight electronics check.

synopsis: GA pilot reported experiencing an airborne conflict during departure having to take evasive action. Reporter cited an increase in traffic due to the lifting of stay at home restrictions as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot departed XXL and, while turning right to heading 230 at 2,500 feet, observed conflicting traffic on TCAS. To ensure separation, the pilot climbed to 3,000 feet before returning to 2,500 feet, with no further conflicts reported after handoff to ZZZ1 Departure.

synopsis: Pilot reported a loss of directional control that resulted in a runway excursion and damage to the aircraft.
summary: During landing rollout at 20 mph, the aircraft ground looped right after the left wing gained lift and the right main gear sank into soft pavement. The airplane entered a 6-foot drainage ditch at 10-15 mph, damaging the cowling and landing gear, but resulted in no injuries.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Private pilot encountered airport ground maintenance activity in vicinity of runway during landing.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 15 at ZZZ in 15-knot crosswinds failed to see two individuals mowing the runway edge until touchdown. The pilot continued the landing, passing the first mower and stopping before the second, resulting in no damage but highlighting the need for better runway scans.

synopsis: G280 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on descent into FTW 20 miles in trail of a B767 that resulted in an uncommanded 45 degree roll to the left.
summary: While descending on the WESAT2 arrival into FTW, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Boeing 767, causing a 45-degree left bank and autopilot disconnect. The pilot manually recovered the aircraft, accepted an offset from Fort Worth Center, and was cleared direct to COWTN to exit the event.

synopsis: C-172 Single Pilot reported a critical ground conflict while taxing across the runway with a aircraft executing a departure over the runway.
summary: The pilot held short of Runway XX while a tanker landed, then crossed the runway without hearing a Cessna Citation's departure clearance. The Citation flew low and gear-up over the taxiing aircraft, prompting the pilot to stop and acknowledge a failure to adequately scan for departing traffic.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a cabin fumes event during takeoff resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to ZZZ shortly after takeoff due to a strange cabin odor reported by flight attendants and a deadheading pilot. Maintenance suspected the cause was excessive disinfectant spray in the ventilation system, as no fire or smoke was found.

synopsis: Air carrier ground manager reported potentially hazardous practice of circumventing load planning established company procedures.
summary: The Shift Manager authorized a Load Planner to reopen the Departure Staging Guide (DSTG) by temporarily delaying the flight, circumventing safety policy. This action, driven by a belief that the policy lacks business sense, risks significant weight errors or catastrophic events.

synopsis: Air carrier Ground Personnel reported a parcel of cargo not loaded on board resulting in incorrect aircraft weight.
summary: Cargo Operations reported a 259lb item remained planeside, causing an inaccurate weight manifest and a FAR violation. The resulting 0.18% weight adjustment shifted the center of gravity from 29.4% to 29.0% MAC.

synopsis: Captain reported an uncommanded inflight engine shutdown after compressor stalls, causing a diversion and emergency landing.
summary: During descent into ZZZ, the crew heard a compressor stall noise followed by a number 1 engine failure. Due to thunderstorms at ZZZ, they diverted to ZZZ1, landed safely with fire and rescue escort, and briefed maintenance upon arrival.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reported that ATC instructed them to maintain greater than 250 kts. airspeed below 10,000 ft.
summary: A flight crew descended into ANC on the NEELL 6 arrival, exceeding the 250 kts. limit below 10,000 ft. due to a misunderstanding of ATC spacing instructions. The crew maintained high speed until 4,500 ft., believing ATC clearance overrode regulations, though the flight concluded normally.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported turbulence caused a loss of aircraft control, requiring evasive action to regain aircraft control.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and downdrafts while deviating 80 miles east-northeast around convective activity en route, causing AP2 to disengage and a rapid descent to 500 feet below the assigned 10,400 feet. The pilot manually arrested the descent, and the crew reported the event to ATC and maintenance upon arrival, noting that radar showed clearing heavy returns by over 40 miles.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant expressed multiple concerns regarding company COVID-19 protocols, including alternative jumpseat locations, social distancing in the flight deck, safety equipment demonstrations, and the wearing of protective masks.
summary: A flight attendant reported that FAA exemptions allowing crew to sit in passenger seats compromise safety by hindering communication and evacuation visibility. The reporter also argued that mandatory face coverings delay oxygen mask deployment during decompression and hinder safety demonstrations.

synopsis: Technician reported that Work Cards associated with the use of Biobor JL in aircraft fuel tanks during storage are missing critical information and should be revised.
summary: A technician reported that a task card for draining fuel tanks treated with Biobor JL lacked warnings for required PPE and specific disposal procedures. The reporter requested adding these cautions to the document to ensure safety and compliance.

synopsis: Technicians reported confusion over training related to prioritization of work requirements.
summary: An AMT reported conflicting instructions while assigned to return Aircraft X to service and complete mandatory training under threat of discipline. Management prioritized the aircraft maintenance, leaving the technician conflicted about balancing the two assignments and the potential disciplinary consequences.

synopsis: G-IV flight crew reported an air data computer failure and the arrival flown using standby instruments.
summary: During cruise at FL450, the crew experienced a DADC fault and miscompare, continuing with one unit until descent into ZZZZ. Discrepancies between the remaining DADC and standby instruments forced automation disengagement, resulting in a manual landing on Runway XX using standby instruments.

synopsis: Flight instructor reported there was no NOTAM for a runway closure at JAN airport.
summary: During a training session, a pilot and student searched Foreflight, EFB, and FAA FNS for a NOTAM closing Runway 34L/16R but found only an airport construction graphic. No textual NOTAM existed to confirm the runway closure, which the pilot identified as a critical flight safety issue.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Corporate pilot reported having an altitude deviation while hand-flying the aircraft and attributed it to lack of flying due to the COVID-19 slow down.
summary: The PIC experienced an altitude deviation while flying with autopilot off due to poor CRM and low recent flying from the COVID slowdown. The deviation was immediately reported to ATC and corrected.

synopsis: Private Pilot flying a Helicopter landed in a wilderness area by mistake.
summary: A newly certified helicopter pilot landed an Aircraft X on a gravel bar near Name1 Wilderness with family, intending to camp outside the boundary but potentially landing within it due to outdated navigation equipment. Two armed men confronted the group, forcing a high-power vertical takeoff to avoid them before the pilot departed the area.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Pilot flying failed to lower landing gear during landing maneuver.
summary: An experienced pilot conducting a VFR training flight with a passenger in an Aircraft X failed to extend the landing gear due to distraction and similar warning horn sounds, resulting in a propeller strike and underbelly damage upon touchdown. The pilot executed a go-around, extended the gear, and completed an uneventful second landing with no runway damage reported.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Controller reported using a configuration that did not show an airspace that was open. Controller thought airspace was closed and had an airspace violation.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to display open ZZZ airspace on their scope due to incorrect mid-shift configuration settings. This caused an inhibited auto-handoff for Aircraft X, resulting in the aircraft penetrating ZZZ airspace by one mile before the controller manually completed the transfer after being contacted by ZZZ.

synopsis: A TRACON Departure Controller reported a departing aircraft made an unusually shallow turn on departure and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing satellite sectors issued a heading change to a southbound jet after observing a shallow turn that risked violating the 2,200 ft MVA. The controller attributed the deviation to possible tower instructions or frequency congestion, noting that safe climb altitudes were unavailable due to surrounding VFR and IFR traffic.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying 737-800 aircraft encountered smoke and fumes in cabin after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced smoke and fumes during engine start and climb due to over-serviced hydraulic fluid entering the ventilation system. The crew returned to the airport after oxygen masks failed to allow communication, though the aircraft landed safely with no further smoke during taxi.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain forgot to do a SELCAL check and cited as contributing factors multiple tasks in a short period and having not flown in a long time.
summary: The Captain reported that during the oceanic cruise phase, the crew overlooked a required SELCAL check due to high workload, recent inactivity, and reliance on an uncheckable iPad checklist. The crew later completed the check with ZZ Radio, and the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: A pilot landing at a non towered airport reported initiating a go around due to opposite direction landing traffic not communicating on CTAF.
summary: The Pilot Flying executed a go-around on short final when an experimental jet pilot, low on fuel and scud running, failed to acknowledge traffic and lined up for a head-on landing on the opposite runway. The reporter attributes the incident to the other pilot's lack of airmanship, operating in IMC without qualification, and ignoring runway clearance.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew encountered extreme turbulence in cruise.
summary: The flight crew encountered extreme wind shear and turbulence at FL300 west of ZZZZZ, causing autopilot disconnects, stick shaker activations, and an inability to maintain altitude. After descending to FL280 with ATC approval, the aircraft stabilized in moderate turbulence with winds decreasing from 270/125 to 270/65.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported poor taxiway signage and paint, insufficient lighting and an unfamiliar taxi route caused them to miss a turn onto a taxiway at LFPG airport.
summary: The flight crew misidentified Taxiway D as B while taxiing an unfamiliar route at LFPG due to poor signage and construction. The Captain stopped the aircraft short of the intersection, contacted Ground Control for revised clearance, and safely resumed taxiing without an incursion.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain had an airspeed deviation and cited being rusty due lack of flying as contributing.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ oversped to 265 knots while leveling at 6,000 feet after releasing throttles to scan for traffic. The pilot attributed the incident to underestimating their rustiness from low recent flight time and plans to rely more on the flight director.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a series of miscommunications regarding a boarding passenger who was possibly contagious with COVID-19. After the Captain spent time resolving the issue, it was determined that the passenger could be allowed to board.
summary: The captain and flight attendants experienced confusion regarding a passenger's mask refusal, medical condition, and alleged disruptive behavior at the gate. After verifying with MedLink and the station manager that the passenger was cleared and cooperative, the crew resolved their concerns and allowed the passenger to board.

synopsis: E175 Captain reported airspeed and altitude excursions after encountering severe turbulence on descent into OKC.
summary: The pilot encountered possible severe turbulence during descent into OKC, resulting in a momentary 700-foot altitude loss and airspeed fluctuations of ±15 knots. The event was reported out of an abundance of caution as the severity was borderline.

synopsis: E175 Captain reported an NMAC with a small private jet on descent into PHX.
summary: During descent on the BRUSR arrival into PHX, the pilot encountered a private jet climbing within 500 feet while descending through 13,000 feet. The pilot manually leveled off to comply with a TCAS RA, but ATC issued conflicting descent instructions and ignored the crew's reports of the active resolution advisory.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported not recognizing until cruise that the transponder was set incorrectly. Captain recommended that crews visually confirm checklist items since many pilots are flying infrequently due to COVID-19 reductions in travel demands.
summary: The First Officer discovered the transponder was set to ALT instead of TA/RA during cruise on a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1. The crew corrected the setting, attributing the error to the Captain's failure to visually confirm the item during the pre-takeoff checklist due to reduced flying proficiency.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported interacting with a sick passenger in flight who was possibly exhibiting COVID-19 symptoms.
summary: A flight attendant assisted a passenger experiencing severe airsickness and vomiting during the cruise phase of a flight. The crew contacted ground EMTs upon landing, and the airline confirmed the attendant would retain pay if testing positive for COVID-19 due to the reported exposure.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported forgetting to notify other FAs that the AFT doors were disarmed. Flight Attendant stated not having been in an airplane for an extended time due to the COVID-19 pandemic contributed to the event.
summary: The A FA on an arrival flight disarmed the L1 and R1 doors but forgot to inform the AFT crew, causing them to relay the status via interphone. The reporter attributes this error to inexperience with the aircraft type and a two-month absence from flying.

synopsis: Flight Instructor flying PA-44 Aircraft encountered engine fire during engine start.
summary: During a retraining flight, the crew encountered a left engine hot start failure followed by smoke and flames from the cowl flap area. The pilot shut down the right engine, evacuated the aircraft, and extinguished the fire using a fire extinguisher.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C-525 Captain reported a runway excursion during landing rollout due to right brake failure.
summary: During rollout on a visual approach to Runway XX at ZZZ, the pilot reported right brake failure causing a left swerve. The aircraft departed the runway left using emergency brakes, stopping 6-10 feet off the edge with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Flight Instructor flying a C-172 aircraft encountered engine power reduction after go-around.
summary: During a simulated engine failure training flight, the pilot experienced sudden power loss and strong vibrations above 900 feet. The aircraft landed safely at ZZZ, but the engine exhibited severe vibrations at low RPM, leading to a shutdown and pushback while the airport was NOTAM'd closed.

synopsis: Pilot reported that after checking in on Center frequency, no response was received for some time. The pilot delayed locating an alternative frequency due to the quiet frequencies that have become prevalent during COVID-19 reduction in air traffic volume.
summary: Pilots on an IFR ferry flight at FL390 failed to contact XYY.ZA after a handoff, likely due to an incorrect frequency transfer or low traffic volume. They reestablished contact with ZZZ Center using the charted frequency without traffic conflicts or ATC queries.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain of a corporate jet reported a TFR violation occurred in part because their XM subscription had expired.
summary: The pilot departed VFR from SJT after ATC closed and inadvertently entered a TFR due to expired XM data, fatigue, and complacency. Corrective action cleared the TFR in under 20 seconds, though the crew noted prior ATC permission for other aircraft to transit the area.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported seeing and following a set of horizontal lights which appeared to be PAPI between two parallel runways at PHL. On short final, the crew determined these were not PAPI lights and they gave the misperception of being on a valid glide path.
summary: The flight crew conducted a visual approach to Runway 9L at PHL in darkness, where horizontal red and white lights on an airport structure between runways mimicked PAPIs. This misleading visual cue caused glide path confusion, resulting in a slightly high approach that required a small correction for a safe landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier Ground Personnel reported that several Dangerous Goods shipments were not documented correctly on the manifest.
summary: Ground agents failed to manifest two dangerous goods shipments on Aircraft X due to unfamiliarity with the capture process and tight lockout times. The Captain remained unaware of the unmanifested cargo, which was loaded and departed before the error was corrected.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that Tower instructed them to abort the takeoff roll which was requested by the ARTCC facility due to traffic and staffing issues and could not yet accept the flight into their airspace.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff on Runway XXR at approximately 95 knots after ATC requested cancellation due to ZZZ Center staffing saturation. This resulted in a 30-minute delay, excessive brake and tire wear, and required a 20-minute hold for brake cooling.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported an NMAC event under ATC control during arrival.
summary: During the transition from Center to MCO approach on the BAIRN4 arrival, the crew received a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to uncoordinated VFR traffic at FL105. The pilot attributed the 400-foot separation and required evasive maneuver to a lack of coordination between MIA and MCO controllers.

synopsis: Technician reported aircraft engines were operated without oil during preservation for aircraft storage.
summary: A mechanic signed off a task card for draining oil on Aircraft X without tagging the cockpit or draining the tanks, leading to an engine run with no oil in either engine or gearboxes. The reporter states this documentation error caused potential internal damage, rendering the engines unsafe for continued operation without verified run data.

synopsis: Private pilot flying PA-28 aircraft encountered nose gear failure during landing rollout.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced a sudden nose-gear mechanical failure during the rollout of a full-stop landing on RWY XXR. The gear collapsed, causing the propeller to strike the ground, but both occupants safely exited the aircraft after performing emergency shutdowns.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft attempting to land on the wrong runway resulting in another aircraft executing a go-around.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a student trainer aircraft for Runway X, but the pilot landed on Runway Y, likely due to expectation bias from recent flight school changes. The controller issued a go-around and re-cleared the aircraft for Runway X, resolving the conflict with pattern traffic without incident.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict and attributed it to staffing levels due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Satellite sector issued a divergent heading to resolve a conflict between a VFR aircraft with an alternator issue and an arrival at 5,000 feet. The controller attributed the error to high workload, reduced staffing, and communication challenges across multiple frequencies.

synopsis: ZJX Center Controller reported the data tags for two aircraft with similar callsigns acquired on the wrong target and the flight plans were not accurate.
summary: An air traffic controller experienced automation issues where Aircraft X and Y were tagged incorrectly due to wrong flight plans. Aircraft X, actually departing a different airport in ZMA airspace, was climbed to 26,000 feet and handed off after the controller identified the data block errors.

synopsis: ZKC Center Controller reported that an aircraft with no transponder caused a NMAC.
summary: An air traffic controller managing high and low altitude sectors reported a near miss between Aircraft X at 5,500 feet and an Air Tractor at 5,400 feet. The controller attributed the difficulty in detecting the untransponder-equipped Air Tractor to weak primary radar returns and recommended transponder use for better visibility.

synopsis: A Tower Local Control trainee reported an aircraft reported sighting a drone in the Tower airspace.
summary: A pilot reported a possible UAS near the runway threshold during short final, prompting a controller to advise a following P28A and divert both aircraft to a different runway. The delay in notifying authorities stemmed from attempts to visually confirm the sighting before police investigation.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported he had inadvertently pushed the thrust levers into detent setting on takeoff, which was not recognized until reaching cruise flight.
summary: The Pilot Flying inadvertently left thrust levers in the takeoff detent during departure, resulting in TO-1 thrust persisting until cruise. The error, attributed to mental fatigue and high workload, was corrected after the crew identified the discrepancy during the cruise checklist.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported re-routing issues associated with the deferral of a flight's CPDLC system.
summary: A dispatcher cleared Flight AB to defer a CPDLC malfunction after misinterpreting NOTAMs and failing to identify RNP4 airway restrictions due to time pressure and working alone. The error was discovered the next day, prompting a recommendation to reset CPDLC circuit breakers rather than deferring the equipment.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having to remove a passenger showing symptoms of illness.
summary: The Captain removed a visibly ill, disoriented passenger after the forward door closed because the CSM failed to screen the passenger or brief the crew. The incident resulted from poor gate screening and a lack of communication, forcing the Captain to act to ensure the safety of the crew and other passengers.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain described a near-collision on the ramp when a Citation was not properly secured at shutdown and began to roll toward them.
summary: A Citation Sovereign crew taxiing on a sloped ramp turned rapidly near a fuel truck and Phenom 300, then rolled back 30 feet toward them. A line person and the Citation pilot stopped the aircraft with chocks, narrowly avoiding a collision and injury due to the Citation's unsafe speed and the ramp layout.

synopsis: EMB-135LR First officer reported an NMAC event during arrival.
summary: The flight crew at 13,000 feet received an aural traffic alert and a climb Resolution Advisory while 8 miles from ZZZZZ. They climbed to 13,300 feet to avoid traffic 400 feet below, then descended back to 13,000 feet after being cleared.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an unstabilized approach resulting in a go-around.
summary: A low-time First Officer flying a visual approach to Runway X became unstable due to excessive speed at 1,000 feet AFE after delaying configuration. The Captain initiated a go-around, and the crew subsequently completed a stable landing after receiving vectors.

synopsis: EMB Captain reported Tower advised of a track deviation on ILS approach to IAH.
summary: The pilot hand-flew an ILS 8R approach at IAH due to a fluctuating localizer and received a Tower override to turn left for being south of course. The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft, attributed to the off-course deviation, and completed the landing after switching to magenta needles.

synopsis: Challenger 350 Captain reported losing N1 in the number 2 engine, resulting in a HMU [Hydro Mechanical Unit] failure in the engine.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the flight crew experienced right engine N1 fluctuations and a subsequent thrust drop to 70% with yaw, attributed to a HMU failure. The crew descended to FL310 and diverted to ZZZ1, landing uneventfully after receiving FADEC and engine fault messages.

synopsis: Flight crew reported missing a crossing restriction during approach.
summary: The pilot monitoring and pilot flying missed the mandatory 1,500-foot crossing altitude at ZZZZZ while on an ILS X approach to ZZZ. The error resulted from complacency due to light traffic and visual conditions, expectation bias regarding the clearance, and an incomplete approach briefing.

synopsis: Challenger 350 flight crew reported a life raft inflated while at cruise and having to divert.
summary: During cruise at FL450, an uncommanded life raft inflation broke its cabinet, prompting a descent to 11,000 feet and diversion to ZZZ. The crew contained the deployment, landed safely with no injuries, and attributed the cause to a possible faulty valve or unknown malfunction.

synopsis: Pilot reported getting the run around from Maintenance and eventually getting the problem resolved.
summary: The Captain and First Officer discovered a broken main deck lock in position 5R was withheld by ground handlers and Local Maintenance before departure. The crew challenged this non-disclosure, reviewed the MEL, and forced the defect to be properly deferred before the flight.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying CRJ-200 aircraft encountered a Near Mid Air collision with a Cessna aircraft.
summary: A departing crew from ZZZ received a TCAS Resolution Advisory after ATC instructed a right turn toward a non-communicating Cessna. The pilots executed a climb to avoid the conflict, noting the Cessna was 300–400 feet below, and attributed the incident to the GA aircraft's lack of radio contact and conflicting ATC instructions.

synopsis: Pilot reported being on the incorrect frequency and thinking it was odd that no other aircraft were heard while landing.
summary: The pilot flying Aircraft X on a GPS approach to ZZZ1 mistakenly contacted the UNICOM frequency instead of Tower due to missing clearance instructions. The pilot landed without communication, later identified the correct Tower frequency, and completed a return flight to ZZZ2 without incident.

synopsis: Pilot reported a communication issue resulted in an altitude deviation.
summary: Pilots enroute at 14,000 feet climbed to FL270 after hearing a clearance from Center, but ATC later instructed a descent stating they were not cleared. The crew suspected the clearance was intended for another aircraft with a similar call sign due to controllers managing multiple sectors during reduced traffic.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported an NMAC while in the traffic pattern at FA44 with an aircraft transiting through the pattern. Instructor noted that traffic from a nearby airport frequently transit through FA44 traffic pattern posing a recurring risk of mid-air collision.
summary: A glider instructor and student encountered a Cessna 172 at 1,000 feet MSL while climbing from Willis Gliderport (FA44). The near-mid-air collision occurred because the Cessna transited the pattern without monitoring Willis UNICOM, a recurring hazard caused by Lantana training aircraft using the airport as a waypoint.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 First Officer reported NMAC with opposite direction landing traffic.
summary: A MEDEVAC pilot departing VFR from an uncontrolled field executed an evasive turn east after a wrong-way practice approach aircraft failed to break off despite radio warnings. The near-miss occurred because the inbound aircraft continued descending on a collision course while the MEDEVAC flight was past V1.

synopsis: Cirrus SR22 pilot reported after departure their door became unlocked and that this was a recurring problem.
summary: The pilot of a 2015 Cirrus SR22 aborted takeoff after discovering the pilot's door top latch was unlocked, landing to secure it. The pilot attributes the recurring issue to improper repairs by the service center and believes the defect is not unique to this aircraft.

synopsis: Pilot reported experiencing a loss of alternator.
summary: A pilot experienced alternator failure during a CPL training climb from ZZZ, which recurred after flap retraction on the return leg. The flight continued with radios and transponder off to conserve battery, using GPS for separation, and landed safely; a separate panel tear was found unrelated to the electrical issue.

synopsis: Pilot reported a critical ground conflict that resulted in a prop strike.
summary: A tailwheel biplane pilot taxiing on Taxiway X nosed over after braking to avoid a head-on collision with Aircraft Y, which entered the taxiway from a hangar without radio communication. The incident resulted in propeller damage and engine stoppage, with the reporter attributing the near-collision to Aircraft Y's failure to announce position or check for traffic.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported confusion between company published departure procedure and Jeppsen chart.
summary: The flight crew at ALB identified a discrepancy between Jepp and ACARS data regarding minimum clean-up altitudes for Runway 28. They elected to use the higher Jepp altitude for safety, later discovering that ACARS data should have been prioritized per company guidance.

synopsis: B737 pilot reported diverting due to an engine failure.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring on a Boeing 737 experienced a number one engine failure during descent while deviating around weather. They secured the engine, diverted to a clear airport due to thunderstorms at the original destination, and completed a successful single-engine hand-flown landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported concerns with wearing masks during pre-flight crew briefings.
summary: The pilot reported that wearing a face mask during the pre-flight crew briefing compromised safety by preventing the assessment of facial expressions and reducing the session to a lecture. Consequently, the lead flight attendant asked questions already covered, indicating the briefing was ineffective and degraded crew collaboration.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported inconsistent use of masks per guidelines by crewmembers.
summary: A pilot reported that four crewmembers intentionally violated company mask policies during a five-day trip, including on deadhead and working legs. One crewmember was detained by the CDC for 30 minutes, and the pilot noted widespread non-compliance among uniformed pilots at the return airport.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported concerns with re-qualification training courses after not flying due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: A pilot with over X years of experience reported that re-qualification training for returning to the X/Y fleet after long absences is unsafe and inadequate. The reporter argues that current short courses fail to restore necessary proficiency, risking incidents due to insufficient simulator time and lack of full qualification for pilots off the fleet for more than two years.

synopsis: Captain reported taxiway crossing MCO Runway 17R is very rough and should be noted in charting.
summary: The pilot reported that the taxiway surface is very rough, particularly when expediting across runway 17R. They recommended adding a note to the taxi chart to proceed extra slow to prevent issues when expediting for 17R traffic.

synopsis: Captain reported receiving a dispatch message during cruise of unreported dangerous goods onboard.
summary: The flight crew received a dispatch message two hours into the flight identifying dangerous goods on board, contradicting a pre-push notification stating no dangerous goods were planned for the flight.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported rejecting a takeoff in response to multiple warning lights. The aircraft had been in storage and anti-ice circuit breakers had been collared and not removed by Maintenance prior to flight.
summary: The Captain and First Officer missed collared probe heater circuit breakers during preflight due to interruptions and normalization of deviation regarding a faulty panel. They rejected the takeoff at 30 knots after a Master Caution illuminated, returned to the gate, and discovered the maintenance error before resuming flight.

synopsis: All cabin and flight Crew left airplane with cleaning crew still on board.
summary: A flight attendant and ramp agent assisted a passenger with a rolling walker while the sanitizing crew cleaned the aircraft. The flight crew deplaned before sanitization was complete due to a lack of awareness regarding the required sequence, though all personnel exited safely.

synopsis: Air carrier Maintenance employee reported adverse health symptoms after exposure to an aircraft just cleaned using electrostatic spraying.
summary: A crew member on Aircraft X experienced choking, gagging, and shortness of breath after electrostatic cleaning was performed by a small crew using filtered masks. The reporter attributes these health effects to unknown chemicals used during the cleaning process and expresses concern for the safety of employees and passengers.

synopsis: Lead Aircraft Technician reported an aircraft in storage had both engines run with no oil in either the main oil tank or accessory gearbox.
summary: A lead AMT reported that Aircraft X's #1 and #2 engines were run during preservation maintenance with empty oil tanks and drained accessory gearboxes. The technician concluded this caused undetermined heat damage to bearings, rendering the engines potentially unserviceable and deeming further proving runs dangerous and unsupported by manuals.

synopsis: A GA pilot reported his feet became stuck in the rudder pedals causing a runway excursion during takeoff.
summary: The pilot aborted take-off and exited the runway due to jammed rudder pedals caused by inappropriate footwear. The incident did not meet Part 830 reporting requirements.

synopsis: Bonanza 36 pilot reported momentary loss of aircraft control during landing resulting in wing tip ground contact.
summary: During a practice engine-out landing with a curved final approach, a gust caused the pilot's left wing to scrape the runway, resulting in minor cosmetic damage. The pilot executed a go-around, and an A&P mechanic confirmed the aircraft remained airworthy despite the dent.

synopsis: Luscombe Pilot reported loss of directional control during landing resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot experienced a runway excursion on short final to Runway XXR due to a wind shift to a quartering tailwind causing a left veer. Regaining control by lowering the tail wheel allowed a safe stop in the grass without damage to the aircraft or property.

synopsis: Cessna P210 pilot reported some damage resulted from an off-field landing following inflight engine failure.
summary: The pilot experienced a total engine failure during the VFR pattern approach while reducing power at 80 knots IAS. Suspecting high altitude and mixture issues caused the quit, the pilot executed an obstacle avoidance maneuver that resulted in a right wing strike on a steel pole during landing.

synopsis: Piper Warrior pilot reported loss of control of aircraft during touchdown due to a wind gust.
summary: During landing on Runway XX at ZZZ, a left gust caused the aircraft to swerve, prompting the pilot to intentionally stop in the grass at the intersection with Taxiway XX to avoid damage. ARF assisted in pushing the aircraft back, and subsequent inspections of the plane, runway, and grass revealed no damage or leakage.

synopsis: PA-32 pilot reported landing safely after loss of all electrical power.
summary: The pilot experienced total avionics and electrical failure shortly after departure, forcing a diversion to a non-towered airport where landing gear status could not be verified. After contacting the tower via mobile phone, the pilot received a light gun clearance to land following a visual gear check by ATC.

synopsis: GA pilot experienced an airspace incursion while returning from a practice flight. Pilot reported not being fully prepared for the flight and had not flown lately due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: A pilot conducting a currency flight in a general aviation aircraft became disoriented during night maneuvers and returned to ZZZ. The pilot attributed the incident to poor night vision protection, inadequate aircraft setup, and unintentionally entering ZZZ Class D airspace without communication.

synopsis: Cirrus SR20 pilot reported receiving a traffic advisory from ATC, locating traffic and descending approximately 400 feet to the avoid conflicting traffic.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight at 5,000 feet MSL reported a potential conflict with a VFR aircraft at 5,400 feet. After ATC advised of convergence, the pilot descended to 4,600–4,700 feet to avoid the traffic.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported they allowed an aircraft to fly below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller assigned Aircraft X to 12,000 feet, causing it to descend below the 12,700-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude (MVA) over a mountain ridge. The controller admitted the error resulted from a 15-degree turn that failed to clear terrain, attributing the incident to returning from leave without reviewing the airspace.

synopsis: Flight Crew operated 737-700 aircraft in violation of Minimum Equipment List restrictions.
summary: The Captain and Dispatch added tanker fuel despite a deferred #2 thrust reverser under MEL 78-1-01, which prohibits such fueling. The Captain failed to identify this conflict, though the flight proceeded safely with good weather and no performance issues.

synopsis: MD11 pilot reported oil issue in number two engine. Aircraft was diverted to check on problem.
summary: The flight crew diverted Flight ABC to ZZZZ due to a dropping #2 engine oil quantity, which fell from 9 to 3 quarts during descent and landing. They shut down the engine immediately after touchdown to prevent damage, citing vague AOM guidance and the risk of an in-flight shutdown over mountains as the cause for the precautionary landing.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported while taxiing to gate Ramp advised them of fire on the number 1 engine.
summary: During landing rollout on Runway XXL, Engine #1 rolled back and shut down. Although no cockpit fire warnings appeared, Ramp Tower reported a tail pipe fire, prompting the crew to discharge both fire bottles before being towed to the gate.

synopsis: E175 Captain reported the aircraft was damaged when the jetway was pulled away with the external air conditioning hose still attached.
summary: The flight crew reported that a jetway moved rearward while the PCA hose remained connected, ripping the external air intake manifold from the aircraft. The incident occurred because ramp agents failed to disconnect the hose before moving the jetway, despite the crew's attempts to signal them.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that another Flight Attendant refused to wear a mask during boarding and throughout the flight. Reporter expressed concern that the health of passengers and other cabin crew were put at risk.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a Flight Attendant refused to wear a mask during boarding, citing personal beliefs. This non-compliance created an uncomfortable work environment and increased health risks for the crew and passengers throughout the flight.

synopsis: Light sport aircraft pilots reported a loss of directional control resulting in runway excursion and damage to the landing gear.
summary: During a touch-and-go training flight, the aircraft veered right immediately after touchdown despite pilot corrective inputs, forcing an evacuation onto the grass. The crew reported the landing gear was completely gone, though no injuries or airport damage occurred.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported on the takeoff roll the aircraft's left engine failed and the instructor initiated an RTO.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced a left engine failure during a touch-and-go takeoff on Runway XX. The crew aborted the takeoff, exited to Taxiway XX, and attributed the failure to heat after the engine restarted an hour later.

synopsis: EUG TRACON Controller working a radar sector reported one aircraft descended below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude and another flew off course into confliction with a VFR aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller descended Aircraft X below the 8,700-foot MVA while assisting with a TFR, prompting a climb instruction and IFR cancellation. Later, Aircraft Y deviated from its RNAV departure toward a VFR aircraft, requiring a stop and course correction after the controller missed the initial altitude verification.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Small Transport pilot reported a passenger medical situation inflight.
summary: During cruise, a passenger suffered a medical emergency involving uncontrollable cramping and loss of consciousness, prompting a diversion to ZZZ2. Due to a communications blackout, the crew relayed the emergency via another aircraft, landed safely, and transferred the passenger to paramedics while logging maintenance for soiled seats.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported forgetting to turn on the probe heat and stated lack of flying was a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot forgot to activate probe heats during the taxi checklist flow, leaving them off for the entire 13,000-foot VFR flight. The error occurred due to rustiness after a three-month absence from flying and insufficient pre-flight review of standard operating procedures.

synopsis: Technician reported overlooking the axle sleeve being removed with the old tire and wheel assembly and not reinstalled, causing repetitive damage to the aircraft at other stations.
summary: A mechanic replacing tires on an MD-11 in ZZZ2 failed to inspect the axle sleeve, allowing it to remain with the old tire. This caused subsequent anti-skid transducer damage and a broken hubcap at ZZZ1, where the missing sleeve was later discovered.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported an airborne conflict with an aircraft that was not on correct frequency.
summary: During a Part 91 training flight in the traffic pattern, the instructor and student executed a go-around after another pilot overshot a turn and aligned with their runway. The other pilot, who was high and fast, admitted he never saw them and had used an incorrect frequency due to tower closure confusion.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported loss of directional control during landing rollout due to high crosswind gust resulting in a ground contact.
summary: The solo pilot of Aircraft X experienced a ground incident while taxiing at ZZZ after landing in strong crosswinds. A 48-knot gust lifted the tail, causing the propeller and left wing to strike the ground, resulting in engine failure and the aircraft spinning into the gravel.

synopsis: BK117 Captain reported temporary loss of aircraft control during flight over mountainous terrain in turbulent weather.
summary: The pilot of a BK117 helicopter experienced a severe pitch-down and roll during a descent in mountainous terrain, attributed to retreating blade stall caused by high altitude, heat, and wind shear. The crew recovered the aircraft, received a Mast Moment Exceed caution, and diverted to land after realizing they were in Class B airspace.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an airframe overspeed in cruise that likely resulted from the autothrust not being engaged during takeoff. Captain noted that the failure to see the FMA indications resulted from a lack of proficiency and recency of flying.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced an airframe overspeed at FL300 due to autothrust failure to engage and a failure to monitor FMA indications after level-off. The crew corrected the speed by manually reducing thrust and deploying speed brakes, attributing the error to distraction and lack of proficiency following a seven-week absence.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported a cargo fire warning and returning to departure airport.
summary: The crew returned to ZZZ after a main cargo deck fire warning at FL350, landing overweight on Runway XX following a false left engine indication. Post-landing, brake heat blew four fuse plugs, while ground inspections confirmed no actual fire or smoke.

synopsis: MD-11 First Officer reported nil braking action during landing rollout on a wet runway.
summary: The crew landed on a wet, ungrooved runway using flaps 50 but experienced severe hydroplaning and braking degradation near the intersection with another runway. Unable to exit or turn due to runway lights and width constraints, they stopped at an angle and were towed to the gate without aircraft damage.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew experienced a high work load during an approach which resulted in unstable approach and a missed approach. The crew cited lack of experience and recent flying as contributing.
summary: A captain with two months of inactivity and an inexperienced first officer became task-saturated during rapid RNAV approach vectors at ZZZZ due to ATC language barriers and weather. They executed a go-around for an unstable approach but landed safely on a subsequent attempt.

synopsis: Air carrier Mechanic reported that wearing a mask and safety glasses causes the glasses to fog up, resulting in safety concerns when working on ladders, lifts, and in tight places. Mechanic also expressed concern that while working with chemicals, they could inadvertently be transferred to the mask.
summary: A mechanic reported that wearing a mask and safety glasses while working on ladders, lifts, or in tight spaces caused fogging, blinding them during tasks like pinning cannon plugs or handling Skydrol. The reporter concluded that current PPE practices jeopardize safety and recommended re-evaluating OSHA compliance to prevent accidents caused by impaired vision.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported engine malfunctioning and having to make a 180 turn back to the airport to land safely.
summary: During a touch-and-go in a Cessna 172S, the instructor and student experienced sudden RPM fluctuations and power loss shortly after liftoff. The instructor executed a 180-degree turn to land safely on the opposite runway, attributing the event to an unexplained engine issue rather than the suspected magneto timing.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported a critical ground conflict during landing with an overflying aircraft attempting to land on same runway.
summary: A pilot on left traffic for Runway XX at ZZZ was overtaken from above by a Cessna cleared as third in line, likely due to the Cessna mistaking the pilot for the Cherokee ahead. The Cessna executed a go-around before touchdown, while the pilot noted that TCAS might have prevented the conflict.

synopsis: Small aircraft instructor pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern.
summary: A Piper Malibu pilot misinterpreted ATC sequencing at ZZZ and cut off a PA-28 Archer on final approach, forcing the Archer pilot to execute an emergency avoidance maneuver. The near-miss resulted from the Malibu pilot's poor situational awareness and ambiguous tower instructions regarding landing order.

synopsis: Helicopter instructor reported an NMAC during takeoff with another helicopter.
summary: A pilot and student executing an RNAV departure from a ramp hover encountered a news helicopter crossing at the same altitude. The student performed a quick stop to avoid a collision, which the pilot attributed to a lack of Tower communication regarding the conflicting departure clearances.

synopsis: PA-32 Pilot reported possible airspace violation due to GPS failure.
summary: A VFR pilot entered Class D airspace due to a GPS antenna wiring failure that caused signal loss and outdated position data. The pilot corrected the loose connection and concluded that equipment failure caused the conflict, recommending backup navigation or IFR operations to prevent recurrence.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: MHW Tower controllers reported a departing aircraft notified them they took off over a vehicle which was on the runway.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a takeoff clearance to Aircraft X, which departed after a construction vehicle crossed the active runway without permission. The controller attributed the incident to a breakdown in construction team procedures and recommended replacing the single point of contact with dual radio-equipped personnel.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported the First Officer descended below glidepath below the ATC Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: During a visual approach, the First Officer dialed 7000 feet and selected Level Change, causing the aircraft to descend below the glidepath. Approach subsequently advised the crew they were below minimum vectoring altitude.

synopsis: A319 pilot reported an oil leak on departure caused them to shut down an engine and return for a landing.
summary: During departure climb, the First Officer reported decreasing right engine oil quantity, which reached zero and triggered an ENG 2 OIL LOW PR warning. The crew followed SOPs to shut down the right engine, diverted, and landed safely due to an oil leak.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying 737-700 aircraft delays departure due to reported inbound Beech 1900 aircraft.
summary: The pilot at ZZZ delayed departure for 30 minutes due to uncertainty about a Beech 1900 that had canceled IFR to ZZZ but was not communicating or visible on radar. The delay ended after Center confirmed the aircraft had diverted VFR to a different airport, resolving the potential collision risk.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing a low speed buffet alert during cruise due to having the aircraft in the incorrect configuration with autothrottles not engaged. Lack of flying was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The Captain forgot to re-engage autothrottles after disconnecting them to trim the aircraft in cruise at FL340. This caused low-speed buffet alerts in turbulence, requiring a descent to FL320 for recovery, attributed to pilot complacency after returning from leave.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a taxiway incursion partially due to expectation bias.
summary: The pilot taxied without a clearance after mishearing the tower's instruction to contact ground as a taxi authorization. The error resulted from expectation bias due to recent non-standard combined frequency operations during reduced pandemic activity.

synopsis: CL-300 First Officer reported an uneventful diversion after attempting two weather challenging mountainous airport approaches.
summary: A CL-300 First Officer diverted after severe turbulence and wind shear on mountainous approaches to ZZZ and ZZZ1 caused a stall warning and loss of airspeed despite good ground weather. The crew executed a go-around, deviated from the missed approach to avoid turbulence, and landed safely at ZZZ2, attributing the event to localized mountain wind conditions.

synopsis: Pilot reported clearance was different than what they had filed and would like to see HPN ATC Facilities re-open.
summary: The SIC reported that ATC issued a clearance to a fix not on the filed flight plan, causing a routing discrepancy. The crew queried ATC, received a heading to correct the FMS, and proceeded to the destination after verifying the updated routing.

synopsis: B-777 Captain reported a dangerous situation as related to the carriage of DG [Dangerous Goods] due primarily to a communication breakdown between flight crew and Dispatch/DG Specialist.
summary: The flight crew encountered a Dangerous Goods manifest error requiring both forward and aft cargo air conditioning for dry ice, compounded by poor coordination between the DG specialist and Operations. The crew resolved the discrepancy by consulting Operations, adjusting fuel flow, and activating both systems to ensure safety despite the confusing documentation.

synopsis: Pilot reported a taxiway incursion and cited being off for a month and a half as a contributing factor.
summary: A pilot returning after a month and a half off received conflicting taxi instructions to join runway B via taxiway A instead of G. The crew side-stepped to B on A, highlighting the need to use direct routes or request clarification when unsure.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported loss of directional control during takeoff roll.
summary: During takeoff roll on Runway 22, the First Officer lost directional control when the aircraft veered hard left despite right rudder input, causing it to slide off onto the grass. The First Officer attributed the incident to a potential steering actuator failure or incorrect engine spool-up.

synopsis: CE-750 flight crew reported an NMAC event during cruise.
summary: The flight crew received a climb Resolution Advisory during cruise and climbed to 8,500 feet before descending to 8,000 feet. The event resulted in a minimum separation of 300 feet, which the reporter noted is difficult to prevent.

synopsis: Pilot reported communications issues due to Tower Controller working multiple positions on same frequency due to facility staffing issues.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that minimum manning forced the use of a single frequency for Tower, Ground, and Clearance Delivery. When four aircraft were present, radio garbling caused confusion and resulted in unsure landing clearances.

synopsis: Pilot reported while on a sightseeing trip they went too low, pilot eventually caught the mistake and climbed back to a normal altitude.
summary: The pilot, an experienced CFII, descended below the cleared 1,000 feet MSL to 650 feet MSL during a sightseeing photo flight due to lost situational awareness from infrequent flying. He immediately climbed back to altitude, noting no danger of ground impact but acknowledging a violation of FAR 91.119(b).

synopsis: Pilot instructor and student reported distraction in the cockpit resulted in executing a touch and go without ATC clearance and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: During an IFR instrument training flight, the instructor and student misinterpreted a landing clearance as a touch-and-go due to expectation bias and high workload while coaching autopilot use. They executed a touch-and-go instead of a full stop, requiring a subsequent correction from Tower after becoming airborne.

synopsis: Pilot reported an alleged airspace violation while being under flight following and handed off to a Tower by Approach Control. Reportedly, Tower Controller was working numerous frequencies/positions and advised pilot that he had violated the Class Delta airspace.
summary: The pilot entered ZZZ Class D airspace while attempting to contact an understaffed Tower operator handling both Ground and Tower duties. The pilot attributes the incident to the operator's workload preventing timely contact, though the pilot also plans to verify contact before entering controlled airspace in the future.

synopsis: Mooney M20 pilot reported the landing gear collapsed after landing.
summary: After touchdown and braking, the aircraft skid and the left main gear collapsed on the taxiway. The crew shut down the airplane and deplaned passengers safely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a high-wing aircraft experienced a near-miss with a low-wing aircraft while descending from downwind to base at ZZZ Airport. The other aircraft passed 150 feet above and 100 feet ahead, likely due to entering the pattern behind the reporting aircraft without being seen or heard.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported flying too low to the ground on a visual approach to HLM airport.
summary: The pilot reported a lower-than-normal approach to HLM RWY 23 caused by extremely faded and confusing displaced threshold markings. This inability to identify the proper runway markings resulted in inadequate clearance over trees and a house during the steep approach.

synopsis: Pilot reported being rusty after lack of flying due to the COVID-19 pandemic resulting in communication issues with ATC.
summary: A pilot returning from leave taxied and took off on Runway XXR, admitting to setting an incorrect transponder code and miscommunicating altitude to Tower while climbing to 1,000 MSL. The pilot attributed these errors to being rusty after a long absence and resolved to double-check preflights and communications.

synopsis: UAV pilot reported a TFR incursion.
summary: A drone operator filmed riot aftermath in an active emergency zone, relying on initial LAANC clearances and police approval without rechecking for Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs) during the flight. The operator later discovered a TFR had been issued hours earlier, though no conflict with manned aircraft occurred.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Single Pilot reported seeing lights on the runway while departing which ended up being two vehicles that the controller did not acknowledge knowing about.
summary: During a Part 91 ferry flight takeoff from Runway XXL, the pilot observed two vehicles on the runway end while accelerating and continued the departure, passing them at 200–300 feet. The pilot reported that the controller failed to abort the takeoff or answer queries about the vehicles, which were facing the opposite direction.

synopsis: Pilot reported overtaking previous slower departure which pilot lost sight of due to cockpit issue resulting in a NMAC.
summary: The pilot departed behind a slower VFR aircraft on the same heading and altitude, losing visual contact when the autopilot disconnected. Concerned about terrain and traffic, the pilot climbed to 8,500 feet before re-establishing visual contact and returning to the assigned 8,000 feet.

synopsis: First Officer reported error made during flight caused by a malfunctioning Fire Warning System, which caused an Air Turnback and Emergency Landing.
summary: During a cargo flight, the crew incorrectly executed the belly cargo fire checklist instead of the Main Cargo Fire checklist due to ambiguous EICAS messages and lack of specific training. This led to a delayed emergency descent, a high-speed landing at the departure airport, and subsequent tire fuse plug failures, though no actual fire was confirmed.

synopsis: Pilot of a SUAS (Small Unmanned Aircraft System) reported that while conducting a mission in controlled airspace, local law enforcement and ATC were unable to locate the filed flight plan.
summary: A Part 107 remote pilot operating a SUAS in Class B airspace was questioned by police who could not locate the pilot's LAANC flight plan via ZZZ Tower or the FAA. The pilot continued the flight under 100 feet after confirming with an Air Traffic Controller that towers cannot review filed LAANC data, highlighting a communication gap for law enforcement.

synopsis: Pilot reported oil and engine problems resulting in a divert and landing with smoke, and oil all over the place.
summary: The pilot experienced a progressive oil pressure drop and manifold pressure loss during cruise, leading to a complete engine failure with smoke and flames on final approach to ZZZ. The aircraft was successfully landed on Runway XXL and taxied to Taxiway XX.

synopsis: PA18 pilot reported being pushed off the taxiway into the grass by wind gusts and the nose of the aircraft contacted the ground.
summary: A pilot taxiing a light aircraft at ZZZ after landing encountered a gust that pushed the tail left, causing the aircraft to veer off the taxiway. Applying heel brakes with the stick forward resulted in the aircraft tipping onto its nose near a taxi light due to shifting winds.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a Low Altitude Alert from ATC due to towers close to the flight path of the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew descended below 3,000 feet on a visual approach to SDF Runway 17L, triggering a low altitude alert due to proximity to radio towers. The First Officer climbed to 3,000 feet to regain separation after the crew missed the obstacle heights during chart review.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude deviation during arrival. Captain stated rustiness due to lack of flying was a contributing factor.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer descended below 6,000 feet on the ZZZZZ Arrival due to misinterpreting a clearance to intercept the ILS XR as a descent to 4,000 feet. ATC queried the descent and ordered a level-off at 5,000 feet, attributing the error to crew fatigue and miscommunication.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an unstabilized approach resulting in a go-around. Unfamiliarity with the airport and rustiness from lack of flying were cited as contributing factors.
summary: A Captain and First Officer flying into unfamiliar mountain airport ZZZ executed a go-around after an unstable visual approach caused by high altitude, gusty winds, and automation confusion. The crew successfully landed on a second attempt following a debrief that identified the Captain's rustiness and poor descent planning as primary causes.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Captain reported the NOTAMs and construction markings at this location were insufficient to prevent a taxiway incursion.
summary: The pilot attempted to taxi at BIH toward Runway 8-26 but encountered unclear NOTAMs, poor markings, and barricades, forcing a 180-degree turn with construction worker assistance. The pilot subsequently required marshaling through a tight ramp area with less than one foot of clearance from a trailer, citing unsafe conditions and inadequate diagrams.

synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with a helicopter while attempting to land.
summary: A fixed-wing pilot executed a go-around after a helicopter, cleared for an autorotation landing on Runway XX, deviated from instructions and converged on the pilot's final approach. The pilot attributed the incident to the helicopter pilot not following controller instructions and ATC failing to cancel the helicopter's landing clearance or ensure safe sequencing.

synopsis: Pilot reported that the Runway 16 PAPI lights at MYL were not on and there was no NOTAM regarding the outage.
summary: A pilot reported that the PAPI for Runway 16 at McCall Airport (MYL) appeared inoperative during arrival, despite no NOTAM indicating it was out of service. The reporter requested verification of the system's status and proper NOTAM issuance if the equipment remains non-functional.

synopsis: CL30 Captain reported confusion over the wording of a SID.
summary: Pilots reported that the Midway 5 Departure at MDW is confusing due to conflicting instructions between the chart's heading requirements and tower-assigned headings. They argued this unnecessary switch from navigation to heading mode increases workload in crowded airspace and recommended an all-navigation procedure instead.

synopsis: UAS pilot reported that while operating a drone to photograph an airport building, a helicopter company at the airport had concerns about safety of operations.
summary: A Part 107 pilot operated an sUAV under 180 feet AGL at ZZZ airport with manager permission but no NOTAM. Although the pilot landed to avoid a departing helicopter and confirmed no safety conflict with the pattern pilot, company employees filed a report with the FSDO due to communication concerns.

synopsis: A Controller working combined sectors reported they requested the sectors be split due to workload but they were not and did not notice an aircraft on an assigned heading was flying below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined satellite sectors became task saturated while handling 12 to 14 aircraft, causing Aircraft X to approach an obstruction at 2,000 feet. The controller climbed the aircraft to 3,000 feet after a low altitude alert sounded, attributing the incident to task saturation from monitoring excessive airspace after the sector was combined against their request.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an airspace violation occurred due to lack of coordination. Traffic volume was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X entered ZZZ Tower's Delta without coordination during pattern work due to high photo flight volume and staffing shortages preventing sector splits. The controller admitted failing to point out the aircraft to ZZZ Tower first, attributing the error to extreme workload and lack of prior knowledge of the flight.

synopsis: Pilot reported exceeding 250 knots below 10,000 feet.
summary: The Captain reduced airspeed from 268 to 250 kts during climbout on the ZZZZZ SID after noticing managed speed was not set. The reporter attributed the event to the Captain having only 35 hours in seat and being on their second flight in two months.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An air carrier pilot departing an airport reported shutting down one engine due to a oil leak and returning to their departure point.
summary: The crew experienced a right engine oil quantity and pressure loss during climb, resulting in an engine shutdown and MAYDAY declaration at 23,000 feet. They returned for a single-engine ILS approach and landed safely after following ECAM procedures.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying A300 aircraft encountered hydraulic system failure in flight.
summary: The flight crew managed a green hydraulic system failure at FL340 by following ECAM and QRH procedures, declaring an emergency, and landing safely at ZZZZ. Post-landing inspection revealed a fluid leak from the left pylon, with the system quantity recovering after engine shutdown.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported their brakes failed while on landing roll and they had a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported a runway excursion during landing caused by a total loss of brake pressure and nose wheel steering failure, compounded by gusty crosswinds. The pilot attributed the mechanical failure to rushed maintenance and unresolved prior write-ups regarding the braking system.

synopsis: Inspector reported right hand nose gear door of a C680 was not in over center position when nose landing gear retracted, causing damage to the door and an unsafe nose gear indication.
summary: A maintenance vendor reported that during gear retraction after takeoff, the right nose gear door was damaged because it was not in the over-center position. The reporter attributed the incident to a design flaw and recommended pilot verification of door stops and improved post-maintenance checks.

synopsis: GA pilot reported while downwind, they almost had a NMAC while trying to avoid an unknown aircraft.
summary: A pilot on a left downwind for Runway 5 at Deland Municipal reported an unknown aircraft maneuvering within 500 feet of their left wing. The pilot executed a right turn to evade, but separation decreased to 400–500 feet before the other aircraft turned north and climbed away.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported taking off with incorrect transponder code and cited lack of flying due to the COVID-19 as a contributing factor.
summary: A flight instructor and student departed from ZZZ in the SFRA with the transponder incorrectly set to VFR code 1200 instead of the required 12XX. The instructor attributed the error to a lapse in pre-takeoff checks caused by returning to duty after a three-month absence.

synopsis: Pilot reported experiencing a track heading deviation and cited rustiness and lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot reported that while departing XXL on the ZZZZZ departure, the aircraft failed to turn right after crossing ZZZZZ1 because it remained in RWY Track instead of Managed Nav. The pilot intervened to initiate the turn, attributing the oversight to insufficient monitoring and reduced recent flight experience.

synopsis: Corporate pilot reported that while on an RNAV approach, the Universal UNS-1E FMA dropped the IAF and redrew the final approach course. Reporter stated this had happened previously on the same routing.
summary: Pilots flying Aircraft X enroute to APF experienced an FMS anomaly where the UNS-1E dropped the UGYOW fix and commanded an incorrect turn. The controller canceled the approach and provided radar vectors after the FMS error caused confusion, which the crew attributed to a system defect.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a loud hum during climbout emanating from the door and having to return to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced a loud noise from the main cabin door seal during climb through FL210, despite prior maintenance checks. The crew descended and returned to ZZZ due to the unresolved issue, which was attributed to a faulty door seal.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reported smoke and what appeared to be overheating of electronics, landed aircraft safely.
summary: During the downwind leg of the ZZZZZ arrival, the flight crew reported a thump followed by cabin smoke and sequential generator failures. The Captain hand-flew the ILS in heavy rain after an autopilot failure, landing safely and deplaning passengers at the gate without evacuation or injury.

synopsis: Flight crew reported overshooting altitude and then returning to assigned altitude. The Captain stated lack of flying was a contributing factor.
summary: The Pilot Flying hand-flew a climb from 3,000 to 6,000 feet while distracted by weather, causing an overshoot to 6,300 feet. The crew corrected to 6,000 feet after ATC confirmation, attributing the deviation to manual flight distraction and recommending autopilot use in congested areas.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported the placement of the EFB mount can restrict tiller movement.
