summary: The pilot reported that after landing, the First Officer's EFB power cord caught on the tiller during a taxiway turn, restricting steering. The cause was poor EFB placement, prompting a recommendation to relocate the device to its original position.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported a hydraulic system failure and having to land the aircraft.
summary: The crew experienced a total loss of Hydraulic System 3 pressure due to a burst line during the arrival phase. They manually extended the gear, landed safely with degraded braking and steering, and were tugged to the gate after maintenance confirmed the fluid leak.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported forgetting to turn on three of the four window heat switches during pre-flight.
summary: The Captain forgot to activate three window heat switches during ground preparation at ZZZ due to fatigue, distractions, and a misjudged technique regarding ground temperature indications. Although no icing was encountered en route to ZZZ1, the Captain acknowledged the error and noted that the First Officer was not informed of the temporary switch-off plan.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a taxiway incursion, citing distraction with aircraft condition and lack of recent flying as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine aircraft taxiing after an annual inspection mistakenly entered Taxiway Alpha instead of the cleared Taxiway Uniform. The error resulted from the pilot's preoccupation with aircraft systems checks and complacency due to the deserted airport and infrequent flying.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported landing at home airport but due to construction and ATC clearance was confused causing a runway incursion and a go-around.
summary: A pilot taxiing via Runway 32 due to construction failed to hold short of Runway 35, causing a runway incursion and a go-around for an arriving aircraft. The pilot attributed the error to confusing markings and non-standard routing, prompting the controller to avoid future runway taxi instructions in this area.

synopsis: PA-28R Cherokee Pilot reported an NMAC event during takeoff roll with a nordo aircraft that initiated an opposite direction takeoff.
summary: A departing aircraft on Runway XX at ZZZ was forced to reconfigure for a short field takeoff after an unknown twin-engine Cessna entered the runway without announcement. The intruder cleared the departing aircraft by 100 feet and did not respond to radio warnings.

synopsis: Cessna-172 pilot reported an NMAC event in VFR landing pattern with trailing aircraft .
summary: A pilot entering left downwind for RWY XX at ZZZ observed Aircraft Y on the same leg at co-altitude and 500 feet left after Y took off without further calls. The pilot maneuvered to maintain safe spacing following this proximity.

synopsis: Piper J-3 Cub pilot reported off airport landing due to engine failure.
summary: The pilot of a J3 aircraft experienced an engine stoppage due to fuel starvation during a delivery ferry flight, forcing an off-field landing that bent the right main gear. The cause was a corroded fuel indicator wire providing inaccurate readings, with a stuck carburetor float also suspected as a contributing factor.

synopsis: Pilot flying experimental aircraft encountered city vehicle on runway during takeoff.
summary: The pilot attempted a takeoff on Runway 29 while a city truck entered the runway, resulting in a low-altitude pass over the vehicle due to gusty winds and P-factor. The Airport Manager, an administrative assistant without aviation experience, blamed the pilot for continuing the takeoff and denied it was a runway incursion.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Private Pilot flying with Instructor in small aircraft encounters illegal flying maneuvers by instructor.
summary: During a personal flight, a CFI in the right seat took control and conducted hazardous low-altitude passes near a residence, prompting the reporter to seize control and climb to 1300 feet to return safely. The reporter alleges the CFI lied in a subsequent NASA report to cover up his poor judgment and violation of minimum altitude regulations.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reported accidentally retracting the landing gear on the runway during a touch and go that resulted in a prop strike and partial landing gear collapse.
summary: The pilot retracted landing gear instead of flaps during a touch-and-go takeoff roll, causing a prop strike and partial gear collapse. The incident resulted from a late decision to perform a touch-and-go to avoid a long taxi, despite the pilot's preference for full-stop landings in complex aircraft.

synopsis: RV8 pilot reported a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of a first-flight RV8 departed the runway midpoint at 45 knots during landing on Rwy XXL, regaining control at 20 knots using wheel brakes. The report cites possible causes including pilot inexperience, inadvertent braking, tailwheel mis-adjustment, excessive touchdown speed, and failure to maintain full back stick.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported an NMAC event with a nonreporting aircraft while in landing pattern.
summary: Pilots on left downwind at an uncontrolled airport climbed and turned left to avoid an aircraft flying opposite direction 100–200 feet below. The reporter attributed the conflict to the other pilot's dangerous entry procedure and lack of radio communication.

synopsis: BE-58 Single Pilot reported receiving an FAA report for reckless operations of aircraft (FAR 91.13) after completion of low altitude flight.
summary: A pilot flying VFR at 500 ft AGL and 160 kts in Class G airspace crossed the threshold of Runway X at ZZZ while a single-engine aircraft was on approach. The pilot received an FAA report citing reckless flying despite believing they were clear of obstacles and other traffic.

synopsis: Maule M5 pilot reported trying to stop in time to make runway exit a ATC assigned taxiway, aircraft made a U turn and hit a taxiway sign.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing after landing on Runway XXL, exited too fast for the directed Taxiway XX, causing an uncontrolled U-turn where the tail struck a sign. The pilot attributed the incident to their own error in speed management and successfully cleared the aircraft to continue taxiing.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Maintenance inspection on light transport aircraft was incorrectly recorded as being completed.
summary: Technicians and a tracking system updater incorrectly marked a partially completed 12-year inspection as finished, resetting the due date and removing it from the aircraft's to-do list. The error was discovered during a pre-purchase inspection, causing the aircraft to be grounded until the inspection was fully completed.

synopsis: An Approach Controller reported an aircraft did not comply with their vector in a timely manner and flew below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X during arrival, but the pilot deviated from headings, causing the aircraft to enter a 4,000-foot Minimum Vectoring Altitude area while below that altitude. The controller attributed the incident to pilot deviation, noting the Low Altitude Alert did not trigger and the aircraft narrowly avoided terrain.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an altitude deviation during approach. Lack of flying and proficiency were contributing factors.
summary: The Pilot Flying descended in Level Change mode during arrival at ZZZ, busting the 7,000-foot restriction while reprogramming for a runway change. The crew immediately disconnected the autopilot to correct the altitude, attributing the error to low proficiency and distraction from managing multiple tasks.

synopsis: EMB-145LR Captain reported a fumes event prior to pushback.
summary: Flight crew and maintenance identified smoke and odor from Pack 2 during engine start after boarding. The crew deplaned passengers, MEL'd Pack 2, reloaded, and departed to ZZZ1 with a delay.

synopsis: Lead Flight Attendant reported the red tag was not put in place after disarming the door.
summary: The pilot, acting as the first-time A in over 15 years, failed to secure the red strap after disarming R1 due to nervousness and distraction while donning a face mask before opening L1. The reporter suggests a policy review regarding mask usage for the A to manage added tasks like phone calls and PAs.

synopsis: Technician reported errors and omissions in Work Cards relating to portable fire extinguishers on company aircraft being returned to service after storage.
summary: A mechanic working on Aircraft X returning from short-term storage reported that water fire bottles are not installed, while Halon and LAV extinguishers were removed and weighed per specific AMM steps.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot back taxiing to depart a non towered airport reported an aircraft landed opposite direction.
summary: The pilot back-taxied Runway 13 for a Runway 31 departure while a Stearman landed on Runway 13, creating a runway incursion. The pilot attributed the near-miss to low sun obscuring the Stearman, reduced radio volume preventing communication, and the inability to see behind while taxiing.

synopsis: KC-135 Captain reported experiencing temporary loss of control due to severe turbulence.
summary: A crew of nine flying a tanker at FL390 encountered severe turbulence and heavy precipitation while over storms, losing 1,300 feet in three seconds. The pilot climbed to FL410 to exit the weather, and post-event checks confirmed no injuries, no wing damage, and the boom remained stowed.

synopsis: C172 Instructor Pilot reported his solo student lost directional control in a crosswind landing and veered off the runway.
summary: A solo student pilot swerved off the runway onto grass due to a crosswind gust, bumping a light with the wheel pant before returning to the runway under control. The instructor subsequently directed the student to maintain aileron input into the wind during landing.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway excursion due to faulty rudder controls.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft but lost rudder control, causing it to depart the runway and strike a log. The pilot attributed the incident to suspected rudder ineffectiveness and admitted they should have postponed the flight for mechanical evaluation.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot landed and rolled left of the centerline with throttles not fully retarded, causing an inability to maintain the runway. To avoid a groundloop, the pilot committed to the grass on the east side, resulting in no damage or injuries.

synopsis: SCT TRACON Controller reported experiencing an airborne conflict between an air carrier and a GA aircraft.
summary: Air Traffic Control vectored Aircraft X for a visual approach to Runway 24R, but the aircraft drifted toward Runway 25L traffic (Aircraft Y) which was not in sight. The controller instructed Aircraft X to correct back to Runway 24R, attributing the deviation to unfamiliar pilots operating at LAX.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Approach Controller reported they vectored a departing aircraft below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X at 2,000 ft to allow an ILS arrival to pass overhead before climbing it to 5,000 ft. The aircraft failed to climb as expected, entering a 3,900 ft Minimum Vectoring Altitude at 2,800 ft, prompting a low altitude alert and an expedited climb instruction.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported they had to issue a go around and diversion to another runway due to a disabled aircraft on their runway.
summary: A VFR aircraft ground looped on the runway while Aircraft X was on final, causing the Local Controller to close the runway. The reporter cancelled Aircraft X's approach, cleared it for a visual approach on a different runway, and handled the landing due to the Local Controller's workload.

synopsis: Pilots reported being advised that the aircraft was flown with open write ups on three legs.
summary: The pilot departed on the first flight of the day with three open maintenance logbook discrepancies. The pilot attributed the error to overlooking the unclosed items during preflight while focusing on a fuel audit and disinfecting the work area due to COVID-19.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a miscommunication problem with TPA TRACON resulting in an altitude deviation and attributed it partly due to not flying because of COVID-19.
summary: The SIC, acting as PF, departed PIE with an initial altitude of 16,000 feet but was instructed by ATC to descend to 12,000 feet due to a suspected clearance miscommunication. The controller attributed the error to potential Tower oversight and noted strained operations for both pilots and ATC personnel during the pandemic.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported attempting to land at an airport with a closed Control Tower and other aircraft landing on an unlit runway at night.
summary: The crew attempted to land at PDK at night with the tower closed and VASI/PAPIs inoperative, but executed a go-around due to conflicting traffic on an unlit runway. They eventually landed on their third attempt after Approach vectored them and a ground-holding aircraft cleared the runway.

synopsis: E175 pilot reported receiving a TCAS alert for traffic on the parallel runway.
summary: The pilot reported that TRACON paired aircraft on parallel final approaches, causing an Airbus to approach from behind and lower at higher speed, which triggered a TCAS alert. The pilot attributed this dangerous workload increase to unnecessary pairing practices and recommended staggering approaches to prevent future events.

synopsis: Air taxi pilot reported that smoke in the cockpit resulted in a diversion.
summary: The pilot encountered unknown cockpit smoke during flight, suspected an electrical fire, and requested priority handling to land at ITR. After shutting down electrical systems and evacuating via the crew hatch, the aircraft was parked safely away from fuel pumps.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying 737-900 aircraft found empty beer can in cockpit during pre-flight.
summary: During preflight, the First Officer discovered an empty beer can in the cockpit garbage bag, violating the FOM policy. The crew suspects the can was left by cleaners or contract maintenance personnel who accessed the aircraft overnight to address a lav waste system issue.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying A319 aircraft landed with lower than planned fuel.
summary: The Captain executed a go-around during the flare phase of a CAT III autoland due to an FCC fault, then landed with low fuel reserves after ATC issued an early descent. The reporter attributed the fuel issue to the go-around, early descent, and a flight plan discrepancy showing incorrect Mach and flight level data.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying A319 aircraft discover a Manual discrepancy pertaining to the number of required survival kits on board.
summary: The Captain of Aircraft X departed for ZZZ1 and ZZZ after conflicting reports on survival kit requirements between Flight Attendants, Maintenance, and manuals. The reporter suspects Flight Ops and Flight Attendant paperwork is incorrect and requests synchronization with Maintenance records.

synopsis: B737 Flight Crew encountered an un-commanded inflight engine shutdown that resulted in a diversion.
summary: The crew experienced a #1 engine flameout during descent from FL 330, which auto-relit after 15-20 seconds. They diverted to ZZZ1, landed with Flaps 15, and shut down the engine after maintenance observed abnormal surging, suspecting a prior foam ingestion event.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew encountered a Hydraulic System failure during climb that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: During climb out, the crew experienced a rapid #3 hydraulic fluid leak causing system failure. They dumped 75,000 lbs of fuel at FL260, returned to ZZZ for an uneventful landing, and attributed the failure to a stab trim issue.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 3 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that high EGT indications resulted in an engine shutdown.
summary: During descent, the #2 engine EGT fluctuated to 1007 degrees with an intermittent 'X' on the indicator. The crew performed a precautionary shutdown, received ILS vectors, and the Captain executed an auto land.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported a fumes event which was not communicated to the entire Flight Attendant crew in order to provide a complete evaluation of the event. The reporter experienced health issues.
summary: A cabin crew member reported smelling a musty odor midflight and later developing a headache during descent on Aircraft X. The crew was not informed of the subsequent fume event investigation until boarding the next flight, resulting in a lack of immediate medical attention and communication.

synopsis: Technician reported being distracted by possible lay-offs and did not complete a work order correctly.
summary: A mechanic reported being reprimanded for failing to install "Pitot and Static Port covered" placards on the captain's yoke after referencing Maintenance XXX-XX-00 in the log. The mechanic attributed the error to distraction while tagging closely spaced circuit breakers and underlying stress regarding potential layoffs.

synopsis: Technician reported work card discrepancies for two different types of aircraft and being pressured to continue working after finding these errors.
summary: Mechanics performing maintenance on Type X and Type Y aircraft found conflicting and incorrect steps in work cards, such as referencing non-existent ECAM systems. They completed the tasks despite errors due to fear of job loss, citing poor card production and a lack of immediate clarification systems as the root cause.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway incursion partially due to incorrect DXR airport taxiway diagram.
summary: The pilot accidentally crossed a hold-short line while taxiing to Runway 26 via Romeo due to faded markings, vegetation distractions, and charts that inaccurately depicted the taxiway layout. The reporter attributes the error to these compounding factors and calls for chart corrections and improved surface markings.

synopsis: Pilot reported an altitude deviation due to excessive climb rate.
summary: The safety pilot reported that the pilot flying, who was refreshing skills after a COVID-related break, overshot a cleared climb to 7,000 feet by 200 feet due to an excessive climb rate. The pilot flying corrected the altitude after the safety pilot issued multiple warnings during the enroute phase.

synopsis: UAV operator reported a TFR miscommunication that resulted in an airborne conflict with an aircraft.
summary: The crew launched a UAS for fire mapping after receiving clearance, but encountered unexpected traffic within the TFR boundary. Investigation revealed the TFR was not actually activated, prompting an immediate safe landing and a new procedure to verify TFR status before future flights.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NMAC with a non-communicating aircraft approaching on a crossing runway.
summary: A training aircraft on final approach to Runway 32 executed a go-around at 400 ft. MSL due to a conflict with Aircraft Y on intersecting Runway 27. The reporter attributed the conflict to Aircraft Y's failure to monitor the radio frequency, citing their claim that the tower was closed and they could not find the frequency.

synopsis: C172 Instructor reported a NMAC with an opposite landing aircraft.
summary: A flight instructor and student departing Runway 01L at Concord (CCR) experienced a loss of separation with an inbound aircraft on a straight-in approach to Runway 19R. The instructor attributed the incident to departing with opposite-direction traffic within four miles and underestimating the inbound aircraft's groundspeed.

synopsis: C172 Pilot reported a critical ground conflict while in position on active runway.
summary: The pilot held on active Runway 36 while Aircraft Y overflew within 50 feet AGL during an approach to the 1,000-foot markers without making traffic announcements. Aircraft Y subsequently aborted the landing and departed the flight path, while the pilot proceeded with takeoff after the departing traffic on Runway 35 called crosswind.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported being issued taxi instructions in at SEA airport to hold at a geographic position marking that is not depicted on the normal SEA airport taxi diagram. Reporter suggested that the marking which appears only on the low visibility chart should not be used in taxi clearances when airport is not in low visibility conditions.
summary: The flight crew held on a taxiway at SEA after vacating Runway 16L due to an occupied gate. They struggled to locate a low-visibility geographic position marking on Taxiway B instructed by the South Ramp Controller because it was not depicted on their normal taxi chart.

synopsis: Piper 28R Single Pilot reported gear collapse on landing after a Tower visual check low pass.
summary: The pilot reported that during approach to ZZZ, the landing gear indicator light failed to display. After the tower verified the gear was down via a fly-by, the aircraft landed and the gear collapsed.

synopsis: Pilot reported an NMAC with an aircraft in an SFRA due to being at the wrong transitioning altitude.
summary: A pilot flying northwest at 1,900 feet in the BAL-DCA VFR flyway encountered opposite-direction traffic 100 feet above due to using an incorrect altitude. The pilot attributed the conflict to personal unfamiliarity with recommended flyway altitudes and a lack of specific altitude advisories from Potomac Approach.

synopsis: Pilot reported concerns with the limitations imposed by the SFAR concerning the ability to exercise instrument privileges.
summary: An instrument pilot objected to SFAR restrictions on recent flight experience, stating they lack required hours and approaches despite holding valid endorsements and recent solo time. The pilot argued these rules deny IFR privileges unless flying with a safety pilot, citing virus risks and suggesting subjective competency assessments instead.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported seeing multiple helicopters near the runway end and also reported the aircraft encountered winds resulting in a prop strike.
summary: The instructor and student landed a training aircraft in a crosswind, but the student failed to apply correct rudder and aileron inputs, causing a runway excursion and propeller strike. The aircraft was recovered and taxied to the ramp with no engine damage, though the instructor noted a go-around or stronger control intervention would have been safer.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported the gear indicator light was not displaying green during final and gear collapsed during landing.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing with a faulty gear indicator, a tower visual confirmation and subsequent go-around were performed. Upon the second landing, the landing gear collapsed.

synopsis: CE-560 XL flight crew reported a passenger notified them of smoke in the cabin during approach. The flight crew completed the checklist memory items, donned their oxygen masks and landed without further incident.
summary: During an enroute check at 3,000 ft near ZZZ, pilots detected cabin smoke and an oily fuel odor, likely caused by an engine or APU bearing oil seal leak vaporizing in the compressor. The crew donned oxygen masks, executed a short visual approach, and landed safely before evacuating passengers with no fire risk found.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported flying into a restricted area and attributed it to weather and not receiving ATC flight following.
summary: The pilot overflew restricted airspace R-XXXX while en route from State Y to State Z at 8,500 feet due to early VOR tracking and route changes. The incident was discovered post-landing when directed to contact ZZZ Control, with the pilot citing reluctance to request flight following due to perceived ATC staffing shortages.

synopsis: Pilot flying C-501 aircraft reported deviation from landing clearance.
summary: A pilot conducting currency training was urgently directed by ATC to taxi near persons and light aircraft due to a reported runway deviation. The pilot expressed discomfort with jet blast exposure but completed the flight safely, with no injuries reported.

synopsis: GA pilot reported a NMAC at SAV airport.
summary: The pilot reported a near miss with an aircraft possibly departing SAV while flying track 010 near the Class C inner shelf. The other aircraft approached on a 230 heading, prompting an immediate climb that resulted in passing 100–200 feet vertically and 300–500 feet horizontally above the intruder.

synopsis: Instructor and student pilots reported they experienced an NMAC that required evasive action.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a training aircraft at 3,000 feet MSL executed a steep descending right turn to avoid a collision with another aircraft heading directly toward them. The other aircraft did not alter its course, prompting the instructor to take control and maneuver after ATC authorized necessary avoidance actions.

synopsis: Captain reported ATC issued a climb 2,000 feet above the filed altitude, crew took the altitude and did not question ATC. Another Center Sector Controller eventually asked crew why they were going to newly assigned altitude instead of filed altitude.
summary: A pilot reported that during climb, a Center Controller cleared the aircraft to FL300 instead of the filed FL280, causing confusion when the next sector controller questioned the altitude. Although no traffic conflicts occurred, the pilot attributed the communication gap to reduced staffing and noted the crew should have questioned the unexpected clearance.

synopsis: Student Pilot flying C-172 reported loss of aircraft control during touch and go with crosswind that resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: A pilot practicing soft field landings at ZZZ was lifted off the runway by an unexpected right gust while throttling up, causing a deviation into the infield and a collision with a taxiway light. The incident resulted in minor wheel pant damage, with the pilot attributing the event to the gust combined with premature power application before the aircraft was fully settled.

synopsis: SLC Tower Controller reported an aircraft went around twice due to windshear and also reported that the way the Tower cab positions are split up are not flexible and not safe.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined positions reported that Aircraft X executed two wind shear go-arounds, creating a conflict with departure traffic while the controller was distracted by complex taxi operations. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to rigid regional staffing mandates that prevented necessary position adjustments for real-time workload.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: ZLA Center Controller reported losing separation due to traffic volume, watching too large of an area and the COVID-19 configuration.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined sectors issued conflicting clearances to Aircraft X and Y due to high workload and four data blocks in close proximity, triggering a conflict alert. The controller attributed the loss of separation to being overwhelmed and the Flight Line Manager's failure to provide assistance despite verbal indications of excessive workload.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported a loss of separation event and made reference to COVID-19 staffing levels as a contributing factor.
summary: A Radar/Tower controller managing reduced COVID-19 staffing lost separation between IFR practice Aircraft Y and departing Aircraft X due to distraction by handoff automation and misremembering Aircraft Y's altitude. The controller attributed the incident to traffic building faster than expected and failing to maintain situational awareness during complex operations.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported landing after an unstable approach due to thunderstorms and wind shear.
summary: The flight crew attempted to land ahead of a thunderstorm but encountered gusty winds exceeding 50 knots and a windshear advisory on final approach. The aircraft arrived high and fast, triggering a terrain warning and exceeding flap limits, yet the pilot executed a safe landing in heavy rain.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported controller denial of heading request to avoid weather.
summary: During a SID climb from 12,000' to 23,000', the crew requested a weather avoidance turn to 055°, but ZZZ Departure Control directed a turn to 090°. This directive caused the aircraft to encounter continuous moderate turbulence, which the pilot attributed to the controller's refusal to consider the crew's weather radar observations.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported being notified by a Flight Attendant during passenger deplaning of a strong rubbery odor" which was noticed during final approach. First Officer notified Maintenance, completed necessary documentation, and relayed information to the Captain."
summary: Flight attendants and deadheading pilots detected fumes during approach to ZZZ but delayed informing the flight deck until after landing. The First Officer reported the event to maintenance after the Captain had departed, noting no injuries occurred but acknowledging the communication delay.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Captain reported an NMAC with a UAV on approach to ICT.
summary: A pilot on final approach to Runway 14 at ICT observed a drone approximately 100–200 feet below and to the left of the aircraft. No avoidance maneuvers were required, and the pilot continued the stable approach while notifying ATC of the encounter.

synopsis: E-175 flight crew reported being notified that their previously completed flight they unknowingly transported undocumented Dangerous Goods.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X discovered dry ice was loaded in the aft cargo for a live animal shipment, despite it being absent from the manifest and load sheet. This discrepancy was only revealed through casual conversations with a tug driver and ramp agent, as company HAZMAT officials could not confirm the dry ice's presence.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported forgetting to turn off APU and later exceeding the APU ceiling.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced APU altitude exceed warnings during climb after the Captain missed the after-start flow and failed to notice the running APU during the after-takeoff checklist. The crew followed QRH procedures to shut down the APU, completing the flight without further incident.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported wearing a COVID-19 mask hindered her ability to smell smoke in the cabin.
summary: A flight attendant reported that wearing a face mask shortly after takeoff hindered their ability to detect smoke, which they eventually smelled strongly. The Captain speculated the smoke was from outside, and the attendant requested revoking mask mandates to prevent impaired safety duties.

synopsis: Technician reported insufficient training as the factor in not following procedures during a horizontal stabilizer jackscrew lubrication.
summary: A mechanic servicing a CRJ900 horizontal stabilizer gearbox lubrication task skipped manual shaft rotation steps, instead cycling the trim switch to spread grease. Another mechanic reported this deviation to inspection, citing insufficient training and concerns over the flight-critical nature of the skipped procedures.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported their nose gear collapsed while landing.
summary: The pilot reported a nose wheel shimmy and subsequent strut failure during the landing rollout of a propeller aircraft. The nose gear collapsed, causing the propeller to strike the runway, though the aircraft remained on the surface and came to a stop.

synopsis: PA-28 flight crew reported loss of directional control during instructional flight resulting in runway excursion.
summary: During a student pilot's pre-solo evaluation landing, strong gusting crosswinds caused the aircraft to veer left and lose directional control despite rudder corrections. The instructor took command but could not prevent the aircraft from exiting the runway into grass, resulting in no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported experiencing a runway incursion after landing.
summary: The pilot inadvertently entered Runway XYR instead of Taxiway Bravo while taxiing after landing at ZZZ, a non-towered airport. The error resulted from complacency due to familiarity, reduced recent flight time, and a violation of sterile cockpit procedures during the rollout.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a CFTT incident citing unfamiliarity with the airport and issues relating to the surrounding terrain.
summary: The First Officer reported a visual approach over mountainous terrain where a late flap 45 configuration and reliance on radar altimeter triggered a glideslope and 'pull up' alert. The Captain landed safely between the 1,000 and 1,500 foot markers, though the reporter attributed the confusion to terrain-induced radar altimeter discrepancies and deferred judgment due to recent time off.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported an icing encounter that necessitated a deviation from an assigned altitude.
summary: The pilot encountered rapid icing and pitot blockage while descending from 8,000 ft into clouds, causing loss of altitude and VSI indications. After activating pitot heat and de-icing, the pilot completed an RNAV 1 approach to ZZZ airport, attributing the event to unexpected summer icing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported an NMAC event during landing practice with a nonreporting aircraft entered the landing pattern.
summary: A pilot conducting touch-and-go maneuvers at an airport with skydivers reported a near-midair conflict when Aircraft Y entered the pattern below from a 45-degree left downwind. ForeFlight alerts prompted the pilot to maneuver away, as Aircraft Y appeared unaware of the pilot's presence and passed directly underneath.

synopsis: Gyroplane pilot reported loss of control during takeoff roll resulting in runway excursion.
summary: The pilot aborted a takeoff on Runway XX after a rotor speed decrease indication caused the aircraft to veer left and stop on the embankment with damaged blades. The incident resulted from the pilot's inappropriate application of back pressure instead of reducing power, likely triggered by a rotor speed indication failure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a track heading deviation when executing a 360 turn resulting from confusing a fix name which sounds like the number 360.
summary: The pilot, flying an IFR approach with new avionics, misinterpreted a controller's "Direct ZZZZZ" clearance as a "360" turn due to phonetic similarity and controller urgency. This confusion, combined with task saturation while troubleshooting the new equipment, caused an altitude deviation that led to the approach termination.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported NMAC and cited reoccurring issues with ATC Tower.
summary: A student pilot and instructor on a touch-and-go at ZZZ received a clearance to climb upwind that directed them toward a converging aircraft behind them. The pilot attributed the near miss to the nose obscuring the view and poor traffic management by the tower controllers.

synopsis: Pilot reported a track heading deviation and cited lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot not flying departed ZZZ on the ZZZZZX departure but deviated one mile west and south of the initial curve. The reporter attributes the error to the pilot flying's distraction by visual terrain, low recent proficiency, and the decision to hand-fly a busy departure in mountainous conditions.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having inadequate cleaning supplies to sanitize their cockpit equipment.
summary: Flight crew reported that while ground COVID-19 protocols were followed, the aircraft lacked effective alcohol-based wipes for cockpit touch points. Only ineffective Sanicom and M-Zone screen wipes were available, prompting a recommendation to replace them with alcohol-based alternatives.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported receiving an RA alert during initial approach to BUR airport.
summary: A pilot flying into BUR on approach for Runway 8 received a Traffic Advisory at 2,400 feet and an RA to climb due to a general aviation aircraft 400–500 feet below. The crew executed the climb, confirmed separation, and continued the approach after Tower consultation.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported experiencing fatigue from extended work hours and additional duties due to change in flight schedules in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: Flight attendants reported fatigue after working over 18 hours with only one break due to extended ground stops and additional service duties during COVID-19. They stated this caused impaired judgment and recommended a layover to reduce duty time and ensure safety.

synopsis: Air carrier flight attendants reported that a passenger was vaping in the lavatory and was not wearing a personal protective mask during the flight.
summary: Flight attendants reported a passenger vaping in the aft lavatory during cruise, triggering a smoke alarm. The Captain spoke with the passenger after deplaning, and the crew recommended adding no-vaping placards to restrooms and safety cards.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported a sick passenger boarded a flight, but was removed from the flight prior to departure.
summary: During boarding, a Flight Attendant moved a passenger after a neighbor reported feeling ill with a sore throat and cough. Per Medlink, the ill passenger was not approved to fly and was removed, but the flight departed with the correct passenger count.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Mechanic reported that after performing work on the nose gear door, the aircraft had nose gear problems in flight. Mechanic was concerned that fatigue due to changes in work schedule hours contributed to a possible error.
summary: A mechanic installed a RH nose landing gear door bumper on Aircraft X and later questioned if the work caused a subsequent return to field. The mechanic attributed potential errors to fatigue from a disrupted sleep schedule and noted that the door stop can falsely indicate a locked position.

synopsis: Pilot reported another pilot had a loss of electrical power on a C182 during flight after engine replacement due to alternator connection not installed correctly.
summary: A Cessna 180 lost all electrical power en route during a cross-country flight due to incorrectly attached generator connections by the mechanic. The failure remained undetected until battery depletion because the aircraft lacked a voltmeter, relying only on an amp meter.

synopsis: PA-31 pilot reported not reconnecting the nose landing gear scissors pin prior to flight, resulting in a runway excursion on landing.
summary: The pilot departed a Chieftain for ZZZ in rain and low ceilings but forgot to reinstall the nose gear linkage pin before takeoff. Upon landing, the unsecured nose wheel turned 180 degrees and dragged, causing the aircraft to pull right until the main gear dropped off the runway ledge, resulting in a safe stop and subsequent maintenance tow.

synopsis: Piper M600 pilot reported loss of directional control after landing due to the apparent failure of the nose wheel steering.
summary: The pilot of a Piper M600 exited the runway during landing after the nose wheel steering failed to respond to inputs, causing an immediate hard right turn. The aircraft stopped in the grass after the nose gear collapsed, which the pilot attributed to a mechanical failure of the steering system.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor and student pilot reported the student had a runway excursion during a solo training flight.
summary: A student pilot and instructor reported a runway excursion at ZZZ during landing where the aircraft veered off the west edge at 40 mph. The pilot attributed the incident to overcorrecting for a wind gust and unintentionally applying the left brake, resulting in no injuries or runway closure.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported precautionary landing in a field due to engine failure.
summary: The pilot performed a precautionary landing in a field due to an engine failure. No specific aircraft type, phase of flight, or further cause details were provided in the narrative.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported ATL TRACON vectors commercial aircraft outside of Class B airspace on approach.
summary: A Part 121 crew reported that ATC vectored them out of Atlanta Class B airspace during approach to assign visual approaches, despite a functional ILS. The pilot deemed this unsafe, arguing it exposes IFR traffic to potential midair collisions with non-ADS-B VFR aircraft operating legally in the airspace.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported issues with the service provided by SLC Tower and cited Controller workload as a contributing factor.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ reported that an overloaded SLC Tower controller failed to issue a Bravo clearance, forcing the aircraft to orbit in turbulence and high engine temperatures. The delay occurred because the controller prioritized Clearance Delivery duties, only clearing the aircraft after the pilot called again.

synopsis: GA pilot flying small aircraft encounters skydiver in front of aircraft during taxi at ASD airport.
summary: A pilot at ASD stopped taxiing after a skydiver landed off the designated zone in front of the aircraft. The pilot attributed the incident to the current location of the skydiving landing zone and recommended moving it to the south end of the field.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported engine was missing and smelled of gas during climbout. They decided to return to the departure airport and landed safely.
summary: An instructor and student pilot experienced occasional engine roughness and a gas odor while climbing to 3,500 feet MSL during training. They returned to ZZZ, advised ATC, and landed uneventfully after slipping the aircraft as a precaution against potential power loss.

synopsis: Technician reported not installing streamers on landing gear after disconnecting squat switches and not reconnecting the squat switches after ADS-B maintenance.
summary: A mechanic troubleshooting an ADS-B failure on Aircraft X left squat switches disconnected without installing marker streamers due to distraction, fatigue, and inadequate turnover communication. The aircraft was released for service with the switches still disconnected, creating a safety risk.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZOB Center Controller reported forgetting to ask 3 different aircraft if they had weather and NOTAMs for their landing airport.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to confirm weather and NOTAMs for three aircraft approaching BAX airport due to reduced staffing and infrequent approach clearances. Although no NOTAMs existed and all aircraft arrived safely, the controller recognized a lapse in preparation and plans to refresh procedures for rare tasks.

synopsis: A Controller working Local Control Combined with Controller in Charge reported an aircraft reported sighting a drone in their airspace but was unable to find the appropriate checklists to report the incident according to the rules.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Local 3 and CIC duties reported a drone sighting near the final approach but failed to complete required notifications due to a malfunctioning reporting webpage and an unavailable UAS checklist. Consequently, the event was not reported to the Domestic Event Network, PCT, or broadcast on the ATIS as required.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported receiving a CFIT alert from the Approach Controller. Pilot crew also described difficulty communicating with the very busy controller.
summary: Pilots and an approach controller were involved during a busy ILS approach in mountainous terrain with a tailwind. Poor communication and conflicting vectors caused confusion and a terrain alert, but the crew executed a go-around and eventually landed safely after re-establishing a stabilized approach.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that the over-wing doors were not armed and the aircraft had been flown for several days in this condition. The aircraft had recently come from storage and the escape slides had not been enabled for deployment by Maintenance.
summary: The flight crew discovered unarmed over-wing exit slides during the before-start flow on an aircraft recently removed from storage. Maintenance reset the system after finding the slide pins, likely installed during mothballing, had not been removed, potentially allowing the aircraft to fly unsafe for several days.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported being notified that the flight release had not been signed prior to departure. The FO stated that technology challenges as a result of COVID-19 procedures contributed to the event.
summary: The First Officer and Captain discovered via ACARS after reaching top of climb that the flight release was unsigned due to unreliable iPad signing procedures mandated by COVID-19 protocols. The reporter attributes the error to technology challenges and recommends a system checklist to prevent dispatching manifests without a signed release.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a taxiway incursion due to expectation bias.
summary: The flight crew, fatigued after a long duty day, took a wrong turn on Taxiway 1 due to expectation bias, a missed NOTAM, and distraction from an after-landing checklist. Tower directed them to taxi via the runway to correct the error, citing ambiguous instructions and airport construction as contributing factors.

synopsis: PA-28 Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at X04.
summary: A pilot practicing landings in an Archer at X04 avoided a collision with a silent light sport aircraft that turned crosswind early. The G1000 traffic alert prompted an immediate climb, preventing impact within 200 feet, while the pilot attributed the near miss to Archer blind spots and the other pilot's lack of radio calls.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported feeling dizzy along with another Flight Attendant and attributed it to having to wear a protective mask.
summary: During cruise, a pilot and flight attendant felt dizzy while holding due to a thunderstorm, attributing the symptoms to prolonged mask use. The crew recovered during descent but reported that mandatory mask wear hinders safety briefings and poses a significant operational risk.

synopsis: Technician reported miscommunication during a functional check of the engine fuel shut off valves, resulting in the inadvertent discharge of both engines' fire bottles.
summary: During an operational test of engine fuel shutoff valves, a mechanic accidentally discharged both engine fire bottles by pressing the wrong switches in the cockpit. The reporter confirmed the discharge, completed the original task, and suggested installing a shield over the discharge switches to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: GA pilot reported aircraft was too high but instead of going around, reporter decided to land aircraft resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The sole pilot, acting as PIC, executed a slip to correct a high approach but forced a fast landing instead of going around. This caused the aircraft to skid sideways into the grass, resulting in no damage or injury.

synopsis: Pilot reported receiving a traffic alert shortly after takeoff requiring immediate evasive action. Pilot noted that the PHL TRACON Controller seemed incredibly busy, thereby potentially missing the conflict.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 1 received a Traffic Alert from PHL Approach to turn 270 degrees after a conflict with an aircraft in ILG Class D airspace. The pilot attributed the delay to high workload, looking for unseen traffic, and avionics not being in traffic mode, though the conflict was resolved.

synopsis: Pilot reported recently installed taller power-line poles located near WI14 airport and drop zone pose a safety threat to aircraft and skydivers.
summary: A power company installed new, taller poles 200 feet from the airport threshold, creating a safety risk for landing, departing, and skydiving operations. The FAA deemed notification of airport management unnecessary despite the power company's report.

synopsis: Pilot flying PA28 aircraft veered off flight path on approach and landed off runway.
summary: A pilot flying a fleet aircraft inbound to ZZZ for grass landing practice veered left on final approach and landed off the designated grass strip into a dirt/grass area. The pilot attributed the incident to uncertainty regarding alignment with the runway and noted that no damage occurred to the aircraft or ground.

synopsis: C421 Captain reported a runaway pitch trim system during cruise. Captain disconnected the autopilot, regained control of the aircraft and landed at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise, a pilot flying an unfamiliar aircraft experienced autopilot oscillation and runaway nose-up pitch trim. After manually trimming the aircraft and pulling the circuit breaker, the crew regained control and made an uneventful landing for an operational check.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilots reported entering the incorrect routing in the FMS resulting in a track heading deviation.
summary: Pilots flying a multi-leg mission experienced an FMS routing error after a runway change due to wind shear, causing the aircraft to skip arrival fixes and fly direct. The deviation was caused by incomplete verification of the modified flight plan, leading to an ATC query before the crew corrected the route and reloaded the approach.

synopsis: PA-18 pilot reported a runway excursion upon landing.
summary: A pilot and student lost directional control during landing in a modified Super Cub when the student inadvertently applied the left brake. The aircraft departed the runway left due to delayed rudder correction, with contributing factors including improper seat installation, aft CG, and trim system issues, resulting in no damage.

synopsis: Pilot flying BE36 aircraft ran off end of runway on landing.
summary: The pilot flew a higher straight-in approach to Runway 22 in rain, touching down late and failing to go around despite noticing an increased tailwind. The aircraft overran the runway end at 5–15 knots after maximum braking was applied.

synopsis: F11 TRACON Controller reported a conflict after an aircraft came over at the incorrect altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Orlando arrivals and student practice approaches at SFB issued a heading to Aircraft Y without evaluating proximity to Aircraft X, which was at an incorrect altitude. The controller attributed the loss of separation to high workload, delayed sector splitting, and underestimating flight school traffic volume.

synopsis: A Center Controller reported a pilot reported severe turbulence that caused an injury.
summary: An air traffic controller routed Aircraft X through a congested gap in convective weather, issuing a descent to 19,000 feet based on pilot reports. The pilot subsequently encountered severe turbulence in the next sector, sustaining a head injury, though the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: Center Controller reported clearing an aircraft for a NA (Not Authorized) Approach, and observing the aircraft descend below the MEA.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared an aircraft for an RNAV approach to ZZZ airport, but the pilot descended below terrain because the approach was Not Authorized per a missed NOTAM. The controller attributed the error to ERIDS display issues, high traffic volume, and inadequate briefing on the procedure's status.

synopsis: A11 TRACON Controller reported an aircraft had an NMAC with another aircraft the Controller had just terminated radar with.
summary: Air Traffic Control issued traffic advisories to Aircraft X and Y outside Class C airspace, but the pilots failed to see each other. Aircraft X reported an emergency climb to avoid a near collision with Aircraft Y, attributed to frequency congestion, traffic complexity, and pilot visibility limitations.

synopsis: Global Express Captain reported a brief period of loss of aircraft control due to an unforecasted high altitude severe weather encounter.
summary: The flight crew encountered an unforecast high-altitude thunderstorm during cruise in VMC, causing autopilot and auto-throttle disengagement, stall warnings, and overspeed indications. The Pilot Flying executed a brief evasive maneuver to return to course and altitude, followed by a thorough post-flight inspection.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported executing a go-around due to a quartering tailwind and then electing to divert to filed alternate.
summary: The Captain and First Officer executed a missed approach below 200 feet due to an unstable approach caused by gusting tailwinds and inoperative EGPWS windshear mode. With no suitable runways available and deteriorating weather, the crew diverted to their filed alternate.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported forgetting to get a landing clearance from Tower.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring forgot to contact Tower at the specified point while managing landing configurations, resulting in a landing on Runway XXR without clearance. The crew attributed the error to the pilot's inexperience and distraction, though Tower issued no immediate comment upon runway exit.

synopsis: Flight Crew flying aircraft encountered Headwind Shear on takeoff roll.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff on RWY 15 at V1 (154 KT) due to a 'HEADWIND SHEAR' alert caused by rapidly shifting winds not in the ATIS. After a maintenance inspection confirmed brake temperatures were safe, the aircraft successfully departed on the second attempt.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported the Captain used improper taxi procedures causing the taxiway excursion.
summary: The flight crew experienced a taxiway excursion on taxiway Lima after the Captain removed both hands from the tiller to block sun glare, causing the aircraft to veer off the centerline. The nose gear settled off the paved surface, requiring the aircraft to be towed back to the ramp due to improper tiller use.

synopsis: Pilot flying C99 aircraft encountered passenger door opening inflight.
summary: During initial climb, a faulty cabin door sensor failed to indicate an unlocked air-stair door, which subsequently opened causing a loud bang and wind noise. The pilot reduced power, executed a shortened pattern, and landed safely on the departure runway with no visible airframe damage.

synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC on final to FNL airport.
summary: A flight instructor and student on a visual approach to FNL encountered Aircraft Y cutting in front during final approach after Tower misidentified traffic positions. The pilot executed a go-around and turned north, attributing the conflict to a miscommunication between Tower and Aircraft Y, who lacked radar traffic awareness.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported electrical problems and landed at alternate airport.
summary: The pilot reported an alternator failure at 8,000 feet caused total electrical loss, disabling radios, transponder, and navigation while climbing to 10,000 feet. Unable to communicate or squawk, the crew landed at the visible airport and notified Flight Service via cell phone.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: AA5 pilot reported an NMAC with a light twin at 7,000 feet in the vicinity of ZZZ, citing the failure of his transponder as possibly contributing.
summary: A VFR pilot flying a GTN750-equipped aircraft encountered a faulty GTX345-R transponder and returned to ZZZ airport. While under Class B airspace, the pilot executed a 500-foot descent to avoid a head-on conflict with Aircraft Y, attributing the near miss to the lack of transponder output preventing ADS-B detection.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported UIM VOR is NOTAMed out of service. However, the VOR approaches for F51 and 3F9 which use UIM VOR as primary navigation are not NOTAMed out of service/unusable.
summary: A pilot reported that the UIM VOR out-of-service NOTAM was not visible during a default 4 NM route search, despite affecting F51 and 3F9 approaches. The reporter warned that pilots might miss this information and recommended NOTAMs explicitly list these approaches as unusable.

synopsis: Lear 45 pilot reported a possible altitude deviation due to GPS failure.
summary: Pilots reported a GPS failure and an early descent on a flight from ZZZ1 to ZZZ3, caused by a controller's mistaken assumption of the destination airport. Post-landing, radar data indicated the descent began 9.7 miles prior to the required waypoint, prompting an investigation into the failed GPS antenna and FMS.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a track heading deviation after accidentally pressing the heading select switch.
summary: The pilot flying accidentally selected the heading switch instead of level change on the MCP during a descent to 6,000 feet on the ZZZZZ1X arrival, causing an unintended left turn. Approach control issued a corrective heading within five seconds, and the pilot attributed the error to button proximity and reduced recent flying experience.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of another air carrier on approach to MEM.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft while joining the RWY 09 localizer at 3,000 feet, causing significant bank angles and a momentary stick shaker. They manually recovered, completed a visual approach, and landed safely, attributing the event to insufficient spacing in light winds.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported during climbout they received a route change that was not on the filed route.
summary: The flight crew departed ZZZ with a route change requested from Dispatch that ATC had not received, causing a clearance mismatch after takeoff. Confusion arose from expectation bias, time compression, and a PDC format showing "NONE" for revised segments, leading the crew to re-file the correct route in the air.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an unstabilized approach and setting up to land on a closed runway with anticipation of changing to landing runway later.
summary: A check airman and trainee First Officer on Aircraft X failed to reprogram the FMS for Runway Y after a STAR change, causing an overshoot due to high workload and poor communication. The crew corrected the deviation and stabilized the approach after ATC vectors, attributing the error to untimely training and automation differences.

synopsis: CE-560XL Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV while on final approach.
summary: A pilot on final approach to Runway 19 at TEB observed a twin-rotor drone 200 feet below and ahead on the approach course. The crew passed over the drone without deviating from the localizer or glideslope and reported the sighting to the Tower.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported departing a runway and then observing an aircraft departing from a crossing runway causing an airborne conflict.
summary: Pilots departing from Taxiway Alpha at ZZZ Tower encountered a potential collision with an aircraft climbing from Runway YY due to a lack of separation advisories from a trainee controller. The crew avoided the conflict by holding altitude and turning right, noting the controller attributed the issue to visual separation despite no prior notification.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an unstabilized approach, disconnected the autopilot and stabilized at 500 feet and landed uneventfully.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to XXR exceeded 1,300 FPM below 1,000 feet AGL while correcting a late descent to capture the glide slope. The event was caused by a lapse in monitoring descent rates by both pilots, though the landing remained uneventful.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported experiencing a track heading deviation due to FO entering the wrong heading on the PFD. Captain and ATC caught the mistake and corrected the heading.
summary: The First Officer, acting as pilot flying on a localizer approach to ZZZ, selected an incorrect 347-degree course instead of 273 degrees, causing an unintended turn. The Captain disengaged the autopilot to hand-fly the correction, attributing the error to the First Officer's skill decay after three months off duty.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported experiencing a course deviation and stated being away from flying was a contributing factor.
summary: The First Officer and Captain flew an Aircraft X type into ZZZZZ, overshooting the final approach course due to unsequenced FMS and distraction by automation. The Captain corrected the deviation, and the crew landed uneventfully after recognizing their failure to maintain proper scan discipline.

synopsis: Flight crew reported not flying the assigned heading on departure and being corrected by ATC. The crew referenced lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: A fatigued, low-frequency crew mistakenly turned direct to fix ZZZZZ1 after an FD Mode Off warning during climb to FL190, deviating from the briefed runway heading. ATC queried the deviation and corrected the aircraft to maintain the original SID heading, attributing the error to haste and rustiness.

synopsis: Pilot reported due to light weight and high climb rate the aircraft received a Resolution Advisory.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS RA during climb to 7,000 feet caused by rapid ascent toward crossing arrival traffic at 8,000 feet. The pilot attributed the event to failing to reduce climb rate upon visual contact, noting it was their first flight after a two-month absence.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a track heading deviation. ATC questioned their routing and the crew realized they had an amended clearance.
summary: The First Officer and Captain departed on an incorrect FMS departure due to failing to cross-check the PDC amendment during preflight. Air Traffic Control identified the deviation eight minutes after takeoff, cleared the aircraft to a fix 50 miles away, and the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: A SR22 Instructor Pilot reported a NMAC with opposite direction landing traffic at a non-towered airport.
summary: Two pilots in Aircraft X missed Aircraft Y on opposite runways during landing due to Aircraft Y's incorrect radio frequency and non-standard straight-in approach. The crew executed a go-around, missing the other aircraft by 100 feet, with no TCAS warnings or radio contact received prior to the event.

synopsis: A PA-32 pilot landing with a complete electrical failure reported they did not realize their landing gear had not extended and made a gear up landing skidding off the runway.
summary: The pilot and two passengers experienced a progressive electrical failure during climb, losing engine monitoring, transponder, and radios, leading to a gear-up landing at an uncontrolled airport. The pilot attributed the accident to misdiagnosing the complete electrical failure as a minor avionics issue and failing to verify gear extension before touchdown.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported issues relating to a circling approach to Runway 32 at RDU and ATC communication issues for the circling approach.
summary: An instructor conducting an instrument rating practical test at RDU requested a missed approach due to tailwinds on Runway 32. The Tower Controller canceled the clearance, vectored the aircraft across active final approaches without coordinating with Departure, and the pilot alleged this punitive vectoring was dangerous retaliation for refusing a tailwind landing.

synopsis: PA-28 Instructor reported an NMAC event while complying with ATC departure instruction.
summary: A pilot with a student deviated from a 4,000 ft clearance to avoid a collision with an unreported multi-engine aircraft after receiving a direct routing from Center. Although initially flagged for possible pilot deviation, supervisors later confirmed the climb was a necessary safety decision.

synopsis: Aerial pilot reported an NMAC event during takeoff with another aircraft in landing pattern due to a communications breakdown.
summary: The pilot of a departing aircraft at ZZZ misunderstood a Cessna 172's radio call regarding a touch-and-go on Runway XY. This miscommunication caused the pilot to take off without visual contact, resulting in a 150-foot separation as the Cessna crossed the departure path.

synopsis: Pilot reported fuel starvation caused loss of power and an immediate landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a complete engine power loss at 900 feet AGL during a go-around pattern due to the right fuel tank intake un-porting from climb angle. The pilot executed a forced landing approach, switched to the left tank, and regained power just before touchdown on Runway XYL.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reported radio interference on PGV CTAF 122.8. Pilot reported a local radio station as the possible source.
summary: Pilots experienced significant interference on CTAF 122.800, likely from a local radio station, which distracted the crew and forced them to lower the volume to monitor other operational radios. A system check revealed no aircraft or radio discrepancies, and other aircraft in the area reported similar interference.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with an aircraft on very short final.
summary: The pilot on short-final for RWY XX executed a go-around after Aircraft Y, operating on the wrong frequency, performed a tight diving base that overflew and nearly struck their aircraft. The near-miss resulted from Aircraft Y's incorrect frequency usage, non-standard pattern entry, and failure to monitor CTAF traffic.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported a NMAC with a skydiver.
summary: A VFR pilot climbing to 6,500 feet north of Lake Elsinore encountered a skydiver at the same altitude and executed an aggressive right bank to avoid a mid-air collision. Although the pilot believed they were clear of published drop zones, ATC subsequently vectored them right to heading 360 shortly after the event.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reported a NMAC while conducting touch and goes with a student at an uncontrolled airport.
summary: An instructor and student in a training aircraft encountered Aircraft Y on final approach at un-towered BDN, leading to a near collision during the student's takeoff. The pilot attributed the event to delayed visual acquisition and hesitation to abort, noting that high traffic volume at the airport warrants a control tower.

synopsis: GA pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at VDF airport.
summary: The pilot overtook Aircraft Y by approximately 200 feet while turning downwind during touch-and-go operations. The close call resulted from the pilot's tight pattern and failure to account for speed differences, causing a loss of visual separation with no damage.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported loss of directional control and a runway excursion after landing due to a failed tire probably related to heavy braking.
summary: The pilot executed a short-field landing with maximum braking, causing the left main tire to fail and the aircraft to veer off the runway onto the grass. The probable cause was excessive braking that locked the wheel on the rough surface, resulting in a flat tire and a NOTAM issuance.

synopsis: Pilot reported an ongoing problem with loss of radio communications with Anchorage Approach while flying near a commercial radio station that reportedly bleeds through the ATC frequencies. Reportedly, the radio station is located 5 NM south of PABV airport.
summary: A pilot flying northbound from PALH lost radio contact with Anchorage Approach on 118.6 due to interference from a commercial broadcast station near PABV. The reporter recommends changing the frequency to 125.15 to eliminate the bleed-through and ensure clear communications in the Mat-Su Valley.

synopsis: Pilot reported landing without clearance due to a sticky radio switch and lack of incoming radio transmission, and thinking the Tower was closed due to COVID-19.
summary: A pilot landed at ZZZ without radio contact due to a sticking intercom switch and expectation bias that the tower was closed. The pilot assumed the tower was closed based on misinterpreting ASOS as ATIS and failed to verify the transmit light, resulting in an uneventful landing at an operational tower.

synopsis: Pilot reported listening to the ATIS which stated the Tower was closed, and started a taxi towards the runway when Ground called the pilot and advised Tower was still open.
summary: The pilot received an ATIS stating the tower was closed, but Ground Control clarified it was still open and issued a taxi clearance. The controller admitted posting the closure early to avoid forgetting, and the tower closed shortly after the pilot's takeoff.

synopsis: PA-28- pilot reported steering issues after landing which then lead to a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of an Archer aircraft left the runway during the landing roll after residual left rudder input caused the nose gear to turn left. This resulted in a collision with three runway side lights, denting the right flap and wing leading edge, though no landing gear or propeller damage occurred.

synopsis: Pilot reported losing control of aircraft due to crosswind on landing resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff on RWY XX due to an unanticipated crosswind causing directional control loss and a runway excursion. No injuries or apparent damage occurred, though the landing gear will be inspected.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot departed airport without communication with Tower. Pilot mistook LOCAL time for ZULU time, and departed the airport when Tower was open.
summary: The pilot experienced radio failure and confusion over Tower closure times (Zulu vs. local) while taxiing and departing from ZZZ. After repairing the radio in cruise, the pilot successfully contacted the Tower and landed without incident.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they began taxiing out without clearance. Captain stated lack of flying was a contributing factor.
summary: The Captain initiated taxi from Gate YY to Runway XX without clearance, mistakenly believing the First Officer had received it while radios were congested. Ramp Control stopped the aircraft, and the reporter attributed the error to reduced proficiency following a long layoff.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported getting confusing intersections and routings they were not familiar with and were also concerned about being routed more than 50 miles off shore by ZJX Center, which reportedly does this often.
summary: During enroute weather reroutes from EYW to ZZZ, the flight crew encountered ATC-issued fixes missing from their databases and exceeding 50 NM offshore limits. The reporter attributes the confusion to ZJX Center using outdated chart data and poor coordination during a flow change, requiring a handoff to ZHU for correct routing.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate jet Captain reported the co pilot descended too low on a Visual Approach despite their instructions and received a Terrain Alert.
summary: During final approach, the Pilot Flying descended rapidly due to workload from a departing aircraft, ignoring the Pilot Monitoring's warnings about terrain. A terrain warning activated, but the crew continued to an uneventful landing after the Pilot Flying momentarily leveled off without climbing as requested.

synopsis: CE680 pilot reported they parked in an area designated for commercial aircraft because it was not properly marked and had to be towed to the correct area. The tug driver told the pilot to release brakes and the aircraft rolled backwards prior to being attached to the tug.
summary: The pilot released the parking brake after a line service agent requested it, but the tug was not attached, causing the aircraft to roll 75 feet backward. The nose wheel scissors spun 180 degrees, exceeding the 90-degree limit, though the aircraft remained on the paved surface without hitting anything.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a waypoint crossing altitude dropping out of the FMS and not knowing why resulting in an altitude deviation.
summary: The First Officer flying a ZZZZZY arrival inadvertently lost the FL240 crossing restriction at ZZZZZ intersection after updating the descent speed in the FMS, causing an uncommanded descent of approximately 1,200 feet. The crew corrected the deviation, notified ATC, and completed an uneventful arrival after being cleared direct to ZZZZZ1.

synopsis: A319 pilot reported a NMAC at altitude requiring an RA maneuver.
summary: An Airbus A319 crew at FL390 received a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to a B-2 bomber flying below its assigned altitude. The First Officer and Captain manually climbed to FL393 to avoid a near mid-air collision, attributing the incident to controller and B-2 crew situational awareness failures.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported construction related taxiway markings confusion at DFW airport in the vicinity of Runway 17R and taxiways EG, EH, EF.
summary: A pilot reported two incidents at DFW where aircraft incorrectly held short of Runway 17R between taxiways EG and EH due to confusion over a closed EF taxiway and misleading painted markings. The reporter attributes these errors to pilots mistakenly expecting three hold-short points and suggests issuing a warning or implementing a temporary hotspot.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported receiving a cabin pressure master warning during departure and executed a return to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a cabin pressurization warning while climbing through 12,500 feet in an aircraft recently removed from storage. They returned to the departure airport, landed safely, and suspected the cause was a forgotten configuration change during storage, though the exact switch position remained uncertain.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported auto-thrust did not engage and loss of both flight directors during climb.
summary: Pilots reported that during takeoff and climb, the autothrottle, LNAV, VNAV, and flight directors failed to engage or provided false guidance. Consequently, they hand-flew the aircraft, requested radar vectors, and descended to FL270 to avoid RVSM airspace, landing safely without identifying a specific cause.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported a land gear malfunction/warning after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced a gear disagreement and gear door issue shortly after departing ZZZ. After performing the alternate extension procedure and a flyby to verify gear lock, they returned to ZZZ for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported landing safely after receiving a right main landing gear warning.
summary: The crew executed a missed approach after the right main gear failed to indicate down, experiencing a loud noise and jolt during retraction. Despite conflicting cockpit warnings, the aircraft landed safely with the gear visually confirmed down by the tower, requiring maintenance to pin the gear post-landing.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported equipment problems that made it difficult to continue working.
summary: The pilot diverted Aircraft X to ZZZ due to a lack of fire detection or protection. The diversion calculation software crashed during the event, forcing the pilot to rely solely on WSI fusion and Jeppesen for weather and NOTAMs.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported brake temperatures high on taxi for takeoff, resulting in a return to gate and maintenance placing Autobrakes on MEL.
summary: The flight crew of Flight ABC in Aircraft X experienced a brake temperature light illumination and inability to taxi after a long taxi on Runway XXR due to windy conditions. Maintenance identified and deferred a faulty auto brake system, allowing the aircraft to depart for ZZZ2 uneventfully after repairs.

synopsis: Ramp personnel reported finding undocumented Hazmat in cargo compartment which had been mistakenly transported.
summary: The loadmaster and offloading crew discovered a Hazmat box in the bulk cargo bin at ZZZZ that should have been offloaded at ZZZZ1. The aircraft unknowingly transported the item without required paperwork, resulting in its removal.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported flight assigned clearance routing not authorized in company Operations Specifications manual.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X departed ZZZZ despite missing CAT II Ops Specs and incorrect routing permits. The flight held over Countries Z and X while ATC and Flight Control coordinated a reroute, made possible by the aircraft's tankered fuel.

synopsis: B767-200 Captain reported discovering at the gate that 4 tires had failed, possibly related to a fault in the brake system.
summary: The pilot reported a smooth landing and taxi where four tires (2 and 5) blew without noticeable vibration or antiskid activation. Maintenance later identified a wiring issue as the cause, while the pilot suspected a momentary brake lockup on the left side.

synopsis: B767-200 Captain reported a gear door problem and landed with out incident.
summary: The flight crew experienced gear disagree and door EICAS messages after retraction, triggering QRH procedures and an alternate extension with delayed green lights. They performed a low approach for visual confirmation and landed with gear doors open while ATC had emergency equipment standing by.

synopsis: Technician reported performing a routine, scheduled inspection on the number two engine VG actuating system and finding a screwdriver resting on the W1 wire loom of an EMB-175 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic discovered a screwdriver left under the W1 harness during an inspection of the #2 engine VG actuating system on Aircraft X. No damage occurred, but the tool posed a potential FOD risk, prompting recommendations to improve tool control and final area inspections.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Technician reported a work order was missed and not completed.
summary: A mechanic reported failing to apply a work order for LED light installation after reading a digital message, likely due to excessive workload while staffing the desk alone during over 150 flights.
