summary: A student pilot attempted takeoff on runway 27C in Aircraft X, triggering a stall warning due to a faulty airspeed indicator. The instructor took control, managed the climb using power settings and control feel, and landed safely on runway 27L after diagnosing the known instrument issue.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported receiving a windshear warning on takeoff and failing to perform the Wind Shear Maneuver.
summary: During an IMC takeoff, the First Officer encountered a wind shear caution but failed to execute the escape procedure by not advancing thrust levers or making the callout due to misperception of automatic thrust. The Captain also missed the callout, but the crew maintained control, recovered, and later briefed on improving communication and procedure adherence.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported after encountering a bleed malfunction a critical step was missed in the QRH due to task saturation.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring missed a QRH step during a BLEED 1 LEAK event while climbing to FL250, causing the crew to return to ZZZ. The reporter attributed the error to task saturation from managing ATC communications, weather deviations, and the abnormal situation simultaneously.

synopsis: Captain reported that task saturation during a go around resulted in an altitude deviation.
summary: The pilot hand-flew a windshear escape at ZZZ in IMC, encountering an Engine 2 Bleed Overpressure message and climbing to 3,200 ft instead of the cleared 3,000 ft. The deviation resulted from task saturation, severe weather, and delayed automation use during the recovery.

synopsis: E175 First Officer reported the stall warning system continued to activate even though there was no apparent change in airspeed or aircraft attitude.
summary: The crew of Aircraft Z experienced intermittent AOA Limit and WSHR Fail EICAS messages and a brief stick shaker activation during an ILS approach into ZZZ in tropical storm conditions. The pilot flying deemed the shaker false due to stable flight parameters, completed the landing, and noted persistent AOA and ADS failures after taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: Technician reported discovering a component that was missing and not installed while troubleshooting an anti-skid discrepancy;
summary: A mechanic discovered a missing magnetic flux ring on the #5 Main Landing Gear wheel assembly while troubleshooting an anti-skid status message MEL. The wheel assembly was subsequently replaced on a later date.

synopsis: Technician reported incorrect external markings on numerous aircraft in violation of FAR's.
summary: The First Officer reported that Aircraft X arrived at the gate with FAA-required markings outside the FO window incorrectly stenciled in white instead of red on a white background. The issue was documented in Log XXXXXXX.

synopsis: Technician reported receiving two portable fire extinguishers from the stores without parts tags filled out correctly.
summary: A mechanic reported receiving two water fire extinguishers from stores with blank next due dates on M175-e tags, requiring immediate reweighing. The report questions whether the Non-Rotable Parts Tag shelf life correctly indicates the next weigh or hydro date and suggests a new program to prevent future compliance issues.

synopsis: Technician reported that an open maintenance item was overlooked on audit and the aircraft was delivered to the terminal for revenue service.
summary: A mechanic reported an open DFDAU verification item on Aircraft X remained unsigned in AirVault after the aircraft was released for revenue service. The reporter attributed the release to unclear AMM instructions, lack of guidance from Operations Control, and a failure of the maintenance audit to catch the unresolved defect.

synopsis: RV-10 pilot reported they were distracted by an electrical issue and forgot to switch fuel tanks causing the engine to stop in flight. The pilot landed the aircraft successfully.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine stoppage due to forgetting to switch fuel tanks while distracted by intermittent low amp readings. After advising ATC, the pilot landed safely at ZZZ with no incident.

synopsis: Pilot reported power loss on the right engine caused an inflight shutdown and a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X experienced a right engine power loss at 4,500 ft cruise, feathered the propeller, and diverted to ZZZ1 under IFR. The aircraft landed uneventfully and is now under maintenance to determine the cause of the power loss.

synopsis: Cessna P210 pilot reported that an engine oil leak occurred in cruise flight resulting in a diversion.
summary: The pilot experienced rough engine running and low oil pressure at FL190 while operating LOP, indicating a magneto issue and an oil leak at the turbocharger return line. After requesting an expedited descent from ATC, the pilot landed safely at ZZZ without incident.

synopsis: Cessna 182 Single Pilot reported a critical ground conflict on landing with opposite direction landing aircraft.
summary: Aircraft Y landed on the opposite runway during my landing phase, forcing me off the runway. The reporter states Aircraft Y made no radio calls on the local frequency, though no damage occurred to either aircraft.

synopsis: PA-46 Pilot reported loss of directional control on landing resulting in a runway excursion and a ground strike.
summary: The pilot of a PA-46M600 experienced a runway excursion to the right during landing at ZZZ1 after the nose gear failed to steer. The pilot attributes the incident to a flawed nose gear design that caused the wheel to caster and force the aircraft off the paved surface, resulting in wingtip and propeller damage.

synopsis: P-210 Pilot reported an engine out landing due to improper operation of a fuel boost pump.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine stoppage during a low-speed landing on the northerly runway after leaving the fuel boost pump on, which likely flooded the engine at idle power. The pilot landed safely, restarted the engine by turning off the pump, and concluded the incident was unlikely to have caused a reported runway light strike.

synopsis: Airline Ramp Personnel reported flight crew refused Dangerous Goods cargo due incorrect ground handling resulting in the contents spilling onto the ramp.
summary: Ground personnel failed to secure locks on a pallet before transport, causing it to slide on the ramp and shift its contents. The load was subsequently refused for flight because it contained dangerous goods.

synopsis: First Officer reported being instructed to secure the number two engine for a single engine taxi to the gate, but accidentally shut off both engines.
summary: The First Officer accidentally pulled the number one engine start lever to cutoff while securing the number two engine for a single-engine taxi at ZZZ, causing both engines to shut down. The crew restarted the number one engine and taxied to the gate without further incident, attributing the error to rushing after a two-month leave.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an unstabilized approach and flaps not at final setting before 1,000 feet AGL. Captain stated he should have commanded the First Officer to go-around and cited lack of recent flying as a contributing factor.
summary: A returning First Officer and a Captain on a post-leave flight executed a high-energy visual approach with late flap configuration below 1,000 feet. The crew stabilized for a safe landing but attributed the unstable approach to lack of currency, poor communication, and failure to initiate a go-around.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported smoke in the cockpit during climb that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew of a ZZZZ-ZZZZ aircraft experienced a burning smell and smoke from the right forward window heat during climb to 40,000 ft. The crew returned to ZZZZ, deactivated the window heat, and deferred the malfunction per the MEL before departing again without further issues.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew and TRACON Controller reported an airborne conflict for skydive operation aircraft which maneuvered too close to a commercial fixed winged aircraft.
summary: Pilots descending on an RNAV STAR between 9,000 and 7,000 ft received a TCAS RA when a skydiving Cessna turned toward their path. The crew leveled off at 8,000 ft after the Cessna descended through their altitude without ATC separation, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they executed three go-arounds before successfully landing on the fourth attempt. Captain cited gusty conditions, lack of recent flying and unfamiliarity with airport as contributing factors.
summary: A pilot flying their first flight in 83 days at an unfamiliar airport executed three go-arounds due to wind changes, an unstabilized approach, and a stick shaker activation caused by speed loss during a turn. The pilot attributed the incident to lack of proficiency, stress, and terrain, but eventually landed safely.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported the aircraft was not properly configured for approach per company procedures. Reporter cited the need to fly more frequently.
summary: A new pilot reported being advised post-flight for failing to configure the aircraft by 1,000 feet due to a misunderstanding of company procedures. The incident involved turning too close to the FAF, maintaining excessive speed, and leaving power on during glideslope capture, attributed to a lack of recent flight hours.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported that while attempting to lose altitude on an unstable approach the Captain exceeded a 45-degree bank angle and a flap overspeed occurred. A second overspeed occurred during the subsequent go-around.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain's lack of descent planning and poor manual handling caused an unstable approach, excessive bank angles, and flap overspeeds, necessitating a go-around. The incident resulted from inadequate briefing, tunnel vision, and refusal to use automation or accept assistance.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a runway incursion which resulted from a call sign misunderstanding. A contributing factor was that the Tower Controller was managing multiple frequencies and runways.
summary: Flight ABCD crew inadvertently entered Runway XXR after mishearing a takeoff clearance intended for another aircraft due to ATC call sign confusion. The crew queried Tower upon alignment, received a hold-short instruction, and was subsequently cleared for takeoff with no safety compromise.

synopsis: Airline Captain reported an uneventful RTO event due to warning light illumination during takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot aborted the takeoff roll at 60 knots after a hydraulic low indicator illuminated. The cause was unknown but possibly linked to recent gear servicing, and the pilot successfully executed normal abort procedures.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported that there are two types of CPR devices available on board, however flight attendants are qualified to use only one, which requires removal of the personal protective mask in order to use. Reporter requests training on the other device to keep everyone safe in a COVID-19 environment.
summary: A flight attendant reported that current one-person CPR training requires removing PPE to use a pocket mask, increasing infection risk in a COVID environment. The reporter argues that training on Bag Valve Masks would maintain safety for crew and passengers while ensuring effective oxygenation before ALS arrival.

synopsis: Air carrier maintenance technicians reported that the rudder was inadvertently damaged while preparing to perform rudder lube on an aircraft that was being returned to service from storage.
summary: Mechanics damaged the rudder while removing flight control locks on an aircraft coming out of storage. The damage occurred when they used hydraulic systems to move the rudder instead of manually supporting the trailing edge with an additional person as required by the AMM.

synopsis: Lead Technician reported ground damage that was misidentified by Ramp and CSM personnel was severe enough to remove the aircraft from service for repairs.
summary: During pushback, a tug struck Aircraft X's right nose landing gear door, bending the retraction push-pull rod. Although a Ramp CSM cleared the flight, Maintenance later found the rod broken, grounding the aircraft and causing the reporter to attribute the incident to ramp pressure for on-time departures.

synopsis: Glider Pilot and Observer reported a Critical Ground Conflict after landing while still in the runway safety area with departing traffic.
summary: During a training rope break, a glider recovery team crossed a runway while Aircraft Y commenced takeoff. Despite the team broadcasting "STOP" on CTAF, Aircraft Y continued its roll and passed the recovery team by approximately 50 feet.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC with a gyrocopter in the pattern at DWH airport.
summary: A training flight executing a touch-and-go on Runway 17R had to make an evasive left turn after a gyrocopter taking off from parallel Runway 17L drifted into the extended upwind. The reporter attributed the midair collision risk to ATC clearing the gyrocopter while the aircraft was on short final and instructed to make left closed traffic.

synopsis: SR-22 pilot reported diverting to a nearby airport when he experienced a power loss and high cylinder head temperatures.
summary: During the second leg departure, the pilot experienced rising cylinder head temperatures, engine chugging, and power loss at 11,000 ft due to a loose turbo manifold hole and unsecured fuel lines. The pilot diverted to a nearby airport, avoiding mountains, and landed safely after power partially recovered; the aircraft is now grounded for repairs.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reported diverting to a nearby airport after noting a CO LEVEL HIGH aural alarm.
summary: The pilot received a high CO alarm during climbout and executed an expedited landing at a restricted Air Reserve Base. The alarm was later attributed to the air conditioning recirculation being left on instead of off per the checklist.

synopsis: Citabria pilot reported using a restricted airport without prior permission.
summary: The pilot landed a Citabria at ZZZ without realizing a NOTAM required eight hours of prior permission for runway use. The incident resulted from the pilot's complacency in assuming the small, abandoned airport did not have closure restrictions.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of electrical power and having to land while NORDO.
summary: The pilot experienced total electrical failure enroute due to a loose alternator terminal and fatigued wires. After losing GNS530w comms and squawking 7600, the pilot continued VFR to ZZZ3, used a handheld radio to enter Class D airspace, and landed safely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported they landed on the opposite runway than what was in use at a non towered airport.
summary: A pilot landed on the inactive Runway 32 instead of the active Runway 14 due to failing to assess airport operations or confirm the active runway. No incident occurred as other aircraft in the pattern likely took corrective action, prompting the pilot to adopt a new flyover procedure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Private Pilot reported being wrongly accused of performing aerobatics over airport.
summary: The pilot of a turbine aircraft was approached by a law enforcement officer on the ramp who mistakenly accused him of aerobatics and unsafe flying. The officer likely confused the pilot with another aircraft performing stunts, as the pilot had only conducted non-aerobatic formation and photo flybys.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported experiencing an electrical and avionics failure while conducting a training flight. While attempting to speak to the student without using a headset, the instructor noted it was difficult to communicate because the COVID-19 mask muffled the voice.
summary: During a dual VFR flight, the instructor and student experienced a total avionics failure suspected to be caused by a short in the right seat headset jack or push-to-talk switch. After restoring power by removing the jack, the student landed safely at ZZZ, though communication was hindered by the instructor's face mask.

synopsis: Corporate pilot reported having to execute a missed approach after a delayed approach clearance left the flight too high to conduct a stabilized approach. The pilot stated that the Controller was very busy working multiple frequencies and asked flights to stand by for call backs.
summary: Pilots conducting an ILS approach reported an unstable descent due to delayed visual clearance from an overworked controller managing multiple frequencies. The crew executed a missed approach at 800 feet AGL but completed a safe landing on the subsequent attempt.

synopsis: Center Controller reported a Supervisor who had tested positive for COVID-19 had interacted with controllers. Controller suggested allowing only essential workers in the building.
summary: A controller at ZZZ ARTCC tested positive for COVID-19 after exposure to a supervisor who also tested positive while working on-site. The reporter attributes this unsafe situation to management allowing non-essential personnel, including supervisors, to enter the facility despite the pandemic.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported confusion after reviewing the fuel load for the flight.
summary: During preflight, the First Officer and Captain identified an ACARS performance data error for a short flight that initially showed Takeoff thrust without an Assumed Temperature. Dispatch corrected the Block fuel and provided a new OFP with an Assumed Temperature, preventing a potential unsafe takeoff with excessive thrust settings.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported communication issues between the flight deck crew and flight attendant crew regarding odor in the cabin.
summary: During climbout from ZZZ, flight deck airflow decreased and cabin crew reported a "dirty socks" smell, though other attendants later described a bird strike odor. Post-flight inspection revealed a bird strike on the right engine, and the Captain attributed the continued flight to FA1 failing to relay the accurate bird strike observations to the flight deck.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a particular aircraft is allowed to keep flying without ADSB using an outdated MEL.
summary: Maintenance applied an outdated MEL for inoperative ADSB out, allowing the aircraft to fly multiple legs despite FAA requirements. The reporter states the MEL is unusable as written and the aircraft should have been grounded due to unavoidable ADSB airspace entry.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reports several wing navigation lights are overheating and maintenance continues to just do a reset. Pilot reported landing at night with no navigation lights.
summary: The pilot reported recurring inoperative wingtip navigation lights on multiple aircraft, including a CRJ, resulting in a night landing at busy airport ZZZ without lights. The pilot suspects a fleet-wide temperature sensor issue causing Maintenance to rely on temporary resets rather than permanent repairs, creating ground collision risks.

synopsis: SA227 Captain reported dual failure of the fuel quantity gauges and resulting operation of the aircraft with less fuel than planned.
summary: The pilot experienced dual fuel quantity indicator failures and a magnastick malfunction during a flight, compounded by an inadvertent fuel pump switch-off. The discrepancy was identified postflight via logbook review, attributed to system failures and complacency in verifying fuel levels.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported aft galley trash cart broke free from its restraints during landing and rolled into the cabin area.
summary: On an ERJ-175 landing, a rear galley trash cart dislodged despite being secured and rolled into the cabin aisle, stopping at row 19. The reporter attributed the incident to failing safety latches and brakes under vibration, noting a passenger claimed an elbow impact though no visible injury occurred.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a ground delay due to an inoperative APU and failure of Ground Support Equipment with temperatures of 108 degrees F.
summary: Lead flight attendant reported a one-hour departure delay on Aircraft X due to a broken APU and an exploded air start machine battery in 108-degree heat. Passengers and crew suffered extreme cabin temperatures, with two passengers overheating, while ground equipment failures and fuel delays prevented timely air starting.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that upon arrival at destination, a COVID-19 positive passenger on board as well as the crew, had to be medically assessed before being allowed to leave the aircraft.
summary: Flight attendants and pilots on Flight ABC remained on board after arrival in ZZZZ while a medic assessed a COVID-positive passenger. Although initially cleared to leave, three flight attendants were later required to stay until the passenger deplaned to meet minimum crew requirements.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing partial power loss.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power surging and diverted to ZZZ after ATC suggestion. Partial power was restored, allowing a safe landing at ZZZ, which ATC subsequently verified.

synopsis: Pilot reported a broken bracket cause the propeller control cable to detach, causing loss of prop control and a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a variable pitch propeller control failure at 15,500 feet while descending to ZZZ airport, prompting a priority landing request. A mechanic later identified a broken propeller bracket arm that disconnected the control cable from the governor, which was subsequently repaired.

synopsis: Pilot reported an electrical system failure that resulted in a diversion.
summary: Two pilots flying a new aircraft on a ferry flight experienced repeated total electrical system failures due to a corroded battery lead and a contaminated voltage regulator. The crew diverted to ZZZ3 using cell phones after avionics failed, and a mechanic repaired the electrical issues and an unrelated engine defect on the ground.

synopsis: Instructor reported observing student have a runway excursion upon landing.
summary: A student pilot flying Aircraft X veered off the runway to the left during a solo landing after applying brakes at touchdown, causing the aircraft to swerve and strike a sign. The reporter attributes the incident to the student's over-control and brake application, resulting in substantial left-wing tip damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported overshooting final and possibly having a NMAC with another aircraft also on final.
summary: The pilot flying a right traffic pattern for Runway 20R overshot final due to a tight pattern and executed a steep correction. This resulted in a likely NMAC with Aircraft Y on the parallel runway's short final, as reported by the pilot.

synopsis: Corporate pilot and ATC reported multiple flight plans filed and the wrong one was used causing the deviation.
summary: Pilots and controllers experienced clearance confusion due to duplicate flight plans, causing the aircraft to deviate into an active MOA during climb. The pilot attributed the error to ATC issuing a clearance based on a canceled plan and subsequent read-back failures, while the controller cited a pilot deviation from the filed route.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported problems with the engine overheating and having to make an expedited landing.
summary: The pilot reported a multi-cylinder CHT rise and engine failure during climb from ZZZ, likely caused by a faulty right magneto. After diverting to ZZZ2, the engine recovered, allowing a safe landing; the aircraft is now grounded for repairs.

synopsis: Pilot reported a runway excursion while under training for the aircraft.
summary: An instructor flying a tailwheel aircraft lost directional control during a 3-point landing due to focusing on pitch correction rather than runway alignment. The aircraft veered off the right side of the runway at slow speed but stopped without damage or injury.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Traffic Controller reported assigning a correction vector heading after mistakenly assigning a previous vector which resulting in the aircraft flying below MVA.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X into a 2,800 ft MVA at 2,500 ft while sequencing it behind Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the error to poor judgment and high workload, noting that maintaining 3,000 ft would have prevented the obstruction conflict.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a taxiway incursion and stated distraction from COVID-19 pre-flight related procedures contributed to the event.
summary: The pilot reported that the flight crew failed to obtain release clearance from Ramp Control before switching to Ground for taxi after pushback. The pilot attributed this procedural error to external distractions and internal threats, noting that Ramp Control prefers to initiate the frequency switch themselves.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported non functional PAPI lights at airport for a specific runway and the safety hazards it could pose in weather conditions, especially when crews are not flying as often due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: A pilot in a type X aircraft landed on Runway YY with a tailwind due to rain and night conditions, avoiding Runway X where PAPI lights were inoperative. The reporter noted that a heavy type Y aircraft would have been forced to use the non-functional lights, citing reduced pilot proficiency and poor airport maintenance as safety concerns.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported concerns with lack of flying and the possibility of being paired with a First Officer who has also not flown in months.
summary: A Captain on reserve expressed concern that pairing pilots with abbreviated training and months of inactivity, including displaced First Officers and demoted Captains, creates significant safety threats. The reporter questions how crews can mitigate risks when both pilots lack recent flight time and consolidation training before assignment.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Small Transport Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV while descending through 10,000 feet.
summary: A pilot reported spotting a stationary black and red object, estimated to be a drone, approximately 200 feet above the aircraft while descending through 10,000 feet. The object was visible for only two seconds during a VFR scan, leaving insufficient time to react.

synopsis: Captain reported missing an ATC communication, resulting in Low Alt alert and a Missed approach and go around.
summary: During an RNAV GPS approach in VFR conditions, the crew descended below the ATC-mandated 6,800 ft hold altitude due to a missed instruction, triggering a low altitude alert. The crew climbed back to 6,800 ft, cancelled their IFR flight plan, and completed a visual approach with no safety impact.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported 'strong cigarette smoke-like' odor during initial approach for landing.
summary: During descent below 16,000 ft into ZZZ, the crew detected an intermittent cigarette smoke odor with no visible smoke. Priority handling was requested from ATC as a precaution, and the smell dissipated after the aircraft blocked in.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported experiencing a speed deviation during departure and stated lack of flying contributed to the event.
summary: The pilot reported an airspeed deviation to 285 kts while climbing from ZZZ after ATC changed the altitude clearance to 19,000 feet. The event was caused by the pilot being behind the aircraft and automation, compounded by a lack of proficiency due to an 80-day absence from flying.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported receiving a GPWS terrain alert on arrival into BOI, followed by recognition of an unstabilized approach that resulted in a go-around.
summary: The flight crew flew an RNAV X 28R approach into Boise, exceeding the 180-knot speed restriction at CUBAR by mistake due to VFR distraction. This triggered terrain alerts and an unstable approach, forcing a missed approach before a safe landing was achieved on the second attempt.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported they noticed a loss of brake pressure while taxiing and after parking observed flames from the leak. Pilot extinguished the flames.
summary: The pilot discovered a soft right brake and fluid leak while parking on the ramp, then observed a fire between tires 3 and 4 during the walk-around. The pilot extinguished the fire within one minute using an onboard extinguisher before maintenance arrived to monitor the continuing fluid leak.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing an unstabilized approach resulting in a go-around. The crew also stated they overshot their altitude during the go-around.
summary: The crew flew a ZZZ arrival at 250 knots unconfigured, expecting ATC to manage speed, but received a visual clearance too late to stabilize. They executed a go-around due to excessive descent rate, overshot 2,000 feet from task saturation, and attributed the event to delayed slowing and reduced operational proficiency.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported being distracted with having to verify that a passenger had a medical condition and therefore did not have to wear a mask. During the distraction the Flight Attendant missed the Captain's PA 'prepare for takeoff' and was not seated as the flight departed.
summary: The #2 Flight Attendant was not in her jumpseat for takeoff after becoming distracted by a passenger mask issue and borrowing a tablet. She remained in the forward galley at the crew's direction to avoid injury, attributing the error to stress from new pandemic procedures.

synopsis: Technician reported installing a new PBE on an aircraft without informing, nor training the flight crew on how to use it.
summary: A maintenance technician activated a new PBE part number in the system to replace expiring units, but inflight crew were not trained on the new equipment. The reporter noted that using the X form would have triggered necessary crew coordination, and suggested removing the new PBEs to maximize yield from existing stock.

synopsis: EMB500 Captain described the minor air conditioning problem, the incorrect loading of the FMS and subsequent track deviation.
summary: A single pilot at a busy metropolitan airport rebooted the aircraft to fix a failed air conditioning system, losing pre-flight checks and FMS data. Rushing to reload systems while stowing bulky luggage caused the pilot to create a departure situation.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Center Controller reported they cleared a corporate jet aircraft for an approach to an airport that only authorized Air Taxi operations.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for a visual approach despite a NOTAM restricting landings to scheduled Air Taxi aircraft only. The pilot cancelled their IFR clearance and landed safely, though the controller noted the ambiguous restriction caused confusion and plans to use memory joggers to prevent future errors.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported an aircraft was unable to comply with the climb rate required on the SID and flew below two Minimum Vectoring Altitudes.
summary: The pilot departed without advising an inability to meet the required climb gradient, causing the aircraft to descend 2,000 feet below Minimum Vectoring Altitudes due to multiple departures. The reporter attributes this to a lack of departure order information and recommends resuming rolling notifications.

synopsis: Center Controller reported an airspace violation and traffic conflict while opening a sector from one Controller working three sectors which were unmanageable due to weather deviations and volume.
summary: An air traffic controller assumed a chaotic sector with incorrect flight plans, unentered hold messages, and high-altitude holding aircraft, leading to an unresolved conflict between two aircraft where one received a resolution advisory. The incident resulted from inadequate briefing, poor coordination, automation errors, and an unauthorized airspace deviation that distracted the controller.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported they left an engine running after parking at the gate. They cited as contributing factors the failure to complete a checklist due to distraction.
summary: A Line Check Airman flying as First Officer on a line-check flight failed to shut down Engine #1 after parking due to distractions from ground personnel and checklist non-compliance. The engine was discovered running by the Captain approximately two minutes later and was subsequently shut down.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing a taxiway incursion and stated that Ground Control did not issue direction of turn instructions as they typically do and appeared to be overworked.
summary: The Captain inadvertently turned right instead of left onto taxiway B while taxiing from Spot XX to Runway XXL at ZZZ, deviating from the B K Z clearance. Contributing factors included time pressure from a delayed departure, stress, and a lack of specific turn instructions from an overworked Ground controller, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported an uneventful Missed Approach and landing due to an unstable approach during previous approach.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around at 300 feet during a visual approach to ZZZ due to being below the glide path, indicated by four red PAPI lights. The reporter attributed the unstable approach to an over-correction in pitch and recommended disengaging the autopilot earlier to trim the aircraft properly.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they refused to accept an aircraft when questions arose concerning airworthiness after engine fail during start.
summary: Following a report of sparks from the right engine fan blades on a Boeing 767, the Captain refused to accept the aircraft after a mechanic performed an insufficient inspection and failed nine engine start attempts. The incident highlighted unsafe maintenance practices, including an unauthorized sign-off and a lack of qualified personnel to verify the engine's airworthiness.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the flight was left high by ATC on arrival which contributed to missing step down altitudes and receiving a low altitude alert as the flight descended.
summary: Pilots on ZZZZZ5 arrival into ZZZ were left 5,000 feet high by Center and miscommunicated with Approach regarding descent clearances. The crew descended rapidly in Level Change, failed to capture the VNAV path due to potential equipment issues, and landed visually after a low altitude alert.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported flying the JACKSON ONE SID as published and told by ATC they were off course.
summary: Pilots flying the JACKSON ONE SID experienced a faulty FMS database that prematurely cued a left turn before the OED VOR. ATC advised maintaining heading for traffic separation, noting this is a known issue with the departure requiring manual navigation to green needles.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on departure.
summary: The pilot reported that wake turbulence from a preceding 717 caused a left wing dip at 600 feet during climb, prompting Tower concern about the turn to GRITZ. Despite the disturbance, the aircraft remained on the correct flight path with no deviation.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they are not being provided with proper disinfectant wipes and PPE.
summary: A cabin crew member reported finding no disinfectant wipes on two different aircraft that RONed at separate stations. The crew member used personal supplies to clean the flight deck, noting a lack of provided PPE and recommending wipes be a mandatory go/no-go item for RONs.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported landing without a clearance from Tower and stated that fatigue and lack of recent flying contributed to the event.
summary: The flight crew landed at ZZZ1 without transmitting a landing clearance to Tower due to fatigue and task saturation during a visual approach. Although the crew missed the radio call, Tower had provided a green light, and the aircraft taxied to the gate uneventfully.

synopsis: Technician completing a routine check on stored aircraft reported finding torn speed tape in the Pack 1 and 2 inlets and exhaust. Reporter could not visually verify if the tape had entered the system due to the duct bends.
summary: A mechanic inspecting Aircraft X in long-term storage found torn speed tape on Pack 1 and 2 inlets and exhausts. Unsure if debris entered the ducts, the mechanic replaced the tape and installed streamers to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: CRJ flight crew reported they forgot to remove one of the pitot tube covers before takeoff but were able to continue to their destination.
summary: The crew climbed out in thunderstorms with the standby pitot cover still installed, likely due to a rushed preflight acceptance checklist. Although the flight continued safely with normal instruments, the cover was confirmed on the ground, highlighting a failure to verify equipment rather than rote responses.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported retracting the flaps during climb before the appropriate airspeed and stated that fatigue, hunger, and excessive heat in the aircraft contributed to the event, and the COVID-19 mask was a distraction.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring retracted flaps before reaching appropriate speed during climb due to fatigue, heat, and obscured PFD visibility. The Captain corrected the nose attitude, allowing the aircraft to accelerate safely despite high density altitude.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported taking off without a clearance and stated that being distracted by the COVID-19 pandemic and the state of the airline contributed to the event.
summary: The flight crew departed Runway XXR without a specific takeoff clearance, mistakenly assuming it was included in the taxi clearance. The pilot attributed this error to complacency, expectation bias, and external stressors related to the pandemic and airline downsizing.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew experienced an altitude deviation while descending on approach and attempting to slow the aircraft. Crew stated that loss of situational awareness and Captain's lack of recent flying contributed to the event.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring descended below the cleared 3,000 feet crossing altitude at ZZZZZ intersection during a visual approach due to high workload and premature de-automation. Approach Control alerted the crew to the deviation, which was corrected after the pilot flying lost situational awareness while managing speed and configuration.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported an unstable approach while on flight to maintain landing currency.
summary: The First Officer, pilot flying on a visual approach with an inoperative radio altimeter, descended below 1,000 feet without being fully configured for landing. The crew attributed the unstable approach to the First Officer's lapse in situational awareness and over-reliance on the Captain's radio altimeter.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported an altitude deviation citing distraction and not working for several months as contributing factors.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring, returning from leave, neglected duties while distracted by landing prep, allowing the aircraft to descend below the 17,000-foot arrival floor to 15,500 feet. The Pilot Flying leveled off after ATC queried the deviation, holding altitude until reaching the arrival fix.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot described the need to understand all implications resulting from the failure of GPS.
summary: The reporter identified a Honeywell iMMR defect causing GPS signal loss that invalidates pre-departure RAIM checks. This risk could force diversions during landing if flights are dispatched relying on GPS approaches that become unavailable due to the faulty receiver.

synopsis: First Officer reported they failed to comply with two RAs during takeoff so as to avoid flying toward terrain and a possible GPWS warning.
summary: Tower cleared the departing aircraft for takeoff while another was on final, causing a TCAS RA conflict at 8,300 feet due to insufficient separation. The crew descended then climbed to avoid terrain, resulting in a second RA before the conflict cleared, with the pilot attributing the event to tower placing the aircraft too close.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported encountering unexpected severe turbulence which caused an uncontrolled altitude deviation.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew encountered severe turbulence despite no radar returns, causing VNAV/LNAV disengagement, a 500–600 foot altitude deviation, and a brief overspeed warning. The crew manually controlled the aircraft to regain altitude and re-engaged automation after exiting the turbulence.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the First Officer's window came open while taxiing. The Captain reports this is a recurring issue in the aircraft type with First Officer's not be trained correctly to ensure their window is secured.
summary: During taxi out, the First Officer's R2 window popped open after cabin service personnel failed to properly lock it following a wash, despite the handle appearing secured. The Captain attributes the incident to inadequate Operations Manual guidance, noting that visual checks and manual bumps are insufficient to verify window security.

synopsis: Flight crew reported an uncommanded power rollback in the right engine, which resulted in an inflight shutdown and a subsequent landing.
summary: During descent from 15,000 to 11,000 feet into ZZZ, the crew experienced an uncommanded power rollback and subsequent loss of the right engine, indicated by zero fuel flow and low oil pressure. The crew followed QRH procedures to perform an in-flight shutdown and completed a safe single-engine landing, though the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported company policy was not followed regarding Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) when the pilot crew arrived at the gate.
summary: The flight crew reported no PPE or disinfectant wipes were provided on the flight deck prior to departure. Consequently, the pilot used personal wipes from home, noting that gate agents should supply proper disinfectants to reduce flight deck access.

synopsis: First Officer reported an uncommanded inflight engine shutdown, causing a partial single engine landing.
summary: The pilot flying reported an engine failure on Engine #1 during a night arrival into ZZZ, caused by an FMC-induced throttle movement that led to an EGT exceedance. The crew successfully restarted the engine but elected to land single-engine with the left throttle at idle due to recurring vibration, noting they should have declared an emergency and notified cabin crew earlier.

synopsis: Crew reported crossing the runway hold-short line after turning on the wrong taxiway during taxi for takeoff at Reno.
summary: The flight crew at RNO crossed the hold short line of Runway 16L while taxiing, assuming clearance because instructions directed them to Taxiway C on the opposite side. Tower ordered an immediate stop as a Cessna 172 began its takeoff roll, but the Cessna departed safely and the crew subsequently received clearance to cross and take off.

synopsis: First officer reported that ATC denied their requested deviation for weather avoidance, and cited nonstandard phraseology by the controller.
summary: Pilots requested a five-degree right deviation for weather avoidance while IMC between TEUFL and GEEYE. Jacksonville Center denied the request, citing traffic separation, and offered a thirty-degree turn toward additional weather before the crew reached VMC and remained on course.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported receiving calls on Guard frequency to contact JAX Center on different frequencies, but the Controller who responded appeared to have no knowledge of the frequency changes.
summary: While en route to RSW, the flight crew received conflicting frequency instructions from JAX Center via Guard, leading to a communication gap and an agitated controller. The pilot attributed the incident to internal JAX Center coordination issues regarding the Guard frequency change and descent clearance to FL 240.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported a 'Slow Airspeed Warning' situation during a weather related go-around event and cited lack of flying time as a contributing factor.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain executed a go-around during a heavy rain ILS approach due to deteriorating weather and crosswinds. The event was caused by the PF's delayed weather update and poor crew coordination, where the Captain raised the landing gear instead of setting flaps, triggering a low airspeed warning.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported missing an altitude crossing restriction while on arrival.
summary: The Captain struggled to meet a 280-knot crossing restriction at ZZZZZ1 while in LNAV/VNAV PATH due to FMS limitations on the flat Plan page. After admitting the issue to ZZZ Approach, the crew received a descent clearance to FL190 without further vectors, noting retirement distractions as a contributing factor.

synopsis: B737-800 fight crew reported the flight attendants notified them of a smoky odor in the cabin following an encounter with a flock of birds during takeoff. The flight crew elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered a bird strike at 50 feet after departing ZZZ, damaging the nose and causing a cabin odor. After consulting Dispatch and Maintenance, they returned to ZZZ and landed safely following the report of 11-12 birds struck.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported this non movement area near Taxiway A is difficult to see at night. Reporter did not provide the airport.
summary: The pilot reported that during night taxiing from taxiway L to spot X, sporadic blue reflective stakes bordering an island were invisible due to aircraft lighting angles. This required the pilot to alert the Captain to prevent a collision, forcing a quick left-right maneuver to avoid the island.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported the Captain executed a go-around after experiencing an unusual rolling tendency on final approach.
summary: During the first approach below 1,000 ft AGL, the crew experienced unusual rolling tendencies and executed a go-around. On the second approach, the aircraft floated slightly, and the Captain failed to deploy thrust reversers after landing, though the crew cleared the runway safely.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported inadvertently moving the pack switches to off instead of high flow causing a cabin depressurization during climbout.
summary: The First Officer inadvertently turned the air conditioning packs OFF while climbing through 5,000 feet, causing a cabin altitude warning above 20,000 feet. The crew donned oxygen masks, descended to 10,000 feet, and returned to the departure airport due to the error caused by heat, distraction, and muscle memory.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the difficulties experienced with Dispatch and Clearance Delivery as they requested an alternate route to avoid thunderstorms.
summary: The crew encountered uncooperative Dispatch and Clearance Delivery while attempting to reroute a night flight to avoid thunderstorms. Despite receiving a revised release, Clearance Delivery initially provided the original storm-bound routing, forcing the crew to rely on ATC to clear them around the weather after takeoff.

synopsis: Air Carrier Pilot Crew reported while using the autopilot, ATC informed them the aircraft was off course.
summary: Pilots flying an autopilot-coupled approach to ZZZ from ZZZZZ to ZZZZZ1 were advised by Approach Control they were off course due to an FMS profile deviation. The crew later learned from ATC that a known profile issue existed, prompting them to hand-fly the final approach after receiving confusing intercept instructions.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported difficulty communicating with the tug driver during pushback because the tug driver was wearing a mask in compliance with COVID-19 procedures. Reporter suggested the mask was not necessary when the driver was alone in the tug.
summary: A tug driver wearing a COVID mask communicated muffled commands to the cockpit crew during ground operations. The reporter states this hindered understanding of non-routine instructions and recommends drivers not wear masks covering their mouths to ensure clear communication.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported landing without a clearance, citing fatigue and scarcity of other aircraft operating due to COVID-19 reductions as contributing.
summary: The pilot failed to contact Tower at the FAF during a visual approach due to fatigue, late hour, and low traffic. After landing, the pilot switched frequencies and received taxi instructions, noting that crew briefing on vigilance or proactive ATC contact could have prevented the error.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported failure to call for the Before Push checklist, then also failing to call for the Before Taxi checklist, citing lack of flying due to COVID-19 cutbacks as contributing.
summary: The Captain missed the Before Push Checklist due to expectation bias, leading to the Before Taxi Checklist being skipped and a takeoff warning horn sounding with flaps up. The crew stopped, completed the missed checks, and continued the flight uneventfully.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger refused to comply with COVID-19 mask requirements in flight.
summary: A flight attendant assisted a passenger experiencing motion sickness by providing aspirin and a sick bag after the passenger soiled clothing. The attendant repeatedly requested the passenger wear a mask in her seat, noting she was unaccompanied, and provided another sick bag upon landing.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger was upset with the airline's COVID-19 policies when observing other passengers removing their masks to eat and drink.
summary: A cabin crew member reported a passenger confrontation regarding mask policies and seat changes during boarding and flight. The passenger became agitated after being informed that masks may be removed for eating and that weight restrictions prevented her seat change, eventually demanding the crew member's name.

synopsis: Air carrier flight attendant reported a passenger was upset with being told to comply with regulations regarding their child seat. Flight Attendant suggested many passengers seem more stressed than usual because of COVID-19 pandemic procedures.
summary: Cabin crew identified a rear-facing infant car seat blocking an aisle seat during descent at 18,000 feet. The passenger initially agreed to move it for landing but became combative when reminded again, though the crew maintained the safety requirement to clear the exit path.

synopsis: Flight Attendant in charge reported an inadvertent slide deployment.
summary: Flight Attendant #1 accidentally deployed the 1L slide at the gate while checking the door handle after the First Officer requested a verification. The slide deployed because upward pressure was applied to the handle, resulting in no injuries before mechanics released it and passengers deplaned.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported having mild symptoms of being ill, but decided to take another two day trip. Flight Attendant continued to feel ill after the two day trip warranting a COVID test, which was positive.
summary: A pilot reported feeling mild illness symptoms before flying a two-day trip but felt fine during operations. The pilot later tested positive for COVID-19 and concluded that not flying while possibly ill would have prevented the infection.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Airline Mechanic reported being notified Hazmat parts he was working were left on board after he departed.
summary: A mechanic performing an A2 check on Aircraft X reseated electrical connections to fix failed inflatable restraint tests, while three unused hazmat batteries remained in the galley. The reporter attributed the oversight to a lack of communication with other mechanics who were cleaning up the parts.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported landing without a clearance.
summary: The First Officer flew an ILS approach in clouds while the Captain managed communications but failed to switch to the Tower frequency. The crew landed without a landing clearance, realized the error while vacating the runway, and subsequently received taxi instructions after apologizing to ATC.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported executing a forced landing on a highway after experiencing power loss associated with high cylinder head temperatures.
summary: The pilot experienced engine overheating and loss of power during a second climb, forcing a forced landing on a highway. The aircraft skidded into grass upon touchdown after the engine failed, resulting in a loss of directional control.

synopsis: Single Pilot reported a possible deviation from the clearance and problems communicating with the controller while airborne.
summary: A pilot and instructor conducting a training flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1 requested an inbound flight plan and squawk code while airborne, contrary to the controller's requirement for a full stop and phone call. The controller provided the clearance after noting a briefing misunderstanding, and the Airport Manager later confirmed this deviation was acceptable only at ZZZ2, not ZZZ1.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor pilot reported an NMAC event immediately after takeoff.
summary: An instructor and student pilot in an aircraft departing Runway 19 encountered Aircraft Y at 500 ft AGL and 1/2 mile south of the airport. The crew executed a nose-down right turn to avoid a collision after Aircraft Y crossed their flight path at the same altitude.

synopsis: C172 instructor was pilot flying and reported not following published procedures, causing a track deviation.
summary: The Pilot Flying, instructing a student, inadvertently flew within 200 feet of Class Bravo airspace at 7,500 feet due to an unnoticed OBS button activation. The pilot concluded that maintaining flight following and monitoring ForeFlight would have prevented this deviation from the planned direct route.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Captain activated TOGA intending to activate frequency select, which resulted in an overspeed and altitude deviation.
summary: A pilot flying an RNAV approach accidentally activated go-around mode by pressing a TOGA button instead of a frequency switch due to aircraft configuration differences. This caused an autopilot disconnect, rapid acceleration, a gear retraction overspeed, and an altitude excursion above the cleared 3,000 feet before the pilot regained control and completed a subsequent uneventful landing.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported student's hard landing resulted in left main landing gear brake damage with limited aircraft control.
summary: A student pilot and CFI experienced a hard landing and tail strike during a student's second landing attempt due to a runway stall and delayed power application. The impact damaged the left brake caliper, causing inoperative brakes and a near ground loop during taxi.

synopsis: Cessna 206 pilot reported an NMAC departing when he had the volume set too low for CTAF communications.
summary: The pilot experienced a radio failure while requesting IFR clearance, leading to a runway incursion with a DA 20 landing aircraft during takeoff. The landing pilot executed a go-around to avoid a collision, and the pilot attributed the incident to the radio malfunction and inadequate visual scanning.

synopsis: CE560XLS First Officer reported an exterior panel missing post flight.
summary: The Captain discovered a missing panel on the aircraft's bottom during post-flight inspection. The reporter, who was not responsible for the exterior preflight check per standard operating procedure, was unaware of the condition.

synopsis: Pilot reported that during taxi another aircraft was blocking entry into the parking area and that parking options were limited due to many parked aircraft since COVID-19 started.
summary: The pilot taxiing to Section X at ZZZ after landing was blocked by a holding twin aircraft, forcing a stop and a clearance change to let the twin exit first. The controller attributed the issue to the pilot's late entry, while the pilot questioned the proper procedure for reporting blocked taxi paths.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported a NORAD aircraft in pattern traffic overtaking them resulted in pilot exiting traffic pattern to avoid conflict.
summary: Pilot of Aircraft Y reported a traffic conflict at a non-towered airport while both aircraft were in the pattern. Due to Aircraft X's unintelligible radio calls, erratic long downwind, and aggressive closing speed, Aircraft Y executed a go-around and a non-standard pattern exit to avoid a collision.

synopsis: Pilot reported taking evasive action on takeoff to avoid a midair collision with an aircraft not following controller's instructions.
summary: The RV-10 pilot and family encountered a converging low-wing single-engine aircraft while climbing through 200 feet AGL after an IFR takeoff clearance. The pilot executed an immediate avoidance maneuver after the tower issued a traffic alert, resulting in the other pilot being reported for deviation from tower instructions.

synopsis: Pilot reported misidentifying landing airport due to MVFR weather and sun glare.
summary: The pilot, unfamiliar with CRG in MVFR conditions, mistook JAX for CRG due to similar runway configurations and haze while being vectored by approach. After realizing the error when tower corrected their position, the pilot was re-vectored and landed safely on RW32.

synopsis: ZAB ARTCC Controller reported staffing issues, TMU lack of airspace knowledge and social distancing concerns.
summary: Air traffic controllers and management faced unsafe conditions during high traffic when TMU and OMIC ordered the opening of an overloaded sector due to airspace knowledge gaps. This resulted in controllers exceeding two-hour position limits, inadequate breaks, and a trainee violating social distancing protocols while working near equipment.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: JNU Tower Ground Controller reported a taxiing aircraft turned the wrong direction and struck a sign which was placed too close to the movement area. The Controller reports users and airport ground workers are confused and not clear about new taxiway markings and procedures which have not been implemented and charted correctly.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X struck a large sign with its right wingtip while taxiing on Taxilane Hotel to Runway 8. The incident resulted from the pilot making an unauthorized sharp left turn and the airport placing an unlighted sign too close to the movement area amidst widespread confusion over new taxiway markings.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a taxiway incursion. Captain cited lack of recent flying.
summary: The First Officer missed a taxi turn to Runway XR due to low recent experience and confusion from a last-minute runway change. Ground control advised the error, and the crew reprogrammed the FMC and followed new instructions to reach the runway without further incident.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported ground personnel advised them to release brakes when they were not connected to a tug and the aircraft rolled backwards.
summary: During aircraft receipt at a fixed jetway, the flight crew released brakes on ground crew instruction while not attached to a tug, causing an uncommanded backward movement. The incident was resolved after the Captain verified the aircraft was secured to the tractor before the final parking attempt.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported they had numbers for a full runway takeoff, but were given and executed an intersection takeoff.
summary: The flight crew of Flight ABC departed from an intersection on Runway YYR using full-length takeoff data due to a lack of situational awareness and inadequate crosschecking. This resulted in an unnecessarily long takeoff roll with only 2,000 feet of runway remaining at rotation, though the flight continued normally.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported departing without proper takeoff data, citing high workload and career uncertainties related to COVID-19 cutbacks as contributing.
summary: The First Officer departed an aircraft without printed takeoff data due to reduced crew, remote location, and disrupted habits that broke situational awareness. The pilot accepts full responsibility for the error, noting that standard crosschecks with marked paperwork would have prevented the unsafe departure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported noticing during preflight that electronic charts for his destination were not loaded in his tablet computer.
summary: A captain transitioning back to the X-type aircraft could not load the correct Jeppesen approach plates on their tablet despite IT assistance and a device reset. The pilot obtained a loaner tablet from operations to ensure the flight proceeded safely, noting that other pilots might face similar chart availability issues for divert airports.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported concern about the airline's policy of dispatching flights with very low fuel reserve.
summary: The flight crew reported that company pressure forced Dispatch to plan minimal fuel, resulting in a landing with only 1,700 lbs despite training requiring 2,000 lbs. The pilot conserved fuel by slowing in cruise and nearly declared MIN fuel, noting that any further vectors would have caused a fuel emergency.

synopsis: EMB-505 Captain reported a battery exceedance message resulted in a diversion.
summary: The flight crew received a battery exceedance EICAS message at FL410 during cruise. After completing the QRH and diverting, they landed and taxied to the ramp without further incident.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot departing a mountain airport reported a traffic conflict with opposing traffic and climbed even though TCAS told them to descend due to the nearby mountainous terrain.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS RA conflict at 8,700 ft. shortly after departing Aspen while an aircraft was on 10-mile final. The pilot climbed to avoid terrain after a second RA, suspecting insufficient separation between the departing and arriving aircraft caused the incident.

synopsis: B767 Captain and First Officer reported multiple air data malfunctions that resulted in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced airspeed and altitude disagreements, followed by rudder ratio and aileron lockout warnings during climb from ZZZ. An unidentifiable aerodynamic rumble worsened with speed, prompting a return to ZZZ and a manual landing after the left autopilot failed to engage.

synopsis: Flight crew reported striking a pole with wing while parking.
summary: During a tight 270-degree ramp turn guided by four marshallers, the aircraft's wingtip struck a security camera pole. The marshallers failed to monitor wing clearance, resulting in damage to the sharklet despite the crew feeling an impact they mistook for a pothole.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a 30 minute delay in response from Dispatch regarding a deviation for weather. Dispatcher cited reductions in staffing due to COVID-19 as contributing.
summary: The flight crew encountered turbulence warnings and attempted to contact Dispatch via SATCOM and ACARS for a route deviation but received no response for 30 minutes due to staffing shortages. The crew eventually coordinated a 150 nm deviation with ATC, noting the delay was unacceptable and could have prevented emergency assistance.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the First Officer made a sudden steep turn on departure while following command bars. The Captain took control of the aircraft and noted that the FO was very tired and had not done a takeoff or landing in over a year.
summary: During departure from ZZZ, the First Officer executed an uncommanded steep left turn while following incorrect GPS command bars, prompting the Captain to take control. The reporter attributes the deviation to the First Officer's lack of recent flight experience and fatigue, noting the departure procedure was not loaded into the GPS despite pre-flight briefing.

synopsis: First Officer reported visual terrain contact to ATC followed by an uneventful landing after EGPWS warning.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an EGPWS warning during the base-to-final turn due to nearby terrain. They maintained visual separation and landed safely, though the reporter noted they should have turned earlier and maintained higher altitude.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported they taxied to the ramp as cleared by EWR Tower and did not contact Ramp Control because it appeared to be closed. First Officer stated that due to the changing responsibilities of controllers, it was difficult to know what the correct procedures were.
summary: The pilot landed at EWR and taxied onto an active ramp area believing it was closed based on Tower instructions and visual cues. The pilot realized the error after contacting Ramp Control, attributing the confusion to inconsistent airport procedures and Tower handling multiple roles during COVID-19.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported false Cargo Smoke Detector alerts in flight.
summary: During climb, the flight crew experienced intermittent Cargo Smoke ECAMs caused by a failed smoke detection function in the CIDS. After a 10-15 minute delay contacting MX Control, they rerouted over land and landed safely at ZZZ without incident.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that continual, significant changes in crew schedules over the past months are causing cumulative fatigue.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported a gear overspeed event on the second-to-last leg of a four-day trip with three consecutive minimum rest overnights. The pilot attributed the error to chronic fatigue caused by constant schedule changes that overrode their bid preferences for fatigue mitigation.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported taxiing to the gate at LGA airport without contacting Ramp Control. The crew cited as contributing factors a confusing ramp diagram and the expectation that Ramp Control was closed due to the pandemic situation.
summary: The flight crew at LGA mistakenly taxied to the wrong terminal gate after assuming Ramp Control was closed due to late hours and unclear chart labeling. A ground agent redirected them, and they subsequently contacted Ramp Control to receive clearance for the correct gate.

synopsis: E170 flight crew reported Flight Deck door malfunctioning in flight.
summary: The flight deck door jammed when the Captain exited for the lavatory, forcing him to rip it open after the pin was removed. The crew secured the door with a beverage cart for landing, resulting in a safe arrival without incident.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger using the restroom numerous times, coughing and having to constantly be reminded to wear a mask.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger made nine lavatory trips and repeatedly removed his mask during taxi and flight due to coughing and illness. The crew notified the pilot, who arranged for a customer service agent to meet the passenger upon arrival, where he deplaned last.

synopsis: Technician reported problems with job cards not being signed off correctly.
summary: Technicians failed to document battery disconnect and reconnect steps in the Aircraft Maintenance Log during short-term storage and return of Aircraft X. A paperwork audit identified the discrepancy caused by miscommunication, leading to corrected records and a reminder to verify work before submission.

synopsis: GA pilot reported engine roughness after takeoff.
summary: The pilot experienced partial engine power loss immediately after retracting flaps during takeoff from ZZZ, likely due to fuel moisture or debris. The engine roughness resolved over the harbor, allowing a safe return to ZZZ1 with no fuel contamination found upon post-flight inspection.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported severe turbulence.
summary: The pilot encountered severe turbulence and rapid altitude changes while descending to 4,000 feet near ZZZZZ1 intersection after ATC vectors through thunderstorms. The pilot disengaged the autopilot to maintain control and stabilized at 3,200–3,300 feet with no injuries or other aircraft involved.

synopsis: Pilot reported loss of directional control and taxiway excursion at C02 airport and cited poor condition of taxiway as contributing.
summary: A pilot taxiing a C02 after a VFR landing reported the aircraft sharply veered right into a dirt mound due to poor taxiway conditions, including potholes and overhanging branches. The pilot shut down the engine and recommended improved maintenance or a NOTAM closure.

synopsis: Cessna Pilot reported a runway excursion and aircraft damage caused possible by a mechanical failure.
summary: The pilot reported that after a stabilized landing in clear conditions, the aircraft veered right and exited the runway, striking a lamp with the propeller. The pilot attributed the loss of directional control to a potential mechanical issue, resulting in propeller damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reported engine was unresponsive to throttle movement and running at reduced power, causing a diversion and reduced power glide, with engine failing on touchdown.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss and EGT gauge failure at 5,000 ft, forcing a reduced power glide to RWY XX. After an uneventful landing, the engine was successfully restarted with normal low-power operation, though the EGT gauge remained at zero.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Student pilot at a non towered airport reported an aircraft departed opposite direction to them from a taxiway adjacent to their landing runway.
summary: During short final to Runway 35, a crop duster took off from an adjacent taxiway without radio calls, flying alongside the reporting aircraft at the same altitude. The pilot landed safely but attributed the incident to the crop duster pilot's frustration with traffic or haste, noting that radio communication could have prevented the conflict.

synopsis: Ground employees reported supertug parking aircraft issues and combining separate parking crews, which undermines current COVID-19 policies.
summary: A ramp agent observed a super-tug crew using PAATS equipment with malfunctioning lights to reposition an aircraft under a protected overhang while the ramp was closed for lightning. This unauthorized operation exposed multiple crews to potential COVID risks and resulted in missed aircraft parking due to staffing and communication failures.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported executing a CAT II confidence check approach which was not authorized.
summary: The Captain and First Officer performed a CAT 2 confidence check approach into ZZZ on an aircraft incorrectly listed with a CAT 2 MEL. Although the approach was successful, the check was later deemed unauthorized because the MEL item was erroneously applied rather than removed.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported loss of situational awareness, resulting in a GPWS warning and requiring evasive action to continue approach.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a GPWS warning during the RNAV (GPS) 16L approach at night when the aircraft descended below the glide path. The Captain manually recovered the aircraft after the First Officer called the deviation, resulting in an uneventful landing despite delayed reaction due to distraction.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported navigation system failure during climb.
summary: During climb out, the crew experienced an IRS 2 failure causing FMS/GPS disagreement and loss of autopilot, autothrottle, and flight director. They returned to the departure airport for a visual approach backed by a manually tuned ILS, landing safely despite a nuisance GPWS alert.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported Flight Director malfunction on approach.
summary: During a visual approach to Rwy XX, the crew cycled flight directors at 1000 ft, causing the aircraft to descend below the glide slope while flight directors remained centered. The pilots detected the deviation via PAPI and an aural warning, leveled off, and landed uneventfully, attributing the error to fatigue and failure to monitor flight mode annunciators.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported a Trailing Edge Flaps Disagree Message on final approach that resulted in a Go Around and a precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a TE FLAP DISAGREE message on final approach to Runway XX in ZZZ while selecting flaps from 20 to 25. They executed a go-around, performed the QRH checklist, and landed with priority handling before reporting the flap malfunction to maintenance.

synopsis: Commercial flight crew reported inability to communicate with ramp crew.
summary: The flight crew attempted to push back without functional headsets, leading to a misunderstanding of hand signals where the tug driver pushed without clearance. The aircraft moved away from the gate before the crew could stop the operation, highlighting a need for working communication equipment or standardized signal verification.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported experiencing a stick shaker event after executing a go-around due to windshear.
summary: During an ILS approach at 500 AGL, the crew executed a go-around after Tower reported 40-knot windshear, but communication overload and delayed positive rate calls led to a microburst-induced airspeed loss and stick shaker. The aircraft recovered after full power application and was vectored for 25 minutes before landing uneventfully.

synopsis: CRJ pilot reported a Drone near their aircraft while on approach in Class B airspace.
summary: During a visual approach below 1,000 feet, the Captain and First Officer observed a white object, later identified by a passenger as a drone, approximately 1,000 feet away. The crew landed safely and reported the possible UAV operating within Class Bravo airspace to MSP ground.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported COVID-19 related cleaning supplies are not being provided by company and having to use personal supplies.
summary: The flight crew reported a lack of disinfectant wipes in the flight deck, forcing them to use personal supplies for cleaning. The reporter attributed this to the airline not providing proper PPE and suggested gate agents distribute wipes during check-in.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an inflight engine shutdown that resulted in a precautionary landing.
summary: During cruise at FL410, the crew experienced an Engine 1 failure with high EGT, performed an immediate shutdown, and later restarted the engine. The engine shuddered on approach, forcing a single-engine landing; the crew noted they should have advised flight attendants and requested priority handling earlier.

synopsis: Captain reported a Rear Bay Overheat Warning, causing a diversion.
summary: The First Officer and Captain flying Aircraft X on a Part 135 leg experienced a transient Rear Bay Overheat indication at 7,000 ft MSL during climbout. They diverted to ZZZ3 for an overweight landing, which was completed without incident, though the crew later realized they had delayed completing memory items due to poor communication.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported entering an expected fix in the FMS before it was issued by ATC but forgot to hit execute, leaving the aircraft high and not making the crossing restriction.
summary: The flight crew failed to meet a 35-mile, 10,000-foot crossing restriction at ZZZ airport after their FMS deleted the programmed constraint during a weather deviation. Complacency and reduced situational awareness caused the error, but the aircraft was vectored by Approach and landed normally with no further issues.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported working an overloaded desk and overall staffing issues.
summary: A dispatcher reported managing 30 aircraft due to uneven desk splits and phone routing that prioritized their code-share calls. The reporter attributed the workload to insufficient morning staffing and recommended spreading desks evenly, adjusting phone settings, and encouraging pilots to use direct extensions.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a propeller strike on landing due to oscillations following a ballooned landing.
summary: During landing in 170/14G22 winds, the pilot induced oscillations following a ballooned approach caused a right engine propeller strike. Post-flight inspection revealed damage to the propeller blade tips, highlighting the need for timely go-around procedures.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported jump-seat harness to be installed incorrectly.
summary: A crew member reported that the aft jump-seat harness was installed incorrectly again due to mechanics failing to properly reinstall the middle bolt. The reporter noted this recurring issue has persisted for years despite previous reports and promised work orders.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger did not comply with wearing a face mask.
summary: A cabin crew member reported a passenger who repeatedly wore a face mask on his chin despite being provided one and warned three times. The crew member notified the flight deck after the passenger continued to remove the mask whenever the crew member was not looking.

synopsis: Maintenance Inspector reported an inability to complete a task card because of procedural issues concerning correct jacking of aircraft.
summary: A mechanic inspected the right main landing gear using an axle jack instead of jacking the aircraft as required by the job card. This prevented full access and risked inaccurate measurements, leading to a recommendation to reschedule the task for after the aircraft is jacked.

synopsis: Technician reported experiencing confusion and deferred the wrong bleed valve and applied the wrong MEL.
summary: A mechanic troubleshooting a BLEED 2 fault on an ERJ 175 deferred the wrong valve due to rushing and confusing two adjacent valves with identical part numbers.
