Contract Maintenance later identified the error, which occurred because the mechanic misidentified the high stage bleed valve as the nacelle pressure regulating shutoff valve.

synopsis: Beechcraft D 50 pilot reported engine failure on approach.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine failure due to fuel mismanagement during a straight-in approach, causing a loss of directional control and a half-mile deviation into restricted airspace at low altitude. After feathering the engine and climbing, the pilot exited the restricted area and landed safely at ZZZ.

synopsis: Flight Instructor reported swerving off the runway onto grass while taking off to avoid a skydiver.
summary: An instructor and student in a training aircraft aborted a takeoff due to a skydiver approaching the runway at low altitude. The instructor took control to swerve onto the grass and climb out safely after the student initially rotated, avoiding a collision as the skydiver landed near the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: GA pilot reported error in VFR Charts.
summary: A VFR pilot flying from EWB to 08R was denied clearance by OQU Tower to transit Class D airspace at 2,000 feet, despite the route remaining south of PVD's 10nm ring. The controller stated airspace above 1,299 feet fell under PVD Approach authority, contradicting the chart's depiction of OQU's 5nm limit extending to 2,500 feet.

synopsis: Tower Controller in Charge reported the Local controller did not notice a departing aircraft had aborted their takeoff and allowed an arriving aircraft to land.
summary: Local control cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while Aircraft Y was landing, but the student pilot inadvertently reduced power, causing Aircraft X to stop at the runway end. The Controller in Charge was distracted by a phone call regarding ACE-IDS issues and did not visually scan the runway to prevent the conflict.

synopsis: Corporate flight crew reported responding to two RA's for traffic they had not been advised about when switching from Approach to Tower frequency.
summary: The crew received two TCAS Resolution Advisories and one Traffic Advisory while on a visual approach through 5,000 feet in busy airspace near a major airport. The conflicts involved three VFR training aircraft not on ATC frequencies, causing vertical separations of 200 feet before the crew was cleared to land.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported Horizontal Situation Indicator failure in flight.
summary: During climb to FL370, the Captain's HSI failed with electrical fumes and a bright flash, causing the crew to run the Smoke, Fire or Fumes QRH. Dispatch and Maintenance advised a return to ZZZ, where the aircraft landed safely with fire trucks standing by, though post-flight inspection found no issues.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a flap overspeed on departure climbout.
summary: The Captain, flying with a distracted First Officer, experienced rapid acceleration and a Flap Overspeed ECAM during departure cleanup after being distracted by anti-ice and radio duties. Maintenance inspected the aircraft and returned it to service, while the Captain attributed the event to crew distraction and task saturation.

synopsis: A-321 flight crew reported an NMAC event while on Approach control vectors for final approach course.
summary: The Pilot Flying on Aircraft X avoided a near-midair collision with Aircraft Y, a Cessna with an inoperative transponder, by manually climbing while leveling at 4,000 ft. The incident occurred because TCAS and ATC provided no warnings, and the Cessna was operating illegally in the Class-B floor with equipment failure.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A319 flight crew reported Terrain Warning on approach.
summary: A Captain and First Officer flying into ZZZ accepted a visual approach to Runway XX on a left downwind, triggering a GPWS warning while crossing a mountain ridge east of the field. The Captain attributed the event to accepting a prohibited circling clearance due to unfamiliarity with local terrain restrictions and runway length concerns.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported an go around and priority landing after flaps failed to fully deploy.
summary: The flight crew received a TE disagree EICAS message when selecting flaps to 25, causing the flaps to stop at 23 or 24 and forcing a go-around. The aircraft landed uneventfully on a longer runway after priority handling, marking the third report of this specific flap issue in three days.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported having maintenance items that were not properly written up in the aircraft maintenance logbook.
summary: The crew discovered that minor repairs from an ICAO ramp inspection were not documented in the maintenance logbook before a return flight. Consequently, they switched to another aircraft, departing nearly an hour late, attributing the oversight to a misunderstanding regarding documentation requirements for routine maintenance.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported a rejected takeoff due to unreliable airspeed indications with a 30 kt. difference between pilot's and first officer's airspeed.
summary: During takeoff roll at ZZZ, the Captain and First Officer rejected takeoff due to a 30-knot airspeed discrepancy caused by a leak in the Captain's Pitot-Static system. The crew safely stopped the aircraft and returned to the gate for maintenance, attributing their successful handling to recent recurrent training.

synopsis: Captain reported a rejected takeoff due to a right side window warning message.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff on Runway 19R at MCI due to a right-side window EICAS alert, which was cleared by the QRH checklist. After departing again, the alert recurred post-V1 but was resolved once more, allowing an uneventful flight to ZZZ caused by a component failure.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported an MEL item that was not provided to the flight crew prior to the flight.
summary: A dispatcher reported that a crew failed to receive an airborne MEL amendment for Engine No. 3 Fire Detection Loop B due to a missed ACARS broadcast. The dispatcher attributed the oversight to the high volume of existing MELs and the swing shift dispatcher's workload, subsequently sending the amendment manually.

synopsis: ERJ175 Captain reported during climb out and over water the radio altimeters began to give a terrain warning.
summary: The flight crew experienced erratic RA indications and an oral 'Terrain' warning during initial climb on the SID from ZZZ. The warning ceased before an escape maneuver was required, attributed to a faulty RA with two previous write-ups.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported NMAC on descent.
summary: During descent on the STAR into ZZZ at 12,000 MSL, the flight crew received a TCAS level-off RA to avoid a small general aviation aircraft. The crew complied with the resolution advisory, visually identified the intruder passing underneath, and landed safely without further incident or ATC traffic callouts.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported missing the IFR release time due to general aviation traffic in the pattern and the Tower being closed.
summary: The crew taxied onto the runway while waiting for a general aviation aircraft to exit, but their release time expired. Unable to reach Center by radio, they exited the runway, called by phone, and received a new short release time before lining up again.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported concerns with SUN Tower opposite direction procedures resulting in traffic conflicts.
summary: Pilots reported a Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) Resolution Advisory while turning final at SUN Airport due to simultaneous departures. The crew attributed the conflict to ATC launching outbound traffic before the arrival was established on final, compounded by terrain restrictions and task saturation.

synopsis: G200 flight crew reported deviating to an alternate airport after experiencing pitch oscillation anomalies and an amber elevator indication in cruise flight at FL410.
summary: The flight crew experienced pitch oscillations, elevator indications, and an electrical smoke odor at FL410, prompting autopilot disconnection and a descent to FL220. After brief vibration and speed reduction, the aircraft landed safely at ZZZ, though the specific cause remains unknown.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported descending to a lower altitude after experiencing a power loss at FL410 while penetrating weather.
summary: The Captain flew the aircraft through convective activity at FL410, exceeding the FMC maximum altitude due to rising static air temperature, which caused engine rollbacks and radio static. The crew descended to FL380 to restore engine performance and communications, with the First Officer noting the Captain's decision to penetrate the storm was unsafe.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Flight crew reported two waypoints with similar names in close proximity.
summary: A crew flying from ZZZ to DAL deviated 25 degrees right after misinterpreting a clearance for waypoint KRKEE as TURKI due to similar names. The error was detected by a subsequent controller, and the crew recommended renaming one waypoint to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported safety concern with ground crew operations during taxi.
summary: The reporter suggests ground crew use headsets during taxi-in to the gate. Currently, the nose marshaller focuses on the J-line and misses wing walker signals, so the reporter recommends updating Ground Ops procedures to require headset communication in the Safety Zone.

synopsis: Flight crew reported finding evidence of a bird strike on aircraft during morning walk around inspection.
summary: The First Officer discovered a bent fan blade and dried blood on the number 2 engine during a preflight walkaround, indicating an undetected bird strike from the previous terminating flight. The flight was cancelled because the blade damage exceeded allowable tolerances.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported runway and taxiways signs at MMUN Airport were not illuminated at night.
summary: Pilots landing at night on Cancun Runway 12R reported that many runway and taxiway signs were unilluminated. The cause was unknown, but the crew recommended regular inspections and fail-safe procedures to ensure sign lights are operational after sunset.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported an uneventful resolution to an airborne conflict due to a communications breakdown between flight crew and ATC during approach.
summary: During arrival between FL 200 and 10,000 ft, the crew received a TCAS Traffic Advisory for a converging aircraft below after ATC issued a descent clearance and a partially blocked direct instruction. The crew slowed descent to avoid conflict, clarified they had not received the direct clearance, and continued safely once the situation was resolved.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported the autopilot overshot an assigned altitude during climb.
summary: During climb out of Denver, the autopilot failed to level at the 10,000 ft KIDNG restriction despite correct FMC data, peaking at 10,700 ft. The pilot manually descended to 10,000 ft before re-engaging the autopilot, attributing the altitude deviation to a VNAV glitch.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a miscommunication when asking for advice for documenting a scratch in the logbook at an outstation.
summary: The Captain, Dispatch, and Maintenance discussed a fuselage scratch during a through-flight, where Dispatch and Maintenance incorrectly advised the Captain could decide not to log it based on a misunderstood policy. The Base Chief Pilot later confirmed no such policy change existed, stating the scratch should have been recorded as a new defect at the out station.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported poor communication between the various parties involved caused the aircraft to be fueled incorrectly.
summary: The Captain and Operations Agent experienced a departure delay on Aircraft X due to poor communication regarding fuel loading. The Captain added fuel to the inoperative center tank despite MEL restrictions, causing weight and balance software errors and requiring manual calculations before the flight departed with 16.8 FOB.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported ELT in the OFF position.
summary: A flight attendant discovered the ELT in G2 was OFF instead of ARMED during an equipment check and notified the Captain. Although Tech Ops initially claimed the switch could be turned on by crew if needed, the Captain directed the attendant to move it to ARM, where it passed a self-test.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported communication issues related to wearing a face mask.
summary: Cabin crew reported that mandatory face coverings hampered safety communications during passenger briefings, PA announcements, and pre-flight briefings. The reporter stated that masks muffled speech, making it difficult to comprehend messages from flight attendants and the captain.

synopsis: Captain reported a collision during taxi with conflicting traffic at taxiway intersection.
summary: A pilot taxiing for an Eastbound VFR departure collided with a high-wing single-engine aircraft on taxiway Charlie at ZZZ airport. The reporter attributed the incident to blind spots, a sharp taxiway intersection, and a lack of ground control warnings due to combined controller duties during high traffic.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Single Pilot reported an uneventful forced landing caused by faulty fuel gauge.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 1,400 feet AGL due to a frozen fuel gauge and incorrect emergency procedure, forcing a safe landing in a farmer's field. After refueling and clearing the strip, the aircraft departed without injury or damage.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported contacting ATC on guard and being advised they were NORDO for 150 miles.
summary: Pilots on a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1 at FL340 became NORDO for 150 miles after failing to monitor frequency XYX.Z due to conversation and reduced traffic. They eventually contacted ATC on the correct frequency, received a descent clearance, and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: PA-44 Check Airman reported executing a last minute go around when hearing 'scraping noise' due to a gear up landing.
summary: An instructor and student pilot in a single-engine aircraft missed the landing checklist due to traffic alerts and student performance issues, resulting in a gear-up near-landing. The instructor took control, executed a go-around, and completed a normal landing after verifying the gear.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with another small aircraft that ATC issued traffic for and was displayed on the reporter's ADS-B.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in Aircraft X experienced a near miss with Aircraft Y while cruising at 4,500 ft during a night cross-country training flight. The reporter attributed the incident to Aircraft Y's pilot selecting an improper altitude and failing to scan for non-ADS-B traffic, necessitating a 20-degree left offset.

synopsis: C175 Flight Instructor reported a runway excursion occurred when he failed to properly communicate to his student his intention to take control of the aircraft.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced a propeller strike and runway excursion during landing in gusty crosswinds due to an uncommanded nose-low attitude. The incident occurred because the instructor failed to verbally claim controls, resulting in conflicting inputs that prevented proper recovery.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew reported rejected takeoff when First Officer's seat slid back.
summary: During takeoff roll at 100 knots, the First Officer's seat slid back, preventing control access. The Captain rejected the takeoff because the seat was not properly secured, and both pilots deemed the situation unsafe for flight.

synopsis: C402 pilot reported rejected takeoff due to left engine failure.
summary: The pilot reported that the left engine quit while advancing power for takeoff on the runway. The takeoff was subsequently aborted.

synopsis: Air Taxi Captain reported excessive vibration on descent which caused the aircraft to be removed from service at the destination airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced intermittent vibration during cruise and descent on Aircraft X, caused by a loose screw piercing the horizontal stabilizer plate. Maintenance confirmed the defect after landing, resulting in the aircraft being grounded for repairs and delaying the next flight.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported the taxiway signage at RNO airport was confusing and contributed to a taxiway incursion.
summary: The Captain taxied off runway 16L at Lima and mistakenly entered taxiway Bravo instead of Alpha due to misinterpreting signage. Ground Control immediately corrected the error and cleared the aircraft to continue to the gate via Bravo, with the pilot citing a need for better diagram familiarity.

synopsis: E175 flight crew reported 'low altitude alert' from ATC during a mountainous terrain departure.
summary: The flight crew deviated from the SID to intercept an airway directly, causing a reduced climb rate that triggered an ATC terrain alert. ATC instructed an expedited climb and a turn, though the crew remained in VMC and clear of terrain throughout the event.

synopsis: E175 pilot reported diverting to an alternate airport after experiencing loss of #2 hydraulic system.
summary: The crew diverted due to a rapid Hyd 2 fluid loss that resulted in total system pressure failure during the turn. They executed checklists and used the alternate gear extension handle to achieve a safe landing after notifying all relevant parties.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a gate agent put a passenger in a seat which they shouldn't have.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a gate agent incorrectly seated a passenger in seat XB on a [type aircraft] due to confusion. The passenger kept his mask above his mouth throughout the flight, and the crew member noted the gate agent's prior threat of disciplinary action for moving passengers to seat XA.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger refused to wear a face mask during the flight.
summary: Flight Attendant B reported a passenger refused to wear a mask throughout the flight despite multiple warnings from cabin crew and a Customer Service Agent. The passenger and his wife argued with the crew, prompting the Flight Attendant to notify the Captain, who then contacted ZZZ1.

synopsis: Flight Attendants reported a passenger complained that another passenger did not wear a face mask during the flight.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a passenger in seat XX was not wearing a mask while snacking and drinking, prompting an angry complaint from passenger YX. The crew member stated they could not intervene because the passenger was consuming food and beverages.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger being confrontational about wearing a face mask.
summary: A Flight Attendant reported a passenger who threw almonds, repeatedly removed his mask, and threatened the crew during the flight. After the passenger was met at the gate, his traveling companions made the crew feel unsafe in the terminal and on the tram.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a possibly intoxicated person was removed from flight.
summary: During boarding, the pilot and a flight attendant identified a passenger in seat XB as intoxicated due to slurred speech, alcohol odor, and agitation. They agreed the passenger needed to be removed from the aircraft after he admitted to drinking and was rude to other guests.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported moving a passenger due to a dirty seat and for social distancing.
summary: Cabin crew resolved a seating conflict involving a passenger and ground agents during boarding by manually reassigning the guest to row XA. The crew bypassed computer restrictions to move the passenger, ensuring accurate counts and an on-time departure.

synopsis: Technician reported that during down jacking, they neglected to remove the tail stand, resulting in damage to the forward fuselage skin.
summary: A maintenance crew damaged the forward belly skin of Aircraft X while downjacking it for a gear check after failing to remove the tail stand. The reporter attributed the incident to the missing safety alarm on the tail stand and recommended installing alarms on all company tail stands.

synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with another aircraft while under ATC flight following.
summary: A pilot conducting a skydiving drop received a traffic advisory at 4,000 ft MSL and leveled off at 3,000 ft after another aircraft passed 100 feet below. The pilot noted they were already heading 090 and had not received an instruction to stop descending.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a NMAC with another aircraft while attempting to land at an airport where the tower was closed due to COVID-19 staffing.
summary: A pilot with a student in an uncontrolled traffic pattern at ZZZ experienced two near-midair collisions with Aircraft Z and Aircraft A due to straight-in approaches and speed differences. The pilot attributed the incidents to disrupted traffic flow, reduced tower hours, and other pilots' failure to follow right-of-way rules.

synopsis: Instructor Pilot reported loss of power in the right engine due to oil loss and diverted to another airport.
summary: A pilot and student flying a twin-engine Baron experienced a right engine failure during a STOL contest due to a connecting rod breaking through the case. After noticing oil pressure loss and yawing, they diverted, feathered the failed engine on short final, and landed safely despite high winds and oil leakage.

synopsis: Center Controller reported the adjacent sector intentionally delayed in accepting a handoff causing the Controller to have an airspace deviation.
summary: An air traffic controller attempted to hand off Aircraft X at 41,000 ft. but faced communication delays due to the receiving sector using an incorrect frequency and unprofessional conduct. The controller subsequently restricted the aircraft's climb to 40,000 ft. and then 37,000 ft. before the handoff was finally accepted after the aircraft entered the receiving sector's airspace.

synopsis: Center Controller reported a frequency transmitter site failure caused a lack of ability to communicate with aircraft directly in a portion of their airspace increasing their workload during a busy period due to weather deviations.
summary: Air traffic controllers experienced transmitter interference causing unintelligible bursts that degraded communications with aircraft below 6,000 ft. The resulting inability to contact aircraft forced reliance on pilot relays, increased workload, and created significant safety issues due to lost communications and frequency congestion.

synopsis: Airline Ground Agent reported the breakroom is not being sanitized properly for COVID-19.
summary: Cabin crew reported that a co-worker tested positive for COVID-19, yet staff were not officially notified and the break-room remained uncleaned. The reporter stated this occurred because the facility was not disinfected daily as promised, leaving employees unaware of the exposure risk.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported the pilot flying exceeded 250 kts below 10,000 ft. on departure when he was distracted looking for traffic.
summary: During climb out, the Pilot Monitoring lost situational awareness while scanning for traffic, causing the aircraft to accelerate to 265 kts. The Pilot Flying corrected the speed with spoilers and power reduction, and the flight continued after encountering wake turbulence.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported aircraft encountered engine alert during takeoff roll.
summary: The First Officer and Captain rejected takeoff at a non-towered high-altitude airport when the Interstage Turbine Temperature gauge turned red and blinked at 95–100 knots. The crew safely stopped the aircraft, deplaned passengers, and attributed the event to an unusual engine indication requiring immediate abort.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported taking off with the flight attendants not seated citing a possible misunderstanding because the FA was speaking through a protective mask.
summary: The pilot reported that after a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1, the crew was removed from their pairing because flight attendants were not seated for departure. The pilot stated they were unaware of this issue until the Captain informed them the following day, as the cabin crew had not raised the concern immediately after the flight.

synopsis: 560Xl Captain reported severe turbulence on descent.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence and rain while descending to ZZZZZ at 11,000 ft, causing autopilot disengagement and a crossing altitude of 11,300 ft. The aircraft landed safely but sustained radome damage, attributed to limited ATC weather intensity data and unavailable NEXRAD guidance.

synopsis: Flight crew reported a loss of aircraft brakes while parking that resulted in a collision with another aircraft.
summary: During post-landing shutdown at the ramp, the aircraft rolled backward despite brake application after the ground power unit disconnected. The Captain attempted to steer away using the nose tiller, but the aircraft collided with another parked aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported overshooting the assigned altitude during climbout. The pilot described the aircraft's weight as very light due to the small passenger count.
summary: The pilot of a lightly loaded departing aircraft failed to reduce power while climbing through 4,000 feet, causing an inability to smoothly level off at the assigned 5,000 feet. Departure Control subsequently instructed the crew to continue climbing to 15,000 feet, with no further safety deviations reported.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported an aircraft issue during cruise resulted in a diversion. First Officer stated they did not have the correct charts onboard the aircraft due to possible cost saving measures by the airline during the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: Flight crew reported an inflight issue while en route from ZZZ to ZZZZ, discovering they lacked Jeppesen terminal charts for destination and alternate airports due to company subscription cuts. The crew identified this as a critical safety risk that could prevent safe landings or violate regulations if communications were lost.

synopsis: ERJ175 flight crew reported multiple EICAS failure messages while in cruise.
summary: During a revenue flight from ZZZ1 to ZZZ at FL330, the crew encountered multiple system failures including spoiler and speed brake faults. They requested priority handling, calculated an increased landing distance, and executed a safe landing with a brace briefing after ATC cleared a visual approach.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported a communication issues with TRACON Control during arrival. TRACON was working departures and arrivals on two frequencies. ATC informed the crew they were short staffed due to COVID-19.
summary: The flight crew descended on the ZZZZZ3 STAR at ZZZ while ATC managed two frequencies due to weather and staffing shortages. The crew landed uneventfully but admitted they failed to query ATC for a specific runway assignment, which caused confusion during the arrival.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a recent trend of being dispatched with minimum fuel loads.
summary: A pilot reported that dispatchers are again releasing aircraft with minimum fuel loads due to management pressure to reduce costs. The pilot attributed this trend to financial concerns overriding safety margins and suggested reinstating safety-based fuel policies.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported an NMAC event during final approach with an nonreporting, no transponder/ADSB glider operating along localizer approach course.
summary: The flight crew avoided a glider while intercepting the ILS localizer at 4,300 ft by executing a descending left turn. The glider, which lacked a transponder or ADS-B, was flying on the localizer centerline at the same altitude as cleared traffic.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported encountering a minimum fuel situation due to severe weather and lack of timely information from Dispatch.
summary: The flight crew diverted from ZZZ to ZZZ4 due to thunderstorms, windshear, and minimum fuel, citing a lack of weather updates and landing data from an IOE Dispatcher. Despite ATC assistance, the crew managed the diversion independently after the Dispatcher failed to provide critical information regarding alternate airports and weather conditions.

synopsis: Ground crew reported brakes were released prior to notification.
summary: Pilots released brakes two minutes before push crew contact, causing the aircraft to move while ground personnel were removing chocks and positioning equipment. This created a serious risk of injury to employees and customers and potential aircraft damage.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported operational control of a flight was lost and explains how it occurred.
summary: A dispatcher and supervisor lost operational control of a diverted flight for 23 minutes after the crew self-diverted, delaying the flight's transfer to the dispatcher's desk. The delay was caused by the supervisor failing to log in immediately upon relief and ongoing computer outages, though the crew maintained communication and flew a direct route.

synopsis: C680 flight crew reported an uneventful air return for bird strike during takeoff.
summary: Pilots encountered a bird strike at 10 feet AGL during takeoff, impacting the left engine pylon and horizontal stabilizer. With no abnormal indications, they executed a precautionary landing for maintenance inspection, which confirmed damage and grounded the aircraft.

synopsis: Airline Captain reported NMAC with a UAV during the turn to final approach.
summary: The pilot and First Officer encountered a drone 10–20 feet from the aircraft while intercepting the ILS 26L localizer at Ontario, CA. The First Officer spotted the drone under the right wing, prompting an ATC report, but no evasive maneuvers or deviations were required.

synopsis: Airline Captain reported a NMAC with a UAV while on a heading to intercept the localizer to final.
summary: The pilot reported a drone passing under the left wing with approximately 100 feet of clearance while intercepting the ILS 18L localizer into CVG. The sighting was immediately reported to Cincinnati Approach Control, but no evasive maneuvers or deviations from ATC instructions were required.

synopsis: Pilot reported a fuel leak while on the ground taking the aircraft out of service.
summary: During preflight, a large fuel leak occurred near the right wing tip due to a malfunctioning refueling panel that failed to stop filling the tank. The Captain deplaned passengers and crew, and the aircraft was placed out of service while maintenance investigated the cause.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported a ground collision with light pole during tug pusbhack from gate.
summary: During pushback at spot XX, a B767 struck a light pole due to the tight stand and ramp personnel error, causing damage to the horizontal stabilizer, tail cone, APU door, and left elevator. The aircraft was towed to a new spot after an hour delay, with the crew recommending additional tail marshals and improved training.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported that during their takeoff roll, FWA ATC Tower gave a full clearance routing to another aircraft. The Captain described concerns with the high level of distraction created during a critical phase.
summary: ATC issued a full route clearance on the tower frequency during the takeoff roll, rotation, and gear retraction of the reporter's aircraft. This created an unsafe situation by hindering cockpit communication, a recurring issue the pilot attributes to ATC failing to use the designated clearance or ground frequencies.

synopsis: MD-11 Flight Crew reported aircraft slow to accelerate during takeoff.
summary: The flight crew reported reduced acceleration and a late rotation near 3,000 feet remaining on a long runway after setting normal takeoff power. They suspect water intrusion into cargo, loading areas, or electronics bays caused the decreased performance or erroneous indications.

synopsis: MD-10 Captain reported Hazmat procedure violation of not signing DG document prior to departure.
summary: The Captain departed without signing the Dangerous Goods paperwork due to multiple preflight interruptions and a last-minute jump seater discrepancy. Operations coordinated with ZZZ to obtain a signed copy after landing, attributing the error to missed verification steps during the preflight flow.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported release issues relating to flights that are not assigned to Dispatcher in a timely manner. Reporter stated this has been a problem since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: A dispatcher discovered six unassigned charter flights scheduled to depart within two hours, causing a safety issue due to missing flight releases. The reporter attributed this failure to managers and staff neglecting duties to assign flights and balance workloads, leaving crews without required documentation.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported arrival crossing restriction not met due to pocket of moderate turbulence encountered during descent.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X deviated from a descent via ZZZZZ1 arrival due to moderate turbulence, crossing ZZZ3 at 13,300 ft instead of the required 13,000 ft or below. The crew complied with a subsequent clearance to descend to 8,000 ft at ZZZZZ4 but noted they failed to notify the original controller due to frequency changes and heavy traffic.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported being advised about a troublesome passenger before the flight and stated the passenger refused to wear a mask claiming a medical condition.
summary: The cabin crew managed a passenger who refused to wear a mask due to claimed medical issues and beliefs, despite X Department intervention. During the flight, the passenger placed shoes in the aisle, creating a trip hazard, and remained unmasked, prompting the crew to compensate an affected passenger after landing.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported confusion about airline policy relating to the face mask policy.
summary: A cabin crew member questioned the airline regarding a contradiction between safety messages stating crew should relay mask policies rather than enforce them and the airline's claim that this instruction is not in their curriculum. The reporter sought clarification on why this specific guidance appears in safety documentation if it is not part of the official training program.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported two passengers not wearing COVID-19 masks during the flight.
summary: A flight attendant reported that passengers in seats XXA and XXB repeatedly removed their face masks and became agitated when reminded of airline policy. The passenger in XXB yelled he could not breathe, refused to comply initially, and later hid his face to avoid visual confirmation of mask usage.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported confusion about airline policy relating to the face mask policy.
summary: Flight attendants repeatedly asked a passenger to wear a mask during boarding, flight, and final approach, but he refused by falsely claiming to be eating or drinking. No enforcement action was taken due to the short flight duration and the passenger's persistent claims.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that another Flight Attendant assigned a non-rev to a seat that was against current policy for social distancing.
summary: During boarding, the D FA authorized a ground agent to seat a non-revenue passenger in a restricted seat, violating social distancing policy. The B FA objected, but the D FA refused to move the passenger, prompting the reporting crew member to file a report regarding the policy violation.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported a passenger was not wearing a COVID-19 mask because he stated that he had a medical condition, but was unable to provide any documentation.
summary: A flight attendant reported a passenger refused to wear a mask during boarding, claiming an undocumented medical condition despite no prior notification to the gate agent. The crew could not enforce compliance or remove the passenger due to potential discrimination claims, highlighting a need for clearer medical documentation procedures.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported they asked a passenger to move to an upgraded seat for social distancing purposes, but the passenger refused.
summary: During boarding, a guest refused to move from seat XXD despite requests from the Flight Attendant and Cabin Services Agent, leading to his removal for acting harshly and questioning exit row compliance. The reporter recommends blocking seats XXDEF to prevent unsafe proximity between crew and passengers.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported notifying the Captain of an 'extremely strong fume smell in the cabin' while preparing to pushback.
summary: Flight Attendants 2 and 4 reported a strong metallic fume smell entering the aft galley and cabin during pre-pushback while the safety demo played. The fumes caused eye irritation and a metallic taste, prompting the crew to immediately inform the Captain.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported another flight attendant did not sit in the assigned jumpseat.
summary: A flight attendant refused her assigned forward-facing jumpseat for taxi, takeoff, and landing, choosing an aft-facing seat and wearing headsets instead. The pilot reported the incident after the flight attendant became verbally abusive when reminded of the requirement to sit in the assigned seat.

synopsis: Flight attendant reported a passenger had to be continuously reminded to wear a mask.
summary: A flight attendant and two other crew members attempted to assist a passenger with an irritated ear mask by providing an N95 alternative, but the passenger refused to wear it during the flight. The passenger finally donned his original mask only upon deplaning.

synopsis: Technicians reported non compliance with Company and Manufacturer's manuals when attempting to repair a door problem.
summary: Two mechanics found Aircraft X's forward entry door handle failed to stow, requiring spring inspection per the FIM, but supervisors and managers ordered them to only lubricate the handle to avoid hangar repositioning. Despite the handle still failing to stow after lubrication, the supervisor signed off the work and issued the airworthiness release.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reported problems with other technicians not following the correct company policy for aircraft checks.
summary: A supervisor notified the hangar that an aircraft grounded over 48 hours required a pitot inspection due to policy violations, but the hangar released the aircraft for service anyway. The reporter attributes this recurring issue to hangar managers failing to follow procedures.

synopsis: C-172S Student Pilot reported loss of directional control on landing resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot overcorrected with excessive rudder and possible brake application after landing far right of the centerline at ZZZ, causing the aircraft to exit the runway and clip a taxiway edge light. The incident resulted in damage to the left wheel strut fairing and uneven tire wear, attributed to poor judgment during high-speed ground corrections.

synopsis: Pilot reported receiving amended clearance inflight repeatedly.
summary: A pilot flying from ZZZ to LGB reported that SOCAL ATC frequently issues complex amended clearances to intercept V394 during busy descent phases. The pilot stated this requires 3–4 minutes of head-down programming in the G1000, preventing traffic scanning and creating an unsafe situation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported flying over a sporting event during a game and wondered if they had violated a TFR.
summary: A pilot conducting a scenic tour flight at 1,800 feet MSL inadvertently entered an active Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) over a venue hosting a game. The pilot attributed the error to confusing venue capacity with actual attendance and plans to review scheduled events during future preflight checks.

synopsis: Center Controller reported an aircraft descended below what the Controller thought was the assigned altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X to cross at FL310, but the pilot descended below that level believing the clearance was for FL300. The controller attributed the communication error to frequency congestion and potential audio muffling caused by mandatory mask usage while working combined sectors.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported autopilot system failure resulting in an expedited landing.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft X experienced autopilot disengagement and MCP altitude display faults during climb, forcing a VFR return to ZZZ. ATC noted a communication breakdown where the crew failed to respond to calls or ACARS despite reporting lost altitude and heading capabilities.

synopsis: Captain reported his five point harness system malfunctioned, trapping him in his seat.
summary: During enroute flight, the Captain's seat belt five-point connector failed, trapping him in the seat. The Captain improvised a partial restraint system using the shoulder harness, resulting in SOP violations and the use of emergency authority due to a lack of company guidance.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported two passengers were abusive to flight attendants after they were reminded of mask requirements.
summary: Flight attendants reported that passengers in seats XX A and B became abusive during cruise after being instructed to wear face masks. Upon arrival, three CSR supervisors met the aircraft.

synopsis: ERJ-145 flight crew reported Autopilot failure on descent caused two overspeed occurrences resulting from extreme pitch down commands.
summary: During descent into ZZZ1, the flight crew experienced two high-speed events where the aircraft pitched down aggressively and accelerated to 280 kts after speed brake extension and autopilot mode changes. The crew manually recovered using Touch Control Steering, landed safely, and attributed the cause to delayed manual intervention when reacting to unexpected automation responses.

synopsis: Airline Captain reported the crew were unaware of the need to contact ground control before pushback on the cargo ramp.
summary: The flight crew contacted Ground Advisory after taxiing on the uncontrolled cargo ramp instead of before pushback, as required when the tower is operational. This occurred because the crew overlooked a Jeppesen note mandating early contact, leading to a controller complaint about potential conflicts.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot deviating right of course for weather reported ATC questioned them when they turned left for further deviations.
summary: The flight crew deviated left to avoid severe weather without notifying ATC while remaining right of course. The controller expressed dissatisfaction with the lack of communication, prompting the captain to file a report emphasizing the need to advise ATC immediately during such maneuvers.

synopsis: Pilot reported questionable maintenance procedures regarding the temporary repair of delamination in the area of the ADG door.
summary: The pilot discovered improper speed tape application on the ADG door during preflight, which could have prevented deployment. Maintenance corrected the repair, allowing the flight to ZZZ1, though management pressure to board before the fix was resolved conflicted with the PIC's safety decision.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported being on final to a Class Bravo airport and having to go-around due to a small aircraft that was not talking to Tower, which caused the airborne conflict.
summary: Two separate reports describe commercial crews on final approach to ZZZ receiving TCAS climb RAs at 800 feet AGL due to uncommunicating general aviation traffic. In both cases, the Captains executed missed approaches to resolve the conflicts and landed safely on subsequent attempts.

synopsis: E-175 Captain reported undocumented Hazmat cargo was transported without flight crew notification.
summary: The flight crew discovered Dry Ice (Hazmat 1) in the aft cargo compartment after loading in ZZZ, a location where it is prohibited. The reporter attributed the error to a lack of specific cargo inquiry and the absence of a NOTAM in the clearance, which would have allowed for removal before departure.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that announcements regarding the safety demonstration changes were not made and that passengers were not advised to remove face coverings and masks in the event of decompression.
summary: Cabin crew performed a manual safety demo without announcing changes or advising passengers to remove masks for decompression. The crew also failed to explain that life vests and oxygen masks were not demonstrated.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger had to be continuously reminded to wear a mask.
summary: A flight attendant managed a non-compliant passenger in seat 4X who repeatedly removed his mask during pushback, inflight, and while sleeping. The crew issued warnings and involved the Captain, who planned to address the passenger upon arrival at ZZZ1, where the gate agent was also notified.

synopsis: Flight attendants reported 3 guests were unhappy with seating arrangements.
summary: Cabin crew reported that guests in seats XX, XY, and XZ were rude and complained about assigned seating due to social distancing and weight and balance requirements. The crew could not move the passengers to sit together despite offering compensation for a previous flight cancellation.

synopsis: Flight attendants reported a passenger not wearing a mask due to a reported medical condition.
summary: A flight attendant reported a passenger on aircraft XXY refused to wear a mask due to medical issues despite no documentation, while the cabin was packed without social distancing. The crew contacted ground agents who failed to intervene, leaving the flight attendant concerned about the unsafe situation caused by unenforced safety policies.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger complained because other passengers were not wearing a mask while they were eating a snack.
summary: A cabin crew member managed a disruptive passenger who loudly complained about four other passengers not wearing masks while eating. The crew offered seat changes and a new mask, which the passenger refused, but eventually secured compliance from the other passengers after reiterating the rules.

synopsis: Flight Attendant was told by an unaccompanied minor that the child's mother had COVID-19 and the child was on the way to stay with family.
summary: During descent, an Unaccompanied Minor informed Flight Attendants that their mother had COVID-19, prompting two crew members and a passenger to assist the child. The reporter noted the minor could potentially be a carrier of the virus.

synopsis: Technician reported a lack of awareness by leadership and lack of support from them caused an aircraft to go out of service, resulting in unreasonable discipline.
summary: Two mechanics on Aircraft X reported that a supervisor accused them of deliberately taking the aircraft out of service after they addressed multiple maintenance items during a night shift. The reporter attributes the conflict to a hostile work environment and management pressure that prioritizes speed over safety, resulting in disciplinary action and stress-related health issues.

synopsis: Pilot reported taxiing in a congested area resulted in a collision with a parked aircraft where both aircraft were damaged.
summary: The pilot of a Stearman tailwheel aircraft collided with parked Aircraft Y while attempting an S-turn in a congested taxi area due to limited forward visibility. The incident caused minor damage requiring a new propeller for the Stearman and a new stabilator for Aircraft Y.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported experiencing a ground conflict and cited reduced level of awareness due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
summary: The pilot reported a potential conflict while taxiing to Runway XXR when Aircraft Y converged on the same intersection without clear sequencing instructions. The controller dismissed the concern, and the reporter attributed the situation to reduced awareness caused by low traffic volumes and multitasking during the pandemic.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported an NMAC event during final approach with a non-reporting departing helicopter traffic.
summary: A pilot and student on final approach in a fixed-wing aircraft executed a go-around and sharp right turn to avoid a collision with Helicopter Y, which entered the runway without stopping or responding to radio calls. The reporter noted that other traffic and ATC could hear their transmissions clearly.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Pilot reported observing a target on his cockpit display on departure but not seeing it out the window. Pilot turned off course to avoid traffic resulting in a NMAC.
summary: The pilot, flying as non-PIC during an IFR climb to 12,000 feet, executed a right turn to avoid a converging RV-6 after the non-flying pilot inadvertently disabled the TCAS display on the MFD. The reporter attributed the conflict to overestimating climb performance, the display change, and a lack of briefing regarding the VFR traffic.

synopsis: Center Controller reported an altitude excursion and referenced wearing a mask may have muffled the transmission.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Aircraft X descending below FL330 after a clearance, noting the pilot's readback was likely muffled by a mask. The controller transferred control to another sector, attributing the potential communication error to the possibility of the pilot mishearing instructions due to the mask.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after experiencing high ITT in the left engine shortly after takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced left engine ITT exceedance and caution messages during takeoff, prompting an immediate return to ZZZ. The crew successfully executed the QRH procedures, maintained 3,000 ft, and completed an uneventful landing after reducing power.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported a rejected take off caused by electrical system failures.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 100 knots due to right generator failure, transformer rectifier loss, and bus tie malfunction causing display flickering. Maintenance resolved the bus tie issue after engine run-ups, allowing the flight to depart with one generator and the APU.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported due to high temperatures and high density altitude at the origin airport, both engines exceeded EGT limits.
summary: The crew performed a 26k takeoff from ZZZ in warm temperatures and 5-knot winds, exceeding EGT limits on both engines. The pilot attributed the over-temperature event to high density altitude and high engine times, noting that cooler conditions or a different wind component might have prevented it.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported being advised about a possible non-compliant passenger regarding mask wear.
summary: A pilot reported that a supervisor boarded a previously non-compliant passenger and two others who initially refused to wear masks at the gate in ZZZ. The crew resolved the issues after repeated instructions, causing a one-minute departure delay, though the pilot noted a lack of specific airline guidance on mask policies.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported having non-compliant passenger.
summary: During level cruise, a pilot reported a non-compliant passenger who verbally abused and physically threatened Flight Attendants after refusing to move from an incorrect seat. The crew felt unsafe due to the threats, attributing the incident to pandemic stress and the passenger's unfamiliarity with airline rules.

synopsis: A-321 Captain reported intermittent ECAM SMOKE AFT CARGO annunciation during taxi at destination airport. Reporter highlighted ramp communication issues upon gate arrival.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent aft cargo smoke warnings during taxi, triggering a fire suppression discharge and a hold on door opening. Upon reaching the gate, ground personnel opened the door before the crew could confirm safety, though no fire was found, highlighting a lack of direct communication methods to ground staff.

synopsis: Airline First Officer reported lost com, NORDO, with ATC due to being unfamiliar with the local operation.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring likely switched to the Departure frequency without Tower clearance after a prolonged stay on Tower frequency during climb. The reporter attributes this error to inexperience with the ZZZ ATC system and failing to cross-check with the Pilot Flying.

synopsis: B757-200 Captain reported inflight ACARS message regarding Hazmat documentation errors, including exceeding max allowed limitation as well as load location error.
summary: The crew received conflicting ACARS messages regarding incorrect Dry Ice documentation while at 2,500 ft, initially requesting a return to departure. After Dispatch clarified the 57 lb overage, the crew leveled at 5,000 ft and proceeded uneventfully to the destination.

synopsis: PC-24 Pilot Not Flying reported an equipment failure resulting in a loss of cabin pressure.
summary: During a Part 135 descent through 36,000 ft., a bleed air failure caused cabin altitude to exceed 10,000 ft., triggering an automatic emergency descent. After donning oxygen masks and descending to 17,000 ft., pressurization normalized, allowing the flight to continue to destination without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Captain reported DIK airport is under construction, the runway lights are inoperative and there are no NOTAMs regarding these conditions.
summary: Pilots landing at DIK on Runway 32 found runway lights inoperative due to sun glare, with no NOTAM issued despite airport operations admitting the lights had failed for weeks. The reporter attributes this hazard to the airport authority's willful disregard for safety and failure to publish required NOTAMs for known equipment failures.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a passenger became argumentative when told they could not switch seats due to social distancing.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a passenger became argumentative when denied a seat switch due to social distancing restrictions. Later, the passenger and his wife removed their masks mid-flight, prompting the crew to intervene and provide a replacement mask.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported a communication breakdown with MC coordinators regarding handling aircraft mechanical diversion. Reporter recommended the need for an SOP delineating responsibilities of Dispatch and MC coordinators.
summary: A dispatcher managed a flight with a Bleed 1 failure at FL300, but a SOC coordinator built a diversion leg to ZZZ3 without communication, preventing fuel verification. This lack of coordination left the crew unaware of the plan and resulted in an incorrect release amendment number.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported ATC assigned holding fix in excess of 50nm offshore due to weather limitations. Reported added Navigation system malfunctioning.
summary: An air traffic controller identified that a flight holding 80nm offshore exceeded the 50nm safety limit due to Software X incorrectly tracking the aircraft onshore and ATC assigning the hold. The controller noted Software X's failure to track accurately and recommended replacing it with Software Y.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported seating issues and concerns with the close proximity of passengers when boarding the flight.
summary: Cabin crew and the Captain reported that ground staff seated strangers together on a small aircraft despite company distancing policies, causing passenger refusal and crew discomfort. The crew proceeded with the flight but filed reports to demand a clear written policy on seating and social distancing.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that when passengers were ordering their drinks, most of them took their face masks off, even though an announcement was made to leave masks on.
summary: Cabin crew reported that passengers removed masks to order drinks despite announcements to keep them on during service. The crew suggested using menu books as sign cards to facilitate communication without requiring passengers to remove masks.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported issues relating to non-revs and where to seat them.
summary: During boarding, a gate agent authorized a non-revenue flight attendant from another airline to sit in the flight deck jump seat. The flight crew denied this request, citing security restrictions, and the gate agent subsequently blocked the individual from boarding.

synopsis: C560XL Captain reported noticing smoke in the cockpit shortly after takeoff resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced smoke from the APU shortly after takeoff, which cleared upon shutdown, allowing a safe landing. Post-flight testing confirmed the APU caused the smoke, leading to a dispatch decision under 91.213 with the APU inoperative for a subsequent empty flight.

synopsis: EMB505 flight crew reported descending due to lack of radio establishment, engine icing indications in icing conditions, and moderate turbulence.
summary: At FL450, the flight crew experienced engine icing, turbulence, and lost communications, prompting an uncoordinated descent to FL320 for warmer air. After re-establishing contact, ZZZ Center reviewed the event, agreed with the crew's actions, and declined to report pilot deviations regarding the priority handling call.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported entering restricted airspace and referenced lack of flying as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot entered restricted airspace R-XXXX during climbout from ZZZ after the autopilot followed a reversed Foreflight course. The deviation resulted from misinterpreting the software's routing and losing situational awareness while managing turbulence and radio changes.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported flying the approach traffic pattern in the wrong direction after Tower had closed.
summary: A pilot departing ZZZ airport after tower closure inadvertently planned a right traffic pattern for Runway XXR instead of the required left pattern due to missing a Chart Supplement note. The error resulted from complacency and expectation bias, though no collision occurred as the pilot corrected the pattern after querying another aircraft.

synopsis: Flight Instructor and student reported terminating flight due to decreased aircraft performance during pattern work.
summary: A commercial pilot and student experienced sluggish climb performance with low rates during two takeoffs despite normal engine instruments. The crew requested priority handling and landed safely, suspecting a wind shift or undetected engine issue as the cause.

synopsis: C180 Pilot reported fuel exhaustion led to having to land on a field.
summary: The pilot experienced fuel exhaustion in an aging aircraft due to unreliable gauges, forcing an emergency landing in a plowed field after a brief engine restart failed to reach the airport. The aircraft sustained no damage or injuries, and maintenance suspects fuel bladder, feed, or carburetor issues.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported VFR transponder certification went overdue due to COVID-19 lockdown.
summary: The pilot reported an oversight causing the aircraft's VFR transponder certification to expire during the COVID-19 lockdown. The aircraft operated outside Class B airspace and at non-towered airports, and the pilot implemented a new tracking system to prevent future lapses.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported departing airport late due to lack of RVR values and below minimum weather.
summary: The flight crew delayed departure at ZZZ due to low visibility and a closed tower while awaiting clarification on using Dispatch-reported RVR. They eventually departed legally after ASOS visibility improved, though the crew noted a lack of clear manual guidance regarding RVR acceptance at uncontrolled fields.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported overshooting an altitude restriction climbing out of LAS. A wake vortex encounter reportedly caused some distraction.
summary: The First Officer reported that while hand-flying a Boeing 737 on the BOACH 8 departure from LAS, the crew overshot the 7,000 ft restriction at ROPPR due to aggressive wake turbulence avoidance. The Captain corrected the altitude to 7,000 ft after the overshoot, attributing the error to missed visual cues and the lack of an audible warning with the altitude window set to FL190.

synopsis: Flight crew reported receiving three STAR changes and multiple vectors from ATC, consequently increasing the workload to the point that errors were made.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple last-minute STAR and runway changes from DEN ATC during the approach, causing high workload, an FMC lockup, and a navigation error. The aircraft was vectored high and rushed to a visual approach, resulting in a stressful landing outside the crew's comfort zone due to ATC's disarray.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported departing with an inoperative safety item that should have been inspected by maintenance prior to departure.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a 35-minute delay for an aircraft swap due to a broken lavatory, followed by a hot cabin requiring APU cooling. During pushback, a Flight Attendant reported a broken aft door banner snap, which was later found installed on the wrong side, likely due to maintenance rushing after the delay.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported seeing a light aircraft on short final to ZZZ airport suffer the effects of jet blast from a company aircraft moving into position on a parallel runway.
summary: A pilot observed a small general aviation aircraft landing on Runway XXL at ZZZ experience severe controllability issues due to jetblast from a large Company aircraft moving forward between the runways. The small aircraft executed a go-around, and the reporter recommends ATC revise procedures to prevent large aircraft from moving near the threshold while small aircraft are landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reported the airline schedulers routinely schedule pilots from night flights to morning flights which causes pilot fatigue.
summary: A pilot reported that a schedule change requiring an early morning deadhead flight after only five hours of sleep created unsafe fatigue stress. The pilot attributed the issue to schedulers ignoring circadian rhythms and recommended mandatory fatigue training for scheduling staff.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported difficulty understanding ATC instructions possibly due to the Controller wearing a face mask.
summary: During descent into ZZZ, a pilot reported that an Air Traffic Controller's instructions were difficult to understand, sounding as if the controller was wearing a mask. The pilot verified every instruction to ensure safety, noting that this communication barrier posed a significant safety threat.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported Electric Stabilizer Trim inoperative.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring encountered inoperative electric stabilizer trim during initial climb from Runway XXR. They executed the QRH checklist, returned for a flaps 15 landing with fire trucks standing by, and logged the discrepancy for maintenance.

synopsis: B737 reported descending below a crossing restriction during arrival.
summary: The flight crew descended 200 feet below the 12,000 ft crossing restriction at waypoint ZZZZZ1 due to FMS VNAV logic conflicting with ATC instructions during a weather deviation. The controller subsequently amended the clearance to 11,000 ft after the crew failed to manually arrest the descent in time.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported Captain aborted takeoff due to Master Caution light illumination.
summary: The Captain aborted the takeoff at 75 knots after an unexplained Master Caution light illuminated. Post-abort, the number 2 Engine Control annunciator was found lit, leading to a taxi back to the gate and an aircraft swap.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported two missed approaches with lack of information about nearest possible alternate.
summary: The crew executed two go-arounds due to windshear and microburst warnings during final approach in gusty conditions. They diverted to a nearby airport not in their FMC or charts due to low fuel, landing safely but noting a need for better alternate airport data.

synopsis: An Air carrier pilot reported an ill passenger. All coordination and service was accomplished appropriately.
summary: The flight crew managed a diabetic collapse on an oceanic flight to ZZZ, coordinating with Medlink and ATC for priority handling. The aircraft received radar vectors and a preferential runway assignment for a normal landing, allowing EMTs to treat the passenger upon arrival.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported an NMAC event during final approach due in part to ATC aircraft traffic sequencing as well as late runway change.
summary: Pilots inbound to Denver on a 16L approach received an RA at 1500 AGL after Aircraft Z encroached on their final from parallel runway 16R. The reporter attributed the conflict to ATC spacing errors, early speed restrictions, and a lack of notification regarding the encroaching traffic.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported ground crew did not follow SOP during pushback.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of radio communication with the ground crew during pushback due to a broken headset cord. Although the tug remained connected and the tow bar was never verbally confirmed as disconnected, the crew set brakes and waited for a supervisor to resolve the equipment failure before receiving clearance to start engines.

synopsis: Captain reported not being stabilized for approach prior to 1000ft. because they had difficulty requesting lower and slower from ATC.
summary: The flight crew encountered high and fast conditions on a visual approach to DEN due to ATC oversight and radio congestion. They stabilized by 600 feet using gear extension and executed a safe touchdown, later debriefing on CRM and stabilized approach criteria.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported two passengers became verbally abusive to the flight attendants when they were asked to follow face mask policy.
summary: Two passengers verbally abused a flight attendant after refusing to wear face masks. The Captain removed the passengers from the aircraft before departure due to the threat of continued abuse, a decision supported by other passengers.

synopsis: Ground employee reported large numbers of aircraft are being moved in and out of storage without proper procedures in place.
summary: Aircraft towing crews reported unsafe conditions while moving aircraft in remote, non-standard storage areas due to high rotation rates and staffing shortages. The lack of designated markings, standard operating procedures for spacing, and safety advocates forced crews to rely on judgment and concrete cracks for clearance, while setup crews lacked warning systems during moves.

synopsis: Ground employee reported that some personnel are allowed to bypass the temperature check.
summary: A crew member reported that some personnel bypassed mandatory pre-work temperature checks, while management instructed others to ignore the violation. The reporter stated that if this group remains unchecked, the crew cannot work with them.

synopsis: Ground employee reported there is a lack of cleaning supplies in the ramp break room.
summary: Cabin crew reported that the ramp break room frequently runs out of cleaning materials despite requests to management. Currently, only one bottle of soap and a few napkins remain, which are insufficient for the next hour.

synopsis: A Customer Service Gate Agent reported a known fault with a jetbridge requires using non standard procedures to operate correctly.
summary: The pilot reported a right canopy retraction failure at the gate, where a ramp agent and mechanic attempted to pull the jetbridge with the canopy down using an unsafe workaround. The pilot challenged this non-compliant procedure, which risks aircraft damage, and notified supervisors after the mechanic incorrectly claimed it was standard operating procedure.

synopsis: Airline ramp personnel reported, during cargo unloading, a Hover board incorrectly transported with battery installed and no battery form attached.
summary: Ramp crew found a green-tagged single-wheel hoverboard in the aircraft pit after a passenger attempted to board it. The device lacked a battery form, appeared to be a rechargeable lithium-ion unit, and did not resemble a mobility device.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reported aborting takeoff due to burning odor in the cockpit.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 95 knots due to a heavy burning rubber odor in the flight deck, suspecting an onboard fire. The aircraft stopped on the runway and returned to the gate for maintenance assessment.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported an error in current NOTAM.
summary: The flight crew encountered a conflicting NOTAM regarding a crane and RVR restriction on DFW Runway 17L, which Approach was unaware of and Jeppesen omitted. Despite the discrepancy, the crew landed safely but reported the issue to safety control to request NOTAM clarification or deletion.

synopsis: Flight Crew reported number 1 engine failed in flight, resulting in an inflight engine shutdown and a diversion.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the crew experienced Engine 1 shudders and an oil temperature spike above redline, suspected to be compressor stalls. They executed the ENG OIL TEMP HI checklist, shut down the engine, and landed uneventfully at ZZZ for inspection.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported Hazmat documentation errors due to late flight crew notification of 'Dry Ice Supplemental Procedures'.
summary: Flight crew and ramp agents at Aircraft X received a late ACARS notification during pushback regarding FOM 10.37 dry ice procedures, which prohibited live animals. The crew later discovered the dispatch paperwork was incorrect and violated company policy, attributing the error to excessive delays, unfamiliar ground staff, and late operational communication.

synopsis: First Officer reported loss of cabin pressure after maintenance had replaced a cargo door sill, resulting in an expedited descent and an air turnback.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude climb to 9,000 feet during climbout after maintenance replaced a rear cargo door seal. The crew donned oxygen masks and returned to the departure airport for a safe landing, with maintenance later suspecting the new seal was faulty.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that during takeoff the galley trash door opened but the trash bin did not move.
summary: A flight attendant flying A position reported that a trash door opened shortly after takeoff due to human error, though the bin remained secured. The crew member safely closed the door with no further incident occurring.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported a cabin fumes event resulting in removal of two flight attendants from flight, who were treated for carbon monoxide poisoning.
summary: Flight Attendants and pilots experienced toxic fumes and haze in a parked aircraft after an air truck was connected due to broken APU and jetway cooling. The crew suffered symptoms like burning eyes and nausea, with hospital tests confirming carbon monoxide exposure, yet the airline resumed operations at the same gate, exposing new personnel and passengers.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported an unsecured galley cart rolled into and hit the aircraft door during landing causing damage.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a loose cart in the main cabin struck and damaged an aircraft door upon landing. The Captain logged the incident, and the reporter recommended double-checking cart locks and brakes before takeoff or landing to prevent future damage.

synopsis: Flight attendants reported that a deadheading pilot did not follow face mask policy during the flight.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a deadheading First Officer in uniform failed to keep his mask covering his nose and mouth during a flight to ZZZ. The crew member instructed him to comply, after which he adjusted his mask, though the reporter urged management to enforce the policy to prevent future non-compliance.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported that a child was not wearing a face mask and was coughing. Parents attempted to put mask on the child, but were not successful.
summary: A flight attendant encountered a child over two years old who refused to wear a mask while coughing profusely. The child kicked the attendant and struggled with parents who claimed previous flights allowed non-compliance, resulting in the child remaining unmasked during descent.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported having trouble with a mother and two young children wearing face masks on the flight.
summary: A flight attendant and captain managed a passenger and her children who refused to wear mandatory masks during the flight. The mother cited medical excuses and claimed the children lost their masks, prompting crew warnings, a captain's announcement, and dispatch notification before the family eventually complied.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported a non-revenue passenger was not wearing a face mask and had to be told to comply with the policy.
summary: A flight attendant reported a non-revenue employee seated in X3 who repeatedly failed to wear a mask covering his nose and mouth despite reminders. The passenger did not eat or drink during the flight, and the crew member expressed frustration over having to police company employees who understand but refuse to comply with mask policies.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported passengers taking off their face masks to order coffee or tea and then waiting for it to cool off, without face masks on.
summary: Cabin crew reported that passengers removed masks to place coffee orders, waited in the aisle without masks, and failed to wait for row completion before unmasking. The crew recommended simplifying service by removing coffee and tea, offering only water and soft drinks.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported only serving sealed drinks and no coffee during flight. Flight Attendant did not feel safe serving coffee.
summary: A cabin crew member served only sealed beverages and declined coffee service during the flight due to safety concerns regarding the COVID-19 pandemic. The reporter noted that the A Flight Attendant had previously opposed extending inflight service and stated an intent to continue prioritizing safety.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported two passengers were not compliant wearing face masks during the flight. Another passenger was uncomfortable with them not wearing the face masks and confronted the crew.
summary: Cabin crew reported that passengers in row XY repeatedly failed to wear masks properly, causing another passenger to confront the crew in the galley. The crew issued a final warning to the non-compliant passengers before the flight ended.

synopsis: Technician reported disagreement between departments concerning Fan Blade mapping and reporting for tracking purposes.
summary: Maintenance Control and Aircraft Records disagreed on attaching fan blades to the engine versus the -9 component for Aircraft X. The reporter attributed this to conflicting interpretations of the manual and unreliable fan maps, urging strict adherence to procedures to keep blades on the engine.

synopsis: Technician reported difficulty in locating correct reference for replacing the Rudder Trim Knob.
summary: A mechanic replaced a loose rudder trim knob on Aircraft X using the AMM instead of the CMM, leading to a rudder trim runaway event on takeoff from ZZZ. The Rudder Trim Control Panel was subsequently replaced, and the report cites the lack of clear AMM direction to the CMM as the cause.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Private Pilot reported an uneventful landing after a power line strike during final approach to landing.
summary: A pilot struck an unmarked power line while practicing an off-field landing at dusk, cutting the wire with the propeller and damaging the wing strut and leading edge. The aircraft returned safely to the airport with a vibrating propeller, and the pilot attributed the incident to poor visibility and lack of line markings.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported making a forced landing on a highway after experiencing engine power loss.
summary: The pilot reported an enroute engine power loss with RPM between 1200-1400 and manifold pressure between 12-13 inches. This forced an emergency landing on a highway, selected as the best illuminated option.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported after announcing on Unicom intentions to enter runway and starting to back taxi, an opposite landing aircraft performed a go-around.
summary: A pilot holding short of Runway XX back-taxed after receiving no radio responses or ADSB data from an inbound single-engine aircraft. The inbound pilot subsequently executed a go-around, passing 200 feet above the back-taxiing aircraft, and admitted to missing the initial radio calls.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi Captain reported while on approach and receiving a heading and altitude instruction from ATC, shortly thereafter receiving a terrain alert from ATC.
summary: A Part 91 pilot descending on a STAR arrival received a TCAS RA to climb and turn away from a canyon while on a controller-issued vector. The pilot noted the original heading would have directed the aircraft toward terrain with a peak of 5,720 ft.

synopsis: A Flight Instructor conducting training in IMC reported a near miss with an aircraft not identified or in contact with ATC.
summary: During an IFR dual training flight in a Cirrus SR-20 at 5,000 feet within a 4,000–6,000-foot block, the instructor and student received a traffic alert from the L3 Skywatch system and executed a right turn to avoid a VFR aircraft. The reporter attributes the conflict to the other pilot operating VFR inside the assigned block altitude despite IMC conditions.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor pilot reported a NMAC with an aircraft on final at an airport with the Tower closed at the time of the event.
